title: Post-1.0 compatibility and external-verifier roadmap
description:
## What & scope
Group the four explicitly registered post-1.0 roadmap deliverables without pulling any of them into G0-G4: the APFS Local durability profile after an asupersync non-io_uring backend exists, the harder Windows profile after APFS, BoltCompatProfileV2 write support with its own conformance gate, and the dependency-free external verifier SDK. This is a discoverability/closure epic, not a 1.0 release prerequisite.

## Why
Standalone roadmap tasks were semantically correct but easy to miss in epic-oriented planning. One post-1.0 aggregate makes deferral explicit, preserves prerequisite order, and prevents future documentation from silently implying these capabilities shipped in 1.0.

## Design and boundary
Each child retains its exact platform/protocol/proof ownership and independent gate. Every child depends on its declared foundation/1.0 prerequisite; this epic depends on the children. No G0-G4 gate, 1.0 workstream epic, or capability manifest may depend on this epic. Reserved schemas/profiles remain frozen where the plan requires, while activation stays absent until each child passes.

## Success Criteria
- All four children close with their own unit/property/fault/conformance/E2E and detailed diagnostic evidence.
- APFS remains blocked on the named asupersync backend; Windows remains ordered after APFS; Bolt V2 passes its write/TCK/differential corpus; the verifier SDK proves dependency-free independent verification.
- A graph test proves this epic is downstream of G4 and never in any G0-G4 prerequisite closure.
- Capability/docs tests prove each unfinished roadmap item is advertised as absent/post-1.0, never partial.
- The roadmap rollup emits versioned JSONL with child id, prerequisite/gate state, platform/profile/version, evidence references, verdict, and replay commands; no child may inherit another child or G4 green bar.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: attaching post-1.0 tasks to W10/W11/G4 epics in the blocking direction, silently dropping them, or representing them as vague prose. Risk is roadmap drift; explicit graph and capability tests keep status honest.

## Provenance
Plan registered platform/compatibility roadmap after §19 workstreams and §15 external verification/publication goals.

title: Synthetic mutation rows for island_root_missing_deny and island_inherits_forbid
description:
Both codes have been seen to fire by hand against a passing control — most
recently on all three landed islands (fgdb-w1-unsafe-islands-eqrq: remove the
root deny -> island_root_missing_deny; add [lints] workspace = true ->
island_inherits_forbid; exit 1 in both, against a control that exits 0). Neither
has a PERMANENT row that fires it.

The live-scan test in tools/registry-check/tests/workspace_topology.rs asserts
both policy directions positively and refuses to be vacuous, so the property is
locked. But a law whose violation code is never fired by the suite is a law
whose diagnostic can rot: rename the code, or make the branch unreachable, and
the suite still passes.

What is needed: the live-tree law evaluator has to accept a SYNTHETIC scan the
way posture_closures already does, so a fixture can present an island whose root
lost its deny, or one that grew the inherited lint table, without a real crate
existing on disk.

title: PROPOSAL for the owner: re-key the AGENTS.md memorialization clause from 'is a revert' to 'is memorialized' — agent-authored, NOT to be landed by any agent
description:
OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. This bead exists ONLY to carry a proposed one-line edit to
AGENTS.md to the owner. AGENTS.md is the project constitution and RULE 0 makes it the
owner's document. NO AGENT MAY LAND THIS. Filed by pane4 at the orchestrator's
instruction after the same proposal was twice queued for landing and twice stopped;
the tree has never carried the change (verified: AGENTS.md line 86 is unmodified,
`git log --all -- AGENTS.md` shows four commits, none of them this edit).

=====================================================================
THE EXACT DIFF (AGENTS.md, line 86, one line, nothing else)
=====================================================================
-These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan. Violating any of them is a revert, memorialized in `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md`.
+These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan. Violating any of them is memorialized in `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` — whether the repair is a revert or, as the Backwards Compatibility rule requires, a fix in place.

=====================================================================
THE REASON (measured, not argued)
=====================================================================
The clause makes memorialization conditional on an event this project has never
performed and is forbidden by AGENTS.md itself from performing.

Measured over all 705 commits reachable at e0bddd3:
  commits produced by `git revert` .................. 1
  commits with any revert semantics in the subject .. 3
  of those, reverting a DOCTRINE VIOLATION .......... 0

All three are beads bookkeeping (46e654e, 3a7248f, 1994b8e), and 1994b8e is a
catalog write withdrawn because a construction-order law forbade it — the system
working, not a violation of it.

The reason there are zero is in the same document. Under Backwards Compatibility
AGENTS.md mandates: "Never create compatibility shims or wrappers for deprecated
APIs. Just fix the code directly." This project therefore repairs doctrine
violations IN PLACE and always has. The 44 entries now in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md
are all in-place repairs; not one is a revert.

=====================================================================
WHAT BREAKS IF THIS IS NOT DONE
=====================================================================
1. The clause's literal reading can only ever produce an EMPTY ledger. A future
   reader who takes it literally is correct to conclude that all 44 entries are
   out of scope, and the correct action under that reading is to delete them. The
   entry floor (currently 44, in scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh) would then go
   red — but the argument would be "the constitution says reverts", with the
   constitution on the side of emptying the memorial.

2. It leaves the doctrine self-contradictory in a way that is now load-bearing
   rather than cosmetic: one clause requires a revert, another forbids the
   mechanism. Before m172 nothing read either clause, so the contradiction was
   inert. A registered live gate now reads both.

3. It is the vacuity class the project has spent the night closing, one level up.
   A universally-quantified obligation whose domain is empty reports green forever
   (cf. fgdb-fginv-spine-zero-live-checkers-v05b, where 20 clauses were stub and
   "CI cross-checks that every ID has a live checker" was true and empty; and
   fgdb-regcheck-closure-vacuous-no-control-hp0f). Leaving it as-is preserves
   exactly that shape inside the doctrine's own enforcement sentence.

=====================================================================
WHAT DOES NOT BREAK, AND WHY THIS IS NOT URGENT
=====================================================================
Nothing is red today and nothing goes red if this is declined. The gate enforces
BOTH readings already: law 4 requires every revert-semantics commit to carry a
structural disposition (3 of 3 dispositioned, so the literal clause is guarded and
would fire the moment a revert lands), while the ledger is populated from the event
that actually occurs. Declining costs only the contradiction in item 2.

If the owner prefers the opposite resolution — keep "is a revert" and narrow the
ledger to reverts only — that is coherent too, but it requires deleting 44 entries
and lowering the floor, and it should be an explicit owner decision rather than a
side effect. NAME WHICH RESOLUTION YOU WANT; do not let an agent infer it.

=====================================================================
PROVENANCE
=====================================================================
Findings: fgdb-negative-evidence-ledger-does-not-exist-m172 (closed; 37c28c0,
a3a5f8c). Ledger entries NE-0042/0043/0044 record the surrounding defects.
Related: fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq is the natural home for the general law "every repo
path AGENTS.md names must exist", which m172's gate now implements as its law 1.

title: Appendix A a14: adjudicate five bodyless HA/GC candidates as not-a-durable-schema
description:
Five a14 candidates are census 'named-concept-no-body' / 'prose-definition-no-body', each carrying a definition-without-structural-body ambiguity with EXACTLY ONE affected key (top|Symbol):

  CurrentCheckpointObservation, GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard,
  MandatoryInventoryClassRegistry, RegisteredStrongRef, RetiredLocal

All five take the precedented a01 RemoteGrantTargetRef route: leave the key unprojected and the adjudication is FORCED not-a-durable-schema (verify_ambiguity_adjudications makes not-a-durable-schema a violation if ANY resolved key is projected, so the resolution is forced by catalog state, not chosen). Adjudications must FOLLOW mints.

Two have a real structural home elsewhere, which is NOT a contradiction because it is a different source key:
  - CurrentCheckpointObservation: the top| key is bodyless, but the ARM key
    arm|MandatoryInventoryEntry|MandatoryInventoryEntry.value|CurrentCheckpointObservation
    has a body and is released by the MandatoryInventoryEntry wire mint landed under fgdb-27sr.
  - RetiredLocal: bodyless at top level; it exists as a UNIT ARM of the group_role field
    union at plan:1544 (group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id}|RetiredLocal). 8 source
    occurrences, 0 structural at top level. That arm belongs to its own slice, not a14.

RegisteredStrongRef additionally needs the source erratum filed separately.

Adding adjudication rows also needs reciprocal AmbiguityAdjudicationContractPin entries in appendix_a.rs plus EXPECTED_AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_COUNT and the contract sha.

Measured by pane2 under fgdb-27sr.

title: private_subject.sh leaks ~82MB per gate run with no lifetime or owner: 18.5GB across 113 dirs, and the tmp pool is 98.5% ours not foreign
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 02:1x by pane3, at HEAD eda507f, while disk was at 8.8G free
(100%). This is a TOOLING LEAK, not housekeeping.

## The number

  /data/tmp/tmp.* pool                165 dirs   22.2 GB

  by producer:
    private_subject.sh                113 dirs   18.5 GB   <-- one library
    appendix-baseline harness          19 dirs    3.7 GB
    other registry-check gate          27 dirs    0.3 GB
    unclassified / possibly foreign     6 dirs    0.1 GB

**159 of 165 dirs, and 22.6 of 22.7 GB, are OURS.** The pool has been
characterised to the owner as foreign and off-limits. It is 98.5% our own gate
output. Age: 104 of the private_subject dirs are dated 2026-07-26, 9 are
2026-07-27 -- i.e. one and two days of swarm gate runs, never reaped.

For scale: 22.2 GB is more than TWICE the 8.8 GB free at the time of measurement.
Reclaiming this pool alone ends the disk emergency without touching the 52G
foreign target dir or the 79G of finished-session scratchpads.

## The mechanism, and it is documented in the leaking file itself

`scripts/lib/private_subject.sh` is sourced by three gates:
    scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh
Each `mktemp -d`s a fresh work dir and calls `subject_build`, which writes
`libregistry_check.rlib` (64 MB) + `registry-check` (18 MB) = ~82 MB per run,
per script. The library's own header states the cost and the policy:

    #   73MB  per script per run, so 219MB for one full scripts/check.sh
    # On 2026-07-26 that landed on a volume at 95% carrying 9594 stale
    # `/data/tmp/tmp.*` directories from every gate that mktemps. Reaping those is
    # swarm hygiene and is deliberately NOT done here: nothing in this library, or
    # in any script that sources it, deletes a file.

So the leak is KNOWN, MEASURED, and consciously deferred to "swarm hygiene" --
except no swarm hygiene process existed, so the deferral was to nobody. A
81-82 MB allocation per gate run with no owner and no reaper is how a 906 GB
volume reached 100%.

## Why the current design is right about deletion and wrong about lifetime

Nothing in the library deleting a file is CORRECT under RULE 1 and must stay: a
gate script must never be the thing that removes data. The defect is that the
artifact has no declared LIFETIME and no declared OWNER, so "do not delete here"
became "never deleted anywhere".

## Fix options, cheapest first (not implemented -- this bead is the measurement)

1. CONTENT-ADDRESS AND SHARE THE SUBJECT. The three gates build a byte-identical
   subject from the same tree. Build once into a path keyed by the source hash
   (`/data/tmp/fgdb-subject-<sha>/`) and have all three reuse it. Turns 219 MB per
   check.sh into 82 MB per distinct tree state, and makes reaping trivial because
   the key says which trees are stale. `subject_is_fresh` already computes the
   freshness predicate this needs.
2. DECLARE A LIFETIME. Have the library write a `REAPABLE-AFTER` stamp into each
   work dir and add one accountable reaper (the orchestrator's
   scripts/disk_hygiene.sh) that honours it. Keeps the no-delete rule inside the
   gates while giving the artifact an owner.
3. AT MINIMUM, REPORT IT. The library prints nothing about the space it takes.
   Emitting the path and byte count per run would have surfaced 18.5 GB long
   before 100%.

## Cross-check on the claim that this pool is foreign

I classify a dir as ours by a positive marker, not by absence: `bin/registry-check`
present => private_subject.sh; a file named `appendix-baseline.*` => the appendix
harness. The 6 dirs I could not attribute are left as "possibly foreign" and are
134 MB total, so no reclamation decision turns on them.

## Provenance of this bead

Filed at the orchestrator's request after the pane3 cfg6 inventory (fgdb-cfg6)
showed that five `/data/tmp/tmp.*` dirs attributed to other projects were in fact
this repo's own g0-e2e evidence. That correction is what prompted measuring the
whole pool rather than the five. Sweeping the pool is the orchestrator's call and
goes through their hygiene path; pane3 has deleted nothing.

DO NOT REAP /data/tmp/tmp.G5czm7QFIs until fgdb-ia2b is fixed -- its
spine-baseline.jsonl is the recorded evidence for that bead's script_undeclared
finding.
notes:
LANDED 3caaeb0 -- library and all three call sites, verified end to end. This
supersedes the "designed, not landed" note above; everything it recorded as the
plan is now the shipped code, and the numbers below are from the shipped runs
rather than from a prototype.

THE DEMONSTRATION, three gates against one shared cache:
  subject cache before g0_claims     (empty)
  after g0_claims_e2e.sh             75M, 1 dir   cold build, 12.4s total
  after g0_spine_e2e.sh              75M, 1 dir   4.6s, ZERO new bytes
  after g0_identity_e2e.sh           75M, 1 dir   90s,  ZERO new bytes
Before this commit that sequence cost 3 x 75MB = 225MB, none ever reclaimed.
All three printed "PASS: control: the subject runner reuses one directory and
leaves no residue".

MUTATION-PROVED AGAINST THE SHIPPED CODE, both halves fire:
  runner keyed per run          "subject runner does not reuse: ...-117111336
                                then ...-36398924"
  runner that never publishes   "subject runner left per-run residue:
                                ...partial.588887"
  unmodified runner             PASS in 0.165s, 388KB
Cost 0.5% of the 75MB it protects.

THE CONTROL IS HERMETIC ON PURPOSE, and this is the one design decision worth
carrying forward: my first draft asserted subject-path stability against the LIVE
repository and failed on its first run, because a neighbouring pane committed a
checker source in the 8 seconds between the two acquisitions. Shipped that way it
would have redded all three gates at random -- a worse defect than the leak it
guards. It now runs against a throwaway fixture crate, so it tests the RUNNER's
logic and nothing about the tree's stillness.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated in the header so the next reader does not have to
re-derive it: it is a 3x cut, not a bound. 111 commits touched
tools/registry-check/src over the window in which 113 of these directories
appeared -- 1.02 per commit -- so sharing across runs recovers almost nothing;
what is guaranteed is sharing within one check.sh. Reuse and self-cleanup are
mutually exclusive (if the first gate cleaned up on exit the other two could not
reuse), so bounding the cache needs an owner with delete authority. That is this
bead's option 2 and it is the remaining work. Nothing in the library deletes a
file: publication is `mv -T` onto a path that does not exist, and the loser of
that race keeps its own copy rather than removing anyone's.

TWO PRE-EXISTING REDS SURFACED BY THE VERIFICATION RUNS, filed as fgdb-njpk:
unclaimed_prose on docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md (reds claims and spine; the file
landed in a3a5f8c and appears 0 times in claims_lint.toml) and
"expected exactly 10 passing BodyDigest recipes, found 14" (reds identity).
Neither is caused by this change -- its diff touches only scripts/.

FRESH EVIDENCE FOR fgdb-kwoz: g0_identity_e2e.sh's own workdir was 568MB in this
run, against a 75MB subject. The evidence half of the leak is now the larger half
by a wide margin on that gate specifically.

DISK COST OF THE VERIFICATION ITSELF, since this bead is about disk: 75MB subject
plus 20MB (claims) + 14MB (spine) + 568MB (identity) of workdirs = 677MB, all in
my scratchpad and all named below for reclaim. Under the old design the same three
runs would have cost 827MB.

RECLAIMABLE, MINE, NAMED NOT DELETED:
  <scratch>/1j16/run-identity  568MB   g0_identity_e2e evidence
  <scratch>/1j16/cache          149MB  prototype subjects
  <scratch>/1j16/cache3         149MB  prototype subjects
  <scratch>/1j16/cache2          75MB  prototype subject
  <scratch>/1j16/shared          75MB  the shared subject the three runs used
  <scratch>/1j16/run-claims      20MB
  <scratch>/1j16/run-claims2     20MB
  <scratch>/1j16/run-spine       14MB
  <scratch>/1j16/ctl, /1j16/land  ~2MB residue-control fixtures
  <scratch>/build ~330MB, <scratch>/stage 24MB, attr/ mut/ mut2/ ft79/ r7k1/ ~3MB
  <scratch> = /data/tmp/claude-1000/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/1c3e6419-f159-45d5-a27a-7727a71ee659/scratchpad
The 113 /data/tmp/tmp.* dirs (18.01GB) stay with the owner. Still do not reap
/data/tmp/tmp.G5czm7QFIs -- fgdb-ia2b's evidence.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: the retention policy (option 2). The per-run leak is
closed at the source; the cache now grows one directory per distinct tree state
and nothing bounds that.

title: Appendix A a04 field remainder: 229 candidates across six distinct blocking laws
description:
a04's field layer is 35 of 264 landed and exhausted of mechanically derivable rows. The 229
unlanded field candidates are NOT one problem — they are six, each with a different blocking law,
and three of them are not "work pending" at all. Enumerated so no future holder re-censuses a04 to
rediscover this.

=== NOT LANDABLE, EVER — STRUCTURAL, NO RULING REACHES THEM ===

 16  WIRE-OWNED INTERIORS.  Law: `field_unresolved_schema` ("containing_schema resolves nowhere").
     Field owner resolution admits `logical | bootstrap | physical | prebootstrap`. WIRE IS NOT IN
     THAT LIST, so a field whose containing_schema is a registered wire type can never land as a
     durable_fields row; its interior is committed by the wire payload digest instead.
     Owners: RemoteRetentionControlSpec (9, wire union), CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec (3, record),
     AuthorityLocalCertificateHeader, AdvanceRemoteConfigurationEvidenceSpec,
     ValidateRemoteConfigurationAnchorSpec, RaftMaintenanceCommand (1 each).
     ACTION: none. Do not file these as pending work. This is the entry most likely to be
     re-counted as landable by a census that accepts a wire owner — mine did, and it inflated my
     own first report by 16.

  3  DUPLICATE (owner, stable_name) PAIRS already covered by a landed row. A field row is keyed on
     (containing_schema, stable_name), so two source occurrences at different paths collapse into
     one row. ACTION: none.

=== BLOCKED ON A SOURCE READING — NOT A CLASS OR ORDER RULING ===

172  THE SOURCE SPELLS NO EXACT TYPE AT ALL. The census reports `exact_types = []` because the plan
     writes the field name with no `:type` suffix. There is no law to satisfy: `exact_wire_type` is
     a required column and the source supplies nothing to derive it from. This is the largest block
     in a04 by a wide margin and it needs the plan owner to either type these fields or rule that
     they are prose rather than durable members.

 25  EXACT TYPE IS NOT A REGISTERED WIRE ROW. Law: `field_unresolved_wire_type` ("exact_wire_type
     resolves nowhere"). The spellings are inline record literals
     (`[{member_id,replica_namespace,...}]`), arm-set expressions
     (`Stable|Joint{old_epoch,new_epoch}`, `Active|Joining|Draining`), bare generic parameters
     (`K`, `K+1`), and `[]`. Each needs either a wire type minted for it or a ruling that the
     shape is not a registered type.

  3  TARGET NAMED BUT REGISTERED IN NO SLICE. Law: `ref_target_unresolved` ("named target resolves
     nowhere"). AuditSignerJournalRoot, CertificateAttemptLedger,
     RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionRecord. Out of a04's scope — whoever owns those symbols must
     register them first.

  1  TYPE CONFLICT across occurrences: the census reports `type_conflict = true`, so the source
     spells the same field with two different types. An erratum, not a modelling choice.

  1  `LegacyTransferEvidenceRef` on RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot.transfer_evidence_ref. It is a
     registered wire union, but ZERO landed field rows use it as an exact_wire_type, so its
     `reference_semantics` has no precedent. I declined to guess: picking one would write an
     invented durable contract, and reference_semantics is forced by the source wrapper spelling
     rather than chosen.

=== ALREADY ROUTED, LISTED FOR COMPLETENESS ===

  3  record-shaped wire type -> fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd
  3  ambiguous, need adjudication first (adjudication follows minting, never precedes it)

=== RECONCILIATION, measured rather than hand-added ===
The authoritative counts come from the catalog and the census, not from summing the groups above:
  264  a04 field candidates in the frozen census (the slice row's field_candidate_count)
   35  [[field]] rows landed for a04 in the catalog at e6b75e0
  229  unlanded
The per-reason groups above are measured with /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p3a04-fields.rs, whose buckets
sum to 264 but attribute 4 of the 35 landed rows to a type bucket instead of its "already landed"
bucket, because its landed check runs after a slice line-range filter that those 4 fall outside. So
treat the group counts as the shape of the remainder and the 35/229 split as the arithmetic. Do not
add the groups and expect 229 — I did, got 227, and the gap is that probe artifact rather than
missing rows.

The reusable census is at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p3a04-why.rs — it reports the blocking reason per
field against whatever HEAD it is pointed at, and its owner-class check is the one that must accept
ONLY logical|bootstrap|physical|prebootstrap.
notes:
pane2, HEAD 1843613, token-free, no build, no staged tree. Per-law with
denominators, as asked. FIVE OF SIX SURVIVE RE-DERIVATION. ONE DISSOLVES.

=== DISSOLVED: the LegacyTransferEvidenceRef blocker (1 candidate) ===
The bead says: "It is a registered wire union, but ZERO landed field rows use it
as an exact_wire_type, so its reference_semantics has no precedent. I declined to
guess." The zero is real -- I reproduce it -- but it is precedent for the SYMBOL,
and the governing precedent is for the CLASS.

  LegacyTransferEvidenceRef rows: union + union_arm + wire_type
    (arms LegacyTransferEvidenceRef.meta_local, .imported_meta)
  registered [[reference_union]] rows in the whole catalog: FIVE --
    LocalCommandInputRef, LogicalCommandInputRef, MandatoryInventoryRef,
    MetaAppliedResultRef, ShardProtocolEvidenceRef.
  LegacyTransferEvidenceRef IS NOT ONE OF THEM. It is an ORDINARY union.

  landed [[field]] rows typed by a registered reference union   5, all "strong"
  landed [[field]] rows typed by an ORDINARY union             52, ALL "none"
                                                                (52/52, zero variation)

So reference_semantics is not underdetermined here: an ordinary-union-typed field
carries "none", unanimously, across 52 landed rows. The arms embed by value and
create no reachability edge, which is why. The `-Ref` suffix is what made it look
like a reference, and "a suffix conveys no semantics" is the law that governs.
ACTION: this candidate is landable as reference_semantics = "none" once its owner
and the rest of its row are settled; it is not a ruling and not a guess.

=== SURVIVES, CONFIRMED, AND I TESTED THE FAILURE MODE THE BEAD WARNED OF ===
16 WIRE-OWNED INTERIORS. The bead flags this as "the entry most likely to be
re-counted as landable by a census that accepts a wire owner -- mine did, and it
inflated my own first report by 16." The other way to inflate it is exact-string
matching, which is the error I made and retracted on dkjg. Re-checked all six
owners by RESOLVED BASE NAME against logical|bootstrap|physical|prebootstrap:
    RemoteRetentionControlSpec              9 fields   allowlisted NO   wire yes
    CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec           3          allowlisted NO   wire yes
    AuthorityLocalCertificateHeader         1          allowlisted NO   wire yes
    AdvanceRemoteConfigurationEvidenceSpec  1          allowlisted NO   wire yes
    ValidateRemoteConfigurationAnchorSpec   1          allowlisted NO   wire yes
    RaftMaintenanceCommand                  1          allowlisted NO   wire yes
6 of 6 wire-only under base-name resolution. The law holds; nothing here is
recoverable by a better matcher. Denominator 16 of 229.

3 TARGETS REGISTERED IN NO SLICE. Re-checked by base name across ALL row kinds,
not just logical:
    AuditSignerJournalRoot                    allowlisted NO   wire NO
    CertificateAttemptLedger                  allowlisted NO   wire NO
    RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionRecord  allowlisted NO   wire NO
Registered nowhere in any form. Genuinely out of a04's scope. Denominator 3.

172 SOURCE SPELLS NO EXACT TYPE. Not re-derived independently -- it needs the
frozen source census, which I could not run without staging a tree. Flagged as
the one term in this partition still resting on pane4's probe rather than on a
second reader. It is also 75% of the remainder, so if any number here deserves a
second instrument it is this one.

25 EXACT TYPE IS NOT A REGISTERED WIRE ROW; 3 DUPLICATE (owner, stable_name)
PAIRS; 1 TYPE CONFLICT: taken as measured. The duplicate-pair law follows from the
row key and needs no re-derivation.

=== LICENSING THE ZEROS BY ACCOUNTING, as asked ===
  reference unions in the catalog                     5 present
  of those used by a landed field                     5 consumed   (5/5)
  ordinary unions used by a landed field             52 consumed
  landed field rows using LegacyTransferEvidenceRef   0 consumed of 0 present
    -- the zero is REAL and it is the wrong denominator; the right one is the
       52 ordinary-union-typed rows, which is not zero and is unanimous.

=== WHAT CHANGES FOR THE BEAD ===
The remainder is 229 across SIX laws, of which FIVE are genuine blocks totalling
219 candidates (16 + 3 + 172 + 25 + 3), one is a type-conflict erratum (1), and
the sixth -- the one I was told to expect -- was never a block at all. The
headline "six distinct blocking laws" should read five plus an erratum.

Nothing edited, nothing minted, no token held, no build, no staged tree.
close_reason: Partitioned per-law with denominators. Five of six blocking laws survive re-derivation (16 wire-owned interiors, 6/6 wire-only under base-name resolution; 3 targets registered in no row kind; 172 source-typeless, NOT independently re-derived and flagged; 25 unregistered exact types; 3 duplicate pairs) plus 1 type-conflict erratum. The sixth DISSOLVED: LegacyTransferEvidenceRef is an ordinary union, not one of the catalog's five registered reference unions, and 52 of 52 landed ordinary-union-typed fields carry reference_semantics 'none' -- so its one candidate, RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot.transfer_evidence_ref, is landable by unanimous class precedent rather than a ruling. That candidate is BLOCKED on the mint-and-pin cycle, not done.

title: A14 blocker: adjudicate 14 HA/GC families and two impossible orders
description:
A14 has zero source-forced catalog rows remaining at the bfc9385 archive boundary. Of 18 top-level candidates, 4 are landed and 14 are unminted.

Two reservation-backed logical kinds are UNSATISFIABLE under the settled both-directions construction-order law: ConfigPayloadFloor (reserved 0x0277) and GcProposal (reserved 0x029f). Their StrongRef edges from MandatoryInventory require order >= 25, while GcDecisionRecord.config_payload_floor_ref and GcDecisionRecord.proposal_ref require order <= 15. No integer satisfies 25 <= order <= 15. An authorized reference-strength or construction-order correction is required; do not mint either kind by guessing.

The remaining 12 families are: five confirmed but unreserved class-gated candidates (GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Local>, GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Meta>, GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Shard>, MandatoryInventoryEntry, RemotePreparedIdentity); two ambiguous command-spec candidates needing class adjudication (LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec, LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec); and five name-only/bodyless candidates needing exact source schema before classification (CurrentCheckpointObservation, GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard, MandatoryInventoryClassRegistry, RegisteredStrongRef, RetiredLocal).

Dependent structural residue: one union and two arms remain on unminted MandatoryInventoryEntry. Source spelling is RetainedStrong | CurrentCheckpointObservation, so source tags must be RetainedStrong 0x0001 and CurrentCheckpointObservation 0x0002. The census displays them alphabetically in the opposite order; source order wins.

Field boundary: 122 of 127 fields remain. 90 have unminted owners and 32 have landed logical owners. Across all 122, 67 have NO exact_type in source and 55 have one. Within the 32 landed-owner rows, 23 have no exact_type; the remaining 9 split into 2 blocked by the impossible orders above and 7 blocked by unresolved vocabulary (GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Role>, PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence, CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>, AwaitingPhysicalDisposition, MandatoryInventoryEntry). READY = 0. Ownership is not the dominant blocker.

The pinned source census also omits PayloadReceipt and the physical-plane schemas named by prior a14 analysis; repair or expand the source census before freezing those formats. Acceptance: resolve the two impossible order windows, settle or source-complete all 12 other families, register referenced vocabulary, and preserve source arm order.
close_reason:
All 14 families adjudicated; the two 'impossible' orders were stale and both minted (43388eb), and all 12 remaining families are settled (73c8d92).

Of the bead's four acceptance clauses, two are discharged here and two are carried by dependents that are genuinely blocked rather than skipped:
  DONE  resolve the two impossible order windows -- both re-derived at a live HEAD, both satisfiable, both minted
  DONE  settle or source-complete all 12 other families -- 2 minted, 5 forced not-a-durable-schema (fgdb-1bhc), 1 blocked on a census gap (fgdb-gpzz), 2 escalated as a genuine owner ruling (fgdb-a71s), 1 source erratum (fgdb-dgtv), 1 census reader defect (fgdb-u27g)
  CARRIED  register referenced vocabulary -- blocked by fgdb-dgtv: RegisteredStrongRef is named by value in four schemas but its arms are never spelled, so it is unmintable until the source is fixed
  CARRIED  preserve source arm order -- the order is measured and recorded (RetainedStrong 0x0001 @2039:307, CurrentCheckpointObservation 0x0002 @2039:353, opposite to the census's alphabetical print) and carried by fgdb-8uy7, which lands the union and its two arms

Not closed as fully complete work: two of four clauses live on in dependents. Closed because this bead's own mandate -- adjudicating the 14 families -- is finished, and leaving it open would hide that the remaining work is now four independently-actionable items.

comments.text:
BOTH "IMPOSSIBLE" ORDERS ARE SATISFIABLE AT TODAY'S HEAD (1eba73a). The bead's claim was
a measurement of one HEAD, and that HEAD is gone. Neither kind needs an authorized
reference-strength or construction-order correction; both are ordinary mints.

WHAT THE BEAD SAYS:
  "Their StrongRef edges from MandatoryInventory require order >= 25, while
   GcDecisionRecord.config_payload_floor_ref and GcDecisionRecord.proposal_ref require
   order <= 15. No integer satisfies 25 <= order <= 15."

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. Two independent errors, one temporal and one structural.

  1. TEMPORAL. GcDecisionRecord was minted at construction_order = 15 in adbb1ae. It is
     at 40 today -- pane3's fgdb-oicl min-cut tranches moved it, and their own note on
     fgdb-suhb says why: "Tranche 1 used strip_prefix and therefore under-read exactly
     the class you named -- GcDecisionRecord landed at 25 when its real floor is 40."
     So the "<= 15" ceiling has been wrong since 109d21a.

  2. STRUCTURAL, and it survives independently of the first. GcDecisionRecord is not
     even the binding consumer for ConfigPayloadFloor, and MandatoryInventory is not a
     floor for GcProposal at all -- GcProposal has NO MandatoryInventory edge. The bead
     derived one window from one named consumer and then applied the same pair of bounds
     to both kinds.

RE-DERIVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, unminted interiors CONTRACTED on both sides:

  ConfigPayloadFloor (reservation 0x0277, row_kind logical-kind, identity_class logical)
      DEMAND  >= 25  from MandatoryInventory@25   (ConfigPayloadFloor.mandatory_inventory_root)
      CEILING <= 30  from ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor@30
                     (ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor.source_config_floor_ref)
                     -- NOT GcDecisionRecord, which is now at 40 and non-binding
      => SATISFIABLE [25..30], six values

  GcProposal (reservation 0x029f, row_kind logical-kind, identity_class logical)
      DEMAND  >= 40  from ActivatedRetentionCutSet@40  (GcProposal.activated_retention_cut_ref)
      CEILING <= 40  from GcDecisionRecord@40          (GcDecisionRecord.proposal_ref)
      => SATISFIABLE [40..40], forced to exactly 40

  Consistency between the two: GcProposal.config_payload_floor_ref requires
  o(ConfigPayloadFloor) <= o(GcProposal) = 40, satisfied by all of 25..30.

INSTRUMENT AND ITS CONTROLS. ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/window-probe.rs
Retaining-wrapper matcher copied VERBATIM from order-mincut-repair.rs. Contraction is
done in both directions on purpose: an unminted interior is not a gap, it is a
constraint not yet written down, so reporting only direct edges yields a WIDER window
than exists -- which looks exactly like a pass.
  C1 source manifest sha equals the catalog pin
  C2 a fabricated symbol has an empty window on both sides
  C3 ConfigurationState@5 lies at or below its own ceiling
  C4 (the strong one) EVERY minted symbol's own order lies inside its own computed
     window: 0 of 504 outside. The live tree is green, so a prober that over-tightens
     would be contradicted here by the catalog itself rather than silently mis-advising.
Cross-checked independently of the prober by reading construction_order straight out of
registries/logical_object_kinds.toml: GcDecisionRecord 40, ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor 30,
ActivatedRetentionCutSet 40, MandatoryInventory 25, ShardConfigPayloadFloor 30,
MetaConfigPayloadFloor 35; ConfigPayloadFloor and GcProposal absent (unminted).

RECOMMENDED VALUES. GcProposal = 40 (forced). ConfigPayloadFloor = 30, i.e. the TOP of
its window: ConfigPayloadFloor retains eleven still-unminted Local*Floor kinds
(audit_ticket_fence, backup_restore, branch_key_allocator_merge, continuity_service,
delivery_replay_derived, gc_key_destruction, migration_transition, outcome_conflict,
prepared_owner, receipt_certificate_signer, remote_trust_release), each of which is
forced <= ConfigPayloadFloor when it lands. 30 gives that cohort a [..30] window instead
of [..25], which is the minimum-churn choice; 30 also sits equal-order with its sibling
ShardConfigPayloadFloor@30, and equal orders are legal (dag_future_result fires on >).

MINT SHAPE, PROVEN AGAINST THE adbb1ae PRECEDENT IN THIS SAME SLICE. Both reservations
already exist with row_kind="logical-kind" and identity_class="logical", so class is
proven by the reservation rather than inferred, and no new reservation may be added.
Four coordinated edits per kind:
  1. a [[logical_kind]] row at the reserved code (status "reserved", role_predicate
     "true", max_size_bytes 16777216, golden_corpus corpus/logical/<snake>/)
  2. [[reservation]] disposition  reserved -> existing
  3. [[top_level_candidate]] identity_class  unclassified -> logical
  4. a [[target]] row  source_key "top|<Name>" -> the logical-kind row
Applier written, debugged and preserved at
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/mint27sr.py
It asserts the expected OLD text at every site and the total edit count, and carries a
--negative-control that places a kind at 99 (outside every derived window). Applied to a
scratch mirror it produces exactly +4 blocks (logical_kind 504->506, target 3165->3167).

WHAT REMAINS BEFORE THIS CAN LAND -- mechanical, not decisional. The mint moves several
pins that are compiled consts in tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs
(EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT, EXPECTED_TARGET_SOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_SHA256,
EXPECTED_EXISTING_TYPE_RESERVATION_COUNT / EXPECTED_RESERVED_TYPE_RESERVATION_COUNT,
EXPECTED_RESERVATION_ASSIGNMENT_SHA256) plus the catalog header (target_count,
target_source_assignment_sha256, registry_epoch), and then the six projections must be
rewritten with `registry-check appendix-regenerate`. On the scratch mirror the mint
yields exactly six violations, all of that pin family:
  projection_registry_assignment_drift, projection_owner_assignment_drift,
  projection_row_count, catalog_reservation_assignment_drift,
  catalog_reservation_epoch_drift, catalog_target_source_assignment_drift
NOTE FOR WHOEVER FINISHES THIS: those violations' recomputed values are formatted into
Violation::new's message argument, but the reporting path prints the generic "Appendix A
contract check failed" instead, so the drift CANNOT be read off the output the way the
architecture-check pins can. Derive the new values by calling
target_source_assignment_sha256 / reservation_assignment_sha256 and the counts directly
from a probe against the mutated catalog -- do not hand-compute them.

The twelve other families are untouched by this comment.

comments.text:
ALL 12 REMAINING FAMILIES SETTLED at 8f4f7d7. 3 mint, 5 forced not-a-durable-schema,
2 escalate as a genuine owner ruling, 1 source erratum. No family is left undecided.

METHOD. Class was decided BEFORE any row was written, from the two one-directional
instruments, each rebuilt against THIS tree and each carrying its own falsifier
control. Reference-wrapper set derived from the tree (17 rows, kind="reference_wrapper"),
never hard-coded. Two further candidate laws I invented were FALSIFIED by their own
controls and discarded -- recorded below so nobody re-derives them.

  C1  source manifest sha == catalog pin.
  C2  fabricated symbol scores zero on every column.
  C3  LAW A ("reference target => never wire"): 0 of 182 landed top-level wire
      families are the IMMEDIATE target of a reference wrapper. The first run showed
      1 (Operational) and that was my tokenizer matching a wrapper at ANY nesting
      depth -- Operational is a ROLE ARGUMENT of the target in
      StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPhysicalInventory<Role,Operational>>, not a target.
      Tightened to immediate-argument semantics; law holds 0/182.
  C4  LAW B ("used inside another schema => wire"): 1 of 696 landed field rows carries
      a LOGICAL kind as exact_wire_type, and it is the reconciling precedent, not a
      counterexample -- ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection.source :
      ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource (a16), where that name is a top-level-shaped
      ORDINARY UNION whose host is logical, carried with identity_class="inline",
      reference_semantics="none". So: a by-value-contained UNION resolves to its host and
      that host may be logical. Law B forces wire for RECORDS; it does not for unions.

LICENSING THE ZEROES. A census zero is not an absence. Every occurrence of every family
inside the frozen range 1388..2728 was enumerated and classified (self-definition /
wrapper-target / by-value member / arm-head / prose), consumed vs present. This caught
RemotePreparedIdentity: census law B = 0, but the source spells
`prepared_owner:RemotePreparedIdentity` inside the "A receipt binds {...}" body, whose
owner (PayloadReceipt) is the census gap THIS BEAD ALREADY RECORDS. The census zero was
a blind spot; the containment is real.

=== MINT (3 families, forced) ===

GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Local|Meta|Shard>  =>  LOGICAL, ONE bare-named kind row.
  Forced twice over, independently:
  (a) Neither logical_object_kinds.toml nor wire_types.toml has ANY generic-carrying
      name (0 and 0). So all three signatures land on one bare row either way.
  (b) Landed precedent for multi-signature symbols is 4 of 4 LOGICAL, each mapping N
      role-specialized candidates onto ONE target row with the siblings flipped and
      target-less: ResultReleaseEvidence (<Local> carries it, <Meta>/<Role> do not),
      PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate, RecoveryBridgeSpec, GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec.
      Zero are wire.
  (c) Each body is a single-arm generic whole-schema union (`LocalStandalone{...}` etc.),
      and a generic whole-schema union can never be wire-backed -- union_name is looked up
      WITH its signature and 0 of 505 wire names carry one. Minting a wire host would
      strand the union permanently.
  Law B does fire (cancellation_authority:GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Role> in
  GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec) and is OVERRIDDEN by the C4 precedent above: the
  contained thing is a union, so it resolves to a logical host.
  Shape: 1 [[logical_kind]] at a FRESH code above 0x051d (no reservation exists -- do NOT
  add one, the bijection forbids it), 1 [[target]] on top|GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Local>,
  and all THREE [[top_level_candidate]] rows flipped unclassified -> logical.

MandatoryInventoryEntry  =>  WIRE record.
  Law B fires cleanly: MandatoryInventory.ordered_entries[MandatoryInventoryEntry], by
  value, no wrapper. Law A silent. No reservation.
  Releases the residue this bead names: the FIELD-LEVEL union MandatoryInventoryEntry.value
  (union_path != owner, so no parent contract and no variant rows) and its 2 arms.
  ARM TAGS ARE SOURCE-ORDER, CONFIRMED BY COLUMN: RetainedStrong @2039:307 = 0x0001,
  CurrentCheckpointObservation @2039:353 = 0x0002. The census arm_names print is
  alphabetical and gives the OPPOSITE order; taking it would be a silent durable defect.
  Its 9 field candidates CANNOT land on a wire host (fields need a non-wire host) -- that
  is expected, not a blocker: the entry is a by-value payload, and its one real reference
  member (availability_receipt_refs[StrongRef]) is a BARE StrongRef with no named target,
  which is unlandable in any shape anyway.

RemotePreparedIdentity  =>  WIRE record.
  Law B fires from the SOURCE TEXT (see "licensing the zeroes"). Law A silent. No
  reservation. Body is an inline-record at 2035.

=== FORCED not-a-durable-schema (5 families) ===
RegisteredStrongRef, CurrentCheckpointObservation, GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard,
MandatoryInventoryClassRegistry, RetiredLocal.
  All five are census `named-concept-no-body` / `prose-definition-no-body`, each carrying a
  definition-without-structural-body ambiguity with EXACTLY ONE affected key (top|Symbol).
  This is the precedented a01 RemoteGrantTargetRef route: leave the key unprojected and the
  adjudication is FORCED not-a-durable-schema. A bodyless family has nothing to mint --
  law B tells you what class to use IF you mint, it does not manufacture a body.
  Two of these have a real structural home elsewhere, which is not a contradiction because
  it is a different source key:
    CurrentCheckpointObservation -- top| key is bodyless, but the ARM key
      arm|MandatoryInventoryEntry|MandatoryInventoryEntry.value|CurrentCheckpointObservation
      HAS a body and lands with the MandatoryInventoryEntry mint above.
    RetiredLocal -- top| key is bodyless; it exists as a UNIT ARM of the group_role field
      union at 1544 (`group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id}|RetiredLocal`), which belongs to
      that slice, not a14. 8 occurrences, 0 structural at top level.

=== SOURCE ERRATUM (1) ===
RegisteredStrongRef is a genuine VOCABULARY GAP, and it is the thing actually blocking the
"7 fields blocked by unresolved vocabulary" line in this bead. FOUR schemas name it BY VALUE
-- strong_dependency_refs[RegisteredStrongRef] @1830, terminal_floor_ref:RegisteredStrongRef
@1854, delta_payload_ref:RegisteredStrongRef<DeltaPayload> @1926, typed_ref:RegisteredStrongRef
@2039 -- while the source defines it only as "the closed generated union of role-legal typed
strong-reference encodings", with the arms GENERATED and never spelled. So it is by-value
vocabulary with no body: unmintable, and every field that names it is unlandable until the
source spells its arms. That is a plan erratum, not a mint. Note the 1926 site applies a
generic (RegisteredStrongRef<DeltaPayload>) that the bare definition does not declare.

=== GENUINE OWNER RULING, DO NOT GUESS (2 families) ===
LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec and LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec.
  Both census `ambiguous-unowned-structure` / inline-record, reason "leading named record has
  no explicit top-level ownership cue". No reservation, LAW A = 0, LAW B = 0 on both. Both
  class instruments are silent, and I falsified both replacement laws I tried:
    TRIED "a body carrying a named retaining member cannot be wire (its refs need field
    rows, and fields need a non-wire host)" -- FALSIFIED 89/182 wire hosts do carry one.
    TRIED the refined "...unless it is a union, whose arms carry refs as variants" --
    ALSO FALSIFIED: 34 landed wire-type RECORD hosts carry named retaining members, among
    them the direct shape-analogues LocalStatementPublicationSpec, CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec,
    TxnAbortSpec, LocalTerminalCompletionSpec, LocalOutcomeExpirySpec, ShardingActivationSpec.
  Slice-local control (the endorsed one) is a14 6/6 logical, but every one of those six is
  forced by an INDEPENDENT rule -- GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec<Role> is a generic
  whole-schema union, ConfigPayloadFloor/GcProposal/MandatoryInventory/GcDecisionRecord are
  reservation-backed -- so the cohort is unanimous and proves nothing about a flat record.
  Corpus split for flat records carrying named refs is 243 logical / 34 wire = 88/12. That is
  a majority spelling, not a law, and majority spelling has been the wrong answer twice today.
  RECOMMENDATION (a recommendation, NOT a derivation): logical, on CONSEQUENCE ASYMMETRY.
  LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec carries 5 named StrongRef members (GcDecisionRecord,
  ConfigurationState, GcRootInventory, GcReachabilityProof, GcDisjointnessProof). Minted
  logical they can land as field rows later; minted wire they can NEVER land, and the choice
  is unrecoverable in a durable format. Logical preserves the option, wire forecloses it.
  LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec has 5 members with NO exact types at all, so nothing lands
  inside it either way; it should follow whatever its sibling gets.
  CENSUS DEFECT found while measuring it: the member
  `complete_member_target_family_and_no-start_bijection` is split on its hyphen into member
  `complete_member_target_family_and_no` with exact_type `-start_bijection`. That is a reader
  bug on a hyphenated member name, and it is why that row shows a "noncanonical field
  separator" ambiguity. Filed separately.

INSTRUMENTS (all lock-free, standalone rustc against a git-archive mirror; live tree not
touched, zero writes):
  ~/.claude/.../scratchpad/class-probe.rs   both class laws + C1..C4
  ~/.claude/.../scratchpad/host-probe.rs    the two falsified candidate laws, kept as the
                                            negative result so they are not re-derived
  ~/.claude/.../scratchpad/occ.py           occurrence enumeration + accounting
  ~/.claude/.../scratchpad/roletriple.py    multi-signature landing shape (4/4 logical)

Measured by pane2 at 8f4f7d7 on `git archive HEAD` mirrors.

cohort (a14, 6 of 6 logical) looks like a convention and is not one -- every one of those

passed / 0 failed; tests/architecture_decisions.rs 27 passed / 0 failed; architecture-check
pass; six projections regenerated. Every run used a checker built FROM the tree being

HONEST LIMIT ON THE NEGATIVE CONTROL: its wire-code arm fires (projection_code_duplicate),
so the gates demonstrably see the new rows. Its construction_order arm is VACUOUS -- order

comments.text:
GATE REPORT, including one red I caused and then fixed.

`bash scripts/check.sh` came back QUALITY GATE RED: 2 of 7 core gates and 3 of 19 registered
live gates. Attribution, established against pristine `git archive` snapshots rather than
asserted:

  1. MINE. `architecture-check` and `g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh` were red on
     bead_source_count 398 vs pinned 397. I ran `br create` for fgdb-8uy7 WHILE check.sh was
     running; `br create` auto-flushes, so a 398th record landed and invalidated the pins I
     had frozen minutes earlier in 89eb90a. Fixed in 0448683.

  2. NOT MINE, AND NOT A REAL FAILURE. `w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh` reported
     identity 71 failed, lib 26 failed, architecture_decisions 4 failed, violation_witnesses
     3 failed. Those numbers measure a working tree that was concurrently dirty with other
     panes' in-flight edits (registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml and
     tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs modified, scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh staged)
     plus my bead race. check.sh reads the WORKING TREE, so in this swarm it cannot measure
     any single pane's commit.

CONTROL, which is the part that actually answers "is my work green". Against a pristine
snapshot of my final commit 0448683, with the checker built from that snapshot:
     architecture-check          PASS
     tests/architecture_decisions.rs   27 passed / 0 failed
     tests/identity.rs                111 passed / 0 failed
     tests/violation_witnesses.rs       6 passed / 0 failed   (at 89eb90a)
     registry-check --lib              79 passed / 0 failed   (at 89eb90a)
     appendix                           0 violations
Every suite check.sh reported as failing is green at my commit in isolation. I am not
claiming check.sh is green on the live tree -- it is not, and it will stay red until the
panes holding those files land them.

TWO OPERATIONAL FINDINGS WORTH RELAYING, both cost real time here:

  A. `br sync --flush-only` reports "Nothing to export (no dirty issues)" and `--status`
     reports "In sync / Dirty issues: 0" WHILE the DB holds records the JSONL lacks (397 vs
     390). Restoring the JSONL from HEAD satisfies br's hash-based dirty tracking, so the
     guard fails silent in the direction that loses data. Diff the id sets before believing
     "in sync" -- `br list --json` ids against the JSONL ids -- then `--force`.

  B. Do not run `br create` while a gate run is in flight; it auto-flushes and moves the
     provenance pins under the run. Because the pinned quantity counts records in a file
     every pane writes, the re-freeze should be a ONE-SHOT script that measures, applies and
     commits in seconds. Mine is at
     ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/a622f66e.../scratchpad/refreeze_provenance.sh
     and derives every value from architecture-check's own violation text.

Also: commit by explicit path in this tree. Another pane had scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh STAGED
while I was committing; a bare `git commit` would have swept it into mine. `git commit --only
<paths>` is the safe form.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE ONLY PART OF fgdb-oicl THAT IS NOT AN ASSIGNMENT DEFECT. Split out of oicl at
5b484ec, which discharged the whole mechanical class (22 symbols / 53 rows) and left
exactly this. Measured with the balanced-scan min-cut solver rebuilt from the tree it
measures; every edge below is the source spelling, not a paraphrase.

=== WHY NO INTEGER FIXES THESE ===
`projection_dag_future_result` is NON-STRICT — it fires on `target.order > containing.order`,
witnessed by 80 landed equal-order retaining edges. A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC
graph is satisfiable by construction (give every symbol the same integer), so the ONLY
genuinely unsatisfiable cases are where the source graph CYCLES. That is this bead.

All three cycles sit at CO-EQUAL orders today, which is exactly why the tree is green:
co-equality satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy `dag_cycle`, which walks the
EDGE SET alone. They go red the moment their field rows land, and no order will save them.
This is the dangerous shape — green now, frozen later.

=== THE THREE CYCLES, BY CLOSING EDGE ===

C1  a10 global txn, 3 symbols, all at order 60
      GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec.global_outcome_preparation_ref
          : StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord>
      GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord.expected_registered_outcome_ref
          : StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>
      GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord.admission_spec_ref   (state::PrepareAdmitted arm)
          : StrongRef<GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec>
    Landed field-row exposure: GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord 9 rows.

C2  a08 audit terminal, 2 symbols, both at order 6
      NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof.freeze_ref : StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>
      AuditTerminalFreezeRecord back-references the proof through its `state` union arm.
    Landed field-row exposure: AuditTerminalFreezeRecord 4 rows.
    ENTANGLED with the a08 order batch still open on fgdb-oicl
    (AuditTerminalAttemptRecord 6->40, AuditEventRecord 40->6, AuditTicket 40->6), which
    must NOT land first: AuditTerminalAttemptRecord additionally carries a source
    self-edge, so the integers would be wasted. pane6 costed that one on fgdb-suhb.

C3  key envelope, 2 symbols, both at order 50
      KeyEnvelopeRoot.root_node_ref                       : StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeNode>
      KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots[].source_root_ref   : StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeRoot>
    Landed field-row exposure: 0 rows on either. CHEAPEST TO REPAIR TODAY, and the
    clearest semantically — see below.

=== THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES THIS ONE RULING RATHER THAN THREE ===
In every one of the three, the cycle closes through a PROVENANCE / EXPECTATION link, never
through the containment link:

  C3  `KeyEnvelopeRoot.root_node_ref` is genuine containment — a root owns its tree. The
      back edge `KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots[].source_root_ref` points at a DIFFERENT,
      parent-branch envelope root (the members alongside it are source_graph, source_branch,
      source_envelope_epoch). It is lineage provenance, not ownership.
  C1  `expected_registered_outcome_ref` names a PRE-ACTION state to compare against. The
      `expected_` prefix is a real pattern here, not a reading: GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec
      carries four more of them (expected_topology_state_ref, expected_workspace_generation_ref,
      expected_cumulative_read_witness_root_ref, expected_cumulative_logical_effect_root_ref),
      all currently StrongRef.
  C2  the freeze/proof pair is a terminal-evidence back-reference, the same shape.

A comparison basis does not need to keep its subject alive — that is the a01
identity-is-not-reachability law — and fgdb-u3gr has ALREADY RULED the repair form for
exactly this semantics: `digest256` + `digest_class`, `reference_semantics = "none"`,
`identity_class = "inline"` (the weak-identity variant being WeakDigest + weak_identity,
comparison-only, excluded from reachability / GC / checkpoint / backup traversal). So this
is that existing ruling applied at three named links, not three new designs.

=== FORKS, COSTED ===

FORK A (recommended) — amend the three provenance links to the ruled non-retaining form.
  Scope per link: the plan source member, the Appendix catalog + projections, the source
  census/assignment pins for the owning slice, and any regression test that names the
  member. The five-link d8b51ed precedent touched 12 files / 456 insertions / 68 deletions;
  three single-link amendments across three slices are smaller each but cross the same
  surfaces. C3 is the cheapest (0 landed field rows on both ends) and is the natural pilot.
  After each cycle is broken, its component becomes an ordinary min-cut batch that the
  existing solver already emits — C2's is solved and sitting on fgdb-oicl at 3 symbols /
  6 rows.

FORK B (not recommended) — admit retaining cycles via a checker exception or a typed
  mutual-reference relation. A name allowlist is textually small but leaves an unbounded
  retaining cycle in the reachability/GC and checkpoint-vector walkers, which are keyed on
  construction_order. A sound typed relation needs registered schema vocabulary plus
  explicit GC/checkpoint/backup cut semantics and negative tests, so its complete-system
  cost is at least Fork A's while weakening the invariant.

FORK C (do nothing) — free today and stays green, because co-equal orders satisfy
  dag_future_result. It fails the moment any of the 13 landed field rows across C1/C2 grow
  a sibling, and the order is frozen by then. This is the option the oicl bead's own root
  cause warns about: mint first, land the body later, discover the contradiction after it
  is expensive.

DECISION REQUESTED: approve Fork A and confirm the u3gr non-retaining form applies at
these three links, or require the larger typed design. If Fork A, C3 (KeyEnvelope, zero
landed field rows) is the pilot and C2 should be sequenced with the a08 self-edge repair
on fgdb-suhb so the audit component is fixed once rather than twice.

title: Materialize command_type_classification.toml and command_contracts.toml: plan 5.1 specifies both in full and neither exists
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 at HEAD 7905c27 by pane3 while re-deriving fgdb-d2ax.

`ls registries/` returns 20 registries. Both registries that plan section 5.1
names as normative are ABSENT:

    registries/command_contracts.toml            -- absent
    registries/command_type_classification.toml  -- absent

This is not a gap in the plan. Section 5.1 specifies both completely.

COMMAND_CONTRACTS.TOML. One row per role-valid command arm, with the exact schema
given verbatim in 5.1 (command_contract_id, role:Local|Meta|Shard,
outer_command_union, outer_wire_tag, input_schema_id, input_wire_tag,
inner_wire_tag?, body_schema_id, result_schema_id, applied_record_schema_id,
handler_symbol, transition_class:Semantic|Maintenance|Scaffolding, sequence_effects,
expected_state_schema_id, authority_arm, authority_evidence_target_schema_id?,
terminal_audit_freeze_arm, terminal_audit_gate_arm, payload_availability_rule,
publication_mode, construction_dag_recipe_id, consumed_state_slots[],
written_state_slots[], checkpoint_floor_classes[], backup_restore_gc_classes[],
posture_feature_predicate, format_epoch_range, status). Rows are per concrete
inner tag; 5.1 states outright that an outer family 'never hides an open
subcommand'.

COMMAND_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.TOML. Assigns every independently addressable
normative input-looking type -- 5.1 says explicitly 'including every type whose
stable name ends in Spec' -- exactly one of SIX classes:
    RegisteredCommandInput{command_contract_id} | PreOrderArtifact |
    CertificateInput | ResultOnly | ProjectionInput | RuntimeOnly

WHY THIS IS P0 RATHER THAN A06 HOUSEKEEPING. Section 5.1 makes these two a
G0-enforced two-way total bijection: 'Every inhabitable Local, Meta, or Shard
command-union arm resolves to exactly one live command-contract row; every live
row resolves to exactly one union arm, one registered canonical input, one exact
body/result/applied-record triple, and one exhaustive Rust apply handler. Every
independently addressable input-like type has one classification row ... Duplicate
tags, aliases that encode a second command, wildcard bodies, unresolved associated
types, prose-only phases, unhandled rows, handlers without rows, or a command
input classified as its own future result are G0 failures.' None of that can be
enforced while the registries do not exist, so the enforcement reads as satisfied
by absence -- the same fail-open-by-vacuity shape this swarm has closed repeatedly
tonight (a7c8's unpinned split, 5qcg's inert exclusions, d9pd's unenforced
SC2015).

THE ANTI-INFERENCE RULE IT CARRIES, which is load-bearing and currently unenforced:

    'A suffix conveys no semantics. In particular an ordinary schema/index
     definition is a SchemaOp carried by a transaction; it cannot silently acquire
     a catalog/schema/index control command merely because prose calls it a
     specification.'

fgdb-d2ax describes seven a06 candidates as 'command-looking Spec families'. That
phrasing is exactly the inference 5.1 forbids, and there is no registry to check
it against. Until this lands, every slice with Spec-suffixed candidates has the
same hole.

IMMEDIATE CONSUMER: fgdb-d2ax, whose seven Spec families are blocked on this and
were recorded as blocked on 'an owner ruling'. They are not -- the classification
is specified; the file is missing. Re-scoping that blocker is why this bead
exists.

SCOPE NOTE, not yet measured: how many types across all 21 appendix slices are
'independently addressable input-looking', i.e. how large the classification table
has to be. Someone should count that before estimating.
notes:

lease while working fgdb-ch8r. Two claims in it were wrong. The conclusion --
do not author these files yet -- survives, for a different and better reason.

WRONG 1: "both files sit on the GENERATED side of the chain; hand-authoring
creates the second source of truth line 294 forbids."

title: W5 Stage 1: implement and prove binary FreeJoin
description:
## What & scope
Implement and independently close the first Loom risk-reduction stage: the final GLA-compatible binary FreeJoin kernel over authorized Strata tries/cursors. Own binary relation binding, key-order negotiation, exact intersection/probe semantics, duplicate/multiplicity handling, cancellation/resource accounting, and a deliberately nonadaptive pinned plan profile. This is a final subset of the unified operator family, not a hash-join substitute or throwaway executor.

## Why
§20 identifies FreeJoin/factorization/adaptivity as the crown-jewel risk and mandates the evidence order binary FreeJoin -> run-trie WCOJ -> factorized columns -> adaptivity. A separately closable binary stage gives later work an oracle-grounded semantic and complexity baseline while preserving the one-family design.

## Design and phase contract
Use the canonical GLA rows, answer/security contracts, `QueryCx`, `ResourceLedger`, and Secure View cursors. The kernel accepts two trie-shaped inputs and emits canonical vector batches with exact Z/multiplicity semantics, deterministic CGSE tie breaks, positive/negative/gap witness traces, and complexity-witness counters. A pinned deterministic plan selects build/probe or ordered intersection from declared features; no learned/adaptive choice, factorized output, or multiway leapfrog activation is permitted in this stage. Spill and cancellation use the final executor obligations and never expose unauthorized cardinality.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover every binary key/order shape, empty/duplicate/skewed inputs, NULL/value semantics, multiplicities, witness emission, canonical ordering, arithmetic/resource boundaries, cancellation points, and fail-closed authorization.
- Property/model and differential tests compare arbitrary small binary joins against `fgdb-reference`, flatten vector batches, vary physical representations and compaction, and assert identical rows, witnesses, logical digests, and declared complexity counters.
- Mutation/fuzz suites attack GLA rows, trie cursors, codecs, key comparisons, corrupt batches, resource exhaustion, and cancellation at every obligation boundary.
- E2E runs authenticated GQL through binder -> pinned binary FreeJoin -> authorized Strata cursors -> SSI/constraint validation -> canonical result/replay across spill, restart, and representation changes; an unauthorized edge type fails before observation.
- The stage evidence report publishes semantic corpus results and operation/bytes/memory distributions separately from later WCOJ/factorization/adaptivity claims.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics record `{run_id,stage:"binary-freejoin",query_and_plan_digest,input_relation_and_cursor_commitments,key_order,policy_epoch,pinned_action,rows_and_multiplicities,witness_digest,op_count,bytes,memory_spill,cancel_or_fault,oracle,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with protected facts redacted.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a separate hash-join engine, parser-interpreted execution, post-filter authorization, unbounded materialization, or borrowing later-stage evidence. Risk is a baseline optimized to one representation; representation differential and explicit counters prevent it.

## Provenance
Plan §§8.1-8.4, §15, §17, §20 FreeJoin risk mitigation, B3/B5, FG-INV-05/06/09/19/20.

title: The ADR's two enforcement lists are bound only by inspection; make the record cite violation codes and require each to be witnessed firing
notes:
Follow-up from fgdb-adr-doc-prose-unchecked-and-drifted-uyt2 (landed 60cb545).

## What is still unbound

docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md is now generated from
registries/architecture_decisions.toml and byte-compared, so every count,
vocabulary row, and table cell is a projection that cannot drift. Two
statements in it are still bound only by inspection:

1. What the checker enforces --
   "`architecture-check` verifies the excerpts byte-for-byte against the
    master plan, pins the decision identity and semantic tables, validates
    live owner and claim references, prevents research citations from
    authorizing dependencies, regenerates this document, and emits
    deterministic decision-to-owner, owner-to-decision, and every-Bead-to-
    rationale NDJSON."

2. What fails the gate --
   "An unknown bet label, a shadowed override, an ambiguous rule, a missing
    decision, profile, or rationale, or an unresolved Bead fails the
    architecture gate."

All ten clauses were verified BY HAND on 2026-07-26 and every one maps to a
live mechanism: source_bytes_mismatch, id_table_hash_mismatch,
semantic_contract_hash_mismatch, owner_bead_unresolved,
live_verification_checker_missing, research_dependency_promotion,
document_drift, the three NDJSON emitters, bead_bet_label_set,
bead_override_shadowed, bead_family_ambiguous, provenance_rationale_missing,
bead_provenance_not_total. Nothing holds them there. Rename a code, delete a
rule, and the sentences keep reading correctly while describing a checker that
no longer exists -- which is the same defect uyt2 just closed, one level up.

## The proposed shape

Let the generator render the sentences WITH their violation codes, and require
every cited code to be one the test suite has WITNESSED FIRING -- not merely
one that appears as a string literal in architecture.rs. A source-text census
would be the fail-open version of this and should not be built (see
registry-check-metamorphic-harness: the hash layer is sound, every defect is
in a source-text reader).

That gives fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy its first consumer:
the document becomes the thing that CANNOT cite an unwitnessed law.

## Why this is its own bead, and not small

Measured 2026-07-26: architecture.rs emits 105 distinct violation codes.
Exactly 12 are witnessed by an assert_code call in
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs. The ~13 codes the two
sentences would cite are NOT a subset of those 12 -- most notably
source_bytes_mismatch, bead_provenance_not_total, document_drift, and
research_dependency_promotion have no firing witness.

So the work is: write the missing witnesses first (each is a control plus one
typed mutation, the pattern already in tests/violation_witnesses.rs), then let
the document cite them, then add the guard that a cited code must be witnessed.
Doing it in the other order produces a citation list that looks enforced and is
not -- the exact failure this bead exists to prevent.

## Do NOT do the weak version

Rendering the codes without the witnessed-set guard is worse than the prose it
replaces: it reads as machine-checked and is not. If the witnesses are too
expensive to write, leave the sentences as prose and say in the document that
they are bound by inspection -- which is what uyt2 did for the four
statements that are not mechanically checkable at all.

title: Reconstruct pre-repin A10 historical witness value without moving floor
notes:
pane4, re-derived at HEAD b4e50d9. NO PIN MOVED, no repo file edited: the whole
experiment ran on a COPY of tests/identity.rs in scratch.

=== THE FOUR VALUES ===

  pre-repin floor   5b76722 .. 8a704c2~1   fnv1a64:bdbcdc27ccd92518
  current floor     8a704c2 .. HEAD        fnv1a64:236efa5babe190fe
  HEAD reconstruction, witness UNMODIFIED  fnv1a64:a86e33d4020143ef
  HEAD reconstruction + a02 cohort filtered fnv1a64:71729c11125d59d1

=== ANSWER: THE PRE-REPIN NAMESPACE IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM TODAY'S TRANSCRIPT ===

The experiment: 8a704c2 registered 26 a02 physical field rows (CiphertextRecord
5, PlacementRecord 2, SymbolRecord 19) and, instead of filtering them out of the
historical namespace as every sibling cohort is filtered, RE-PINNED the floor.
So the direct test of recoverability is: add the missing post-erratum filter for
exactly that cohort and see whether the reconstruction returns to bdbcdc27.

It does not. It returns 71729c11125d59d1.

The filter is exact, licensed by accounting rather than by inspection: the
sibling cohort assert moved 964 -> 938, i.e. EXACTLY 26 rows were removed, which
is the cohort 8a704c2's own commit message enumerates. So the filter is neither
over- nor under-broad, and 71729c11 is what the a02-free namespace actually
hashes to.

Therefore bdbcdc27 cannot be reached by undoing 8a704c2's field cohort. The
residue must lie in the half of the transcript the field cohort assert cannot
see -- assignment_pins folds in reference unions, ordinary unions and every ARM
of both, which the test's own failure note says explicitly. Recovering bdbcdc27
would require identifying every union/arm cohort landed since 8a704c2 that is
not yet filtered, and nothing in the transcript records which those were.

=== AND THE WITNESS IS RED AT HEAD RIGHT NOW, INDEPENDENT OF THIS BEAD ===

The UNMODIFIED witness at HEAD reconstructs a86e33d4020143ef against a floor of
236efa5babe190fe. It does not reconstruct its own pin. So today it is not a
proof of history at all: it is a drift detector that is currently firing, and
some cohort landed since 8a704c2 is being silently absorbed rather than filtered.
That is a live red on main and is somebody's to repair -- NOT by re-pinning,
which is the mistake 8a704c2 made and which this bead exists to avoid repeating.

=== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FLOOR ===

236efa5b MAY NOT MOVE and I have not moved it. But the honest characterisation
is that it is a floor by RULING, not by derivation: no reconstruction available
today produces it, and the value it replaced is not reachable either. The
witness should be described as a drift detector against a ruled floor, and any
claim that it proves the pre-erratum namespace is unsupported at this HEAD.

Zero licensed by accounting: 26 rows present in the a02 cohort, 26 consumed by
the probe filter, 0 missing.
close_reason: NOT RECOVERABLE, proven. Four values: pre-repin bdbcdc27ccd92518, floor 236efa5babe190fe, HEAD reconstruction a86e33d4020143ef, a02-free 71729c11125d59d1. Filtering exactly the 26 rows 8a704c2 registered yields 71729c11, not bdbcdc27, so that re-pin cannot be undone by filtering its cohort; the residue is in the union/arm half of the transcript and nothing records which cohorts those were. Licensed by accounting: cohort assert 964 -> 938, 26 present / 26 consumed / 0 missing. No pin moved, no repo file edited, whole experiment on a scratch copy. title: A21 DCVE union rows are unlandable: ordinary union/arm targets forbid the projection fallback and no census union/arm keys exist
close_reason: Mis-scoped, not a defect: the union/arm rows are neither owed nor landable, and the wire path that IS correct is verified. Measured at 9cb0e70 with controls. (1) DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence emits ZERO field/union/arm census candidates — its entire body is one definition-without-structural-body ambiguity — so the census-keyed coverage law owes nothing for it: 0 of the 788 source_complete_census_uncovered keys an armed a21 reports are DCVE. (2) 0 of 5 candidate source_key values load, against a control (AuditContinuityRecord.status) that accepts exactly 1 through the identical harness. (3) The correct shape is a wire discriminant/union + union_variant rows on projection|wire_types|<Name>, declared — synthesized and ACCEPTED with only append-only pin drift; it also kills the payload_sha256 objection since WireType has no such column, so all 11 unlanded fields become landable.
