title: Appendix A exact catalog: Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols. This task embeds source-plan lines 1445-1463 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Filesystem durability and writer takeover.** `FilesystemDurabilityProfile` is a signed/checked-in artifact `{ profile_id, profile_version, os/kernel_range, allowed_filesystems_and_mount_predicates, forbidden_layers/options, required_lock_primitive, owner_death_rule, stable_inode_rule, slot_write_rule, file_sync_rule, directory_sync_rule, rename_no_replace_rule, cache_flush_assumption, probe_suite_oid }`. `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` has exactly §5.1's ext4/XFS allowlist; a profile/mount not matching every predicate is not writable. A local `FilesystemInstanceRecord { profile_id, probe_suite_oid, mount_id, filesystem_type, canonical_mount_options, device_chain_digest, directory_device_inode, manifest_device_inode, checked_at, result_digest }` is diagnostic evidence, never a transferable proof or semantic root.

The takeover checker accepts only `NoGuard -> LeaseHeld(identity) -> ClosureRecovered(old_epoch) -> PendingFenceGuard(old_epoch+1) -> FenceRootDurableAndReread(old_epoch+1) -> WriterEnabled(FenceToken)`. Creation is `NoGuard -> StagingInodeLease -> PendingCreationGuard(epoch=1) -> CompleteStagingRootVerified -> RenameNoReplaceAndDirectorySync -> CanonicalRootReread -> WriterEnabled`. `PendingFenceGuard` is linear and can encode/seal exactly one fence-only `RootManifest` preserving the recovered state plus its inactive `RootSlot`; `PendingCreationGuard` can encode/seal only the registered Genesis closure and epoch-1 slot. Neither type implements user-segment, prepared-owner, receipt, Raft, canonical-transition, or general-root traits. `FenceToken` is nonserializable and nonconstructible outside the VFS/commit boundary; it binds the live lease handle, stable directory/root identity, profile, slot generation, and epoch. The fence-only root/slot must retain the exact prior canonical logical root, Raft/audit candidate, prepared root, and durable/applied/visible positions. Every immutable segment trailer records `{ database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, local_writer_fence_epoch, segment_id, sealed_len, inventory_digest, trailer_checksum }`; after promotion the local VFS refuses a seal, prepared-root update, receipt signature, Raft append acknowledgement/proposal, or root publication without the matching live token. Already receipted/ordered records from an older epoch remain strong obligations but cannot authorize new old-epoch publication. The crash matrix cuts after every lease/identity/recovery/object-sync/slot-write/slot-sync/staging-rename/directory-sync/reread step and includes owner death, path replacement, mount drift, stale descriptors, epoch overflow, competing creators, orphan staging, and a lying-sync profile that must be rejected.

**Cipher/encoding/placement records and SymbolRecord.** `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest` is `{ logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len }`. Object AAD is the domain string plus logical OID and this canonical descriptor. `CiphertextRecord` is `{ descriptor, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, object_tag_digest, protected_length }`; `CiphertextId` hashes descriptor+ciphertext+object tag. Immutable `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile }`, and `EncodingId` hashes the domain/version plus its **complete canonical bytes**. Separately, `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }`, where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`. `PlacementId` hashes the placement domain/version plus exactly that descriptor; immutable `PlacementRecord { placement_id, descriptor }` merely stores and cross-checks it. Moving/adding symbols creates a new placement record without changing encoding identity. KEK/wrap epoch is absent from both ciphertext and encoding identity. The authenticated local physical-realization index maps `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, and `PlacementId` to these records with nonretaining locators. An ordinary decoder obtains the complete descriptor/OTI/auth profile from an authenticated `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` (or FGP's authenticated encoding prelude) before accepting any symbol; a bare `SymbolRecord` is never self-authorizing.

```text
SymbolRecord {
  magic="FGEC", format_version:u16, header_len:u16, record_len:u32,
  logical_oid:[u8;32], ciphertext_id:[u8;32], encoding_id:[u8;32],
  object_kind:u16, source_block:u32, esi:u32, symbol_len:u32,
  transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32, flags:u32,
  symbol_mac_profile:u16, symbol_mac_len:u16,
  payload:[u8;symbol_len], symbol_mac:[u8;symbol_mac_len]
}
```

The symbol MAC key/transcript are exactly §5.1's domain-separated construction. All framing/OTI/length fields and payload are MACed. Truncated/noncanonical tails are ignored only in proved-unreferenced staging; a reachable sealed tail triggers authenticated repair or fail-closed recovery.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

## Provenance
Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 1445-1463.

This pin supersedes the pre-d96bf0f range while preserving the self-contained slice contract.

  plan:280   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }

So one arm of a closed union is landed standalone and the other does not exist. That is not a deliberate design; it is what you get when the union is unparseable and someone registers the arm they needed. Any slice that later references placement inherits this.

I AM NOT SHAPING AROUND IT. Minting PlacementDescriptorWithoutId requires first ruling whether a01:1443 and a02:1449 are ONE schema with an erratum in one spelling, or TWO schemas (a root-specialised placement descriptor plus the general one) that share a name. SYMBOLS: NOTHING IS OWED, and this is a step-2 conclusion, not a step-1 one. SymbolRecord is already landed as physical kind 0x0004 with its full transcript and the K_symbol MAC law. Its 19 census field candidates will never become [[field]] rows, because catalog-wide all 53 field-row owners are logical kinds and zero of 59 wire types and zero of 7 physical kinds carry field rows. OFF-TOKEN DESIGN PACKAGE for the remaining a02 families, plus the class ruling written up as asked, plus TWO CORRECTIONS to my own earlier comments in this thread. Nothing here needs the token; all of it is probe-derived against HEAD.

=====================================================================
1. THE CLASS RULING, WRITTEN UP PROPERLY (asked for, and cheap now)
=====================================================================
Applies to all four a02 wire types I have landed (0x003b-0x003e).

FORCED BY THE SOURCE:
 * That the schema is registered at all. Each is a confirmed top-level candidate with an explicit structural body; Appendix A makes an unregistered one unencodable.
 * The member set and order. Verbatim from the source bodies, corroborated independently by the census field-candidate counts (9, 8, 14, 10) matching member-for-member.

FORCED BY LANDED CONVENTION (derivable, not chosen):
 * CLASS = wire/record. All 7 landed physical kinds carry BOTH identity_law and owning_identity, i.e. a physical kind is a content-addressed stored record. None of these four has an identity law in the source, so physical-kind is excluded; among a02's three declared projection classes (physical_record_kinds, wire_types, durable_fields) wire_types is the residual. Note this is convention-derived, not law-enforced: expected_projection_classes is read into a transcript and is NOT checked, so nothing would have stopped a wrong class mechanically.
 * IDENTITY_CLASS flip unclassified -> wire on the candidate row. Forced by projection_identity_class, which maps target_kind "wire-type" onto identity_class "wire". Omit it and both catalog_target_class_mismatch and catalog_candidate_class_mismatch fire.
 * NO [[reservation]] row. Reservation bijection law: none of the four is a StrongRef family.
 * STATUS. active for the two descriptors, reserved for the two filesystem rows. See the correction in section 4 — the basis is narrower than I first stated.

DECIDED BY ME (revisit these first):
 * max_size_bytes: 256 for the two descriptors (ContiguousSpan precedent, and both are comfortably under it: a 32-byte identity plus small scalars), 65536 for the two filesystem rows (a15 reserved-shell precedent). Neither is derived from a source bound, because the source states none.
 * allowed_containing_schemas: ["CiphertextRecord"] / ["EncodingRecord"] for the descriptors are READ OFF the source (each is the body of exactly that record), so those are forced. ["*"] for the two filesystem rows is NOT — neither has any container in the source, so there is no list to read off, and ["*"] is a residual on the WeakDigest/MarkerRef precedent.
 * The encoding_context prose wording throughout.

=====================================================================
2. SYMBOLS: COMPLETE, and here is the exactness evidence rather than a coverage number
=====================================================================
The operator's framing is right that exactness matters more than breadth here, so I audited the thing that actually carries the durability claim: FG-INV-09, "Identity recomputation: ObjectId/CiphertextId/EncodingId/PlacementId from registered transcripts; digest-recipe discipline."

Every a02 physical-kind identity law now resolves to a REGISTERED structure:
  CiphertextRecord  ciphertext_id  -> CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest   (a02 wire, active)
  EncodingRecord    encoding_id    -> EncodingDescriptorWithoutId     (a02 wire, active)
  PlacementRecord   placement_id   -> PlacementDescriptorWithoutId    (a01 wire, RESERVED)
  SymbolRecord      symbol_record  -> self-contained, no external schema reference
TWO OF THESE FOUR WERE ONLY MADE RESOLVABLE BY 352bccd. Before it, CiphertextId's and EncodingId's recomputation transcripts named unregistered structures, so FG-INV-09 could not be discharged for them. That is the precise value of increment 1 and it is stronger than the "load-bearing but unregistered" phrasing I used at the time.

SymbolRecord specifically needs nothing further: its transcript already enumerates every serialized header field except the MAC bytes (framing lengths, identities, object kind, source block, ESI, transfer length, OTI, flags, auth profile, payload length) plus the payload, and pins the derivation MAC under K_symbol = KDF(DEK, "fgdb:symbol-auth:v1" || EncodingId). Its 19 census field candidates will never become [[field]] rows — catalog-wide all 53 field-row owners are logical kinds, zero of 61 wire types and zero of 7 physical kinds carry any. Its DefinitionWithoutStructuralBody ambiguity is benign: the body is a fenced code block and the prose mention has no adjacent structural expression.

=====================================================================
3. PLACEMENT: CORRECTION, and the real defect is not what I said
=====================================================================
CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER COMMENT. I wrote that PlacementDescriptorWithoutId "is not a top-level candidate, so it needs an ownership ruling first", implying it was unlanded. IT IS ALREADY REGISTERED — a01 wire type 0x001e, status reserved, encoding_context "Appendix A reference-semantics family PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (a01); exact member layout per plan lines 1388-1444". I reached the wrong conclusion by probing a02's candidate list and never controlling against the whole catalog: exactly the false-negative shape I have been warning about, committed by me two comments after describing it. The lesson generalises — "not in MY slice" is not "not registered".

SO THE ACTUAL PLACEMENT DEFECT IS TWO THINGS, both sharper than "unlanded":
 (a) A STATUS INCOHERENCE, and it is the same defect class 352bccd fixed. PlacementRecord is ACTIVE and its FG-INV-09 identity law depends on PlacementDescriptorWithoutId, which is RESERVED. An active identity law resting on a non-live row is precisely the incoherence that FORCED active for the two descriptors. Screening every wire type catalog-wide, this is the ONLY row in the entire catalog that is reserved while having an active referent. It is an a01-owned row, so the fix is cross-slice, not mine to make unilaterally.
 (b) THE DIVERGENT BODY, now with a concrete consequence. The a01 row pins its member layout to lines 1388-1444, i.e. the a01:1443 spelling (root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id, ContiguousSpan INLINED, root_* members). a02:1449 and plan:280 give a different body (placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, and a location_form union). So the landed registration asserts a layout that a02's own source contradicts. That is why the census emits ConflictingCandidateEvidence, why location_form never parses into a union candidate, and why the Explicit arm is registered nowhere while ContiguousSpan is: the a01-pinned body has no location_form at all, so the second arm was never needed.
 RESOLUTION SPACE, not mine to choose: reconcile the two bodies by erratum; or widen the a01 row to cover both; or rule them two schemas and rename one. All three are a01+a02 cross-slice.

=====================================================================
4. TWO SCREENS THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR, both clean, both with a mechanism
=====================================================================
 * SELF-REFERENCING RETAINING WRAPPERS (the u3gr screen): CLEAN. Zero occurrences of any of the nine retaining wrapper spellings targeting any a02 family across lines 280, 1443, 1445, 1447 and 1449. Nothing from a02 belongs on fgdb-u3gr. Same result cc_2 got on a04.
 * CONSTRUCTION-ORDER CONSTRAINTS: STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE IN a02, which is a stronger statement than "none found". The [[logical_kind]] row schema carries construction_order; [[physical_kind]] and [[wire_type]] do NOT — their key sets are {identity_law, max_size_bytes, name, owning_identity, record_kind, row_id, slice_id, status, transcript} and {allowed_containing_schemas, encoding_context, kind, max_size_bytes, name, row_id, slice_id, status, wire_type_id}. The construction DAG is evaluated over field rows resolved through logical kinds. Since a02 mints only physical kinds and wire types, no a02 row can carry or violate an order constraint. So "derive orders from both directions" has no purchase in this slice, and that is a mechanism, not an absence.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN STATUS RULE, because I overstated its scope in b861833's commit message. I claimed the rule "active iff >=1 already-active referent" holds "without exception across all 15 a02+a15 wire types". True for that population, but tested against all 61 wire types it holds 41/61. The honest rule is therefore: for slice-minted NON-PRIMITIVE structural records, active iff it has an active referent. The filesystem pair are non-primitive with zero referents of any kind, so reserved still follows — the decision stands, the justification was too broad.

=====================================================================

6. NET STATE OF a02
=====================================================================
Landed: cipher and encoding descriptors (352bccd); filesystem durability profile and instance record (b861833). Complete: symbols (nothing owed, FG-INV-09 evidence above). Correctly unminted: FenceToken and PendingFenceGuard, both DefinitionWithoutStructuralBody runtime types — FenceToken explicitly nonserializable and nonconstructible outside the VFS/commit boundary, PendingFenceGuard a linear guard. title: Appendix A exact catalog: Local logical state and durable transaction formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Local logical state and durable transaction formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1464-1543 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**LogicalStatePayload / LogicalStateRoot.** The following is a compact Local navigation projection of generated `LogicalStatePayload`, not a field-exhaustive alternate schema: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,bootstrap_phase:Genesis|CheckpointInstalled|Operational|RecoveryReconciling|RecoveryAbandoned|OperationalPendingIndependentReopen,applied_logical_command_seq,applied_commit_seq,global_transaction_marker_head:StrongMarkerRef?,branch_head_map_root(entries carry StrongMarkerRef),branch_manifest_root,branch_key_epoch_registry_root,key_envelope/grant_registry_root,branch_merge_ledger_root,graph_partition_state_roots,catalog_root,schema_roots,id_allocator_root,identity_continuity_record_ref,constraint_state_roots,resource_ledger_root,privacy_ledger_root,privacy_continuity_record_ref,dp_request_index_root,txn_outcome_index_root:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeIndex>,local_begin_idempotency_index_root:StrongRef<LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex>,local_statement_index_root:StrongRef<LocalStatementIndex>,local_txn_outcome_summary_root:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,local_delta_batch_index_root:StrongRef<LocalDeltaBatchIndex>,local_delta_frontier,terminal_certification_reservation_root:StrongRef<TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Local>>,recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>?,retained_stream_floor,retention_map_root:StrongRef<RetentionMap>,derived_generation_registry_root:StrongRef<DerivedGenerationRegistry>,replay_registry_root,logical_hlc_state,topology_epoch,policy_epoch,revocation_index,replicated_key_wrap/signing/capability-verifier roots,audit_ticket_index_root,audit_root,transparency_root,backup_registry_root,restore_state_ref:StrongRef<RestoreState>?,restore_retention_anchor:RestoreRetentionAnchor<Local>,gc_decision_root,remote_retention_authority_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionObligationRoot>,remote_retention_consumer_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot>,remote_configuration_trust_root:StrongRef<RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot>,sharding_migration_state_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationState>?,config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>?}`. Independent result/cursor/artifact delivery, the imported audit-continuity release head, and the audit visibility pipeline are protocol slots, not fields silently omitted from this semantic projection. The exact bounded `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` and cut lifecycle are defined with `LogicalDeltaBatch` below. `ShardingMigrationState` is `FreezePendingAudit{freeze_ref:StrongRef<ShardingFreezeRecord>}|FrozenVisible{freeze_ref,visibility_advance_maintenance_identity:MaintenanceAppliedRef}|RoleTransitionLocked{begin_ref:StrongRef<BeginRoleTransitionRecord>}|Resolved{terminal_identity}`; no variant names a future semantic command. Remote roots are empty reserved values before W12 preparation. Fresh bootstrap permits Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational; restore/reopen/abandonment follow the exact later state machine and the retention anchor must match each phase. `LogicalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStatePayload>,logical_command_head:StrongCommandRef?}`; fresh genesis alone has no head.

For Local, the activated **semantic** state-slot closure additionally requires `security_state_binding_root`, `valid_time_slice_registry_root`, `constraint_reservation_index_root`, `escrow_ledger_root`, `allocation_reservation_and_disposition_root`, `txn_ownership_directory_root`, `txn_capability_lineage_root`, `artifact_output_request_registry_root`, `replay_manifest_registry_root`, `format_compatibility_state_ref`, `bulk_load_registry_root`, `derived_build_registry_root`, `audit_terminal_freeze_index_root`, and `restore_registry_root`. `local_result_delivery_index_root`, `result_independent_retention_index_root`, and `delivery_lease_registry_root` are obsolete alternate names for the one canonical Protocol slot `result_independent_retention_index`; none is encoded in `LogicalStatePayload`. Semantic owners store only delivery ID/detachment commitments, while RootManifest's protocol root owns the bytes. The audit pipeline is likewise not a payload slot, avoiding a content cycle. Feature-disabled semantic slots use registered empty/None recipes. `state_payload_fields.toml` supplies only semantic fields; `protocol_state_fields.toml` supplies the result/cursor/output/audit slots and forbids duplicate aliases.

The generated common header of every Local/Meta/Shard payload also contains `{incarnation_continuity_profile_id,cluster_incarnation_continuity_record_ref:StrongRef<ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord>?,cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest,continuity_cas_version,service_visibility_epoch,time_authority_binding:Local{registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Local>>}|Meta{registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Meta>>}|Shard{active_projection_ref:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,projected_registry_digest,projected_selected_profile_oid,projection_meta_prefix},restore_registry_root:StrongRef<RestoreRegistry>,terminal_audit_freeze_index_root:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeIndex>}`. `DirectoryBound` uses no external record ref and a fixed local continuity digest; `ExternalCas` requires `Some` and exact byte equality with the live authority. `restore_state_ref` is present only during a live restore, while `restore_registry_root` retains terminal projection/promotion/tombstone evidence. The audit-freeze index is active only in Local/Meta and is the canonical empty reserved value in Shard. Shards may validate only the exact current active/closing/draining profile projection certified in their active Meta projection; they cannot originate profile changes. RootManifest and RootSlot repeat and cross-check the same continuity/profile/digest/version/visibility tuple.

**Local 1.0 durable transaction formats.** Local and W12 deliberately share only embedded value schemas (`TxnCompletionState`, posture-tagged `SemanticTerminalDescriptor`, and `TerminalPublicOutcome`) plus public protocol semantics. They do not share durable registration, workspace, statement, result-owner, outcome, audit-owner, claim, or command objects. A Local decoder rejects every `Global*`, Meta, shard, certified-remote, or global-prefix identity in this family, and a W12 decoder rejects every Local identity. `LocalAuditTicketOwner` is `Operation{txn_token,registration_binding_digest}|Statement{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,statement_seq,statement_idempotency_key}|Control{control_operation_tag,request_idempotency_key,request_basis_commitment}`. `LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord` is `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner,claiming_control_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,claim_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,request_basis_commitment}` and is constructed during the registration/claim apply before its owning Local record. `LocalOperationAuditAdmission` is `NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,ticket_admission_record_ref:StrongCommandRef,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord>,owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation,operation_request_basis_commitment}`. `LocalStatementAuditAdmission` has the analogous NotRequired/PendingUnclaimed/Claimed forms with `LocalAuditTicketOwner::Statement`; protected Local controls use the Control arm through their exact audit admission. No Local field can encode a global transaction ID, registration generation, GlobalControlRecord, or GlobalControlCommand.

The generated Local payload schema corrects the compact navigation list above by requiring `local_conflict_index_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictIndex>` immediately after the statement/outcome roots. Genesis installs the canonical empty index. Its checkpoint vector, `ConfigPayloadFloor`, mandatory inventory, backup closure, restore transform/reconciliation, GC root inventory, key-destruction scan, and role-transition projection each have a generated required row; omission disables SERIALIZABLE operation and is a G0 failure, not a recoverable cache miss.

The same normative schema requires `policy_root_ref:StrongRef<SecurityPolicyRoot>`, `revocation_root_ref:StrongRef<RevocationRoot>`, `constraint_state_directory_root:StrongRef<ConstraintStateDirectoryRoot>`, `local_constraint_reservation_root:StrongRef<LocalConstraintReservationRoot>`, `resource_ledger_root:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerState>`, `escrow_ledger_root:StrongRef<EscrowLedgerRoot>`, and the valid-time contract/slice/temporal-constraint roots activated by the schema. Scalar policy/revocation fields are cross-checks only. Genesis installs canonical empty roots or DenyAll security policy as configured. Every generated checkpoint/floor/inventory/backup/restore/GC/key/transition row covers them; a generic `constraint_state_roots` or untyped `resource_ledger_root` rendering does not satisfy the registry.

`LocalConflictAttemptKey` is `{txn_token_digest,registration_identity}`. `LocalConflictEdge` is `{kind:wr|ww|rw,from:LocalConflictAttemptKey,to:LocalConflictAttemptKey,coordinate_or_predicate_domain,proof_ref:LocalConflictProofRef,first_observed_statement_seq,edge_digest}` where `LocalConflictProofRef` is a generated closed union over version, absence/range, path, constraint, and final-write proof objects. `LocalConflictEntry` is `{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,registered_snapshot,start_logical_command_seq,terminal_logical_command_seq?,state:Active|PrepareAdmitted{admission_generation}|Committed|Aborted|ReadClosed,statement_frontier,workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,cumulative_write_summary_ref:StrongRef<LocalWriteSummary>?,incoming_edges[LocalConflictEdge],outgoing_edges[LocalConflictEdge],overlap_interval:{start_prefix,closed_prefix?},detail_state:Detailed|Compacted{summary_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictSummaryLeaf>}}`. Arrays/maps use canonical key/digest order and exact deduplication; an edge must appear byte-identically in both endpoint projections.

`LocalConflictIndex` is `{generation,basis_logical_command_seq,entries[LocalConflictAttemptKey->LocalConflictEntry],safe_snapshot_frontier,overlap_close_floor_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictOverlapFloor>,root_digest:BodyDigest<LocalConflictIndex>}`. `LocalConflictIndexBasis` is the nonretaining typed `{basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,index_generation,index_root_digest,basis_logical_command_seq,safe_snapshot_frontier,overlap_close_floor_digest}` used by serialization/final-certification inputs; a bare `WeakStateIdentity` is insufficient. Registration atomically inserts Active with workspace zero. Every successful statement publication atomically replaces that exact entry with its successor statement/workspace/witness/write summary and all newly proved bidirectional edges. Prepare admission replays `may_affect` in both directions against every overlapping entry, reruns the registered SCC algorithm, and atomically selects PrepareAdmitted; commit, admitted abort, active cancel, or read close installs the terminal prefix and state in the same command as outcome/attempt changes. Terminal completion changes no serialization decision but retains the entry through its postcondition lifetime.

`LocalConflictOverlapFloor` is `{closed_through_start_prefix,safe_snapshot_frontier,oldest_live_overlapping_start,retained_detailed_attempt_key_commitment,retained_edge_proof_commitment,checker_version}`. `LocalConflictCompactionSpec {expected_index_basis:LocalConflictIndexBasis,sorted_selected_terminal_keys,sorted_summary_leaf_refs[StrongRef<LocalConflictSummaryLeaf>],no_future_overlap_edge_proof_ref:StrongRef<LocalNoFutureConflictEdgeProof>,expected_oldest_live_overlapping_start,expected_attempt_outcome_statement_workspace_retention_discharge,terminal_audit_gate}` may replace detail only when every possible future transaction has a start/snapshot beyond the selected entry's closed overlap interval and no live witness can add an edge; it never deletes the authenticated summary or changes public outcomes. Every follower reconstructs `may_affect`, verifies symmetric edges/proofs and workspace transport, and reruns SCC before signing `LocalSerializationCertificate`, whose `snapshot_and_conflict_index_basis` field is exactly `LocalConflictIndexBasis`. Missing/stale/asymmetric evidence, unsupported exact witness semantics, or resource exhaustion conservatively aborts/waits. Write-skew, multi-edge rw cycles, same-I/O-batch writers, read-only dangerous structures, statement-workspace transport, restart, checkpoint, compaction, and detail-retirement races are permanent oracle/model tests.

`LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundDetailed{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredDetailed{terminal_ref:StrongRef<LocalNeverRegisteredRecord>,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|ExpiredTombstone{scoped_key_digest,txn_token_digest,capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}`. `LocalBeginReservationSpec` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,canonical_begin_request_digest,operation_class:ReadOnly|ReadWrite,isolation_profile,transaction_error_policy,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis:None|Validated{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment},scoped_begin_idempotency_key,expected_index_absence:WeakAbsenceProof,staging_resource_reservation_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. comments.text:
QUALIFIED-ARM IDENTITY CHECK — VERDICT: THE SIX ARE REFERENCES, NOT UNIONS. MINT NOTHING FOR THEM. Read-only, no token, run before writing a single row. Also corrects my own hypothesis about which class they belong to.

=== 1. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SPELLS ===
Six a03 member unions came out of the census carrying ::-qualified arms. The plan text at their sites:
    1482  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1484  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1484  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1486  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1486  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1488  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1528  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
And the parent, defined ONCE at plan line 1470:
    `LocalOperationAuditAdmission` is `NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}
      |PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,ticket_admission_record_ref:StrongCommandRef,
        operation_request_basis_commitment}
      |Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord>,
        owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation,operation_request_basis_commitment}`
THE DECISIVE OBSERVATION: `NotRequired` — the SECOND arm at every one of the six sites — is itself one of the parent's three variants. The `::` qualifier is written once and the sibling relies on context. So each site is a 2-of-3 NARROWING of one existing closed union, not a new two-arm type. Three distinct subsets appear: {PendingUnclaimed,NotRequired} and {Claimed,NotRequired}.
Minting these as six [[union]] rows would create six duplicate types over two parents, and would also collide on names — my first naming pass produced OperationAuditAdmission x3 and StatementAuditAdmission x3, which duplicate logical schema names and fail G0 outright. The collision was the symptom; this is the cause.

=== 2. I HAVE TO CORRECT MY OWN FRAMING: THIS IS NOT THE fgdb-a9c8 CLASS ===
I flagged these as the a9c8 variant-qualified class. That was a hypothesis and inspection refutes it. a9c8 was about `StrongRef<Enum::Variant>` — a variant-qualified strong REFERENCE, which the plan normatively forbade and which was repaired by rewriting the source to `StrongRef<Family>` plus a mandatory arm predicate. Our six contain no StrongRef at all; they are member TYPE expressions naming a subset of a closed union's variants. Related in shape, different in kind, and the a9c8 remedy (rewrite the source) does not transfer — nothing here is prohibited. Also note a9c8's cited coordinate has drifted: grepping the current plan for its `Enum::Variant` prohibition text returns nothing, so that wording has moved or been reworded since 2026-07-22. Do not navigate by a9c8's line numbers.

=== 3. AN ASYMMETRY THAT SPLITS THE SIX, AND CHANGES THE REMEDY FOR HALF ===
The two parents are NOT in the same state, which is invisible unless you check both:
    LocalOperationAuditAdmission ... structurally defined at 1470; census emits it as a union
                                     candidate PLUS its three arms (4 census rows). MINTABLE as a
                                     parent union; the three operation_audit_admission sites can then
                                     be modelled as narrowed references to it.
    LocalStatementAuditAdmission ... defined ONLY by prose analogy at 1470 — "has the analogous
                                     NotRequired/PendingUnclaimed/Claimed forms with
                                     LocalAuditTicketOwner::Statement". NO structural body anywhere.
                                     Census emits ZERO union candidates for it.
    CONTROL, same probe, same run: LocalAuditTicketOwner returns 4 (union + 3 arms), so the probe
    does find parents that exist. A zero here is real absence, not a broken query.
So the three statement_audit_admission sites reference a parent that has no landable body — the same "referenced but never structurally rendered" class as RootManifest and LogicalCommandRecord in the epic's C4 bucket. They cannot be modelled against a landed parent union until that parent acquires a body, which is a source question and not a modelling choice. Had I minted, I would have invented LocalStatementAuditAdmission's three arms out of a prose sentence.

=== 4. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE a03 WORK-LIST ===
a03 is a from-scratch slice: 49 of 49 union candidates and 129 of 129 arm candidates unlanded.
    17  top-level unions, union_name = containing schema, mechanical
    26  nested member unions that are genuinely new types and need a chosen, globally unique union_name
     3  operation_audit_admission narrowings -> model as references to LocalOperationAuditAdmission
     3  statement_audit_admission narrowings -> BLOCKED on a parent with no structural body
The census pin (union_candidate_count = 49) does not move: these remain census CANDIDATES either way. What changes is how each is discharged — a target row for a real union, versus a reference/adjudication for a narrowing. The coverage law accepts a target, an approved adjudication, or a covering arm/wire interior contract, so the narrowings need one of the latter two rather than a [[union]] row.
NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and I am not guessing: which of those two discharge forms the checker actually accepts for a narrowing, and whether the catalog has an existing row shape that expresses "member admits a named subset of a parent union's variants". That is the next measurement and it should be made before any row is written. Also unresolved: `LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation` and `::Statement` appear as single-variant pins inside the parent's own arm bodies at 1470 — a seventh site of the same construct, one variant rather than a subset, which the same answer should cover.

=== 5. WHY THIS CHECK WAS WORTH RUNNING BEFORE WRITING ===
It cost one read-only probe and no token. Without it the increment would have minted six duplicate union types over two parents, three of them with arms invented from a prose analogy, and the G0 name-collision failure would have surfaced only after the rows and their projections were written — i.e. after the expensive part. The naming collision was the tell, and the right response to a mechanical rule producing duplicates is to ask whether the things are actually distinct, not to disambiguate the names.

a03 UNION WRITE ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED — I MIS-SEQUENCED THE SLICE. The unions cannot land first; the identity kinds must. Measured with a rebuilt checker, catalog restored byte-identical to HEAD, token released. Not a u3gr-style wall — ordered work I put in the wrong order.

=== 1. WHAT I BUILT AND INSERTED ===
Generated the 17 top-level a03 unions (containing_schema == union_path, so union_name is mechanical and needs no naming judgment) plus their 46 arms in SOURCE order, plus the 63 matching [[target]] rows that catalog_projection_target_missing requires. Row-id derivation was controlled against three landed rows before generating anything: sha256("union|{cs}|{up}")[:16] and sha256("arm|{cs}|{up}|{arm}")[:16], kebab of union_name (not containing_schema) for the nested case, and generic signatures flattened into the kebab. All three controls exact. Arm tags came from ArmCandidate source positions, never the census's sorted arm_names print — that ordering differs and would have mis-tagged.
Counts after insertion reconciled exactly: union 32 -> 49, union_arm 77 -> 123, target 552 -> 615.

=== 2. WHY IT CANNOT LOAD — THE PREREQUISITE I MISSED ===
    17  projection_ordinary_union_unresolved_schema
    80  projection_ordinary_union_wire_contract_mismatch
     4  pin drift (projection_row_count, projection_registry_assignment_drift,
        projection_owner_assignment_drift, catalog_target_source_assignment_drift)
identity.rs:2018 requires a union's containing_schema to resolve in EXACTLY ONE identity class (logical, physical, bootstrap, prebootstrap, wire). Measured: 0 of my 17 owners resolve in ANY class. a03 has 89 top-level candidates and only 2 landed logical kinds, so essentially nothing this slice's unions hang off is registered yet.
identity.rs:2029-2074 then requires each top-level ordinary union to be backed EITHER by a same-name logical kind parent with identical lifecycle, a bound within the object bound, no broader role scope and self-only containing-schema closure, OR by a same-name union/discriminant WIRE parent with identical lifecycle, max size and closure — plus one wire variant per arm, with parent kind "discriminant" iff every arm is unit and "union" otherwise.
So the correct order for this slice is: MINT THE IDENTITY KINDS -> then the unions -> then the arms. That is exactly the order the a16 lane used ("mint the core time-plane logical kinds", then "mint the ten unreserved union hosts and complete all fourteen top-level role unions"). I went straight for the unions.

=== 3. THE REAL SHAPE OF THE NEXT INCREMENT ===
Per owner, two decisions that are NOT mechanical and should not be rushed:
  (a) IDENTITY CLASS — logical kind (an independently addressable durable object) versus wire type (an embedded value schema). This is a source-reading judgment per owner and it determines which of the two backing laws applies. Of the 17: names like LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex and LocalStatementIndex read as durable objects; DeliveryTransitionAppliedRef, ResultManifestRef, ResultActivationAppliedRef and LocalAuditTicketOwner read as embedded value schemas. I have NOT verified any of these against the source and am not guessing.
  (b) CODE ASSIGNMENT — fresh codes above 0x051d, minted directly, with no reservation for a non-StrongRef family (the reservation bijection law). Mint at status="reserved": activating a logical kind trips the compile-time assertions in crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs, which include_bytes! the projection and count active rows.
If the wire path is chosen for a union, its 46 arms additionally need one wire VARIANT row each, and the parent's kind must match the arm payload shape.

=== 4. METHOD NOTE — I NEARLY REPORTED MAIN AS RED OFF A STALE BINARY ===
My first run of the inserted catalog reported 105 violations including reservation epoch/assignment drift, and the reverted catalog still reported 7 against a tree that git said was byte-identical to HEAD. Both were artifacts: the probe binary was linked against an rlib built at the start of the session, which bakes in the EXPECTED_* counts and pin literals. Rebuilt from HEAD's own source, HEAD loads clean (LOAD_OK, 552 targets) and registry-check all exits 0, and the inserted catalog reports 101 rather than 105 — the four reservation/epoch entries were pure instrument noise.
The substantive 97 (17 + 80) are identical under both binaries, because they come from identity.rs structural logic rather than from pinned constants, which is why the conclusion survives. But the near-miss is the point: I was one step from filing "main is red" against a correct tree. Rule that caught it, and it is already on the a15/ovok trails: when a cached tool tells you the DATA is broken, control the TOOL first. Rebuild the rlib at the start of every hold and after every checker edit; never carry one across holds.

=== 5. STATE ===
registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml restored byte-identical to HEAD (git diff empty over registries/ and tools/). Catalog token released. Nothing half-applied. The generated 17 unions / 46 arms / 63 targets are staged off-repo and remain valid input for whoever does the mint increment first — they will need no regeneration, only the kinds landing ahead of them.
NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: the identity class of any of the 17 owners, and whether the checker accepts a narrowing (the six ::-qualified members from my earlier verdict) as a target, an approved adjudication, or a covering arm/wire interior contract. Both are read-only measurements and both should precede the next write.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: RootManifest, configuration, Raft, and cross-group trust prelude
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for RootManifest, configuration, Raft, and cross-group trust prelude. This task embeds source-plan lines 1544-1589 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Replica-local RootManifest** is a closed four-posture, role-tagged union. Its common header is `{generation,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,incarnation_continuity_profile_id,cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest,continuity_cas_version,service_visibility_epoch,replica_id,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id}|RetiredLocal,group_id,filesystem_profile_id,filesystem_instance_digest,local_writer_fence_epoch,physical_generation_lease:Active{descriptor:PhysicalGenerationLeaseDescriptor}|Retired{descriptor:RetirementLeaseDescriptor},metadata_tree_bootstraps:GeneratedMetadataTreeBootstrapSet,object_location_index_root,local_encoding_root,local_key_opener_root,raft_state_root:StrongRef<RaftStateRoot>?,nonretaining_predecessor_root_digest}` and exactly one payload. Local, Meta, and Shard require the `Active` arm. `RetirementLeaseDescriptor` is a distinct compact descriptor protecting the RetiredLocal proof closure and is created under the same prepublication inode/nonce contract; it cannot be decoded as an active generation lease. `Local` is `{applied_logical_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,prepared_payload_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalPreparedPayloadRoot>,audit_visibility_protocol_state_ref:StrongRef<AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Local>>,local_applied_logical_command_seq,local_visible_logical_command_seq,local_applied_index,local_visible_index,local_durable_index,maintenance_applied_index}`. `Meta` is the corresponding `{applied_global_state_root_ref,meta_prepared_payload_root_ref,audit_visibility_protocol_state_ref:StrongRef<AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Meta>>,global_applied_logical_command_seq,global_visible_logical_command_seq,meta_applied_index,meta_visible_index,meta_durable_index,maintenance_applied_index}`. `Shard` is `{applied_shard_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,shard_prepared_payload_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardPreparedPayloadRoot>,shard_protocol_state_ref:StrongRef<ShardProtocolState>,shard_applied_index,shard_visible_index,shard_durable_index,maintenance_applied_index,global_applied_logical_command_seq,audit_visible_global_prefix}`. `RetiredLocal` retains only its compact certified transition/retirement/audit proof closure and explicitly forbids semantic, prepared, Raft, protocol, or service roots.

For Local/Meta the protocol state owns the sole pipeline ref, visible audit outcomes/external head, and independent delivery lifecycles. RootManifest does not duplicate a direct pipeline or visible-state-root edge: its applied semantic root equals the protocol pipeline applied tail, while its visible sequence/index values equal the pipeline visible endpoint selected inside that protocol state. For Shard, `ShardProtocolState` contains only role-valid result/cursor/artifact transport, physical progress, and imported Meta visibility projections; it has no Local/Meta audit pipeline or semantic authority. Every active-role tuple byte-matches hard state, snapshot, configuration, prepared records, protocol state, restore state, and semantic state. Genesis, restore bridge, takeover, and Local-to-Sharded activation must all construct the role-valid initial protocol state before the first manifest; no active manifest can omit it. Cross-role/group/incarnation/continuity/visibility/protocol substitution is invalid.

`InitialProtocolStateRecipe<Role>` is the generated pre-order contract that makes that requirement executable: `{role_and_group,target_incarnation,target_service_visibility_epoch,source_kind:FreshGenesis|Restore|RoleTransition|Takeover,source_recovery_or_transition_projection_commitment?,semantic_applied_and_visible_endpoint_recipes,inherited_or_empty_audit_queue_recipe:LocalMetaOnly{pipeline_recipe,visible_outcome_index_recipe,external_continuity_recipe}|ShardInapplicable,independent_result_cursor_artifact_error_delivery_recipes,protocol_resource_escrow_recipes,capability_invalidation_suspension_or_transfer_recipes,physical_recovery_progress_recipe,security_barrier_recipe,complete_protocol_slot_bitmap,cross_plane_conservation_commitment,body_digest}`. Every active `protocol_state_fields.toml` slot appears exactly once; a source-kind/role matrix rejects missing, extra, or semantically impossible recipes. Pending/released output recipes retain bytes, policy, escrow, and release evidence but no target-era lease or send capability. Takeover preserves the exact prior Protocol state through its adoption record rather than reconstructing it from semantic state.

The universal first-manifest construction order is `semantic payload/command record/state root -> role-valid Protocol state from InitialProtocolStateRecipe -> PreparedOwnership root -> Consensus/Raft hard state, log, snapshot, configuration, and state root -> create/authenticate/fsync generation-lease inode and fsync its directory -> construct PhysicalGenerationLeaseDescriptor -> RootManifest -> RootSlot`. Every later publication uses the same lease-inode-before-manifest tail. A first-manifest builder may hold body recipes for later objects but no earlier object contains a future ObjectId. `PendingCreationGuard`, `PendingRestoreCreationGuard`, and `PendingRoleTransitionCreationGuard` each carry the exact role-valid Semantic/Protocol/Prepared/Consensus/bootstrap/physical-lease recipe commitments and complete slot bitmaps; their encoders accept only the registered source-kind closure. Genesis creates an empty Local/Meta audit pipeline with applied=visible and no barrier, or a Shard Protocol state with its genesis Meta projection. Restore reconstructs the projection's applied/visible split and pending queue. Role transition creates Meta `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` and Shard `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` Protocol arms; migrated owners are suspended or transferred without E-era send authority. Mandatory closure, backup/restore, checkpoint/snapshot, GC, format, role-transition, and orphan-cleanup walkers include the exact lease descriptor/inode proof class. Negative first-manifest fixtures delete, duplicate, substitute, or cross-role every plane root and lease field and must fail before write mode or service exposure.

A RetiredLocal manifest is authenticated and recoverable only as a compact terminal proof posture: ordinary open, resurrection, Raft participation, receipt issuance, and service advertisement fail before any logical object is exposed. A `MetadataTreeBootstrap` embeds `{tree_kind,tree_generation,tree_key_id,root_oid,cipher_descriptor,ciphertext_id,encoding_descriptor,placement_records,tree_key_opener,closure_digest}`; generated exact role-specific bootstrap unions replace erased lists. Each authenticated internal edge carries the exact child identity/cipher/encoding/placement/wrap/AAD fields defined in `durable_fields.toml`; parent ObjectId is absent because it is not known before parent encoding. Tree-root bootstrap edges are strong, ordinary locator entries are nonretaining, and semantic/protocol/prepared/terminal-proof marking decides liveness before realization resolution. RetiredLocal trees may locate only their compact proof closure. The predecessor is weak, and independently hashed markers use authenticated nonretaining subobject locators.

The preceding role union is the sole authoritative RootManifest schema; the obsolete `logical_state_root_oid`, `global_state_root_oid`, direct `audit_visibility_pipeline_ref`, and duplicate visible-root fields are unregistered. Generated field fixtures require exactly one applied semantic root and one role-valid protocol root, with the latter's authenticated pipeline selecting the visible root.

`MetadataTreeBootstrap.closure_digest` commits only the already-built metadata-tree closure. That same generation MUST NOT contain any entry—strong, weak, or physical-locator—for its current `RootManifest`, `RootSlot`, or bootstrap bytes; the slot bootstrap is the current manifest's sole opener. This is a construction rule in the generated DAG checker, not merely a GC classification.

**ConfigurationState and Raft persistence.** `ConfigurationState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id},group_id,configuration_epoch,form:Stable{voters[],storage_members[]}|Joint{old_voters[],new_voters[],old_storage_members[],new_storage_members[]},sorted_member_descriptors[{member_id,replica_namespace,consensus_signing_key_epoch,payload_receipt_key_epoch,roles,failure_domains[]}],raft_quorum_rule,payload_recoverability_predicate,failure_domain_map,gc_ack_policy,predecessor:WeakConfigurationIdentity?,transition_nonce}`; the ObjectId of these bytes is its identity and is not stored inside itself. Stable/joint quorum validation and the one-member specialization are exactly §14.2. Every same-group receipt/certificate carries `configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>` plus `payload_predicate_digest`, and its database/security-namespace/incarnation/role/group must match the enclosing log, hard state, snapshot, prepared root, manifest, and command. Another group imports it only through `RemoteConfigurationRef`, whose signed adoption evidence and retention floor are the explicit nonrecursive trust base; identical member lists, epochs, or a bare config OID never authorize cross-group replay.

Every durable posture has the Raft layer; single node is a one-member configuration. `RaftLogSegment` carries the exact domain/index/term/entry fields and a generated closed command union over Local semantic txn/control, Meta semantic txn/control, Shard prepare/decision/control, and `Maintenance{command:RaftMaintenanceCommand}`. `RaftMaintenanceCommand` is the role-tagged outer union `Local{command_ref:StrongRef<LocalMaintenanceCommand>}|Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<MetaMaintenanceCommand>}|Shard{shard_id,command_ref:StrongRef<ShardMaintenanceCommand>}`; role/group validation rejects substitution. `RaftHardState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,current_term,voted_for?,log_first,log_last,commit_index,applied_index,visible_index,configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,snapshot_ref?,maintenance_applied_index,certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptLedger>,prepared_order_attempt_root_ref:StrongRef<PreparedOrderAttemptRoot>,audit_signer_journal_root_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerJournalRoot>,protocol_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity}`.

`LocalMaintenanceCommand`, `MetaMaintenanceCommand`, and `ShardMaintenanceCommand` each contain the generated role-valid subset of certificate-plan/attempt/publish, order-attempt install/retire, audit signing-attempt staging/supersession, audit visibility (Local/Meta only), protocol result/cursor/artifact/error activation and disposition, prepared-owner recovery, physical progress, and backup/restore protocol operations. The former seven common families are ordinary concrete inner tags, not a second closed union; every inner tag has one command-contract row and one outer route. Maintenance advances Raft/maintenance indexes and its declared nonsemantic planes only; it never advances semantic sequences/HLC/heads or mutates a semantic payload. It uses the same live writer/incarnation/configuration guards and configured quorum durability and is included in snapshots/floors/backup/restore/GC. A self-staleness fixture fails any maintenance handler that changes semantic order.

`RaftConsensusCutProjection<Role>` is the prebuilt snapshot-self-excluding `{database/security namespace/incarnation/role/group,last_included_index:K,term_at_K,vote_and_commit_state_at_K,configuration_at_cut_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,prospective_configuration_refs,log_prefix_digest,retained_suffix_begin_index:K+1,certificate_prepared_remote_obligation_and_configuration_floors,format_first_target_escape_latch,takeover_adoption_head_projection,snapshot_slot:SelfExcluded{InstallThisSnapshot},body_digest}`. It contains no `RaftHardState`, `RaftStateRoot`, current-snapshot ref, or future snapshot identity; the takeover-head projection contains only its current typed ref. The construction-DAG generator rejects any path from this projection back to the snapshot under construction.

`RaftSnapshot` is a role-tagged exact **applied-cut** union. Common fields are `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,last_included_index:K,term_at_K,configuration_at_cut_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,semantic_applied_position_at_K,maintenance_applied_index_at_K,prepared_ownership_state_ref,consensus_cut_projection_ref:StrongRef<RaftConsensusCutProjection<Role>>,retained_suffix_begin_index:K+1,certificate_and_remote_obligation_floors,log_prefix_digest,log_to_all_planes_proof_ref:StrongRef<LogToAllPlanesProof>,body_digest}`. Local/Meta payloads carry the applied semantic state root at K, the complete role-valid `AuditVisibilityProtocolState` after every maintenance entry through K, its possibly earlier visible semantic root/position and unresolved candidate queue, the prepared root, configuration/checkpoint/floor selectors, and state-vector digest. Shard carries its applied semantic root, `ShardProtocolState`, prepared root, imported visible Meta prefix, and matching selectors. The invariant is `last_included_index = K = successor RaftHardState.applied_index_at_cut`; the retained log suffix begins exactly K+1. Construction is cut projection -> snapshot -> successor `RaftHardState{snapshot_ref}` -> successor `RaftStateRoot`, never a cycle. Every semantic/protocol/prepared/consensus object through K is owned by the snapshot closure, and none is also owned as a suffix entry; every object after K is suffix/prepared owned and absent from the cut. An unresolved Local/Meta candidate may cross the visible sub-prefix because the snapshotted protocol state owns its complete queue/closure. This is never described as a visible-only cut.

Configuration transitions bind proposal/post-apply configurations, current configuration equals the applied-tail configuration, and release uses the recorded configuration chain. Takeover preserves an origin-E protocol state under E+1 only through exact `TakeoverAdoptionRecord` validation. `RaftStateRoot<Role>` is `{hard_state_ref:StrongRef<RaftHardState<Role>>,retained_log_segment_refs,configuration_state_refs,matching_applied_cut_snapshot_ref:StrongRef<RaftSnapshot<Role>>?,prepared_and_certificate_ledger_refs,remote_obligation_floor_refs,transition_lock_refs,format_first_target_escape_latch:FormatFirstTargetEscapeLatch<Role>,takeover_adoption_head:TakeoverAdoptionHead<Role>,role_protocol_state_ref,unresolved_candidate_closure_refs,body_digest:BodyDigest<RaftStateRoot<Role>>}`. The hard-state and matching snapshot refs agree; genesis may have no snapshot, while a successor snapshot install follows the projection -> snapshot -> hard state -> root order above. Every reply follows a durable RootManifest publication of the appropriate semantic/protocol/consensus state.

`AuthorityLocalCertificateHeader` is the mandatory prefix of every authority-local quorum-signed receipt, certificate, proof, checkpoint/ack/floor, topology/GC/reconfiguration/activation barrier, and certificate-ledger entry: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,authority_group_role,authority_group_id,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,signer_epoch}`. Object-specific schemas below abbreviate it as `SameGroupCertificateHeader`; that alias is valid only inside the owning group. An imported export leaf instead begins `ImportedCertificateDomain {database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,authority_group_role,authority_group_id,authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,payload_predicate_digest,signer_epoch}` and contains no raw `StrongRef<ConfigurationState>` across groups. The generated certificate-domain checker requires the authority-local transcript, imported embedded canonical configuration, `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence`, and outer `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef` to agree exactly; old-incarnation, old-configuration, wrong-role, or wrong-predicate substitution fails before object-specific validation.

Every authority-local quorum artifact also obeys one universal signing protocol. `CertificateUnsignedBodyDigest<T>` is the registered domain-separated transcript recipe over every semantic field of certificate schema `T`, including its full authority/configuration/predicate header and pre-minted scalar `certificate_attempt_id`, but excluding exactly `certificate_attempt_plan_ref`, the canonical lock/share arrays, and aggregate/signature fields. A certificate schema contains no future certificate-ledger publication ObjectId or applied identity: the later ledger entry points to the completed certificate. It excludes no subject, topology, sequence, closure, result, policy, epoch, or verifier field. Before the first signature, a nonsemantic Raft maintenance entry quorum-roots `CertificateAttemptPlan {certificate_attempt_id,certificate_kind,subject_identity,authority_domain,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,certificate_schema_id,certificate_schema_version,canonical_unsigned_body_digest:CertificateUnsignedBodyDigest<T>,canonical_signer_subset[{signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_epoch}],threshold,signature_algorithm_and_encoding}` in `CertificateAttemptLedger`; this changes no semantic sequence or HLC. Each selected signer durably installs its distinct `CertificateSignerLock {plan_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptPlan>,certificate_attempt_id,subject_identity,certificate_schema_id,canonical_unsigned_body_digest,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_epoch,state:Locked}` in its fenced signer journal before emitting `CertificateSignatureShare {lock_ref:StrongRef<CertificateSignerLock>,signer_id,signing_key_id,canonical_signature_bytes}`. Signer identity/key/epoch make lock bytes and ObjectIds distinct. The completed certificate carries `certificate_attempt_plan_ref`, the sorted exact lock/share bijection, signer-subset bitmap, and canonical aggregate or canonical signature-set encoding outside its unsigned-body transcript; its validator recomputes `CertificateUnsignedBodyDigest<T>`, verifies every share, exact planned subset/threshold, and the aggregate/ordered-set bytes. A `CertificatePublish` maintenance entry records `CertificateAttemptRecord::Published` after the bytes exist. Thus plan -> per-signer locks -> shares -> certificate -> ledger publication is acyclic while semantic-field substitution still changes the signed digest. Signer order, signature encoding, and exact quorum subset are fixed by the plan, so crash/retry/leader change reproduces one certificate byte string and ObjectId. A signer refuses any other digest for that plan/subject.

An unavailable planned subset may be replaced only through the nonsemantic maintenance command `CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec {plan_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptPlan>,expected_ledger_state:Planned|Collecting,sorted_signer_journal_closure_refs,complete_share_bitmap,quorum_impossibility_proof_ref:StrongRef<CertificateQuorumImpossibilityProof>,no_certificate_or_export_publication_proof_ref:StrongRef<CertificateNonpublicationProof>,successor_signer_epoch_or_configuration,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Apply creates `CertificateAttemptAbandonment` only when the observed shares cannot meet threshold, every signer capable of completing the planned quorum has durably closed that plan at the named journal generation, and no certificate/export was published; otherwise it rejects. The ledger moves `Absent -> Planned -> Collecting -> Published` or `Planned|Collecting -> AbandonPending -> Abandoned`, never between terminal arms. A successor uses a new `certificate_attempt_id`, the same registered subject and unsigned-body digest unless the semantic owner itself legally changed, and a legal subset under the then-current configuration; it retains old plans, locks, shares, closures, and abandonment proof through the retirement floor. The role-local `CertificateAttemptLedger` recovers partial collections and permits at most one Published certificate identity per `(certificate kind,subject identity,unsigned-body digest)`; conflicting published digests are fatal evidence. The generated field table injects `certificate_attempt_id`, `certificate_attempt_plan_ref`, and the exact lock/share set into every routing, read, prepare, constraint, decision, checkpoint, projection, GC, derived, key, topology, backup/restore, acknowledgement, and `ExportLeaf` certificate even when a compact prose schema omits it. G0 generates include/exclude, signer-substitution, duplicate/missing-share, threshold, aggregate-mutation, abandonment, successor-subset, and maintenance-self-staleness fixtures for every registered certificate schema; only the named construction/signature fields may be excluded. Crash tests stop before/after each plan/lock/share/publication/abandon stage and across leader/configuration change.

**W12 global/shard formats (reserved now, activated only by the W12 feature epoch).** There is one meta consensus group and one consensus group per data shard. A raw `StrongRef` never crosses those group boundaries: every registration, basis, routing proof, prepare/decision/checkpoint certificate, fragment batch, apply acknowledgement, or topology proof used by another group is carried as `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>` and therefore has the two-sided retention/GC obligation in the reference contract. All groups remain inside the declared trusted database-process boundary; object-scoped `ShardCryptoCx` unwrap permits reduce accidental key exposure but are not a TEE or shard-compromise-isolation claim. Meta alone owns semantic time and global authority.

`RemoteGrantTargetRef` is the generated closed tagged union over every role-valid registered grant target, with one stable wire tag and exact role/posture matrix per target; raw `StrongRef` plus a kind sidecar is forbidden. `RemoteRetentionObligationRoot` is the authority-group authenticated map `(authority_domain,grant_id) -> Active{grant_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>,target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,consumer_domain,minimum_floor}|TransferredOut{transfer_record_ref:StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferRecord>,new_authority_domain,target_identity,migration_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor>}|TransferredInPending{transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,source_transfer_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,new_meta_grant_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>,legacy_target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,consumer_domain,minimum_floor}|TransferredIn{transfer_evidence_ref:StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferEvidence>,legacy_target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,consumer_domain,minimum_floor}|ReleaseApplied{tombstone_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>}|AckPublished{tombstone_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,release_summary_key,retain_ack_through}`. Transfer variants exist only for the one certified Local-to-Meta transition; ordinary reconfiguration uses the successor-grant handshake. Pending retains the already-built new grant and certified legacy target without naming future grant evidence. Release terminal states have no strong path to active target state, while transfer states retain exactly the migration floor/wrapper until adoption.

`RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot` is the consumer-group authenticated map `(authority_domain,grant_id) -> Acquired{grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,local_consumer_set_commitment}|AuthorityTransferPending{transfer_evidence_ref:LegacyTransferEvidenceRef,old_authority_domain,new_authority_domain,local_consumer_set_commitment}|AuthorityTransferAdopted{adoption_record_ref:StrongRef<RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionRecord>,new_authority_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}|ReleaseRequested{request_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord>,frozen_consumer_set_commitment}|ReleaseCertified{request_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord>,request_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>>,frozen_consumer_set_commitment}|Acknowledged{ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,release_summary_key,retire_after_floor}`. `ReleaseRequested|ReleaseCertified` encoders reject any added consumer under the old grant. The release-state identity is an already published weak root/record identity strictly before the request spec, never the request's future result.

`RemoteRetentionControlSpec` is the closed role-valid union `AcquireGrant{grant_spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantSpec>}|RegisterConsumerGrant{grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,expected_consumer_root_digest}|RequestConsumerRelease{request_spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec>}|PublishConsumerReleaseEvidence{request_certificate_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>,request_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>>}|ApplyAuthorityRelease{apply_spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseApplySpec>}|PublishAuthorityReleaseAck{ack_certificate_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>,ack_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>}|ConsumeReleaseAck{ack_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,expected_frozen_consumer_set_commitment}|AdoptLegacyAuthorityTransfer{adoption_spec_ref:StrongRef<RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec>}`. There is no generic transfer arm: old-Local transfer records are created only by `BeginRoleTransitionSpec`, Meta transfer evidence only by the certified activation projection, and a consumer uses only the exact adoption arm above. The generated role matrix fixes each arm to authority, consumer, or transition-consumer posture and rejects a record/evidence type in the wrong arm. This union is included in Local/Meta/Shard control registries. Checkpoint/configuration floors classify every authority/consumer/transfer entry plus unpublished certificate-ledger evidence. Crash tests cut before/after all six release transitions and every transfer/adoption/publication transition.

Trust-chain compaction also has an input/result split. `RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot` is the consumer-local authenticated map `authority_domain:ConsensusDomain -> CurrentEvidence{evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,trust_generation,minimum_consumer_floor}|ValidatedAnchor{anchor_ref:StrongRef<ValidatedRemoteConfigurationAnchor>,trust_generation,minimum_consumer_floor}`; it is strongly rooted in every Local/Meta/Shard payload, covered by every checkpoint/vector/configuration floor, and is the sole selector of current imported trust. `AdvanceRemoteConfigurationEvidenceSpec` is the ordinary role-valid CAS `{authority_domain,expected_trust_generation,expected_selected_evidence_or_anchor,successor_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,direct_joint_transition_proof,minimum_consumer_floor}`; apply verifies the exact predecessor/anchor and atomically selects `CurrentEvidence(successor,generation+1)`. Meta shard adoption and every shard application of a Meta configuration projection that changes authority must embed the same expected selector/generation and successor evidence and perform this CAS atomically; topology/configuration can never advance while trust remains behind.

Anchor compaction is legal only after reissuing/advancing every live wrapper, grant, backup, replay manifest, prepared owner, and certificate-ledger entry to the selected current evidence. `RemoteTrustCompactionPrecondition` is the generated exhaustive `{consumer state/checkpoint/floor basis,current evidence ref,scanned typed root classes,zero_live_reference_commitment_to_every_predecessor_evidence,current-wrapper inventory commitment}`. `ValidateRemoteConfigurationAnchorSpec` is `{authority_domain,current_configuration_evidence_ref,ordered_predecessor_evidence_refs,precondition_ref:StrongRef<RemoteTrustCompactionPrecondition>,expected_consumer_state,expected_trust_root_generation,expected_current_anchor_digest?,validation_policy_oid,transition_chain_digest}`. Apply verifies every transition while predecessors remain rooted and the precondition proves no surviving object still binds one. It constructs `ValidatedRemoteConfigurationAnchor {authority_domain,through_configuration_oid,through_epoch,current_configuration_canonical_bytes,current_configuration_bytes_digest,current_member_verification_key_set,current_payload_predicate_digest,validated_transition_chain_digest,zero_old_evidence_commitment,validation_policy_oid,input_spec_digest:WeakDigest,consumer_applied_identity:WeakAuthorityAppliedIdentity}` and atomically selects its strong anchor at generation+1. Those retained verification keys and the full domain/predicate authorize validation of a `ValidatedCheckpointSuccessor`; a digest alone cannot. `WeakAuthorityAppliedIdentity = Local{command_oid,logical_command_seq}|Meta{command_oid,global_logical_command_seq}|Shard{command_oid,shard_raft_index}` is nonretaining. A later checkpoint successor or ordinary advance replaces the anchor atomically; no trust gap is legal. Only after the anchor command is checkpoint-cut and the zero-live-old proof remains valid may predecessor evidence retire. Both specs are explicit Local/Meta/Shard control variants; no result is prebuilt with its future command.

`TopologyState` is the meta-owned routing authority `{topology_epoch,form:Stable|Joint{old_epoch,new_epoch},partition_scheme:SourceRange{partition_function_oid}|HubVertexCut{vertex_owner_function_oid,edge_owner_function_oid,replicated_hub_profile},meta_group_id,meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,sorted_shards[{shard_id,group_id,configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,state:Active|Joining|Draining,failure_domains,key_access_profile}],sorted_range_or_hub_assignments,constraint_owner_function_oid,id_allocation_owner_map,copy_basis_global_prefix?,cutover_global_prefix?,predecessor_topology_identity:WeakDigest?,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef?}`. Assignments are total and nonoverlapping, identify one canonical data/edge owner plus explicit read-only replicas, and use imported configuration evidence rooted in `RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot`. `Joint` retains both maps/configurations until its typed retirement floor. A meta configuration transition constructs a same-routing successor with the phase-appropriate meta config; shard adoption constructs a successor replacing exactly one imported shard config. A scalar epoch cannot authorize routing, prepare, ID allocation, constraints, or GC.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.
