=== 0. CORRECTION FIRST: THE GENERIC-FAMILY BLOCKER IS ALREADY GONE ===

In my previous comment I said no further a01 increment was available without a cross-slice ruling, and named the ExportLeaf<T> generic-family contract as the largest blocker. That was WRONG WHEN I WROTE IT. Commit 4081560 ("feat(a16): generic-family field hosts and the five generic embedded unions") had already extended field-row containing_schema resolution to the generic-free family — the same law I2a gave ordinary unions — and it landed BEFORE my own 2D commit. I asserted a blocker from an earlier analysis instead of re-deriving it against current HEAD, which is precisely the mistake I had written a lesson about one increment earlier.

identity.rs now reads:
    let containing_family = generic_free_family(f.containing_schema.as_str());
    let containing_logical = logical_by_name.get(containing_family);
with the comment "one registered kind row commits every expansion of its family ... The family is only a *lookup*; every downstream contract (tag uniqueness, anchor matching, BodyDigest recipes) still keys on the exact signed containing_schema, so two expansions never merge."

PROVEN EMPIRICALLY, not inferred: I spliced two real ExportLeaf<T> field rows into a scratch copy of HEAD and validated. The only finding was a row_id derivation nit (the derived suffix is `export-leaf-t-...`, because lower_kebab turns `<T>` into `-t-`), which is a naming rule, not a blocker.

=== 1. THE 12 UNCOVERED a01 FIELD KEYS, RE-PARTITIONED ===

LANDABLE TODAY, no ruling required (2 keys). Both proven green in scratch:

  ExportLeaf<T>.domain                              ImportedCertificateDomain
  RemoteRetentionGrantSpec.authority_configuration_ref  StrongRef<ConfigurationState>
Both types are FULLY DEFINED in the plan, in slice a04:
  a04:1558  `ConfigurationState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id},group_id,...}`
  a04:1570  `ImportedCertificateDomain {database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,authority_group_role,authority_group_id,authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,payload_predicate_digest,signer_epoch}`

=== 2. THE ANNOTATION / SEMANTIC-BINDING / EVIDENCE LAYER (CATALOG-SCALE) ===

This is not an a01 choice and should not be made as one. Today the catalog has ZERO annotation, semantic_binding, expansion_binding, and evidence rows across ALL 21 slices, with all four EXPECTED_*_COUNT consts pinned at 0.

The completion law is per-TARGET, not per-slice (appendix_a.rs, the definition_status=="complete" block). Every complete target requires:
  - exactly one annotation
  - exactly one semantic binding
  - at least one static evidence row covering G0
  - at least one runtime evidence row, planned or live
  - a source-reconciled top|/field|/union|/arm| contract
So the layer is roughly four rows per target. Current cost, by slice, at 534 targets:

  a04  16 (~64)         a10  16 (~64)    a06 11 (~44)   a20 10 (~40)

Semantic bindings and evidence rows are NOT derivable — they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs and gate. Those are per-owner knowledge.

PROPOSED SHAPE, for the other slice owners to adopt or contest:
 (a) Freeze the four row schemas and their pin mechanics ONCE, in one reviewed increment, before any slice authors a single row. Getting this wrong after 2000 rows exist is a mass migration.
 (b) Generate annotations from the census the way projections are generated today, with a sanctioned writer command and a byte-diff law, so annotation drift is impossible by construction. Do not hand-author 2136 rows.
 (c) Author semantic bindings and evidence per slice, by that slice's owner, since only they know the checker/test/gate IDs.
 (d) Sequence it AFTER the residual field/union/arm coverage of each slice, never before: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so every target minted later needs its own four rows anyway. Front-loading it just means editing the same rows twice.
 (e) Nobody should flip definition_status="complete" until (a)-(d) are done for that slice, because the flip arms all of these laws simultaneously, plus source_complete_census_uncovered and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved.

 - File the tracked items as beads in ONE batched br create pass with the architecture bead-provenance pins re-frozen in the SAME commit, under the catalog token, so architecture-check is never transiently red for the other five agents.

     and only the pin reconstruction fails, with a message that never says "you forgot to name your
     rows". And a SECOND tranche must APPEND to the existing closure; a script that skips when the
     closure is already present fails silently in exactly the same way.
  3. A census that accepts a wire-type owner as valid will overcount landable fields. Field owner
     resolution is logical|bootstrap|physical|prebootstrap only.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: W12 Genesis, role transition, and activation formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for W12 Genesis, role transition, and activation formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1590-1658 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Fresh W12 genesis and one-way Local-to-W12 activation.** `ShardedGenesisCertificate` is the first object in the construction order: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,genesis_nonce,meta_group_id,meta_configuration_canonical_bytes_digest_and_payload_predicate,meta_initial_protocol_recipe_commitment,meta_initial_prepared_and_consensus_recipe_commitment,sorted_shards[{shard_id,group_id,configuration_canonical_bytes_digest_and_payload_predicate,failure_domains,key_access_profile,initial_protocol_recipe_commitment,initial_prepared_and_consensus_recipe_commitment}],topology_and_partition_recipe,generated_initial_meta_projection_slot_recipes[one_per_MetaProjectionSlot],initial_global_prefix,complete_per_group_durable_slot_bitmap_commitment,root_authority_policy_and_key_epoch,configured_root_authority_signatures}`. It commits no future evidence, payload, topology, projection, checkpoint, or root ObjectId/digest. Construction is certificate → per-group `RootAuthorityTrustArtifact` and Genesis configuration evidence → consumer-local `GenesisMetaProjectionPayload` objects → Topology/ActiveMetaProjection roots → Semantic roots → role-valid Protocol roots → Prepared/Consensus roots → manifests/slots. `GenesisMetaProjectionPayload` is `{genesis_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardedGenesisCertificate>,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,ordered_slot_values[{slot_tag,typed_canonical_value,source_recipe_digest}],exhaustive_slot_bitmap,configuration_evidence_refs[StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>],availability_floor}`. Its bitmap equals the complete generated `MetaProjectionSlot` registry—not a five-slot subset—and it has no raw remote-group edge. Every Genesis evidence and `InitialProtocolStateRecipe` byte-matches the root-authority-signed role/group entry, and every group verifies the complete first-manifest slot bitmap before emitting its barrier. A self-selected member signature or bare digest is not a trust anchor.

Existing Local databases activate W12 only through one offline, audited, one-way role transition. Before freeze, the coordinator claims the sole exact Appendix A `ServiceVisibilityEpochReservation` under the external reservation-authority protocol; its target epoch is strictly above both the source and external floors, use requires Usable time evidence, and abandonment permanently burns it. No shorter role-transition-specific encoding exists. The coordinator then pre-mints `ShardingRoleTransitionPlan {database/security namespace/incarnation,migration_nonce,service_epoch_reservation_ref:StrongRef<ServiceVisibilityEpochReservation>,source/target service visibility epochs,source Local group/configuration and expected basis prefix,new Meta and sorted shard group/configuration canonical bytes+payload predicates,fresh per-group log-origin nonces,topology/partition body,projection checker/version,local_to_global_projection_ref:StrongRef<LocalToGlobalProjection>,sorted_local_to_shard_projection_refs[StrongRef<LocalToShardProjection>],activation checkpoint/vector/floor body recipes,expected hidden shard barrier predicates,legacy_artifact disposition table,legacy_retention_authority_transfer_plan_ref:StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferPlan>,cursor transition policy,external continuity/catalog predecessors,rollback_cutoff,completeness_digest}`. Reservation fields byte-match the plan and refer to no future plan identity. Projection objects are pre-order recipes over the existing Local basis plus deterministic freeze result and contain no result/root identity. Every payload field and mandatory inventory class has exactly one disposition `ReencodeForMeta|PartitionAndReencodeForShard{exact shard set}|CertifiedLegacyCarry{promise class,terminal transition}|ArchiveBeforeBegin{archive requirement}|RejectWithBlocker{reason}`. They cover graph/version/constraint/identity/allocator/branch/key/history/derived/replay/backup/cursor/outcome/capability/DP/resource/audit/transparency/prepared/certificate/remote-trust/retention state. Freeze is invalid while any blocker remains.

`ShardingFreezeSpec {plan_ref:StrongRef<ShardingRoleTransitionPlan>,expected_operational_state,expected Local applied/visible state heads and logical/commit/HLC prefixes,drain inventory,expected_audit_pipeline_ref:StrongRef<LocalAuditVisibilityPipeline>,terminal_audit_gate}` rejects new work and drains every active transaction; unadmitted work is explicitly cancelled, every receipted/ordered owner is terminal or covered by the plan's exact transfer, and the pre-freeze audit pipeline is empty (`applied_tail == visible`) after exact advancement. Apply constructs `ShardingFreezeRecord {spec_ref:StrongRef<ShardingFreezeSpec>,applied_control_ref,source_basis_identity:WeakStateIdentity,assigned frozen prefix,branch/schema/policy/revocation/key/audit/continuity commitments,terminal txn/outcome/prepared proof,live promise inventory,plan_digest,deterministic_frozen_result_commitment,state:FreezePendingAudit}`. It does **not** name its future payload/root. The ordinary command apply builds the candidate root and pipeline successor; that pipeline alone owns the candidate until external audit resolution and an exact gap-free `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local>` make the freeze candidate visible and change migration state to `FrozenVisible`. The freeze transition may begin only from an empty predecessor pipeline and no later command may append behind it except audit advancement or `ShardingUnfreezeSpec`, preventing a hidden post-freeze tail. Only after `FrozenVisible` may transition artifacts be consumed. Unfreeze is legal only from that visible state before Begin, invalidates this plan generation, and requires a newly audited plan/freeze.

Before Begin can be proposed, every new replica directory is prepared under a linear `PendingRoleTransitionCreationGuard {migration_nonce,target_role_and_group,target_manifest_staging_inode_identity_and_filesystem_profile,local_whole_inode_lease,root_publication_sequencer,plan_and_configuration_commitment,initial_protocol_state_recipe_ref:StrongRef<InitialProtocolStateRecipe<Role>>,first_semantic_entry_recipe_commitment,initial_prepared_recipe_commitment,initial_consensus_recipe_commitment,first_manifest_and_slot_recipe_commitment,complete_durable_slot_bitmap,exact_allowed_staging_inventory,role_transition_signature_lock_ref,unconsumed}`. It may create only uniquely named, unreachable transition staging bytes for those exact recipes, the first-entry authorization closure, and its signature lock; it cannot publish `manifest.root`, serve traffic, issue ordinary receipts, or accept another migration nonce. New-group members sign `RoleTransitionJoinAcceptance` only after rereading that complete Semantic/Protocol/Prepared/Consensus/bootstrap staging closure and bitmap. `RoleTransitionReadyCertificate {root-authority domain,plan_ref,service_epoch_reservation_identity,source/target service epochs,sorted new-group acceptances,complete configuration/log-origin/initial-plane-recipe/staging availability commitment,old-Local freeze visibility certificate identity,expiry policy,threshold signatures}` is pre-order evidence that every group can complete. After the dual transition certificate and external continuity reservation receipt exist, the guard may order/apply only the registered first entry under a RoleTransitionOnly lease; it then follows the universal construction order and publishes one complete hidden Meta/shard manifest. Meta begins with an empty AuditSystem-ready pipeline while service-hidden; Shard begins with `ShardProtocolState::RoleTransitionPreparedHidden`. Migrated pending/released output owners enter the recipe as suspended/transferred promises with no E2 lease or send authority. The guard never publishes a headless or plane-incomplete destination manifest and never becomes an ordinary writer token. Creation, restore, and takeover guards cannot substitute for it.

The final old-Local entry is `BeginRoleTransitionSpec {plan_ref,freeze_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardingFreezeRecord>,freeze_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>>,role_transition_ready_certificate_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionReadyCertificate>,expected_frozen_visible root/head/prefix,legacy authority-transfer set,migration retention floor recipe,terminal_audit_gate=StructurallyInapplicable{ShardingRoleTransitionAuthority}}`. The portable certificate byte-matches the freeze candidate, exact visible endpoint, releasing RootManifest/slot, and ready-certificate commitment; no Semantic object references the Protocol pipeline. Acceptance is a terminal Raft seal, not merely an apply-time flag: before any voter acknowledges the Begin `AppendEntries` at index `I`, it durably installs `RaftRoleTransitionSeal {plan_digest,begin_command_digest,terminal_local_raft_index=I,log_origin commitments}` in its `RaftStateRoot` and thereafter rejects every entry or snapshot extending beyond `I`. Once a quorum has accepted Begin, Local recovery may only finish this transition or enter an explicitly fenced restore/clone; it can never unseal and resume Local writes. Apply constructs `BeginRoleTransitionRecord`, advances to `(Lf,Cf,Hf)`, installs the canonical `RoleTransitionLocked` state, and applies the precommitted old-Local side of every authority transfer. The certificate requires both quorum-durable seals and quorum apply through Begin, eliminating the committed-but-unapplied append window.

Every old-Local and new-Meta signer first persists `RoleTransitionSignatureLock {migration_nonce,plan_digest,dual_transcript_digest,state=Locked}` in its staging/certificate ledger; quorum intersection plus the one-digest rule prevents two certificates. `RaftRoleTransitionCertificate` is the unique dual-domain transcript `{database/security namespace/incarnation,plan_ref and digest,migration_nonce,service_epoch_reservation_identity,source/target service visibility epochs,frozen-visible source commitment,Begin input/record weak identities plus Local command/marker/MMR/checkpoint chain digests,Lf,Cf,Hf,projection identities/digests,old Local/new Meta domains/configurations/predicates,all pre-minted log origins,sorted shard domains/configurations and expected hidden-ready barrier predicates,topology,external continuity/catalog predecessors,legacy-retention transfer commitment,migration-floor recipe,rollback cutoff,old-Local quorum seal+apply signatures,new-Meta join+signature-lock quorum signatures}`. It names no future state root, barrier, activation record, or result.

Portable `RoleTransitionContinuityReservationManifest` commits that certificate, epoch reservation, exact prior continuity head, terminal Local seal, destination groups/endpoints, and target epoch. External CAS changes `Operational{posture=Local,epoch=E}` to `RoleTransitionReserved{migration_nonce,transition_certificate_digest,source_posture:Local,target_posture:Sharded,source_service_visibility_epoch:E,target_service_visibility_epoch:E2,service_epoch_reservation_id,source_local_group_and_terminal_seal_commitment,target_group_topology_and_endpoint_commitment,transition_writer_authority_digest,lease_policy:RoleTransitionOnly}` and returns reference-free `RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt {continuity_prior_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,continuity_reserved_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,continuity_cas_receipt_bytes_and_digest,service_epoch_reservation_claimed_head_bytes_and_digest,service_epoch_reservation_consumed_head_bytes_and_digest,reservation_consumption_receipt_bytes_and_digest,manifest_digest,target_service_visibility_epoch,authority_signatures}`. `RoleTransitionContinuityReservationImportRecord` is the Meta/bootstrap-local owner `{manifest_ref,portable_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,claimed_head_ref:StrongRef<ReservationAuthorityHead>,consumed_head_ref:StrongRef<ReservationAuthorityHead>,consumption_receipt_ref:StrongRef<ReservationConsumptionReceipt>,continuity_reserved_record_ref:StrongRef<ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord>,exact_transcript_match_digest,body_digest}`. The fixed external order is continuity CAS first, then the reservation's direct `ClaimedForUse -> Consumed` CAS whose `applied_use_identity` is that reserved-continuity head. A crash between them leaves a hidden roll-forward state; recovery can only finish the same consumption, and no combined receipt or destination publication exists until both receipts verify. No destination manifest publication is legal before this receipt and its imported consumed-reservation proof. Once it exists, sealed Local cannot serve or obtain OrdinaryWrite authority, and destination groups may use RoleTransitionOnly solely for hidden bootstrap/projection/service preparation. A crash here is unavailable but roll-forward-only; it never creates overlapping Local and Sharded service.

No consumer directly references an old-group object. `CertifiedRoleTransitionRef` is the **bootstrap** consumer-local imported leaf `{certificate_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,embedded_dual_transcript_and_digest,old_local_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,new_meta_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,old_and_new_signature_sets,consumer_group_role,consumer_group_id,certificate_availability_evidence,source_transition_retention_grant_evidence}`. Its sole retention evidence is the already-existing source/root-authority migration grant established before Begin; it contains no new-Meta grant, activation record, hidden root, or evidence that activation will create. This bootstrap ref is therefore legal in destination first-entry specs. After hidden Meta activation and its audit visibility advance, `CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef` is constructed as `{bootstrap_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,activation_record_and_hidden_root_evidence,activation_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,new_meta_grant_evidence_bijection,legacy_transfer_finalize_record_and_visibility_certificate_evidence,meta_successor_floor_body_commitment,consumer_group_role,consumer_group_id,successor_availability_evidence}`; every field already exists, and it cannot be built by the activation it names. `CertifiedTransitionArtifactRef<T>` adds `{transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,artifact_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,artifact_digest,artifact_kind,source Local configuration evidence,consumer role/group,artifact availability evidence,source migration retention grant evidence}` for bootstrap. `CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<T>` is the closed stage union `Bootstrap{artifact_ref:CertifiedTransitionArtifactRef<T>,legacy_promise_class,source_local_prefix,transition_or_expiry_or_archive_condition}|Successor{transition_successor_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef>,artifact_identity,artifact_digest,legacy_promise_class,source_local_prefix,terminal_condition,successor_owner_acknowledgement}`. Long-lived floors, consumers, service preparation, and retirement must upgrade to Successor before the source migration grant can release. These are the only legal references to Local projections, outcomes, cursors, delivered bytes, replay/backup manifests, verifier keys, or other still-live Local artifacts from Meta or a shard. They never reinterpret a Local `StrongRef` as consumer-local.

`LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferPlan` is the pre-order Local object `{migration_nonce,old_local_domain:ConsensusDomain,new_meta_domain:ConsensusDomain,old_local_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,new_meta_configuration_canonical_digest,sorted_entries[{old_grant_id,old_grant_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>,target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,new_meta_grant_id,new_meta_grant_body_recipe,transfer_nonce,required_consumer_adoption_predicate}],complete_old_authority_root_digest,complete_transfer_commitment}`. `BeginRoleTransition` creates one `LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferRecord {migration_nonce,plan_entry_index,old_grant_id,new_meta_grant_id,old_local_domain,new_meta_domain,consumer_domain,target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,target_identity,target_closure_inventory_digest,transfer_nonce,state:TransferredOut,assigned_local_logical_command_seq}` per entry and replaces every matching old authority-map entry atomically. No record names future Meta evidence or adoption.

Activation constructs the already-planned new Meta grant records and installs `TransferredInPending` entries; it cannot construct grant evidence or a transfer certificate for the root it is still building. After the hidden activation root and its audit visibility advance exist, Meta constructs `RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence` for each new grant, then `LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferEvidence {transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,source_transfer_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,plan_entry_projection,old/new authority domains,consumer_domain,target_identity,target_closure_inventory_digest,old_local_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferRecord>>,migration_retention_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,new_meta_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}`. `RetentionAuthorityTransferFinalizeSpec` names the exact pending-entry/evidence bijection and current MetaPending floor; apply changes every TransferredInPending to TransferredIn and constructs/selects the MetaSuccessor floor. Only then does the Meta quorum create `LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,evidence_ref:StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferEvidence>,transition_identity,old/new grant identities,old/new authority domains,consumer_domain,target_identity,target_closure_inventory_digest,transfer_nonce,activation_finalize_and_audit_visibility_identities,one_digest_signer_lock_ref:StrongRef<CertificateSignerLock>,quorum_signatures}` and export it under the ordinary floor. `LegacyTransferEvidenceRef` is `MetaLocal{evidence_ref:StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferEvidence>}|ImportedMeta{certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferCertificate>}`. A consumer orders `RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec {transfer_evidence_ref:LegacyTransferEvidenceRef,expected_old_authority_domain,expected_old_consumer_entry_digest,new_meta_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,expected_new_authority_domain,complete_local_consumer_set_commitment}` and apply creates `RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionRecord`; only then may it treat Meta as release authority.

`ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor` is the closed role tag `SourceLocked{plan_ref:StrongRef<ShardingRoleTransitionPlan>,source_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>,source_config_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>,source_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<MigrationSourceInventory>,transfer_record_refs[StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferRecord>],legacy_promise_inventory_ref:StrongRef<LegacyPromiseInventory>,rollback_cutoff}|MetaPending{bootstrap_transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,legacy_artifact_registry_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyArtifactRegistry>,pending_transfer_entry_refs[StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>],source_retention_evidence,continuity_reservation_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,target_service_visibility_epoch,required_finalize_bitmap}|MetaSuccessor{transition_successor_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef>,legacy_artifact_registry_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyArtifactRegistry>,transfer_evidence_refs[StrongRef<LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferEvidence>],consumer_adoption_commitment,new_meta_and_shard_operational_checkpoint_cut_requirements,archive_expiry_cursor_outcome_replay_backup_terminal_conditions,retirement_predicate}`. `MetaPendingMigrationFloorRecipe` contains every MetaPending field as a pre-order body recipe but no future new-Meta grant/evidence ObjectId; `ShardingActivationSpec` consumes that recipe plus certified source retention projection, and apply constructs grants -> pending entries -> MetaPending floor. Finalize later constructs new grant evidence -> transfer evidence -> `CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef` -> MetaSuccessor. No arm points to a predecessor floor; any spec referencing a floor uses `StrongRef<ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor>` plus an exact required-arm predicate, never `StrongRef<Enum::Variant>`. Service preparation and every long-lived consumer require the MetaSuccessor arm/successor wrapper. Discharge requires every transfer adopted, every new group on a superseding Operational checkpoint/cut, and every legacy promise terminally disposed; only then may the source/bootstrap migration grant enter the six-stage release handshake.

The terminal old-Local `manifest.root` is retired explicitly rather than ignored. `RetirementReadinessRef` is the closed union `MetaLocal{checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,activated_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedRetentionCutSet>}|ShardRemote{checkpoint_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardCheckpointCertificate>,activated_cut_ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardActivatedCutAck>}`; `ShardActivatedCutAck`, `LegacyPromiseTerminalRecord`, and `LegacyPromiseTerminalAck` are registered role-specific checkpoint/cut and legacy-disposition schemas with exact authority/configuration/availability fields, not aliases. `LegacyDispositionRef` is `TransferAdoption{record_ref:StrongRef<RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionRecord>}|MetaTerminal{record_ref:StrongRef<LegacyPromiseTerminalRecord>}|ShardTerminal{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<LegacyPromiseTerminalAck>}|Archived{grant_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveRetentionGrant>}`.

`RetiredLocalManifestRecipe` is the sequence-neutral `{replica_id,terminal_source_manifest_identity,terminal_source_root_identity,terminal_source_logical_and_commit_prefix,filesystem_instance_digest,terminal_role_transition_seal_digest,compact_physical_inventory_digest,stable_retired_header_and_body_fields,late_bindings:[BindThisRetirementCertificateLeaf,BindThisCatalogReceipt,BindThisRetirementAuditEvidence],basis_digest:RetiredLocalManifestBasisDigest}`. The registered basis transcript covers every stable field/late-binding tag but no future ObjectId. `LegacyLocalRetirementAuthorizeSpec {transition_successor_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef>,meta_migration_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor>,required_floor_arm:MetaSuccessor,complete_floor_discharge_proof_ref:StrongRef<MigrationFloorDischargeProof>,sorted_new_group_readiness_refs[RetirementReadinessRef],all_transfer_adoption_and_legacy_disposition_refs[LegacyDispositionRef],expected_meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_old_replica_set_digest,expected_external_posture_catalog_version,sorted_replica_retirement_recipes[RetiredLocalManifestRecipe],terminal_audit_gate}`. After its exact gap-free release, `LegacyLocalRetirementAuditEvidence` is the portable certified projection of the Meta ticket/event/resolution, external batch CAS, and `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>` plus the authorization result, configuration, trust, and availability; it contains no raw Meta `StrongRef`. The Meta quorum creates `LegacyLocalRetirementCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,authorization_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,authorization_audit_evidence_commitment,transition_identity,discharge_commitment,expected_old_replica_set_digest,sorted_replica_recipe_basis_digests,external_posture_cas_basis,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. `LegacyLocalRetirementCatalogReceipt` binds that certificate, recipe-basis set, prior/result catalog versions, transition, replica set, AuthorizedPendingReplicas, CAS receipt, and signatures. Order is authorize -> gap-free visibility release/evidence -> certificate -> catalog CAS receipt -> per-replica retirement; no future identity is prehashed.

`LegacyLocalRetirementGuard` is a linear, nonexportable guard acquired separately per old replica. It authenticates inode, terminal Local root/seal, exact recipe basis, certificate/export leaf, catalog receipt, and imported audit evidence, then binds the three late slots and constructs the final RetiredLocal body. The durable field is uniformly `terminal_role_transition_seal_digest`. It first overwrites the alternate slot with RetiredLocal and syncs/rereads it, then overwrites the former active slot with the byte-identical recipe/body and syncs/rereads it; no acknowledgement is legal while either valid slot is Local. The guard cannot append Raft, revive state, issue receipts, reclaim bytes, or publish another root. Recovery rejects ordinary open and exposes only compact proof closure.

Each replica emits `LegacyLocalRetirementAck {database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,transition_identity,retirement_certificate_identity,catalog_authorization_receipt_digest,replica_id,replica_recipe_basis_digest,prior_active_and_alternate_slot_generations,written_retired_slot_generations,retired_slot_manifest_identities_and_body_digests,no_active_local_slot_proof,filesystem_instance_digest,compact_physical_inventory_digest,terminal_role_transition_seal_digest,two_slot_reread_and_durability_proof_digest,replica_signing_key_epoch,replica_signature}`. After the exact ack set, catalog completion moves to RetiredAll. `LegacyLocalRetirementFinalizeSpec` names authorization/certificate/both catalog receipts, exact ack bijection, Meta configuration, `expected_migration_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor>` with required MetaSuccessor arm, discharge proof, and terminal gate. Its gap-free release yields exact `LegacyLocalRetirementFinalizationCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,finalize_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,finalize_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,transition_identity,retirement_certificate_identity,catalog_completion_receipt_digest,sorted_replica_ack_commitment,expected_replica_set_digest,reclaimability_predicate_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}` rooted by the certificate ledger.

Physical cleanup is separately narrow and durable-before-delete. `RetiredLocalReclamationPlan` is `{transition_identity,replica_id,both_retired_slot_identities,finalization_certificate_identity,catalog_completion_digest,sorted_targets[{target_identity,expected_physical_realization_digest,operation_id,method}],preserved_proof_inventory_digest,archive_legal_hold_backup_predicate_commitment,plan_digest}`. Before each irreversible action the offline tool durably records `RetiredLocalReclamationProgress {plan_digest,target_ordinal,operation_id,state:Requested|Completed{pre_and_post_physical_root_digests,receipt_digest}}` in the external retirement ledger; retry is idempotent by operation ID. `RetiredLocalReclamationGuard` verifies both retired slots, ack, final certificate, catalog, cut, predicates, plan, and current realization, and may touch only the selected target while preserving both compact slots/proof closure. Completion emits `LegacyLocalReclamationCompletionReceipt {transition_identity,replica_id,both_retired_manifest_identities,plan_digest,complete_target_receipt_bijection,reclaimed_inventory_digest,preserved_proof_inventory_digest,method,completed_at,time_authority_evidence_digest,authority_signature}`. It cannot create any database writer token or mutate semantics. Crash/partial/hold/proof-preservation tests cover each target boundary.

`LocalToGlobalProjection` is the pre-order recipe `{migration_nonce,source_local_basis:WeakStateIdentity,deterministic_freeze_result_commitment,Lf,Cf,Hf,ordered_global_payload_field_recipes[one per generated field],legacy_artifact_registry_recipe,attempt_summary_genesis_recipe,authority_transfer_recipe,complete_source_field_and_object_coverage_digest,semantic_equivalence_digest}`. `LocalToShardProjection` is `{migration_nonce,target_shard_domain:ConsensusDomain,source_local_basis:WeakStateIdentity,deterministic_freeze_result_commitment,partition_assignment,ordered_shard_payload_field_recipes[one per generated field],ordered_meta_projection_slot_recipes[one per MetaProjectionSlot],history_key_derived_prepared_retention_recipes,complete_source_range_and_field_coverage_digest,semantic_equivalence_digest}`. They contain no future freeze result, transition certificate, target object, checkpoint, or root identity. `ActivationMetaProjectionPayload` is built only after the certificate as `{transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,projection_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedTransitionArtifactRef<LocalToShardProjection>>,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,ordered_slot_values[{slot_tag,typed_canonical_value,source_recipe_digest}],exhaustive_slot_bitmap,remote_configuration_evidence_refs[StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>],availability_floor}`; its bitmap equals every generated `MetaProjectionSlot`.

Activation checkpoints use `CheckpointBasis = Genesis|Global{WeakGlobalCommandIdentity}|LocalActivation{transition/projection commitment,frozen Local weak head,Lf,Cf,Hf}`; shard projection checkpoints use the analogous LocalActivationProjection basis. Fresh Meta genesis has no head, and every later record uses `Prior`. `GlobalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStatePayload>,global_command_head:StrongGlobalCommandRef?}`. Thus every registration, statement registration/publication, admission/cancel/read close, policy/key/topology/GC/remote-retention transition, directory publication, decision-certificate/global-delta publication, activation, and restore bridge enters one contiguous Meta command-record chain.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

Blocker named with its count: 1 union, 1 parsed arm, 1 UNPARSED arm. No rows landed here.

THE SYMBOL: CapabilityMigrationIndex, a05, whole-schema union (union_name == containing_schema ==
union_path). Its host is a landed logical kind at construction_order 30, so the class is settled and
the collision predicate is satisfied — top_level_shape holds, no wire parent, logical-backed by

    "ordinary union must exactly match one conflict-free, FULLY PARSED source union

The census reports parsed_arm_count = 1 (`Consumed`), unparsed_arm_count = 1. The source union has
an arm the census could not parse, so the candidate's arm set is INCOMPLETE. Landing it would freeze
a closed union that is missing an arm — the same class of silent durable-format defect as an
inverted arm tag, except the checker catches this one.

WHY MY SWEEP MISSED IT, and the correction is now in the tool: I filtered on `arm_set_conflict`,
which is false here, and never looked at `unparsed_arm_count`. Those are different failures —
conflict means two occurrences disagree, unparsed means one occurrence was not fully read. The
sweep predicate now rejects `unparsed_arm_count > 0 || arm_set_conflict` before any class or
collision reasoning. Rarity is why it survived: only 3 of 573 census unions carry an unparsed arm,
so nothing else I have landed was exposed, and I re-checked a12's four (parsed 3, unparsed 0 each)
before landing them.

CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER REPORT: the re-sweep total is 8 landable unions, not 9 — a14 four
(landed, eaf5320), a12 four (landed, 9a56a24), a05 ZERO. The 9 I reported counted this one.

is malformed for the census grammar (an erratum), or the grammar needs to cover the shape it uses.
Both are outside what an applier can decide, and neither is a class or order question, so it belongs
with neither l6xd nor fgdb-tuw1. Handing a05 back rather than holding it against a blocker I cannot
move; its union layer is otherwise complete at 19 landed.

WHAT LANDED UNDER THIS BEAD (d16080b): five reservation-backed role-transition kinds at their own
reserved codes with disposition flipped reserved -> existing — CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef
0x026d@29, LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferCertificate 0x02ef@29,
RoleTransitionMetaServicePrepareCertificate 0x0421@31, RoleTransitionShardOperationalAck 0x042a@30,
ShardingFreezeSpec 0x0486@29. Orders derived from BOTH reference directions; two are two-sided with
consistent windows (29..=30 and a degenerate 29..=29) and three have a floor and no ceiling.

a05 STANDS AT: 29 logical kinds, 58 wire types, 19 of 20 unions, 59 of 60 arms, 10 of 720 fields.

WHAT I COULD NOT LAND, AND WHY IT IS NOT a05's FAULT. I derived, emitted, spliced and pin-cleared a
37-row StrongRef field tranche — every row with a resolvable target, the DAG satisfied, no
self-edge, tags from SOURCE column order, four pins re-frozen from the loader's own drift, and the
frozen-history witness extended. It is staged at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p3a05c and it is NOT landed,
because `appendix-regenerate` verifies its inputs before writing and refuses while the

fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx and fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8, neither carrying
