title: Appendix A exact catalog: W12 retention, compaction, reconfiguration, GC, and topology formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for W12 retention, compaction, reconfiguration, GC, and topology formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1791-1889 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:


The autocommit-write arm byte-matches the preparation retained by `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord` and is legal only for committed WriteReturning. Its `AtomicProtocolDetach` publication creates `ResultDeliveryOwner::AutocommitWriteTerminal`, charge transfer/Protocol escrow, a PendingVisibility, ReleasedAwaitingActivation, or legal inline ActiveDeliverable record/index leaf, and only `{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` in the semantic frontier. Independent Protocol retention—not activation or client ACK—is the result postcondition. Matching retry returns the same applied record and owner commitments; a different bitmap, participant set, frontier, public bundle, result arm, or predecessor fails. ReadYourWritesCapability and ordinary terminal success remain unavailable until TerminalReady and its exact audit release; output bytes remain unavailable until the result owner is ActiveDeliverable. No prose “mirror” is sufficient evidence.

Attempt-history compaction is cumulative and has three separately ordered phases; deterministic apply never manufactures a quorum signature. `AttemptLookupKey` is the closed tag `ByAttempt{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,global_txn_id,registration_generation}|ByOutcomeCapability{capability_domain_commitment,scoped_token_digest}`. `PublicNeverRegisteredOutcome` is the frozen `{posture,public_reason:PublicReasonProjection,original_response_commitment}` copied from `NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle`. `TerminalAttemptSummaryLeaf` is `NeverRegistered{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,internal_reason_class,public_outcome:PublicNeverRegisteredOutcome,audit_terminal_commitment,internal_staging_generation,internal_terminal_global_prefix}|Terminal{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,attempt_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByAttempt,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,operation_class,internal_terminal_global_prefix,public_outcome:TerminalPublicOutcome,audit_terminal_commitment}`. The summary retains protected frozen response bytes and therefore must retain the full binding; the later expiry rewrite alone may replace it in lookup indexes with a payload-free `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Meta>` tombstone. A NeverRegistered leaf has no optional or synthetic attempt identity: absence of registration is part of the tag's meaning. Both public outcomes are copied byte-for-byte from their detailed bundles and include the original response commitment; neither leaf has a retaining edge to audit detail. Internal reason/generation/prefix fields are never serialized by the public status projector. `TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot` is a canonical authenticated persistent map from keyed lookup hashes to leaves plus `{summary_generation,covered_closed_prefix,leaf_count,root_digest}`. Its membership proof is consumed server-side after exact capability validation; the client receives only the frozen public projection plus a blinded proof projection, never the full leaf/path containing attempt keys, prefixes, or authority bindings. A successor root must equal the prior root plus the command's sorted insertions, proven by `PersistentMapExtensionProof`; it may structurally share map nodes but contains no `StrongRef` to a predecessor summary root, audit detail, or heavy attempt evidence, and an existing key can only be an identical idempotent leaf.

`NeverRegisteredEvidence` is `{begin_reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,terminal_record_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredTerminalRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,outcome_capability_key:AttemptLookupKey::ByOutcomeCapability,staging_generation,authenticated_detailed_value_proofs:{global_begin_idempotency_index:NeverRegisteredDetailed,global_outcome_directory:NeverRegisteredDetailed},no_reservation_binding_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoReservationBindingProof>,audit_terminal_commitment,absence_of_exported_registration_or_shard_import_commitment}`. `NoReservationBindingProof` is generated from the current begin-index terminal leaf, the reservation-key uniqueness proof, the Meta prepared/certificate/export roots, and the registered inverse-reference index for reservation identities; it proves that this reservation was never consumed by registration or exported, without inventing an attempt/family key. `NeverRegisteredFloorSpec` is `{basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,basis_begin_index_digest,basis_outcome_directory_digest,basis_prepared_root_digest,basis_certificate_ledger_digest,basis_reservation_inverse_index_digest,sorted_evidence_refs[StrongRef<NeverRegisteredEvidence>],expected_prior_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,candidate_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,extension_proof_ref:StrongRef<PersistentMapExtensionProof>,exact_detailed_to_compacted_begin_and_directory_rewrite_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply revalidates every detailed value and nonbinding proof against current roots, inserts the exact never-registered summary leaves, atomically changes begin-index and outcome-directory entries from Detailed to Compacted while preserving their same replay ref, and creates compact `NeverRegisteredFloorRecord {assigned_global_logical_command_seq,source_command_digest:WeakDigest,rewritten_lookup_key_commitment,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,applied_global_prefix}` with no retaining edge to its command/spec/evidence. It creates, burns, or rewrites no attempt/family/conflict entry and can never change the previously returned reason or response bytes.

`GlobalOutcomeExpirySpec` is a separate ordered control `{capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,expected_begin_index_entry:BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredCompacted,expected_outcome_directory_entry:CompactedTerminal|NeverRegisteredCompacted,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,expected_verifier_key_and_profile_floors,expected_begin_retry_and_lookup_floors,expected_retention_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedHistoryCut>,permanent_begin_tombstone_body,permanent_outcome_tombstone_body,terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<MetaControl>,terminal_audit_gate}`. The evidence must classify the replay object's exact window `Expired` for this action, the two compact leaves and replay identity must agree, and every promised retry/lookup floor must be closed. Apply atomically changes both leaves to `ExpiredTombstone` values containing the same scoped-key/token/capability commitments and expiry-evidence digest, drops the replay edge only in that transition, and permanently prevents key/token reuse. A valid old capability thereafter returns `TokenExpired`; an invalid or unauthorized input remains `NotVisibleOrUnknown`. Expiry does not remove the internal terminal summary leaf or fabricate an attempt identity.

`AttemptDeltaCompletionEvidence` is `Committed{global_delta_batch_ref:StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>,global_delta_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,published_frontier_at_or_beyond_commit_proof_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDeltaFrontierProof>}|NoDeltaApplicable{terminal_kind:Aborted|ReadClosed,proof_digest}`. `AttemptCompactionEvidenceRef` is the exact closed union `MetaDecision{record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>}|MetaConstraintRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<ConstraintReleaseRecord>}|MetaAuditTerminal{visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,audit_outcome_identity_and_commitment:WeakDigest}|MetaResultDisposition{disposition:ResultDispositionRef}|MetaWorkspaceRelease{evidence:WorkspaceReleaseEvidenceRef}|MetaBackupRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<BackupReleaseRecord>}|MetaReplayRetention{record_ref:StrongRef<ReplayRetentionRecord>}|MetaRemoteRelease{record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>}|ShardPostVisibility{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>}|ShardConstraintRelease{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardConstraintReleaseAck>}|ShardWorkspaceRelease{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardWorkspaceReleaseAck>}`. `IndependentAttemptObligationRef` is `Result{retention_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord>}|Backup{retention_ref:StrongRef<BackupIndependentRetentionRecord>}|Replay{retention_ref:StrongRef<ReplayRetentionRecord>}|RemoteGrant{grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}|CapabilityFloor{floor_ref:StrongRef<CapabilityLookupFloor>}`. `ClosedAttemptEvidenceBundle` is the heavy pre-order closure `{sorted_terminal_ready_outcome_refs[StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>],begin_idempotency_and_public_status_proof_refs[StrongRef<BeginPublicStatusProof>],sorted_evidence_refs[AttemptCompactionEvidenceRef],sorted_delta_completion_evidence[AttemptDeltaCompletionEvidence],statement_terminal_summary_proof_refs[StrongRef<StatementTerminalSummaryProof>],result_delivery_disposition_proof_refs[StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>],workspace_generation_and_local_overlay_release_proof_refs[StrongRef<WorkspaceReleaseProof>],workspace_remote_grant_release_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardWorkspaceReleaseAck>],overlap_close_proof_refs[StrongRef<ConflictOverlapCloseProof>],complete_selected_attempt_and_public_outcome_commitment}`. `ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec` is `{compaction_id,basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,basis_attempt_index_digest,basis_begin_index_digest,basis_outcome_directory_digest,basis_conflict_index_digest,basis_authoritative_floor_digest,basis_pending_root_digest,selected_terminal_attempt_keys[],evidence_bundle_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptEvidenceBundle>,expected_prior_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,candidate_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,extension_proof_ref:StrongRef<PersistentMapExtensionProof>,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_refs[IndependentAttemptObligationRef],terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies every selected attempt is `TerminalReady` and audit-visible and that its candidate leaf exactly reproduces the detailed `TerminalPublicOutcome`; decision/certificate publication, every admitted shard post-visibility acknowledgement, committed Global-delta publication/frontier, and applicable abort/read-close no-delta proof must be complete. Every statement is `Published|Failed|Abandoned`; every statement output is NoResult/NotApplicableTerminal or, together with every terminal/autocommit result, Acknowledged, ReleasedUnacked, or independently retained; every workspace overlay and remote grant has exact release evidence or a listed independent owner; overlap is closed; and no untransferred backup/replay/retention/capability obligation remains. Apply creates unsigned compact `ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord {compaction_id,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,source_command_digest:WeakDigest,through_global_prefix,terminal_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,selected_attempt_commitment,selected_public_outcome_commitment,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,meta_checkpoint_identity:WeakDigest}` with no retaining edge to the command/spec/evidence and inserts it into `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot {generation,entries[compaction_id->StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord>],nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`. Build does **not** advance the authoritative floor, rewrite detailed indexes, or release heavy evidence. Generated plane-negative fixtures reject both former `StrongRef<AuditOutcomeRecord>` back-edges.

Only after the compact record and its audit visibility advance are durable does the Meta quorum create `AttemptCompactionAttestation {SameGroupCertificateHeader,compaction_id,floor_record_identity:WeakDigest,build_control_identity:WeakGlobalCommandIdentity,build_resulting_root_identity:WeakDigest,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,selected_attempt_commitment,selected_public_outcome_commitment,through_global_prefix,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref:StrongRef<CertificateSignerLock>,quorum_signatures}`. It has no strong edge to the compact record, build command/root, prior floor, spec, or heavy evidence; the certificate is the exact portable release proof, not a semantic command identity. The certificate ledger temporarily retains the build closure until publication. `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec` is `{floor_record_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord>,attestation_ref:StrongRef<AttemptCompactionAttestation>,expected_pending_entry_digest,expected_prior_authoritative_floor:WeakDigest,expected_summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,exact_selected_attempt_index_rewrite_commitment,exact_selected_outcome_directory_rewrite_commitment,exact_overlap_closed_conflict_rewrite_commitment,exact_begin_status_result_workspace_remote_grant_and_statement_closure_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply revalidates monotonic extension, removes exactly that pending entry, replaces selected detailed family/attempt/outcome entries with `CompactedTerminal{capability_replay_ref,summary_root_ref,leaf_key_digest,public_outcome,lookup_floor}`, removes only proved overlap-closed conflict detail, and leaves every independently retained result/workspace grant/backup/replay/capability object rooted by its own typed lease or floor. The installed public outcome must byte-match the authenticated leaf and the pre-compaction detailed response. It installs `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor {summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,closed_through_global_prefix,retained_active_attempt_commitment,still_live_independent_obligation_commitment,last_update:Genesis|NeverRegistered{applied_prefix,record_identity:WeakDigest}|Closed{attestation_ref:StrongRef<AttemptCompactionAttestation>}}`. This floor has no strong/CRSR path to the previous floor, the build record, spec, or heavy evidence. Fresh Meta Genesis and Local activation both create the canonical empty `TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot`, empty `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot`, and `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor{closed_through=0,last_update=Genesis}`; therefore the first extension has a real prior root. `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorInstallSpec` is the closed tag `InstallNeverRegistered{spec_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredFloorSpec>}|BuildClosed{spec_ref:StrongRef<ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec>}|PublishClosed{spec_ref:StrongRef<GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec>}`. Heavy evidence becomes reclaimable only after `PublishClosed`, its audit visibility advance, and an activated checkpoint cut covering the publish/build command and certificate-ledger transfer, subject to every independent live floor. Neither phase decides, aborts, or times out prepared work. Status tests race build, audit visibility advance, attestation, publish, expiry, and post-cut detail reclamation and require identical validated-capability response bytes, service epoch, and privacy shape before expiry and the exact privacy-collapsed expiry response afterward.

`MetaConfigurationTransitionSpec` is `{phase:ProposeJoint|CommitJoint|CommitNew|CommitRetirementFloor,basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,prospective_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,candidate_closure_proof_ref:StrongRef,expected_global_prefix,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,resulting_topology_body_digest,paired_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>?,paired_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor>,required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>,prepared_ownership_transfer_refs[StrongRef<MetaPreparedOwnershipTransferRecord>],terminal_audit_gate}`. Deterministic apply constructs a `TopologyState` successor with identical epoch, form, shard assignments, and routing but the phase-appropriate current/joint/new `meta_configuration_ref` plus this applied control; no topology object may retain the retired Meta configuration as current. Every phase is separate, and `CommitRetirementFloor` proves the new set owns all Meta prepared, certificate, and certified-remote obligations. The sole transfer format is the role-specialized `PreparedOwnershipTransferRecord<Meta>` defined above; no later generic or cross-role encoding exists. A current Meta prepared root may carry a prior-configuration entry only in that exact transfer state, and old ownership releases only after new ownership plus Raft/snapshot/apply/GC acknowledgement.

Shard membership is Meta-authorized and later Meta-adopted. `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationSpec` is `{shard_id,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,old_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_meta_remote_trust_generation,expected_meta_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,joint_and_final_canonical_configuration_bytes_and_digests,transition_nonce,payload_predicates,required_checkpoint_floor_remote_prepared_certificate_obligations,successor_evidence_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`; its applied `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationRecord` fixes the one permitted transition and current trust selector. Each `ShardConfigurationTransitionSpec` consumes the certified record and transfers every old-configuration owner. After `CommitRetirementFloor`, old and new quorums create `ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,authorization_identity,old/joint/new configuration identities,final_floor,through_shard_index/global_prefix,remote_obligation_commitment,predecessor_remote_configuration_evidence_identity,old_and_new_quorum_signatures,one_digest_signer_lock_ref}`. The successor `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence::Successor` is authenticated from the currently trusted predecessor and both quorums; new members alone cannot bootstrap it.

`RemoteGrantRetirementPlan` is the Meta-local pre-order object `{plan_id,basis_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,basis_remote_trust_generation,retired_authority_domain,retired_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,sorted_entries[{old_grant_id,old_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,target_identity,consumer_domain,target_closure_commitment,disposition:ReplaceWithSuccessorGrant{successor_grant_body_recipe,required_consumer_adoption_predicate}|Release{release_request_body_recipe},required_six_stage_transition:RequestConsumerRelease->PublishConsumerReleaseEvidence->ApplyAuthorityRelease->PublishAuthorityReleaseAck->ConsumeReleaseAck->Acknowledged,completion_predicate}],complete_old_grant_set_and_target_coverage_digest,expected_consumer_root_digest,completion_floor_body_recipe}`. It names no future request, tombstone, ack, applied record, or result; adoption verifies the exhaustive old-grant set before selecting it. `ShardConfigurationAdoptionSpec` is Meta input `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,adoption_evidence_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_old_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_remote_trust_generation,expected_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,expected_successor_evidence_digest,old_grant_retirement_plan_ref:StrongRef<RemoteGrantRetirementPlan>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies the direct trust transition and atomically CASes both the topology shard entry and `RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot` selector/generation; neither may advance alone. Only then may the six-stage handshake release old-configuration grants and membership. Stale trust generation, anchor, topology, old/new signature domain, or successor bytes reject with no partial adoption.

Distributed GC separates preflight, semantic authorization/quarantine, physical completion, and aggregate completion. A stage-4 certificate is not release completion. `PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection` is the reference-free `{authority_domain,configuration_oid,configuration_digest,canonical_configuration_bytes,payload_predicate_digest,trust_transition_proof_bytes,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence` is `{authority_domain,consumer_domain,grant_id,target_identity,release_nonce,ack_leaf_bytes_and_identity,authority_configuration_evidence:PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection,summary_entry_key,summary_inclusion_proof,permanent_release_proof_floor,authority_signatures}` and contains no CRSR, new retention grant, or cross-group strong edge. `GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef` is the closed role-checked union `AuthorityPublished{publish_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionAckPublishRecord>,summary_entry_ref:StrongRef<RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>}|ConsumerAcknowledged{consume_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumeAckRecord>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,current_no_old_grant_ref_proof_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionNoOldGrantProof>}|ImportedPermanent{evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence>}`. The candidate's ownership/consumer role selects the one legal arm; every arm proves stage 5 or stage 6 plus the permanent summary floor. A request, stage-4 certificate, tombstone, plan, unsigned identity, or a newly granted CRSR cannot inhabit it. A shard first orders `ShardGcPreflightSpec {basis_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_shard_raft_index,basis_global_prefix,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_epoch,complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>,candidate_derivation_profile,excluded_obligation_commitment}`. Apply creates `ShardGcPreflightRecord {source_spec_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightSpec>,basis identities,generated current/cut/prepared/certificate/lease/key/derived/backup/replay/restore/remote inventories,exact_candidate_local_reclaim_set,excluded_obligations,candidate_set_digest}`; only afterward does the quorum create `ShardGcPreflightEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,candidate_set_digest,root_inventory_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. Meta likewise builds `MetaGcPreflightRecord` for its local physical universe before ordering `GlobalGcAuthorizationSpec {basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,exact_meta_candidate_set,sorted_shard_preflight_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardGcPreflightEvidence>],exact_per_shard_candidate_commitments,excluded_global_obligation_commitment,completed_remote_release_proof_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply creates `GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord` authorizing only those bounded sets; a planned remote release is not completion, and an active/ReleaseRequested grant target is never a reclaim candidate.

Each participant next orders a role-specific **Semantic quarantine** command. `GcMemberOperationPlan` is the exact `{generation,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,storage_member_id,storage_profile_oid,target_inventory_digest,canonical_action_body_recipe_and_digest}`. `GcOperationFamily` is `{family_id,base_target_set_commitment,base_generation_zero_plan_set_commitment,successor_operation_id_recipe,max_generations,body_digest}`. `ShardGcApplySpec` is `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_epoch,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_local_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest}`. `MetaGcApplyQuarantineSpec` is the exact Meta-local `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_meta_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest,terminal_audit_gate}`. Followers recompute from the **current** Semantic state, both RootSlots, Protocol/Prepared/Consensus state, and the candidate result. They require `reclaim_set ⊆ authorized_set ∩ preflight_set`, disjointness from the current reachable set, and exact family/base-plan coverage; “unchanged or stronger” is not a relation. Apply creates the role-specific reclaim-authorization record and `GcSemanticState::Quarantined` only. Every object encoder, dedupe lookup, prepared receipt, command validator, and root publisher rejects a new retaining edge or realization selection to a quarantined identity. A registration racing the cutover basis is either included/terminalized under the old epoch or rejected for later retry. `TopologyRetirementFloor` is `{cutover_record_ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransitionRecord>,through_global_prefix,old_owner_inventory,remaining_certified_remote_obligations,backup_floor,key_floor,retention_floor,prepare_floor,external_backup_and_key_receipt_refs[StrongRef],required_meta_ack_set,required_shard_ack_set}`. `TopologyRetirementAck` carries `SameGroupCertificateHeader` and `{floor_ref:LocalMeta{StrongRef<TopologyRetirementFloor>}|RemoteMeta{CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<TopologyRetirementFloor>},satisfied_floor_digest,signature}`; only meta encodes `LocalMeta`, and every shard encodes `RemoteMeta`.

Movement has three distinct pre-order global-control specs so apply never consumes ambient evidence. `TopologyCopyBeginSpec` is `{move_id,old_topology_ref,new_joint_topology_ref,new_final_topology_ref,affected_ranges,copy_basis_global_prefix,old/new_shard_configuration_refs[RemoteConfigurationRef],source_checkpoint_certificate_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardCheckpointCertificate>],transfer_plan_ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransferPlan>,expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs,terminal_audit_gate}`. `TopologyCutoverSpec` is `{move_id,copy_record_ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransitionRecord>,cutover_global_prefix,sorted_transfer_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<TopologyTransferAck>],new_owner_catchup_certificate_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardCheckpointCertificate>],active_attempt_closure_proof_ref:StrongRef<TopologyAttemptClosureProof>,old/new_shard_configuration_refs[RemoteConfigurationRef],expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs,terminal_audit_gate}` and proves every old-epoch registration has exhaustive Terminal or `AbortForPostCutoverRetry` evidence before ownership switches at the next prefix. `TopologyRetireOldSpec` is `{move_id,cutover_record_ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransitionRecord>,topology_retirement_floor_ref:StrongRef<TopologyRetirementFloor>,sorted_meta_ack_refs[StrongRef<TopologyRetirementAck>],sorted_shard_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<TopologyRetirementAck>],terminal_audit_gate}`. Each apply constructs one `TopologyTransitionRecord {move_id,phase:CopyInProgress|CutoverCommitted|OldOwnersRetired,command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,phase_predecessor:NoneForCopy|Copy{ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransitionRecord>}|Cutover{ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransitionRecord>},copy_basis_global_prefix,cutover_global_prefix?,affected_ranges,evidence_commitment,resulting_topology_ref,assigned_global_logical_command_seq}`. The predecessor is the immediately prior same-move phase; completed moves do not form an unbounded strong chain. Source bytes/keys remain live through final retirement and its two-sided remote floors.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

title: A08 gated residue: lifecycle source-shape and construction-DAG closure
description:
## Scope

Finish the W12 lifecycle catalog only after the remaining source-shape and
construction-DAG gates are discharged. The forced tranche is carried by
`fgdb-a08-w12-lifecycle-pr7j`; do not recreate its 17 reservation-backed kinds,
3 unions/13 arms, 107 fields, or 140 targets.

## Exact measured residue

Measured from the a08 Appendix census (111 top-level, 1,112 field, 42 union,
142 arm candidates) after subtracting the landed forced tranche:

- 56 top-level candidates remain unclassified: 38 source-confirmed bodies,
  13 ambiguous bodies, and 5 name-only occurrences. The first 51 require a
  top-level identity-class ruling; the 5 name-only occurrences lack an exact
  durable body, so a class label alone cannot mint them.
- 22 unions and 74 arms remain on 19 of those unminted hosts. An ordinary
  union cannot land before its containing schema has one registered identity.
- 1,005 field candidates remain. Of these, 714 are source-shape gated exactly:
  1 conflicting type, 608 with no exact type occurrence, 19 ambiguous, 61
  inline-union/array shapes without a settled field representation, and 25
  exact types that resolve nowhere.
- The remaining 291 dependency-shaped fields include 10
  `dag_future_result` edges, 7 `dag_self_edge` predecessors, the exact 2-edge
  `dag_cycle`
  `AuditTerminalFreezeRecord.typed_no_terminal_proof_ref ->
  NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof ->
  AuditTerminalFreezeRecord.freeze_ref`, and 19 `ref_target_unresolved`
  references. The other 253 require their containing kind, ordinary/reference
  union, or named reference target to be registered first.

## Blocking laws

- A fresh logical code is legal only above the live `0x051d` high-water, only
  when no reservation exists, and only after checking that the symbol is not
  already a wire type. A reservation-backed symbol must use its reservation.
- `dag_future_result` is non-strict in order equality and fires only when
  `target.construction_order > containing.construction_order`; the 10 held
  rows were synthesized and actually fired that code. Equal-order controls
  passed.
- `dag_self_edge` rejects a retaining self-reference at every order. A lineage
  predecessor needs a source-backed nonretaining digest/adjacency
  representation; changing it is not a catalog guess.
- `dag_cycle` rejects the two retaining freeze/proof edges as one SCC. At
  least one source reference must become nonretaining or otherwise change
  before either row can land.
- `ref_target_unresolved` rejects a reference whose named target has no
  registered logical identity.
- A field row must use its containing kind's exact `construction_order`.
  Non-reference fields use `identity_class = "inline"`; reference fields use
  the settled logical/physical field class appropriate to the target.

## Control evidence

Every blocked reference was synthesized alongside the same known-boring
`StrongRef<ConfigurationState>` control. The control passed while the subject
produced the named violation. The 92 landed direct references were also
validated together as one cycle-free cohort; adding both held freeze/proof
edges produced the exact SCC above.

Dependencies: the top-level class/source-shape decision tracked by
`fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd`, and the latent source-DAG
closure tracked by `fgdb-owlp`.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Strata run, identity continuity, allocator, and lease formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Strata run, identity continuity, allocator, and lease formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1890-1909 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**AdjRunSegment**: `{ graph, branch_projection, source_partition, direction, edge_type, source_ordinal_map_id, destination_map_table[{partition,ordinal_map_id}], source_ordinal_range, edge_count, seq_range, codec_table, offsets_ef, encoded_neighbor_lists, stable_eids, origin_birth_orders, branch_admission_orders?, marker_aware_retire_or_hole_data, property_locators, canonical_stable_id_digest, checksum }`. Each destination carries either stable VId or a destination-map-table slot plus ordinal. Mutable labels do not identify a primary run; per-list codec governs legal rank/select/skip operations. The `stable_eids` and `origin_birth_orders` columns are stored under the registered identity-column codec of §6.2/§6.3 — order-preserving run-header prefix dictionary plus delta/FOR-coded slot suffix — named in `codec_table` and covered by `canonical_stable_id_digest` over the decoded stable IDs.

**IdentityContinuityRecord / IdAllocatorState / IdRangeLease**: `IdentityContinuityRecord` binds `{database_security_namespace_id,allocation_epoch,predecessor_digest,external_registry_id,cas_version,status,issued_at,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`; its external registry/witness copy is the anti-rollback authority and its Chronicle copy is checked against it under `AllocationContinuityProfile::ExternalCas`, the only arm in which this record exists. Under `AllocationContinuityProfile::DirectoryBound` — bound 1:1 to the slot's `IncarnationContinuityProfile` — there is no external record: the fenced local allocation-continuity journal record, ordered under the whole-inode fence with the fixed local continuity digest exactly as the incarnation record registers for that profile, is the continuity basis, and the registered Appendix F residual-risk row scopes block-level/volume-snapshot rollback outside that posture's declared threat model, allocation included; W12, Meta, and Sharded postures require `ExternalCas`. Allocator state binds `{graph_id,element_kind,allocation_epoch,identity_continuity_record_ref,topology_epoch,per_partition_high_water,spent_range_commitments,exhausted_partitions}`. Pre-order `IdRangeGrantSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` binds the requested range, allocator basis, `authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>`, and issuance profile/window. `IdRangeLease<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,lease_id,graph,element_kind,allocation_epoch,partition,half_open_range,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,time_authority_profile_oid,issuance_not_before,issuance_not_after,permanent_spent_commitment,body_digest}`; its authenticated transcript covers the complete authority binding and profiled window. `ShardIdRangeLease` is the distinct shard-owned `{authority_projection:ShardAuthorityBindingProjection,meta_grant_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaIdRangeGrantCertificate>,shard_id,lease_id,graph,element_kind,allocation_epoch,partition,half_open_range,shard_install_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef::Shard,time_authority_profile_oid,issuance_not_before,issuance_not_after,permanent_spent_commitment,body_digest}`. The applied tag must match the owning Local/Meta/Shard state machine and assigned position; role substitution or a digest-only authority projection is unencodable. Use consumes fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`; expiry ends issuance authority only through matching `Expired` evidence and every epoch/range pair remains permanently spent and can never overlap or recycle.

An identity becomes externally stable at its **first escape**, not at transaction commit. `AllocationValueKind` is the closed union `VertexId{graph,partition}|EdgeId{graph,partition}|GeneratedKey{graph,generator_id,key_type}`. `TxnAllocationSlotKey` is `{posture:Local|Sharded,attempt_identity,statement_seq_or_terminal,tmp_ref_ordinal,value_kind}` and is never a client value. `EscapingAllocationCause` is `PublishedStatementResult|LaterStatementWorkspace|ProcedureOrUdfBoundary|DurableProvenanceOrAudit|TerminalResultPreparation`; the `TerminalResultPreparation` arm is optional because a terminal-only value may instead be assigned in finalization before publication. `EscapingAllocationBinding` is `{slot_key,permanent_value,lease_ref:Local{lease_ref:StrongRef<IdRangeLease>}|Shard{lease_ref:StrongRef<ShardIdRangeLease>},lease_offset,escape_cause,first_escaping_statement_seq,canonical_binding_digest}`. The permanent value must equal the role/kind/epoch/partition/offset encoded by its lease; generated-key encoders additionally obey the registered generator profile. A binding is immutable, namespace-scoped, and cannot be repurposed for a different temporary reference, attempt, kind, or create.

Local orders `LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec {registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,expected_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,expected_allocator_root:WeakStateIdentity,sorted_binding_recipes[],sorted_lease_refs[StrongRef<IdRangeLease>],fresh_lease_use_evidence_refs[StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>],expected_unconsumed_offsets_and_spent_commitment,resulting_allocation_binding_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnAllocationBindingRoot>,resulting_workspace_generation_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}` before the first escaping manifest/workspace/procedure object is constructed. Apply checks a canonical bijection between recipes and fresh offsets, marks every offset consumed in `IdAllocatorState`, installs `EscapingAllocationReservationRecord {source_spec_ref,applied_control_ref,registration_ref,sorted_bindings,resulting_binding_root_ref,permanent_spent_commitment}`, and advances the workspace generation atomically. The statement publication or later terminal preparation names that record and can encode only its permanent values. A lost response retries the same record and result bytes.

In Sharded posture, the shard owning each disjoint range first orders `ShardEscapingAllocationReserveSpec {registration_projection_ref,workspace_generation,lease_ref:StrongRef<ShardIdRangeLease>,sorted_binding_recipes_for_this_shard,fresh_lease_use_evidence_ref,expected_shard_allocator_root,resulting_shard_binding_root_ref}` and installs both the consumed-offset state and `ShardEscapingAllocationReservationRecord` in one shard command. Its quorum exports `ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,reservation_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardEscapingAllocationReservationRecord>,workspace_generation,sorted_bindings,permanent_spent_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. Meta then orders `GlobalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec {registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>,expected_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,sorted_shard_evidence_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence>],complete_tmp_ref_to_permanent_value_bijection,resulting_global_binding_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnAllocationBindingRoot>,successor_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply rejects a missing, duplicate, overlapping, foreign-range, wrong-workspace, or nonparticipant binding and makes the global workspace's mapping authoritative. Shard holds remain independently rooted until Meta publication and the ordinary two-sided retention release; a Meta failure cannot make a certified slot reusable.

`TxnAllocationBindingRoot` maps every escaped `TxnAllocationSlotKey` to exactly one binding and carries `{generation,attempt_identity,through_statement_seq,sorted_spent_commitments,root_digest}`. Rebase and finalization must preserve all existing leaves and may append only new escapes; if the logical create disappears, conflicts with a constraint, or changes kind/partition, the attempt aborts or records `AbandonedAllocationTombstone {binding_digest,attempt_terminal_identity,reason_class,permanent_spent_commitment}`. Abort, no-op, statement failure after reservation, lease expiry, compaction, branch fork/merge, topology movement, backup/restore, and same-identity recovery retain the spend through the allocator's cumulative spent commitment even after detailed binding evidence is cut. `AllocationBindingCompactionSpec` may replace closed-attempt detail only with a checked cumulative spent-range extension and exact tombstone commitment; it never returns capacity. Tests force crash/lost response before and after every Local, shard, and Meta publication; expose an ID to a later statement and force rebase; abort after exposure; retry under a new process; expire a lease; restore an old backup; move a partition; and prove that the visible value is stable and no offset is ever issued twice.

Confined temporary references also require durable allocation **before** their permanent values enter a capsule or shard effect basis; “assign in commit order” is not an ambient counter operation. `FinalizationAllocationPlan<Role>` is the sequence-neutral pre-order object `{role,registration_identity,admission_generation,finalization_generation,expected_allocation_binding_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnAllocationBindingRoot>,allocator_basis:WeakStateIdentity,topology_and_owner_basis,sorted_mappings[{slot_key,value_kind,permanent_value,lease_ref,lease_offset,source_intent_ordinal}],sorted_lease_use_evidence_refs[StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>],exact_before_lease_cursor_and_high_water_values,exact_after_lease_cursor_and_high_water_values,permanent_spent_extension_commitment,complete_confined_tmp_ref_bijection,exhaustion_and_checked_overflow_proof,body_digest}`. It excludes every previously escaped slot, has no future command/result/root, and must map every and only remaining create/generated-key reference in the normalized effect set.

Local `LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` names that plan, and its apply atomically updates `IdAllocatorState`, installs `FinalizationAllocationReservationRecord<Local> {plan_ref,registration_identity,finalization_generation,sorted_mappings,permanent_spent_extension_commitment,applied_control_ref,state:Active}`, and installs the Active final-certification/constraint/resource/escrow holds. Only afterward are final effects, terminal result preparation, capsule, and terminal audit bytes constructed, and each strongly names the reservation record. Commit atomically replaces it with `Consumed{terminal_input_identity,marker_identity}`. Cancel or abort replaces it with `AbandonedSpent{terminal_or_cancel_identity,tombstone_summary_ref}`; because durable plan/effect candidates may already name the values, capacity is never returned.

In Sharded posture, each allocation-owner shard orders `ShardFinalizationAllocationReserveSpec` before constructing `ShardEffectBasis`, consumes exact offsets in its authoritative leased-range ledger, and exports `ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,reservation_record_ref:StrongRef<FinalizationAllocationReservationRecord<Shard>>,sorted_mappings,permanent_spent_extension_commitment,topology_and_configuration_basis,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. The effect basis and routing certificate bind the exact certified evidence. `GlobalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` requires a canonical bijection over all such evidence and every remaining temporary reference, holds those reservations, and cannot remap them. Global commit/abort disposition is projected back to every shard; participant loss retains the spent reservation until recovery applies that disposition. Meta never guesses a shard's next slot and a shard never uses an uncertified Meta mapping.

`FinalizationAllocationTombstoneSummary` is the compact cumulative `{role_and_owner,allocation_epoch,sorted_spent_ranges_or_offsets,attempt_and_finalization_generation,terminal_disposition_commitment,predecessor_summary_digest:WeakDigest,body_digest}`. Checkpoint, configuration, backup/restore, role transition, topology movement, prepared/final-certification, and GC inventories retain every Active reservation and cumulative consumed/abandoned spend. Tests race two candidates on the same allocator basis, crash before/after reservation/capsule/audit/order, cancel and abort, force rebase/partition movement, expire leases, restore an old allocator root, and exhaust every high-water counter; exactly one mapping wins, overflow fail-closes, and no permanent value is ever reused.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

## Provenance
Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 1890-1909.

A09 MINT PLAN — FOR REVIEW BEFORE ANY registries/** WRITE. Measured at HEAD a6cd40f in a `git archive HEAD` snapshot; catalog token NOT held (pane3-a03 has it). Every table below is probe-derived with controls; nothing is asserted from the slice prose alone.

=== 0. THE INVARIANT THAT SHAPES THE WHOLE PLAN (measured, not assumed) ===
Across all 813 reservations, `disposition = "existing"` <=> a projection row exists for that symbol. Exactly: existing&projected 88, existing&unprojected 0, reserved&projected 0, reserved&unprojected 725. Zero exceptions in either direction.
CONSEQUENCE: minting a projection row for an already-reserved family REQUIRES flipping its reservation disposition reserved -> existing IN THE SAME INCREMENT. Omitting that flip lands a row on the wrong side of a 813-row invariant.
Second, from appendix_a.rs:10618-10641, the class chain is: a symbol with NO checked-in projection row MUST stay identity_class="unclassified" (catalog_candidate_class_unproved); a symbol WITH one must carry exactly that class (catalog_candidate_class_mismatch); and a [[target]] must agree with the class implied by its target_kind (catalog_target_class_mismatch). So the projection row, the candidate flip and the target are ONE ATOMIC UNIT. This is precisely the failure that reverted pane3's 17/46/63 landing: targets whose symbols had no projection row can never resolve a class, no matter how exactly the counts reconcile.

=== 1. BASELINE: ALL 20 FAMILIES ARE UNMINTED ===
0 of 20 a09 census families have a projection row; all 20 sit at identity_class="unclassified"; a09 has 0 landed [[target]] rows (control: a01 has 227). Census: schemas=20 fields=162 unions=4 arms=12 ambiguities=148.
StrongRef/reservation correspondence is perfect and is the bijection holding: 6 families are StrongRef targets AND reserved; 14 are neither. No family is one without the other.

=== 2. STAGE 1 — THE SIX RESERVED LOGICAL KINDS (zero judgement; code and class are PRE-ASSIGNED) ===
Rule 1 of the five-class definition (plan:282) is mandatory, not discretionary: "All StrongRef<T>, Conditional*Ref<T>, and weak-digest target types MUST resolve to rows in this registry [logical_object_kinds]." All six are StrongRef targets, so their class is forced. Their reservation rows ALREADY carry row_kind="logical-kind", identity_class="logical" and an assigned code, so the mint does not choose a code — it consumes the reserved one.
  symbol                                code    class    inbound refs (measured)                                     outbound (a09->a09)
  IdRangeLease                          0x02d5  logical  2: EscapingAllocationBinding.lease_ref,                     none
                                                            LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec.sorted_lease_refs
  IdentityContinuityRecord              0x02d6  logical  1: GlobalStatePayload.identity_continuity_record_ref (CROSS-SLICE) none
  ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence       0x044d  logical  1: GlobalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec.sorted_shard_evidence_refs none
  ShardIdRangeLease                     0x0458  logical  2: EscapingAllocationBinding.lease_ref,                     none
                                                            ShardEscapingAllocationReserveSpec.lease_ref
  TxnAllocationBindingRoot              0x04b1  logical  3: FinalizationAllocationPlan.expected_allocation_binding_root_ref, none
                                                            GlobalEscaping…/LocalEscaping… resulting roots
  EscapingAllocationReservationRecord   0x04e1  logical  0 measured typed inbound                                    none
YOUR SIX CHECKS, per row, for all six:
 (1) ALREADY EXISTS AS A WIRE TYPE? NO — none of the six has any projection row in any of the five registries. Checked across wire/logical/physical/bootstrap/prebootstrap, not wire alone. This is the dbvf 0x001e lesson applied: "no reservation" and "does not exist" are different questions, and here I checked existence directly rather than inferring it.
 (2) RESERVATION DISPOSITION: all six ARE already reserved and MUST NOT get a new reservation row. The action is a disposition flip reserved -> existing at the SAME code. The 813=813 partition is untouched — no row added, no row removed. The mint-above-0x051d route DOES NOT APPLY to any of these six; their codes are 0x02d5..0x04e1, all BELOW the 0x051d high-water, and inventing fresh codes above it would orphan the reservations.
 (3) CANDIDATE identity_class FLIP: required for all six, unclassified -> "logical". Field order in the candidate block is row_id, slice_id, symbol, generic_signature, source_key, source_kind, identity_class, source_locations — match on the symbol…identity_class run, not a slice_id-anchored regex.
 (4) CONSTRUCTION ORDER, derived from BOTH directions: all six have zero measured outbound a09->a09 typed edges and are referenced BY the Stage-3 spec/binding families. That makes them a lower layer than every unminted spec, and it is derived from the referenced side as well as the referrer side. HONEST LIMIT: these edges come from typed field candidates only. The slice prose also describes relationships that are not typed fields — e.g. TxnAllocationBindingRoot "maps every escaped TxnAllocationSlotKey to exactly one binding", and EscapingAllocationReservationRecord names sorted_bindings and resulting_binding_root_ref. Those imply TxnAllocationBindingRoot -> EscapingAllocationBinding and EscapingAllocationReservationRecord -> TxnAllocationBindingRoot, neither of which appears as a typed edge. I will confirm each against the field rows at mint time rather than freeze an order that only the referrer side supports.
 (5) RESERVED->ACTIVE FLIP / COHORT CHECK: NOT APPLICABLE. No status flip is proposed for any of the six — these are new rows, not lifecycle changes to existing ones. The A01 incomplete-activation cohort 0x0012..=0x0026 is a WIRE range in a01; all six of these are LOGICAL codes in a09 and none is inside any cohort range. Checked explicitly rather than assumed, because this is exactly what forbade the dbvf flip.
 (6) ORDERING: these are kinds only. No union or arm is introduced in Stage 1.
ATOMIC UNIT PER ROW (four edits, all in one increment): [[logical_kind]] projection row at the reserved code + [[target]] with target_kind="logical-kind" + [[top_level_candidate]] identity_class flip to "logical" + [[reservation]] disposition flip to "existing".

=== 3. STAGE 2 — THE TWO TOP-LEVEL CLOSED UNIONS AND THEIR ARMS ===
Census-parsed, so no a02-style naming pathology here: AllocationValueKind arms {EdgeId, GeneratedKey, VertexId}; EscapingAllocationCause arms {DurableProvenanceOrAudit, LaterStatementWorkspace, ProcedureOrUdfBoundary, PublishedStatementResult, TerminalResultPreparation}. Two further unions are FIELD unions inside Stage-3 records and must not be lifted to top level: EscapingAllocationBinding.lease_ref {Local, Shard} and TxnAllocationSlotKey.posture {Local, Sharded}.
 (1) exist already? NO. (2) neither is a StrongRef target and NEITHER IS RESERVED, so NO RESERVATION MAY BE ADDED — adding one fires reference_source_reservation_orphan. Per class rule 5 these are wire_types, so any code comes from the wire space (existing wire high-water 0x003f, 62 rows), NOT from the 0x051d reservation high-water, which governs the reservation table rather than the wire code space. (3) candidate flip unclassified -> "wire". (5) no flips, no cohort interaction. (6) ordering is enforced here: union host row BEFORE its arms, and both AFTER Stage 1, because arms target schemas that Stage 1 mints.
NOT PROPOSED FOR THIS INCREMENT: the two field unions, which belong with their Stage-3 host records.

=== 4. STAGE 3 — THE REMAINING TWELVE, WHICH NEED A CLASS DECISION I AM NOT MAKING ALONE ===
AbandonedAllocationTombstone, AbandonedSpent, AdjRunSegment, EscapingAllocationBinding, FinalizationAllocationPlan, FinalizationAllocationTombstoneSummary, GlobalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec, IdRangeGrantSpec, LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec, ShardEscapingAllocationReserveSpec, ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence, TxnAllocationSlotKey.
None is a StrongRef target, so rule 1 does NOT force them to logical, and the class is a genuine judgement between class 1 ("commands/specs/records … represented here ONLY WHEN they are independently addressable logical objects") and class 5 (inline records and union hosts). Two are clearly inline (TxnAllocationSlotKey, which the source says "is never a client value"; AbandonedSpent, a state arm). AdjRunSegment is the hardest: class 1 lists "runs" but only when independently addressable, while class 2 covers physical realizations — and it is the one family in the slice with its own checksum and canonical_stable_id_digest. comments.text:
HANDBACK (pane2). Landed 8804045 at base d8f99e1. a09: 0/162 field candidates -> 27/162; 2/148 adjudications -> 27/148; top-level targets unchanged at 35.

LANDED: complete field tables for the three fully self-contained families, each as [[field]] + [[target]] + field-type-ambiguous [[ambiguity_adjudication]] (one atomic unit — 79/79 landed ambiguous field targets appendix-wide carry an adjudication):
  IdentityContinuityRecord 9, IdRangeLease<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> 13, TxnAllocationBindingRoot 5.
Reusable driver preserved at ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/a09-field-increment/ (apply.sh, converge.py, gen_a09_*.py, gates.sh, probe, a09_census.txt). apply.sh is BASE-INDEPENDENT: it re-renders from generators and converge.py parses every new pin out of the loader's own drift text. HEAD moved 4x during this increment and it re-derived clean each time. Point it at any fresh `git archive HEAD` tree.

=== LAW 1, NOT PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN DOWN: A [[field]] ROW MAY NOT HANG OFF A WIRE-ONLY SCHEMA ===
identity.rs resolves `containing_schema` against logical|bootstrap|physical|prebootstrap ONLY — wire_names is NOT in the `resolves` disjunction — so a wire-hosted field fires field_unresolved_schema. Exceptionless appendix-wide: 1273 wire-owner field candidates, 0 landed field targets; 453 logical + 48 bootstrap, 0 wire. Unions are the opposite: 113 of 334 have wire containing_schemas, which is why the wire-hosted RECORDS look landable and are not.
CONSEQUENCE FOR a09, and it is permanent until the epic revisits it: AllocationValueKind (7 fields), EscapingAllocationBinding (9), TxnAllocationSlotKey (5) = 21 of the 162 candidates CANNOT take field rows while their hosts are wire types. Do not attempt them; the fix is a class decision at the epic, not a mint here.
Probe reconciliation that proves the predicate: per-slice logical+bootstrap LANDED must SUM to the catalog's field| target count (410+48 = 458 = 458).

=== LAW 2: THE FIELD identity_class VOCABULARY IS FIVE, NOT THREE — OWNER_RULINGS IS STALE ===
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/OWNER_RULINGS.md still says a field admits only logical|physical|inline, and broadens it to "every non-reference field takes inline". Both are SUPERSEDED at HEAD by commit 722ff22, whose own comment states the admitted set is scalar|inline|logical|physical|bootstrap_local and that narrowing it "would reject 124 landed rows (95 scalar, 29 bootstrap_local)". Reported as a measurement, per the standing instruction. Corpus is then decisive and exceptionless:
  strong|conditional|external_root -> identity_class MUST be "logical" (checker-forced, 233/233)
  primitive wire type (u8/u16/u32/u64/bytes/digest256/id256/oid256) -> "scalar"
  record-shaped wire type (AuthorityBoundHeader, AppliedControlRef, ...) -> "inline"
Do not apply the OWNER_RULINGS "inline everywhere" line to primitives; it lands 95 rows against precedent.

=== LAW 3: THE HISTORICAL WITNESS IS HISTORY, NOT A PIN — AND ITS COUNT ASSERT IS VACUOUS ON YOUR COHORT ===
tests/identity.rs::idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen reconstructs the pre-A10-CommandRef-erratum namespace by removing every post-erratum field cohort, then asserts A10_COMMAND_REF_ERRATUM_PREVIOUS_FIELDS_PIN. Any new field cohort breaks it. The fix is a new `post_erratum_<slice>_field` predicate + bumping the `pre_erratum.fields.len() + N` offset — NEVER re-pinning the constant, which would silently corrupt the witness.
THE TRAP: that `+ N` count assertion is INSENSITIVE to an unfiltered new cohort, because both sides grow by the same amount. It passes; only the pin assertion fires, one assert later. So the count assert cannot be used to tell you whether you filtered correctly.
This lock fires ONLY in tests/identity.rs. registry-check all was 0 failures with the witness broken.

=== LAW 4: g0_identity_e2e.sh HAS A SECOND LITERAL CLASS THAT A '"key":value' SWEEP MISSES ===
The counts that move (target_count, projection_fallback_count, target_source_assignment_sha256) are already read FROM THE CATALOG at runtime and need no edit — someone landed that fix. But BODY_RECIPES is an explicit array and the script asserts EXACT closure over it (`${#BODY_RECIPES[@]}`), so any new digest_class="body" row fails the e2e until registered as an ENTRY (never by bumping a count). My literal sweep matched '"key":value', reported all 21 pins correct, and looked exactly like a pass. Only running the e2e found it. Sweep for array members and `-eq` comparisons too.

=== WHAT REMAINS IN a09, WITH THE EXACT BLOCKER ON EACH ===
(A) 21 fields on the three WIRE-HOSTED records — blocked by LAW 1 above. Epic-level class decision, not a mint.
(B) 27 fields on three LANDED logical hosts, all measured, two nearly free:
    ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence (6, order 12, role-shard) — FULLY UNBLOCKED. Its one typed ref, StrongRef<ShardEscapingAllocationReservationRecord>, is minted at 0x044e order 10 <= 12. Do this one first.
    ShardIdRangeLease (15, order 10, role-shard) — one blocker: `meta_grant_ref: CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaIdRangeGrantCertificate>`. MetaIdRangeGrantCertificate is NOT registered but IS a09-reserved at 0x034c with disposition reference-only at a09:1892 — i.e. exactly the ShardEscapingAllocationReservationRecord case a predecessor already landed: mint the reference-only shell at ITS reserved code, flip reserved->existing, NO top_level_candidate and NO class flip, target form projection|logical_object_kinds|<Symbol>, and it MOVES projection_fallback_count. Note also `authority_projection: ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` is a LOGICAL kind (0x0109, order 10), and a logical kind is never a field's exact_wire_type (0 of 119) and cannot become a wire type (disjointness_dual_class) — so model it StrongRef + target_schema_id, order 10 <= 10 is legal because dag_future_result is non-strict.
    EscapingAllocationReservationRecord (6, order 14) — TWO blockers. `registration_ref` -> LocalAttemptRegistration is order 15 > 14, so dag_future_result fires; construction_order is NOT in the append-only pin and this kind has ZERO inbound typed refs appendix-wide, so raising it to >=15 is a free mechanical repair. `source_spec_ref` -> LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec is unregistered AND unreserved.
(C) 121 unadjudicated ambiguities (148 - 27). 132 of the 148 are field-type-ambiguous and follow the landed field rows one-for-one; the rest are 9 ambiguous-schema-owner, 2 unparsed-record-item, 2 conflicting-candidate-evidence, 1 unowned-structural-fragment, 1 definition-without-structural-body.
(D) 10 unminted top-level candidates, unchanged from the previous handback, including the AdjRunSegment logical-vs-physical question (a09 is the only slice declaring physical_record_kinds and AdjRunSegment is its only candidate) and IdRangeGrantSpec (source_kind=name-only, population-of-one precedent).

=== ONE MEASUREMENT A SUCCESSOR WILL WANT AND WOULD OTHERWISE REDO ===
Is a [[reservation]] REQUIRED for a StrongRef target? Nearly, but not a law: 229 of 230 landed StrongRef-target fields have one; the single exception is CommitMarker. So minting a strong ref to an unreserved symbol (e.g. LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec) would be the second exception in 230 — and note that creating the ref is itself the instrument that FORCES the target's class to logical under plan:282 rule 1, which is how the class question my predecessor declined to judge can be settled by measurement rather than opinion.
