title: Appendix A exact catalog: Key destruction, backup, publication, and release formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Key destruction, backup, publication, and release formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2057-2156 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**KeyWrap / KeyDestroyRecord / BackupManifest.** `KeyWrap` binds `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,logical_oid,ciphertext_id,dek_id,scope:Recipient|Database|BranchEpoch{graph,branch,write_epoch,object_creation_boundary:ObjectCreationBoundary}|Replica|Backup,wrap_algorithm,wrap_key_id,wrap_key_epoch,wrapped_dek,aad_bytes,aad_digest,issuer_signature}`; BranchEpoch AAD is exactly the branch-object transcript, while every other scope has its own registered transcript. Namespace-key escrow uses separately typed `ObjectIdKeyWrap` for `K_oid`. Rewrap creates only a new wrap; re-encryption creates a new CiphertextId and EncodingId realizations. `KeyDestroyFloorRef` is `Checkpoint{checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>}|Configuration{floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>}` and `KeyDestroyExternalAckRef` is `Backup{ack_ref:StrongRef<BackupKeyReleaseAck>}|LegalHold{ack_ref:StrongRef<LegalHoldReleaseAck>}|RemoteConsumer{ack_ref:StrongRef<RemoteKeyConsumerReleaseAck>}`. `KeyDestructionTarget` is the closed union `KmsKeyVersion{kms_authority_id,key_uri,key_version}|HsmObject{hsm_cluster_id,slot_id,object_handle_digest}|StorageMemberReplica{consensus_domain,member_id,material_class,material_identity_digest}`; canonical target identity is `H(domain,canonical(target))`. `KeyDestructionOperationPlan` is `{operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target:KeyDestructionTarget,canonical_request_transcript_digest,required_receipt_profile_oid}` and plans are sorted by target identity with no duplicate target or operation ID.

`KeyDestroyProposal` is the pre-order body `{key_identity,expected_key_state:RetainedDecryptOnly,basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest,exact_root_slot_generations,checkpoint_and_configuration_floor_refs[KeyDestroyFloorRef],generated_scanned_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,zero_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,backup_legal_hold_and_external_consumer_ack_refs[KeyDestroyExternalAckRef],threshold_authorization_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestructionAuthorization>,sorted_destruction_operation_plans[KeyDestructionOperationPlan],complete_target_set_digest,expected_state_conditions,terminal_audit_gate}`. The generated inventory includes every branch epoch, envelope node/root/grant, advancing-grant obligation, reachable ciphertext/wrap/opener, prepared/certificate/audit/outcome/result/workspace/replay/DP/backup, current or prospective configuration, and signing/verifier dependency. Apply atomically installs `KeyReferenceQuarantine {key_identity,quarantine_generation,proposal_identity:WeakDigest,installed_at_logical_command_seq,target_set_digest,no_new_reference_rule_id}` and one immutable Semantic `ExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord {operation_id,key_identity,quarantine_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceQuarantine>,target:KeyDestructionTarget,idempotency_token_digest,canonical_request_transcript_digest,required_receipt_profile_oid,state:AuthorizedUndispatchedRecipe,source_command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,assigned_logical_command_seq}` for every and only plan, then moves the key to `DestroyPending`. This record is an authorization recipe, never a mutable physical-status record. The canonical operation-root map is keyed by target identity and proves a plan/record bijection.

Only after the quarantine's role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>` exists may `KeyDestructionDispatchInitializeSpec` create one Protocol `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<KeyDestruction>::Armed` per authorization recipe. `KeyDestructionDispatchMarkSentUnknownSpec` durably advances an attempt before transport eligibility. The generated `KeyDestructionDispatchGuard` then rereads both RootSlots, the complete current Semantic/Protocol/Prepared/Consensus inventory, the exact key quarantine and no-new-reference proof, current/prospective configurations, writer fence, continuity head, service/security authority, target provider profile, and time evidence, and acquires the registered destruction hold immediately before the byte-identical request is submitted. KMS, HSM, and storage-member provider profiles must expose authenticated idempotent registration/status and monotonic terminal evidence; an unsupported provider cannot be configured as a destruction target. Recovery queries the same operation ID first, and a signed NotRegistered response permits only the same request under a fresh guard. `KeyDestructionReceiptImportSpec` moves the Protocol attempt to TerminalReceiptImported. Timeout, local expiry, provider ambiguity, or process death neither retries with a new ID nor implies destruction.

Key-destruction terminal evidence is target-typed. `ExternalKeyDestructionProviderReceipt` is the KMS/HSM-issued portable `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=KeyDestruction},target:KmsKeyVersion|HsmObject,destruction_result:Destroyed{target_terminal_counter,provider_evidence_digest}|AlreadyDestroyed{matching_prior_operation_id,target_terminal_counter,provider_evidence_digest},completed_at:AuthorityInstant,time_authority_profile_oid,provider_key_id,provider_key_epoch,signature}`. `AlreadyDestroyed` is accepted only when provider evidence cryptographically binds the same target and canonical request lineage. A current member imports it through `ExternalKeyDestructionReceiptImportRecord {operation_record_ref,dispatch_attempt_identity,portable_receipt_ref:StrongRef<ExternalKeyDestructionProviderReceipt>,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_authority_commitment,imported_at_maintenance_index,body_digest}` before any completion transition.

`StorageMemberKeyDestructionReceipt` is the same-group member-issued `{header:FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target:StorageMemberReplica,canonical_request_transcript_digest,key_material_identity_and_inventory_digest,pre_operation_physical_root_digest,post_operation_physical_root_digest,destroyed_or_crypto_erased_probe_digest,member_monotonic_counter,completion_counter,completed_at:AuthorityInstant,time_authority_profile_oid,member_signature}`. Its header proves the exact current configuration/member/writer/quarantine fence and that Started was durable before the first irreversible byte/key action; it is imported through `StorageMemberKeyDestructionReceiptImportRecord` under that same group. An external-provider receipt cannot stand for a storage member, and a member fence receipt cannot stand for KMS/HSM authority. `KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef` is the closed union `ExternalProvider{receipt_ref,import_record_ref}|StorageMember{receipt_ref,import_record_ref}` with target-discriminant equality. `TargetCompletionBijectionProof` binds the proposal target-set digest, canonical operation-root digest, sorted typed terminal receipt/import identities, and proves exactly one valid matching arm per target/operation with no missing, extra, duplicate, substituted, or conflicting result.

`PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence` is the independently verifiable, Protocol-object-identity-free `{dispatch_contract_id,key_identity,quarantine_generation,source_publication_evidence_commitment,operation_plan_and_authorization_recipe_commitment,sorted_terminal_attempt_and_receipt_commitments,complete_target_bijection_commitment,provider_status_lineage_commitment,configuration_fence_continuity_and_authority_commitment,signer_set_epoch,canonical_signatures}`. Its source commitment is over the exact role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>`; it is not hard-coded to a Local/Meta visibility certificate. `KeyDestroyFinalizeSpec` is `{proposal_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyProposal>,expected_quarantine_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceQuarantine>,quarantine_publication_evidence:CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>,sorted_operation_record_refs[StrongRef<ExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord>],dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence>,typed_terminal_receipt_refs[KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef],target_completion_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TargetCompletionBijectionProof>,exact_current_role_payload_and_root_slot_identities,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,current_prospective_configuration_set_digest,current_complete_generated_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,current_zero_reference_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,no_new_reference_since_quarantine_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoNewKeyReferenceProof>,expected_state_conditions,terminal_audit_gate}`. It requires current-root/configuration/slot equality or a registered quarantine-preserving successor proof, zero retaining references, byte-matching role-valid quarantine publication evidence, the exact proposal/recipe/Protocol-terminal/typed-receipt bijection, and no raw Protocol reference. Apply selects `DestroyedPendingCertificate` and creates compact `KeyDestroyRecord {key_identity,quarantine_generation,proposal_identity:WeakDigest,finalize_spec_identity:WeakDigest,complete_target_set_digest,operation_and_receipt_commitment,verified_current_inventory_digest,applied_finalize_identity:WeakAuthorityAppliedIdentity,terminal_audit_commitment}`; the record has no strong path to proposal, finalize, receipts, scanned inventories, old floors, Protocol attempts, or a future certificate.

Only after that record, its resulting durable root, and its required audit visibility advance exist may the current quorum create `KeyDestructionCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,key_identity,quarantine_generation,key_destroy_record_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyRecord>,post_finalize_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,operation_and_receipt_commitment,verified_current_inventory_digest,finalize_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. The Meta analogue uses `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>` through the generated role arm. `KeyDestroyCertificatePublishSpec {key_destroy_record_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyRecord>,certificate_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestructionCertificate>,expected_key_state:DestroyedPendingCertificate,expected_quarantine_generation,expected_current_state:WeakStateIdentity,terminal_audit_gate}` is the sole transition to final `Destroyed` and installs a compact certificate-index edge. Heavy inputs remain owned by the key lifecycle and certificate ledgers until publication's audit visibility advance plus an activated cut; compact result/receipt commitment/certificate remain through the crypto-erasure evidence floor. No state reaches final `Destroyed` if any reachable or independently obligated object can still require the key, any target lacks a receipt, or the certificate is absent.

Backup content and publication-envelope references are distinct identity classes. `BackupSourceIdentity<T> {source_authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,source_cluster_incarnation,object_kind,object_id,canonical_digest}` is nonretaining evidence and is never accepted by local or remote mark traversal. `BackupContentSubject<T>` is the closed union `SourceObject{expected_source:BackupSourceIdentity<T>}|RecoveryProjection{backup_id,projection_digest}`; generated type/kind rows make `RecoveryProjection` legal only for `T=BackupRecoveryProjection`. A manifest body, signature set, manifest, publication receipt, or transparency proof is never smuggled into this union: those objects are constructed only after the content-inventory root is fixed.

The root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>` is `{backup_id,archive_authority_id,inventory_key,subject:BackupContentSubject<T>,archived_byte_digest,archived_length,protection_profile,required_recovery_proof_class}`. It can be embedded while the final inventory root is not yet known. The externally resolvable content reference `BackupArchiveRef<T>` is `{entry:BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,inventory_leaf_index,inventory_inclusion_proof}` and is constructed only after the final content inventory exists. Its proof must authenticate the exact entry under that root and a current matching archive-retention grant. Live source entries use `SourceObject`; the recovery projection uses its dedicated arm.

Publication-envelope artifacts use the disjoint portable `BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T> {backup_id,publication_bundle_id,archive_authority_id,artifact_kind:ManifestBody|ManifestSignatureSet|Manifest,expected_canonical_digest,expected_length,authenticated_locator,publication_receipt_digest,receipt_artifact_index}`. Generated type/kind rows make each artifact tag legal only for its exact `T`. Resolution requires the separately supplied authentic `BackupPublicationReceipt`, byte-equality with the indexed locator/digest/length row in that receipt, and a current matching `ArchiveRetentionGrant`; the reference is not a content-inventory leaf and contains no content-inventory inclusion proof. The receipt itself and any later transparency inclusion are carried by their own portable evidence types and cannot self-locate through a future receipt.

Portable recovery is specified by one plane-complete object rather than inferred from inventory names. `RecoverySlotDisposition` is the closed union `TransformCurrent|CarryPriorEvidence|RecreateCurrentAuthority|ReconcileExternal|SuspendProtocolOwner|DiscardReplicaLocal{registered_law_id}|Reject`. `PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Role>` is `{role_and_group,source_manifest_identity,source_slot_generation_and_digest,semantic_cut:{applied_state:BackupInventoryRoleStateRef<Role>,visible_state:BackupInventoryRoleStateRef<Role>,applied_and_visible_positions},protocol_cut:{protocol_state:BackupInventoryRoleProtocolStateRef<Role>,maintenance_generation_and_index,audit_pipeline_and_pending_queue_inventory:StructurallyInapplicable|Present{inventory_entry_ref},result_cursor_artifact_error_escrow_inventory,security_barrier_state},prepared_cut:{prepared_root:BackupInventoryRolePreparedRef<Role>,live_owner_inventory},consensus_cut:{applied_cut_snapshot,retained_suffix,configuration,certificate_and_attempt_ledgers,remote_obligation_floors},checkpoint_and_floor_cut,external_continuity_reconciliation_inputs,bootstrap_reconstruction_inputs,sorted_slot_dispositions[{slot:DurableStateSlotRef,disposition:RecoverySlotDisposition}],complete_durable_state_slot_coverage_proof,body_digest}`. The `BackupInventoryRole*Ref` families are generated closed role-specific unions over exact root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>` targets; no erased archive ref and no final inventory-root digest is legal inside the projection.

`BackupRecoveryProjection` is `Local{common,local_cut:PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Local>}|Sharded{common,meta_cut:PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Meta>,sorted_shard_cuts[PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Shard>],exact_global_barrier_and_partition_bijection_proof}`. Every activated `durable_state_slots.toml` row and mandatory inventory class has exactly one disposition. `AbandonedByCas{predecessor:RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor,abandonment_authority_seed_digest,contract_id:CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>,terminal_import_ref:StrongRef<ExternalTerminalImportRecord<CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>,Role>>,portable_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>>>,operation_id,action_body_digest,result_restore_abandoned_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,prior_lease_closure_disposition}`. The two no-mutation arms are prebootstrap terminal evidence, not fake continuity heads: same-identity cleanup leaves the pre-existing Operational incarnation and its older catalog endpoint untouched, while absent-clone cleanup relies on authenticated absence plus permanent allocation/nonreuse dispositions. The action kind `RestoreContinuityAbandon` has two statically distinct universal-dispatch rows: `PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityAbandonContract` uses `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate`, while `CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>` uses the audit-visible canonical abandonment-operation candidate and ordinary Protocol publication evidence. Each requires the same-plane profile-valid catalog cleanup disposition and CASes only an actual `RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor` to `RestoreAbandoned`; their attempts, request bindings, evidence, and imports cannot cross-decode. A `RestoreFencePending` predecessor transfers the complete `PortablePriorLeaseClosureContinuationPackage` into `PendingInheritedFromFence`; all other restore predecessors carry `Complete` or `NotApplicableNewIdentity` as appropriate. Already-applied is terminal only when the authority returns an authenticated existing equivalent `RestoreAbandoned` head for the same operation, seed, incarnation, plane, and closure disposition.

Same-identity recovery CASes `Operational{posture}(I_current) -> RestoreFencePending`, durably fences every online/offline prior-incarnation lease issuer, proves the complete cohort inventory expired or revoked, then CASes `RestoreReserved(J)` with `J > max(I_current,I_backup,retired_incarnation_floor)` and the exact barrier/acquisition-plan commitments. Clone recovery CAS-creates exactly one previously absent target database/security namespace into `CloneReserved(J)` under a nonreusable identity-allocation receipt whose claimed intended-use commitment already fixes the acquisition operation; it never traverses the source continuity chain as target authority. Promotion never jumps directly to Operational. It first acquires a nonexpiring hidden catalog reservation, then CASes `RestoreReserved|CloneReserved|RoleTransitionReserved -> PromotionCatalogPending`, activates the exact reserved catalog row, and only then CASes to `Operational{lease_policy=PromotionReceiptRequired}` using the composite four-lineage receipt. The catalog row remains admission-hidden until that final receipt exists. An irreconcilable no-endpoint conflict before finalization uses rooted catalog-tombstone and continuity-abandon operations; restore must choose a higher incarnation, while a role-transition source remains terminally sealed and can proceed only through fenced restore/clone. DirectOrdinary is reserved for fresh/direct service activation whose catalog and continuity publication are one externally atomic authority operation. Abandonment changes exactly the registered `RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor` to `RestoreAbandoned`, advances the retired floor through the abandoned incarnation, and permanently forbids an Operational successor at that incarnation. A later same-identity recovery must move `RestoreAbandoned{retired through J} -> RestoreFencePending{target K}` for a new restore ID with `K > J` and a fresh recovery authority, inherit and finish any pending issuer closure, and only then enter `RestoreReserved` with one exact complete prior-lease barrier; no state at J is resurrected and no direct Abandoned -> Reserved shortcut exists. No other source or target posture is registered in v1. Checked overflow fails. Only one direct successor can win for a target identity, no acquisition send or recovery/transition write precedes its exact claimed plan, and continuity, lease/time guards, service-catalog reservation/activation, promotion receipts, and open/session admission all byte-match the active state/posture/incarnation/service epoch.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

title: Ruling: KeyDestroyProposal field wire vocabulary is underspecified
description:
## What and scope

Eight otherwise-local A15 `KeyDestroyProposal` field candidates cannot be projected because Appendix A names a value, state predicate, digest, or gate but does not define the exact wire shape the durable-field registry requires. This is an owner vocabulary ruling, not permission to guess a schema or amend the normative plan. It is distinct from `fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd`: that bead starts with a registered record/union wire type and asks which `identity_class` its containing field takes; this bead cannot yet name a legal `exact_wire_type` at all. A ruling here may subsequently consume the identity-class convention if it chooses a record or union wire shape.

## Exact unresolved vocabulary and blocked A15 rows

Each item blocks exactly one `KeyDestroyProposal` field row; total blocked rows: **8**.

1. `expected_key_state:RetainedDecryptOnly` — 1 row. The source supplies a required lifecycle-state value, not the containing enum/type name. `RetainedDecryptOnly` occurs as a state variant and is neither a builtin nor a registered wire type. Minting it as a standalone wire type would silently turn a value into a schema.
2. `basis_state:WeakStateIdentity` — 1 row. The source names `WeakStateIdentity`, but it is only a name-only Appendix candidate and is neither builtin nor registered. The source does not define whether this is a digest, an inline record, or another canonical state-identity wire shape.
3. `key_identity` — 1 row. No exact type, cardinality, identity class, or transcript recipe is stated at this occurrence. Other key identifiers in the plan have multiple noninterchangeable meanings, so name similarity cannot select one.
4. `expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest` — 1 row. The source says “digest” but not which durable digest class or canonical transcript/recipe produces it.
5. `exact_root_slot_generations` — 1 row. The source does not state the element/record type, whether it is scalar or collection-valued, the ordering rule, or cardinality.
6. `complete_target_set_digest` — 1 row. The source does not identify the digest class or the exact canonical target-set transcript/recipe.
7. `expected_state_conditions` — 1 row. The plan uses several semantically different condition families; this occurrence supplies neither a closed wire union/record nor exact cardinality.
8. `terminal_audit_gate` — 1 row. This recurring shorthand has no single registered wire type or exact local shape at this occurrence; choosing among gate/check/evidence forms would be semantic invention.

## Controlled measurement and interpretation

The lookup that found these absences also found the released `KeyDestructionOperationPlan` wire type and the released `expected_current_configuration_ref` field, and rejected a fabricated type/name. Thus the probe is working. Reading Appendix A A15 lines 2057-2059 establishes what the absence means: the proposal spells the eight member names but does not provide enough type/cardinality/transcript detail to emit legal `[[field]]` rows. The global landed-field precedent screen found no exact precedent for any of the six shorthand members. This is not an `identity_class`-only gap because the checker cannot first resolve a legal exact wire type.

## Required ruling

For each of the eight members, state the exact durable wire type and cardinality. For digest members, also state the digest class and canonical transcript/recipe. For `expected_key_state`, name the containing lifecycle enum/type and confirm `RetainedDecryptOnly` is a required value rather than a standalone type. For `basis_state`, define or bind `WeakStateIdentity`. For any newly chosen record/union type, apply the separate identity-class convention ruling rather than inventing an A15-only class.

## Success criteria

- Eight exact wire shapes/cardinalities are stated in a durable owner-visible rule or normative erratum.
- Each digest-like field has one unambiguous canonical recipe.
- The eight A15 field rows can be emitted without guessing and pass registry-check/G0 negative fixtures.
- No reservation is introduced for a non-StrongRef family; any required mints precede field/adjudication consumers.

## Provenance

Measured by pane5 against the post-I8 A15 state. I8 landed the three missing StrongRef prerequisites in `a8d7fcb`; these eight are the complete remaining `KeyDestroyProposal` field residue after that commit.
close_reason: Closed after c1e0317 landed the three source-forced consumers and comment 626 recorded the owner-ready five-fork matrix. WeakStateIdentity Branch B is disproved: CheckpointInstallSpec, GlobalCheckpointInstallSpec, ShardCheckpointInstallSpec, and DistributedSerializationCertificate co-locate WeakStateIdentity with a separate WeakDigest of that basis, so Branch A is source-distinct and landed. Remaining owner forks: (1) expected_key_state consumer +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication; a seven-arm carrier adds 16 projection and 16 exact-target shell rows before DestroyPending payload members, and depends on lifecycle carrier, seven tags, and payload-shape rulings; scalar branch has no union shell but needs the complete discriminant table. (2) key_identity consumer +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; opaque id256 has no producer rows, structured form adds one wire/target plus four member field/targets and depends on identity-domain/transcript versus member-shape ruling. (3) expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; depends on digest class/transcript and identity-set versus body/membership/fence commitment. (4) exact_root_slot_generations +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; either record shape adds one wire/target plus two member field/targets and depends on fixed-pair versus exactly-two-entry cardinality/order ruling. (5) complete_target_set_digest +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; depends on sorted-identity transcript versus authenticated-set tree/root algorithm. No further implementation is authorized until those producer rulings are made.

comments.text:
POST-RULING SOURCE/GENERATED-LAW ANALYSIS. The eight fields are not uniformly blocked. Three consumer shapes are forced by source; five remain genuine vocabulary forks. Generated union cost is measured, not estimated: an N-arm union expands to 2N+2 projection rows and 2N+2 exact target rows before payload-member rows.

FORCED CONSUMERS

1. basis_state. KeyDestroyProposal spells basis_state:WeakStateIdentity exactly, cardinality one, and the ControlCommand law makes state CAS inputs comparison-only. Therefore the A15 consumer row is forced: exact type WeakStateIdentity, one, nonretaining. Marginal A15 cost is one field plus one target. What remains unresolved is the shared producer type, not this use. Branch A defines WeakStateIdentity as a newtype/record: at least one wire row plus one target and all member rows/targets. Branch B makes it a normative alias/edit to WeakDigest: no new wire row, but changes the source census/convention for roughly seventy uses. A local A15 substitute would be wrong.

2. expected_state_conditions. ControlCommand line 1912 supplies the exact source-ordered closed arms WeakStateIdentity | WeakMarkerIdentity | ExpectedEpoch | ExpectedIndex, says these CAS expectations are comparison-only, and uses collection syntax; the A15 field is therefore cardinality many over that four-arm union. Marginal consumer cost is one field plus one target. The union shell costs 10 projection plus 10 target rows. WeakMarkerIdentity exists; WeakStateIdentity, ExpectedEpoch, and ExpectedIndex still need shared producer rulings. Flattening this to one digest is cheaper but requires a source erratum; it is not a source-conforming branch.

3. terminal_audit_gate. The SequenceNeutralSpec law requires exactly one TerminalAuditGate even when compact Appendix prose omits it, and line 2699 fixes the exact three source-ordered arms: StructurallyInapplicable{StructuralAuditExemption}, NotRequired{NonRequiredAuditEvidence}, Required{StrongRef<AuditTicket>, StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>, StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>}. There is no legal A15-local gate/check/evidence choice.

GENUINE FORKS

4. expected_key_state. The lifecycle law forces the compared value RetainedDecryptOnly, but does not force its wire carrier. Branch A registers the full seven-arm lifecycle state Generated | Active | Retiring | RetainedDecryptOnly | DestroyPending{quarantine_generation,target_set_digest} | DestroyedPendingCertificate | Destroyed: 16 projection plus 16 target shell rows, excluding DestroyPending payload members, then one A15 field/target. Branch B registers a fixed scalar lifecycle tag and requires the RetainedDecryptOnly discriminant here: one A15 field, one target, one final adjudication, plus a normative discriminant/validator table and no union rows. Omitting the field is not a branch because the source explicitly carries it.

5. key_identity. The source proves same-identity equality through proposal, quarantine, operation, finalize, and record, but never defines bytes. Branch A uses a domain-separated opaque id256: 32 bytes, one field plus one target plus one adjudication, no new wire row. Branch B defines KeyIdentity as a structured record such as namespace/material-class/key-id/key-epoch: one wire row/target plus four member rows/targets plus the proposal field/target/adjudication, with larger bytes and local validation. Neither shape follows from name similarity.

6. expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest. Equality to the current prospective configuration set is forced; digest class and transcript are not. Branch A hashes a domain-separated count plus sorted ConfigurationState object identities. Branch B hashes canonical configuration bodies/membership/fence epochs. Both cost one digest256 field, one target, one adjudication, and 32 bytes; B additionally requires canonical body closure and recipe/proof logic. The plan does not select one.

7. exact_root_slot_generations. The root law forces both fixed slots and both u64 generations to be captured and reread, but not their encoding. Branch A is a cardinality-one record {slot0_generation:u64,slot1_generation:u64}, 16 bytes: one wire row/target, two member rows/targets, and the proposal field/target/adjudication. Branch B is exactly two source-ordered entries {slot_index:u8,generation:u64}, cardinality many, at least 18 bytes before framing: the same row count, plus an exact-count/no-duplicate/order law and a source cardinality clarification. A free-form collection is not legal because the machine has exactly two slots.

8. complete_target_set_digest. Lines 2057-2059 force the committed set to be the unique sorted canonical KeyDestructionTarget identities and keep it distinct from operation IDs and the canonical operation-root digest; TargetCompletionBijectionProof binds both separately. They do not give the set-digest transcript. Branch A hashes domain, count, and length-delimited sorted target identities. Branch B uses an authenticated map/Merkle-set root over those same keys. Both cost one digest256 field, one target, one adjudication, and 32 bytes; B also adds a tree/root algorithm and proof vocabulary.

Bottom line: basis_state, expected_state_conditions, and terminal_audit_gate are source-forced consumers with shared prerequisite mints. expected_key_state, key_identity, expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest, exact_root_slot_generations, and complete_target_set_digest require owner vocabulary choices. This bead should remain open only for those five decisions and the three shared producer definitions, not as a blanket eight-field blocker.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation. This task embeds source-plan lines 2157-2246 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Rollback-protected authority time.** Canonical logical HLC orders database state; it is never an expiry clock. Process-local monotonic time may enforce a short-lived in-memory use budget and drive advisory timers; ambient wall time is display-only. Any authorization, lease-validity, expiry, release, retirement, key destruction, archive downgrade, restore fencing, or retention-cut decision uses the following rollback-protected authority-time contract or fails closed.

`AuthorityInstant` is `{time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick:u128}` and compares only within one domain/epoch; windows are closed-open: `not_before <= true_authority_time < expires_at`. `AuthorityInterval` is the exact `{earliest:AuthorityInstant,latest:AuthorityInstant}` with byte-identical domain/epoch fields and `earliest.tick <= latest.tick`; intervals from different domains/epochs are never ordered, intersected, or bridged by scalar conversion. `TimeAuthorityProfile` is the immutable threshold-signed `{schema_version,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick_scale,external_registry_id,ordered_signers[{signer_id,key_id,verification_key}],threshold,maximum_source_uncertainty_ticks,maximum_challenge_round_trip_ticks,maximum_guard_use_ticks,comparison_semantics:ClosedOpen,unavailable_policy:FailClosed,predecessor_profile_digest:WeakDigest?,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`.

External time evidence is reference-free. `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` is the fresh challenged signed `{profile_oid,profile_digest,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,challenge_nonce,subject_digest,intended_use_digest,authority_sequence,possible_time_interval:AuthorityInterval,external_registry_head_digest,external_registry_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. It never claims process-local send/receive counters.

`ShardTimeAuthorityProjection` is the shard-local certified Meta projection `{source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,source_meta_time_registry_generation,selected_profile_oid,sorted_profile_projections[{profile_oid,profile_digest,issuance_state:ActiveForIssuance|ClosingRequested|IssuanceClosing|IssuanceQuiescent|Draining|Retired,verification_live_through_commitment}],time_authority_registry_head_digest,verifier_and_offline_issuer_floor_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,typed_projection_payload_identity_and_digest,projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,body_digest}`. Its certificate's `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload` arm is exactly `TimeAuthorityRegistryProjection` and byte-matches the payload identity/digest and source prefix/effect. It is installed only through the exact contiguous ActiveMetaProjectionRoot time-authority slot and is invalid after that source prefix/configuration/trust or retention evidence ceases to be current.

`LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness` is the nonportable `{process_incarnation_id,challenge_nonce,send_monotonic_tick,receive_monotonic_tick,checked_elapsed_ticks,monotonic_source_profile_id,conversion_to_authority_uncertainty_ticks,body_digest}`. `TimeAuthorityObservationImport` is the closed role-local union `Local{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Local>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Meta{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Meta>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Shard{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_meta_time_authority_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeAuthorityProjection>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_projection_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}`. The import verifies the portable profile identity/digest, current registry or certified projection, role/group/configuration/fence, same-nonce local round trip, interval, subject, intended use, and signatures before any local validator may consume it. Challenge nonce, subject, and use are signed. Replay, wrong profile/domain/epoch, noncurrent registry head, excessive checked round trip/uncertainty, process-incarnation mismatch, role substitution, or signature failure is unusable.

`time_bound_subjects.toml` is the single exhaustive source for the closed `TimeBoundSubject` union. Each row names one concrete durable schema or one exact capability variant, its canonical pre-evidence transcript recipe, profile/window field tags, legal intended uses, evidence owner, expiry/retirement transition, and retention floor. It forbids raw refs, a generic object arm, a generic capability arm, and overlapping transcripts. `TimeValidationEvidence` is the already-built role-local immutable `{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,subject:TimeBoundSubject,intended_use_digest,classification:Usable{not_before,expires_at,validated_process_incarnation_id,guard_deadline_local_monotonic_tick}|NotYetValid{not_before}|Expired{expires_at},validator_version,validation_digest}`. `Usable` exists only when the imported portable observation's `possible_time_interval.earliest >= not_before`, the local round-trip witness belongs to the current process incarnation, and `checked_add(possible_time_interval.latest.tick,maximum_guard_use_ticks)` succeeds in the same domain/epoch and is `< expires_at`; its local guard deadline is derived with checked arithmetic from the same receive tick and conservative remaining budget. A linear use guard can be constructed only in that same process incarnation while its current monotonic tick is strictly before the recorded deadline. Durable Usable bytes surviving restart therefore authorize nothing until a fresh observation/import/evidence exists. `NotYetValid` exists only when `possible_time_interval.latest < not_before`; `Expired` only when `possible_time_interval.earliest >= expires_at` and remains durable across restart. An interval overlapping either boundary yields no evidence and the uniform retryable `TimeAuthorityUnavailable`, before any protected lookup or disclosure. Tick addition, bound normalization, challenge-round-trip subtraction, and profile drain arithmetic are checked; overflow, saturation requirement, or domain/epoch mismatch yields `TimeAuthorityUnavailable` and never wraps.

The v1 arms bind the canonical pre-evidence body, never a future object that embeds the evidence, and are exactly: `TxnOutcomeCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeSubscriptionCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeBufferedResultCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeArtifactOutputCapabilityBytes`, `MergeOutcomeCapabilityBytes`, `ReadYourWritesCapabilityBytes`, `MacaroonTokenBytes`, `OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort`, `MutationPermitRecord`, `ReadPermitRecord`, `AuthorizationLease`, `TxnOwnershipLease`, `PrivacyExecutionLease`, `ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`, `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`, `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis`, `ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis`, `ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis`, `TxnOutcomeLookupWindow`, `FollowerLeaseRead`, `IdRangeLease`, `ShardIdRangeLease`, `ClusterIncarnationLease`, `PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecordLocal`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecordMeta`, `ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection`, `NewDatabaseIdentityReservation`, `ServiceVisibilityEpochReservation`, `AllocationEpochReservation`, `ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline`, `ReplayArchiveRecord`, `ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow`, `ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow`, `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow`, `BackupPublicationFreshness`, `BackupTransparencyFreshness`, `TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis`, `CrossLogTransparencyFreshness`, `PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis`, `VerifierKeyWindow`, and `IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow`. The three restore-source arms map exactly to `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Local>`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Meta>`, and the Shard projection schema; the prebootstrap owner belongs only to `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` and its prebootstrap time validator. Each row explicitly maps the arm to its exact schema and window field tags; aliases such as `FollowerReadLease`, `IdRangeIssuanceLease`, `RestoreSourceLease`, or `ReplayArchiveLease` are unregistered. Capability arms contain the exact capability kind plus header-and-body digest; they cannot overlap. `MacaroonTokenBytes` validates one presented root or attenuated token and therefore contains its exact token kind plus canonical header/body/caveat-chain digest. Output-basis arms contain role, owner/delivery generation, complete authority commitment, policy, and exact window.

The formerly shorthand window names above are generated exact schemas, not aliases for two loose timestamps. Their common canonical prefix is `{subject_kind,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant,subject_body_digest,intended_use_set,owner_plane_and_slot,body_digest}`, with both instants byte-matching the profile domain/epoch and `not_before < expires_at`. Their subject-specific closed suffixes are: `ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis<Role>{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,error_delivery_id,error_generation,protected_error_policy_ref,replay_count_and_ceiling,public_error_digest}`; `TxnOutcomeLookupWindow<Role>{authority_bound_header,capability_commitment,outcome_index_key_commitment,lookup_floor_generation,verifier_key_ref}`; `ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline<Role>{authority_bound_header,reservation_kind,reservation_id,reservation_generation,resource_ledger_basis_digest,expiry_disposition}`; `PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow{cohort_recipe_id,continuity_domain_id,database_security_namespace_id,prior_incarnation,issuer_id,issuer_configuration_identity_and_digest,issuer_authority_epoch,covered_generation_and_counter_ranges,issuer_fence_receipt_digest,cohort_closure_row_bytes_and_digest,time_domain_id,time_authority_epoch,last_legal_issuance_or_renewal_counter,maximum_issued_or_renewed_expires_at:AuthorityInstant,issuance_ledger_accumulator_and_range_completeness_commitment,window_digest}`; `ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow{archive_authority_id,grant_id,grant_generation,grant_subject_set_digest,grant_head_digest_and_cas_version}`; `ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow{archive_authority_id,hold_id,release_generation,participant_set_digest,prepared_head_digest_and_cas_version}`; `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role>{authority_bound_header,grant_id,generation,recipient_id,graph,branch,envelope_epoch,coverage_cut,grant_record_digest}`; `BackupPublicationFreshness{backup_id,publication_operation_id,publication_bundle_id,publication_authority_head_digest_and_cas_version,receipt_request_binding_digest}`; `BackupTransparencyFreshness{backup_id,transparency_operation_id,required_policy_digest,checkpoint_identity_and_digest,inclusion_subject_digest}`; `TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis{log_id,security_domain_id,witness_policy_oid,checkpoint_body_digest,log_size,claim_class}`; `CrossLogTransparencyFreshness{source_checkpoint_digest,target_log_id,target_policy_oid,target_log_size,target_checkpoint_digest,cross_log_receipt_digest}`; `PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis{role_and_group,configuration_identity,payload_predicate_digest,storage_member,prepared_ownership_id,base_closure_inventory_digest,receipt_body_without_freshness_or_signature_digest}`; `VerifierKeyWindow{verifier_kind,key_id,key_epoch,verification_scope_digest,retention_floor_digest}`; and `IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow<Role>{authority_binding_public_commitment,dispatch_contract_id,operation_id,attempt_generation,target_identity,source_gate_commitment,status_or_send_action_digest}`. The cohort window's common `expires_at` must byte-equal the exhaustive signed `maximum_issued_or_renewed_expires_at`; no lifetime, nominal duration, counter arithmetic, or derived expiry field exists. Generation rejects a suffix without its exact prefix, a prefix reused for another subject, an embedded future evidence ref, or a named window whose owner/expiry transition is absent.

`MacaroonRootIssuanceReceipt` is the portable signed `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,root_token_id,root_issuance_sequence,canonical_issuance_request_digest,idempotency_key_digest,root_token_body_digest,canonical_root_token_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,root_not_before,root_expires_at,issuer_counter,authority_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `MacaroonRootIssuanceRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the local durable root-issuance owner `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,root_token_id,issuance_receipt_ref:StrongRef<MacaroonRootIssuanceReceipt>,canonical_issuance_request_digest,idempotency_key_digest,root_token_body_digest,canonical_root_token_digest,canonical_root_token_bytes_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalCapabilityBytes>,replay_retention_floor,issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,root_issuance_sequence,time_authority_profile_oid,root_not_before,root_expires_at,maximum_attenuation_expiry_equal_to_root_expiry,revocation_subject_commitment,state:Live|Revoked{revocation_evidence_ref}|Expired{time_validation_evidence_ref},body_digest}`. Online issuance creates exactly one record and publishes the matching reservation successor in the same RootManifest generation before returning canonical bytes; exact retry joins and returns the retained identical bytes. The root token ID, request/idempotency commitment, receipt sequence, and byte digest are permanent through the replay floor, while attenuated presentations are derived byte variants and never create inventory rows.

`OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochFenceReceipt` is the portable signed result of moving one non-exportable counter-backed issuer epoch to verify-only/disabled-for-root-issuance: `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,issuer_epoch_configuration_digest,permitted_root_sequence_range,permitted_hardware_counter_range,last_legal_root_issuance_sequence,returned_issuer_counter,issuer_epoch_state:VerifyOnly|Disabled,authority_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,fenced_at:AuthorityInstant,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort` is the signed bounded inventory subject `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,issuer_epoch_configuration_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,cohort_not_before,permitted_root_sequence_range,permitted_hardware_counter_range,maximum_root_lifetime_ticks,derived_maximum_possible_expiry,last_legal_root_issuance_sequence,returned_issuer_counter,issuer_epoch_fence_receipt_digest,range_and_maximum_expiry_derivation_proof,issuance_scope_ceiling_commitment,attenuation_semantics_oid,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. Its checker derives the maximum possible expiry from the configured maximum root lifetime, last permitted counter/sequence, and challenged fence interval; an asserted maximum without that derivation is invalid. It represents every root token that could have been issued by that epoch even when individual bytes are not locally enumerable; it does not validate a presented token. The offline issuer MAC/verify-only service and verification material remain rooted through the derived cohort maximum expiry. Post-fence attenuation of a pre-fence root is legal only under the exact narrowing law and does not create a new cohort member; post-fence root minting is rejected by the hardware counter/fence and by verification. `MacaroonTokenBytes` remains a use-time `TimeBoundSubject` so an individual presented token can be classified, but the rotation inventory tracks online `MacaroonRootIssuanceRecord` rows and offline issuer cohorts—not every possible attenuated byte string.

Each unsigned-body transcript includes its `time_authority_profile_oid`, both bounds when the object has a window, and every authority/domain/generation field, excluding only signatures/MAC and the later `TimeValidationEvidence` reference. Generation performs a two-way total check: every active `durable_fields.toml` time-bearing field set has exactly one nonoverlapping subject row, and every subject row resolves to one live schema/variant, owner floor, and transition. A status-only check may consume a runtime guard; an ordered expiry, release, tombstone, retirement, compaction, or reclamation must retain the exact durable evidence in its applied transition.

A successful Usable validation creates a linear, nonserializable `TimeUseGuard` bound to observation, subject, intended action, process incarnation, and remaining monotonic use budget. It is consumed immediately before the protected observation/irreversible step and cannot survive restart, over-budget suspend, clone, serialization, or replay. Local monotonic time measures only challenge/use age; it never establishes absolute time. Expired evidence is durable and monotone for its one bound canonical release/expiry action. Every canonical transition whose legality depends on expiry strongly retains the exact evidence; a scalar deadline or timeout alone never changes canonical state or cuts retention.

`TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role,generation,profiles[profile_oid -> ActiveForIssuance{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_generation}|ClosingRequested{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,freeze_generation,reservation_index_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role>>}|IssuanceClosing{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref,closing_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt>,local_close_cut}|IssuanceQuiescent{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref,closing_receipt_ref,own_reservation_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure<Role>>}|Draining{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,issuance_fence_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>,subject_inventory_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>>,drain_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>>,maximum_old_subject_expiry}|Retired{profile_identity_and_digest,terminal_summary_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>>,retired_at_registry_generation}],selected_profile_oid,profile_retirement_floor,body_digest:BodyDigest<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>}`. Profile keys are unique and canonical. In steady state exactly one selected profile is `ActiveForIssuance`; from ordered intent through quiescence there are zero Active profiles and exactly one selected `ClosingRequested`, `IssuanceClosing`, or `IssuanceQuiescent` profile. After activation exactly one successor is Active and the predecessor is Draining. No issuance encoder accepts ClosingRequested, IssuanceClosing, IssuanceQuiescent, Draining, or Retired. The registered body transcript excludes only `body_digest`. Exact activation is `TimeAuthorityProfileTransitionSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> {completion_authority:TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,original_admin_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,expected_time_authority_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,expected_registry_generation,expected_selected_profile_state:IssuanceQuiescent,retiring_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_closing_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt>,issuance_fence_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>,epoch_transition_plan_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionPlan>,external_registry_transition_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionReceipt>,epoch_transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,old_profile_subject_inventory_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>>,old_observation_and_verifier_retention_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>>,configuration_retention_basis:RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role>,drain_floor_set:RoleTimeAuthorityDrainFloorSet<Role>,terminal_audit_gate}`. It verifies the complete intent/dispatch/closing/quiescence/fence/inventory bijection and atomically selects the successor for new issuance while retaining the predecessor as Draining. Completion cannot widen the original authorization, change the successor, sets, operation IDs, or resources, or solicit a fresh client choice after the irreversible fence.

Exact retirement is `TimeAuthorityProfileRetirementSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> {cleanup_authority:TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority<Role>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,expected_time_authority_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,expected_registry_generation,epoch_transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,retiring_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,complete_current_root_subject_scan_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role>>,sorted_subject_dispositions[TimeSubjectDisposition<Role>],complete_subject_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof<Role>>,old_observation_service_shutdown_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityShutdownReceipt>,old_verifier_key_retirement_floor_ref:StrongRef<VerifierKeyRetirementFloor>,configuration_retention_basis:RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role>,retirement_floor_set:RoleTimeAuthorityRetirementFloorSet<Role>,terminal_summary_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`. Every inventory row appears exactly once. Meta's retirement floor set contains one matching ack from every configured shard. Apply first verifies the heavy closure, deterministically creates `TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>`, selects `Retired{terminal_summary_ref}`, and releases the drain hold only after shutdown, zero-dependency verifier/offline-issuer floors, shard floors, and paired all-plane/configuration floors are durable. The detailed proof/transition/admin-authority closure survives until the retirement candidate is audit-visible and its cut activates, then becomes collectible; no terminal state indefinitely retains completion or cleanup authority. Activation/retirement, issuance closing/reservations/quiescence, compaction, and every failure boundary are permanent registry/model/DPOR gates.

`PortableContinuityAuthorityObservation` is the continuity authority's challenged, reference-free signed `{database_security_namespace_id,continuity_profile_id,current_continuity_record_digest,current_cas_version,cluster_incarnation,member_writer_id,lease_generation,scope,lease_status:Active,authority_tick,time_authority_observation_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,time_observation_interval:AuthorityInterval,intended_irreversible_action_digest,challenge_nonce,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `ShardContinuityAuthorityProjection` is the exact Shard-local `{source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,portable_continuity_head_and_lease_scope,source_head_digest_and_cas_version,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,typed_projection_payload_identity_and_digest,projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,body_digest}` whose certificate uses the `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload::ContinuityAuthority` arm. `ContinuityAuthorityCurrentBasis<Role>` is the generated closed role union `Local{current_root_manifest_and_slot_identity,current_logical_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,current_continuity_record_ref:StrongRef<ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord>,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,writer_fence_epoch}|Meta{current_root_manifest_and_slot_identity,current_global_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,current_continuity_record_ref:StrongRef<ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord>,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,writer_fence_epoch}|Shard{current_root_manifest_and_slot_identity,current_active_meta_projection_root_ref:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,continuity_projection_slot_ref:StrongRef<ShardContinuityAuthorityProjection>,source_meta_prefix_and_configuration,writer_fence_epoch}`. The Shard projection contains the complete portable continuity head/lease scope plus its certified Meta source, configuration, retention, and trust evidence; it is never a digest-only head.

`ContinuityAuthorityObservationImport<Role>` is the role-local `{role_and_group,current_basis:ContinuityAuthorityCurrentBasis<Role>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableContinuityAuthorityObservation>,time_observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,exact_current_basis_observation_time_and_action_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}`. The imported head/CAS/incarnation/member/generation/scope must equal the current rooted basis, not merely a valid authority signature. `IncarnationLeaseGuard` exists only from the exact current role-bound import for the same member/generation/scope/window/action and same current process-incarnation time budget. Every segment/object/root seal, prepared-root publication, receipt, Raft proposal/ack, certificate, and RootSlot publication consumes a fresh action-bound guard. Cached validity, canonical HLC, OS wall time, or a signature over an older/uninstalled continuity head never authorizes a write. Portable continuity receipts and certificates carry only the portable observation or its digest.

`ClusterIncarnationLease` is `{continuity_record_digest,cas_version,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,restore_id?,member_writer_id,scope:RecoveryOnly|OrdinaryWrite|RoleTransitionOnly,lease_generation,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,nonce,authority_signature}`. `CommitCx` contains a nonconstructible `IncarnationLeaseGuard`; recovery gets `RecoveryCommitCx` with only RecoveryOnly and role migration gets a guard whose encoders accept only transition objects. Immediately before every irreversible action, code validates the inode lease/fence, exact external continuity head/CAS version, action-bound authority observation/evidence, live member lease, and operation scope. Authority outage, ambiguity, expiry, or rollback poisons publication; cached validity is insufficient. `RootSlot` and every role payload carry the continuity digest/CAS version, service visibility epoch, and time-authority binding.

Prior-incarnation/archive edges use exact nonlocal types. `PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T> {restore_id,source_backup_manifest_digest,source_cluster_incarnation,target_cluster_incarnation,source:BackupArchiveRef<T>}` is legal only for content-inventory objects in restore plans/results/bridges/evidence/provenance and never enters the current mark set; `T=BackupManifest|BackupManifestBody|BackupManifestSignatureSet` is a generated negative. `RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity` is `{restore_id,source_backup_identity:{source_database_id,source_database_security_namespace_id,source_cluster_incarnation,backup_id,backup_manifest_digest,publication_bundle_id,archive_retention_grant_id,archive_grant_subject_set_digest,archive_inventory_root_digest,permitted_inventory_digest},target_holder_identity:{target_database_id,target_database_security_namespace_id,target_incarnation,target_service_visibility_epoch,recovery_authority_digest},archive_authority_id,lease_lineage_id,holder_authority_digest}`. Stable identity deliberately excludes grant and lease generations. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest` is `BLAKE3("fgdb.restore-source-lease-state.v1" || canonical(lease_identity,generation,selected_grant_generation_and_digest,window_profile_domain_epoch_and_bounds,archive_counter,holder_and_subject_set_commitment))`; it is derived entirely from portable archive-authority state and is never a keyed Local/Meta ObjectId or body digest. `PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof` is the reference-free signed `{archive_authority_id,grant_id,selected_generation,selected_grant_digest,ordered_predecessor_generation_and_digest_chain,current_head_digest_and_cas_version,unchanged_subject_set_digest,window_coverage,archive_monotonic_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt` and `RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt` are distinct portable external receipts with `ExternalActionRequestBinding`, the stable lease identity, exact predecessor generation and portable lease-state digest for renewal, selected grant generation/digest, complete signed `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof` bytes and digest, resulting lease generation/window/counter, resulting `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest`, and signature. The lineage proof names request/result-head commitments but never its enclosing receipt digest, so receipt construction remains acyclic.

Before a target database exists, `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner` is a registered prebootstrap artifact schema, not a logical object: `{identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,predecessor_owner_digest?,portable_plan_digest,source_gate_digest,record_kind:Acquire{receipt_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt>}|Renew{receipt_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt>},selected_archive_grant_generation_and_digest,grant_lineage_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof>,lease_window_successor_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<LeaseWindowSuccessorProof>?,lease_lineage_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof>,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,archive_monotonic_counter,recovery_authority_public_commitment,journal_id,owner_publication_journal_head_generation_digest_and_cas_version,owner_publication_dispatch_state_generation_and_digest,relocation_chain_head_commitment,body_digest}`. It deliberately contains no inode, path, local mirror identity, or mutable dispatch-root locator. The acquire/renew terminal payload must journal the complete signed lineage proof before this owner can become Current; a digest-only result is invalid after restart or relocation. `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent` stores `owner_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner>` plus checked generation/portable-state/lineage commitment and resolves it only through the authenticated current journal head and relocation chain. Acquire creates generation one; registered prebootstrap renewal creates `g+1`, advances Current, and makes the prior artifact reclaimable only after the successor/head/capsule publication is durable. Relocating the cache inode changes neither owner identity nor authority; a stale mirror that cannot prove the current head/relocation chain is unusable. This owner is never a current-database authority record.

`LeaseWindowSuccessorProof` is an independently addressable registered logical schema with the closed body `SameEpochNonshrinking{lease_identity,prior_and_successor_generations,same_profile_domain_epoch,prior_and_successor_bounds,checked_nonshrinking_bounds_and_counter,archive_authority_signature}|CrossEpochHandoff{lease_identity,prior_and_successor_generations,old_and_new_profile_identities,dual_signed_transition_proof,no_gap_coverage_proof,checked_domain_mapping,archive_authority_signature}`. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint` is the reference-free signed contiguous-range summary `{lease_identity,start_generation_and_predecessor_head,end_generation_and_complete_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,ordered_operation_id_idempotency_request_result_head_and_outcome_accumulator,complete_generation_range_and_no_fork_proof,unchanged_holder_subject_archive_authority_and_permitted_inventory_commitment,start_and_end_archive_counters,predecessor_checkpoint:Genesis|Prior{complete_checkpoint_bytes_and_digest},provider_status_and_operation_nonreuse_floor,checkpoint_availability_and_retention_certificate,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It cannot omit a generation, summarize an unresolved operation, change subject/holder/inventory, or refer only to unavailable bytes. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof` is the reference-free signed `{lease_identity,selected_generation,selected_portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,lineage_basis:Genesis|Checkpointed{complete_prior_checkpoint_bytes_and_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint},ordered_generation_operation_request_and_result_head_commitments_after_basis,unchanged_holder_subject_and_archive_authority_commitment,current_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,archive_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`; it never names a keyed Local/Meta record or body digest. Prebootstrap owner generations retain the complete checkpoint artifact; canonical `RestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpointImport<Role>` carries a full `AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>`, the complete portable checkpoint, current lease-lineage proof, and exact byte-match proof. The current canonical lease record and then its release operation summary retain the latest import through the provider status/nonreuse/retention floor; checked lease-history compaction may replace earlier details only when the checkpoint covers them and remains independently available.

Canonical `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest},record_kind:AcquireImported{prebootstrap_owner_digest,receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt>}|RenewImported{receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt>,lease_window_successor_proof_ref:StrongRef<LeaseWindowSuccessorProof>},selected_archive_grant_generation,selected_archive_grant_digest,grant_lineage_proof_ref:StrongRef<PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof>,lease_lineage_proof_ref:StrongRef<PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof>,lineage_basis:Genesis|Checkpointed{checkpoint_import_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpointImport<Role>>},time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,archive_monotonic_counter,body_digest}`. The portable state digest byte-matches the receipt, authority head, observations, proofs, checkpoint basis, and all portable projections; the keyed role-local `body_digest` and ObjectId remain separate. The first Local/Meta bridge imports the latest prebootstrap generation—not necessarily generation one—with the full current authority header. Later renewal constructs `prior+1`, preserves all stable identities/subject sets, advances the counter, and carries exact successor and lineage proofs; raw tick comparison across domains or authority epochs is invalid. The prior visible registry strongly owns the old record until renewal finalize becomes visible, after which the weak predecessor digest plus signed lineage proof/checkpoint avoids an unbounded strong chain without making historical status evidence disappear.

`ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource` is the closed union `Bootstrap{bootstrap_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate>,bootstrap_projection_identity_and_digest,source_lease_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}|Refresh{meta_control_projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,typed_meta_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}`. `ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection` is `{source:ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource,source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,lease_identity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,selected_grant_generation_and_digest,window_profile_domain_epoch_and_bounds,archive_counter,holder_and_subject_set_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,body_digest}`. Bootstrap validates the exact `RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate` and its certificate-free payload; Refresh uses only `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload::RestoreSourceLease`, must name the same restore/plan/shard/lease lineage and unchanged holder/subject/inventory/recipient commitments, and may advance only `g -> g+1` with the exact successor proof. A Shard never owns a canonical lease record and cannot renew or release it.

`RestoreArchiveRef<T> {source:PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_inventory_leaf,leaf_proof}` contains no strong lease-generation edge. `RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T> {source:BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_grant_subject_leaf,grant_subject_leaf_proof,publication_receipt_binding}` is legal only for exact publication-envelope artifact kinds and proves the locator row against the lease-bound publication receipt/grant subject set. Every reference and registry common field must match both source and target identities. Before the bridge, resolution uses the current prebootstrap owner; afterward Local/Meta resolution requires the latest canonical live lease record and Shard resolution requires the exact current certified projection, plus subject-preserving grant lineage, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, and the exact inventory/grant proof.

Source acquisition precedes canonical target creation and is externally recoverable. Pre-send `RestoreIdentityKeyPlan` is the closed union `PreserveSameIdentity{identical_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_identity_and_commitment,recover_and_rewrap_operation_recipe,target_rewrap_recipient_commitment,required_key_equality_proof_profile,required_zero_plaintext_persistence_proof_profile}|CloneFreshIdentity{distinct_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,recover_source_k_oid_for_decode_operation_recipe,create_target_k_oid_operation_recipe,target_k_oid_recipient_commitment,required_source_key_nontransplant_proof_profile}`. It contains only recipes, expected identities, and proof profiles. Post-provider `RestoreIdentityKeyDispositionEvidence` is the distinct closed union `PreservedSameIdentity{plan_digest,identical_namespace_proof,recover_and_rewrap_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_commitment,target_rewrapped_k_oid_commitment,key_equality_proof,zero_plaintext_persistence_proof}|ClonedFreshIdentity{plan_digest,distinct_namespace_proof,recover_source_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,create_target_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,target_k_oid_commitment,source_key_nontransplant_proof}`. Clone source `K_oid` and DEKs authorize source decoding only; every target ciphertext receives a fresh target DEK under the newly created target identity.

`RestoreClaimedTargetAuthorityRecipe` is the pre-claim closed union `RecoverSameIdentity{expected_operational_or_fence_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,restore_id,source_backup_identity,planned_target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,prior_lease_fence_plan_commitment}|CloneNewIdentity{identity_reservation_id,expected_reserved_head_digest_and_cas_version,claim_id,claimant_identity,target_database_and_security_identity,target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,continuity_profile:DirectoryBound{filesystem_profile_id,mount_device_directory_and_target_manifest_inode_identity,target_manifest_staging_inode_creation_nonce_digest,whole_inode_fence_identity,parent_directory_durability_recipe,fixed_local_continuity_recipe_and_digest,zero_existing_root_slot_proof_recipe,directory_bound_creation_evidence_recipe_digest}|ExternalCas{expected_continuity_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,enter_clone_reserved_operation_recipe,recovery_only_lease_recipe}}`. It contains no resulting claimed/reserved head and no plan digest field that would make the plan self-referential. DirectoryBound carries no external continuity head or CAS recipe; ExternalCas requires both.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

FIRST, A COUNT CORRECTION. The standing trail says "15 unreserved unclassified candidates". The live figure is 33. A candidate needs a call when it has no [[target]], no [[reservation]], no [[source_symbol_disposition]], and no minted logical kind. The 15 was an earlier, narrower reading; plan on 33.

METHOD, and its limits stated up front. Two probes: one for definition-site evidence (census owner_statuses, definition_kinds, body_conflict, source locations, and whether the census renders a structural BODY), one for USAGE across the whole appendix field census (bare-type use, StrongRef target, nested/list use, arm-token match). THE LIMIT, stated because it changes how one bucket must be read: my usage scan covers Appendix A FIELD types only. It does not see references from command contracts, Appendix B intents, or ordering prose. So "no external use" means "no Appendix A field names it", NOT "not durable". Several symbols in that bucket are the command-contract-owned specs and authorities the trail already identified, and they will be referenced from the command_contracts registry instead. ONE CALL IS DECIDED, WITH SOURCE PROOF. `Retired` is NOT a top-level schema — it is a union arm token of the TimeAuthorityRegistry profiles issuance-state union. FIVE HAVE NO STRUCTURAL BODY AT ALL, which is the cleanest discriminator the census offers: CommitCx, MacaroonTokenBytes, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest, PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent, ReplayArchiveLease. CommitCx is an asupersync capability context (see AGENTS.md doctrine 3) and is categorically not a durable format — it is the Cx the writer holds, mentioned in ordering prose. MacaroonTokenBytes and PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest are byte/digest value types. PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent and ReplayArchiveLease are named states/leases whose bytes live in another schema. AuthorityInstant and AuthorityInterval (3 and 2 members) are almost certainly wire types: they are time VALUES, inlined everywhere, with no lifecycle of their own.
