2 rows x 6 columns).

THE THREE DRIFTED CLAIMS

D1. L7 "covers all 294 Beads records". Declared floor 401, corpus 404 at the
    time of measurement (406 by the time this landed). The bead reported
    294-vs-364; both numbers had already moved again.

D2. L7 "The binding table and class counts are pinned." The binding table is
    still exact-pinned (binding_hash, equality). The five class counts became
    monotone FLOORS at 4a01ce8 earlier the same day. The sentence describes
    the design that commit falsified.  <- NOT IN THE BEAD, found by measuring.

D3. L14 source-block table, "Inclusive lines" for plan-reviewed-bibliography-v1
    read 3120-3123. Registry and the architecture.rs source_expected pin both
    say 3196-3199; the plan moved at bfdc44d. The other five cells of that row
    and all six of the other row were correct.  <- ALSO NOT IN THE BEAD.

WHY, IN ONE NUMBER

  docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md      1 commit  (f805ec7, its birth)
  registries/architecture_decisions.toml   48 commits
  tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs 51 commits

The control is exact: the two byte-compared siblings track their registries
1:1 -- THREAT doc 1 commit / threat_model.toml 1; TOPOLOGY 4 / 4. The
unchecked document was 1 / 48. It had never been edited since the day it was
written, because nothing ever asked it to move.

NOT MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE BY NATURE (4) -- named, and deliberately left alone

N1. L3 "This record freezes the reasoning that governs the architecture."
    Editorial framing. No artifact can contradict it.
N2. L5 "The source excerpts are historical evidence, not proof that an
    implementation or gate is complete." A negative epistemic disclaimer --
    nothing can falsify a statement about what is NOT proven.
N3. L5 "Time-sensitive market, foundation, and research statements retain
    their original review date." [[external_review_source]] rows carry dates,
    but no anchor binds an excerpt SENTENCE to a review row. Checkable only
    after such an anchor exists -- real work, belonging with the
    external-review chain, not something to fake here.
N4. L5 "changing one requires a fresh external-source review rather than
    silently rewriting the frozen rationale." A process obligation on humans.
    A checker can see that a row was added, never that a review happened.
    Asserting the row IS the review would be a check that cannot fail for the
    right reason -- worse than no check.

The regenerated document now SAYS N2-N4 are unchecked, in its own prose,
rather than presenting them as if something enforced them.

TRAP CHECK: is any drift a code bug wearing a doc bug's clothes?

No -- all three are genuine document drift and the code is right in each case.
But the NAIVE FIX was a code bug: rendering "all 401 Beads records" from the
registry would have reintroduced exactly the defect fgdb-lzol removed hours
earlier -- an equality over a shared, multi-writer corpus, stale again on the
next `br create`. The document therefore renders the PROPERTY the gate
enforces (bead_provenance_not_total: the closure is total) and renders the
five counts as FLOORS, labelled as floors.

Two doc claims I tried to break and could not:
  - "Each issue resolves through exactly one precedence tier" IS enforced --
    bead_override_shadowed and bead_family_ambiguous reject the two-match
    case; it is not first-match-wins.
  - "future orphan Bead fails the architecture gate" IS enforced by
    bead_provenance_not_total. The known orphan defect (7u5m) was a
    DIAGNOSTIC-MESSAGE gap, not an enforcement gap, so the sentence was true.

===========================================================================
2. WHAT WAS BUILT -- ONE READER, EXTENDED
===========================================================================

architecture.rs::validate_sources was already the ONLY reader of the document.
It still is. Added to the same module, copying the two siblings rather than
designing anything new:

  architecture.rs   generate_document() / check_document()
                    document_drift_violation() / document_generation_violation()
                    validate_document_glosses(), wired into validate_architecture
                    CATEGORY_GLOSS / RELATIONSHIP_GLOSS / PRECEDENCE_GLOSS
  bin               --write; drift is a violation (exit 1), not a load error
  check.sh:103      coverage label was "(CHECKED-SOURCE region)", now
                    "(generated document)" like its two siblings

No parallel doc-scanner. claims_lint.toml and lint.rs untouched -- pane3 owns
the marker-citation surface and landed docs/**.md in their own commit. Disjoint:
that closes citations, this closes content.

The three gloss tables are the mechanism that lets the prose state what it
binds without restating it: the phrases live in code, the membership lives in
the registry, and the guard requires them to be equal sets in BOTH directions.
Without it the table fails open -- a newly declared category simply would not
appear while the document went on claiming to cover the vocabulary.

===========================================================================
3. MUTATION PROOF -- five mutations, all FIRED, with named numbers
===========================================================================

M1  the pre-fix committed document, replayed through a depth-matched fixture
    root -> architecture_document_matches_registry FAILED. The other three
    document tests still PASSED: they test the generator, not the committed
    bytes, and that separation is the point.

M2  the generator silently stops rendering the floors table (source mutation)
    -> "the record stopped projecting 5 of 48 registry facts:
        [>=401, >=98, >=245, >=19, >=39]"
    THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A byte-compare CANNOT see M2: run --write
    and the document loses the table too, and the gate is green forever. That
    is the vacuity mode specific to a generated document, and it is why the
    accounting exists. 48 is pinned on BOTH halves -- the fact list is DERIVED
    from the registry, and every element must appear in the rendered bytes.

M3  validate_document_glosses not wired into validate_architecture
    -> expected "document_gloss_missing", got {"closed_set_mismatch"}. FAILED.

M4  a 13th category enters registry.allowed_categories (fixture registry)
    -> left: 49, right: 48. FAILED. The domain half of the accounting.

M5  check_document() always returns true (source mutation)
    -> "a hand-restored bead count must be rejected". FAILED. The negative
       fixture is not vacuous.

Inside architecture_neg_hand_edited_document_is_rejected, five on-disk
rejections are proved live: D1 (the 294 sentence restored), D2 ("pinned" for
the floors), D3 (the 3120-3123 range restored), a one-character edit inside a
frozen excerpt, and -- asked LAST, on purpose -- the weak truncation control.
An emptied file only proves the reader opens it, so it cannot stand in for the
four mutations inside regions the generator owns.

The operator-facing half is pinned too: the exact code (document_drift), its
contradiction class, and a message that must name both the document and the
--write repair command.

===========================================================================
4. GATES
===========================================================================

  cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   exit 0
  cargo fmt --check                            exit 0
  cargo check --all-targets                    PASS
  cargo test --workspace                       PASS
  file-coverage closure                        PASS (185 tracked)
  shell lint (bash -n + shellcheck)            PASS
  registered live gates                        19/19 on an uncontended run,
                                               including g0_architecture_decisions_e2e
  tests/architecture_decisions.rs              39 passed / 0 failed
  architecture-check --root .                  violations: 0, outcome: pass

One clippy red WAS mine and is fixed: manual_is_multiple_of in the thousands()
byte formatter, plus a doc_lazy_continuation on a doc comment.

UBS: the workspace-wide red is 937 critical over 113 FILES, the known
false-positive class. Attributed by line: of the citations in my three files,
exactly THREE fall inside my added ranges, and all three are one Info-level
"collect::<Vec<_>>() then for" observation on the strip-the-floors control.
Zero critical and zero warning are attributable to the 669 lines added here.

Also verified: all four g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh failure fixtures still
exit 1 with the exact codes that script asserts, and none of them gains a
document_drift. checker_index.toml needs no new row -- the architecture rows
are unit = "artifact", so the binary and test artifacts already cover this.

===========================================================================
5. TWO THINGS THE NEXT PANE SHOULD KNOW
===========================================================================

A. clippy verifies LOCK-FREE. Build slots were saturated for ~25 minutes and
   `cargo clippy` was unobtainable. clippy-driver needs no slot and no
   package-cache lock, exactly like the rustc recipe already in use:
     clippy-driver --edition 2024 -D warnings --crate-type rlib \
       --crate-name registry_check tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o /tmp/x.rlib
     clippy-driver --edition 2024 -D warnings --test --crate-name adr \
       tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs \
       --extern registry_check=/tmp/x.rlib -L /tmp -o /tmp/t
   Both found real -D warnings failures in seconds. This closes a gap: the
   lock-free recipe covered compile+test but not lint.

B. A check.sh run is NOT VALID across a concurrent commit. A run taken while
   HEAD moved 82e1a93 -> 0754359 showed 3 red registered gates (appendix_a
   binary: a cargo .fingerprint write race; g0_identity_e2e: another pane's
   dirty WIP; w1_cross_crate_determinism: the identity test). The uncontended
   run of the same tree had 19/19 green. Re-run before believing a red.

===========================================================================
6. FOLLOW-UP, filed separately, NOT done here
===========================================================================

The record still contains two statements that are true but bound only by
inspection: the list of what architecture-check enforces, and the list of gate
failure modes. Every clause of both was verified by hand today -- all ten map
to live violation codes -- but nothing holds them there. The strong version is
to let the record CITE violation codes and require every cited code to be one
the suite has WITNESSED FIRING, which would give
fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy a consumer. Only 12 of
architecture.rs's 105 codes are witnessed today, so that is its own bead.
close_reason: Measured 61 checkable claims: 58 true, 3 drifted (294-vs-401 bead count; 'pinned' after 4a01ce8 made the class counts floors; 3120-3123 vs 3196-3199 since bfdc44d -- the last two not in the bead). 4 statements are not mechanically checkable by nature and are named as such in the document rather than covered by a check that could not fail. Fix: the record is now generated from its registry by the SAME reader that already verified its excerpts, byte-compared, with --write. Five mutations proved both directions; the decisive one is that a generator dropping the floors table is invisible to a byte-compare, caught by projected-fact accounting pinned on both halves (5 of 48 / 49 != 48). Landed 60cb545. Follow-up fgdb-7cem.

title: Build registry-generated durable codecs, walkers, and golden corpora
description:
## What and scope

Implement the missing W1 owner repeatedly named as `w1-generated-parsers`: registry-generated, bounded canonical durable encoders and decoders; exact generated Rust tagged unions and reference wrappers; reachability, GC, checkpoint, backup, construction, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers; and the complete cross-version golden and mutation corpus for every frozen G0 identity, field, command, state, language, and format row. This is foundational format machinery, not the W10 import/export `fgdb-formats` surface and not W2 storage publication.

## Why

Gate G0 freezes every durable identity, field, tag, digest recipe, version law, and capability predicate before implementation. W1 must then make those registries executable without creating a second hand-maintained allowlist. The current graph and several descriptions refer to `w1-generated-parsers`, but no task owns it. Without an explicit owner, checker rows for generated encoder/decoder round trips and golden-corpus replay remain stubs, Appendix renderings can drift from Rust bytes, and later workstreams can invent local codecs. B1 requires one identity universe; B5 requires byte-replayable canonical semantics; both fail if registry rows and executable bytes are not in a total bijection.

## Normative design

The checked G0 registries and their checked-in schema annotations are the sole generator input. Generate exact Rust types and bounded canonical encoders/decoders for all five identity classes: content-addressed logical objects, physical records, bootstrap frames, restore-only prebootstrap artifacts, and inline wire types. Generate every `durable_fields.toml` field/tag, containing-schema-specific reference union, command/state arm, role/posture specialization, language-contract arm, and reserved-but-unavailable tag. No prose name, suffix, wildcard arm, generic `RegisteredStrongRef`, or manually duplicated list may grant encodability.

Generation emits deterministic checked-in artifacts and a regeneration manifest containing input registry hashes, generator version, output hashes, row counts, and ordered row-to-symbol mappings. CI regenerates into an isolated directory and byte-compares every output. Adding, retiring, or changing a row without the matching generated artifact and golden/mutation evidence fails. Reserved rows generate typed unavailable arms that can be decoded only under their registered compatibility rule and can never advertise a live capability.

Encoders use declared format major/minor, canonical little-endian fixed integers, canonical unsigned LEB128 only where registered, deterministic field order, checked arithmetic, length-before-allocation, per-kind resource bounds, and the pinned CanonicalScalarProfile. Decoders reject duplicate tags, noncanonical encodings, unknown required flags, retired or experimental production tags, illegal role/posture arms, cross-class references, missing required fields, trailing ambiguity, and resource claims before allocation. Additive-minor unknown fields are skipped only when the exact registered length-delimited compatibility rule permits it; breaking-major mismatches fail closed.

Generate exact reference and retention walkers from the field table, including strong, currently-followed conditional, weak identity, locator, archive/prior-incarnation, bootstrap-root, and W12 certified-remote semantics. Generate the concrete construction DAG for every command tag and activated state slot, not merely one family-level order. Generated checks reject self, mutual, future-result, role-invalid, missing/extra target, wrong-strength, and cross-consensus local-StrongRef edges.

Every digest field consumes one registered TargetDigest, TranscriptDigest, WeakIdentityDigest, or BodyDigest recipe. Encoder, decoder, field-table checker, golden-vector harness, and mutation corpus call the same generated include/exclude recipe. This task produces canonical plaintext and digest transcripts; W2 object identity supplies keyed ObjectId/CiphertextId/EncodingId/PlacementId cryptographic realization and publication, and must consume these generated bytes rather than re-encode them.

The generated code remains std-only except for the explicitly allowed foundation crates, uses Rust 2024 nightly, and has `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. It does not use serde, parser generators, proc-macro dependencies outside the closed universe, or host locale/tzdb.

## Invariants and interactions

Directly supports FG-INV-07 construction and registry closure, FG-INV-09 identity transcript recomputation, FG-INV-12 canonical value and representation equivalence, and FG-INV-19 replay artifact identity. A checker flips from stub to live only with its implementation and negative tests in the same change; no runtime capability activates merely because a codec exists.

Consumes the completed G0 epic, including the exhaustive Appendix A catalog, identity and durable-field registries, command/state contracts, language contracts, format arms, scalar/semantic profiles, and capability/activation rows. Produces the canonical format layer consumed by `fgdb-reference`, W2 Chronicle/ECS/bootstrap, every later durable subsystem, backup/restore, conformance, fuzzing, and replay. The W10 `fgdb-formats` task continues to own CSV/JSONL/Parquet-lite/Arrow/archive interchange projections, not these authoritative durable codecs.

## Acceptance criteria and tests

- A total two-way bijection proves every live or reserved registry row has exactly one generated type/field/arm/codec/walker entry and every generated entry resolves to exactly one row. Orphans, aliases, duplicate tags, wildcard arms, and hand-written extra variants fail.
- Regeneration from a clean checkout is byte-identical and emits a deterministic manifest with per-registry input hashes and per-output hashes.
- Cross-version golden vectors cover every identity class, top-level schema, inline type, union arm, field, command/state arm, reference wrapper, digest recipe, role/posture specialization, and unavailable reserved tag. Encode-decode-encode is byte-identical where accepted.
- Mutation/property suites remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, truncate, extend, corrupt, weaken, cross-role substitute, and cross-version substitute every normative field/arm/reference class and prove typed rejection. BodyDigest mutations name the exact recipe and mismatching byte offset.
- Fuzz targets cover every generated decoder and walker under adversarial lengths, varints, nesting, tags, and feature predicates; there are no panics, hangs, unchecked arithmetic paths, or allocations before validated limits.
- Construction and reachability tests compare generated DAG/walkers against the registry and Appendix rendering for every command tag and activated state slot.
- Locale, timezone, platform, target-endian, and iteration-order perturbations leave canonical bytes unchanged under the same pinned profiles.
- Checker-index rows `idr_generated_encoder_decoder_roundtrip` and `idr_golden_corpus_replay` become live only when the corresponding artifacts and negative tests land. The W2 identity checker remains stub until keyed cryptographic recomputation is implemented there.
- E2E script `scripts/w1_generated_formats_e2e.sh` regenerates into an isolated directory, byte-compares checked artifacts, compiles the generated types, replays every golden corpus, plants representative defects in temporary fixtures, and emits versioned JSONL. It exits on the first mismatch.
- Detailed JSONL includes event schema version, registry, row/schema/field/arm ID, format version, role/posture, input and output digest, resource bound, checker, outcome, mismatch offset, artifact references, deterministic seed, and replay command. Protected bytes and keys never enter logs.

## Risks and rejected alternatives

Rejected: hand-written codec inventories, serde-derived durable enums, generator output that is not reproducible, treating registry parse success as byte-level proof, delaying golden corpora until each engine subsystem, and making W10 interchange formats authoritative. Risk: the exhaustive G0 catalog is large; generation and corpus sharding must stay deterministic and independently replayable rather than weakening coverage.

## Provenance

Plan sections 5.1, 18.1, 19 W1; Appendix A canonical format rules; G0 epic identity/format clauses; the missing `w1-generated-parsers` references in the W1 epic and foundation-type interactions.
close_reason: Duplicate of fgdb-w1-generated-parsers-i3k; exhaustive corpus work is already owned by fgdb-w1-format-test-corpora-lyf. Additional audit requirements were preserved as comments on those canonical beads.

title: Epic G0: exact Appendix A durable-schema catalog and ownership closure
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the complete Appendix A durable-format contract as a set of exact, reviewable catalog slices and generate one closed schema-to-owner-to-checker matrix across them. The child tasks embed every source-plan byte from Appendix A and assign every schema, field, arm, reference, digest transcript, role restriction, state transition, and compatibility rule to its granular implementation bead. This epic is the constitutional format-closure proof; it does not replace subsystem implementation.

## Why
The audit found that architectural summaries were strong but exact type families could disappear between workstreams. Durable bytes are the public recovery/replay/compatibility contract, so “covered in spirit” is not enough. G0 must freeze even reserved W12 arms before Local implementation begins, while later workstreams retain phase-correct ownership.

## Design and ownership
The catalog is partitioned only for reviewability and CLI size. Concatenating its ordered slices exactly reconstructs Appendix A from the audited plan revision. Each slice generates rows in durable_fields.toml; the epic generates cross-slice reference DAG, state-transition, construction-order, authority-bearing, lifecycle-owner, compatibility, invariant/evidence/cost, verification, and gate-consumer matrices. Every row names one implementation owner and may name multiple consumers. Wildcards, “and similar,” unexpanded generic/role arms, bare StrongRef arrays, duplicate logical schema names, or aliases with different body hashes fail G0.

## Success Criteria
- Ordered child slices cover Appendix A continuously from its heading through the final transparency contract with no gap, overlap, truncation, or paraphrase.
- A checksum/line-range manifest proves exact reconstruction of the audited Appendix A text.
- Every exact named type/field/arm/state/transition/reference/digest/role constraint has a stable catalog row and exactly one implementation owner.
- Generated construction and reference DAGs are finite, role-correct, future-result-free, and closed across slices.
- Unit tests cover catalog parsing, stable IDs, generic/role expansion, ownership uniqueness, and exact reconstruction.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests reject missing/duplicate/reordered slices and fields, unknown arms, weakened references, cross-role substitutions, and digest drift.
- Simulation and E2E matrices map every durability/dispatch/recovery/authority boundary to task-specific scenarios and detailed redacted JSONL diagnostics with replay artifacts.
- Cross-version golden vectors and compatibility fixtures cover every durable schema; all downstream gates reject unowned or unchecked rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a single oversized CLI argument, summaries as normative bytes, and treating the catalog as one implementation task. The partition preserves exact content while keeping review and mutation reliable.

## Provenance
Complete normative Appendix A of the audited comprehensive plan.

comments.text:
G0 / APPENDIX A REALITY CHECK — measured against HEAD bdac80c, not impression. Every count below survived a positive control; where I could not control something I say so. Probed a fresh checkout of HEAD, never the working tree (cc_1 holds catalog and is mid-edit), and rebuilt the registry_check rlib fresh because a stale one bakes in EXPECTED_* and reports violations against correct data.

=== 1. WHERE THE 21 SLICES ACTUALLY STAND ===

  slices at definition_status=complete .... 0 of 21
  slices with >=1 landed target ........... 13 of 21
  slices with ZERO landed rows ............  8 of 21  (a05, a08, a09, a12, a13, a14, a18, a21)

Census coverage across all 21 slices:
  field keys            11,683   of which     622 covered ( 5.3%),  11,061 uncovered (94.7%)
  uncovered unions         523
  uncovered arms         1,556
  unadjudicated ambigs   8,034
  landed targets           549   (514 across a01-a21 + 35 owned by the g0 slice)
CONTROL on the coverage predicate: per-slice targeted field counts must sum to the catalog's own field| target total. 210 = 210, PASS. Without that reconciliation every number here would be untrustworthy — my first attempt at this predicate under-reported by keying on schema_family instead of schema_owner.

REMAINING COVERAGE ITEMS PER SLICE (uncovered fields + unions + arms + unadjudicated ambiguities), ascending — this is the honest ranking of 'closeness':
  a01     6          a02    28          a11   191          a14   231
  a10   240          a09   326          a20   345          a13   422
  a12   439          a04   523          a06   762          a05 1,341
  a03 1,394          a16 1,528          a17 1,599          a21 1,757
  a19 1,912          a07 1,796          a15 2,020          a08 1,995
  a18 2,319
There is a CLIFF after a02. a01 and a02 are within reach; the third-closest slice is 30x further out than a01. Any plan that assumes the lane is uniformly ~60% done is wrong: it is two slices nearly coverage-complete and nineteen barely started.

=== 2. WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS TO CLOSE ONE SLICE — MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED ===

I flipped a01 (the closest slice, 6 residual coverage items) to definition_status=complete in a scratch copy and let the checker enumerate the bill. It does not load: 1,138 violations.
    227  complete_slice_annotation_missing
    227  complete_slice_semantic_binding_missing
    227  complete_slice_static_evidence_missing
    227  complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing
    227  complete_slice_target_declared
      2  complete_slice_source_contract_unverified
      1  slice_census_pin_mismatch
THE HEADLINE: a01's visible residual is 6 items. Its actual last mile is ~1,138, i.e. roughly 190x the visible number, and 1,135 of those are PER-TARGET work over 227 targets. I had previously costed this layer at 4 rows per target; the measurement shows FIVE actions — the four metadata rows plus flipping each target off definition_status=declared, which complete_slice_target_declared enforces and which nobody has mentioned on any trail.
Good news buried in it: only 2 complete_slice_source_contract_unverified remain, so the union/arm source-checker gap that blocked a01 in July is essentially closed by 2C's coverage generalization. That was the historic blocker and it is no longer the binding one.

=== 3. STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS RANKED BY BREADTH — THE SEQUENCING ANSWER ===

  iz2x  (annotation/semantic-binding/evidence layer)  blocks 21 of 21 slices.  MEASURED: annotations 0,
        semantic_bindings 0, evidence 0, expansion_bindings 0 catalog-wide. No slice can reach complete
        without it, unconditionally. It is the universal gate.
  u3gr  (self-referencing retaining wrappers)         blocks  7 of 21 slices, 10 members.  MEASURED with
        both known errata as passing controls: a03 LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration; a06 MetaPreparedCommandRecord,
        ShardPreparedPayloadRecord; a08 MetaConstraintReservationRecord, ShardPrepareRecord,
        TopologyTransitionRecord; a10 PreparedCommitRecord; a13 KeyEnvelopeNode;
        a16 TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>; a21 WitnessPolicy. a04 screened CLEAN.
  ovok  (indexed-map union spelling)                  NOT MEASURED — see section 4.
  owlp  (latent order violations)                     NOT MEASURABLE until field bodies land, by its own
        definition. It is a future-detection gap, not a present blocker.

SEQUENCING CONCLUSION, and it is not the obvious one. iz2x has by far the widest reach, but it CANNOT simply be done first: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so every target minted later needs its own four rows anyway. Doing iz2x before a slice's coverage is complete means editing the same rows twice. The critical path is therefore per-slice: coverage -> then iz2x for that slice -> then complete. What iz2x genuinely blocks TODAY is only a01 and a02, because they are the only slices whose coverage is near done. So the highest-value sequencing is: freeze the iz2x row schemas and pin mechanics ONCE now (cheap, one reviewed increment, no rows), then let it be applied per-slice as each slice's coverage closes. Freezing it late, after ~2,000 rows exist across slices, is a mass migration. Freezing it now costs one increment.
u3gr is second: 7 slices, and unlike iz2x it is a SOURCE erratum — the plan spells something unlandable — so it needs a spec decision, not catalog work, and it will silently block those 7 slices at their last mile regardless of how much coverage they accumulate first.

=== 4. WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT IN A POSITION TO JUDGE ===
 - ovok's breadth. I did not measure it. I know the shape (indexed-map union spelling leaving an unsatisfiable order) but not which slices carry it, and I will not guess a number into an epic assessment.
 - Whether the plan can be errata'd at all for u3gr's 10 members. That is a spec-owner decision about the normative source; I can only say the two laws are jointly unsatisfiable as spelled.
 - Whether the iz2x annotation layer is genuinely GENERATABLE. I proposed generating annotations from the census (source_annotation_contract_mismatch already forces them to byte-match census exact_type/cardinality, which strongly suggests derivability) but I have NOT proven it by building a generator. Semantic bindings and evidence are definitely not derivable — they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs.
 - Any runtime or implementation readiness. G0 is the format freeze; W1-W12 execution is entirely outside what I measured. Nothing here says whether the database works.
 - Calendar or effort estimates. I have no throughput data I trust. I can say a01 is ~1,138 checker-enumerated items from complete; I cannot say how long that takes, and the per-item cost is very uneven (a generated annotation is not comparable to a hand-authored evidence row).
 - The 8 zero-target slices. I measured their census sizes but have not read their source, so I cannot say whether they are large-but-mechanical or genuinely hard.

=== BOTTOM LINE ===
Gate G0 is roughly 5% through its census coverage with zero slices complete, and the last mile per slice is ~190x its visible residual because the annotation/evidence layer has never been started anywhere. The two things worth doing before more slices accumulate rows are (a) freeze the iz2x row schemas and pin mechanics in one reviewed increment, and (b) get a spec decision on u3gr's 10 members, because both get monotonically more expensive with every target that lands.

comments.text:
STRUCTURAL FINDING, EPIC-LEVEL: THE COMPLETION LAW IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE FOR ANY SHORTHAND MEMBER THE PLAN DOES NOT TYPE INLINE. This is not a01-local and no amount of ruling or adjudicating can clear it. Found while designing a disambiguation rule for a01's 74 non-exact sources; the rule turned out to be the wrong deliverable.

=== THE MECHANISM, verbatim (appendix_a.rs:7418) ===
    let source_is_exact = ambiguity_is_discharged
        && !field.type_conflict
        && matches!(field.exact_types.as_slice(), [_])
        && matches!(field.cardinalities.as_slice(), [_]);
    if !source_is_exact {
        if target.definition_status == "complete" {
            out.push(... "source_annotation_contract_ambiguous" ...)
        }
        continue;
    }
matches!(x, [_]) requires EXACTLY ONE element. Measured over a01: all 74 non-exact field targets have signature (0 exact_types, 1 cardinality) - zero types, not competing types. So the third conjunct is false and source_is_exact is false. The first conjunct, ambiguity_is_discharged, IS satisfiable by a maps-to-source adjudication - and a01 has already landed exactly such adjudications for five of these members in 2H - but discharging the ambiguity does not SUPPLY a type. An adjudication clears field.ambiguous; it cannot make exact_types non-empty.

CONSEQUENCE: a field target whose plan text gives no inline type can never be part of a complete slice. The plan will not grow inline types by itself, so this is permanent until something changes in (a), (b) or (c) below.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT a01-LOCAL ===
These are shorthand members - the "shorthand field has no exact type" census class. a01 has 74 of them among its field TARGETS alone, and a01 is the most-covered slice in the catalog. Every slice that lands field targets over prose-rendered schemas will accumulate them. My earlier reality check said the completion layer was the universal blocker; this is a second universal blocker sitting behind it, and unlike the annotation layer it cannot be discharged by doing more work at the slice level.

=== IT IS THE u3gr PATTERN AT COMPLETION SCOPE ===
u3gr is two laws jointly unsatisfiable for one member shape (reference_semantics forced strong by the source wrapper, dag_self_edge forbidding it). This is the same shape one level up: the annotation contract demands a census exact_type, the census cannot produce one for a shorthand member, and the adjudication mechanism that exists to resolve exactly this class does not feed the predicate that consumes it. Both are "the catalog is internally consistent and the goal state is unreachable".

=== THE THREE POSSIBLE RESOLUTIONS, and my read ===
 (a) PLAN ERRATUM adding inline types for every shorthand member. Correct in principle, enormous in practice (74 in a01 alone, likely many hundreds catalog-wide), and it puts normative-source edits on the critical path for a format freeze. I do not recommend it.
 (b) LET AN ADJUDICATION SUPPLY THE TYPE. The natural fix and the smallest: extend the maps-to-source adjudication row (or add a sibling row kind) to carry the ruled exact_type, and have source_is_exact accept an adjudicated type where the census has none. This preserves every guarantee that matters - the type is still recorded, reviewed, pinned and byte-matched against the annotation - while making the goal state reachable. It also retroactively validates the 2G/2H pattern, where a01 already ruled five such members from landed precedent and pinned the rulings.
 (c) WEAKEN THE COMPLETION LAW to accept a zero-type census source. Worst option: it drops the byte-match that currently prevents an annotation from silently disagreeing with the source.
My recommendation is (b), and it is checker/scaffold work, not slice work. It should be decided before any slice invests in the annotation layer, because (b) changes what an annotation row must contain.

=== WHAT I MEASURED ALONG THE WAY, still useful under (b) ===
Of a01's 74 untyped members, 47 are DETERMINED by unanimous catalog-wide name-family precedent and 27 are not; zero have no precedent at all. The derived rule, where precedent is unanimous:
  *_bytes -> bytes    *_commitment -> digest256   *_coverage -> bytes    *_domain -> ConsensusDomain
  *_domains -> bytes  *_epoch -> u64              *_floor -> u64         *_index -> u64
  *_key -> id256      *_nonce -> bytes            *_oid -> oid256        *_proof -> bytes
  *_set -> bytes      *_signatures -> bytes       *_threshold -> u16     *_zeroes -> bytes
The 27-item residue is dominated by three split families, each with a KNOWN discriminator rather than genuine doubt: *_digest splits 32 digest256 vs 3 WeakDigest (discriminator: WeakDigest iff the member points at a concrete target schema, digest256 otherwise - the ruling a01 already made in 2G); *_identity splits 11 RemoteObjectIdentity vs 3 (RemoteObjectIdentity where the source spells it); *_id splits across id256/digest256/bytes (grant_id already ruled digest256 in 2B as an H() output). So under (b) the 74 would be roughly 47 mechanical + 27 precedent-guided, not 74 hand decisions. That is the rule the operator asked for - it exists and it is cheap - but it cannot be applied until (b) makes an adjudicated type mean anything to the checker.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===
I have not measured how many shorthand members exist in the other 20 slices, only that a01 has 74 among its targets and that nothing about the mechanism is a01-specific. I have also not verified that (b) is implementable without disturbing the existing adjudication pin mechanics; that is for whoever owns the checker.

SWEEP FOR UNSATISFIABLE COMPLETION LAWS — result: ONE NEW INSTANCE, making FOUR in the class. Read-only against HEAD. No remedy proposed as authorized.

METHOD: enumerated every law gated on definition_status == "complete" (12 codes), characterized the input signature each demands, then measured whether any real population can present it. Where possible I measured EMPIRICALLY by flipping a slice to complete in a scratch copy and reading what the checker emits, rather than reasoning from the source alone.

=== NEW INSTANCE #4: A SLICE OWNING A projection| FALLBACK TARGET CAN NEVER COMPLETE ===

MECHANISM, appendix_a.rs:11109 and :11126, both inside the same `for row in closure_targets` loop over EVERY target of a complete slice:
    if row.definition_status != "complete" {
        out.push("complete_slice_target_declared", ... "complete slice contains a target that is still declared")
    }
    let source_contract_supported = row.source_key.starts_with("top|")
        || row.source_key.starts_with("field|")
        || (row.target_kind == "union" && row.source_key.starts_with("union|"))
        || (row.target_kind == "union-arm" && row.source_key.starts_with("arm|"))
        || ordinary_union_wire_source_supported;
    if !source_contract_supported {
        out.push("complete_slice_source_contract_unverified", ...
            "...reference-only and projection fallback targets remain declared")
    }
A source_key of the form projection|... matches none of the five accepted prefixes. Critically the second check is NOT gated on the target's own status, so:
  - leave the target declared -> complete_slice_target_declared fires
  - flip the target to complete -> complete_slice_source_contract_unverified STILL fires
Either way the slice cannot be complete. The law's own message says such targets "remain declared", which is precisely the state the sibling law forbids inside a complete slice. This is the u3gr shape - two laws jointly unsatisfiable - lifted to slice-completion scope.

MEASURED POPULATION: 98 targets across 12 slices (551 targets total; source_key forms are top 134, field 210, projection 84, arm 91, union 32).
    g0 35   a04 16   a10 12   a15 9   a06 6   a02 3   a03 3   a19 3   a17 4   a20 4   a01 2   a07 1
EMPIRICAL CONTROL, two independent slices, both exact: flipping a01 to complete emits exactly 2 complete_slice_source_contract_unverified against a predicted 2; flipping a04 emits exactly 16 against a predicted 16. So the ordinary_union_wire_source_supported escape rescues ZERO of them, and the static count is trustworthy.

CAN AN ADJUDICATION OR RULING CLEAR IT? PROVABLY NOT, and this is worse than the zero-exact-type case. That one at least consults adjudications (ambiguity_is_discharged is a real conjunct, it simply cannot supply a missing type). Here the test is a pure structural match on the source_key PREFIX with no adjudication, ruling, or override consulted anywhere in the expression. The only way to satisfy it is for the target to stop being a projection| fallback, i.e. to acquire a real source construct - and the fallback exists precisely because the projection row has none. Note also that the e2e's phase 3e asserts every checked-in projection requires one target, so the fallback target cannot simply be deleted while its projection row exists.

=== LAWS SWEPT AND FOUND SATISFIABLE (they demand work, not impossibilities) ===
  complete_slice_target_missing (11057)          needs >=1 target. trivial.
  complete_top_level (11087)                     census pin over top-level keys; satisfiable by targeting or
                                                 not-a-durable-schema adjudication.
  complete_ambiguity_adjudication (11100)        census pin; satisfiable by adjudicating all slice ambiguities.
  complete_slice_annotation_missing (11137)      needs one annotation per target. work, not impossible.
  complete_slice_semantic_binding_missing (11150) same shape.
  complete_slice_static_evidence_missing (11161)  same shape.
  complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing (11172) same shape.
  source_complete_census_uncovered (7182)        every census key targeted, adjudicated, or arm/wire-covered.

  source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved (7311) one approved final adjudication per raw ambiguity, no extras.
                                                 a01 is at 2 outstanding, so approachable.

My empirical flip test only exercises LOAD-TIME laws. When a slice is flipped to complete the catalog fails to load, so verify_source never runs and the two source-pass laws (7182, 7311) were characterized by reading the source only, not by measurement. I judge them satisfiable from their predicates and from a01's approach to zero, but I have not proven it the way I proved the projection| case. IS INSTANCE #4 A CHECKER GAP OR A REAL CONTRADICTION? ANSWER: BOTH, IN MEASURED PROPORTIONS — and the 98 is three different problems wearing one violation code. Your instinct that "projection is absent from the accepted list, not rejected by a rule" is correct for part of it and wrong for the majority.

=== THE 98 DECOMPOSES THREE WAYS ===

  (A) 14 targets — DEFINITE CHECKER GAP, no owner decision needed.
      source_key is a REAL census arm key but target_kind is "wire-type", e.g.
        arm|KeyDestroyExternalAckRef|KeyDestroyExternalAckRef|Backup      (a15, x8)
        arm|NewDatabaseIdentityTargetCreationCommitment|...|Dir            (a19, x2)
        arm|ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind|...|CatalogActivate      (a20, x4)
      The law accepts arm| ONLY when target_kind == "union-arm":
          || (row.target_kind == "union-arm" && row.source_key.starts_with("arm|"))
      These are the per-arm WIRE VARIANT rows — the a15 KeyDestructionTarget pattern the a01 2C trail
      documented as an approved shape. The source contract exists and is a plain census arm key; the
      vocabulary simply does not admit the (arm| source, wire-type target) pairing. This is exactly the
      unimplemented case you described, and we can fix it ourselves.

  (B) 25 of the 84 projection| targets — PROBABLE CHECKER GAP, needs per-case confirmation.
      16 have BOTH owner and member present in Appendix A text; 9 have the owner present but not the
      member. So there is plan text to reconcile against; whether it is reconcilable in the census's
      terms I have not established per row.

  (C) 59 of the 84 — GENUINELY SOURCELESS, and NOT a plan erratum either.
      The symbol does not occur anywhere in Appendix A. The dominant sub-class is REGISTRY-INVENTED
      ROLE SPECIALIZATIONS: RaftSnapshotLocal / RaftSnapshotMeta / RaftSnapshotShard,
      RootManifestMeta / RootManifestShard, CheckpointStateVectorMeta / CheckpointStateVectorShard.
      The plan spells a SINGLE role-tagged construct; the registry created one kind per role. The a04
      pre-work brief flagged this same divergence independently ("logical_object_kinds has RootManifest
      0x0007 active + RootManifestMeta/Shard 0x0104/0x0105 ... while a04 reserves single role-tagged
      RaftSnapshot"). Others are registrar-named constructs: SegmentTrailer, whose name cc_1 explicitly
      recorded as a naming ruling because "the source supplies NO name".
      For these, projection| is the HONEST source key — it correctly says "this row has no source". The
      law then correctly refuses to call such a target source-reconciled. Nothing is contradictory; the
      registry contains rows the plan does not.

=== SO WHAT IS THE ACTUAL DECISION? ===
Not "erratum vs checker fix". It is: MAY A SLICE CONTAIN REGISTRY-INVENTED ROWS AND STILL BE COMPLETE?
If yes, the completion law needs a sanctioned category for source-free registry rows. If no, those rows
must move somewhere that is not a completing slice — note g0 already holds 35 of the 98, the largest
single holding, so segregating registry-infrastructure rows into a non-completing owner is a shape the
catalog already partly uses. That is a registry-modeling question for the owner, and it is a different
question from u3gr.

=== DO THE FOUR SHARE ONE ROOT CAUSE? NO — THEY ARE THREE DIFFERENT MISMATCHES ===
All four are "the law set assumes something about the source that is not true", but the DIRECTION differs,
and the direction determines the fix and the owner:
  u3gr              the SOURCE CONTAINS a construct no legal row shape can express     -> source erratum, owner
  zero-exact-type   the SOURCE OMITS information a law requires (types)                -> owner: erratum vs relax the test
  #4 part (C)       the REGISTRY CONTAINS rows the source does not                     -> registry-modeling, owner
  #4 parts (A)+(B)  the VOCABULARY omits a form both source and registry already use   -> checker fix, ours
  dbvf              a missing lifecycle law, plus a transient that self-resolves        -> checker fix, ours
So the owner is deciding about THREE things, not four and not one: (1) u3gr, (2) the zero-exact-type test,
(3) whether registry-invented rows may live in a completing slice. Items (A), (B) and dbvf are ours to fix
without escalation — that removes 14 targets definitely and up to 25 more probably, i.e. up to 39 of the 98,
and it unblocks nothing on its own because most affected slices hold rows in category (C) as well.

=== METHOD NOTE, because it nearly produced a wrong headline ===
My first run of this measurement reported 68 of 84 absent from the plan. That was FALSE. I had written
r'\\b' inside a raw string, so the regex matched a literal backslash followed by 'b' and never matched
anything. The positive control caught it instantly: ConfigurationState and RootSlot both reported "absent"
when both are demonstrably in Appendix A. Corrected escaping gives 16 / 9 / 59 with the control reading
in / in / out as expected. Ninth instance today of "the tool reported OK because it was never asked the
right question" — and the first where the broken tool was the measurement I was about to escalate.

For every violation code C the checker can emit, BOTH must exist and be exhibited:

=== WHAT A SATISFYING WITNESS LOOKS LIKE, CONCRETELY ===
Take dag_self_edge, one of the five instances. Trigger: a field row whose target_schema_id equals its
containing kind. Satisfying witness: a field row that IS a retaining self-reference in the SOURCE and still
lands — and you cannot write one, because catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch forces "strong" and
dag_self_edge forbids it. The harness fails at authoring time, in one file, with the two law names in the
error. That is u3gr found in minutes by construction instead of in a multi-tick investigation.
Same for the pair I filed today: ordinary_union_field_mismatch's satisfying witness needs an embedded union
whose anchor field row is legal, and for a WIRE host no such row exists because :1558's resolves disjunction
omits wire. Authoring the witness surfaces the disjointness immediately.

=== DECLARED EXEMPTIONS, WITH REASONS, RATHER THAN SILENT GAPS ===
Some codes should be exempt and the exemption should be a data row with a reason, in the same spirit as the
unsafe-boundary ledger:
  * the 11 completion codes — EXEMPT UNTIL [III] RESOLVES, reason recorded, and the exemption itself becomes
    the tracking artifact for [III]. When [III] lands, the exemption is removed and the witnesses must exist.
  * registry_assignment_drift / registry_epoch_mismatch — their satisfying state is "the live catalog", which
    the whole gate already asserts continuously; a synthetic witness adds nothing.
  * bodydigest_pin_mismatch — the satisfying witness is a live recomputed pin, already covered by the
    BODY_RECIPES block in g0_identity_e2e.sh.
Everything else should carry a witness or an explicit, reasoned exemption. No silent absences — that is the
same principle as making the awk fixtures print what they expected to find.

=== HONEST ASSESSMENT OF COVERAGE ===
37 of 65 codes (~57%) are mechanically witnessable from small synthetic fixtures and cover the two families
where every instance found today lives — dag_ and the union/arm families. 5 bodydigest codes are harder but
tractable. 11 completion codes cannot be witnessed at all today, and that fact is itself the highest-value
output. 10 misc codes need per-code triage before I would promise anything; I have not read them all and will
not claim otherwise. So a first cut covering dag_ + ordinary_union_* + union_arm_* + union_ is 27 codes, is
where all five instances live, and is worth building before the remaining 38 are triaged.

=== WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT MOVE, IN THE OPERATOR'S OWN TERMS ===
cc_1 made the pin sites DERIVE instead of re-copying literals, and made the fixtures PRINT instead of exiting
silently. Both killed a class. This is the third of the same kind: assert that every law is PASSABLE, not
merely reachable. Five instances found by hand across two law families in one day is the evidence that
hand-finding does not scale; the sixth is presumably already in the 38 codes I did not sweep.

=== WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED ===
Whether the harness can share fixture infrastructure with the existing identity tests (I have not read their
fixture builders in enough detail), the real cost of authoring 27 satisfying witnesses, and whether any
mechanical family hides a code whose satisfying witness is expensive for a reason I have not anticipated.
This is a design, not an estimate.

comments.text:
METHOD NOTE — HOW THE NUMBERS ON THIS TRAIL WERE MADE CORRECT. Everything measured is on beads; this is the part a successor cannot reconstruct from the numbers.

=== THE CONTROL PATTERN, STATED GENERALLY ===
Every probe must, IN THE SAME RUN, demonstrate a known-present case AND reject a fabricated one. Not one or
the other, and not in a previous run. A probe that only reports its answer is an untested instrument, and a
near-zero answer from an untested instrument is indistinguishable from a broken one.
  Exemplar 1: before believing which targets lack a census key, assert that every target ALREADY keyed
              resolves — 344 found / 0 NOT FOUND. A single miss would have invalidated the whole result.
  Exemplar 2: before believing which symbols are absent from the plan, assert ConfigurationState and
              RootSlot read PRESENT and a fabricated name reads ABSENT. This caught a regex that matched
              nothing, in a measurement I was one step from escalating.
The pattern generalises past probes: a detector you just wrote is an untrusted tool too, and the first thing
to test it against is output you already know is good. My damage-scan for eaten backticks flagged 16/9/8/4
"hits" that were entirely my own column-aligned tables.

=== THE SPECIFIC TRAPS, EACH OF WHICH COST REAL TIME ===
 1. TEXT PRESENCE IS NOT A CENSUS KEY. A symbol rendered only as an inline nested brace emits no key at all.
    ContiguousSpan is written at a01:1443 and a02:1449 and has none. Cost: category (B) reported as 25; the
    census-term answer is 1.
 2. SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT PRODUCES FALSE POSITIVES. MetaAppliedResultRef contains MetaAppliedResult; a plain
    `in` test conflates a generated reference-union name with the domain concept it was derived from.
 3. r'\\b' IN A RAW STRING MATCHES A LITERAL BACKSLASH, not a word boundary. Reported 68 of 84 symbols absent
    from the plan. Never reported onward — the control caught it.
 4. A WITNESS GENERATED FROM THE SAME CODE PATH THE LAW USES PROVES NOTHING. Witnesses must be independent
    hand-authored data. The same applies to ratchets: extract codes from the checker SOURCE, not from a list
    the checker also consumes.
 5. A DERIVATION THAT LOOKS MECHANICAL IS NOT SYNTHESIZED IF THE SOURCE SPELLS IT OUT. I expected
    WithoutId/WithoutDigest to be a generator rule; it accounted for ZERO rows, because
    CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest is written at a02:1449 and therefore gets a census key.
 6. A PROBE WHOSE SCOPE COVERS A DIFFERENT POPULATION THAN THE BUCKET YOU ARE CLASSIFYING WILL SILENTLY
    MIS-COUNT. R4 came out as 23 instead of 5 because I tested owner presence with a TEXT probe while the
    bucket was defined census-side — two messages after making that exact distinction the headline of a
    correction. Knowing a trap is not the same as having tooling that cannot fall into it.
 7. A CONTROL MUST EXERCISE THE CASE YOU ARE GENERALISING ABOUT. a01 (2/2) and a04 (16/16) were real controls
    that contained none of the 14 rows I then generalised to. Two passing controls, wrong conclusion.
 8. NEVER TRUNCATE A TOOL WHOSE OUTPUT IS THE ANSWER. `beads_safe_to_commit.sh | tail -1` shows the guidance
    line, not the classification. That is how I put main red for ~15 minutes by committing a created bead
    without its pin re-freeze.

=== THE UNIFYING SHAPE ===
Every one of ten instances today was a SUCCESS SIGNAL CONFLATED WITH A CORRECTNESS SIGNAL — an exit status, a
"Comment added", a green loader, a fresh-looking binary. Each is real evidence that SOMETHING completed; none
is evidence the RIGHT thing completed. The habit that catches all of them: after any operation, ask "what
would I observe if this had silently done nothing?" and go look for exactly that.

=== WHAT I WOULD TELL THE NEXT AGENT TO DISTRUST FIRST ===
Your own most recent correction. The two worst errors on this trail were both committed inside classifiers I
had just built to exploit a distinction I had just established and written up — the freshly-learned lesson
creates confidence without creating tooling, and that gap is where the error lands. Re-run the control on the
instrument you built to avoid the mistake you just made.

THE ESCAPE TEST — banking this because it is tacit, it cost me a full increment to learn, and it should cost the next agent nothing.

RULE: before designing ANY vocabulary widening (a new disjunct in an accepted-prefix or source-contract law), first test whether the rows you intend to admit are ALREADY admitted by an existing escape. Do it BEFORE the design, not after building and gating one.

HOW: the law that matters is usually gated behind slice completeness and therefore dormant (zero slices are complete today), so it cannot fire on the live tree. Arm it in a scratch copy — `git archive HEAD` into a temp dir, flip only the owning slice's definition_status from declared to complete, rebuild the rlib, and read which row_ids the loader names for your violation code. Split on '\n[[' and edit the block rather than regexing, because slice rows contain '[' inside expected_projection_classes.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE TWO MINUTES: it discriminates rather than just being cheap. The same test in one session killed category (A) and validated R1.
  * Category (A), 14 arm|/wire-type target rows: armed a15 fired complete_slice_source_contract_unverified EXACTLY ONCE, naming a15:prebootstrap-kind:wrapped-key-artifact and none of the 14. They already pass via the fifth disjunct ordinary_union_wire_source_supported, which consults the projection instead of matching a prefix. My proposed sixth disjunct would have admitted NOTHING. I had already built, pin-chased and gated that increment.
  * R1, 13 generated reference-union rows: arming a04/a06/a10 fired on all 10 non-g0 rows, so they are genuinely rejected and R1 is real work. The remaining 3 are g0, which is not a [[slice]] and can never be armed — matching cod_1's independent finding that all 10 g0 rows are structurally exempt.

THE FAILURE MODE IT PREVENTS, stated precisely because my own controls did not catch it: I verified the COUNT of rows matching one clause of the disjunction, in both directions, and the count was correct. I never evaluated the FULL disjunction those rows are tested against, so I reported a clause-level measurement as a verdict. "How many rows would this clause admit" is not "how many rows are currently rejected". A positive control on a predicate cannot tell you the predicate is the operative one — control the QUESTION, not only the measurement. Related tell: I noticed the pin cascade would be empty and read that as the change being cheap; it was actually the change being inert.

title: Scaffold the canonical Appendix A annotation catalog and generated identity projections
description:
## What & scope
Land the shared G0 catalog infrastructure that every Appendix A slice A01-A21 requires before substantive rows can be added. The canonical machine-readable source is one checked-in `registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml` containing the complete 21-slice manifest plus 21 explicit logical slice sections and the structured schema annotations needed to regenerate all identity projections. The existing logical/physical/bootstrap/prebootstrap/wire/durable-field TOMLs remain checked-in normative projections for consumers, never independently hand-authored authorities.

## Why
The Appendix epic partitions one exact contract into 21 reviewable slices, but all slices need the same stable row-ID grammar, source pins, type-ID census, generator, owner/reference closure, and projection-diff check. Making each slice invent that substrate duplicates authority and creates conflicts; making identity own it recreates the dependency cycle because identity depends on the completed Appendix epic.

## Design
`appendix_a_catalog.toml` contains one source manifest (plan path, Appendix range/hash, exact ordered A01-A21 ranges/counts/hashes/adjacency) and structured annotations grouped into 21 logical slice sections. Annotations cover schema/field/arm IDs, class/tags, exact types/cardinality/layout, role/posture/authority/locality, reference/cut/construction semantics, generic and role expansions, digest recipes, ownership/consumers, compatibility, checker/scenario/gate bindings, and declared/complete state. One shared generator/checker in the existing registry-check surface emits and byte-diffs `logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml`, `wire_types.toml`, and `durable_fields.toml`. `durable_fields.toml` remains the sole downstream input to generated reachability/GC/checkpoint/backup/DAG/compatibility/size/fuzz walkers; they never reinterpret the source catalog. Use std-only SHA-256 with standard vectors for source pins; retain FNV only for noncryptographic assignment fingerprints. No per-slice checker modules, binaries, tests, or E2E scripts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Strict schema/version/unknown-key validation for the catalog, manifest, slice, annotation, binding, and status rows.
- Exact raw-UTF8-LF SHA-256 proof of Appendix A lines 1384-2654 and all 21 contiguous ordered slices; missing, duplicate, reordered, overlapping, gapped, truncated, off-by-one, wrong-hash, or wrong-Bead mutations fail.
- One stable row-ID grammar and full top-level type/code reservation census allow declared cross-slice references without wildcards; complete slices require all concrete fields/arms/rules.
- Deterministic generation and byte-diff of all six checked-in projections; repeated generation is byte-identical and reports first file/line/byte divergence.
- Cross-slice exact-owner, owner-Bead/crate, reference, role/generic expansion, construction-DAG, compatibility, checker/scenario/gate, and planned/live evidence closure; no residual `<T>`, `<Role>`, generic StrongRef, fallback owner, or unresolved arm.
- Existing identity tests and G0 identity E2E cover source reconstruction, generation diff, ownership, cross-slice closure, mutation corpus, deterministic redacted JSONL, and SHA-256 vectors; scripts/check.sh runs the gate.
- This scaffold proves static catalog infrastructure only. Runtime codecs, goldens, simulation, recovery, public protocols, and later W12 behavior remain mandatory under their named downstream owners and do not block G0 definition.

## Provenance
Plan §5.1 annotation/generation law; complete normative Appendix A; Bead fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-91ol.
