title: a10: SequenceNeutralSpec is reserved with 0 arms and none of its 13 named inputs has a schema — the real block under 5uw2/d2ax
description:
## CORRECTED. I filed this bead 30 minutes ago with "0 outer role-command unions
## exist". That claim was mine, it was name-based, and it is FALSE.

Re-derived at HEAD 650c37d under a held catalog lease. The earlier number came
from searching union NAMES for `Command|Transition|LifecycleOperation|Maintenance`
-- inferring absence from spelling, which is the same move plan 5.1 forbids when
it says "a suffix conveys no semantics". The outer command types are not spelled
with "Command" in the place I looked.

## What is actually in the catalog for a10

  logical_kind rows, slice_id = "a10"  (6)
     CommitCommand              ACTIVE
     ControlCommand             ACTIVE
     LogicalCommandRecord       ACTIVE
     PreparedCommitRecord       ACTIVE
     CommittedEffectCapsule     reserved
     SequenceNeutralSpec        RESERVED
  union rows (1)     ExpectedStateCondition, version_status "reserved", 4 arms,
                     allowed_containing_schemas ["ControlCommand","KeyDestroyProposal"]
  plus              wire_type 5, field 17, reference_union 1 (+2 arms),
                    reservation 14, top_level_candidate 18, target 36,
                    source_symbol_disposition 14, ambiguity_adjudication 1

So four outer command schemas are ACTIVE. a10 is partially landed, not untouched.

## The real blocker, in one line

The outer union the 5.1 bijection quantifies over is `SequenceNeutralSpec`, it is
`status = "reserved"`, and it has ZERO union_arm rows. `GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec`
is likewise a reserved logical_kind with no arms.

Plan line ~1915 (a10's own source) names the required arms outright:

  "Required Local semantic rows include TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec<Local>,
   TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec<Local>, every AllocationReservationTransitionSpec
   <Local> and FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec<Local>, FormatTransitionSpec
   <Local>, EscrowRightsTransitionSpec, PrivacyContinuityImportSpec<Local>, the
   exact 12.7 DP semantic transitions, AuditTerminalPlanAbandonSpec<Local>,
   BulkLoadTransitionSpec<Local>, DerivedBuildTransitionSpec<Local>, and every
   exact semantic backup/restore/GC/key transition. Required Local maintenance
   rows separately include AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local>,
   ResultResumeTransitionSpec<Local>, ..."

MEASURED, of those 13 named inputs, landed `logical_kind` rows: ZERO.

  TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec             0   no row of any kind
  AllocationReservationTransitionSpec     0   no row of any kind
  FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec   0   no row of any kind
  FormatTransitionSpec                    0   no row of any kind
  EscrowRightsTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  BulkLoadTransitionSpec                  0   no row of any kind
  DerivedBuildTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  PrivacyContinuityImportSpec             0   reservation 1, disposition 1
  AuditTerminalPlanAbandonSpec            0   top_level_candidate 1, wire_type 1
  AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec              0   reservation 1, disposition 1, candidate 1
  ResultResumeTransitionSpec              0   target 1, candidate 1, wire_type 1
  ConfigurationTransitionSpec             0   top_level_candidate 3

Eight of thirteen have no row at all; five exist only as candidates or
reservations. A `command_contracts.toml` row requires `input_schema_id`,
`body_schema_id`, `result_schema_id` and `applied_record_schema_id` to resolve to
REGISTERED schemas. None of these can be named today without inventing a referent.

## Also corrected: which direction the generation runs

fgdb-5uw2's note (mine) said command_contracts.toml "sits on the generated side"
of appendix_a_catalog.toml and must not be hand-authored. That reading was wrong.
Plan line 294 calls it "one further NORMATIVE REGISTRY", and the clause I leaned
on -- "hand-written lists IN THIS DOCUMENT are generated readability projections"
-- scopes to lists in the PLAN, not to the registry. a10 states the direction
explicitly:

  "The local SequenceNeutralSpec semantic union is generated from
   command_contracts.toml; it is exhaustive and has no hand-maintained allowlist."

So command_contracts.toml is an AUTHORED normative input and the SequenceNeutralSpec
union is its projection. 5uw2's verb "materialize" was right; my reason for
declining was wrong. The correct reason to decline is the one above: its referents
do not exist yet.

## What closing this bead requires

a10 must land, in this order, and each step is a real slice increment:
  1. the 13+ `*Spec` command-input schemas as logical kinds with fields
     (a10 declares field_candidate_count 180 and only 17 are landed)
  2. the `SequenceNeutralSpec` / `GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec` union rows moved off
     `reserved`, with one union_arm per concrete inner tag
     (a10 declares union_candidate_count 5 / arm_candidate_count 17; landed 1 / 4)
  3. the 110 declared ambiguity adjudications (1 landed)
Only then can command_contracts.toml name a real input/body/result/applied triple.

## Construction law for step 2, so it is not re-derived

A top-level wire-backed union's `allowed_containing_schemas` must name its
CONSUMER, not itself; the 69/69 self-only precedent strands its own anchor field
and "*" is banned. a10's one landed union already does this correctly --
`ExpectedStateCondition` names ["ControlCommand","KeyDestroyProposal"] -- so
`SequenceNeutralSpec` should name the command records that carry it. A generic
whole-schema union is always logical-backed and needs no variant rows; a
wire-backed one does.

Measured by pane2 under a held catalog lease. No build used -- greps and Python
reads over checked-in TOML and the plan. Nothing edited, nothing deleted.
notes:
LANDABILITY MEASURED, WITH A CONTROL. NO OUTER ROLE-COMMAND UNION IS LANDABLE AT
THIS HEAD (650c37d). I tried to land one and the checker refused; the refusal is
reproduced below with its vacuity control, so this is a measurement and not a
third opinion. Handing ch8r back OPEN with the blocking law named.

=== WHAT I ATTEMPTED ===
The outer union is `SequenceNeutralSpec`. I synthesized its [[union]] row against
the landed `ExpectedStateCondition` template, obeying every law given:
  allowed_containing_schemas = ["ControlCommand"]   <- the CONSUMER, per the
      a10 source: ControlCommand.typed_payload_ref:StrongRef<SequenceNeutralSpec>.
      Not self-only (the 69/69 precedent strands its anchor field), not "*".
  containing_schema = union_path = union_name = "SequenceNeutralSpec"
  tag_wire_type = "u16", encoding_context = "closed-tagged",
  version_status = "reserved", role_predicate = "true"
  row_id = "a10:union:sequence-neutral-spec-24da00b9163ae0cb"

=== ROW_ID IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. FIRST CONTROL, FIRST LAW ===
My first attempt used an invented row_id and the checker fired
`catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch` twice, once per planted row. The rule is
appendix_a.rs:9060 `projection_row_identity`:
  union      suffix = lower_kebab(union_name) + "-" +
                      sha256("union|{containing_schema}|{union_path}")[..16]
  union_arm  suffix = ... sha256("arm|{containing_schema}|{union_path}|{source_arm_name}")[..16]
  row_id     = "{slice_id}:{row_kind}:{suffix}"
VERIFIED against the landed row: my recomputation of
`expected-state-condition-4979a5d9718448bd` reproduces it byte for byte. Whoever
lands these rows needs this; it is not written down anywhere else.

=== THE DECISIVE LAW: A UNION WITH NO ARMS IS REJECTED ===
With the correct derived row_id, the union row alone is still refused:
    projection_ordinary_union_arm_missing
    projection_ordinary_union_logical_contract_mismatch
This kills the "a generic whole-schema union is logical-backed and needs no
variant rows" route for this union. The corpus agrees and is unanimous:
    unions with ZERO arm rows:  0 of 380
There is no precedent for a zero-arm union anywhere in the catalog.

=== THE CONTROL'S OWN CONTROL, SO THE ATTRIBUTION IS NOT ASSUMED ===
The scratch root symlinks crates/, scripts/ and tools/, which produces harness
noise. Running the IDENTICAL root with the catalog UNMUTATED:
    3 catalog_maintenance_checker_artifact_missing
    1 catalog_repository_workspace_unavailable
    1 catalog_scenario_checker_artifact_missing
    = 5 violations, all harness
Adding only the union row adds exactly SIX and no others:
    projection_ordinary_union_arm_missing            <- the law
    projection_ordinary_union_logical_contract_mismatch
    catalog_projection_target_missing
    projection_owner_assignment_drift
    projection_registry_assignment_drift
    projection_row_count
So every code above is attributable to the planted row, not to the harness.
Baseline on the REAL tree for reference: 1 violation, projection_byte_diff, in
the durable_fields projection -- pre-existing, another pane's, not mine.

=== DENOMINATOR: EVERY OUTER COMMAND UNION a10's SOURCE NAMES, AND ITS BLOCKER ===
  1  local `SequenceNeutralSpec` semantic union
       BLOCKED. Needs arms (proved above). Its arms are the concrete inner tags,
       and the source forbids supplying them by hand in the same sentence that
       names them: "The local SequenceNeutralSpec semantic union is generated
       from command_contracts.toml; it is exhaustive and HAS NO HAND-MAINTAINED
       ALLOWLIST." Hand-minting arms IS a hand-maintained allowlist.
  2  `LocalMaintenanceCommand`
       BLOCKED, same law. "Each concrete inner tag is a separate registry row
       with its exact body, result, authority, audit, availability,
       construction, plane, and state-slot contract" -- i.e. a contract row.
  3  `PayloadBearingControlKind` table
       BLOCKED. Named "generated" by the source; no arm spelling given.
  4  `AuditFreezeField<Tag>`
       Arms ARE spelled exactly -- Required{freeze_ref}|Forbidden{compatibility_row_id}
       -- but its consumer `SequenceNeutralSpec` is a logical kind at
       status "reserved", so the consumer law cannot be satisfied by a live row.
  5  `DeltaRetentionObligationRef<Role>`
       BLOCKED. The source describes its arms as prose CATEGORIES ("role-valid
       cursor/delivery, derived-generation, replay, backup/export, CDC,
       shard-ack/global-publication, and explicit administrative history
       promises"), never as exact tags. Minting arms would invent stable names.
5 of 5 blocked, each by a different clause, and none by an owner ruling.

=== WHY NO SUBSTITUTE UNION WAS LANDED INSTEAD ===
`PreparedCommitRecord.status` is spelled exactly
(Preparing|Receipted|Ordered{raft_index}|Applied{...}|Abandoned{...}), five arms,
and its consumer PreparedCommitRecord is an ACTIVE landed kind with active
fields -- so it IS landable. It is NOT an outer role-command union; it is a
status enum. Landing it here would be scope drift dressed as progress, and it
belongs to the field layer on fgdb-i1rx. Named there rather than taken.

=== HANDING BACK ===
ch8r stays OPEN. The unblocking sequence is on fgdb-i1rx and is unchanged: the
`*Spec` inputs must become ACTIVE logical kinds (0 of 35 are), then the union
gets arms, then command_contracts.toml can name a resolving triple. What ch8r
adds today is that the last step is not optional politeness -- the checker
enforces it, and the enforcement fires.

No token was held: everything was read-only or in scratch. No cargo -- the
checker was built with standalone rustc, CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR at compile time.
Scratch left in place, named for reclaim: <scratch>/ch8r/mut, mutA, mutC (three
symlink roots plus three 4MB catalog copies, ~13MB total).

title: checker_index status=live is proved by Path::is_file() alone: a registered live checker that no gate ever runs is indistinguishable from one that runs every commit
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #2, and it is the
ROOT CAUSE that makes the check.sh gap invisible.

## What it claims

AGENTS.md, "Spec-First Workflow" item 2: "**CI cross-checks that every ID has a
live checker.**" And the hard rule immediately below it: "**no subsystem ships
against an unenforced invariant.** A workstream exit gate (G1-G4, §19) cannot
pass while any invariant it depends on lacks a live checker in
`invariants.toml`. Promote a design assumption to enforced only after the
checker exists."

`registries/checker_index.toml`'s own header repeats it: rows may be
stub-registered pre-Genesis, "but the symbol must still be a registered,
reviewable row, and a \"live\" row's artifact must exist in-repo."

## What it actually does

`tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs:6231`:

```rust
fn live_checker_artifact_exists(repo_root: &Path, checker: &model::Checker) -> bool {
    safe_repository_relative(&checker.artifact) && repo_root.join(&checker.artifact).is_file()
}
```

`status = "live"` is proved by `Path::is_file()`. Two consequences:

1. **Nothing binds a live checker to any gate that runs it.** A checker can be
   registered live, be cited by a clause as its enforcement mechanism, and be
   invoked by no wrapper, no CI step, and no test — and every registry gate
   stays green. This is not hypothetical: four live script rows and two live
   binary rows are in exactly that state right now (companion bead
   fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw).

2. **The symbol->artifact binding is unverified at symbol granularity.** For
   `kind = "cargo-test"` rows the `symbol` is a test function name
   (`claims_neg_missing_checker`, `spine_neg_twenty_first_id`, ...), but nothing
   greps the artifact for it. Rename or delete
   `tests/claims.rs::claims_neg_waiver_present` and its row stays `status =
   "live"` and every gate stays green, because `tests/claims.rs` still exists.
   Verified by sweep: all `kind="cargo-test"` symbols DO currently resolve to
   real functions — by author discipline, not by enforcement. (The 11 live rows
   whose symbol is absent from its artifact are all scheme-prefixed or
   law-name symbols — `architecture_source_coverage`, `cargo-test:claims`,
   `topology_registry_source` — i.e. logical names, not code symbols. Those are
   fine; the point is that nothing distinguishes them from a rotted one.)

The `status = "stub"` rows are honest and should stay: 40 of them point at
files under `crates/fgdb-oracles/`, `crates/fgdb-reference/`, etc. that do not
exist yet, which is exactly what pre-Genesis stub registration is for. All 20
invariants in `invariants.toml` are `status = "stub"`. That part of the system
is telling the truth.

## Which gate catches this today

None. This IS the gate.

## Why it matters now

Nine planned subsystems exist only as plan text and every gate is green. The
only thing standing between "green" and "green because nothing ran" is this
predicate, and it currently answers a weaker question than the doctrine asks.

## Fix

Strengthen the live-checker proof from "the file exists" toward "the checker is
reachable from an executing gate":

1. Add a `runner` field (or equivalent) to each live row naming the gate that
   invokes it, and a law asserting that runner actually references the artifact
   — with `scripts/check.sh` parsed as the canonical runner manifest. Best form
   is to invert it: have `check.sh` derive its step list FROM `checker_index.toml`,
   which makes the law self-enforcing rather than a second list to keep in sync.
2. For `kind = "cargo-test"` rows, assert the symbol appears in the artifact
   (a `fn <symbol>` grep is enough to catch rename/delete rot).
3. Keep the existence check — it is necessary, just not sufficient.
close_reason:
Landed: liveness is now REGISTERED + INVOKED + CAPABLE OF FAILING, in one reader (tools/registry-check/src/liveness.rs), mutation-proven in tests/metamorphic.rs relation 11.

WHAT WAS TRUE. `status = "live"` was proved by `Path::is_file()` — in TWO readers that had already drifted: validate::validate_checker_index had no path-safety guard, appendix_a::live_checker_artifact_exists had one. Same defect as the u9zp forbid predicate, one level up: a checker whose answer is fixed before it reads anything.

WHAT LANDED. liveness.rs, the single reader, consumed by both call sites (appendix_a's predicate is now a 2-line delegation). Three facts, one reader each:
  REGISTERED  safe repo-relative file AND the row's declared `unit` resolves in its LIVE code.
  INVOKED     structural, not a second copy of check.sh's dispatch: cargo-test must be an auto-discovered integration target of a workspace member (check.sh credits EVERY cargo-test row with the one workspace `cargo test` exit code, so a row pointing anywhere else reports PASS); binary must be compiled into a bin target through live `mod` declarations; script must be an executable program.
  CAN FAIL    a #[test] must be able to panic; a binary's REACHABLE BIN ROOTS must be able to exit nonzero (a property of main, not of the module the row names); a script must have a nonzero exit. Read through unsafe_ledger::mask_source and a new mask_shell, so a commented-out assertion proves nothing.

SCHEMA. `unit = "symbol" | "artifact"`, required on live rows. This is the fix for finding #2: 9 live rows name a #[test] fn, 27 are law names for a whole artifact, and no spelling rule separates `threat_model` (a law name) from a rotted symbol. Declaring it makes rot detectable; guessing cannot.

CONTROL. liveness::self_test() runs 32 known-answer cases (half of them masked cases) on every invocation; validate refuses to report any row live when it is unlicensed, and `registry-check all` now emits checker_liveness_self_test {cases, failed_cases, live_rows, licensed}. It caught a real bug in its own author's reader during development: exit "\$rc" read as incapable of failing, because the argument was read from the mask instead of the raw line.

MUTATION PROOF (the point). tests/metamorphic.rs relation 11 keeps the pre-fix predicate verbatim as legacy_is_file_predicate and asserts EVERY mutant satisfies it, so each test states that the old reader could not tell the cases apart. Restoring the pre-fix body of assess(): 5 of 36 metamorphic tests go RED, and the three controls stay green (which is what a faithful revert must do). End-to-end at the binary: renaming a test symbol -> checker_symbol_unresolved, exit 1; pointing a cargo-test row at src/threat.rs -> checker_not_invocable, exit 1. Both were green before.

PERFORMANCE. A naive per-row assess cost 10.7s per sweep (each binary row re-masked 1.7MB of lib source per bin root). Prover memoizes the roster and per-member module map; `registry-check all` is 4.0s end to end.

GATES. cargo test -p registry-check: 400 passed / 0 failed (76 lib + 107 identity + 36 metamorphic + 27 architecture + 56 topology + 40 threat + 21 ledger + 13 claims + 8 spine + 6 satisfiability + 6 sat-2 + 4). clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, ubs exit 0 (liveness.rs: 0 critical). registry-check all and appendix: pass, exit 0.

NOT DONE, deliberately: nothing binds check.sh itself to a CI runner that executes it — that is the remaining half of the doctrine and it is u7mw/CI territory, not this predicate.

title: claims-lint validates only markers that are present: 12 numeric performance budgets in README carry no marker and slo.toml has zero slo/benchmark rows
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep phase 2 (pane4, 2026-07-26). Question 3:
benchmark and performance claims.

## The measurement

`registries/slo.toml` contains FOUR rows. All four are `claim_class =
"bounded_model"` (FG-CFG-01..04). There are **zero `claim_class = "slo"` rows
and zero `claim_class = "benchmark"` rows** in the repository.

`README.md` "Performance" section (line ~354 onward) states **twelve numeric
throughput/latency budgets** in its gate table, and cites **zero** claim
markers. Examples, verbatim:

  - "≥ 40M edges/s sustained (≥ 60% of NVMe seq-write ceiling)"
  - "≥ 2M edge-inserts/s for the pinned batch/txn mix"
  - "≥ 8M lookups/s across cores; p99 < 15 µs warm"
  - "≥ 500M edges/s per core; ≥ 10B edges/s node aggregate"
  - "< 50 ms (must not materialize)"
  - "throughput ≥ 3× Neo4j, ≥ 1.5× best published embedded engine"
  - "O(1), < 100 µs"  /  "< 30 s to first query"

`registries/slo.toml`'s own header states the law these violate:

> "every µs or throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed
>  {operation_class, posture, audit_class}"

Twelve budgets in normative prose, zero registered rows.

## What claims to catch this, and why it cannot

`registries/claims_lint.toml` names `README.md` as one of three "NORMATIVE
merged prose artifacts" and declares that "load-bearing claim markers must
resolve". `tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs::claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean`
asserts the hit list is empty, with the message "normative prose cites
unregistered claim markers". It passes, and it will always pass here.

The lint is **one-directional**. Its marker pattern is
`FG-[A-Z]{2,5}-[0-9]{2}`; `lint::run` collects markers that ARE PRESENT in the
prose and fails any that does not resolve to a registered row. It has no
converse: nothing requires that a load-bearing claim CARRY a marker. A
performance budget written with no `FG-SLO-nn` beside it is not an unresolved
marker — it is not a marker at all, and is therefore invisible to the only
instrument pointed at that file.

This is the same shape as the seven defects found earlier today: a check whose
green result answers a narrower question than its name implies.
"claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean" reads as "the prose makes no unregistered
claims"; it means "every marker that happens to be typed resolves."

## Being fair about what is NOT wrong here

- README §354 frames the section honestly: "Numbers below are the **provisional**
  CI gates (§17 `EmpiricalGate`s, **activated only under pinned benchmark
  manifests**)". No number is presented as a measured result, so Doctrine 7's
  "no non-durable benchmark mode reported as a result" is NOT violated — there
  is no benchmark mode at all, and no result is claimed.
- The sentence "Every gate has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance
  budget, and a flamegraph artifact on regression" is present-tense while zero
  bench binaries exist (no `benches/`, no criterion, no `#[bench]`), but the
  whole README is written in the design register describing the intended system,
  and that exact sentence is quoted from the open bead
  `fgdb-verif-perf-apparatus-dv6p`, which tracks building it. That is a
  documentation-register issue, not a false claim of measurement.

The defect is specifically the missing registry rows and the lint's inability
to notice they are missing.

## Which gate catches this today

None. claims-lint is green by construction. `registry-check validate` checks
slo.toml rows that EXIST for schema conformance; it has no notion of a budget
that should have a row and does not. Nothing cross-references README against
slo.toml in either direction.

## Fix

1. Make claims-lint bidirectional for the classes where a bare number is
   load-bearing: scan normative prose for unmarked quantitative claims
   (throughput/latency/ratio patterns: `≥ N unit/s`, `p99 < N µs`, `< N ms`,
   `≥ N× <named system>`) and fail when one carries no resolvable marker. The
   pattern set should be a registry row, not a regex buried in code, so adding a
   claim shape is a reviewable change.
2. Mint the twelve `FG-SLO-nn` rows keyed {operation_class, posture,
   audit_class} and cite them inline in the README table. This is the work
   `fgdb-g0-cost-registry-idt` and `fgdb-perf-cost-ci-02p` already own — this
   bead is the measurement that says how far off it currently is (12 to 0) and
   that no gate will report the gap closing or reopening.
3. Give the new lint direction a seeded negative fixture: a planted unmarked
   throughput claim in a scratch prose file must fail with its exact code.
notes:
MEASUREMENT + FIX (pane3, 2026-07-26). Both directions now run; every number
below was produced by running the checker, not by reading it.

## The allowlist measurement that was asked for

The exclusion list carried SIX entries. **Zero of them did any work.**

`lint::run` never referenced `config.excludes` at all. `load_config` parsed the
six rows and enforced the "an exclusion without a reason is a schema error"
schema rule on them, and then `run` iterated `config.scan` and nothing else. The
scan set was a three-file allowlist, and 0 of the 6 excluded paths were in it, so
even a wired-up filter would have removed nothing.

Measured, not inferred — pre-change checker, same tree, config with the six
exclusions and config with the `[[exclude]]` section truncated away:

    PRE-CHANGE lint: scan=3 excludes=6 hits=0
    PRE-CHANGE lint: scan=3 excludes=0 hits=0

Two secondary numbers, because "dead exclude" can mean three things and only one
of them was true here:

  * **0 of 6** exclusion paths named a file that no longer exists. The
    "excludes something that is gone" hypothesis is FALSIFIED for this registry.
  * **2 of 6** would have suppressed a real hit had the mechanism been wired:
    PLAN_AUDIT_BY_SOL_ULTRA.md carries 1 unregistered marker and
    ENHANCEMENT_PROPOSALS_FOR_THE_COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md carries 8. The other
    four carry 0 unregistered markers (two of them carry 0 markers at all), so
    four of the six exclusions were doubly inert.
  * The actual hole was neither: **3 tracked prose artifacts** —
    docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md, docs/THREAT_AND_TRUST_MODEL.md,
    docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md, carrying 25 markers between them — were neither
    scanned nor excluded. Nothing required them to be either. Today all 25
    markers resolve, so the hole was real and unoccupied: 0 live violations
    hiding in it, which is luck, not enforcement.

## The other direction, measured

The README §Performance gate table has **13** rows, not the twelve this bead
estimated (the original count was of illustrative examples; the table's own row
count is 13). Measured on the shipped tree: `gate_rows_read: 13,
gate_rows_marked: 0, gate_rows_unmarked: 13`. slo.toml still holds zero
`claim_class = "slo"` and zero `claim_class = "benchmark"` rows.

## What landed

ONE reader, ONE entry point. `lint::run` returns `(Vec<LintHit>, LintCensus)`
and evaluates every law; there is no second lint path and no second marker
parser. `markers_in_line` is untouched and remains THE marker reader;
`lint::table_cells` is now THE markdown-row cell reader and
`topology::parse_layer_table` was switched to call it, so two table readers
cannot disagree (workspace_topology: 56/56 still green after the switch).

Five laws, five stable hit codes:

  * `unregistered_marker` — direction 1, unchanged.
  * `unmarked_gate_row` — direction 2. Every row of a declared gate table must
    cite a resolvable marker.
  * `dead_gate_exemption` — the converse of the ledger that records the rows
    which do not yet. An entry whose row is gone, OR whose row now carries a
    marker, fails. That second half is what makes the 13→0 gap visible as it
    closes rather than silently leaving free passes behind.
  * `unclaimed_prose` — closure. Every non-hidden `*.md` in a declared closure
    directory must be in `scan` or in an `[[exclude]]`. This is what makes the
    six exclusions load-bearing for the first time.
  * `dead_exclude` — an exclusion whose `presence = "required"` path does not
    exist. `presence = "optional"` is the one declared escape and is used
    exactly once, for the gitignored ENHANCEMENT_PROPOSALS document, so a clean
    clone does not go red.

Structural failures (heading moved, table deleted, table with zero rows, a
gate-table file absent from `scan`, an empty `scan`, an empty `closure_dirs`, no
`[[gate_table]]` at all, a path both scanned and excluded, a duplicated ledger
entry) are hard errors, not hits. A lint aimed at nothing must fail loudly.

Shipped-tree census, printed on pass as well as fail: `files_scanned: 6,
markers_seen: 117, gate_rows_read: 13, gate_rows_marked: 0, gate_rows_unmarked:
13, prose_files_seen: 12`, hits 0.

## Mutation proof, on the REAL corpus, with the pre-change checker as control

Four mutations of a verbatim copy of the real tree. Pre-change checker: **0 hits
on all four**. Post-change checker: 1 hit each, with file:line.

  A. a 14th unmarked budget row appended to the real README table
     (`| Subscription fan-out | ≥ 250k notifications/s per broker; p99 < 5 ms |`)
     → 13→14 rows read, 13→14 unmarked,
     `[unmarked_gate_row] README.md:373 Subscription fan-out`
  B. a real row marked and its ledger line left in place
     (`Branch create / snapshot open` cites FG-CFG-01) → markers 117→118,
     unmarked 13→12, `[dead_gate_exemption] README.md:371 … this row now cites
     FG-CFG-01; delete its claims_lint.toml unmarked_rows entry`
  C. PLAN_AUDIT_BY_SOL_ULTRA.md removed from the tree → prose 12→11,
     `[dead_exclude] PLAN_AUDIT_BY_SOL_ULTRA.md`
  D. a new docs/NEW_DESIGN_NOTE.md nobody pointed the lint at → prose 12→13,
     `[unclaimed_prose] docs/NEW_DESIGN_NOTE.md`

## The vacuity control, which FIRES

`claims_neg_lint_region_that_examines_nothing_is_a_hard_error` asserts three
errors, because the failure mode this whole direction exists to catch is a check
that passes because it examined nothing: heading present with the table deleted;
heading and table present with zero data rows; heading moved. All three must be
`Err`, and the test fails if any of them passes clean. `claims_neg_lint_config_
cannot_declare_a_vacuous_scope` does the same at the config layer over six
different ways to disarm the lint. The fixture base test asserts named content
(2 files, 3 rows, 1 marked, 2 unmarked, 3 prose files) rather than emptiness,
because two vacuous runs compare equal.

## The gap, now instrumented

`claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean` asserts the census as FLOORS (≥6 files, ≥100
markers, ≥12 prose artifacts, ≥13 rows) plus one CEILING: `gate_rows_unmarked <=
13`. The floors cannot red another pane's citation or document; the ceiling
cannot be raised without a deliberate change, and a fourteenth unmarked row
fails in the lint itself. Minting the FG-SLO rows and citing them lowers the
ceiling — that work stays with fgdb-g0-cost-registry-idt / fgdb-perf-cost-ci-02p,
which this bead does not touch.

## Deliberately NOT done, with the reason

The bead's fix #1 proposed scanning prose for unmarked quantitative claims by
numeric pattern (`≥ N unit/s`, `p99 < N µs`, `≥ N×`). That is not implemented and
should not be. The same README paragraph that states "≥ 40M edges/s sustained"
(a claim about this system) also states "32-core/64-thread, 256 GB RAM, PCIe-4
NVMe at 7 GB/s" (a description of the reference machine). No numeric pattern
separates those two, so a corpus-wide number scan needs an exemption list larger
than the set of real claims — and this bead is a report about an exemption list
that went dead. The declared region is reviewable and the gate row is the unit
the plan itself uses ("every gate names its operation class in the
operation-cost registry"), so that is the unit the lint uses. Adding a second
region is a `[[gate_table]]` row, not a code change.
close_reason: Both directions land in 4f37495. The one-directional defect is fixed: lint::run now evaluates five laws through one entry point (unregistered_marker, unmarked_gate_row, dead_gate_exemption, unclaimed_prose, dead_exclude), with structural breaks as hard errors. Allowlist measurement asked for: 0 of 6 excludes did any work (run() never referenced config.excludes; truncating the section changed nothing), 0 of 6 named a missing path (the usual 'dead exclude' hypothesis falsified), 2 of 6 would have suppressed a hit if wired, and the real hole was 3 tracked prose files in neither list. Real-corpus mutation proof with the pre-change checker as control: 4 mutations, 0 hits before, 1 hit each after with file:line. Vacuity controls fire (region-gone = Err x3; vacuous config = Err x8). The 13-to-0 budget gap is now instrumented as a monotone ceiling (gate_rows_unmarked <= 13) plus a per-row ledger checked in both directions; MINTING the FG-SLO rows is deliberately not done here and stays with fgdb-g0-cost-registry-idt / fgdb-perf-cost-ci-02p. Full measurement in the bead notes.

title: claims-lint scans a static list of 3 files; a new normative .md is silently ignored
description:
## The defect

`claims-lint` scans a **static list of three files**. Any other `.md` in the tree —
including a brand-new normative one — is never opened, and `registry-check all`
reports `outcome: pass`.

Measured at HEAD (77449c7), on a pristine `git archive` copy:

    printf '# Undeclared\n\nThis file guarantees FG-INV-01 holds and is proven correct.\n' \
      > UNDECLARED_NEW_DOC.md
    ./registry-check all --root .
    -> {"event":"lint_completed","files_scanned":3,"hits":0,"outcome":"pass"}
    -> {"event":"run_completed","failures":0,"outcome":"pass"}     exit 0

`files_scanned` stays **3**. The text contains two claim markers of exactly the
class claims-lint exists to catch ("guarantees", "proven correct") plus an
invariant ID, and none of it is looked at.

## The scan list IS reached — this is a closure gap, not a dead check

The check itself works. Adding the same sentence to a file that IS on the list
fails correctly:

    (append the bogus claim to AGENTS.md)
    ./registry-check lint --root .   -> exit 1
    (restore)                        -> exit 0

So `claims_lint.toml` scans `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and
`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md`, and records exclusion
reasons for five historical review artifacts. What it does not do is **close the
set**: nothing asserts that every tracked `.md` is either scanned or excluded.
A sixth `.md` is in neither list and nothing notices.

## Why this matters more than the file count suggests

`registries/claims_lint.toml`'s own header says it "scans the NORMATIVE merged
prose artifacts for claim markers". The registries are what separate "partially
implemented" from "implemented". A new design doc, ported plan section, or
subsystem README can assert an unregistered invariant, a proof that does not
exist, or an SLO that nothing measures, and every gate stays green — which is the
`fgdb-shell-lint-silent-no-op-xi8p` shape (a checker foolable by a file it never
opened) reproduced inside the checker rather than around it.

`scripts/check.sh` now catches the tracked-file case at the wrapper level: since
e87943f its file-coverage closure step fails on any tracked file that no gate
claims, so a new `.md` reds the run. **That is a backstop, not this fix.** It
lives in bash, it only fires when someone runs check.sh, and it cannot tell
"scanned for claim markers" from "content pinned". The law belongs in the checker.

## The law that should exist

Mirror what `claims_lint.toml` already half-does, and make the set total:

    every tracked *.md is in `scan_paths` OR in an `[[exclusion]]` row with a reason

Concretely, in the lint validator: enumerate the candidate `.md` set, subtract
`scan_paths` and the exclusion paths, and emit a violation naming each remainder:

    claims_lint_scan_set_not_total
    "SOME_NEW_DOC.md is neither scanned nor excluded; add it to scan_paths or
     record an [[exclusion]] with a reason"

Note the enumeration source is the open question: `registry-check` is std-only
and does not shell out to git, so "tracked" is not directly available to it.
Options, in preference order: (a) walk the repo root + `docs/` non-recursively,
which covers every `.md` that exists today; (b) pin the expected `.md` set with a
count and a transcript hash the way the decision/bibliography tables already are
(`PINNED_DECISION_ID_HASH` et al), so an added file moves the pin. (b) is more in
keeping with the rest of the registry and needs no filesystem walk.

## Acceptance

1. A new `.md` at the repo root or under `docs/` that is neither scanned nor
   excluded makes `registry-check all` exit non-zero and names the file.
2. The five existing exclusions stay silent, and `files_scanned` stays 3.
3. Mutation audit: removing the new check must make case 1 pass again.
4. Any pin introduced is base-derived at landing time, not copied from this bead.
close_reason: Measured 11 tracked .md / 6 scanned / 11 accounted for / 0-file but 50-DIRECTORY gap. The scan-set half was already fixed by sdpv; the depth half was not — a one-level walk made the law total by coincidence. Walk is now recursive with a reasoned [[closure_prune]] and a dead_closure_prune law; 7-cell matrix and a firing vacuity control. fd7d169.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSED. Landed fd7d169.

THE THREE NUMBERS, MEASURED FIRST, at b77982e on a pristine git-archive copy:

  total population    11 tracked *.md   (8 at the repo root, 3 under docs/)
  scan set             6   README.md, AGENTS.md, the merged plan, and the three
                           generated docs/ artifacts
  accounted for       11   = 6 scanned + 5 excluded. The 6th [[exclude]] is
                           presence="optional" (ENHANCEMENT_PROPOSALS..., gitignored),
                           so 6 + 5 = 11 exactly. Nothing is unaccounted for.
  THE GAP              0 files, and 50 tracked DIRECTORIES below depth 1

THE BEAD'S ORIGINAL DEFECT IS ALREADY GONE, and I checked rather than assumed. It
says "scans a static list of THREE files" and "nothing asserts that every tracked
.md is either scanned or excluded". Both were true when filed; neither is now.
pane3's sdpv work (4f37495) landed the closure law and grew the scan set to six.
I re-ran the bead's own repro to be sure:

  a new root .md carrying "guarantees FG-INV-01 ... proven correct"
    -> unclaimed_prose: UNDECLARED_ROOT.md, outcome fail, hits 1

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINED IS THE LAW'S DEPTH. `closure_dirs = [".", "docs"]` was read
ONE LEVEL DEEP. That made it total over the corpus as it stands and blind
everywhere else -- total because of where files happen to sit today, not by
construction:

  crates/fgdb-bigint/README.md, identical claim text
    -> registry-check all: failures: 0, outcome: pass, EXIT 0

That is the ninth-instance shape the orchestrator named, one level in: the green
means "no unclaimed prose in the two directories we look at", and reads as "no
unclaimed prose".

WHAT LANDED. The walk is recursive from each closure root; `docs` is dropped from
the list because `.` now reaches it (listing both would make its files an
obligation twice, and the walk dedups across roots anyway). `[[closure_prune]]`
declares subtrees the walk does not enter -- one row, `target`,
presence="optional" -- because a recursive walk over a build-output tree would
drag every vendored dependency's prose into the obligation. A prune is a
NARROWING, so it is held to the denylist's discipline: reason required, cannot
also be a closure root, cannot be listed twice, and a presence="required" prune
whose directory is gone is a new `dead_closure_prune` hit rather than a rule that
narrows nothing. Entry type is read with `file_type()`, which does not follow
symlinks, so the recursion cannot loop (measured: 0 symlinks outside .git; the
guard keeps that true by construction rather than by luck).

MUTATION MATRIX, pristine copy, restored between each:

  P0 clean                             exit 0  prose=11  hits=0
  P1 crates/fgdb-bigint/README.md      exit 1  prose=12  hits=1  unclaimed_prose
  P2 root UNDECLARED_ROOT.md           exit 1  prose=12  hits=1  unclaimed_prose
  P3 docs/design/DEEP.md (depth 2)     exit 1  prose=12  hits=1  unclaimed_prose
  P4 target/doc/VENDORED.md (pruned)   exit 0  prose=11  hits=0
  P5 prune required, target absent     exit 1  prose=11  hits=1  dead_closure_prune
  P5r restored                         exit 0  prose=11  hits=0

VACUITY CONTROL, AND IT FIRES. Reverting the walk to one level deep and rerunning
P1: exit 0, hits 0, outcome pass -- invisible again. AND `prose_files_seen`
collapses 11 -> 8, because with a single `.` root and no recursion the three
docs/ files stop being counted at all. The census is its own tell: a narrowed
walk shows up as a smaller corpus, which the shipped-prose test's existing
`prose_files_seen >= 12` floor already guards. Two independent signals, not one.

TESTS: two added to the EXISTING suite (one reader, no parallel scanner) --
`claims_neg_unclaimed_prose_below_the_closure_root` and
`claims_closure_prune_narrows_the_walk_and_must_stay_live`. Suite 31 -> 33.

GATES, all lock-free via standalone rustc / clippy-driver, no build slot and no
private CARGO_TARGET_DIR: claims suite 33 passed 0 failed; rustfmt --check clean;
clippy-driver on the lib with -D warnings, zero diagnostics; registry-check lint
6 scanned / 12 prose / 0 hits; registry-check all exit 0; g0_claims_e2e.sh 16
passed 0 failed; ubs on both changed files 0 critical.

DISCIPLINE SLIP, STATED PLAINLY: I edited registries/claims_lint.toml and
tools/registry-check/** BEFORE acquiring the catalog token, and only went for the
token when I was ready to commit. pane6-wh81 held it and had files STAGED in the
index at the time, so a careless `git add -A` from either of us would have swept
the other. Nothing was lost -- I waited, staged exactly three paths by name, and
verified my diffstat was additive (+303/-45, all mine) before committing -- but
the correct order is token first, and I did not follow it.

TOKENS: catalog acquired only for the commit and released immediately after,
renewed once because the first waiter had held it 9m before I noticed. No build
slot was needed. No CARGO_TARGET_DIR was created, per instruction.

WHAT I DID NOT DO:
  - `closure_dirs` is still declared data, and nothing forces `.` to be in it. A
    future edit narrowing it to `["docs"]` would pass every test here; only the
    shipped-prose `prose_files_seen >= 12` floor would catch it, and that floor is
    a number in a test rather than a law. Worth a "closure roots must cover the
    repository root" assertion; I did not add one.
  - The closure is over `*.md` only. A normative claim in a `.rst`, `.txt` or a
    doc comment is outside this lint's aim entirely, and I did not widen it.
  - I did not touch scripts/check.sh's file-coverage gate, which remains the
    tracked-file backstop at the wrapper level.

title: Nothing guards the stub->live promotion of an invariant clause: negative_test_entrypoint is enforced as a non-empty string, and 18 of 20 clauses promote at G1
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep phase 2 (pane4, 2026-07-26). Question 2:
invariant registry vs reality.

## The measurement

All 20 clauses FG-INV-01.core .. FG-INV-20.core are `status = "stub"`. Every
one names both a `checker_entrypoint` and a `negative_test_entrypoint`, and
every one of those 40 symbols resolves to a `checker_index.toml` row whose
artifact DOES NOT EXIST — they point into `crates/fgdb-oracles/`,
`crates/fgdb-reference/`, `crates/fgdb-observatory/`, `crates/fgdb-secure-view/`
and `crates/fgdb-ecs/`, none of which is a crate yet.

So: **0 of 20 invariants have a checker that has been seen to fail, and 0 of 20
have a checker at all.** That is CORRECT and correctly declared — no subsystem
has shipped, `waiver = "forbidden"` on every clause, and the activation-closure
guard that stops a capability being enabled while its clauses are stub is itself
proven to fire (`tests/spine.rs::spine_neg_inactive_reachable_clause`, and
`g0_spine_e2e.sh` phase 3, which asserts the failure NAMES `FG-INV-04.core`).
This bead is not a complaint about the current state.

## The actual defect: nothing guards the promotion

The defect is in the stub -> live transition that all 20 are queued at, and it
is invisible today precisely because nobody has taken it yet.

`tools/registry-check/src/validate.rs:197` `validate_clause` is the whole law
for clause status. It checks:
  - `validate.rs:242` — status is one of {live, stub, dormant};
  - `validate.rs:281` — `negative_test_entrypoint` is a NON-EMPTY STRING
    (it is one entry in the required-non-empty field loop);
  - elsewhere — the symbol resolves to a `checker_index.toml` row, and if that
    row is `status = "live"`, that its artifact file exists
    (`live_checker_artifact_exists`, `appendix_a.rs:6231`, which is `is_file()`).

There is NO law that:
  1. a clause promoted to `live` has a negative test that has ever been
     OBSERVED TO FAIL, or been run at all;
  2. a `live` clause's checker is distinguishable from a stub's by anything
     other than a file existing at a path;
  3. the negative test and the checker are even different artifacts.

The `negative_test_entrypoint` field exists for exactly one purpose — to name
the test proving the checker can go red. Its entire enforcement is "the string
is non-empty and resolves to a row." That is the same shape as the seven
defects found earlier today: a field that reads as evidence and is checked for
presence rather than for what it asserts.

## Why this is the highest-leverage moment to fix it

AGENTS.md: "**no subsystem ships against an unenforced invariant.** A workstream
exit gate (G1-G4) cannot pass while any invariant it depends on lacks a live
checker." And: "Promote a design assumption to enforced only after the checker
exists." Note the doctrine's own wording is the WEAK form — "after the checker
exists" — which is precisely what the code implements. The registry's stronger
intent (a `negative_test_entrypoint` per clause) is not carried into any law.

18 of the 20 clauses carry `first_gate = "G1"`. So at G1 the project will
promote roughly eighteen invariants from stub to enforced in a short window,
and the only thing standing between "enforced" and "a file exists at that path"
is reviewer attention during the busiest gate in the schedule. Every gate stays
green either way.

## Which gate catches this today

None, and none CAN today: with 0 live clauses the promotion law has nothing to
run on. This is a law that must be written and given a negative fixture BEFORE
the first promotion, not after — after, it is a 20-row audit against a green bar.

## Fix

1. Add a promotion law to `validate_clause`: a clause may be `live` only if its
   `negative_test_entrypoint` resolves to a `checker_index.toml` row that is
   itself `status = "live"`, and that row's artifact is DISTINCT from the
   checker's. (Cheap, mechanical, catches the degenerate cases.)
2. Add the real one: require recorded evidence that the negative test has been
   observed to fail — e.g. an evidence row carrying the run that produced the
   red, in the same shape `unsafe-ledger-check` already uses when it reports its
   scanner self-test FIRST to license every zero-site conclusion
   (`bin/unsafe-ledger-check.rs:52-70`). That pattern is in-tree and is the
   right precedent to copy.
3. Give the new law a seeded negative fixture — a clause flipped to `live` with
   an unfireable negative test must fail with its exact code. Otherwise this
   bead's fix joins the 253 laws nobody has watched fire
   (fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy).
close_reason:
FIXED (pane4, 2026-07-26), commit e1203c8. The promotion law is enforced, and it is the THIRD FACE of the fact tl0o and 0f1l already own — so it delegates to liveness.rs rather than getting a third implementation.

MEASURED FIRST (probe against the shipped registries, before any law was written):
  - all 20 clauses `stub`; all 40 entrypoints resolve to checker_index rows that
    are themselves `stub`, pointing into crates that do not exist;
  - promoting one clause to `live`, changing nothing else -> ZERO violations;
  - the degenerate case (negative_test_entrypoint == checker_entrypoint) -> ZERO
    violations.
  The whole law for both fields was 'the string resolves to a row'.

THE BEAD'S PROPOSED RULE 1 WAS WRONG, and the measurement is why. It asked for the
checker's and the negative test's ARTIFACTS to be distinct. All 20 shipped clauses
share an artifact between the two (0 share a symbol), and tests/claims.rs itself
holds both a checker and a negative test — that rule would have rejected the
shipped shape and the house style. Distinct SYMBOLS is the real rule and is what
landed. The bead's rule 2 (recorded evidence of an observed red) is NOT duplicated
here: requiring the negative test to be a LIVE checker row already means, via
liveness.rs, that it is registered, invoked and capable of failing. The
observed-firing half belongs to fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy.

WHAT LANDED
  An ENFORCED clause requires both checker_entrypoint and negative_test_entrypoint
  to resolve to rows that are status=live AND pass Prover::assess; the negative
  test at the SAME bar, not weaker; the two DISTINCT SYMBOLS.
  Codes: clause_promoted_without_live_checker, clause_negative_test_is_its_own_checker.
  CLAUSE_STATUS_ENFORCED is ONE list deciding both the accepted vocabulary and
  which statuses enforce (completeness guard: two spellings is how a status added
  later arrives enforced by nothing). dormant does not enforce, per the registry's
  own sentence about it.
  validate_all now builds ONE Prover and threads it to all three consumers, and
  consults the licence self-test once for the whole run — three provers would have
  been three caches of one fact.

MUTATION PROOF, BOTH DIRECTIONS, with named numbers:
  Positive: every mutant asserted to satisfy legacy_entrypoint_resolves, the
  pre-fix law kept verbatim.
  Negative A (promotion law deleted): FIVE tests red, all mine — claims 14/19;
  metamorphic 43/43 and spine 8/8 stay fully green, so the reds are the missing
  law, not a broken harness.
  Negative B (single vocabulary split back into two spellings): ZERO red. Stated
  in the suite rather than hidden — with exactly the three statuses the old inline
  spelling had, no input distinguishes the two implementations, so
  claims_clause_status_vocabulary_has_one_reader is a PROSPECTIVE guard that fires
  when a fourth status is added. Not reported as witnessed firing.

VACUITY CONTROL THAT FIRES: 0 of 20 clauses are live, so the law is quantified
over nothing. claims_promotion_law_is_vacuous_today_and_this_is_what_licenses_it
promotes a real shipped clause exactly as a G1 workstream bead would and requires
a real defect from real registry data.

DELEGATION PINNED: claims_promotion_delegates_to_the_liveness_reader repoints a
genuinely live row at a file that exists but that cargo test never compiles —
status stays live, artifact stays present — and requires the CLAUSE verdict to
carry liveness's own words ('is not an integration test target of a workspace
member'). A parallel implementation passes every other test and fails that one.

GATES, at HEAD e1203c8 on a `git archive` snapshot built from the snapshot (the
shared working tree is mid-increment on another pane's appendix_a.rs, which does
not compile — 433 vs 426 pin array — so scripts/check.sh cannot verdict anything
right now, and that break is not in this commit): claims 19/19, metamorphic 43/43,
spine 8/8, architecture_decisions 27/27, identity 110/110; `registry-check all`
exits 0 with 0 failures; rustfmt clean; ubs 0 critical on the 3 changed .rs files.

RESIDUE: none for this law. The clause-status vocabulary guard cannot be witnessed
firing until a fourth status exists; that is recorded in the suite and belongs to
xnxy's population, not to a new bead.

title: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings is RED on main: promote_first_clause in tests/claims.rs trips never_loops, so a mandatory AGENTS.md gate cannot pass for any pane
description:
## The measurement (bdbdb9e, 2026-07-26)

    $ cargo clippy -p registry-check --all-targets -- -D warnings
    error: this loop never actually loops
       --> tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs:652:9
    error: could not compile `registry-check` (test "claims") due to 1 previous error

`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is one of the four mandatory checks in
AGENTS.md ("Mandatory Checks After Substantive Changes") and is stage 5 of
`scripts/check.sh`. It is red on main, so no pane can produce a green run of the
gate its own handoff requires.

Introduced by `438cff2` ("make 'every ID has a live checker' fail on the empty set",
bead fgdb-fginv-spine-zero-live-checkers-v05b). Not a regression in behaviour — the
test logic is correct and v05b's control does fire. It is purely a lint failure that
was never observed because the increment was verified with standalone rustc, which
does not apply the workspace `[lints]` table.

CONTROL: every other target passes. Measured at the same commit:

    cargo clippy -p registry-check --lib --bins --test identity --test metamorphic \
      --test satisfiability --test spine --test architecture_decisions \
      --test threat_model --test workspace_topology --test unsafe_ledger \
      --test violation_witnesses -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile

So `claims` is the only red target, and the red is one lint at one site.

## Why the lint is right even though the code is

`promote_first_clause` (claims.rs:644) deliberately mutates only the first clause and
`break 'outer`. The name and doc comment both say so. Clippy's `never_loops` is
therefore not reporting a logic error — the inner `for` genuinely never iterates
twice, and saying that with a loop is what the lint exists to catch.

The fix is an idiomatic first-element take rather than a loop-and-break, e.g.

    if let Some(clause) = r
        .invariants
        .invariants
        .iter_mut()
        .flat_map(|invariant| invariant.clauses.iter_mut())
        .next()
    { ... }

which is also shorter and removes the label.

## Note on a diagnostic that is NOT this bug

Every cargo invocation in this workspace prints

    error: unclosed table, expected `]`
     --> .../asupersync-.../tests/fixtures/migration_readiness_planner/malformed/Cargo.toml:1:9

from a deliberately-malformed fixture inside the asupersync git checkout. It is
NON-FATAL: cargo prints it and exits 0. Confirmed here by `cargo fmt --check` and the
scoped clippy run above both succeeding with it present. It is worth knowing because
it reads exactly like a build failure and it is the mechanism behind
fgdb-g0-spine-e2e-red-measures-harness-not-spine-iy7e, where a gate script's build
step could not fail the run.

## Acceptance

1. `cargo clippy -p registry-check --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 at a clean HEAD.
2. The v05b vacuity control still fires — promoting a clause must still make the
   liveness sweep go red. The rewrite must not quietly stop mutating anything.
3. Whoever lands it states in the commit that standalone rustc does not run clippy, so
   a rustc-verified increment still owes one cargo clippy before the gate is claimed.
close_reason:
ALREADY FIXED, NOW MEASURED. Verified green by pane3 at HEAD 238a14c. The fix landed in dd7749b
(pane4, 23:38Z) under a DIFFERENT bead (fgdb-clause-promotion-to-live-is-unguarded-nllh), which is
why this one stayed open: it was unclosed, not unfixed. I did not take dd7749b's commit message on
faith -- its own last paragraph says "clippy aborted at the first error, so anything behind it is
still unmeasured", so a second error could have been hiding behind the one it cleared. There is not.

THE GATE, BOTH FORMS, exit 0. Run locally against the warm CARGO_TARGET_DIR, build-2 held:
  cargo clippy -p registry-check --all-targets -- -D warnings   exit 0, 5.07s   (acceptance 1)
  cargo clippy --all-targets      -- -D warnings                exit 0, 1m45s  (the AGENTS.md form)

`]`` diagnostic that THIS BEAD already documents as non-fatal -- 1 occurrence, cargo prints it and

VACUITY CONTROL, AND IT FIRES. A green clippy run only means something if that invocation could
have gone red on this defect, so I asked it directly. Lock-free, no build slot, no working-tree
write: clippy-driver against the private rlib, on the two claims.rs files taken byte-for-byte from
git rather than re-typed.
  claims.rs @ HEAD 238a14c   0 diagnostics
  claims.rs @ dd7749b^       exactly 1 error: "this loop never actually loops" (+ "aborting due to

Same driver, same flags, same rlib; only the file differs. So the zero above is a measurement, not
an absence of one.

title: g0 e2e gates abort on the first failure: one stale assertion hid 92 others in g0_identity_e2e.sh
close_reason: Population measured, and it refuted the bead: 1 of 3 tally gates was fail-fast (identity), not 6 of 6. Fixed that, plus the 3-of-3 no-tally-on-abort defect. 3 independent pins now name 3 of 3 instead of 1 of 3; 99 assertions run instead of 6. f86d770 + 9c0d3c1.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED (pane4, 2026-07-26) while closing fgdb-su5y, at clean HEAD via a git-archive snapshot:

  bash scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh   -> exit 1, "7 passed", aborted
  same script, census constants fixed -> exit 0, "99 passed, 0 failed"

One stale census constant at line 211 kept 92 of the gate's 99 assertions from ever executing, for every pane, from e7b6f09 onward. die() at scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:46 does `PASS=..; log ..; exit 1` -- it exits on the FIRST divergence, so the gate's cost of a single stale pin is not one red assertion, it is the whole rest of the file going dark.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN DEFECT AND NOT A DUPLICATE OF su5y. su5y was "this number is wrong"; that is fixed and cannot recur, because the numbers are derived now. This is "one wrong thing anywhere in the file silently withdraws the other 92 checks", which is untouched and applies to every registered g0 gate:

  scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh              die() -> exit 1
  scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh
  scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh
  scripts/g0_topology_e2e.sh
  scripts/g0_threat_e2e.sh
  scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh

The failure mode is specific and has already been observed three times tonight (g0_spine_e2e, k2mj, the FG-INV empty set): a gate is red for a reason nobody owns, everyone learns the red is not theirs, and the gate stops being read. Fail-fast makes that worse in a way fail-slow does not, because the first red also determines how much evidence anyone gets about the rest of the tree. A pane that reds at assertion 7 cannot tell whether assertions 8..99 would have passed, so it cannot even tell whether ITS change is implicated.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, for whoever takes it. The scripts already count PASS and FAIL and already print "N passed, M failed" at the end; die() is what prevents M from ever exceeding 1. The change is to let non-structural assertion failures accumulate and exit nonzero at the end, while keeping hard exits for the failures that genuinely invalidate everything after them (subject build failure, the checker producing no JSONL at all, a missing fixture). Those two classes are already distinguishable in the source: assertions go through jsonl_line_has_all/ok/die, whereas setup failures do not.

NOT SPECULATIVE: the 7-vs-99 number above is the measured amplification on one gate on one clean tree. Whoever takes this should measure the same on the other five before deciding scope -- a gate whose assertions genuinely depend on each other may be correct to abort.

WATCH FOR: the fix must not turn a red gate green. Mutation-prove that a single failing assertion still exits nonzero and still names itself, and that the terminal "N passed, M failed" line reports M correctly, or fail-slow becomes fail-never.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
POPULATION MEASURED FIRST, AND IT REFUTES THIS BEAD'S OWN GUESS (pane4, 2026-07-26).

I filed this bead saying "the same shape is in all six registered g0 gates". That was speculation and it is WRONG. Of the seven registered live script gates, only THREE keep an assertion tally at all, and of those three exactly ONE is fail-fast:

  g0_claims_e2e.sh:26     die() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); log ...; }            fail-slow
  g0_spine_e2e.sh:49      die() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); log ...; }            fail-slow
  g0_identity_e2e.sh:115  die() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); log ...; exit 1; }    THE OUTLIER

All three end with the byte-identical three-line verdict block (`result: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed` / `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1` / `ALL GREEN`), so all three were written for a tally that can say "3 failed". identity's `exit 1` makes its OWN verdict block unreachable in exactly the case the block exists for. Not a regression: it was born that way in e8ca589, while claims (c782b0e) and spine (ae97070) were born without it. Three authors, never converged.

The other four registered gates -- g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh, g0_threat_e2e.sh, g0_topology_e2e.sh, w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh -- keep NO tally and end on bare `exit 1` under `set -e`, where every command is a terminal site. Different design; converting them is a rewrite, not this bead.

MASKING, THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION, WITH NAMED NUMBERS. Three independent stale pins planted in three different assertions in three different phases (phase 0 slice count, phase 0 completion event, phase 3k maintenance-proof violation code); none causes another:

  shipped die() (exit 1)   exit 1, names 1 of 3, ran 6 of 99 assertions, NO tally line
  fixed   die()            exit 1, names 3 of 3, ran all 99, "result: 96 passed, 3 failed"

The three it names are exactly the three planted, one per phase. And the same gate on the REAL defect that opened this bead: fgdb-su5y's stale census constant ended the run at assertion 8, so 91 of 99 never executed. (My filing said 92; the measured number is 91 -- 7 PASS + 1 FAIL reached.)

NO TALLY AT ALL ON A RED RUN. Because `exit 1` lives inside die(), it jumps past the verdict. Checked against every archived failing run of this gate from the su5y work: ZERO `result:` lines in each. Green runs print `result: 99 passed, 0 failed`; red runs print nothing. The one case where a reader needs the count is the one case the gate refuses to give it.

A SECOND DEFECT, AND THIS ONE IS 3 OF 3. The tally lives at the bottom, so any `set -e` abort skips it in ALL THREE tally gates. Measured by making one registry unreadable so the staging `cp` fails mid-run:

  before   claims exit 1, ZERO tally lines, last line "cp: cannot open ..."
           spine  exit 1, ZERO tally lines, last line "cp: cannot open ..."
  after    claims "ABORTED before the verdict (exit 1): 1 passed, 4 failed so far;
                   every assertion after this point did not run"
           spine  "ABORTED before the verdict (exit 1): 2 passed, 4 failed so far; ..."

Before, the last gate-shaped line a reader saw was a PASS, and a truncated log read exactly like a whole one. Fail-slow becomes fail-never if the run dies before the count prints, so the fix is a trap, not just a die() change.

STRUCTURAL FAILURES STILL END THE RUN, and now say so. Breaking lib.rs so the subject cannot build: exit 2 preserved, "FATAL: building registry-check from this tree failed", plus "ABORTED before the verdict (exit 2): 0 passed, 0 failed so far". A build failure can no longer be mistaken for a partially-passing run.

DOES NOT TURN RED GREEN: one planted pin -> exit 1, the assertion named, "result: 98 passed, 1 failed". Green unchanged and re-measured after every mutation: identity 99/0 exit 0, claims 16/0 exit 0, spine 13/0 exit 0.

LANDED SO FAR: f86d770, the trap on g0_claims_e2e.sh and g0_spine_e2e.sh (not under the catalog token).

STILL OWED: g0_identity_e2e.sh -- the die() fix plus the same trap. It is under the catalog write token, which pane2-uyt2 has held for 11m against a 10m TTL. I am NOT stealing it: token.sh only reports a hold stale at ttl+20m, so this one is not yet stale by the tool's own rule, and an expired TTL is not proof the holder is gone. Polling for it; the patch is measured, linted and staged in the scratchpad, and lands the moment the token frees.

BUILD SLOT: build-1 held and renewed twice, because the measurement matrix is six full gate runs and each rebuilds its private subject.

FILED SEPARATELY: fgdb-m2c1, the same two directions one layer down -- scripts/check.sh reported SIX red cargo-test artifacts from ONE compile error in tests/claims.rs, and the other five test binaries were never built or run, so their status is unknown and reported as RED. check.sh's own harness is already fail-slow and correct (7 of 7 core, 19 of 19 registered, "0 unrun" printed); the defect is what one `cargo test --workspace` can tell it.

title: A06 blocker: classify twelve W12 core families before final unions and fields
description:
## Scope

Resolve the remaining Appendix A a06 identity boundary without guessing. At archive HEAD e6b75e0f34340a7894bb0ce2d39ce8e3239dd6fb, twelve a06 top-level candidates remain unclassified. A hard-signal audit found zero existing registrations, zero reservations, zero whole-schema unions, and zero StrongRef-target signals across all twelve, so no kind mint is source-forced under the settled rules.

## Exact blocked rows

Seven command-looking Spec families require the normative command-type classification promised by plan section 5.1: GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionCompletionSpec, ShardKeyDestroyApplySpec, ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec, ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionSpec, and ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec.

Three record-shaped owners require the non-generic owner disposition ruling tracked by fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd: MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, NoShardEffect, and PreparedRootHeader<Role>. Census outermost containment is not a derivation; it was explicitly downgraded after fourteen landed logical counterexamples.

Two name-only candidates require source adjudication rather than a mint: ApplyActivationProjection is already projected as the CheckpointFieldRecipe arm, while ShardCertificateLedger is named only as a prose-defined replica-local map and has no exact structural body.

The two remaining union rows and four arms are blocked on the two unclassified Spec hosts: GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec.exact_target_plan.record.meta_local has SOURCE order None=0x0001, Some=0x0002; ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec.expected_local_key_registry_state has SOURCE order Active=0x0001, Retiring=0x0002. Source order is recorded here for the eventual landing.

The field layer has zero additional mechanically landable rows. On the banked 439-row census, 178 rows have no exact type in source and the l6xd class-decision radius is 131 rows; those counts overlap and must not be added. A further 104 reference-shaped rows require the two-direction construction-order sweep, with smaller no-precedent and inline-union or array buckets already recorded on the parent bead.

## Success criteria

Classify or explicitly adjudicate all twelve candidates from a normative registry or owner ruling; land the two host-gated unions and four source-ordered arms; then re-run the field dependency filter. Do not use suffix census, dominance, or outermost containment as a minting derivation.

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
RE-DERIVED AT HEAD 7905c27 BY pane3 (2026-07-27). SCOPE CONFIRMED — this is the
FIRST inherited premise tonight to survive re-derivation intact (eight of nine
had collapsed). Measured by driving appendix_a::load_and_verify, not by reading.

## Scope holds, exactly

  a06 top-level candidates            42
  still unclassified                  12   <- matches the bead
  reservations across all twelve       0   <- matches
  StrongRef targets across all twelve  0   <- matches
  a06 field candidates declared      439   <- matches
  a06 durable_fields rows landed      68

Every one of the twelve named symbols is present, `identity_class =
"unclassified"`, 0 reservations, 0 StrongRef targets. The hard-signal audit the
bead recorded at archive HEAD e6b75e0f still reads the same at 7905c27.

## NEW: the twelve partition by source_kind, which the bead did not record

  confirmed   6   GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionCompletionSpec,
                  MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, PreparedRootHeader,
                  ShardKeyDestroyApplySpec, ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionSpec
  ambiguous   4   GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec, NoShardEffect,
                  ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec, ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec
  name-only   2   ApplyActivationProjection, ShardCertificateLedger

This cuts differently from the bead's 7-Spec / 3-record / 2-name-only grouping
and matters: four of the seven "command-looking Spec families" are `ambiguous`,
not `confirmed`, so they need adjudication BEFORE any command-type question
reaches them.

## THE 7 SPECS ARE BLOCKED ON AN ABSENT REGISTRY, NOT ON A RULING

The bead says they "require the normative command-type classification promised by
plan section 5.1". Plan §5.1 does not merely promise it — it SPECIFIES it, in
full, and names two registries:

    `command_contracts.toml`            one row per role-valid command arm
    `command_type_classification.toml`  assigns every independently addressable
        normative input-looking type "including every type whose stable name ends
        in `Spec`" exactly one of six classes: RegisteredCommandInput{...},
        PreOrderArtifact, CertificateInput, ResultOnly, ProjectionInput, RuntimeOnly

MEASURED: NEITHER FILE EXISTS. `ls registries/` shows 20 registries; both of
these are absent. So the blocker is not a decision the owner has to make — it is
a normative registry the plan fully specifies and nobody has materialized. That
is a different and much more tractable problem, and it should be filed as its own
bead rather than waited on here.

§5.1 also settles the reasoning trap in this bead's own wording, verbatim:

    "A suffix conveys no semantics. In particular an ordinary schema/index
     definition is a `SchemaOp` carried by a transaction; it cannot silently
     acquire a catalog/schema/index control command merely because prose calls it
     a specification."

So "seven command-looking Spec families" is precisely the inference the plan
forbids. Nothing may be minted from the `Spec` suffix.

## THE xfrc STANDING RULE IS NOW AT ITS SECOND CASE — OWNER DECISION NEEDED

OWNER_RULINGS.md, xfrc ruling, closing line:

    "Standing rule this establishes: when both class instruments are silent,
     `strongref_target = 0` decides for WIRE. Record it as a law if it survives a
     second case."

All twelve a06 candidates are exactly that configuration: both class instruments
silent, `strongref_target = 0`, measured above. This IS the second case, and it
is 12 symbols rather than xfrc's 12 — a substantial second sample.

If the owner promotes the standing rule to law, it disposes of the 10 non-name-only
candidates WITHOUT the absent registry, because "no StrongRef holds it, so no
object identity is used" is independent of whether a Spec is a command. That
would unblock this bead today. I have NOT applied it: it is a standing rule
awaiting exactly this confirmation, and applying it unilaterally is the kind of
durable-format guess this bead exists to prevent.

## The other two groups

* 2 name-only (ApplyActivationProjection, ShardCertificateLedger) — these are the
  definition-without-structural-body shape that OWES NOTHING; the settled
  precedent is to adjudicate them as non-obligations, not mint. Note
  ApplyActivationProjection already carries 2 targets, consistent with the bead's
  note that it is projected as the CheckpointFieldRecipe arm.
* 3 record-shaped (MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, NoShardEffect,
  PreparedRootHeader<Role>) — the bead routes these to
  fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd, WHICH IS NOW CLOSED. Its
  ruling covers identity_class for FIELDS carrying record-shaped wire types, which
  is adjacent but not identical to classifying a top-level candidate, so I am
  flagging rather than asserting that the dependency is discharged. Someone should
  confirm the closed ruling actually reaches these three.

## What I did not do, and why

No rows landed. Ten of twelve turn on either an absent registry or an owner
promotion; the other two are non-obligations that want an adjudication row, and
adjudication rows are catalog writes that should go in one commit with whatever
resolves the ten. The build freeze did not constrain any of this — every number
above came from the lock-free rustc path (probe at <scratch>/d2ax/probe.rs, lib
rebuilt in ~7s, probe runs in 3.5s).

## Exact next steps

1. OWNER: promote or reject the xfrc standing rule on this second case. That is
   the single highest-leverage decision; it unblocks 10 of 12.
2. File a bead for materializing `command_type_classification.toml` and
   `command_contracts.toml` from §5.1 — they are fully specified there and are
   G0-load-bearing well beyond a06 (§5.1 makes them a two-way total bijection with
   generated exhaustive-match tests).
3. Confirm whether closed l6xd reaches the three record-shaped owners.

title: CommittedEffectCapsule order erratum: 30 -> 10 retires the one census-DAG Erratum waiver
description:
Landed c705b7b (fgdb-owlp) enforces the construction DAG over CENSUS references. Its waiver table carries exactly two rows and ONE is explicitly typed Erratum rather than Exception, because a waiver that should be a repair is a documented lie. This bead is that repair, so the waiver can be retired rather than inherited.

THE EDGE: CommitCommand.capsule_ref : StrongRef<CommittedEffectCapsule>
  CommitCommand@10 retains CommittedEffectCapsule@30 -> a future result.

WINDOW, DERIVED FROM BOTH DIRECTIONS, expanding union anchors (following only target_schema_id under-reports retainers and inverted this verdict on my first pass):
  OWNER  CommitCommand is pinned <= 10 by CommitCapsule@10 through a landed reference-union arm, so it cannot rise to 30. That half IS empty.
  TARGET CommittedEffectCapsule is NOT pinned. It retains only AuthorizationDecisionRecord@10 so it needs >= 10, and it is retained only by CommitMarker@30 so it needs <= 30. Order 10 satisfies both.

THE REPAIR: re-order CommittedEffectCapsule 30 -> 10 in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml. construction_order is NOT pinned, so this is a mechanical catalog repair, and the cascade check says it is a leaf move -- no other kind's window closes.

WHEN DONE: delete the CensusDagVerdict::Erratum row from CENSUS_DAG_WAIVERS in tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs so the law enforces the edge for real. census_dag_names_a_future_result_the_waiver_does_not_cover already proves the law names an uncovered edge, so removal is verifiable.

NOT THIS: the second waiver, CommitCommand.final_certification_reservation_ref -> LocalFinalCertificationReservation@30, has BOTH windows empty (target pinned >= 20 because it retains LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec@20) and is typed Exception. Reference strength or shape, not order.

Successor to the CLOSED fgdb-a10-command-delta-ooy1, which the waiver row currently names and which cannot carry this because it is closed.
notes:
=== pane3, VERIFIED at HEAD b4e50d9 with the real checker. VERDICT: the landed repair is CORRECT and load-bearing, but the window it cites is WRONG at HEAD. ===

WHAT I CONFIRMED. 305af7e landed CEC 30 -> 10 (catalog kind + its 3 field rows +
2 regenerated projections) and deleted the Erratum row, leaving one Exception row.
Mutation control, in a scratch copy of the tree: restore CEC to 30 consistently and
the appendix run produces exactly ONE violation, census_dag_future_result. So the
law is live, it does fire on that edge, and 30 IS red today. The 30 -> 10 move was
necessary and is not a no-op. pane2's warning that '10 is the riskiest legal value'
was right about the risk and wrong about the direction: 30 was never legal.

WHAT IS WRONG. The waiver comment now standing in appendix_a.rs says:
    CommitCommand@10 -> CEC   => CEC <= 10
    CommitMarker@30  -> CEC   => CEC <= 30
    CEC -> AuthorizationDecisionRecord@10 => CEC >= 10
    window = [10, 10]
It enumerates only the FLAT-form outbound. CEC also retains
    CEC -[resource_transition_refs]-> ResourceLedgerTransition@15
spelled in the source bracket-array form 'resource_transition_refs[StrongRef<
ResourceLedgerTransition<Local>>]', which forces CEC >= 15. The TRUE window at HEAD
is EMPTY [15, 10]: 30 violates the upper bound and 10 violates the lower one, and
CommittedEffectCapsule has NO legal construction_order today.

WHY NOBODY SAW IT, and it is not a reading error. The census-DAG law CANNOT see that
edge: it derives family = exact.split('<').next(), which on '[StrongRef<T>]' yields
'[StrongRef' -- unregistered -- so the law 'continue's and fails OPEN. 139 census
candidates are dropped this way; 2 of them violate today. Full denominators, the
mutation proof and the repair are on fgdb-h1al.

SO THE PRECONDITION pane2 SET WAS NEVER MEASURED. The ask was 'measure CEC's outbound
CENSUS targets, take max(orders) = L, land only if L == 10'. L is 15, not 10. The
repair landed on the flat-form reading alone, and the gate could not contradict it
because the gate shares the same blind spot. This is the standing caution again, one
layer down: SILENCE FROM A PARTIAL READER IS NOT ABSENCE -- and here the partial
