comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TWO COUPLED DEFECTS ON ONE a01-OWNED ROW, both blocking a02 completion and neither resolvable inside a02. All probe-derived; controlled where a bare absence would otherwise have been the finding.

THE ROW: `a01:wire-type:placement-descriptor-without-id`, wire_type_id 0x001e, status "reserved", encoding_context "Appendix A reference-semantics family PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (a01); exact member layout per plan lines 1388-1444".

DEFECT 1 — STATUS INCOHERENCE, and it is the same class already fixed once in this slice. `PlacementRecord` is an ACTIVE physical kind whose FG-INV-09 identity law is BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)). So an active identity-recomputation transcript rests on a non-live row. That is exactly the incoherence that FORCED status=active for CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest and EncodingDescriptorWithoutId in 352bccd, where CiphertextRecord and EncodingRecord are the active dependants.
MEASURED CATALOG-WIDE, not asserted: screening all 61 wire types against the rule "active iff at least one already-ACTIVE row references it", 41 conform, 19 are foundational primitives that are active without a named referent because they are used via allowed_containing_schemas ["*"] (StrongRef, WeakDigest, MarkerRef, AuthorityBoundHeader, HlcTimestamp and similar — my referent detector only finds name mentions, so it undercounts them), and PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is THE ONLY ROW IN THE CATALOG that is reserved while having an active referent. One row, one exception, and it is this one.
FIX: flip 0x001e to active. It is an a01 row, so an a02 increment must not do it unilaterally.

DEFECT 2 — THE PINNED BODY CONTRADICTS a02's SOURCE, and this is why a02's placement family cannot be modelled at all. Three renderings exist and two disagree materially:
  plan:280   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
  a01:1443   { encoding_id, root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id,
               ContiguousSpan { root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len,
                                root_symbol_inventory_digest } }
  a02:1449   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
a01 renames two members, root-prefixes two more, and INLINES ContiguousSpan instead of carrying the `location_form` union at all — consistent with a root placement always being contiguous. a02 and plan:280 agree with each other and disagree with a01. The landed row's encoding_context pins the layout to lines 1388-1444, i.e. the a01 rendering.
DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES, all three observable today:
 (a) The census emits ConflictingCandidateEvidence on the family ("the same schema source key has divergent structural bodies").
 (b) Because two bodies compete, `location_form = ContiguousSpan{...} | Explicit{...}` never parses as a union. a02 is the ONLY slice of 21 with zero union candidates and zero arm candidates — controlled: every other slice is nonzero (a01 13/36, a03 49/129, a07 92/245, a15 51/162, a16 31/79, a21 64/196), so the zero is real rather than a broken probe.
 (c) One arm of a closed union is registered standalone and the other does not exist anywhere: ContiguousSpan is a02 wire type 0x000a, active; `Explicit` has 0 catalog rows and 0 wire_types rows. That asymmetry is not a design choice — it is what happens when the union is unparseable and someone registers the arm they needed.

RESOLUTION SPACE, deliberately not chosen — all three are a01+a02 cross-slice and (2) amends a normative appendix:
 (A) Erratum reconciling the two bodies to one rendering, then re-pin the a01 row's encoding_context and let location_form parse.
 (B) Widen the a01 row to cover both renderings explicitly, if the intent is genuinely one schema with a root specialisation.
 (C) Rule them TWO schemas that collide on a name — a general PlacementDescriptorWithoutId and a root-specialised one — and rename one. Note ContiguousSpan's landed allowed_containing_schemas is already ["RootBootstrap", "PlacementRecord"], which is weak evidence for the two-context reading.
My own lean is (C) or (A); I am not deciding it.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG HERE, stated so nobody re-derives it:
 * Not an ordering problem. a02 cannot carry a construction_order at all — [[physical_kind]] and [[wire_type]] rows have no construction_order key, and the DAG is evaluated over field rows resolved through logical kinds.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ANSWER TO "BAD ROW OR MISSING LAW": IT IS A MISSING LAW — and more precisely a MODELLING GAP, which is the worse of the two. Plus a CORRECTION to my own claim in this bead and in commit 2db58b3.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I wrote that PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is "the ONLY row in the catalog that is reserved while having an active referent". THAT IS WRONG. It was only true of the population I screened — wire types. Sweeping ALL classes for "an active row that names a reserved row", there are TWO:
    PlacementRecord (active [[physical_kind]], a02)      -> PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (reserved [[wire_type]], a01)
    LocalCommandOrigin.RecoveryBridge (active [[wire_type]], g0) -> RecoveryBridgeSpec (reserved [[logical_kind]], a19)
All four statuses individually verified. This is the same false-negative shape I have now hit three times: a probe confined to one population, reported as a catalog-wide fact. "Only row in the catalog" should have been "only wire type", and I did not control it across classes before writing it down.

WHY THE CHECKER PERMITS IT — three findings, each controlled:
 1. NO LAW COMPARES A REFERRER'S STATUS TO ITS REFERENT'S. Grepping identity.rs for containing.status / containing_kind.status returns nothing. There is no active-implies-active rule anywhere.
 2. `reserved` IS DELIBERATELY REFERENCEABLE, and correctly so. It appears in the valid-status set at identity.rs:872 and :1620, and the only lifecycle rejections are for "retired" | "experimental" (identity.rs:1425 for parents, :2628 for union arm targets). That is right: the whole catalog is built from reserved shells that legitimately reference one another before activation, so a blanket "reject reserved targets" rule would be wrong and would break a15's entire key-destruction family.
 3. AND THE DECISIVE ONE: for this instance there is NO EDGE TO CHECK. The [[physical_kind]] row schema is exactly {identity_law, max_size_bytes, name, owning_identity, record_kind, row_id, slice_id, status, transcript} — it has NO typed target field of any kind. PlacementRecord's dependency on PlacementDescriptorWithoutId exists ONLY inside the transcript free-text string, "BLAKE3(\"fgdb:placement:v1\" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId))". Same for the second instance: the dependency lives in an encoding_context string. So the checker is not failing to apply a law it has; it has no representation of the dependency at all.

SO THE VERDICT, stated as asked:
 * The ROW is wrong and should be flipped to active — cheap, a01's call, defect (1) of this bead.
 * There IS a missing law, and the correct statement of it is NARROW: "an ACTIVE row's identity law or encoding context may not depend on a NON-ACTIVE row." Not "reserved is unreferenceable", which would be false.
 * But that law is currently UNENFORCEABLE for exactly the rows where it matters, because physical-kind and wire-type dependencies are expressed in prose rather than as typed edges. Implementing it therefore means one of: (a) parse schema names out of transcript/encoding_context and check their lifecycle — cheap, slightly fragile, and it would catch both known instances today; or (b) give physical_kind and wire_type a typed dependency field so the edge exists in the model — more faithful, and it would also make FG-INV-09's "identity recomputation from REGISTERED transcripts" mechanically checkable rather than prose-checkable, which is what let CiphertextId and EncodingId sit on unregistered structures until 352bccd.
 I lean (b) as the real fix with (a) as an immediate guard, but this is a checker-contract decision above a slice increment, and the two known instances are in a01/a02 and g0/a19 — four slices — so it wants its own bead and owner rather than being folded into this one.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD: defect (1) is still real and still a01's to flip, but it is now one of two instances of a class rather than a unique anomaly, which strengthens the case for the law and weakens the case for treating the row as a one-off typo. Defect (2), the divergent body, is unaffected by any of this.

comments.text:
BODY CONTRADICTION RESOLVED — AND THE BEAD'S CAUSAL MODEL IS WRONG. Measured at HEAD 52fae53 against a `git archive HEAD` snapshot, never the working tree (pane6-a17 has uncommitted checker edits). Every number below carries a control; the census probe refused to run until my extracted appendix matched the catalog's own pinned sha256 (71a48b67…, MATCH=true), which caught an off-by-one trailing newline on the first attempt.

=== 1. WHICH BODY IS AUTHORITATIVE: a02:1449, AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS ===
The plan names PlacementDescriptorWithoutId at exactly 3 lines appendix-wide plus narrative (280, 1443, 1449) — enumerated over the WHOLE plan, not the owning slice.
  * 280  (narrative)  `{encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form}`, location_form "either one fully described contiguous span … or an explicit canonical symbol/locator inventory"
  * 1449 (a02, DEFINITIONAL) "`PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` **is** `{encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form}`, where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{…} | Explicit{…}`"
  * 1443 (a01) "…reproduce the root's exact `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest`, complete `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`, and **specialized** `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId {…}` byte-for-byte"
THE DECIDING WORD IS "specialized", and it is not my gloss. (i) The adjective run at 1443 is deliberate and contrastive — cipher is "exact", encoding is "complete", placement alone is "specialized". (ii) Plan line 344, the §5.1 RootBootstrap narrative, independently says RootBootstrap supplies "a complete **specialized `ContiguousSpan` placement descriptor** containing placement epoch, failure-domain policy and domain ID, segment/offset/length, and symbol-inventory digest" — which enumerates exactly a01:1443's members, including the tell-tale "policy AND domain ID" pair. (iii) "specialized `<Name>`" is an established plan idiom for an instantiation of a named schema, used the same way at 966, 1404, 1804 and 2407.
MEMBER CORRESPONDENCE IS 1:1 WITH ZERO UNMATCHED: 4 of 8 member names are byte-identical (encoding_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len) and every remaining one is a mechanical requalification (root_placement_epoch/placement_epoch, root_failure_domain_id/failure_domain_id, root_symbol_inventory_digest/symbol_inventory_digest, failure_domain_policy_id/failure_domain_policy). Two independent schemas would not share 4 inner member names exactly.
So the answer is the bead's option (B) — ONE schema with a root specialisation — not (A) or (C), and it needs NO normative amendment. This CONFIRMS what a621c9e already landed: the row's encoding_context now cites 1449 as authoritative and calls 1443 "the specialized root-bootstrap RECONSTRUCTION … not a competing schema". I derived that independently from the source before reading the row, so this is a convergence, not a restatement. DEFECT 2 IS CLOSED.

=== 2. THE BEAD'S CAUSAL CLAIM (b) IS FALSE — RESOLVING THE BODIES DOES NOT UNBLOCK THE UNION ===
The bead states "Because two bodies compete, `location_form = ContiguousSpan{…} | Explicit{…}` never parses as a union." I tested that by rewriting the appendix in memory (line count asserted unchanged, so slice ranges stay valid) and re-running census_appendix_source:
  BASELINE (HEAD)                                  a02 unions=0 arms=0
  VARIANT A: reconcile a01:1443 members to a02      a02 unions=0 arms=0   <- bodies fixed, union still dead
  VARIANT C: rename a01:1443 to RootPlacement…      a02 unions=0 arms=0   <- bodies split, union still dead
Both variants DO clean the schema: under A and C the family collapses to exactly the 4 correct fields {encoding_id, failure_domain_policy, location_form, placement_epoch}, where the baseline census currently merges both renderings into a 6-field Frankenstein carrying placement_epoch AND root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy AND failure_domain_policy_id. So the body conflict is real and worth closing — it just is not what blocks the union. The two defects are INDEPENDENT.

=== 3. THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: THE UNION NAME IS snake_case ===
The census's union-name extractor is `trailing_upper_identifier` at tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs:1996-2004, whose last line is `(start < bytes.len() && bytes[start].is_ascii_uppercase()).then_some(...)`. A union whose name does not begin with an ASCII uppercase letter is never recognised. Single-variable experiments, everything else in the sentence held byte-identical:
  location_form   (baseline, snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  zz_unique_form  (arbitrary snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  qq_other_form   (arbitrary snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  LocationForm    (CapitalCase)               unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
  ZzUniqueForm    (arbitrary CapitalCase)     unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
  Location_form   (ONE-CHARACTER FLIP l->L)   unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
The one-character flip is the decisive control: identical name, identical arms, identical everything, and the outcome moves 0 -> 1. Both arms parse the moment the initial is uppercase, so the arm bodies were never the problem either.
IT IS A SOURCE ERRATUM, NOT A CHECKER GAP, and that is measured rather than asserted: across the whole appendix there are 11 backticked `Name = Arm{…} | Arm{…}` constructs, 10 CapitalCase and exactly ONE lowercase-initial — location_form. The checker convention is right and parses every other one; a02:1449 is a lone outlier that names its union after the field instead of giving it a type name. Widening the checker to accept snake_case union names would change census semantics for all 573 appendix unions to rescue a single site, which is the wrong trade.

=== 4. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH ===
fgdb-bpt6 ("the location_form closed union and its Explicit arm are unregistered and unparseable") is NOT blocked by this bead's body contradiction. It is blocked by the naming erratum in §3. The dbvf -> bpt6 edge as currently justified is mis-attributed; closing dbvf's remaining work will not unblock bpt6 by itself. Filing the erratum separately.

=== 5. WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, WITH ITS COST MEASURED ===
Defect 1 (status 0x001e reserved -> active) is still open and still correct: PlacementRecord is an active physical kind whose FG-INV-09 transcript names PlacementDescriptorWithoutId, so an active identity law rests on a non-live row. I flipped it in the snapshot to price it rather than guess:
  load_catalog_file            -> 1 violation, projection_registry_assignment_drift (wire_types::registry)
  appendix-regenerate          -> exit 1, projection_files=0 changed_files=0, violation on appendix_a_catalog::catalog_row
So the flip is NOT a one-line edit. `registry_assignment_drift` hashes "released codes, tags, names, LIFECYCLE STATES, and union arms", so a status change moves the assignment pin and, per the sibling message, "an epoch changes only with an intentional row add/retire and pin update" — it needs the wire_types epoch bump plus the assignment re-pin plus projection regeneration, then the loader-invisible sites. From the build-environment trail, a WIRE bump moves `target_source_assignment_sha256` in scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh but must NOT touch the phase-2h negative fixture (that one targets logical_object_kinds only) and must NOT touch `ordinary_top_level_union_fixture` in tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs (that tracks the durable_fields epoch). Bounded, but a real pin chase under the catalog token, not a drive-by.

comments.text:
RESERVATION DISPOSITION RESOLVED — AND DEFECT 1's PRESCRIBED FIX MUST NOT BE LANDED. Measured at HEAD a6cd40f in a `git archive HEAD` snapshot; the live tree was never edited. Both findings carry controls in both directions.

=== 1. RESERVATION DISPOSITION: NONE, AND NONE MAY BE ADDED ===
Both sides of the bijection were measured rather than inferred.
  * Catalog side: 813 [[reservation]] blocks at HEAD; the count naming PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is ZERO. Controls: the first reserved symbol re-resolves in the file (true), a fabricated symbol does not (false).
  * Source side: census_plan_references over the whole plan yields 1150 distinct symbols; PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is NOT among the StrongRef targets. Controls: two known-reserved families (ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut, ActiveMetaProjectionRoot) both read true; a fabricated family reads false. ContiguousSpan and PlacementRecord also read false, consistent with wire/physical families being referenced structurally rather than by StrongRef.
VERDICT: the family is correctly unreserved and MUST STAY unreserved. Adding a [[reservation]] row would fire reference_source_reservation_orphan and break the frozen 813 = 813 partition. There is also NOTHING TO MINT: the family already exists as a01:wire-type:placement-descriptor-without-id at wire_type_id 0x001e, so the "mint above 0x051d" route does not apply either — that route is for families with no row at all. No rows to land.

=== 2. THE STATUS FLIP IS FORBIDDEN BY A LANDED LAW — THE ROW IS RESERVED BY DESIGN ===
This bead says "FIX: flip 0x001e to active". I priced that flip end-to-end and it is not merely expensive, it is illegal. tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs:4104-4112, test idr_a01_incomplete_activation_cohort_is_reserved, asserts:
    let wire = r.wire.filter(|row| (0x0012..=0x0026).contains(&row.wire_type_id));
    assert_eq!(wire.len(), 21);
    assert!(wire.iter().all(|row| row.status == "reserved"),
            "incomplete A01 wire rows must not be consumable");
0x001e sits inside 0x0012..=0x0026. The cohort, enumerated at HEAD, is 21 rows and 21 of 21 are reserved:
  0x0012 AppliedAbortRef            0x0013 AppliedControlRef        0x0014 AuditCandidateRef
  0x0015 AuthorityAppliedRef        0x0016 CertifiedRemoteStrongRef 0x0017 CommandRef
  0x0018 ConditionalCoordinateRef   0x0019 ConditionalGlobalCommandRef
  0x001a ConditionalGlobalTxnInputRef  0x001b ConditionalMarkerRef  0x001c ConditionalShardCommandRef
  0x001d ConsensusDomain            0x001e PlacementDescriptorWithoutId   0x001f RemoteObjectIdentity
  0x0020 StrongCiphertextRef        0x0021 StrongCommandRef         0x0022 StrongGlobalCommandRef
  0x0023 StrongShardCommandRef      0x0024 WeakGlobalCommandIdentity 0x0025 WeakMarkerIdentity
  0x0026 WeakShardCommandIdentity
CONTROL, and it is the one that matters: the test is GREEN at unmodified HEAD (1 passed) and RED with only my flip applied (1 failed, "incomplete A01 wire rows must not be consumable", 74 others still passing). So the failure is caused by the flip and by nothing else, and the law is real and currently satisfied.
THEREFORE the row is not reserved by oversight. It is held reserved as a member of a deliberate 21-row A01 incomplete-activation cohort, and it activates when A01's activation completes — together with CommandRef, StrongCommandRef and the other nineteen. The bead's framing of defect 1 as a one-row status typo is wrong, and so is the inference from the CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest/EncodingDescriptorWithoutId precedent in 352bccd: those two are a02 rows and are NOT in the a01 cohort range, which is exactly why they could be flipped individually and this one cannot.
The underlying observation the bead makes is still true and still worth keeping — an active PlacementRecord identity law does rest on a non-live row — but it is a KNOWN, BOUNDED consequence of holding A01 reserved, shared by every consumer of those 21 rows, not a defect in this row. It is discharged by A01 completing, not by a spot flip.

=== 3. WHAT THE FLIP WOULD HAVE COST, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT ===
For whoever activates the cohort later, the mechanics are now known and were dry-run to a clean loader in the snapshot: status flip -> registry_assignment_drift, because assignment_pins hashes "type|{id}|{name}|{kind}|{status}|{union}|{tag}" (identity.rs:1097-1113) and lifecycle state is inside the pin. The full set is exactly three files and six lines: registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml (row status + [[projection_epoch]] wire_types 12->13), registries/wire_types.toml (regenerated: registry_epoch 12->13, status), tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs (expected_epoch 12->13 at :1221, and const WIRE :1070 abfaaab5851ca67f -> the recomputed value the loader prints). appendix-regenerate then goes exit 0 with projection_files=6 changed_files=1 published_files=1. Two pin sites from the build-environment trail correctly do NOT move for a wire bump: the phase-2h negative fixture (logical_object_kinds only) and ordinary_top_level_union_fixture (durable_fields epoch). And scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh needs no hand edit — target_source_assignment_sha256 is DERIVED there via catalog_manifest_value, not hard-coded.

=== 4. STATE ===
No catalog write was made and no catalog token was taken, because the correct action turned out to be "do not edit". The live tree is untouched by me; the concurrent modification to registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml is another agent's [[target]] row work and touches no status or registry_epoch line. dbvf's defect 2 is closed (a621c9e, independently confirmed); defect 1 should be RECLASSIFIED from "flip this row" to "consequence of the A01 cohort hold, discharged by A01 activation", and the fgdb-bpt6 edge remains mis-attributed per my previous comment.

title: Appendix A source erratum: RegisteredStrongRef is by-value vocabulary with no spelled body
description:
RegisteredStrongRef is by-value vocabulary with no spelled body, and it is what actually blocks the '7 fields blocked by unresolved vocabulary' line in fgdb-27sr.

FOUR schemas name it BY VALUE, no wrapper:
  plan:1830  strong_dependency_refs[RegisteredStrongRef]
  plan:1854  terminal_floor_ref:RegisteredStrongRef
  plan:1926  delta_payload_ref:RegisteredStrongRef<DeltaPayload>
  plan:2039  typed_ref:RegisteredStrongRef   (MandatoryInventoryEntry.value.RetainedStrong)

The source defines it only as 'the closed generated union of role-legal typed strong-reference
encodings, never a raw ObjectId' -- the arms are GENERATED and never spelled. So the census
emits it as named-concept-no-body with zero arm candidates.

AND every field that names it is unlandable. That is a plan erratum, not a mint.

that the bare definition does not declare.

Fix requires the source to spell the arm set (or declare the generation rule normatively), after
which the family lands as a wire-backed union with an exact union_variant bijection.

Measured by pane2 under fgdb-27sr.

title: No gate runs a prover: proof_lanes checked_by cannot resolve until a lake/lean/TLC runner is registered
description:
RESIDUE of fgdb-proof-lane-checked-is-only-file-existence-0f1l (pane4, 2026-07-26). Filed
because 0f1l made the gap SAFE, not because it closed it.

## The measurement, at commit d1699fb

  - 10 proof lanes, all `status = "declared"`.
  - Zero `.lean`, `.tla`, `.cfg`, `lakefile*` or `.thy` files in the repository.
  - Zero invocations of `lake`, `lean`, `tlc`, `tla2tools` or any prover anywhere
    in `scripts/`, `scripts/check.sh`, or the checker sources.
  - `registries/checker_index.toml` therefore contains NO row that could be named
    as a lane's `checked_by`: there is no gate to name.

## What 0f1l changed, and what it deliberately did not

Before 0f1l, `status = "checked"` was `Path::is_file()`. A `.lean` file reading
`theorem foo : False := sorry` satisfied it, and so did an empty file. Now a
`checked` lane must name a `checked_by` gate that `liveness::Prover::assess`
proves live (registered + invoked + capable of failing), and the artifact itself
must be able to fail — Lean must state a proposition and carry no
sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide in live code; TLA+ needs a `.cfg` naming an
INVARIANT or PROPERTY with an operand.

So the failure mode is now LOUD instead of SILENT: promoting a lane to
`checked` today produces `proof_lane_gate_undeclared`, and naming any existing
row produces `proof_lane_gate_unresolved` or `proof_lane_gate_not_live`. There
is no spelling of the registry that gets a green `checked` row without a real
runner. That is the whole reason this is a residue bead and not an open defect:
**the first proof artifact cannot land without its runner landing in the same
change.** Nothing is silently unenforced.

## What is actually owed

1. A gate that runs the prover — a `scripts/*.sh` invoking `lake build` (Lean)
   and `tla2tools`/TLC with the model's `.cfg` (TLA+), registered in
   `checker_index.toml` with `status = "live"`, `kind = "script"`. It must exit
   nonzero on a failing proof — `liveness` already enforces that a registered
   script has a nonzero exit in LIVE code, so a runner that swallows the prover's
   status will be rejected as `checker_cannot_fail`.
2. The toolchain question this project has not answered: Lean and TLA+ are
   external toolchains, and Doctrine #1 closes the DEPENDENCY universe (crates
   linked into the build), not the developer toolchain — `shellcheck` and
   `rustfmt` are already required by `scripts/check.sh` on the same footing. That
   reading should be written down explicitly before somebody reads the closed
   universe as prohibiting a prover and quietly drops the formal lanes instead.
3. Then, per lane: the artifact, its `.cfg` where TLA+, `checked_by`, and the
   status flip — in ONE change, since the reader requires all of them together.

## Two things NOT owed, measured so the next author does not redo them

  - The `declared` -> `checked` transition needs no new law: the lane reader and
    the clause-side law (`proof_lane_declared_while_clause_promoted`) already
    cover both halves, and both are mutation-proved in
    `tests/metamorphic.rs` relation 12 and `tests/claims.rs`.
  - `axiom` and `native_decide` are currently reported as admits with no
    disclosure escape. If a real lane needs one, the fix is a disclosure FIELD on
    the lane row (so the claim is machine-checkable), not widening the reader —
    widening it restores exactly the hole 0f1l closed.

=====================================================================
WHAT THE PROOF LANE PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
This boundary is the load-bearing part of this bead. Quote it exactly.
=====================================================================
Lane: lean-version-chain. Artifact: formal/lean/VersionChain.lean.
Invariant: FG-INV-03.core — "Every physical version chain is finite, acyclic,
strictly newer-first by commit order, and every link remains within one owning
object generation."

THE MODEL. A chain is presented by its older-link function on commit-order
positions: `older a = some b` means the link at position a points to the next
older version at b, with `gen a` its owning object generation.

ASSUMED (hypotheses — the per-link obligations the STORAGE LAYER must establish,
NOT proven here):
  * newer_first:    older a = some b  ->  b < a
  * one_generation: older a = some b  ->  gen a = gen b

DERIVED (actually proven, in core Lean 4, no mathlib, no sorry/admit/axiom/
native_decide):
  * reach_le        — everything reachable is no newer (transitive newer-first)
  * reach_lt        — a proper step strictly decreases commit order
  * acyclic         — no link reaches its own position
  * reach_antisymm  — reachability is antisymmetric, so the only cycle is empty
  * reach_gen       — one owning generation, transitively over whole chains
  * walk_length_le  — FINITENESS WITH AN EXPLICIT BOUND: a chain from position a
                      has at most a+1 links. Lean accepts the walk's recursion
                      only because newer_first makes it decrease.
  * walk_ne_nil     — every position is its own newest link

SO, PRECISELY: finiteness and acyclicity are NOT assumed — they are CONSEQUENCES
of the strict newer-first step. A List-shaped model would have assumed both and
proven nothing about storage. What is assumed is the two per-link facts.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated so nobody overstates it later:
  1. It does NOT prove the storage layer establishes newer_first or
     one_generation. That is the oracles' half of FG-INV-03 and those oracles do
     not exist (see 1xxa: 0 of 20 FG-INV checkers exist).
  2. It does NOT cover arena decode, generation substitution, the debug/property
     oracles, or fuzz — the other half of FG-INV-03's enforcement column.
  3. It says NOTHING about the physical representation of a link on disk. It is
     about chain SHAPE only.
  4. FG-INV-03.core remains status = "stub" and MUST. THE LANE IS CHECKED; THE
     INVARIANT IS NOT. Nothing here promotes any invariant.

title: Freeze the exact DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence schema and consumer matrix
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the missing exact durable schema for DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence, the independently addressable evidence referenced by Appendix A LifecycleAuthoritySource::PresentedCapability (plan line 2623) and ResultResumeTransitionSpec (lines 1510/1498 family). The plan names this StrongRef target but never defines its body, role shape, field/tag set, digest transcript, construction order, or retention law. This task is the explicit spec repair; no catalog slice or implementation may infer those bytes from the English name.

## Design obligations
Audit every consumer and capability family, then choose and freeze exactly one role-safe schema: explicit complete authority binding or generated role arm; capability kind and canonical presented-byte/header/body commitment; replay/lineage subject and current-or-consumed-predecessor relation where applicable; verifier-key identity/ref and format/version epoch; exact presentation/session/channel binding; profiled time basis plus TimeValidationEvidence::Usable for the subject/action; nonwidening/current-security-state proof; validation action/scope; deterministic outcome; body digest and transcript exclusions. The record must be constructed before the authorized lifecycle/resume action, contain no future command/result/root edge, disclose no capability bytes or protected subject in diagnostics, and retain every key/profile/replay basis needed for deterministic revalidation. Decide explicitly whether role is a generic expansion or a closed tag; a role-erased or ambient-role record is forbidden.

The generated compatibility matrix must enumerate every legal consumer/action and reject cross-kind, cross-role, wrong presentation binding, stale service/security state, expired/not-yet-usable time evidence, wrong key/version, replay-lineage drift, widening, action substitution, and use after retirement. W10 capabilities is the unique implementation owner and fgdb-warden is the primary validation/key-selection crate; lifecycle/read/result command owners are consumers.

## Acceptance criteria
- The omission and all source/consumer anchors are recorded; no existing exact definition is silently assumed.
- One stable logical schema ID plus complete concrete field, tag/arm, role, reference-strength/target, digest, construction, compatibility, redaction, owner/consumer, checker/scenario/event/gate rows land in the canonical Appendix catalog and generated logical/wire/durable-field projections.
- The A21 reference and every earlier result/lifecycle reference resolve to that one schema; no alias, wildcard, bare polymorphic ref, or duplicate role-local definition remains.
- Static mutation tests reject each missing/duplicated/retagged/weakened field, role/kind/action/presentation/time/key/lineage substitution, future edge, and secret-bearing diagnostic.
- Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, time/key rotation, restart/replay, lifecycle, resume, and public-surface behavior remain planned under W1/W9/W10/W12 and verification owners until their checker rows are live; this G0 repair claims only the exact schema contract.

## Provenance
Plan lines 1510 and 2623; Appendix A A21 owner/reference-closure audit.

## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

This is the final committed self-contained schema, compatibility, construction, status-classification, ownership, and redaction contract. It supersedes all provisional design comments and must be implemented in the catalog/checker rather than refined in the Markdown plan.

`DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` is the one independently addressable validation object for the four durable capability kinds, with stable `ObjectKind=0x028f`, schema major 1, `canonical_max_size_bytes=16384`, and no role-specialized object-kind aliases. `DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis` is the exact embedded two-arm union `0x0001 Local{selected_pre_action_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,security_state_binding_ref:StrongRef<SecurityStateBindingRecord<Local>>,security_state_binding_digest:TargetDigest<SecurityStateBindingRecord<Local>>,current_security_slot_digest:TargetDigest<CurrentSecuritySlot<Local>>,current_service_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentServiceAuthority<Local>>}|0x0002 Meta{selected_pre_action_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,security_state_binding_ref:StrongRef<SecurityStateBindingRecord<Meta>>,security_state_binding_digest:TargetDigest<SecurityStateBindingRecord<Meta>>,current_security_slot_digest:TargetDigest<CurrentSecuritySlot<Meta>>,current_service_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentServiceAuthority<Meta>>}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. The mandatory embedded `validation_context` has exactly the stable `u16` tags `0x0001 CurrentLocal{current_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Local}|0x0002 CurrentMeta{current_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta}|0x0003 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{current_meta_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_meta_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta,transition_successor_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef>,source_local_service_visibility_epoch,target_meta_service_visibility_epoch,source_principal_commitment,target_principal_commitment,source_authority_commitment,target_authority_commitment}`; Shard is uninhabited and every other tag is reserved-invalid. The complete referenced binding must be the one selected by the current state; equal policy/revocation scalars under a different root, slot, service epoch, or authority commitment fail. The migration arm accepts only the post-activation Successor stage defined by `CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<T>`; Bootstrap or a raw Local strong ref is forbidden. Its four source/target commitments are pre-action projections of the certified legacy artifact and current Meta header; field `0x0011` must select Narrowed and its proof must establish equal principal plus no-wider target authority over those exact commitments. It never references the downstream lifecycle/migration authorization decision, spec, or command, so the content-address graph remains acyclic.

The four migration-context commitment fields have exact types and byte recipes rather than opaque scalar meanings: `source_principal_commitment:TargetDigest<CertifiedLegacyLocalPrincipalBinding>`, `target_principal_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentMetaPrincipalBinding>`, `source_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CertifiedLegacyLocalAuthorityBinding>`, and `target_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentMetaAuthorityBinding>`. They are respectively `BLAKE3("fgdb:target:certified-legacy-local-principal-binding:v1" || canonical(transition_successor_identity,certified_legacy_issuance_binding_identity_and_body_digest,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant_identity,principal_identity))`, `BLAKE3("fgdb:target:current-meta-principal-binding:v1" || canonical(selected_pre_action_state_identity,current_meta_security_binding_identity_and_body_digest,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant_identity,principal_identity))`, `BLAKE3("fgdb:target:certified-legacy-local-authority-binding:v1" || canonical(transition_successor_identity,certified_legacy_complete_AuthorityBoundHeader_Local,certified_legacy_security_slot_commitment))`, and `BLAKE3("fgdb:target:current-meta-authority-binding:v1" || canonical(selected_pre_action_state_identity,current_meta_authority_bound_header,current_meta_security_slot_digest))`. The Narrowed proof in field `0x0011` must open those exact certified/current projections and prove identical database security namespace, cluster incarnation, tenant identity, and principal identity; the target Meta scope, purposes, graph/schema/admin ceilings, disclosure ceiling, and policy/revocation-effective permissions are each subsets of the source Local grant; and the E-to-E2 service-epoch change is exactly the named certified successor transition. Commitment equality without those identity and nonwidening predicates is insufficient.

The registered `DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` is a closed `u16` union with exactly twelve arms: `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome` targeting `StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>` with the corresponding decoded `AuthorityBoundHeader` role predicate; `0x0003 LocalSubscriptionCursor|0x0004 MetaSubscriptionCursor|0x0005 LocalBufferedResult|0x0006 MetaBufferedResult|0x0007 LocalDurableArtifactOutput|0x0008 MetaDurableArtifactOutput` targeting `StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>` with the corresponding role and exact Resume-body-subkind predicate; `0x0009 LocalMergeOutcome|0x000a MetaMergeOutcome` targeting `StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>`; and `0x000b LocalReadYourWrites|0x000c MetaReadYourWrites` targeting `StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>`. Every arm stores its one ref plus its required decoded predicate; no associated type, generic target, or ambient role is serialized. `DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef` is the exact Local-only `u16` union `0x0001 TxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:SubscriptionCursor}|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:BufferedResult}|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:DurableArtifactOutput}|0x0005 MergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}|0x0006 ReadYourWrites{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid, and each wrapper's certified artifact predicate requires a decoded Local replay header and the exact named subject/subkind.

`DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof` is the exact same-role `u16` union `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Meta>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0003 LocalSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0004 MetaSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0005 LocalBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0006 MetaBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0007 LocalDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0008 MetaDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0009 LocalMergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest,required_header_role:Local}|0x000a MetaMergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest,required_header_role:Meta}|0x000b LocalReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}|0x000c MetaReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Meta>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Each proof byte-matches the selected replay ref, current state root, subject identity, current capability commitment, generation, and complete authority header. `DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof` is the migration-only `u16` union `0x0001 TxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0005 MergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest}|0x0006 ReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Every ref in that union must select `Successor`, the same `CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef`, source Local prefix, and legacy promise class as the selected legacy replay; together they byte-match the frozen Local current owner/lineage leaf, subject identity, capability commitment, generation, and complete Local authority header. `DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis` is the exact embedded union `0x0001 SameRole{proof:DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof}|0x0002 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{proof:DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof}`. CurrentLocal/CurrentMeta accept only SameRole with the matching role; LegacyLocalToMetaMigration accepts only the migration arm, so a raw Local strong ref can never occur in a Meta-owned validation object. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey` is exactly `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,role_and_group,subject_basis_identity,capability_lineage_token_digest}`. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>` is exactly `{lineage_key:ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey,terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,subject_basis_identity,public_floor_set_commitment,last_capability_commitment,last_generation,expiry_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_subject:ReadYourWritesCapabilityBytes,required_classification:Expired,nonreuse_and_lookup_floor,body_digest:BodyDigest<ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>>}` and carries no replay ref or capability bytes. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageState<Role>` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 Current{current_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,current_capability_commitment,current_generation,subject_basis_identity,floor_set_commitment}|0x0002 CurrentWithConsumedPredecessor{current_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,predecessor_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,current_capability_commitment,predecessor_capability_commitment,current_generation,consuming_request_digest,recovery_until:SuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal,subject_basis_identity,floor_set_commitment}|0x0003 ExpiredTombstone{tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>>}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Role>` is exactly `{role_and_group,generation,entries:CanonicalMap<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey,ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageState<Role>>,root_digest:BodyDigest<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Role>>}`. MigrationLiveSuccessor{selected_meta_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,capability_migration_index_root_identity,index_key:{transition_identity,legacy_capability_commitment},live_successor_leaf_identity,live_successor_leaf_body_digest,current_successor_replay_identity,initial_validation_identity,canonical_migration_request_digest,membership_attestation:AuthenticatedMapMembershipAttestation,selection_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Current Txn, delivery-owner, merge, and RYW proof arms expand their respective `selected_*` shorthand to tags `0x0001..0x0004`; their legacy counterparts expand to `0x0005..0x0008`; and `live_successor_entry_membership_commitment` expands to tag `0x0009`. The referenced root/record object IDs, outer proof refs, validation-context state identity, subject/replay/commitment/generation, and membership attestation must byte-match the selection. `selection_digest = BLAKE3("fgdb:transcript:durable-capability-membership-selection:v1" || canonical(exact_arm_tag,all_preceding_arm_fields))`; `AuthenticatedMapMembershipAttestation` has the registered map kind/root/key/leaf/path-or-threshold-attestation transcript and its own `TranscriptDigest`, so a stale owner record plus an unattached scalar digest cannot validate. Every `consuming_request_digest` in this family is exactly the same typed `TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>` as field `0x000f`, not an independently computed digest.

The mandatory embedded `validated_subject` has exactly the stable `u16` tags `0x0001 TxnOutcome|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput|0x0005 MergeOutcome|0x0006 ReadYourWrites`, matching the six distinct capability arms of `TimeBoundSubject`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Every arm is exactly `{presented_replay:0x0001 SameRole{ref:DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef}|0x0002 LegacyMigration{ref:DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef},time_subject_digest:TargetDigest<TimeBoundSubjectBody>,lineage_membership}` and has a mandatory arm predicate tying its subject tag to one exact replay-union tag set. `lineage_membership` has exactly `0x0001 Current{proof:DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis}|0x0002 ConsumedImmediatePredecessor{current_successor_replay:DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef,current_membership_proof:DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof,consuming_request_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,recovery_until:SuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal}|0x0003 MigratedConsumedExactRetry{prior_initial_validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,capability_migration_index_ref:StrongRef<CapabilityMigrationIndex>,live_successor_entry_membership_commitment:DurableCapabilityMembershipSelection::MigrationLiveSuccessor,consuming_request_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,current_successor_replay:DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef}`. Exactly four combinations are legal: SameRole plus Current uses `DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis::SameRole` under matching CurrentLocal/CurrentMeta; SameRole plus ConsumedImmediatePredecessor uses a role-matching current-successor replay and same-role membership proof; LegacyMigration plus Current uses `DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis::LegacyLocalToMetaMigration` for initial migration; and LegacyMigration plus MigratedConsumedExactRetry uses a subject-matching Meta current-successor replay and the live-index proof. Every other cross-product is reserved-invalid. The ordinary predecessor arm authorizes only byte-identical retry of that consuming request and may reproduce only the already-installed successor; it cannot authorize a new effect or reveal current outcome state. The migration-retry arm is legal only under `LegacyLocalToMetaMigration`, points backward to the initial Current migration validation generation, byte-matches that record's legacy subject and exact consuming request, and proves that the same index entry is still `LiveSuccessor`; it may return only that entry's already-installed E2 successor and cannot re-run migration. It never points to a later validation object, so the family graph remains acyclic. Resume subkinds are noninterchangeable. `MacaroonTokenBytes`, permit records, `AuthorizationLease`, and any Shard authority are different validation families and cannot decode as this object.

`DurableCapabilityTimeValidationBasis` is the exact embedded `u16` union `0x0001 CurrentLocal{evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_observation_import_role:Local,required_role_and_group}|0x0002 CurrentMeta{evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_observation_import_role:Meta,required_role_and_group}|0x0003 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_observation_import_role:Meta,required_role_and_group,current_meta_time_authority_profile_oid,retained_legacy_subject_time_profile_oid}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Its tag must equal `validation_context`; `required_role_and_group` byte-matches the selected current state and every observation import nested in the evidence. The migration arm is freshly validated in Meta for the certified legacy subject and exact current migration action using the retained compatible profile; a legacy Local evidence/import, a Shard evidence/import, or an observation from another Local/Meta group cannot inhabit it.

The canonical field table is fixed and contiguous: `0x0001 schema_version:u16=1`; `0x0002 validation_context`; `0x0003 validated_subject`; `0x0004 presented_capability_commitment:TargetDigest<CanonicalDurableCapabilityBytes>` over canonical header, exact body, and MAC bytes; `0x0005 presented_header_digest:TargetDigest<DurableCapabilityHeader>`; `0x0006 presented_kind_body_digest:TargetDigest<ExactDurableCapabilityKindBody>`; `0x0007 verified_mac_transcript_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityMacInput>` over the registered kind-specific MAC domain and canonical header/body; `0x0008 replay_relation:0x0001 Current|0x0002 ConsumedImmediatePredecessor|0x0003 MigratedConsumedExactRetry`, byte-matching subject lineage; `0x0009 verifier_key_basis:0x0001 CurrentLocal{key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>}|0x0002 CurrentMeta{key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>}|0x0003 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{certified_key_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>>,required_stage:Successor}`; `0x000a verifier_key_identity:{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch}`, using and byte-matching the exact `DurableCapabilityHeader` field types and selected key basis; `0x000b capability_format_version:u16`; `0x000c presentation_binding`; `0x000d compatibility_row_id:RegistryRowId`; `0x000e validation_action`; `0x000f action_scope_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>`; `0x0010 time_validation_basis:DurableCapabilityTimeValidationBasis`; `0x0011 authority_relation:0x0001 Exact|0x0002 Narrowed{proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}`; `0x0012 validation_outcome:0x0001 CurrentAccepted|0x0002 ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry{installed_successor_capability_commitment}|0x0003 MigratedConsumedExactRetry{installed_successor_capability_commitment}`, whose retry commitments byte-match the already-existing successor replay object; `0x0013 validator_semantics_registry_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidatorSemanticsRegistry>`; `0x0014 retention_class:0x0001 ThroughConsumerTerminal|0x0002 ThroughInstalledSuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal|0x0003 ThroughCapabilityMigrationIndexTerminal|0x0004 ThroughAuditReceiptResolution`; and `0x0015 body_digest:BodyDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>`. All fields are exactly one and mandatory; optionality exists only inside the selected closed union arm. The key-basis and time-basis tags must equal the validation context; current arms are same-group refs, while migration can retain an old-E key only through the certified Successor wrapper and must use fresh Meta-local time evidence. The semantics field is a full-width registered transcript digest, not an `ObjectId`, a truncated lookup key, or a reference to a fictitious logical object. The body transcript is `BLAKE3("fgdb:body:durable-capability-validation-evidence:v1" || canonical(schema_major=1, fields 0x0001..0x0014))` and excludes exactly field `0x0015`. For each grouped subject/action, generation emits one row for every listed concrete subject, row-declared validation context, and compatible concrete presentation tag; CurrentLocal pairs only with the corresponding Local presentation arm, CurrentMeta only with the corresponding Meta arm, and LegacyLocalToMetaMigration only with ReadyChannelMeta. ReadyChannel expands again over `NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`. It then emits one row per allowed replay relation and outcome: Current -> `CurrentAccepted`; ConsumedImmediatePredecessor -> `ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry`; MigratedConsumedExactRetry -> the same-named outcome. Current Local/Meta rows allow only the row-declared `Exact|Narrowed` authority relation; every migration row requires `Narrowed`. Every row fixes the matching concrete `TimeBoundSubject` arm, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, canonical action-scope recipe, current-state predicate named by the direct consumer, and exactly one retention class. Current rows for `TxnReattach`, `TxnRenew`, `ResultRotateResume`, `SubscriptionPause`, `SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect`, all three subscription ACK actions, `ArtifactOutputResume`, and `ReadYourWritesWait` can select a successor and therefore use `ThroughInstalledSuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal`; their exact ConsumedImmediatePredecessor retry rows only return an already-installed successor and use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`. Audit status uses `ThroughAuditReceiptResolution`. Initial `PostActivationCapabilityMigrate` Current rows can select a LiveSuccessor entry and use `ThroughCapabilityMigrationIndexTerminal`, while MigratedConsumedExactRetry rows only return that existing entry and use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`. The two selection classes require the downstream resolution arm above, so a post-validation CAS loser or other terminal consumer that selected no successor/index entry cannot leak its evidence. No generated row admits a management handle, embedded owner token, Bolt DISCARD/RESET, Shard context, negative-time status classifier, or a presentation class absent from the table.

Each concrete row ID is `dcv:v1:<subject-u16>:<action-u16>:<context-u16>:<presentation-outer-u16>-<presentation-nested-u16>:<replay-u16>:<authority-relation-u16>:<outcome-u16>:<retention-u16>`. Every `u16` is exactly four lowercase hexadecimal digits without `0x`; presentation nested is the ReadyChannel surface or Bolt request-kind tag and is `0000` only for Embedded. Thus the ID encodes the complete presentation cell, is at most 64 ASCII bytes (and therefore within the registered 128-byte field bound), and cannot collide across nested surfaces. The canonical row-set hash is `BLAKE3("fgdb:registry-set:durable-capability-validation-compatibility:v1" || canonical(sorted_complete_rows_with_every_dimension_and_consumer_schema_id))`. Generation proves the row ID is injective over the full tuple, that the sorted set equals the exact expansion above, that the computed longest ID is `<=128` bytes, and that no wildcard, duplicate, omitted cross-product cell, or extra row exists.

The permanent static mutation corpus independently removes, duplicates, retags, reorders, weakens, or changes the type/cardinality of every field and nested arm; substitutes every context/subject/action/presentation/time/key/format/lineage/authority/outcome/retention matrix dimension; injects a future command/result/root edge or a raw capability/MAC/protected-subject field; and changes the exact matrix row-set hash. Its real-CLI redaction scenario injects one unique secret sentinel into a catalog value, capability-like bytes, malformed row ID, and projection value, then requires byte-identical repeated JSONL whose stdout and stderr contain only the stable diagnostic code, sanitized known row ID or `<invalid-row-id>`, registry, and fixed reason class—never the sentinel, attacker value, capability/commitment, protected subject, handle, tenant, or principal.

Any action-specific receipt constructed from a presented durable capability strongly retains this validation ref; management-handle, authenticated-session/embedded-owner, and Bolt V1/V2 release alternatives are distinct authority arms and do not fabricate one. Every concrete matrix row pins subject/subkind, presented role, current authority role, consumer schema and action tag, allowed presentation arm, lineage relation, exact `TimeBoundSubject`, required `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, authority relation, current-state predicate, outcome, and retention class. Cross-kind/subkind/role/presentation substitution, stale service or security state, equal scalar under a different security root, NotYetValid/Expired evidence in a validation row, wrong verifier/key epoch/format, lineage drift, widening, action/scope substitution, use after retirement, and any unregistered row fail uniformly.

Construction is acyclic and fixed: current replay/key plus current authority/security/session request plus `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` plus the fresh same-process linear time-use guard plus any nonwidening proof and current lineage membership -> `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` -> exact lifecycle/transition/admission/receipt spec -> command -> applied result/successor/root. A durable Usable record surviving restart is not authority; each process must revalidate current state and acquire a fresh linear guard. A successor ref appears only in ConsumedImmediatePredecessor or MigratedConsumedExactRetry evidence after that successor already exists; the migration form also points backward to its initial validation generation and never forward to a later one. While its consumer or retry floor remains rooted, the object strongly retains the replay record, verifier key, time evidence and its profile/import basis, complete current authority/security basis, session authorization, and any nonwidening proof. Rejected input constructs no durable validation record. Diagnostics and events emit only a validated catalog row ID, context/action tag, and public outcome class; they never emit raw or committed capability/header/body/MAC values, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/handles, or attacker-controlled row/value text. The G0 schema, compatibility, construction-DAG, and sentinel-redaction checkers may be live once exact; codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, race, migration, and public-noninterference evidence remain explicitly planned under W9/W10/W12 until their real checkers run.

Negative-time status classification is deliberately not another validation object and cannot authorize lookup or effect. `DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0003 LocalMergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0004 MetaMergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}`, with each arm's decoded authority-header role and capability-kind predicate registered in its wire row; The Local basis requires one of the two Local replay arms and ReadyChannelLocal or EmbeddedLocal; the Meta basis requires the corresponding Meta arms. `authority_relation` compares the complete current header/session authority with the replay's issuance header: Exact requires byte equality, while Narrowed requires the named proof over those exact two commitments; widening is uninhabited even when time cannot be classified. The status action-scope digest is recomputed from the exact `TxnStatusLookup` or `MergeStatusLookup` selector, canonical request, presentation-binding digest, capability commitment, and requested scope; its action, request digest, and time-subject digest must byte-match the other basis fields. It is constructible only after header/body/MAC, key, domain, current security, role, session, presentation, kind, request, action scope, time subject, and same-or-narrower authority authentication succeeds; it contains commitments, not raw token/MAC bytes.

`TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence` is the embedded closed `u16` failure union `0x0001 BoundaryOverlap{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,possible_time_interval,not_before,expires_at}|0x0002 CheckedArithmeticFailure{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,operation,operands_commitment}|0x0003 ProfileOrEpochUnavailable{profile_oid,required_domain_and_epoch,current_registry_commitment,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,stable_failure_class}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `DurableCapabilityStatusClassification` is the inline `u16` union `0x0001 Usable{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>}|0x0002 NotYetValid{authenticated_basis:AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:NotYetValid}|0x0003 Expired{authenticated_basis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:Expired}|0x0004 TimeAuthorityUnavailable{authenticated_basis,failure:TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. It is legal only inside `StatusLookup`; the three negative arms cannot read the outcome/merge index, distinguish existence/current state, rotate a capability, or authorize any effect, and may emit only their named public time class. Invalid MAC/domain/security/role/presentation/kind/request produces `NotVisibleOrUnknown` with no classification object. `TokenExpired` additionally requires the existing durable expired requirement arm before send; the inline classifier does not invent expiry or retire bytes.

`LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>` is a generated associated type: Local contains only `AuthorityPermitRef<Local>`, Meta only `AuthorityPermitRef<Meta>`, and Shard is uninhabited. `LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>` is the generated closed union `PresentedPermit{permit_ref:LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>}|RegisteredAuthority{registration_ref:RoleExactRegistrationRef,current_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,nonwidening_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}|PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus{classification:DurableCapabilityStatusClassification}|AuthenticatedSession{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,request_digest}`; only role-valid arms inhabit each operation row. `PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus` is mandatory for a capability-bearing StatusLookup; its Usable arm owns the positive `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` ref and may proceed to the exact protected lookup, while its negative arms may only select the matching public time class. That source is forbidden for every non-status operation, and no ordinary PresentedDurableCapability Lifecycle arm exists. The durable capability kind/subkind is derived from the validation record or authenticated status basis, never repeated as an independently forgeable scalar. `LifecycleOperation` is exactly `RegisterAttempt|PrepareAdmissionScaffolding|RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active|PrepareAdmitted}|StatusLookup{registered_status_kind}|CapabilityManagement{registered_kind,action}`, where the generated associated action type is the disjoint union `Durable{Revoke}|Macaroon{Attenuate|Revoke}`; no generic Rotate or durable Attenuate arm exists. Client-authorized durable rotation is performed only by the exact typed transition surfaces and validation rows `TxnReattach|TxnRenew|ResultRotateResume|SubscriptionPause|SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect|SubscriptionAckBaseline|SubscriptionAckDelta|SubscriptionAckResetOrGap|ArtifactOutputResume|ReadYourWritesWait`; their own authorization/spec/receipt records retain positive validation evidence, and Lifecycle cannot add a second generic rotation path. The separately registered `SubscriptionDeliveryTransitionSpec::RotateCapability` is system-authorized Protocol maintenance with no presented client capability or DCVE compatibility row; it is distinct from Lifecycle rotation and uses only its structural authority arm. The `GlobalControlCommand(kind=CancelActiveAttempt)` and Local `TxnAbortSpec` both require `RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active}`; admitted Local/Meta abort requires `stage:PrepareAdmitted`. `LifecycleEffectClass<Operation>` is a generated associated closed tag: registration and preparation use their exact scaffolding classes; terminal abort uses `TerminalAbortNoEffectReleaseOnly{stage,registered_result_workspace_conflict_and_hold_disposition_schema}`; status is read-only projection; and capability management uses only the exact kind/action class above. There is no nullable permit, catch-all maintenance class, or wildcard rotate/attenuate/revoke row. `LifecycleAuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>` is the pre-result form `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,operation:LifecycleOperation,authority_source:LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>,sequence_neutral_spec_body_digest,requested_snapshot_or_scope_commitment,effect_class:LifecycleEffectClass<operation>,operation_audit_admission_commitment?,decision,authorization_audit_gate:AuthorizationAuditGate}`. The generated Role/operation matrix fixes every authority/source/effect arm, and the source, requested scope, audit evidence, lifecycle stage, and containing command must byte-match. RegisterAttempt uses a PresentedPermit; PrepareAdmission uses `PrepareAdmissionScaffolding` with exact NotRequired proof while its spec embeds the one GlobalMutation decision for complete effects; RequestTerminalAbort uses RegisteredAuthority plus the exact authenticated client request or the distinct administrative record. Capability-bearing status uses PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus; administrative durable revocation requires RegisteredAuthority or AuthenticatedSession, and macaroon attenuation remains in the macaroon/permit family. Protocol/system maintenance uses its registered structural system-authority command arm, never Lifecycle. ReadClose uses GlobalRead; each shard basis uses its own Read decision. A mutation/read/status decision, scalar epoch pair, fabricated zero effect, wrong-stage abort, or `StatusOrMaintenance` alias cannot substitute.

`TerminalAuditGate` is the same-group-only union `StructurallyInapplicable{exemption:StructuralAuditExemption}|NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|Required{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,terminal_resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>}`. comments.text:
Read-only contract adjudication published for scaffold handoff. This is the exact proposed repair; no registry/checker files have been touched.

IDENTITY AND ROLE
- One non-generic logical kind: DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence, stable ObjectKind 0x028f. Do not generate Local/Meta object identities.
- The mandatory closed validation_context is CurrentLocal, CurrentMeta, or LegacyLocalToMetaMigration. Shard is uninhabited. CurrentLocal and CurrentMeta carry the exact AuthorityBoundHeader plus the complete currently selected security-state basis. Migration carries the current Meta header/security basis plus certified Local-to-Meta successor/transition evidence and an exact same-principal/no-wider Meta authorization decision.
- The schema definition may be complete and its static G0 checker live, but codec/golden/fuzz/restart/rotation/runtime behavior remains planned. Do not label runtime evidence active/live.

SUBJECT UNIVERSE
The mandatory closed validated_subject has exactly six arms:
1 TxnOutcome
2 ResumeSubscriptionCursor
3 ResumeBufferedResult
4 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput
5 MergeOutcome
6 ReadYourWrites
Each arm retains the exact role-valid replay record and exact current lineage membership, or the exact consumed-immediate-predecessor plus already-installed successor for byte-identical retry only. Resume subkinds never substitute. MacaroonTokenBytes, permits, AuthorizationLease, and Shard capability validation do not inhabit this schema.

FIELDS AND DIGEST
Use stable tags 0x0001..0x0015:
schema_version; validation_context; validated_subject; presented_capability_commitment over header/body/MAC; presented_header_digest; presented_kind_body_digest; verified_mac_transcript_digest; replay_relation; verifier_key_ref; verifier_key_identity {issuer_id,key_id,key_epoch}; capability_format_version; presentation_binding; compatibility_row_id; validation_action; action_scope_digest; time_validation_evidence_ref; authority_relation Exact|Narrowed{StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}; validation_outcome CurrentAccepted|ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry; validator_semantics_oid; retention_class; body_digest.
The exact final tag numbering must remain contiguous and reserve body_digest last; if the catalog represents embedded unions as separately tagged durable fields, preserve this semantic order and pin every nested arm/tag too.
Body digest domain is fgdb:body:durable-capability-validation-evidence:v1 over schema major 1 and every preceding canonical field; it excludes only body_digest. Raw capability bytes, MAC bytes/material, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/public handles, and future command/result/root identities are forbidden.

PRESENTATION
- FgpReady binds a StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>, READY/service binding, session/channel/transcript generations, and canonical request digest.
- Embedded binds the exact authorized host session generation and canonical call digest.
- BoltCompatProfileV1 is always rejected because plan line 1050 forbids capability presentation.
- Because line 1052 normatively defines post-G4 Bolt V2 bookmarks as ReadYourWritesCapability values, reserve one explicit BoltV2Bookmark presentation arm and planned compatibility row for ReadYourWrites only, pinned to negotiated BoltCompatProfileV2 and the exact bookmark/RUN/session digest. There is no generic Bolt arm and no V1 row.
- LegacyLocalToMetaMigration is FGP CAPABILITY_MIGRATE only.

EXACT ACTION MATRIX
- TxnOutcome: TXN_STATUS current only; Reattach and Renew current or exact predecessor retry. Renew also requires its separate fresh successor-window evidence.
- ResumeBufferedResult: rotate/resume current or exact predecessor retry; ACK and explicit release current only, with terminal retry authorized by the action-specific receipt/tombstone rather than reclassifying the capability.
- ResumeSubscriptionCursor: pause, resume-after-pause/reconnect, baseline ACK, delta ACK, reset/GAP ACK, and close. Only the plan-defined rotate/resume and idempotent ACK rows may accept exact predecessor retry; terminal close retry resolves through disposition/tombstone.
- ResumeDurableArtifactOutput: rotate/resume, ACK, explicit release, with the same current/predecessor and receipt/tombstone laws as the corresponding plan transitions.
- MergeOutcome: execute and status lookup, current only.
- ReadYourWrites: BEGIN, EXECUTE, EXECUTE_TEXT visibility-floor admission current only; READ_YOUR_WRITES_WAIT current or exact predecessor retry when that operation already rotated the capability.
- All six subjects: one exact PostActivationCapabilityMigrate arm under LegacyLocalToMetaMigration. Retry resolves only through CapabilityMigrationIndex; a retired legacy capability is never generally usable.
- No wildcard StatusOrMaintenance/Rotate row. No generic Attenuate row. Macaroon attenuation stays in the macaroon family; durable revocation is administrative/registered-authority state, not self-authorization by a presented durable capability.
ACK/release/client-control receipts are the later authority objects, but their construction rows must consume and retain this exact validation evidence when a durable capability is the presented source. A management handle or authenticated-session alternative uses its own explicit authority row and does not synthesize this evidence.

CONSTRUCTION AND RETENTION
current replay/key + current authority/security/session + TimeValidationEvidence::Usable + fresh same-process linear use guard + optional nonwidening proof -> DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence -> exact lifecycle/transition/admission/receipt spec -> command -> applied result/successor/root.
A durable Usable record surviving restart is not authority; every process reacquires the linear guard. A successor ref is legal only for consumed-predecessor exact retry after that successor already exists. While the consumer/retry floor is rooted, the validation record strongly retains replay, verifier key, time evidence/profile/import, complete current authority/security basis, session authorization, and any nonwidening proof.

SOURCE REPAIRS
- Type both line-1006 TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec validation inputs as StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>.
- Replace line-2623 PresentedCapability with PresentedDurableCapability and remove the independently forgeable capability_kind scalar, or require it to be a generated projection that byte-matches the exact subject arm.

- Freeze MergeOutcome and RYW current-index membership inside their subject arms.
- Keep CapabilityManagement kind-specific; do not claim a complete rotate/attenuate/revoke wildcard matrix.

OWNERSHIP AND PROOF
Unique semantic owner is W10 capabilities in fgdb-warden. Consumers include fgdb-protocol, fgdb-txn, fgdb-chronicle, fgdb-branch, fgdb-subs, embedded fgdb, fgdb-server, secure-view/read admission, and W12 role-transition/migration paths. Static G0 checkers must separately prove schema exactness, compatibility matrix exactness, construction DAG, and diagnostic redaction. Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, race, migration, and public noninterference rows remain planned.

INTEGRATION PRECONDITIONS
The scaffold must stop hard-coding exactly one unresolved family and synthetic first-use owner/crate/consumer rows; support real owner/consumer/checker/scenario/gate metadata; parse a structured capability-validation compatibility table rather than prose; represent static-live versus runtime-planned evidence honestly; resolve or explicitly declare exact dependency targets; and sanitize diagnostics. title: Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts: registries, claim types, and the format freeze
description:
## What & scope
Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts — is the root of the entire FrankenGraphDB program: before a single line of Genesis implementation code is written, every semantic choice that any workstream could otherwise invent locally is decided, frozen, and machine-registered. G0 lands: the threat/trust model; the six-bet vocabulary; the exact twenty-invariant spine with its clause-granular activation contract; `invariants.toml`, `evidence.toml`, `slo.toml`; the four disjoint identity registries (`logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `wire_types.toml`) — §5.1 defines the restore-only fifth identity class `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` beside them, which G0 also lands — plus the exhaustive cross-indexes `durable_fields.toml`, `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, `state_payload_fields.toml`; registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes and acyclic construction/reference checks; every reserved W12 kind and role-tagged Raft/root/checkpoint variant; the operation-cost registry (Appendix G); frozen tagged `LanguageContract`s for every advertised surface; proof-lane manifests; the per-posture external-authority footprint; and the entire G0 decision batch (SnapshotQuery, fused autocommit arm, BranchRetire, ErasureCut, ExpiryContract, AllocationContinuityProfile, activation batching, identity-column codecs, PackedObjectGroup, tiered FEC, DIFF, externally_verifiable markings, sync-obligation column, Point decision, fgdb-reference allowlist, ArchiveReadOnlyOpen, replay/chaos exposure rows, freshness reservations, RaftHardFrame spike). Before G0 can pass, generated clause coverage also fixes the eleven §19 pre-pass semantic areas (normalized valid-time slice algebra/disclosure; first-escape/finalization allocation; escrow conservation/custody/transfer; complete `SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema; state-shaped independent result and durable artifact-output ownership with explicit release; transaction ownership/reattachment/expiry; one external DP charge/seed/Meta-noise lineage; audit terminal freeze/plan abandonment plus the gap-free visibility pipeline; bulk logical-manifest/staging and derived shadow-build activation; exact Local/Meta/Shard GC physical start/cancel/progress/completion; durable-format advertise/activate/first-write/rewrite/decoder-retirement), each with command/state registry rows, construction-DAG recipes, checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC classes, checker and negative-test entrypoints, and feature-disable behavior (detailed in g0-command-contracts). It also generates and validates README/AGENTS as checked release artifacts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Every failure mode this plan is built to escape — Neo4j's fossilized JVM decisions, JanusGraph's KV impedance mismatch, Kùzu's abandonment — traces to semantics decided implicitly, locally, or late. G0 exists because the plan's method is registry-driven generation with **no second source of truth**: hand-written lists in prose are checked readability projections regenerated and byte-compared by CI, never normative. This is what makes B5 (determinism/evidence/calibrated adaptivity) structural: claims have types (§1 constraint 11), costs are registered claims (constraint 12), and a weaker claim class may never enforce a stronger one. It is what makes B1's One Version Universe honest — every durable byte has exactly one identity class and one registered schema before anything writes it.
