title: Specify command_contracts, type classification, durable_state_slots, and bijection CI
description:
## What & scope
Specify the ordered-transition constitution: `command_contracts.toml` (one row per role-valid command arm), `command_type_classification.toml` (every input-looking type classified), `durable_state_slots.toml` plus its per-plane backing field registries (`state_payload_fields.toml`, `protocol_state_fields.toml`, `prepared_state_fields.toml`, `consensus_state_fields.toml`), the `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml` external-action registry, and the two-way total bijection CI that binds registry rows, Rust enums, handlers, and tests.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's commit mechanism and B5's replayability require that every state transition is a registered, generated, exhaustively-handled command — "adding a phase requires one atomic registry/schema/handler/test change; omission cannot degrade into an unreachable recovery state." This registry is also the substrate for Appendix G: cost rows derive command counts and barrier chains from these rows, so protocol weight cannot accrete unpriced (constraint 12).

## Design — normative detail
**`command_contracts.toml`:** one row per role-valid command arm with exact schema `{command_contract_id, role:Local|Meta|Shard, outer_command_union, outer_wire_tag, input_schema_id, input_wire_tag, inner_wire_tag?, body_schema_id, result_schema_id, applied_record_schema_id, handler_symbol, transition_class:Semantic|Maintenance|Scaffolding, sequence_effects, expected_state_schema_id, authority_arm, authority_evidence_target_schema_id?, terminal_audit_freeze_arm, terminal_audit_gate_arm, payload_availability_rule, publication_mode:SinglePlane|AtomicProtocolDetach{cross_plane_conservation_recipe_id}, construction_dag_recipe_id, consumed_state_slots[DurableStateSlotRef], written_state_slots[DurableStateSlotRef], checkpoint_floor_classes[], backup_restore_gc_classes[], posture_feature_predicate, format_epoch_range, status}` where `DurableStateSlotRef = {plane:SemanticPayload|Protocol|PreparedOwnership|Consensus|Bootstrap, role, slot_tag}`. Rows are per concrete inner tag: an outer `DpTransition`, `RemoteRetention`, configuration, delivery, GC, backup, restore, format, bulk, derived-build, or audit-lifecycle family never hides an open subcommand.

**`command_type_classification.toml`:** every independently addressable normative input-looking type — including every type whose stable name ends in `Spec` — gets exactly one class: `RegisteredCommandInput{command_contract_id}`, `PreOrderArtifact`, `CertificateInput`, `ResultOnly`, `ProjectionInput`, or `RuntimeOnly`. A suffix conveys no semantics: an ordinary schema/index definition is a `SchemaOp` carried by a transaction and cannot silently acquire a control-command classification because prose calls it a specification.

**`durable_state_slots.toml`:** the total cross-plane registry; rows `{plane, role, slot_tag, backing_registry, stable_name, exact_wire_type, reference_semantics, target_schema_id, activation_predicate, initial_value_recipe, transition_writer_contract_ids[], checkpoint_or_snapshot_class, floor_class, backup_class, restore_reconciliation_class, gc_class, role_transition_class, status}`. `state_payload_fields.toml` backs only canonical semantic payloads; `protocol_state_fields.toml` backs the manifest/Raft-maintenance-owned protocol plane; `prepared_state_fields.toml`/`consensus_state_fields.toml` back prepared ownership and Raft hard/snapshot/configuration state; bootstrap slots validate through `bootstrap_frames.toml` but still receive cross-index rows. Every consumed/written command slot must resolve through this table; every active slot names every legal writer; every checkpoint/snapshot/floor/backup/restore/GC/transition walker is generated from it. A feature with no slot, a slot with no writer, an unclassified protocol mutation, or a semantic-payload checker pretending to cover another plane is a G0 failure.

**Bijection CI:** every inhabitable Local/Meta/Shard command-union arm resolves to exactly one live contract row; every live row resolves to exactly one union arm, one registered canonical input, one exact body/result/applied-record triple, and one exhaustive Rust apply handler. Duplicate tags, aliases encoding a second command, wildcard bodies, unresolved associated types, prose-only phases, unhandled rows, handlers without rows, or a command input classified as its own future result are G0 failures. Generated exhaustive-match tests compare registry rows, Rust enums, encoders/decoders, state-machine transition tables, appendix renderings, negative fixtures, and every command family named by a feature contract. **External actions:** `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml` totally registers every action whose transport may escape the process and durably register/charge/reserve/publish/revoke/destroy/release/advance an external authority; ad-hoc call-after-commit code is forbidden; the only publication substrates are the fixed `RootSlot` protocol and the sole prebootstrap-journal exception — G0 permits no third substrate.

**G0 clause-coverage pre-pass (§19, line 1313):** before G0 can pass, generated clause coverage also fixes eleven named semantic areas — normalized valid-time slice algebra and disclosure; first-escape/finalization allocation; escrow conservation/custody/transfer; complete `SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema; state-shaped independent result and durable artifact-output ownership with explicit release; transaction ownership/reattachment/expiry; one external DP charge/seed/Meta-noise lineage; audit terminal freeze/plan abandonment plus the gap-free visibility pipeline; bulk logical-manifest/staging and derived shadow-build activation; exact Local/Meta/Shard GC physical start/cancel/progress/completion; and durable-format advertise/activate/first-write/rewrite/decoder-retirement. Each area must have command/state registry rows, construction-DAG recipes, checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC classes, checker and negative-test entrypoints, and feature-disable behavior; a missing element in any area is a G0 failure.

## Invariants & claim types
Binds FG-INV-07's bijection clause ("`command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm/handler and `state_payload_fields.toml` roots every written state class. Before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership") and FG-INV-08's contiguity clause ("logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their respective sequences"). All artifacts are invariant-class registry rows; the generated walkers they emit back FG-INV-14's mandatory-inventory checker.

## Interactions
Consumes g0-identity-registries' classes and `durable_fields.toml`. g0-cost-registry derives `latency_anatomy.toml` command counts and barrier chains from these rows' `transition_class`, `publication_mode`, and slot lists. g0-format-arms adds frozen rows (fused arm, BranchRetire, ErasureCut, ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec, activation batch specs). w2-commit-protocol/w2-txn-lifecycle implement the Local rows; w12 beads implement the reserved Meta/Shard rows; the protocol-state reference machines — §15.4's canonical-map oracles, owned by verif-differential — are generated from the transition tables, and verif-oracles' independent protocol oracles (§15.2) cross-check the same registered transitions in-sim.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Registry schema validation with negative fixtures for each named G0 failure (duplicate tag, wildcard body, handler without row, Spec-typed object without classification, slot with no writer, unclassified protocol mutation). Bijection test harness that round-trips rows ↔ generated Rust unions ↔ handler symbol table and logs the exact unmatched arm. A cross-plane test proving a semantic-payload walker cannot claim Protocol-plane coverage. Dispatch-registry test: an out-of-registry external call site fails CI in the unsafe-ledger style.

Named suites: `cc_neg_duplicate_tag`, `cc_neg_wildcard_body`, `cc_neg_handler_without_row`, `cc_neg_spec_without_classification`, `cc_neg_slot_without_writer`, `cc_neg_unclassified_protocol_mutation`, `cc_neg_input_is_own_result`, `cc_clause_coverage_eleven_areas` (each §19 pre-pass area resolves rows, recipes, classes, checker/negative-test entrypoints, and feature-disable behavior), property test `cc_bijection_roundtrip` (registry rows ↔ generated unions ↔ handler symbols under random valid row subsets), and fuzz `cc_registry_fuzz` over registry bytes and generated decoder inputs. E2E: `scripts/g0_commands_e2e.sh` regenerates unions/handler tables/walkers from a pinned fixture registry set, runs the two-way bijection harness, the cross-plane coverage test, the dispatch-registry scan over a seeded out-of-registry external call site, and the clause-coverage check, asserting each seeded defect fails with its exact identifier. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: bijection_checked|arm_matched|walker_generated|dispatch_scanned|coverage_area_checked, command_contract_id, role, wire_tag, handler_symbol, plane, slot_tag, outcome, unmatched[]}`; the bijection harness logs the exact unmatched arm/row/handler triple; the dispatch scan logs offending file/line/symbol; the coverage check logs per-area, element-by-element status.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: convention-based command discovery (suffix conveys no semantics); open command families (every inner tag gets a row); a third publication substrate (constitutionally forbidden). Risk: schema rigidity slowing iteration — accepted deliberately; the atomic registry/schema/handler/test change is the intended cost of adding a phase.

## Provenance
§5.1 (lines 294–300), §19 G0 paragraphs (lines 1311–1313).

### Fidelity addendum — exact irreversible-dispatch registry linkage
This bead consumes the exact contracts frozen by `fgdb-g0-irreversible-dispatch-5v75`; it must not recreate a shortened dispatch model. Every command row that authorizes, arms, imports, abandons, or terminalizes an escaping external action names the exact `dispatch_contract_id`, `DispatchOriginPlane`, `DispatchSourceGateKind` arm, authorize/arm/mark-SentUnknown/abandon/import contract IDs, Protocol or prebootstrap attempt slot, portable terminal-evidence schema, and retention floor from `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml`. The sole pre-first-root publication substrate is the generated `prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml` protocol; its journal-head CAS is not an application-action row. Ordinary actions use the RootSlot-published canonical Protocol machine. No command family may introduce a private outbox, informal retry ledger, direct provider call, generic source gate, or third publication substrate.

Two-way CI therefore joins `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, `durable_state_slots.toml`, `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml`, and `prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml`. It rejects a command/dispatch row without its reciprocal edge; a dual-plane action collapsed to one contract; a prebootstrap terminal import decoded as canonical; any send without a durable SentUnknown owner; and a terminal receipt/refusal whose contract, plane, source-gate commitment, or operation namespace differs. Crash/E2E fixtures cover authorization publication through status-first recovery for one action in every registered source-gate arm. Structured logs join `command_contract_id`, `dispatch_contract_id`, `origin_plane`, `source_gate_kind`, `attempt_slot`, `attempt_generation`, `command_or_maintenance_index`, and terminal import kind.

title: Build the Appendix G operation-cost registry and its three CI laws
description:
## What & scope
Build the constitutional cost instrument required by §1 constraint 12: `latency_anatomy.toml` (one row per operation class: five structural quantities) and `stream_capacity.toml` (the maintenance-stream capacity model, FG-CFG-04), their generation from `command_contracts.toml`, the barrier fusion-legality law, and the three CI laws (derivability, coverage, same-change update).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§1.11 gave correctness claims a registry; this registry does the same for cost, so no mechanism can accrete protocol weight without a priced row. It keeps §17's performance gates and the protocol mutually derivable (B5): a gate arithmetically impossible under its class's row is a registry error that fails CI, never an ambitious target. It is also the honesty instrument for B6's agent workloads: SnapshotQuery and the fused autocommit-write arm are the registered fast classes §17's headline numbers measure.

## Design — normative detail
**`latency_anatomy.toml`** carries per operation class: (a) sequenced semantic commands; (b) total Raft log entries including order-attempt and certificate maintenance; (c) the ordered durability-barrier chain — per barrier: plane from `DurableStateSlotRef` (`SemanticPayload|Protocol|PreparedOwnership|Consensus|Bootstrap`), what syncs, amortization law (`per-txn|per-group|per-batch|deferrable`), and the fusion-legality column; (d) external-authority interactions classified `synchronous|episodic`; (e) durable objects minted. Both artifacts are generated where possible from `command_contracts.toml` — command counts from registered command arms, barrier chains from `publication_mode` and consumed/written state slots; hand-declared rows exist only where structure is not yet expressible (external RTT class, group-commit amortization) and each names the contract rows it summarizes. The appendix tables are checked readability projections — CI regenerates and byte-compares them. Claim types are fixed: registry rows are exact structural counts or exact bounds in declared configuration parameters (tilde-ranged columns); every µs/throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class, posture, audit_class}`; the capacity model is FG-CFG-04, never an invariant.

**The nine registered classes (quorum-one posture, concurrency 1):** `SnapshotQuery` point read — 0 commands, 0 Raft entries, no barrier, no external authority, 0 durable objects (sampled Sextant cards are telemetry). Durable autocommit read — 3 commands (`LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec::Autocommit`, `LocalReadCloseSpec`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`), ~6–10 entries, per-command D1 supplement/certificate publication + Raft hard-state append + D2 apply publication, ~6–10 objects. Autocommit write, fused arm — 2 commands NotRequired (fused Register+PrepareAdmit+Reserve+Commit, then `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`; 3 Required), ~4–8 entries, D1 payload barrier (capsule + strong closure + `PreparedCommitRecord` + `RootSlot`, per-txn, group-fusable) + append-reply hard-state + D2 (MAY fuse in quorum-one) + completion, ~15–20 objects. Explicit multi-statement write commit — 5+N commands, ~2–3×(5+N) entries, statements amortize per-group, commit pays the fused-arm chain. Audit-Required write — fused/explicit commands plus ordered `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec`; 7–10 ordered sync points from external ticket-issuance CAS (strictly serial per `AuditDomainId`) through signing under `CertificateAttemptPlan`/`CertificateSignerLock`, D1, Raft closure sync, D2 (two ordered publications), external resolution-batch CAS, `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec`, `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` (fresh time evidence), terminal completion; ≥2 external RTTs. Subscription delta delivery — 0 commands, ~3 per-subject protocol transitions per Required delivery (~2 NotRequired) amortized into batched maintenance entries; one threshold-signed `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` per activation tick under `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch`; ~4–6 objects. Branch create — 2 commands (`BranchEpochBoundaryReservation`, `BranchForkSpec` installing the pre-built `BranchForkBundle`), ~4–6 entries, O(1) data copy. Branch merge (squash) — 3 commands (`MergePrepareSpec`, target `CommitCommand`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`; `MergeRejectSpec` on the pre-effect reject path). Restore open (same-identity) — 4–6 restore controls through `Reconciling -> VisibilityCommitted -> ServicePreparedHidden -> Operational` plus independent reopen; one full D1/append/D2 chain per control.

**Fusion legality:** fusion is legal only where the registry says so, per barrier pair and per posture. Quorum-one: append-reply hard-state publication and post-apply D2 protocol publication MAY fuse into one ordered slot update (no follower observes the intermediate; both sides land in the same `RootManifest`/`RootSlot` closure; the receipted-but-unordered crash window is exactly §5.2's two abandonment arms). Multi-member: MUST NOT fuse (followers reply to append before commit). Fusing against a MUST NOT row fails closed at the G0 conformance gates; a legal fusion still counts as one ordered sync operation, never zero, in §17's ordered-sync-count gate.

**`stream_capacity.toml` (FG-CFG-04):** total same-group ordered-log entries/s as registered functions of live cursors `N`, per-cursor cadence `M`, durable result rate `R`, branch count `B`, audit batch size `k`, activation tick `τ`. Governing law: a commit matching `C` cursors mints ~3·C per-subject transitions Required (~2·C NotRequired); entries amortize below transitions under §12.8 batch rows; the implied external time-observation rate is `N×M` amortized to one per activation tick; user-commit p99 degradation is a stated function of `(N,M,R,k,τ)` and is what §17's sequencer row gates. **Three CI laws:** *Derivability* — every §17 gate names its operation class and counting unit and must be arithmetically consistent (latency gate ≥ ordered-barrier count × pinned measured fsync p50; throughput gate ≤ apply ceiling); a failing gate is a registry error failing the build. *Coverage* — every stated scale objective (§5.6 10k-branch, §17 cursor-scale, governance-profile gates) must have a covering registered scenario or G0 fails. *Same-change update* — any change adding sequenced commands, barriers, external interactions, or per-object identity structure updates both TOMLs in the same change; CI regenerates derivable portions and rejects divergence. The counts are protocol counts, not aspirations: the read is 3 commands because read-close success waits for `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`; the fused write floor is 2 because `TerminalCompletion` consumes durability/visibility evidence of the commit's own publication and FG-INV-07 forbids any pre-order input naming its future applied record — no single-command arm can exist. A smaller row requires changing the protocol and this registry in the same change.

## Invariants & claim types
Implements §1 constraint 12 verbatim ("Every operation class has a row... Every §17 gate must be derivable from that registry... Structure lives in the registry; µs and throughput budgets are `slo.toml` rows and are never invariants"). Rows are exact structural counts (invariant-class registry facts); budgets are slo class; `stream_capacity.toml` is FG-CFG-04 beside FG-CFG-03 in Appendix F; endurance evidence over these rows is FG-EVID-03.

## Interactions
Generated from g0-command-contracts rows. g0-format-arms freezes the class definitions the fast rows bind (SnapshotQuery, fused arm). perf-cost-ci implements the three laws in CI; perf-bench-core/perf-bench-governance/perf-bench-scale pin manifests against these rows; obs-slo wires the `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}` keys; risk-register carries the hardening↔cost same-change rule.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Byte-compare regeneration test (appendix projection vs generated TOML); derivability arithmetic test over every §17 gate with a synthetic impossible-gate negative fixture; coverage test failing on an uncovered named scale objective; same-change test: a synthetic commit adding a command arm without touching `latency_anatomy.toml` fails; fusion-law conformance fixture: quorum-one fused build passes, multi-member fused build fails closed; capacity-model scenario replay logging predicted vs measured head-of-line saturation per (N,M,R,k,τ) point.

Named suites: `cost_regen_byte_compare`, `cost_derivability_all_gates`, `cost_neg_impossible_gate`, `cost_coverage_scale_objectives`, `cost_neg_uncovered_objective`, `cost_same_change_guard`, `cost_fusion_quorum_one_may`, `cost_fusion_multi_member_must_not_fails_closed`, property test `cost_row_derivation` (command counts and barrier chains derived from random valid `command_contracts.toml` subsets always match independent hand computation), and fuzz `cost_toml_fuzz` (mutated registry bytes fail closed with a typed error). E2E: `scripts/g0_cost_e2e.sh` generates both TOMLs from the pinned contract fixture, byte-compares the Appendix G projection, runs derivability arithmetic over every §17 gate (including one seeded arithmetically impossible gate that must fail the build), applies a synthetic commit adding a command arm without a registry update (must fail), runs both fusion conformance fixtures, and replays the capacity-model scenarios. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: row_generated|gate_checked|fusion_checked|scenario_replayed, operation_class, commands, raft_entries, barrier_chain[], external_class, minted_objects, gate_id, barrier_count, fsync_p50_ns, derived_floor, gate_value, outcome}`; every derivability failure logs the full arithmetic inputs; capacity replay logs per-(N,M,R,k,τ) predicted versus measured head-of-line saturation and the divergence, so post-implementation runs can diff against this baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: treating counts as aspirations or letting benchmarks own truth (gates then drift from protocol); µs budgets in the registry (they are slo rows); fusion as an implementation option discovered under load (it is a normative per-posture column). Risk: hand-declared rows drifting from contracts — bounded by requiring each to name the contract rows it summarizes.

## Provenance
Appendix G (lines 3169–3193); §1 constraint 12; §17 method (lines 1234, 1273).

## Fresh-eyes exact normative attachment — Appendix G — exact operation cost registry
The following audited source-plan appendix is embedded verbatim. It is authoritative for every row, arm, caveat, claim boundary, and checker obligation; the preceding elaboration supplies implementation rationale and ownership but cannot abbreviate or contradict this inventory.

## Appendix G — Operation Cost Registry (normative contract)

This appendix is the constitutional instrument required by §1's constraint 12: §1.11 gave correctness claims a registry; this registry does the same for cost, so that no mechanism can accrete protocol weight without a priced row. Two machine-checkable artifacts constitute it. `latency_anatomy.toml` carries one row per operation class stating five structural quantities: sequenced semantic commands; total Raft log entries including order-attempt and certificate maintenance; the ordered durability-barrier chain (per barrier: the plane from `DurableStateSlotRef` — `SemanticPayload|Protocol|PreparedOwnership|Consensus|Bootstrap` — what syncs, the amortization law `per-txn|per-group|per-batch|deferrable`, and the fusion-legality column settled below); external-authority interactions classified `synchronous|episodic`; and durable objects minted. `stream_capacity.toml` carries the maintenance-stream capacity model. Both are generated where possible from `command_contracts.toml`: a class's command count derives from its registered command arms, and its barrier chain from their `publication_mode` and consumed/written state slots; hand-declared rows exist only where structure is not yet expressible there (external RTT class, group-commit amortization) and each names the contract rows it summarizes. Per §5.1's registry discipline, the tables in this appendix are checked readability projections — CI regenerates and byte-compares them — never a second source of truth. Claim types are fixed: registry rows are exact structural counts, or exact bounds in declared configuration parameters where a column is configuration-dependent (the tilde-ranged columns), enforced by the same generation bijection that governs command contracts; every µs or throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; and the capacity model is a configuration-model claim (`FG-CFG-04`, registered beside `FG-CFG-03` in Appendix F), never an invariant.

Counts below are stated for the single-node quorum-one posture at concurrency 1; group commit amortizes every barrier marked per-group or per-batch, and the replicated posture changes barrier behavior (follower append/reply), never command counts. `SnapshotQuery` and the fused autocommit-write arm are the registered fast classes referenced by §17; their rows bind those class definitions to this registry, and every other §17 gate names one of this registry's rows as its operation class.

| Operation class | Sequenced semantic commands | Total Raft entries (incl. order-attempt/certificate maintenance) | Ordered barrier chain (plane · what syncs · amortization) | External-authority interactions | Durable objects minted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SnapshotQuery` point read | 0 | 0 | none — executes against the pipeline's visible endpoint under an existing admission/lease; no order, no barrier | none | 0 (sampled Sextant decision cards are telemetry, not durable protocol objects) |
| Durable autocommit read | 3 — `LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec::Autocommit`, `LocalReadCloseSpec`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` | ~6–10: each command carries its own non-shareable `LocalOrderAttemptInput` plus availability-certificate plan/lock/share/publication maintenance positions | per command: D1 supplement/certificate publication (SemanticPayload/PreparedOwnership · staged closure + `RootSlot` · per-txn), Raft hard-state append (Consensus · log + hard state · per-batch), D2 apply publication (Protocol · maintenance entry + protocol-root slot · per-batch; quorum-one fusion law below) | none NotRequired; synchronous ticket-issuance CAS plus admission visibility under a Required-read profile | ~6–10: registration/outcome records, order-attempt inputs, certificates, result-retention record, pipeline entries |
| Autocommit write, fused arm | 2 NotRequired — fused Register+PrepareAdmit+Reserve+Commit, then `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`; 3 Required (ordered ticket admission precedes protected processing) | ~4–8 | D1 payload barrier (SemanticPayload/PreparedOwnership · capsule + mandatory strong closure + `PreparedCommitRecord` + `RootSlot` · per-txn, group-fusable), append-reply hard-state publication (Consensus · per-batch), D2 apply publication (Protocol · entry + slot · per-batch; MAY fuse with append-reply in quorum-one), completion publication (per-batch) | none NotRequired; synchronous ticket CAS Required | ~15–20: capsule, effect set, delta template, delta batch, authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, prepared record + successor, two availability certificates, order-attempt input, HLC evidence, command, marker, command record, state root, pipeline entry, manifest generation |
| Explicit multi-statement write commit (N statements) | 5+N — `LocalBeginReservationSpec`, registration, N statement publications, `LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec`, `CommitCommand`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` | ~2–3 × (5+N) | statement publications amortize per-group; the commit itself pays the fused-arm chain (D1 closure, append, D2, completion) | as the fused arm | fused-arm census + N statement/workspace-generation records |
| Audit-Required write (commit→TerminalReady) | fused/explicit commands plus the ordered `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec` | commit entries plus admission, resolution-batch import, visibility-advance, and activation maintenance | 7–10 ordered sync points: external ticket-issuance CAS (strictly serial per `AuditDomainId`) → ordered admission + admission audit visibility → event/resolution signing under `CertificateAttemptPlan` quorum-rooting + per-signer `CertificateSignerLock` installs for both payload and order-attempt certificates → D1 prepared-root publication → Raft closure sync → D2 apply publication (quorum-durable maintenance entry + protocol-root slot update: two ordered publications) → external resolution-batch CAS (per-batch) → `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` + visible-endpoint publication (again entry + slot) → `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` (per output; fresh time evidence) → terminal completion | ≥ 2 external RTTs: ticket issuance synchronous per operation; resolution batch amortized per contiguous batch; time authority per activation | fused-arm census + ticket, admission spec, audit event, resolution, gate, batch, CAS receipts, outcome records |
| Subscription delta delivery | 0 — delivery is Protocol-plane maintenance | ~3 per-subject protocol transitions per Required delivery (pending-output publish, activation, ACK; ~2 NotRequired), amortized into batched maintenance entries per flush/activation tick under §12.8's batch specs; audit release amortized across a pipeline range inside one `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` via `sorted_protected_output_release_recipes[]` | per maintenance entry: quorum-durable append + protocol-root slot update (Protocol · per-batch) | one challenge-nonce-fresh threshold-signed `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` per activation subject; amortized to one per activation tick under the registered `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` arm | ~4–6: `DeltaDeliveryEnvelope`, `DeliveredDeltaPayload`, lease time basis, resume replay record |
| Branch create | 2 — ordered `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation`, then `BranchForkSpec` installing the pre-built `BranchForkBundle` | ~4–6 | bundle D1 (availability certificate over the closed inventory · per-op) + append (per-batch) + D2 root publication (per-batch) | none synchronous; identity-continuity authority episodic per allocation-epoch advance | descriptors, closed/successor key epochs, grants, manifests — proportional to bounded envelope-root fanout, O(1) data copy |
| Branch merge (squash) | 3 — `MergePrepareSpec`, target-branch `CommitCommand`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` (`MergeRejectSpec` on the pre-effect reject path) | explicit-commit entries plus prepare | explicit-commit chain, plus the capability-acknowledgement round trip before evaluation may begin | none synchronous | explicit-commit census + `MergeRecord`, `MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord`, ledger and imported-coverage successors |
| Restore open (same-identity) | 4–6 restore controls — guarded restore publication through `Reconciling -> VisibilityCommitted -> ServicePreparedHidden -> Operational`, then independent reopen confirmation | ~2–3 per control | one full D1/append/D2 chain per control; every control passes the audit-visibility pipeline | continuity-head and catalog CAS, episodic (`ExternalCas` posture; DirectoryBound uses its local continuity arm and forbids same-identity restore) | restore state records, phase certificates, promotion receipt, terminal pins |

Barrier fusion is legal only where this registry says so, per barrier pair and per posture — it is a normative column, not an implementation option discovered under load. In a one-member (quorum-one) configuration, the append-reply hard-state publication and the post-apply D2 protocol publication MAY fuse into one ordered slot update: no follower exists to observe the intermediate, recovery cannot observe it (both sides of the fusion land in the same `RootManifest`/`RootSlot` closure), and the receipted-but-unordered crash window fusion touches is exactly the window governed by §5.2's two abandonment arms: an unreceipted, provably unordered attempt may be abandoned under a current fence, and a receipted attempt only after consensus proves it cannot be ordered and every certificate/configuration retention floor has expired — and fusion changes nothing in that law. In any multi-member configuration the two publications MUST NOT fuse: followers reply to append before commit, so the hard-state publication is an independently observable protocol obligation with its own durability meaning. A build that fuses against a MUST NOT row fails closed at the G0 conformance gates, and a legal fusion still counts as one ordered sync operation, never zero, in §17's ordered-sync-count gate.

`stream_capacity.toml` is the maintenance-stream capacity model (`FG-CFG-04`): total same-group ordered-log entries/s expressed as registered functions of the declared scale parameters — live cursors `N`, per-cursor coalesced delivery cadence `M`, durable result rate `R`, live branch count `B`, audit batch size `k`, and activation tick `τ`. Its governing law is fan-out amplification: a commit matching `C` cursors mints ~3·C per-subject protocol transitions in Required postures (~2·C NotRequired) — publish, activation, ACK — because the `Coalesced` provenance arm (§9.5) reduces commits per delivery, never transitions per delivery; ordered-log entries amortize below transitions under §12.8's batch rows — `PublishDeltaPending` across one Ripple flush tick, `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec`/`ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec` per activation tick, audit release across a pipeline range inside one `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` — so entries/s scale with tick rates while per-subject transitions scale with N×M. The model publishes the implied external time-observation rate — `N×M` challenge-nonce-fresh threshold-signed observations/s under per-lease subjects, amortized to one observation per activation tick under the registered `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` arm — and derives head-of-line cost for user commits: semantic commands and maintenance entries share one role/group ordered log, so user-commit p99 degradation is a stated function of `(N,M,R,k,τ)`, and that derived figure is what §17's sequencer/maintenance-stream row gates. The model is a configuration-model claim in the FG-CFG class: it gates configuration acceptance and CI fixture design, never correctness; §12.8's deterministic backpressure remains the honest overload behavior when its assumptions fail.

Three CI laws bind the registry. **Derivability:** every §17 gate names its operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests versus internal probes) and must be arithmetically consistent with its row — a latency gate ≥ the class's ordered-barrier count × the benchmark manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, a throughput gate ≤ the apply ceiling implied by its sequenced-command count and the measured serial apply cost; a gate that fails the check is a registry error and fails the build, not the benchmark. **Coverage:** every stated scale objective in this plan must be covered by a registered `stream_capacity.toml` scenario — the §5.6 10k-branch objective, §17's cursor-scale gate, the governance-profile gates, and any future objective that names a scale parameter; an objective without a covering scenario is a G0 failure. **Same-change update:** any change that adds sequenced semantic commands, ordered durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates `latency_anatomy.toml`/`stream_capacity.toml` in the same change; CI regenerates the derivable portions from `command_contracts.toml`, diffs them against the registered rows and this appendix's projections, and rejects a divergence.

The counts above are protocol counts, not aspirations, and their honesty is load-bearing. The durable autocommit read is three commands because read-close semantic success waits for `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` (Appendix A) and no terminal result returns before `TerminalReady` (§5.2). The fused write floor is two because `TerminalCompletion` consumes durability/visibility evidence of the commit's own publication and FG-INV-07 forbids any pre-order input naming its future applied record — no single-command arm can exist. The audited chain counts both ordered publications of every two-plane advance because §12.8 makes each advance a quorum-durable maintenance entry followed by a protocol-root slot update. Any operation class that wants a smaller row must change the protocol first, and this registry in the same change; that is the entire point.

---

*Fin. The graph database the 2030s deserve, built from parts the 2020s already proved — ours.*

### Attachment closure requirements
A checksum fixture pins this exact appendix range. Generation must enumerate every row/arm with stable IDs and map it bijectively to the owning implementation, unit/property/fuzz/simulation/E2E tests, detailed redacted diagnostic-event schemas, and consuming gate. Missing, duplicate, wildcard, silently weakened, or unowned rows fail CI and gate review.

title: Generate README/AGENTS as checked artifacts and run G0 self-containment checks
description:
## What & scope
Make README and AGENTS generated, checked release artifacts synchronized from the frozen plan and registries, and implement G0's closing verification pass: self-containment, dependency-DAG, justification, and fresh-review checks over the whole G0 corpus.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The no-second-source-of-truth discipline dies if human-facing summaries drift from the registries: agents (B6) and new contributors read README/AGENTS first, so a contradictory summary is an active injection of wrong semantics into every future session. Making the summaries generated artifacts turns documentation drift into a build failure instead of a review hope.

## Design — normative detail
The checked README/AGENTS synchronization is a release artifact generated from the frozen plan; any contradictory summary blocks G0. G0 synchronizes the summaries and validates their normative examples against the registries — every code/type/command/invariant name appearing in a summary must resolve to a live registry row or frozen contract, and every worked example (query snippets under a named `LanguageContract`, command sequences, cost-row citations) is executed or schema-checked against the corresponding G0 artifact. The closing pass runs four checks over the G0 corpus: **self-containment** (every semantic choice a workstream needs is decided somewhere in the frozen artifacts — no dangling "TBD" or prose-only phase; the decision-batch completeness check from g0-format-arms feeds this); **dependency-DAG** (the clause/registry/artifact dependency graph is acyclic and every edge resolves); **justification** (every constitutional decision records its rationale and rejected alternatives — the §2 foundations and §3 adopt/adapt/reject material — so future revisions argue against recorded reasoning, not vacuum); and **fresh-review** (a reviewer who did not author an artifact signs off on it, recorded per artifact). The constitutional rule this enforces: no workstream may invent a missing semantic choice locally — a gap found later is a G0 defect to be fixed at the root, not patched downstream.

## Invariants & claim types
Meta-enforcement of §1 constraint 11's registry separation and the Appendix F preamble (twenty-ID hash, clause DAG, checker existence). The generated-summary law is itself invariant-class ("any contradictory summary blocks G0"); review sign-offs are process evidence, not statistical claims.

## Interactions
Depends on every other g0 anchor (it validates their outputs). gate-genesis consumes its green status; obs-doctor later reuses the example-validation harness for runtime doc checks; risk-register records residual open justifications.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
CI job regenerating README/AGENTS from the frozen plan and byte-comparing against the committed files, failing with a unified diff; example-validation harness logging every extracted normative example, its target registry row, and pass/fail; DAG check with a negative fixture introducing a cycle; self-containment check failing on a seeded "TBD" marker; justification-coverage report listing every decision without a recorded rationale (must be empty); fresh-review ledger complete over all G0 artifacts.

Named suites: `docs_regen_byte_compare`, `docs_neg_contradictory_summary`, `docs_example_validation`, `docs_neg_seeded_tbd`, `docs_dag_neg_cycle`, `docs_justification_coverage`, `docs_fresh_review_ledger_complete`, and fuzz `docs_example_extractor_fuzz` (malformed embedded examples are reported with location, never silently skipped). E2E: `scripts/g0_docs_e2e.sh` regenerates README/AGENTS from the frozen plan and registries, byte-compares against committed files, extracts and validates every normative example, then runs the four closing checks over the full G0 corpus with one seeded defect per check (a contradictory summary line, a TBD marker, a DAG cycle, a missing rationale, a missing sign-off), asserting each is caught and named. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: doc_regenerated|example_validated|check_ran, artifact, example_id, target_registry_row, check_name, outcome, diff_hunk?}`; example validation logs every extracted example with its resolution target and pass/fail; the closing pass logs per-artifact reviewer identity for the fresh-review ledger and a final coverage summary (decisions with and without recorded rationale).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: hand-maintained README with periodic audits (drift is certain); doc-generation from code comments (code does not exist yet at G0 — the plan and registries are the source). Risk: generated docs reading poorly — acceptable; correctness of summaries outranks prose polish at this gate, and generation templates can improve without changing the checked content.

## Provenance
§19 G0 paragraph (lines 1311–1313).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Decide and freeze the entire G0 decision batch: every closed-union arm and registry row
description:
## What & scope
Decide and freeze — every closed-union arm, registry row, and reserved field entailed, with implementation permitted to trail the frozen rows — the complete §19 G0 decision batch. One paragraph per decided artifact below; each lands as concrete registry rows in the identity/command registries plus Appendix F clause amendments.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
These are exactly the decisions that, made late or locally, would fork the format space: fast read/write classes (B6 agent latency), branch/erasure/expiry lifecycles (B1 governance), packing/FEC economics (B2 byte economy), and replay/freshness reservations (B4/B5). Freezing them at G0 lets every workstream build against stable arms while §19 sequences integration, not ambition.

## Design — normative detail
**Operation-cost registry + capacity model:** the Appendix G instrument with its gate-derivability, scale-objective-coverage, and same-commit-update CI laws is itself a decision-batch member; its content is specified in g0-cost-registry — this bead freezes its status as constitutional.

**`SnapshotQuery` read class:** the registered second honest result class — single-envelope, permit-validated, visible-endpoint-pinned, session-owned ephemeral result stream consuming zero sequenced semantic commands and zero Protocol-plane maintenance transitions; no begin reservation, attempt registration, statement records, durable retention, delivery lease, or resume capability; dropped on disconnect; audit-NotRequired by construction. Class selection is bind-time and policy-driven, never a client verb: eligible exactly when `CanonicalStatementClassification` proves ProvenReadOnly single-statement autocommit within declared output/row/time bounds, the effective `AuditCompletenessProfile` does not name the class Required, no DP/Warden-classified operation class, and the namespace's class policy permits it; under a Required-read profile eligibility fails closed with a typed data-independent rejection steering to the durable class. Frozen artifacts: the `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` execution-scope arm (coordinator-local, non-ordered, authorization before every observation, pinning the pipeline's visible candidate root through `AuthorizedSnapshot`/`fgdb-secure-view` under an ordinary snapshot retention lease), `command_type_classification.toml` rows for the non-ordered admission types, the Appendix D `SnapshotQuery` frame family, the `AnswerContract` behavior row (non-resumable, no-replay, no-durable-outcome), and the amended FG-INV-04/FG-INV-20 clauses. Strict-serializable by construction with its own differential oracle against the durable read path; sampled Sextant decision cards under a registered sampling policy.

**Fused autocommit-write arm:** single-statement autocommit writes whose bind-time classification proves eligibility use `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec` — one sequenced semantic command carrying attempt registration, prepare admission, the ordered final-certification reservation, and commit semantics (identical canonical effects, one terminal audit gate, one D1 payload closure, one order-attempt supplement) — with `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` as the second command; floor exactly two commands audit-NotRequired, three Required. The amended observation rule is scoped to exactly this arm: coordinator-local permit verification and admission precede every statement/storage observation (FG-INV-20 preserved) while durable registration lands atomically with the commit; a pre-order crash leaves no durable record; exact retry re-executes from scratch, safe because no identity or result escaped and the autocommit idempotency-key CAS at apply guarantees at-most-once durable effect; apply constructs the compressed `Registered -> PrepareAdmitted -> CommittedPendingPostconditions` outcome lineage. Frozen: its own `command_contracts.toml` row, construction-DAG recipe, and regenerated crash matrices.

**BranchRetire:** `BranchRetireSpec` (ordered semantic control command, own terminal audit gate and contract row) validates the retire request against current head, envelope/write-key epochs, and registry generation, atomically installing a permanent `BranchRetireTombstone`; idempotent retry; from visibility the branch admits no new writes/forks/merges-as-target/grants/subscriptions/statements/snapshots while history reachable via other branches is untouched. Cursors take the no-successor terminal arm (typed `GAP` supersession → `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`); the same capsule carries the `ResourceLedgerState` branch-count release and `EscrowRightsTransitionSpec::RetireBranchOverlay` burning `EscrowBranchSeed` overlay rights with exact conservation proof. `BranchRetireFinalizeSpec` fires only after proved drain (floors, leases, pins, holds, grants, in-flight merges — established by the generated GC walkers), activates the retention cut, and enters the branch's envelope root and write-key epochs into the staged `KeyDestroyProposal`/`KeyDestroyFinalizeSpec` pipeline; fork-time double rotation makes destruction orphan nothing reachable elsewhere. Staged dispositions frozen as rows.

**ErasureCut:** the ordered `ErasureCutSpec` control command installs a permanent `ErasureTombstone` scoped to one arm of `SubjectKey{subject_key_domain_contract_oid,subject_key_commitment}|ElementSet{sorted_element_identities}|PropertySlotSet{sorted_schema_coordinate_slots}` (SubjectKey inhabitable only under a declared `SubjectKeyDomainContract`). The tombstone is an additional visibility conjunct honored across every tier, branch head, and time-travel/valid-time selector within retention; queries observing erased data return typed `Erased{tombstone_ref}` (wire-projected without local references); the tombstone joins effective floors as a permanent root. Frozen: the visibility conjunct, the envelope-DAG wrap-scope arm, the `SubjectKeyDomainContract` schema contract (subject-key profile, covered slots, per-subject wrap-chain derivation, index/constraint posture), the `erasure_obligations.toml` registry (every derived surface an installed cut must reach — Beacon index generations, Ripple views/StatsSegments, vector/FTS outputs, independently retained delivered results — each row naming its walker and completion proof; a surface without a row fails closed), tombstone floors, and crash/restore matrices. Replay downgrades via FG-INV-19's `Redacted` arm, never silent byte-identity breakage.

**ExpiryContract/TTL:** expiry is a visibility predicate, never a mutation. `ExpiryContract` is the immutable schema object `{contract_id, element_kind_and_type, expiry_slot, domain:InstantUtcNanos, default_assignment:NoExpiry|RequireExplicit, visibility_semantics, permitted_selectors, canonical_scalar_profile_oid, schema_epoch, body_digest}` declaring the reserved `_expires_at` property slot; a version whose instant is at or before the pinned evaluation instant is invisible to current reads as an additional §5.3 conjunct; the evaluation instant is the closure-captured profiled authority-time observation entering authorization/plan-cache/certificate/replay keys. Sequencer sees expiry only as one `ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec` control command per epoch tick carrying rollback-resistant `TimeValidationEvidence`; reclamation is lazy via compaction under ordinary floors; Ripple derivations over expiry-bearing inputs must declare exactly one of `ExpiryInsensitive`, explicit `AS OF` basis, or `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick`.

**AllocationContinuityProfile:** the closed union `ExternalCas|DirectoryBound` bound 1:1 to the slot's `IncarnationContinuityProfile`. `ExternalCas` (mandatory for W12/Meta/Sharded): threshold-signed `IdentityContinuityRecord {database_security_namespace_id, allocation_epoch, predecessor_digest, status}` CAS-published outside the rollbackable closure before an epoch issues IDs. `DirectoryBound`: a fenced local allocation-continuity journal record under the same whole-inode fence — an embedded database mints every epoch with no external service; a registered `DirectoryBound` variant may bind epoch advances to a TPM-NV-class local monotonic counter. FG-INV-11's external-monotonicity clause is scoped per profile with a registered Appendix F residual-risk row: under `DirectoryBound`, block-level/volume-snapshot rollback is outside the declared threat model, allocation included.

**Activation batching:** `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec<Role>`/`ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec<Role>` are registered Protocol-plane Maintenance rows carrying canonically sorted per-subject sub-records with a member-completeness commitment; apply is all-or-nothing; a single-subject operation is canonically a one-entry batch (no second durable encoding). `time_bound_subjects.toml` registers `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` whose pre-evidence transcript is the sorted digest set of member lease-basis transcripts; one fresh challenged threshold-signed `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` per activation tick signs the batch subject; per-member window arithmetic verified individually; deriving windows from creation epochs is rejected.

**Identity-column codecs:** registered order-preserving shared-prefix layouts for identity columns (`dst_VId`, `EId`): block-header dictionary carries `allocation_epoch`+`partition_id` prefixes, the `monotone_slot` suffix is fixed-width or delta/FOR-coded; registered as codecs in run/block codec tables, covered by the logical-digest validator so encodings evolve without format-identity change; binary search/SIMD lower-bound on the fixed-width suffix preserves canonical big-endian epoch‖partition‖slot order; ~4 KiB blocks at ≤256 entries presume ≤16 B/entry (raw 128-bit IDs would cap near 95).

**PackedObjectGroup:** a registered `physical_record_kinds.toml` class packing length-delimited canonical plaintext bytes of many small logical objects into one physical record paying one compress/AEAD/FEC/placement pipeline; the pack owns the `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`/`PlacementId` chain, members keep their keyed `ObjectId`s with authenticated `(pack_encoding, offset, length)` locators. Mandatory pack-homogeneity law: one write-key domain, one tenant/authority domain, one retention/floor class — mixed packs fail closed at build; reclamation coarsens to the pack; packing boundaries are the existing group-commit D1/publication boundaries, adding no new ordered barrier.

**FEC reconstructibility class:** reconstructibility is a dynamic property of retention state. An object is Chronicle-reconstructible exactly while re-derivable from the authoritative checkpoint plus retained contiguous logical-command suffix and not reachable from the checkpoint closure; only such objects may carry a reduced-repair `fec_profile`; every sole-source object owes the full budget. Checkpoint-fold recode rule: the install that folds a reduced-repair object into the authoritative closure must either recode it under the full-budget profile (legal without re-encryption — recoding changes only `EncodingId`) or materialize independent full-FEC checkpoint payloads; cut activation fails closed until the chosen path is durable. Scrub failure on reduced-repair objects escalates via `RebuildFromSuffix`; object-level AEAD, keyed `ObjectId` verification, and per-symbol MACs remain mandatory for every profile.

**DIFF operator family:** the reserved GLA row `Diff{endpoint_a, endpoint_b, coverage_contract}` owning §8.1's `DIFF` syntax; streaming over ordered delta batches with registered spill for reordered/aggregated ranges.

**`externally_verifiable` markings:** `TransparencyCheckpoint`, `WitnessPolicy`, inclusion/consistency-proof encodings, the filtered-changefeed delta-commitment format, and MMR leaf/checkpoint transcript recipes carry the marking in their format-registry rows with one compatibility law: a third-party verifier pinned to a witness-policy epoch must verify every checkpoint issued within that epoch; format transitions on marked surfaces ride the dual-quorum policy rotation — operators can never force-upgrade external verifiers inside an epoch. The dependency-free verifier SDK is a registered post-1.0 row.

**Filesystem-profile sync-obligation column:** the per-operation-class sync-obligation column (`frame-pwrite|create|rename|unlink`) is a registered `filesystem_profiles.toml` column probed by `fgdb doctor --write-profile`; under `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` a bootstrap-frame `pwrite` owes only the frame file's declared sync (parent-directory syncs owed exactly by inode-creating/renaming/unlinking operations; lease-inode create+dir-sync paid at physical-generation cadence, never per commit); the counts feed Appendix G's barrier chains.

**Point decision:** `Point(2D/3D)` values are storable scalars but not orderable and not indexable; a declared index over a `Point` property fails closed as a typed error; the canonical byte encoding exists for digests/equality only and is explicitly not a spatial order. Registered spatial non-goal: post-1.0 route is Z-order/Hilbert mapping over B-tree machinery, in-house R-tree only if profiling defeats the curve; the Neo4j differential corpus documents `point()`/`distance()`/point-index divergence.

**`fgdb-reference` dependency allowlist:** the reference engine may depend only on foundation value/type/claim crates plus G0-generated registries and golden vectors; importing any engine crate (`fgdb-txn`, `fgdb-algebra`, `fgdb-exec`, `fgdb-strata`, `fgdb-chronicle`, ...) is a CI-rejected boundary violation; the parser (`fgdb-gql`/`fgdb-cypher`) is the one recorded sharing exception; the ground-truth hierarchy (appendices and golden vectors outrank both implementations) is registered.

**ArchiveReadOnlyOpen:** the registered open class for single-file dataset distribution — `open_archive(path)` verifies the signed `BackupManifest`, object inventory, and transparency checkpoint with the independent verifying-reader machinery, exposes the archived root strictly read-only (no incarnation takeover, no writer, no service promotion or receipt; posture explicitly labeled and structurally unable to impersonate Operational); outside-closure reads fail with typed `HistoryUnavailable`-class refusals; snapshot leases run under a registered read-only filesystem-profile variant.

**Replay-artifact-exposure and chaos-packaging rows:** which replay artifacts may become customer-facing (`ReplayManifest`s, crashpacks, seeds/schedules) is a registered decision row with per-artifact stability classification; the customer product is the `SessionReplayBundle` graded with `ReplayCompleteness` vocabulary. Any customer-facing chaos surface ships behind an fgdb-owned facade crate, claim-typed falsification-only, with fault-injection capabilities absent from production `Cx` profiles by construction.

**Freshness reservations:** the reserved `AnswerRequirement` freshness constraint (§8.3) and the optional freshness field on `SubscriptionDeliveryPolicy<Role>` (§9.5) — a delivery-lag target in watermark/commit-sequence units, never wall clock; slo-class only; runtime breach emits the typed `FreshnessBreach` notice kind with its matching pending-output/lease/receipt/activation and Appendix D wire arms frozen in the same batch.

**RaftHardFrame spike:** a G0/G1 design spike with recorded go/no-go either way; honest scope stated now — per-append scalars alone do not stop closure re-minting (`certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref`, `prepared_order_attempt_root_ref`, `audit_signer_journal_root_ref` churn per commit); skipping per-batch root publication makes the retained log tail a bootstrap input, requiring new FG-INV-08/FG-INV-10 subordinate clauses, a changed generated log-to-state verifier, and takeover coverage; the frame embeds the same namespace/incarnation/writer-fence tuple as `RootSlot`.

## Invariants & claim types
Registers the amended FG-INV-04 clause (`SnapshotQuery` admission reads only the pipeline's visible candidate root and can never observe applied-hidden state), the amended FG-INV-20 clause (SnapshotQuery admission obeys the identical authorization-before-observation rule with equal oracle coverage), FG-INV-11's per-profile scoping plus the registered residual-risk row, and FG-INV-19's `Redacted`-arm erasure clause (an `ErasureCutSpec` never silently breaks a byte-identity claim — the grade weakens attributably). Fast-class counts are Appendix G structural facts; MTTDL over FEC tiers is FG-CFG-01; freshness bounds are slo/FG-EVID-04; domain-granularity erasure policy is FG-CFG class.

## Interactions
Consumes g0-identity-registries (rows land in its registries) and g0-command-contracts (new command rows). g0-cost-registry binds the SnapshotQuery/fused-arm rows. Downstream implementers: w2-fused-autocommit, w2-branch-retire, w2-fec-scrub, w2-object-packing, w2-continuity-profiles, w2-filesystem-profiles, w3-identity-encoding, w4-ttl-expiry, w5-diff-operator, w9-redaction-erasure, w9-activation-batching, w10-snapshotquery, w10-archive-open, w2-transparency, verif-reference, verif-replay-products, w6-freshness, w2-order-raft (spike).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Every listed artifact has its frozen registry rows present and schema-valid, with reserved wire tags allocated; per-artifact negative fixtures (ineligible SnapshotQuery statement silently upgraded → fail; mixed-domain pack → build-time fail; reduced-repair profile on a sole-source object → fail; Point index declaration → typed error; engine-crate import in fgdb-reference → CI fail (the allowlist row and fixture are frozen here; the CI check itself activates once `verif-reference` exists — enforced no later than gate-genesis); MUST-NOT fusion → conformance fail). Crash-matrix skeletons registered for the fused arm and BranchRetire/ErasureCut/restore paths. The RaftHardFrame spike outcome is a recorded decision document either way. A decision-batch completeness check cross-references §19 line 1313's list against landed rows and fails on any absent member, logging the missing artifact by name.

Named suites: `fa_neg_snapshotquery_silent_upgrade`, `fa_neg_mixed_domain_pack`, `fa_neg_reduced_fec_sole_source`, `fa_neg_point_index_typed_error`, `fa_neg_reference_engine_import`, `fa_neg_must_not_fusion`, `fa_neg_creation_epoch_window`, `fa_decision_batch_complete` (item-by-item against §19 line 1313), property test `fa_frozen_rows_schema_valid` over every landed row, and fuzz `fa_reserved_tag_fuzz` (mutated reserved wire tags are rejected as unallocated/retired, never reinterpreted). E2E: `scripts/g0_format_arms_e2e.sh` walks the frozen decision-batch manifest artifact by artifact — asserting registry rows present and schema-valid, reserved wire tags allocated, negative fixtures failing as specified (fixtures whose target crate does not yet exist — e.g. `fa_neg_reference_engine_import` — assert registered-and-pending status instead), crash-matrix skeletons registered, and the RaftHardFrame decision document recorded either way — and exits nonzero naming the first absent member. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: artifact_checked|row_verified|fixture_ran, artifact_name, registry, row_id, wire_tag, fixture_id, outcome}`; the completeness check logs every batch member with found/missing status; every negative fixture logs the exact typed error it provoked so post-implementation runs can diff the error taxonomy against this baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Recorded rejections inside the batch: client-verb read-class selection (bind-time policy only); a single-command autocommit write (FG-INV-07 forbids it); operator-procedure branch retirement (two-phase proved-drain protocol instead); blanket per-subject DEKs at object granularity (schema-declared subject-keyed slots only); per-element expiry retirement transactions (epoch-tick predicate instead); creation-epoch-derived delivery windows; per-object FEC static tiering (dynamic retention-state property); wall-clock freshness bounds. Risk: freezing wrong arms early — mitigated by closed-union extensibility (new arms are new registered rows) and the implementation-may-trail rule.

## Provenance
§19 line 1313; §13 (1025–1029, 1057), §5.2 (403), §5.6 (465–467), §12.6 (910–914), §4.8 (262–266), §4.5 (225), §12.8 (974–976), §6.2/§6.3 (534, 542), §5.1 (342, 348), §5.7 (477), §5.8 (496), §3.4 (157), §15.1–§15.2 (1136, 1152), §9.5 (802), §14 (1070), App C (2759).

title: Specify the five disjoint identity registries, durable_fields, and digest transcripts
description:
## What & scope
Specify and land the identity constitution: the disjoint identity-class registries `logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `wire_types.toml` (plus the restore-only `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` class §5.1 defines beside them), the exhaustive field cross-index `durable_fields.toml`, registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes, generated exact reference unions, acyclic construction/reference checks, and every reserved W12 kind and role-tagged Raft/root/checkpoint variant.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's One Version Universe requires that every durable byte has exactly one identity law before any byte exists. The registries are generated from checked-in schema annotations so appendix pseudo-schemas are checked renderings, never a second allowlist — the no-second-source-of-truth discipline inherited from frankensqlite's registry school. Content addressing plus keyed identity is also the governance story (B6): honest-but-curious storage sees opaque IDs, and identity survives recompression/re-encryption/re-encoding within one keyed namespace.

## Design — normative detail
**Identity pipeline context:** every durable logical object has `ObjectId = BLAKE3_keyed(K_oid, "fgdb:logical:v1" ‖ DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId ‖ canonical_plaintext_header ‖ canonical_plaintext_payload)`; `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId` is an immutable random 256-bit creation identity distinct from catalog `DatabaseId`. Physical protection is one noncircular pipeline: deterministic compression under `CodecProfile` → one object-level AEAD with AAD `("fgdb:object-aead:v1", ObjectId, CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest)` → `CiphertextId` over descriptor+ciphertext+tag → `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId {ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile}` → `EncodingId` → `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId {encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form}` → `PlacementId`; no ID is an input to itself; recoding changes `EncodingId` only.

**The five classes:** (1) `logical_object_kinds.toml` — one stable nonreusable `object_kind:u16` per top-level canonical plaintext schema with keyed `ObjectId` identity; rows declare identity/storage class, schema major/minor + lifecycle status, canonical encoder/decoder, construction-order class, every reference field with GC strength, posture/role/feature compatibility, resource bounds, golden/fuzz corpora; all `StrongRef<T>`/`Conditional*Ref<T>`/weak-digest targets must resolve here. (2) `physical_record_kinds.toml` — non-ObjectId identity laws: `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, `PlacementId`, authenticated metadata-tree locator entries, coordinate-keyed `SymbolRecord`s; never accepted as logical `StrongRef` targets. (3) `bootstrap_frames.toml` — fixed-location mutable frames (`RootSlot`, future registered frames like `RaftHardFrame`) with location/generation/checksum identity; rows fix byte size, offsets, alternation/update protocol, tear-validation rule, opener fields, compatibility gate, recovery test vectors. (4) `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` — restore artifacts predating target `K_oid`, with `PreBootstrapArtifactId` domain-separated hashing, legal only in the registered restore staging structures, never `ObjectId`, never `StrongRef`-able. (5) `wire_types.toml` — every inline record, enum/union variant, discriminant, spec-body tag, reference wrapper, and framing type gets one stable `wire_type_id:u16` plus exact containing-union `wire_tag:u16`, encoding context, version/status, limits, allowed containing schemas; inline types cannot be `StrongRef`ed unless promoted to a top-level logical row. Code spaces: `0x0000`/`0xffff` permanently invalid; `0x0001..=0x7fff` permanent core; `0x8000..=0xbfff` negotiated extension; `0xc000..=0xfffe` test/experimental (production readers reject); retired codes never reassigned; `registry_epoch` changes only on row add/retire.

**`durable_fields.toml`:** one row per canonical field or union arm: `{containing_schema_id, field_tag:u16, stable_name, exact_wire_type, cardinality, identity_class, reference_semantics, target_schema_id?, construction_order, role/posture/feature_predicate, retention_and_cut_rule, version_status, resource_bounds}`. A field absent from the table is unencodable. This table is the sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure, construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers. Generated reference unions are exact (e.g. `LocalCommandInputRef`, `MetaAppliedResultRef`); bare `StrongRef`, `StrongRef<A|B>`, or generic `RegisteredStrongRef` are invalid in normative bytes.

**Digest discipline:** every digest row declares exactly one class: `TargetDigest`, `TranscriptDigest` (with registered recipe), `WeakIdentityDigest`, or `BodyDigest`. A `BodyDigest<T>` row fixes `{domain_separator, schema_major, included_field_tags, excluded_field_tags}` with default recipe `BLAKE3(domain_separator ‖ canonical(schema_major, T excluding exactly the one BodyDigest field))`; unknown exclusions, two body-digest fields, implicit zero placeholders, or self-including computation are G0 errors. A generated construction-DAG test builds the concrete reference graph for every command tag and state slot and rejects self, mutual, or future-result edges. Reserved rows for every W12 kind and role-tagged Raft/root/checkpoint variant land now, implementation trailing.

## Invariants & claim types
Binds FG-INV-09 ("`ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory... every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe") and FG-INV-07's registry clauses ("the concrete durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every field, typed reference, transcript digest, and weak identity is registry-resolved and names already identified bytes; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root"). All artifacts are invariant-class registry rows; golden corpora are conformance fixtures, not benchmarks.

## Interactions
g0-command-contracts layers the command/state registries on these classes; g0-format-arms freezes new rows (PackedObjectGroup, RaftHardFrame reservation, identity-column codecs) into these registries; w1-generated-parsers generates encoders/decoders/golden vectors from them; w2-object-identity implements the ID pipeline; w2-root-bootstrap consumes `bootstrap_frames.toml`; the generated kind/field/reference checker backing FG-INV-07/FG-INV-09's enforcement columns is emitted from `durable_fields.toml` and runs as an independent generated checker in CI and the verification stack.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Schema validation for all five registries plus `durable_fields.toml`; disjointness test (no schema inhabits two classes); code-space law tests (reuse of a retired tag fails; experimental tag in a production fixture fails); construction-DAG acyclicity over every command tag and state slot with negative fixtures for self/mutual/future-result edges; BodyDigest recipe generation test comparing encoder, decoder, field table, golden vectors, and mutation fixtures against one generated recipe; a fixture with an English-named but unregistered field must be unencodable. CI logs per-registry row counts, reserved-W12 coverage, and exact diffs.

Named suites: `idr_schema_valid_all_six`, `idr_disjointness_no_dual_class`, `idr_code_space_retired_reuse_fails`, `idr_code_space_experimental_in_production_fails`, `idr_construction_dag_acyclic` with negatives `idr_neg_self_edge`/`idr_neg_mutual_edge`/`idr_neg_future_result_edge`, `idr_bodydigest_recipe_roundtrip`, `idr_neg_unregistered_field_unencodable`, `idr_reserved_w12_coverage`, property test `idr_reference_targets_resolve` (every generated reference-union arm resolves to a live logical row under random registry subsets), and fuzz `idr_golden_vector_mutation` (bit-flipped golden vectors fail identity/digest verification naming the exact failing recipe). E2E: `scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh` regenerates all five class registries plus `durable_fields.toml` from checked-in annotations, rebuilds the generated reference unions and walkers, replays every golden corpus through encoder/decoder/digest verification, and runs the full negative-fixture set, exiting on the first divergence. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: registry_generated|row_checked|dag_checked|digest_verified, registry, object_kind, wire_type_id, field_tag, recipe_id, outcome, diff?}`; every digest failure logs the domain separator, included/excluded field tags, and the mismatching byte offset, so later format work can diff identity behavior against this baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one flat registry (identity classes have different identity laws; merging invites `StrongRef`-to-placement bugs); naming-convention digests (explicit per-row classes only); prose allowlists (annotations generate the registries). Risk: registry churn during design — bounded by permanent/reserved tag discipline and `registry_epoch` semantics.

## Provenance
§5.1 (lines 276–298, 328, 338), §19 G0 paragraph.

### Fidelity addendum — generated containing-schema reference unions
`durable_fields.toml` must generate a finite, containing-schema-and-role-specific tagged reference union for every polymorphic durable field. Required concrete exemplars are `LocalCommandInputRef`, `MetaAppliedResultRef`, `ShardProtocolEvidenceRef`, and `MandatoryInventoryRef`; each generated arm names exactly one registered top-level target schema and carries that target's canonical typed reference encoding. Bare `StrongRef`, `StrongRef<A|B>`, `StrongRef[]`, `result_refs[StrongRef]`, slash-separated pseudo-types, or a generic `RegisteredStrongRef` without the exact generated arm set are invalid normative bytes. Compact Appendix notation is navigation only and must expand through one exact field-table row.

The generator must build the concrete construction DAG for every command tag and activated state slot and reject self-edges, mutual cycles, future-result edges, role-invalid arms, missing/extra target arms, or an arm whose identity/retention class disagrees with its target registry row. Golden vectors cover every arm/tag; mutation tests swap Local/Meta/Shard targets and substitute same-shaped schemas; fuzz decoders reject unknown/retired/duplicate tags. Detailed generation logs emit `containing_schema_id`, `field_tag`, `generated_union_id`, sorted arm/tag/target triples, role/posture predicate, construction-order class, and reachability strength so a registry diff is auditable without consulting prose.
acceptance_criteria:
### Normative phase and ownership boundary

This bead proves the G0 identity-registry constitution. It does not claim executable W1/W2 byte-format or cryptographic implementation evidence.

HRX owns: strict versioned schemas and fail-closed unknown-key handling; the exact projection of the completed fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-91ol catalog into identity-class, field, digest, and explicit reference-union-arm rows; class disjointness; code/tag range laws; immutable released assignments; retired-code nonreuse; registry_epoch evolution witnesses; union anchor/role/posture/lifecycle/identity/retention closure; schema-level construction/reference closure over completed Appendix A rows; BodyDigest/transcript recipe metadata closure; rejecting registry mutation fixtures; and deterministic row-level JSONL with exact metadata diffs.

Activation requirements remain mandatory downstream and are not waived. fgdb-g0-command-contracts-nf1 extends the DAG over every concrete command tag and durable state slot and owns command/handler/state bijection. fgdb-w1-generated-parsers-i3k owns compiled canonical encoders/decoders, generated field tables and executable encode/digest/decode round trips. fgdb-w1-format-test-corpora-lyf owns checked-in golden, mutation, cross-version and fuzz bytes plus mismatch offsets. fgdb-w2-object-identity-t0f owns full keyed ObjectId/CiphertextId/EncodingId/PlacementId recomputation. Their checker-index rows remain stub until those owners make them runnable.

HRX may close only after fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-91ol supplies complete catalog coverage and every HRX-owned law above is green. It may close while the explicitly downstream W1/W2 checker rows remain stub; Gate G0 composes HRX with the command/state registries, and later activation gates require the byte and cryptographic checkers to become live.
