Yes, the fix needed a scoped binary path, and it took more than scoping.

  BIN is now "$WORK/bin/registry-check", compiled from THIS tree by the gate
  itself. CARGO_TARGET_DIR is no longer read by this script at all.

The shared-dir hazard, measured live while working this bead: g0_spine_e2e.sh
returned **7 passed, 3 failed at 19:22 and 8 passed, 2 failed at 19:24 with no
change to the repo between the runs** — another pane rebuilt
/data/tmp/cargo-target/debug/registry-check in between. A verdict that moves
when the subject does not is not a measurement of the subject. (Same artifact
earlier carried wire_types pin fnv1a64:0f3dcd03f7a9eaf7, absent from the whole
tracked tree, reporting 24 violations against a green tree.)

## EACH SCRIPT PROVES ITS OWN SUBJECT

Every sourcing script runs a two-direction control in ITS OWN tally: the
freshness rule must accept the artifact that run just built AND reject a
backdated one. A gate that passed only because some other script proved the
predicate would be a vacuous pass wearing a fresh name.

The probe is `chmod +x` on purpose. `subject_is_fresh` rejects both a
non-executable file and a stale one, so a merely-unreadable probe would be
rejected FOR THE WRONG REASON and the control would pass while proving nothing
— the precise defect this bead is about. The probe differs from a good artifact
in its mtime and in nothing else, and the library says so, so that a future rule
beyond mtime cannot silence the controls unnoticed.

volume at 95% carrying 9594 stale /data/tmp/tmp.* directories. Nothing in the
library or in any script that sources it deletes a file.

title: Land the threat/trust model, authority lattice, and per-posture authority footprint
description:
## What & scope
Land the deployment-independent threat/trust model, the stable security identity vocabulary, the `EffectiveAuthority` lattice with its sixteen operation classes, the macaroon narrowing (attenuation) laws that define the authority order, and the per-posture external-authority footprint table. Every deployment profile must declare actors, protected assets, assumptions, and out-of-scope failures before selecting any claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6's agent-native story is capability-scoped subgraph authorization; reviewers flag governance/access-control as the unsolved problem of current graph systems, and GitLab's forced migration off Kùzu shows the market shopping for governance-grade embedded engines. A threat model landed at G0 keeps every later security mechanism honestly scoped: no claim outruns its trust assumptions.

## Design — normative detail
**Trust matrix:** the model distinguishes untrusted clients, mutually hostile tenants, honest-but-curious storage, crash-fault replicas, malicious/stale donors, independent transparency witnesses, trusted embedded host code, and a compromised operator/server. The baseline trusts the executing database process and active key boundary to enforce plaintext confidentiality and policy; a compromised server process can exfiltrate what it can decrypt — no TEE/Byzantine-confidentiality magic is claimed. Witnessed transparency/audit may detect only their scoped history/administrative attacks, not undo disclosure. Ordinary Raft tolerates crash faults, not Byzantine replicas. Explicit §3.4-registered rejections: FHE/MPC/ORAM out of the initial threat model; DP and leakage measurements are scoped mechanisms, never substitutes for noninterference.

**Identity vocabulary:** stable identities `TenantId`, `PrincipalId`, `IssuerId`, `TokenId`, `DatabaseId`, `SecurityPolicyEpoch`, `RevocationIndex`, `DecisionPolicyEpoch`, `KeyEpoch`; security and adaptive epoch types have distinct wire tags and Rust newtypes and are never comparable or substitutable. **Authority lattice:** `EffectiveAuthority` binds tenant/subject/issuer/audience, database security namespace and cluster incarnation, token/security-policy epochs, current revocation index, operation classes, graph/branch/label/edge/property/system-field/temporal scopes, procedure/UDF/module ObjectIds and invocation mode, external-I/O classes, replay evidence/resolver closure, redaction profile, and resource ceiling. Operation classes are the closed set `Read, Mutate, Ddl, Subscribe, Analytics, Replay, ExecuteProcedure, InstallModule, ExternalIo, Export, Backup, Restore, Observe, Admin, KeyManage, Replicate`. The lattice's order is defined by macaroon attenuation law: every chain link may only raise effective not-before, lower effective expiry, intersect authority/resource scopes, append accepted caveats, and preserve or further restrict presentation binding (`ServerInternal|SessionBound|ChannelBound`); it cannot extend time, change authority domain, widen disclosure, move cohorts, or weaken binding — narrowing-only by construction. Graph caveats compile to the versioned, deterministic, total, resource-bounded `PolicyIr`, never arbitrary GQL.

**Per-posture authority footprint (§16 item 8):** every registered posture publishes a table stating, for each external authority — identity/allocation continuity (`IdentityContinuityRecord`/`AllocationEpochReservation`), cluster incarnation (`ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord`), time authority (`PortableTimeAuthorityObservation`), audit continuity (`AuditContinuityRecord`), DP registry (`PrivacyContinuityRecord`), archive/grant (`ArchiveRetentionGrant`), reservation (`ReservationAuthorityHead`), catalog (`CatalogAuthorityHead`), the restore dispatch journal's `ExternalCasContinuity` head, transparency witnesses (`WitnessPolicy`), KMS/HSM — whether it sits on a synchronous operation path and exactly where. The v1 footprint: audit continuity touches a Required operation three times (strictly serial `TicketIssued` issuance CAS, admission visibility advance, share of one batched `TicketsResolvedBatch`); time authority per protected-output activation tick (batch-amortized) and per `IdRangeLease` use window; incarnation continuity only at `ExternalCas` lease acquisition/renewal; KMS/HSM only at key-unwrap miss; identity/allocation continuity only at allocation-epoch mint; DP registry only at DP charges; archive/reservation/catalog/restore journal only in backup/restore flows; witnesses only at transparency-proof freshness. The embedded `DirectoryBound` posture's footprint table is empty: zero external authorities.

## Invariants & claim types
Binds FG-INV-20 ("authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability... capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure") — the threat model is the frame in which that invariant's clauses are scoped. The footprint table rows are invariant-class structural facts; non-equivocation claims are conditional on declared witnessed-transparency premises (FG-INV-08); leakage measurements are FG-EVID class.

## Interactions
g0-format-arms consumes the posture vocabulary (AllocationContinuityProfile residual risk); g0-cost-registry's external-authority column prices this table. w1-authz-policy implements permit/policy IR types; w9-threat-tokens implements the macaroon lifecycle; w9-time-authority and w9-audit-continuity implement footprint authorities; w9-authority-surface publishes the §16 table; w2-continuity-profiles implements the continuity arms.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
The threat-model document enumerates every actor/asset/assumption pair with claim-scoping references; a generated check proving every posture has a complete footprint row for all eleven authorities (or an explicit empty declaration); type-level tests that `SecurityPolicyEpoch` and `DecisionPolicyEpoch` do not unify; attenuation-law property tests (chain can only narrow: widening fixtures fail); a review fixture asserting no normative text claims confidentiality against a compromised server process.

Named suites: `tm_actor_asset_assumption_complete`, `tm_footprint_all_postures_eleven_authorities`, `tm_directorybound_footprint_empty`, `tm_epoch_types_do_not_unify` (compile-fail fixtures for `SecurityPolicyEpoch`/`DecisionPolicyEpoch` substitution), property test `tm_attenuation_narrowing_only` (random attenuation chains may only raise not-before, lower expiry, intersect scopes, append caveats, and restrict presentation binding; every widening mutation fails) with negatives `tm_neg_time_extension`/`tm_neg_domain_change`/`tm_neg_binding_weakening`, and the review fixture `tm_no_compromised_server_confidentiality_claim`. E2E: `scripts/g0_threat_e2e.sh` builds the threat-model document and footprint tables from their registry sources, runs the generated completeness check over every registered posture and all eleven authorities, executes the attenuation property suite, and scans merged normative text for claims exceeding the trust matrix, failing with file/line. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: posture_checked|authority_row_checked|attenuation_case, posture, authority, sync_path_position, operation_class, case_id, outcome}`; the footprint check logs every (posture, authority) cell as present/empty-declared/missing; attenuation tests log the mutated field and the typed rejection; the claim scan logs each flagged sentence with its trust-matrix conflict.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected for 1.0 (§3.4): FHE/MPC/ORAM; TEE reliance; Byzantine consensus; TrueTime-class infrastructure (HLC plus consensus-fenced read contracts supply the specified semantics). Risk: footprint drift as mechanisms land — mitigated by making the table a generated registry artifact under the same-change discipline.

## Provenance
§12.1–§12.2 (lines 860–872), §16 item 8 (line 1222), §3.4 (line 157), §19 G0 paragraph.

THE FOUR "UNSPECIFIED VOCABULARIES" FROM THE 2026-07-22 CODEX COMMENT — ALL FOUR RESOLVED BY DERIVATION, NONE BY INVENTION:

1. Deployment-profile product space. NOT a list — a declared product space with named exclusion laws.
   Axes: service_class {Operational, ArchiveReadOnly} x role_posture {Local, Sharded} x continuity_profile {DirectoryBound, ExternalCas, NotApplicable} = 12 cells.
   PX-1 (§5.1): Sharded => ExternalCas. PX-2 (§13.7): ArchiveReadOnly => NotApplicable. PX-3 (§5.1): Operational => not NotApplicable.
   Result: 2 registered (local_directory_bound, local_external_cas), 2 deferred with owner beads (sharded_external_cas -> W12; archive_read_only_open -> fgdb-g0-format-arms-90z, because §13.7 says in terms that its posture row is reserved in the §19 G0 decision batch), 8 excluded. The checker enumerates all 12 and fails on any unresolved cell, AND fails if a registered posture occupies an excluded cell (both directions).

2. ServerInternal/SessionBound/ChannelBound transition matrix. DERIVED, not asserted. §12.2 permits "preserve or further restrict" and forbids moving "Session/Channel binding to a less restrictive class". ServerInternal binds no presentation (rank 0), SessionBound binds session+auth generation (1), ChannelBound binds a transport exporter digest (2). A transition is legal iff to_rank >= from_rank. All 9 cells registered; 6 legal, 3 illegal. The checker DERIVES legality from rank and fails if a declared cell disagrees — so the matrix cannot be edited into unsoundness.

3. EffectiveAuthority dimensions + comparison semantics. 27 dimensions: the 23 of §12.1 in source order, plus effective_not_before / effective_expires_at / accepted_caveats / presentation_binding from §12.2. Each declares ONE narrowing operator from a closed set of 8: fixed, intersect, raise_only, lower_only, append_only, restrict_disclosure_only, restrict_binding_only, current_state_monotone. The lattice has NO independent order — its order IS the conjunction of these operators, which is why every dimension must declare one and an ungoverned dimension is a violation.

4. Leakage StatisticalClaim carrier. FG-EVID-05 added to evidence.toml. The codex comment was right that FG-EVID-01..04 has no leakage carrier; but the required_disclosures did not need inventing — §12.6 names them verbatim ("secret distribution, attacker observations, concurrency assumptions, padding schedule, sampling design, confidence bound, and identity-level cumulative budget"). The row is a transcription.

RULING I MADE, RECORD IT: the footprint table does NOT bind realized operation classes. §16 item 8 names each authority's TRIGGER SITE but never says which of the 16 operation classes the realized path uses. All 11 cells carry operation_class_basis = "trigger_site_only" with operation_classes = [] and deferred_binding_owner = fgdb-w9-authority-surface-gp9j. The checker enforces this as an honesty law: a trigger_site_only cell that names an operation class is a violation (footprint_unsourced_operation_class). Binding them here would have manufactured a G0 fact from a W9 measurement.

THREE LAWS DISCOVERED THAT ARE NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE ELSE:

L1. A stable sort makes a DUPLICATED ordinal invisible to a source-order check. check_sequence sorts rows by ordinal and compares the name sequence; with Read and Mutate both at ordinal 2, the stable sort leaves them in their original positions, the name sequence is correct, and the registry validates clean. My own fixture caught this. Fix: check_dense_order() asserts a collision-free dense 1..n, applied to actors, assets, identities, operation_classes, authority_dimensions, external_authorities. Same "looks exactly like a pass" family as a vacuous fixture — if another registry checks source order by sorting, it has this hole.

L2. Two tables that encode the same law drift independently and only a hash notices. The prohibition table (ATT-X2 "cannot change authority domain") and the dimension table (tenant.narrowing_operator) both encode domain-fixity. Flipping tenant to "intersect" left every semantic check green and moved only semantic_contract_hash. A hash tells you something moved, never that the model became unsound. Fix: prohibition_operator_mismatch cross-checks that a prohibited law's governed dimensions carry an operator that actually forbids the mutation.

L3. A claim-scan rule fires on the sentence that STATES the prohibition. TMS-1 flagged A-NO-TEE's own bounds line, "No normative text may claim confidentiality against a compromised server process." Weakening the subject would have hidden real violations; the qualifier list is the right mechanism. Recorded in the registry next to the rule.

SOURCES READ (so a successor need not re-read): plan §3.4 (line 153-157), §12.1 (860-864), §12.2 (866-868), §12.3, §12.6 (906-916), §13.7 (ArchiveReadOnlyOpen), §16 item 8 (1226-1230), §16 intro, §19 G0 paragraph, §5.1 IncarnationContinuityProfile (lines 225/344/364/1892). Four of these are pinned as checked source blocks in the registry and embedded verbatim in the generated document with fnv1a64 pins, so drift in any of them turns the gate red.

FOLLOW-UPS TO FILE ON CLOSE:
- literal compile-fail fixture for SecurityPolicyEpoch vs DecisionPolicyEpoch substitution belongs to fgdb-w1-authz-policy-10y (G0 can only prove distinct registry/tag/symbol identities; the real newtypes do not exist yet). tm_epoch_types_do_not_unify documents this in its doc comment.
- fgdb-w9-authority-surface-gp9j inherits the realized operation-class binding for all 11 footprint cells.
- fgdb-g0-format-arms-90z inherits the archive_read_only_open posture row; W12 inherits sharded_external_cas.

title: Freeze and enforce the complete workspace crate/layer dependency topology
description:
## What & scope
Freeze and enforce the complete workspace topology: every crate/layer in section 18.1, every legal dependency direction, every unsafe boundary, and the exact build-here versus consume-from-foundation inventory. This is a contract/CI task, not permission to create empty prototype crates; a crate appears only with its first real final-abstraction slice.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The closed dependency universe and layer direction are safety properties. Without one executable map, later work can add an external crate, invert Chronicle/Strata/Loom ownership, duplicate an asupersync or fnx subsystem, link frankensqlite, or relax unsafe policy.

## Design — exact normative contract
The full section 18 contract follows:
## 18. Workspace Layout & the Build-It-Ourselves Inventory

### 18.1 Crates (`fgdb-*` workspace, layered; Cargo-enforced boundaries per frankensqlite)

| Layer | Crates |
|---|---|
| Foundation | `fgdb-types`, `fgdb-bigint` (canonical exact integers), `fgdb-delta-types` (G0/W2 delta schema only), `fgdb-claim`, `fgdb-authz-types`, `fgdb-policy` (restricted verifier IR), `fgdb-resource`, `fgdb-codec`, `fgdb-sketch`, `fgdb-collections`, `fgdb-crypto`, `fgdb-calibrate`, `fgdb-evidence` |
| Unsafe islands | `fgdb-unsafe-simd`, `fgdb-unsafe-arena`, `fgdb-unsafe-vfs` — the only crate roots not using `forbid(unsafe_code)`; every site is ledgered and exposed only through safe APIs |
| Chronicle | `fgdb-ecs` (identity/encoding/bootstrap/object locator), `fgdb-order` (durable Raft log/state core and quorum-one driver), `fgdb-chronicle` (capsule/marker/logical-local roots, allocator, outcomes, checkpoints/retention, recovery/GC/scrub), `fgdb-branch`, `fgdb-keymgr`, `fgdb-audit`, `fgdb-backup` |
| Strata | `fgdb-strata` (label-independent tiers, seal/compact, stable-ID directory), `fgdb-props`, `fgdb-buffer`, `fgdb-scratch` |
| Txn + secure access | `fgdb-txn` (MVCC, Graph-SSI/witness lifecycle, coordinator, final-effect merge ladder), `fgdb-constraints` (branch-scoped canonical enforcement), `fgdb-secure-view` (sole authorized storage/permit facade); depends on Chronicle + Strata + foundation policy verifier |
| Loom | `fgdb-gql` + `fgdb-cypher` (syntax only), `fgdb-bind`, `fgdb-algebra`, `fgdb-planner`, `fgdb-exec`, `fgdb-linalg`, `fgdb-datalog`; all reads flow through `fgdb-secure-view` |
| Ripple | `fgdb-ripple` (Z-sets, circuits, incrementalizer), `fgdb-views`, `fgdb-subs` |
| Beacon | `fgdb-index-core`, `fgdb-btree`, `fgdb-fts`, `fgdb-vector`, `fgdb-pathidx` (2-hop/landmark + the persistent-union-find temporal-connectivity index, §10.7) |
| Prism | `fgdb-prism` (authorized projection bridge, fnx cursor/cache/materialization paths, native kernels) |
| Warden | `fgdb-warden` (issuance/revocation/discharges/policy admin), `fgdb-privacy`, `fgdb-redaction` |
| Surface/operations | `fgdb-protocol` (FGP state machine), `fgdb-bolt`, `fgdb-formats`, `fgdb-udf-vm`, `fgdb-observatory`, `fgdb-system-graph` |
| Aegis | `fgdb-raft` (multi-member protocol over `fgdb-order`), `fgdb-repl` (payload availability, anti-entropy, reconfiguration, fenced GC); future `fgdb-shard` belongs only to W12 |
| Composition | `fgdb` (embedded API), `fgdb-server` (top-level Fabric+Warden+Aegis composition), `fgdb-cli`, `fgdb-python` (allowed fnx-python packaging boundary only), `fgdb-adbc` (C-ABI ADBC packaging at the same boundary; §13.7) |
| Verification | `fgdb-sim`, `fgdb-reference` (executable semantics oracle), `fgdb-oracles`, `fgdb-bench`, `fgdb-conformance`, `fgdb-fuzz` |

G0 materializes `invariants.toml`, `evidence.toml`, `slo.toml`, the unsafe-boundary ledger, feature/conformance matrices, threat model, format registries, proof-lane manifests, and exit-criteria contracts before Genesis implementation.

### 18.2 Built in-house (because the universe is closed)

Compression codecs (EF, delta-varint, bitpacking, snappy, roaring-like), canonical signed-limb exact integers, sketches, ART/radix structures, succinct rank/select, vectorized hash tables, B-tree, HNSW + quantizers + IVF-PQ cold tier, persistent union-find, masked-semiring SpMV/SpMSpV kernels, inverted index + BM25 + Levenshtein automata, tokenizers, CSV/JSONL/Parquet-lite readers, GQL/Cypher parsers (hand-written recursive descent + Pratt — the frankensqlite parser school), the DBSP-style circuit runtime, Raft, FGP, Bolt subset, crypto profiles/primitives not already supplied by an audited foundation, the MMR accumulator + transparency checkpoints, the Sextant calibration scores/ledgers (over asupersync's e-process core), the deterministic UDF bytecode VM (§13.8), bench harness. **Explicitly not built**: async runtime, scheduler, channels, TLS/QUIC/HTTP/gRPC stacks, RaptorQ, macaroons, metrics/OTel, deterministic lab, supervision, cluster membership (SWIM+Lifeguard), Merkle-range anti-entropy, coded symbol distribution, CRDT obligation ledgers, HLC, choreographic projection, LDFI/delta-debug/dual-run/trace-export tooling, Kafka/JetStream clients — all asupersync; graph algorithms & legacy formats — all fnx. The closed-universe constraint, which sounds like an albatross, is the moat: the entire dependency surface is auditable, deterministic under lab, and owned.

## Invariants & claims
Ordinary crates use workspace unsafe_code=forbid; only named fgdb-unsafe islands may contain ledgered narrow allows with bit-identical scalar fallbacks. Allowed source is core/alloc/std, pinned nightly, asupersync, and fnx; frankensqlite is design-only and never linked.

## Interactions and ownership
G0 freezes the map; W1 establishes Cargo policy/checkers; every workstream adds crates/edges only through a registered row. README/AGENTS generation renders it. Release CI compares Cargo metadata, source scans, unsafe ledger, feature graph, target matrix, and build-versus-consume inventory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A registry lists every section 18.1 crate, layer, binary/posture role, unsafe policy, allowed incoming/outgoing layers, activation status, and owner.
- A second registry lists every section 18.2 capability as BuildHere or ConsumeFrom(asupersync/fnx/design-only-frankensqlite), with exact package/source evidence.
- Cargo-metadata CI proves no inversion, cycle, undeclared crate, default-feature escape, external dependency, duplicate foundation capability, linked fsqlite package, or ordinary-crate unsafe relaxation.
- Golden tests freeze graph rendering and feature predicates; mutation fixtures add one forbidden edge/dependency/unsafe site and must fail stably.
- Cross-target E2E runs the checker and builds representative embedded/server/CLI closures; later APFS/Windows profiles activate only through roadmap beads.
- Structured JSONL emits {event_version,crate,layer,activation_status,unsafe_policy,resolved_dependencies,allowed_edges,foundation_capabilities_consumed,built_here_capabilities,violations,workspace_digest,replay_command}. CI requires one event per crate and inventory row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: README-only diagrams, negative-only deny-lists, empty placeholder crates, shim layers, linked fsqlite crates, and foundation reimplementation. Map changes are explicit and accompany the feature bead that needs them.

## Provenance
Plan section 18.1-18.2 lines 1277-1302; Engineering Doctrine 1-3; G0 self-containment.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.
acceptance_criteria: All detailed success criteria, tests, E2E scenarios, and diagnostic-event requirements in the description are mandatory.

All six acceptance criteria met; the crate/layer/unsafe/activation/owner registry and the build-versus-consume inventory are both live, the closed-universe, inversion, cycle, undeclared-crate, default-feature, duplicate-capability, linked-fsqlite and unsafe-relaxation checks run against the LIVE tree from Cargo manifests, golden rendering is byte-exact, and four mutation fixtures plus a synthetic-graph panel prove the laws fire. No residue bead: the one finding (plan §2.1 enumerates no messaging asset row for §18.2's Kafka/JetStream clients) is carried as a checked [[asset_evidence_gap]] whose ABSENCE the checker verifies, and is a plan edit this bead does not own. See the closing comment for the layer ordering, the single registered foundation<->unsafe_islands reciprocal exception, and the five laws.

comments.text:
LANDED a172dd3. registries/workspace_topology.toml (master) + docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md

Replay: cargo run -p registry-check --bin topology-check -- --root .   (--write regenerates the doc)

WHAT IS FROZEN. 14 layers, 70 crate rows (10 active / 59 planned / 1 reserved =
fgdb-shard, W12-only), 3 postures, 3 foundation projects, 51 inventory rows
(23 build_here / 19 consume_from / 9 design_only), 8 named crate-level edges,
1 dependency narrowing (fgdb-reference), 11 pinned plan source blocks.

THE ORDERING, AND THE ONE EXCEPTION THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS FROM THE FILE.
allowed_outgoing_layers is DERIVED and recomputed by the checker, never trusted:
    allowed(L) = { M : M.source_order <= L.source_order }  UNION  { unsafe_islands }
Source order is exactly the §18.1 table order: foundation(1), unsafe_islands(2),
chronicle(3), strata(4), txn_secure_access(5), loom(6), ripple(7), beacon(8),
prism(9), warden(10), surface_operations(11), aegis(12), composition(13),
verification(14).
The UNION term is the exception and it is deliberate: §18.1 lists the islands
SECOND, but foundation codec/crypto/collections kernels consume them (per
fgdb-w1-unsafe-ledger-icp's own consumer list) while the islands consume only
foundation types. That is one reciprocal LAYER pair (foundation <-> unsafe_islands),
registered in [layer_law] with its rationale, and it is the ONLY place where table
order is not dependency order. It is sound only because crate-level acyclicity is
checked separately and unconditionally (Kahn over the live graph) --
[layer_law].crate_graph_must_be_acyclic = true is load-bearing, not decoration; a
mutation test asserts that flipping it to false fails.
Second non-obvious ordering fact: Warden(10) sits ABOVE Txn(5) and there is no
inversion, because the restricted verifier IR is a FOUNDATION crate (fgdb-policy).
Warden administers policy; the secure view verifies it. Anyone who "fixes" this by
making fgdb-secure-view depend on fgdb-warden inverts the layer graph.

LAWS THE CHECKER ENFORCES THAT WERE NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE BEFORE.
1. The crate universe is DERIVED from the frozen §18.1 markdown table, not retyped:
   parse_layer_table() extracts backticked fgdb-shaped tokens per row, and the
   comparison runs BOTH ways (unregistered crate the plan names -> fail; invented
   crate -> fail; wrong per-layer order -> fail). Cross-references inside
   annotations (fgdb-secure-view in the Loom row, fgdb-order in Aegis) are kept for
   coverage and filtered by layer for membership -- that is why membership is
   checked per-layer rather than per-token.
2. INVENTORY COVERAGE IS PROVED BY RESIDUE. Every capability phrase is deleted from
   the frozen §18.2 line (each must occur exactly once at its turn, longest-first);
   what remains must be only { space , . ; & } plus four registered rationale
   allowances. A dropped capability leaves a residue token and names itself. This is
   the instrument that makes "we accidentally rebuilt an asupersync subsystem"
   catchable at registry level; a hand-eyeballed list cannot do it.
3. Activation is a BIJECTION with the live tree, both directions: planned row +
   existing directory -> phantom_crate_directory; directory + no row ->
   crate_undeclared. This is what makes "no empty prototype crates" mechanical.
4. Island roster is cross-checked against registries/unsafe_boundary_ledger.toml
   (path declared in the header) with agreeing statuses: my activation_status=active
   <-> their status=present. Two registries naming the same three islands must not be
   able to disagree. Ownership split preserved: site rows + site<->allow bijection
   are theirs, the crate-level policy column is mine.
5. THE IN-HOUSE TOML PARSER CANNOT READ CARGO MANIFESTS. crate::toml rejects inline
   tables by design and every git dependency is one, so topology.rs carries its own
   line-oriented manifest scanner (single-line inline tables, [dependencies.foo]
   sub-tables, renames via package=, dev/build tables) that FAILS CLOSED on any field
   it does not know. Anyone adding a Cargo-manifest law elsewhere must not reach for
   crate::toml::parse. (Note for a successor: architecture.rs:1262 resolve_workspace_package
   DOES call read_toml on member manifests -- that path can only be erroring today.)

DEFERRALS, reported as `deferred` and never as `pass`.
7 of 8 named edges have no active endpoint; the only live one is
calibrate-over-asupersync, and the suite asserts that live/deferred split explicitly
so the law cannot go vacuous unnoticed. All 3 posture closures are unevaluable while
no composition crate exists. The closure evaluator, cycle detector and manifest
scanner are therefore proved on SYNTHETIC fixtures in the suite -- a green bar
meaning "no composition crate is active" reads exactly like one meaning "no
composition crate is misplaced".

FINDING, recorded not papered over (registered as the single [[asset_evidence_gap]]).
§18.2 attributes "Kafka/JetStream clients" to asupersync, but §2.1's asset table --
the source of our exact per-capability evidence -- enumerates NO messaging row. The
capability is really there in the pinned foundation (src/messaging/, behind the
default-off `kafka` feature backed by rdkafka), so this is a plan documentation gap,
not an invented dependency and not something we should be building. The checker
verifies the ABSENCE, so the gap cannot become an escape hatch: a gap whose asset row
exists is itself a violation (asset_gap_resolvable). Fixing it = add a messaging row
to plan §2.1 lines 58-75, then delete the gap row and set foundation_asset. That is a
plan edit this bead does not own; NOT filed as a bead because creating one deepens the
already-red architecture bead-provenance pin, and the finding is fully carried in a
checked artifact.

ONE JUDGMENT CALL A SUCCESSOR MIGHT REVISIT. asupersync carries
default_features_must_be_disabled = true on basis "workspace_convention_unanimous"
(all 5 live declarations set it); fnx carries false on basis "plan_permits_defaults",
because FG-CON-01 explicitly admits fnx-python's already-pinned transitive binding
runtime and a blanket rule would break exactly that. The asupersync rule is a frozen
convention, not a plan quotation -- that is what the *_basis column records.

MAP CHANGES: a crate/edge/capability row moves WITH the feature bead that needs it,
never after. Both hash pins (id_table_hash, semantic_contract_hash) are duplicated in
tests/workspace_topology.rs on purpose: the binary recomputes from what it reads, so a
coordinated row+header edit stays green, but a constant in a test file does not move
unless someone moves it.

control: architecture_decisions (4 failures -- 3 orphan beads fgdb-5cgb,
fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx, fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8 need
the bead-provenance re-pin cycle) and satisfiability (identity_code_set_is_ratcheted,
42 unregistered appendix codes). Green after my work: workspace_topology 56/56,
identity 99/99, threat_model 40/40, unsafe_ledger 13/13, claims 13/13, spine 8/8
(spine was red since 26cc3a3 -- FG-EVID-05 was added to evidence.toml without moving
the frozen gate table; repaired in a9dfb6f).

title: Activate G3 protocol and external-authority simulation oracles
description:
## What & scope
Build the phase-correct G3 simulation and independent-oracle campaign for the 1.0 networked product. This task activates the generic `fgdb-sim` and `fgdb-oracles` engines against the concrete W9 Warden, W10 Fabric, and W11 multi-member/continuity implementations. It owns live G3 protocol/authority validation; the base verifier beads own reusable engines and Local checker primitives only. Post-1.0 Meta/Shard/W12 behavior is explicitly out of scope and is owned by the separate W12 verification epic.

## Why
G3 promises that the Local database remains correct when its protected outputs, audit/DP/key workflows, wire protocols, external authorities, and Raft ownership are exercised together under loss, retries, partitions, revocation, and leader changes. That promise cannot be discharged by checker schemas registered before the implementations exist. This task closes the phase gap with independent canonical models and executable simulated histories over the actual G3 state machines.

## Normative design
- Instantiate deterministic lab models for every G3 external authority actually used by W9-W11: identity/allocation continuity, audit continuity sequencing, archive/grant, reservation, catalog, restore-dispatch `ExternalCasContinuity`, profiled time evidence, and configured key/KMS completion authorities. Each modeled CAS head is a linearizable register accepting only direct authenticated successors under the registered predecessor-digest law.
- Run Elle-class history checks over each authority chain. Negatives create a double successor at one CAS version, predecessor-digest regression, stale-head resurrection, lost response followed by idempotent retry, and conflicting authority evidence. Ticket admission, recovery, restore reconciliation, status/completeness, and relevant wire admission consumers must all reject forks fail-closed.
- Instantiate independent canonical-map protocol machines for FGP handshake/authentication/posture negotiation, typed child streams, begin/idempotency/status/cancel, result and artifact owner arms, ACK/release/resume, audit ticket/sign/visibility/activation, DP charge/seed/result retention, staged key activation/destruction, multi-member Raft ownership/reconfiguration, backup/restore visibility/service/reopen, and wire-safe status projection. Optimized traces are compared transition by transition, including refusals, retained obligations, evidence identities, and public bytes.
- Attach the independent Local strict-serializability SCC/history oracle to mixed durable writes, read-only/SnapshotQuery, audit-visible versus applied-hidden states, leader loss, reconfiguration, and external-authority interleavings. Production graph algorithms may be a secondary differential only.
- Enforce authorization-before-observation and byte-equivalent public outcomes across FGP, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt V1. Cross-capability result/plan/error/timing classes, revocation during streams, hidden restore endpoints, stale service epochs, donor poisoning, key rotation, DP seed/result invisibility, and parser/resource exhaustion are mandatory negative matrices.
- All campaigns declare filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models. Passing a bounded campaign is falsification evidence, not proof of bug absence.

## Dependencies and phase boundary
Consumes the reusable sim/oracle engines and the completed G2 semantics, then the concrete W9, W10, and W11 epics. It feeds G3 and the 1.0 verification epic. It MUST NOT depend on, activate, or claim coverage for W12 Meta/Shard formats or state machines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests for every canonical transition function, refusal reason, predecessor/CAS validator, projection rule, retained-obligation update, and public-byte encoder; mutation tests prove each validator can fail.
- Property tests generate legal and illegal authority chains and protocol traces, compare optimized versus canonical states after every step, and prove deterministic replay for identical seed/configuration.
- Simulation campaigns cover authority fork/rollback/lost-response, revocation between protected chunks, result disconnect/ACK/release races, audit external-CAS/mirror/visibility/activation, DP charged-crash recovery, key stage/activate/zero/destroy, leader loss and joint reconfiguration, restore hidden/service/reopen, and stale service/capability rejection.
- E2E: boot a three-member Local deployment with all simulated G3 authorities; authenticate through each adapter; execute durable write, SnapshotQuery, subscription, protected result resume, DP request, backup/restore status, audit visibility, leader loss, and joint reconfiguration; inject one authority fork and one revocation; assert fail-closed behavior, identical wire-safe terminal outcomes, no protected-byte leak, legal recovered state, and replayable artifacts.
- Coverage registry CI requires every activated G3 command/state/checker clause to name a live campaign; pending rows are allowed only for disabled features and cannot count toward G3.

## Detailed structured diagnostics
Every unit/property/simulation/E2E verdict emits JSONL with `{run_id,scenario_id,phase:"G3",seed,model_profile_digest,oracle_id,clause_id,authority_kind,cas_version,protocol_machine,role,member_id,configuration_epoch,service_visibility_epoch,logical_commit_raft_applied_visible_audit_positions,attempt_statement_workspace_result_dp_audit_key_backup_restore_ids,transition,expected,actual,verdict}`. Failures additionally emit the complete secret-redacted §15.1 artifact with schedule, crash/fault point, evidence identities, first divergence, and executable `replay_command`; the command is executed in CI for a sampled failure. Gate reports must be reproducible from these records alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: treating early registered checker rows as live evidence; reusing production SCC/graph algorithms as the sole oracle; interpreting transport success as result ACK/release; accepting best-effort authority reconciliation. Risk of model/implementation drift is controlled by generated trace schemas, live dual runs, mutation tests, and phase-gated coverage.

## Provenance
Plan §15.1-§15.4 and §19 Gate G3; Appendix F FG-INV-01, 04, 05, 07, 08, 10, 16, 19, 20. Phase correction: W12 verification is intentionally separate.

title: Run G3 protocol fuzzing and multi-member HA torture
description:
## What & scope
Execute the phase-correct G3 protocol fuzzing, fault-injection, and high-availability torture program over the concrete W9 Warden, W10 Fabric, and W11 multi-member implementations. This task extends the Local durability matrix with network/protocol/authority/member failures required for G3. It does not cover Meta/Shard/W12 transition machines; those have a dedicated post-1.0 verification epic.

## Why
A green Local crash matrix and a language fuzzer do not establish the G3 claim. G3 adds framed untrusted inputs, protected multi-transport output, external CAS authorities, distributed ownership, leader loss, joint configuration, restore visibility, key destruction, and DP/audit retention. Each new boundary creates partial-frame, SentUnknown, duplicated-operation, hidden-state, obligation-leak, and premature-release failure modes that must be attacked after the implementation exists.

## Normative campaign inventory
- Fuzz every FGP frame and state transition, including truncated/oversized/fragmented frames, illegal stream/type transitions, stale and cross-session public handles/tokens, idempotency conflicts, cancellation races, result resume/ACK/release, protected-error silence, flow-control exhaustion, and parser budget exhaustion. Execute the same semantic corpus through HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt V1 adapters and require canonical outcome parity.
- Crash/partition at each G3 ordered, certificate, external-CAS, and physical-side-effect boundary: audit ticket/lock/share/candidate/batch-CAS/mirror/visibility/activation; DP debit/seed/wrap/fragment/result; key plan/stage/certify/manifest/activate/zero/durable destroy/member-or-KMS completion; artifact/result send-guard and owner transitions; backup/restore publication/service/reopen/release; Raft receive/prepare/order/apply/snapshot/joint configuration/final retirement.
- Multi-member campaigns cover leader loss at every prepared/ordered/applied/visible stage, payload/certificate loss, uncertain membership, stale writer and donor poisoning, joint/final configuration floors, two-prefix fenced reads, snapshot+suffix recovery, no timeout-fractured atomicity, and physical retirement evidence.
- Security/continuity campaigns cover authority split brain, stale continuity head, wrong role/domain/incarnation/configuration/grant/permit/service epoch, hidden restore direct-endpoint probes, revocation between chunks, cross-capability result/plan/error/timing differentials, and zero seed/result observability at every DP failure point.
- Recovery/status campaigns cover Unknown and SentUnknown resolution, duplicate/reordered/lost responses, detailed-versus-compacted public byte identity, every Local TerminalPending missing-postcondition combination, obligation owner death, and idempotent retry through scoped capabilities.
- Every scenario declares filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models. LDFI supplies high-yield fault hypotheses; residual random chaos remains a blind-spot guard. Bounded completion and model-qualified sampling reports are separate claim classes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests for each fuzz decoder/encoder invariant, corpus reducer, campaign generator, fault-point hook, model-declaration validator, and adapter normalization rule; malformed-input mutation corpus proves each rejection path is reachable.
- Property/metamorphic tests: encode/decode/refusal round trips; adapter semantic equivalence; duplicate/lost/reordered operations preserve one terminal outcome; adding disconnects cannot release an independent owner; recovery after any generated prefix yields an oracle-legal state.
- Simulation: registry-generated campaigns execute every activated G3 durability/authority/protocol boundary with oracles attached. Matrix-completeness CI fails if an activated command or state transition has no fault row.
- Real-process E2E: run three server processes; execute FGP plus all adapters; kill/partition the leader at every selected phase; rotate/revoke capabilities and keys; recover audit/DP/result/restore states; perform joint reconfiguration and rolling mixed-format restart; assert parity, no leaks, legal ownership, and eventual legal terminal/recoverable state.
- Corpus E2E: replay all minimized prior crashpacks and protocol fuzz regressions; execute each emitted `replay_command`; failures must reproduce the same divergence identity.

## Detailed structured diagnostics
Every fuzz case and torture row emits JSONL `{run_id,campaign_id,scenario_id,phase:"G3",seed,corpus_case_digest,adapter,connection_stream_id,frame_kind,protocol_state,command_class,fault_hypothesis_id,crash_point_id,kill_phase,member_role,configuration_epoch,authority_kind,cas_version,positions_before_after,obligation_owner_ids,expected,actual,oracle_verdicts,recovery_verdict,verdict}`. Passing and failing rows use the same schema. Failures add the complete secret-redacted §15.1 artifact, first differing byte/transition, minimized input/schedule, trace digests, and executable replay command. Gate G3 is regenerated from these records; missing log ancestry means the criterion is not green.

## Interactions and phase boundary
Consumes the reusable Local torture/differential engines plus the live G3 protocol/authority oracle task and completed W9-W11 implementations. Feeds Gate G3 and the 1.0 verification epic. W12 role transition, global certification, distributed GC/key/backup/restore, and Meta/Shard matrices are excluded and cannot be marked covered here.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: fuzzing bytes without protocol state; sampled durability boundaries; clean-shutdown-only HA tests; transport-specific semantics; timeout-based ownership release; calling a lab-only pass proof of live behavior. Matrix growth is managed by registry generation, LDFI prioritization, self-shrinking failures, and lab-vs-live/process campaigns—not by omitting rows.

## Provenance
Plan §15.1, §15.3, §15.4 and §19 Gate G3; Appendix D; Appendix F FG-INV-07, 08, 10, 14, 15, 16, 20.

title: scripts/check.sh prints ALL GATES GREEN while never running 4 of 7 registered-live gate scripts, 2 of 6 gate binaries, and ubs
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #1: this is the
finding that presents most convincingly as a pass, because the wrapper's last
line of output is literally `ALL GATES GREEN`.

## What it claims

AGENTS.md ("Mandatory Checks After Substantive Changes" / "The `cargo test`
gate") designates `scripts/check.sh` as THE convenience wrapper for the whole
quality gate, and says: "When CI is added, wire `scripts/check.sh` as the CI
test step rather than duplicating the commands." Its own header comment
enumerates ten numbered steps "in order, stopping on the first failure", and
`scripts/check.sh:98` prints `ALL GATES GREEN`.

## What it actually does

It runs 3 of the 7 script artifacts that `registries/checker_index.toml`
registers with `status = "live"`, and 4 of the 6 checker binaries.

RUNS: `g0_identity_e2e.sh`, `g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh`,
`g0_threat_e2e.sh`; `registry-check all`, `threat-check`, `architecture-check`.

NEVER RUNS, though each is registered `status = "live"`:
  - `scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh`  (symbol `w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e`)
  - `scripts/g0_topology_e2e.sh`                 (symbol `g0_topology_e2e`)
  - `scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh`                   (symbol `g0_claims_e2e`)
  - `scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh`                    (symbol `g0_spine_e2e`)
  - `topology-check` binary                      (symbol `topology_registry_source`)
  - `unsafe-ledger-check` binary                 (symbol `unsafe_ledger_check`)

It also omits `ubs $(git diff --name-only)`, which AGENTS.md lists in the same
mandatory block as the four cargo commands the wrapper does run.

## What is UNIQUELY lost (cargo test does mitigate part of this)

Being precise, because overclaiming here would be the same sin:

1. `w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh` is uniquely uncovered and is the
   sharpest loss. It is the ONLY checker asserting (a) that two
   `cargo test --workspace` runs over an unchanged tree produce byte-identical
   normalized transcripts, and (b) that every engine crate actually reported a
   green lib suite — its own header names the failure it exists to catch: "a
   crate whose suite silently stopped running ... passes every per-crate gate
   we have." No cargo test can reproduce it; it runs the suite twice and
   compares. Doctrine 4 ("deterministic by default") has no other cross-crate
   checker. It is also the script whose `xargs sha256`/SC2033 bug pinned the
   source tree to the constant sha256("") — i.e. the one gate already proven to
   fail silently green.

2. `g0_topology_e2e.sh` uniquely asserts: two `topology-check` runs are
   byte-identical; output is path-independent (`cmp` against a run from a
   foreign cwd, line 100); seeded violation fixtures each fail with their exact
   code; and an explicit anti-vacuity ratchet at lines 98-101
   (`if ! grep -q '"evaluated_live":1'` → "ERROR: the named-edge law is vacuous").
   None of that is reproduced in `tests/workspace_topology.rs`.

3. The two omitted binaries' exit codes and NDJSON contracts are unexercised.
   Their LIBRARY logic is genuinely covered by `cargo test` — both
   `tests/workspace_topology.rs` and
   `tests/unsafe_ledger.rs::the_real_workspace_passes_its_own_boundary_check`
   scan the real tree. So this is the smallest part of the gap.

4. `g0_claims_e2e.sh` / `g0_spine_e2e.sh` are largely duplicated by
   `tests/claims.rs` and `tests/spine.rs`, which carry the twenty-first-ID and
   reachable-stub-clause negatives at repo scope. Low unique loss.

## Which gate catches this today

NONE. `status = "live"` in `checker_index.toml` is proved by `Path::is_file()`
alone (`live_checker_artifact_exists`, `tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs:6231`),
so a registered gate that no wrapper ever invokes is byte-for-byte
indistinguishable from one that runs on every commit. See the companion bead on
that root cause.

## Fix

Add the four scripts and two binaries to `check.sh`, and add the `ubs` step.
Then make the wrapper DERIVE its step list from `checker_index.toml` instead of
a hand-maintained sequence, so a newly registered live checker cannot be
silently omitted again — a hand-maintained list is exactly the thing that went
stale here. Note `w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh` needs a build slot and
runs the workspace suite twice; it may warrant a separate slower lane rather
than the inner-loop wrapper, but "slow" is a scheduling decision to be made
explicitly, not by omission.
close_reason: Closed: registry-derived runner executes all 7/7 live script artifacts, counts every live artifact, and mutation-proves RED plus UNRUN fail-closed behavior.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORROBORATION — measured on main at 7e9d7e1, 2026-07-26 (pane4).

The omission described above is the smaller half of the problem. Measured just
now, `scripts/check.sh` is not merely incomplete — IT IS NOT BEING RUN AT ALL,
and two of the steps it does list are red on main:

  - STEP 1, `cargo fmt --check`: FAILS, 42 `Diff in` hunks.
  - STEP 10, `architecture-check`: FAILS, exit 1, 11 violations
    (bead-provenance: 353 records vs pinned 338, 5 orphans, both binding
    hashes mismatched).

`check.sh` runs `cargo fmt --check` FIRST, under `set -euo pipefail`. So the
wrapper currently dies on its first step and never reaches ANY of the gates it
does list — the identity E2E, the ADR E2E, the threat E2E, `registry-check all`,
`threat-check`, or `architecture-check`. The string `ALL GATES GREEN` at
`scripts/check.sh:98` is presently unreachable on main.

This closes the loop on why the omissions above went unnoticed for so long: a
wrapper nobody runs cannot report that it is missing gates, and it also cannot
report that the gates it has are failing. The pre-existing red state is tracked
separately in fgdb-zwhh ("Two mandatory gates are red on main"); this comment
is not a duplicate of it, it is the explanation of why nobody saw it.

Two consequences for the fix above:

1. Adding the four scripts and two binaries to `check.sh` is necessary but not
   sufficient. Something must actually RUN the wrapper on a cadence. There is no
   `.github/` in this repo and no CI of any kind; `check.sh` is a file that
   documents an intention. Until a runner exists, every gate in it — present or
   added — is in the same state as the orphaned `w1_*_e2e.sh` scripts described
   in fgdb-orphan-w1-e2e-gates-unregistered-unrun-vuq8: syntactically valid,
   registered, and never executed.

2. The wrapper's fail-fast ordering is itself worth revisiting. `set -e` plus
   `cargo fmt --check` first means one stale format hunk masks the state of
   every downstream gate. A gate runner should report ALL gate verdicts and
   then exit non-zero, rather than reporting the first one and hiding the rest —
   otherwise "check.sh failed" carries almost no information, which is its own
   quiet way of turning a gate into decoration.

comments.text:
HEADS-UP FROM pane4 — I touched scripts/check.sh in e87943f, inside your scope.
Read this before you plan, so you neither duplicate nor revert it.

I was on `fgdb-shell-lint-silent-no-op-xi8p` (make the gate refuse to report green
on a file type it never opened). Building its file-coverage table produced a
claim I could not honestly make: the table names **topology-check** as the
inspector for `rust-toolchain.toml`, `registries/workspace_topology.toml`,
`registries/unsafe_boundary_ledger.toml` and `docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md` — and
check.sh did not run topology-check. A coverage claim naming a gate the script
never invokes is the exact failure the new step exists to prevent, so I added the
two binaries my table depends on.

## What I added (2 of the 6 you list)

    topology-check        (workspace topology + unsafe boundary ledger)
    unsafe-ledger-check   (unsafe-boundary scanner + its own self-test)

Both green at HEAD; both were already `status = "live"` in checker_index.toml.
The stale step list in the header is corrected to 14 steps and now matches the
body — it had never been updated for the shell-lint step either.

## What I deliberately did NOT add — still yours, and named in the header

    scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_topology_e2e.sh
    scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh

plus the `ubs` step you list. I stopped at the two my coverage table needed
because the rest is your bead's judgement, not a side effect of mine. They are
called out by name in a `STILL MISSING (…u7mw…)` block in the check.sh header, so
the omission is now documented in the file rather than only in a bead.

## One thing that may change your plan

Adding `ubs` to check.sh does **not** close the hole you filed. Measured today:
`ubs` exits **0** on `.sh`, `.md`, `.toml` and `.jsonl` while printing "UBS did
not run any scanner: nothing was checked (this is NOT a pass)". Running it from
check.sh would add a step that passes unconditionally for every non-Rust
deliverable. The new file-coverage closure step is what actually covers those
file types; if you wire `ubs` in, it should be for the `.rs` set only, and its
"nothing was checked" output should be treated as a failure rather than ignored.

## Also worth knowing

The new step is enumerated from `git ls-files` at run time, so any gate you add
or remove interacts with it: if you remove a gate, move its files to an exemption
in the same commit or the run goes red naming them. That coupling is intentional
and documented in the header.

title: Pass Gate G1 'The Engine Lives': single-node engine exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Integration Gate G1 — "The Engine Lives." The first convergence gate proper: certifies the single-node engine (W1 bedrock, W2 Chronicle durability core, W3 Strata, W4 transactions/Secure View, plus the *declared* W5 subset) live end to end, with every exit clause below demonstrably green. Nothing past G1 may build on unproven engine behavior. This bead is the gate checklist itself; each clause must be independently demonstrable, logged, and reproducible.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§19's gate discipline exists because the crown-jewel risks (§20: graph-SSI soundness — "central correctness risk"; root/checkpoint recovery closure — "catastrophic") must be retired before W6-W8 fan out in parallel. B1 rests on the commit/recovery machinery certified here; B5's evidence discipline requires the strict canonical replay closure and formally validated witness families *now*; B2's claim that representation changes never change semantics is pinned here as "compaction/label changes preserve logical digests." Full strength before breadth is the market position: the Kùzu-shaped hole is filled by proofs, not features.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) fresh-creation three-phase bootstrap and the embedded authorized path; (2) bounded resources; (3) the declared GQL/Cypher feature subset with its synchronous Unicode bundle and conformance matrix — **full language breadth is not claimed until its binder/operator rows exist**; (4) acyclic durable-object construction; (5) final-capsule/command/pre-minted-merge coherence; (6) stable D1 prepared-root ownership and quorum-one ordered-command crash recovery; (7) generated complete projected checkpoint-vector (`CheckpointStateVector`) plus mandatory genesis or paired-operational checkpoint-floor install plus logical-command/transaction-marker suffix recovery with **no historical-floor retention chain** — including inherited absent bytes under a dominating replacement Provisional cut and proof that it authorizes no new reclamation before separate activation; (8) exact Raft snapshot cut binding; (9) serializable witness families **formally and independently validated**; (10) accepted-filesystem conformance plus the lease-owner-death, fence-root-before-enable, torn-root, marker-tail, stale-writer, bootstrap, and recovery matrices all green; (11) constraint state authoritative; (12) compaction/label changes preserve logical digests; (13) strict canonical replay closure works; (14) every clause reachable by the compiled/negotiated G1 capability manifest is live — otherwise that capability is absent from the manifest.

G1 additionally requires **executable reference/oracle coverage** for: normalized valid-time slices; first-escape and finalization allocation under forced rebase; resource/constraint/escrow atomicity; complete security-root binding (`SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema); generation-fenced transaction ownership and prepare handoff; and the Local audit visibility pipeline exercised with multiple unresolved candidates, out-of-order external completions, batch release, restart, and bounded backpressure. The command/state registries (`command_contracts.toml`, `state_payload_fields.toml`) must demonstrate that **every active Local transition owns an exact rooted result and recovery path**. Hard-failure list — any one fails the gate: a pre-rebase capsule, post-filter authorization, an ambient allocator counter, an implicit result release, or an optional audit fence.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding invariant text (Appendix F): FG-INV-05 — every committed SERIALIZABLE history has an acyclic logical dependency graph; for the Local default the checked graph additionally contains real-time precedence edges, or applies the registered dangerous-structure rule proved to reject every DSG-union-real-time cycle, so the default Local contract is **strict serializable**. FG-INV-06 — every witness conservatively represents all logically relevant positive, negative, gap, valid-time slice, early-stop, and path-cut observations, and refinement preserves their concretization and `may_affect` behavior. FG-INV-07 — before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. FG-INV-08 — logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their respective sequences; every retained checkpoint suffix begins with its exact install command. FG-INV-10 — the two-slot root protocol selects the highest structurally credible authenticated closure; one inode-bound publication sequencer plus external incarnation continuity fences every stale writer. FG-INV-11 — any value is durably reserved no later than its first escape; confined values are reserved by the finalization plan before capsule/effect construction; rebase preserves prior bindings and may append only. FG-INV-04 — applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline. Claim class: G1 evidence is invariant-clause conformance with resolvable checker and negative-test entrypoints and `waiver=forbidden`; no slo/benchmark claim qualifies as G1 evidence (those are G4's).

## Interactions
Blocked by gate-genesis and epics epic-w1..epic-w4. Consumes the declared-subset W5 anchors (w5-parsers, w5-binder, w5-gla-algebra, w5-planner, w5-executor, w5-determinism, w5-answer-contracts, w5-replay); verif-oracles supplies the SCC/Elle/obligation-leak oracles used for witness and history validation; w9-audit-pipeline supplies the Local audit visibility pipeline scenario. Produces the foundation gate-g2 assumes.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- All seven named crash matrices (lease-owner-death, fence-root-before-enable, torn-root, marker-tail, stale-writer, bootstrap, recovery) green under the lab with per-row seeds; logs record matrix row id, injected fault, recovered root generation, and pass/fail decision.
- Witness-family validation bundle per family: formal concretization/may-affect proof artifact, independent small-model histories, gap/negative/path mutation tests; negative test that SERIALIZABLE **rejects** an unverified family.
- Suffix-recovery run with dominating replacement Provisional cut plus reclaim ledger proving zero new reclamation before the separate activation command; exact Raft snapshot cut-binding check.
- Logical-digest differential across compaction and label mutation.
- Strict canonical replay-closure e2e reproducing byte-canonical output from the manifest.
- Audit-pipeline scenario: >1 unresolved candidates, out-of-order external completions, batch release, restart mid-batch, backpressure bound observed and logged.
- Registry CI proof mapping every active Local transition to an exact rooted result and recovery path.
- Five executable negative gates for the hard-failure items, each failing closed.
- Clause-to-evidence map: the gate report carries one row per exit clause (1)-(14) and per G1-additional coverage item, naming the demonstrating artifact (matrix, suite, oracle run, or registry CI check). The clauses not already named above map as follows: (1) the fresh-creation three-phase-bootstrap crash-matrix rows plus an embedded authorized-path walk through `fgdb-secure-view`; (2) a bounded-resources run — reservation ceilings enforced and obligation quiescence reached under the lab; (3) the declared GQL/Cypher subset conformance-matrix run with its synchronous Unicode bundle; (4) the acyclic durable-object construction check from the registry CI; (5) final-capsule/command/pre-minted-merge coherence fixtures; (6) stable-D1-prepared-root-ownership fixtures plus the quorum-one ordered-command rows of the crash matrices; (11) the constraint-authority fixtures (synchronous enforcement authoritative before commit; unavailable or corrupt constraint state fails closed for affected writes); (14) a capability-manifest liveness audit proving every reachable clause of the compiled/negotiated G1 manifest is live and every capability with a dead clause is absent from the manifest. The remaining G1-additional oracle-coverage items — normalized valid-time slices; first-escape/finalization allocation under forced rebase; resource/constraint/escrow atomicity; complete `SecurityStateBinding`; generation-fenced ownership and prepare handoff — each map to their executable reference/oracle runs. A clause or coverage item without a mapped artifact row does not count as passed.
- Detailed logging: every matrix/suite/oracle/audit run above logs {run_id, scenario or matrix-row id, seed, injected fault where applicable, per-clause verdict}; failures carry §15.1 structured replay fields; the gate report must be regenerable from these logs alone, and a criterion whose log chain is incomplete does not count as passed.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Graph-SSI unsoundness is retired inside this gate: unverified witness families are rejected rather than shipped; SNAPSHOT remains an explicit weaker contract, never containment for a false serializable claim (§20). Rejected: performance gating here; language-breadth claims beyond existing binder/operator rows; any waiver path (constitutionally forbidden).

## Provenance
§19 Gate G1 (plan lines 1334-1336); Appendix F rows cited; §20 risk rows.

### Verification-layer classification

The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases.
