title: Implement the fgdb CLI with human and versioned robot modes
description:
## What & scope
Implement the shipped `fgdb` binary as the agent-first and human-friendly command surface over the same embedded/session and FGP contracts as the library and server. Own command parsing and discovery, endpoint/embedded selection, capability authentication, explicit transaction/session commands, query and streaming-result control, SnapshotQuery, CDC/subscription, backup/archive/restore/status surfaces, and stable output/error behavior. Robot mode is a frozen versioned NDJSON protocol; human mode may be ergonomic and decorative but can never contaminate robot stdout.

## Why
B6 is a product property only if agents can operate the database without scraping prose or terminal decoration. Durable results, explicit ACK/release/resume, typed failures, replay identities, and service epochs lose their value if the CLI collapses them into an ambiguous exit code or socket lifetime. Humans still need excellent discoverability and safe defaults, so both postures share one command model while keeping distinct renderers.

## Design and public contract
- `fgdb robot schema` emits the complete canonical schema bundle for the requested supported robot protocol version, including event discriminants, field types, redaction rules, exit-code table, feature/capability requirements, ordering rules, and compatibility policy. Output is data-only NDJSON on stdout with no color, progress bars, prompts, banners, or log decoration.
- Every robot invocation begins with a versioned invocation/result envelope and emits line-oriented canonical events. Event order is deterministic whenever semantics permit; nondeterministic operational observations carry explicit sequence/time/source fields rather than relying on arrival prose. Unknown versions and unavailable capabilities fail before database observation.
- Freeze explicit exit classes for success, usage/schema error, authentication/authorization refusal, unavailable feature, semantic query/transaction failure, retryable transport/leadership condition, sent-unknown/reconciliation required, partial client-side consumption with durable owner retained, and internal corruption. Exit status never substitutes for the terminal event.
- Provide commands for connect/open, prepare/execute, explicit begin/statement/commit/abort/reattach/renew, query cancel, result/artifact ACK/release/resume, status, snapshot query, CDC/subscription, archive open, backup/restore inspection, capability inspection, replay and explain/certificate retrieval. Each command projects the owning canonical API type; it does not invent a CLI-only state machine.
- Human mode supplies concise help, shell completion data, TTY-aware tables/streaming, explicit confirmations only for genuinely dangerous administrative operations, and secret-safe input. Noninteractive human use remains pipe-correct. Configuration precedence and endpoint/profile selection are deterministic and printable; secrets, macaroons, locators, protected facts, DP seeds, and raw internal identities are never logged.
- Structured CLI diagnostics use a separate stderr or explicitly selected JSONL diagnostic sink; robot stdout remains contract data. Broken pipes, disconnect, Drop, SIGINT/cancellation, and terminal rendering cannot ACK or release an independent owner.
- Robot schema fixtures and docs are generated or checked from the same registries/closed unions as FGP and the Rust API. Additive robot-minor changes and breaking robot-major changes follow the durable compatibility discipline; human wording is not a machine contract.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes `fgdb-embedded`, `fgdbd`/FGP, transaction ownership, capability, result/artifact/error delivery, SnapshotQuery, CDC, and archive-open contracts. W10 specialized beads own their semantic/protocol state machines; this bead owns CLI command projection, rendering, schema/versioning, process exit, configuration, and end-to-end operator ergonomics. The W10 epic and G3 prove the live CLI; G4 checks generated robot schemas and documentation against frozen registries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests exhaustively cover command grammar, option/config precedence, endpoint/profile selection, robot-version negotiation, every exit-code mapping, every event encoder/decoder, canonical field ordering, redaction, TTY/non-TTY branching, broken-pipe behavior, and invalid/unavailable-capability refusal. Golden fixtures freeze each robot event and `fgdb robot schema` bundle.
- Property/model tests generate legal and illegal command/event sequences, arbitrary chunk boundaries and Unicode, stale/cross-session handles, config conflicts, and terminal/disconnect races; emitted robot streams validate against the selected schema and never imply ACK/release absent the canonical transition.
- Fuzz parsers, NDJSON decoders, schema negotiation, shell completion generation, and hostile terminal/control characters under strict resource budgets.
- E2E script starts an embedded database and a real `fgdbd`, runs human smoke flows and robot flows for open/connect, write/read, explicit multi-statement transaction, reattach, cancel, result resume/ACK/release, artifact output, SnapshotQuery, CDC/subscription, archive/restore status, authorization refusal, lost response, leader change, and broken pipe; it validates stdout against frozen schemas and asserts byte-equivalent public outcomes across embedded and FGP paths.
- Agent-usability E2E executes only schema-discovered commands from a clean process, verifies every response is actionable without prose scraping, and checks deterministic replay of a captured robot transcript.
- Detailed versioned diagnostics record `{run_id,cli_version,robot_schema_version,invocation_id,command_kind,endpoint_profile,posture,capability_public_commitment,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_txn_statement_result_or_artifact_public_ids,event_seq,transition,exit_class,bytes_or_rows,backpressure,cancel_or_disconnect,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with secrets/protected facts redacted. Tests fail on stdout decoration, missing events, unbounded fields, secret leakage, or an incomplete diagnostic chain.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: scraping human output as robot mode; one unversioned JSON blob; implicit release on process exit; CLI-only transaction/result semantics; logging credentials or protected errors; silently retrying SentUnknown. Risk is schema drift across CLI/FGP/Rust; generated fixtures and cross-surface E2E make drift a gate failure.

## Provenance
Plan Product Shape item 3, Agent Ergonomics Requirements, §13 Fabric/W10, §16.6 compatibility, §19 W10/G3/G4, and B6.

title: a10 residue has no open owner: 0 of 35 Spec kinds active, SequenceNeutralSpec has 0 arms, and ihtt/8kzt/suhb are all closed
description:
## The gap: work not done, no bead open on it

fgdb-a10-command-delta-ooy1 is CLOSED (1d90de6, 2026-07-26, pane4), closed "at
the boundary rather than holding" with its residue enumerated on fgdb-ihtt and
its cross-slice defects filed as fgdb-8kzt and fgdb-suhb.

All three of those are ALSO closed. Measured at HEAD 650c37d, the work they
describe is not done:

  logical_kind rows in the catalog        532   (17 active, 515 reserved)
  logical kinds whose name ends in Spec    35   (0 active, 35 reserved)
  SequenceNeutralSpec                            status "reserved", 0 union arms
  GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec                      status "reserved", 0 union arms

So the slice bead and all three residue beads are closed while ZERO command
inputs are active anywhere in the catalog. This bead is the open owner.

## Precision on one thing the a10 close reason says

It reports "SequenceNeutralSpec minted at its reserved code 0x0432 @10 (class
forced by the reservation, disposition flipped reserved->existing)". That is the
RESERVATION disposition, and it is accurate. The LOGICAL KIND row's own
`status` is still `"reserved"`. Both statements are true of different fields;
anyone reading the close reason as "SequenceNeutralSpec is live" will be wrong.

## What is required, in order

1. The `*Spec` command-input schemas as ACTIVE logical kinds with their fields.
   a10 declares field_candidate_count 180 and 17 are landed. Of the 13 inputs
   plan line ~1916 names by name, EIGHT have no row of any kind
   (TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec, TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec,
   AllocationReservationTransitionSpec, FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec,
   FormatTransitionSpec, EscrowRightsTransitionSpec, BulkLoadTransitionSpec,
   DerivedBuildTransitionSpec) and five exist only as candidates or reservations.

2. `SequenceNeutralSpec` and `GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec` off `reserved`, with one
   union_arm per concrete inner tag. a10 declares union_candidate_count 5 and
   arm_candidate_count 17; landed are 1 and 4, and the one landed union is
   `ExpectedStateCondition`, not a command union.

3. The 110 declared ambiguity adjudications (1 landed).

Only then can fgdb-5uw2 author a command_contracts row whose input_schema_id,
body_schema_id, result_schema_id and applied_record_schema_id resolve.

## Construction laws that decide step 2, recorded so they are not re-derived

- A top-level WIRE-BACKED union's `allowed_containing_schemas` must name its
  CONSUMER. The 69/69 self-only precedent strands its own anchor field, and "*"
  is banned outright. a10's one landed union already models this correctly:
  `ExpectedStateCondition` names ["ControlCommand", "KeyDestroyProposal"].
  `SequenceNeutralSpec` is carried by `ControlCommand.typed_payload_ref:
  StrongRef<SequenceNeutralSpec>` per the a10 source, so ControlCommand is its
  consumer.
- A generic whole-schema union is always LOGICAL-BACKED and needs no variant
  rows; only a wire-backed union needs them.
- A [[field]] row may not hang off a wire-only schema.

## Two things the a10 source decides outright, and neither needs a contract

Plan line ~1917, verbatim:
  "`TxnSubmissionSpec` is not an ordered input: transaction submission is the
   pre-order construction pipeline that yields `CommitCommand`."
  "Ordinary DDL is a transaction-carried `SchemaOp`; the synthetic
   catalog/schema/index control types are forbidden."
`TxnSubmissionSpec` is one of a10's 18 top-level candidates, so its
classification row is determined by the source as PreOrderArtifact, with no
command contract needed. That is one row fgdb-5uw2's
command_type_classification.toml can carry today, and it is worth landing
separately from the blocked half -- see the verdict on fgdb-ch8r.

nothing deleted.

title: claims-lint closure walk is filesystem-based, so any untracked .md reds the G0 claims gate for every pane
description:
LIVE AT HEAD 3aa3f6c (measured 2026-07-27 by pane3 while on 5qcg).

  $ registry-check lint --root .
  {"event":"lint_hit","kind":"unclaimed_prose","file":"docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md",...}
  {"event":"lint_completed",...,"hits":1,"outcome":"fail"}   exit=1

and tests/claims.rs::claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean is RED for the same
reason: 33 passed / 1 failed at HEAD, identical before and after unrelated
changes. cargo test is a hard gate per AGENTS.md, so this blocks every pane's
handoff, and it is nobody's change -- it is a file nobody committed.

ROOT CAUSE. docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md is UNTRACKED. lint::run's closure walk
enumerates the filesystem (std::fs::read_dir, recursive from closure_dirs), so
it accuses any *.md present on disk regardless of whether git knows about it.
AGENTS.md names docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md as a real deliverable ("memorialized
in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md"), so this particular file probably wants
committing -- but the STRUCTURAL defect is that the walk's corpus is the working
directory rather than the tracked set. Any pane's scratch note, WIP draft, or
half-finished doc reds G0 for everyone until it is committed or deleted.

This is not a new discovery: pane2 predicted it verbatim in the 5qcg handoff --
"a filesystem walk also sees UNTRACKED scratch *.md that swarm panes leave at
the repo root, which would fail the gate for every pane -- enumerate tracked
files only, or skip untracked ones." It has now materialized.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM 5qcg. The fix is a tracked-set reader, not an
exclusion-table change. pane2 had written one (an in-tree .git/index v2/v3
parser, std-only per FG-CON-01, with the walk retained for synthetic roots
because g0_claims_e2e.sh and every fixture run over a directory with no .git at
all, and with WHICH source ran reported in lint_completed rather than silently
fallen back to). That work lived in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p2/q5_1785100577/ and
IS GONE -- swept by the disk reclamation. It has to be rewritten.

TWO CHEAPER STOPGAPS, both worse: adding the file to lint.scan breaks a clean
checkout (the scan floor requires every entry to exist), and excluding it is
false -- it is a normative document by AGENTS.md's own reference.

DO NOT confuse this with 5qcg's exclusion-liveness laws (dead_exclude,
unreachable_exclude). Those police the denylist. This is about what the walk
considers a candidate in the first place.
notes:
GENERALIZED 2026-07-27 by pane3 while on d9pd. THE DEFECT IS NOT CONFINED TO THE CLAIMS LINT.

Running scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh at HEAD, `registry-check all` reports TWO
failures, and both are untracked files belonging to other panes:

  {"code":"unclaimed_prose","file":"docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md"}
  {"code":"script_undeclared","row_id":"scripts/g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh",
   "registry":"checker_index",
   "msg":"shell deliverable is neither a registered checker artifact nor a
           [[script_disposition]] row"}

So the checker_index script census has the SAME defect as the claims-lint closure
walk: it enumerates shell deliverables from the FILESYSTEM, so a pane's
uncommitted .sh reds G0 for everyone, exactly as an uncommitted .md does. Any fix
that only teaches the claims walk about the tracked set leaves this one open.
Sweep for the pattern rather than patching one reader -- there are likely more.

IMPORTANT NUANCE, and it argues AGAINST simply ignoring untracked files:
scripts/check.sh's own coverage table already NAMES both of these as expected
deliverables --

  docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md)         -> "g0_negative_evidence_e2e (parses every
                                        entry; each doctrine id, bead and repair
                                        commit must resolve)"
  formal/lean/VersionChain.lean)     -> "g0_proof_lanes_e2e (runs lean on it;
                                        lane lean-version-chain is status=checked)"

and `formal/` is untracked too. These are not scratch notes; they are work
mid-landing whose author has not committed yet. A tracked-set reader makes the
gate green while the deliverable is invisible, which is its own fail-open. The
honest shape is probably: enumerate the TRACKED set for the closure obligation,
and report untracked candidates as a separate, named, non-fatal census line so
they cannot hide -- rather than either failing on them or silently dropping them.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED: 3 of the g0 gates are red at HEAD from these two files
(g0_claims_e2e 15/1, g0_spine_e2e 12/1, and tests/claims.rs
claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean). None is caused by any code change; all three
clear the moment the two files are committed.

title: Convention call: identity_class for record-shaped wire types has no precedent to derive from
description:
## What & scope
A `[[field]]` row must declare `identity_class`, and for three wire types that a03 needs there is no precedent anywhere in the catalog to derive it from. This blocks ten otherwise-mechanical field rows and, more importantly, every future field row whose `exact_wire_type` is a record-shaped wire type rather than a primitive or a reference wrapper. It is a convention call for the repo owner, not a measurement an agent can make. No remedy is authorized by this bead.

## The three types, and the exact gap
These are the `exact_wire_type` values on the ten a03 field candidates that survive every mechanical filter (discharged ambiguity, exactly one exact_type, exactly one cardinality, owner already a registered kind, not a reference wrapper so no construction-DAG edge, not an inline union or array):

    AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>      on AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>      on AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalAttemptRegistration
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalBeginReservationSpec
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on TxnOutcomeRecord
    AppliedControlRef               on LocalStatementIndex.abort_applied_ref  (x2, distinct arm paths)
    AppliedControlRef               on LocalStatementIndex.publication_applied_ref
    LocalStatementPublishedOutput   on LocalStatementIndex.output

MEASURED: **no landed `[[field]]` row in the entire catalog uses any of these three as its `exact_wire_type`.** All three ARE registered wire types, so the row would be structurally legal — what is missing is the convention that says which identity class a record-shaped wire type induces on the field that carries it.

## Why it cannot be derived from the data
`identity_class` takes five values across the 246 landed field rows:

    scalar            84
    logical           68
    inline            46
    physical          19
    bootstrap_local   29

The distribution does not imply a rule for this case. `scalar` is used by primitives (u64 etc.). `logical`/`physical`/`bootstrap_local` name durable identity classes, which fits a field that points at an object — but these three fields do not point at anything, since none is a reference wrapper. `inline` is the plausible candidate for an embedded record, and `AuthorityBoundHeader` is exactly such a record (kind = "record", allowed_containing_schemas = ["*"]) — but "plausible" is not the standard for a durable format contract, and no landed row demonstrates it.

## Why I stopped rather than guessing
`identity_class` is durable-contract data, not annotation. It feeds the generated identity/reachability machinery that `durable_fields.toml` is the sole input to (plan:292). A wrong value here is not a lint failure that surfaces later — it is a wrong byte-level contract that the loader accepts, because every one of the five values is individually legal for a field row. That is the same shape as the errors this gate exists to prevent: a row that loads green and is wrong. Ten rows is not worth the risk of setting the precedent incorrectly, and whatever is chosen here becomes the precedent every later slice copies.

## What a ruling should say
1. Which `identity_class` a field takes when its `exact_wire_type` is a `kind = "record"` wire type (the `AuthorityBoundHeader` case).
2. Whether a generic-signed wire type (`AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>` vs `<Local>`) changes the answer.
3. Whether `AppliedControlRef` — named `...Ref` but registered as a record rather than a `reference_wrapper` — follows the record rule or the reference rule. Its name suggests one and its registration the other, and that disagreement is itself worth ruling on.
4. Whether `LocalStatementPublishedOutput`, which is a landed ordinary-union wire parent rather than a plain record, takes a third answer.

## Success Criteria
- A stated rule mapping wire-type kind to field `identity_class`, with at least one worked example per branch.
- The ten a03 rows land against that rule; the a03 field layer then proceeds to its next filter (23 owner mints, already measured).
- The rule is written where the next slice will find it, not only in a commit body.

## Provenance
Measured read-only by cc_2/pane3-a03 against a git-archive snapshot of HEAD ad4a7fc, source-manifest sha control passing. Full a03 field classification (732 candidates, 296 nominally landable, 432 blocked by instance III) is on the fgdb-a03-local-state-txn-rxjg trail. Same shape as fgdb-normative-predecessor-ref-erratum-j00a: an agent measured the gap exactly and the decision belongs to the owner.
close_reason: Owner ruling implemented and permanently controlled; all ten A03 occurrences are covered by six flat inline fields plus four exact arm-payload contracts.

=== 2. CORRECTION: THE TITLE SAYS "record-shaped" AND 7 OF THE 8 TYPES ARE UNIONS ===
The blocking exact_types are eight distinct names over 23 fields, and I under-scoped
them when filing. Their registered kinds:
    AuthorityBoundHeader            wire_type kind="record"   12 fields (<Local> 8, <Role> 4)
    AppliedControlRef               wire_type kind="union"     5

    ResultManifestRef               wire_type kind="union"     1
So the dominant question is NOT the record case at all: it is what identity_class a
field takes when its exact_wire_type is a UNION wire type. The record case
(AuthorityBoundHeader) is the larger by field count but the minority by type count,
and the two may well take different answers. Note also that five of the seven union
names end in "Ref" or "Owner" while being registered as unions rather than
reference_wrappers — the naming does not predict the registration, which is exactly
why deriving the class from the name would be wrong.

=== 3. ONE QUESTION SETTLED BY THE DATA, SO IT IS NOT PART OF THE RULING ===
construction_order on a field row is NOT a judgment: across all 198 landed field
rows whose owner is a registered logical kind, the field's construction_order equals
the owner's, 198 of 198, zero exceptions. It is derived. Good — that removes one
free parameter from the ruling.

=== 4. A THIRD QUESTION, AND IT MAY MAKE PART OF efa2495 WRONG ===
MEASURED: of the landed field rows, 198 are owned by a registered LOGICAL kind and
ZERO are owned by a registered WIRE type. There is no precedent anywhere in the
catalog for a field row hanging off a wire-type owner.
That matters because in efa2495 I minted ten a03 owners as wire records precisely
because they have zero StrongRef referents — and those ten OWN field candidates.
If "a schema that owns durable field rows is a logical kind" is the rule, then my
class assignment for those ten is wrong and they should be logical, which also
explains the 70 fields above that are stuck behind "owner not a registered LOGICAL
kind" rather than "owner not registered".
I am NOT asserting that rule. The counter-evidence is real: 48 landed field rows
have owners that are not registered at all, so a field owner need not be registered,
and "0 wire-owned" may simply reflect that nobody has needed one yet rather than a
prohibition. Distinguishing "no precedent" from "forbidden" is exactly the call I
cannot make from the data, and it is the same shape as the identity_class question,
so it belongs on this bead rather than in a separate one.

=== 5. WHAT A RULING NOW NEEDS TO COVER ===
  (a) identity_class when exact_wire_type is a UNION wire type (7 names, 11 fields).
  (b) identity_class when it is a RECORD wire type (AuthorityBoundHeader, 12 fields),
      and whether the generic signature <Local> vs <Role> changes the answer.
  (c) Whether a [[field]] row may have a WIRE-type owner at all. If not, the ten wire
      mints in efa2495 need reclassifying to logical — a correction I will make in one
      increment as soon as it is ruled, since the reservation-first rule already tells
      me the codes (none of the ten has a reservation, so fresh above 0x051d).
  (d) construction_order needs no ruling; it is derived from the owner (198/198).

=== 6. WHAT IS STILL MECHANICAL AND NEEDS NO RULING ===
Nothing in the a03 field layer. The next unblocked a03 work is the 152
reference-shaped fields, which need the fgdb-owlp both-direction order sweep first
and are deliberately their own increment. Everything else in a03 waits on this bead,
on fgdb-owlp, or on instance III.

comments.text:
TWO OF THE FOUR QUESTIONS ARE ALREADY ANSWERED BY THE CHECKER, AND A THIRD IS NOW DERIVABLE FROM
PRECEDENT. From pane3. I stopped reasoning from "no landed row does this" and asked the laws directly.

=== METHOD ===
Fixture, not inference: load the live registries with `identity::load_identity` (baseline 0 violations
at HEAD), push ONE synthetic row, re-run `identity::validate_identity`, read what fires. Every
mutation also raises `registry_assignment_drift` — that is the append-only pin reacting to any
insertion, it fires in all four arms including the positive controls, and it is the fixture's own
artifact, not a finding. All measured against a git-archive snapshot; nothing in the repo was edited.

=== QUESTION (c) — MAY A [[field]] ROW HAVE A WIRE-TYPE OWNER?  NO. IT IS FORBIDDEN BY LAW. ===
  A  owner is a WIRE type only          -> field_unresolved_schema: containing_schema "StrongRef"
                                           resolves in no identity class
  B  owner is a LOGICAL kind            -> no field_unresolved_schema        (positive control)
  C  owner is a BOOTSTRAP frame         -> no field_unresolved_schema        (positive control)
  D  owner registered nowhere           -> field_unresolved_schema           (negative control)
A and D are the SAME violation. identity.rs resolves containing_schema against
logical | bootstrap | physical | prebootstrap — wire is not in that list, so a wire owner is not
"unprecedented", it is indistinguishable from unregistered. This was never a convention question and
no ruling can make such a row land.
  CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER EVIDENCE, which is what made this look open: I reported "48 landed
  field rows have owners that are not registered at all", and used it as counter-evidence that a
  field owner need not be registered. Wrong — those 48 owners are BOOTSTRAP frames. Recounted at
  HEAD: of 251 landed field rows, 203 have logical owners, 48 have bootstrap owners, ZERO have wire
  owners and ZERO are unregistered. There is no counter-evidence; the law and the corpus agree 251/251.
  So the correct statement of the rule is "resolves in a non-wire identity class", not "is a LOGICAL
  kind" — and that widening matters, because bootstrap owners are legal and I would have missed them.
WHAT THE RULING ACTUALLY DECIDES, then, is not whether such rows are legal but which disposition each
owner takes. Two options, and the checker forbids keeping both:
  (i)  the owner is misclassified -> move it out of the wire class, and its fields become landable;
  (ii) the owner is correctly wire -> its "fields" are inline structure described by the wire type's
       encoding_context and are NOT [[field]] rows at all, permanently.
Either answer is cheap to apply: all of these owners were minted this session (controlled against
base da16fbb) so nothing is released.

=== QUESTION (d) — construction_order — ALSO A LAW, NOT A STATISTIC ===
Fixture arm B fires `bad_field: construction_order 1 != containing kind's 20`. My earlier 198-of-198
observation was the law being obeyed, not a convention emerging. Nothing to rule.

=== QUESTIONS (a) AND (b) — identity_class — GENUINELY YOURS, AND HERE IS WHY ===
NO law constrains it for a non-reference field. Taking a landed record-typed row and flipping its
identity_class through all five enum values produces only the assignment-pin drift in every case:
  scalar / inline / logical / physical / bootstrap_local  -> no bad_field, no new code
So the checker will accept any of them, and only the corpus can decide. (The one exception is already
a law: strong/conditional references MUST be identity_class = "logical".)

THE CORPUS, tabulated over all 251 landed rows by the exact_wire_type's own registered `kind`:
    wire kind "union"        -> inline  7 of 7   (4 type names, 6 distinct owners)
    ordinary_union           -> inline 13 of 13  (13 distinct union names)
    wire kind "record"       -> inline 23, logical 6
    wire "reference_wrapper" -> logical 52 of 52   (already a law)
    reference_union          -> logical  5 of 5
    builtin                  -> scalar 84, physical 19, bootstrap_local 28, logical 9, inline 4

(a) UNION-TYPED FIELDS ARE DERIVABLE: inline, 20 of 20 with zero counterexamples across 17 distinct
type names and many owners — that clears pane2's ">= 5 landed examples, zero counterexamples"
threshold outright. It settles the seven a03 union names (AppliedControlRef, LocalAuditTicketOwner,
LocalResultDeliveryOwner, LocalStatementPublishedOutput, ResultActivationAppliedRef,
ResultDeliveryServiceAuthority, ResultManifestRef — all registered wire kind "union", status
reserved), i.e. 11 of the 23 no-precedent rows. I am not landing them; I am reporting that they no
longer need YOU.

(b) RECORD-TYPED FIELDS (AuthorityBoundHeader, 12 fields) STILL NEED THE RULING. 23 inline against 6
logical fails the zero-counterexample bar. But the split is not noise: per named type each is
unanimous — ConsensusDomain 8/8, RemoteObjectIdentity 12/12, HlcTimestamp, KeyDestructionOperationPlan
and SecurityStateBinding 1/1 each all inline; every one of the 6 logical rows is WeakDigest, 6/6, and
WeakDigest is a 256-bit digest that NAMES ANOTHER OBJECT while AuthorityBoundHeader is an inline
header that names nothing. Read semantically the answer is inline; read by the stated threshold it is
undecided. That is the whole of what is left of (a)+(b), and it is one call.

=== WHAT THIS DOES TO THE 293 ===
The wire-owner component (a03 67, a05 229 on the full-population basis, a06 131) is not waiting on a
convention — it is waiting on a per-owner disposition under a law that already exists. The
identity_class component shrinks to AuthorityBoundHeader's 12 fields. Cross-checked on a05 in the same

No owner reclassified, no row rewritten, no registry touched. The 122-field disclosure from my
previous comment stands unchanged: those owners were classified from a single criterion (zero
StrongRef referents), and the law above says nothing about which disposition they take — only that

comments.text:
ASKED THE CHECKER AS THE RULING INSTRUCTED. ANSWER: IT IS A GENUINE CONVENTION CALL — `inline` is a
ruling, not a forced law. But the probe returned two hard laws nobody had written down, and one of
them narrows the question. From pane3.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===
Synthesized a [[field]] row per the recipe and ran validate_identity across all five durable
classes, with a positive and a negative control, filtering the append-only registry_assignment_drift
that fires in every arm:

  SUBJECT   exact_wire_type = "AuthorityBoundHeader" on LocalAttemptRegistration
       logical ACCEPTED · physical ACCEPTED · inline ACCEPTED
       wire REJECTED [bad_field: "bad identity_class"] · prebootstrap REJECTED [same]
  SUBJECT   exact_wire_type = "AppliedControlRef" on LocalStatementIndex   — identical result
  POSITIVE  exact_wire_type = "u64" (a builtin scalar)                     — identical result
  NEGATIVE  exact_wire_type = "PaneThreeNotARealType"
       all five rejected with field_unresolved_wire_type — the probe discriminates

3 of 5 classes accepted for the subject. So `inline` is your ruling and the ten rows follow it; the
checker does not force it.

=== BUT THE SUBJECT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE POSITIVE CONTROL, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING ===
A record-shaped wire type and a plain `u64` accept EXACTLY the same three classes. The checker has
no opinion whatsoever about the relationship between exact_wire_type's shape and identity_class.
That means the bead's framing — "record-shaped wire types have no precedent to derive from" —
understates it: NOTHING derives identity_class for ANY non-reference field, record-shaped or
primitive. The ten rows are not a special case awaiting a convention; they are ordinary instances of
a column the checker never constrains. Whatever you rule should be stated as covering every
non-reference field, not just the record-shaped ones, or the same question returns on the next
`u64`.

=== TWO LAWS THE PROBE SURFACED, NEITHER PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN DOWN ===
1. A FIELD's identity_class admits only THREE values: logical | physical | inline. `wire` and
   `prebootstrap` are rejected outright with bad_field "bad identity_class", independent of every
   other column. The catalog's own vocabulary calls these "the five durable classes" and the
   top_level_candidate row does accept all five — but a field row does not. Anyone reasoning from
   "the five classes" about a field row is reasoning from a set that is too big by two.
2. construction_order on a field must EQUAL the containing kind's, and `bad_field` reports it as
   "construction_order 20 != containing kind's 15". This is why my first probe run returned "0 of 5
   accepted" for the subject AND the positive control — the row was malformed on a different axis
   entirely and the class question was never reached. Without the positive control I would have
   reported "no class is legal for a record-shaped type", which is false and would have looked like
   a discovered law.

=== METHOD NOTE ===
The positive control is what made this trustworthy, and it earned its keep on the first run: it
failed identically to the subject, which is the signature of a broken probe rather than a real
result. A subject-only probe would have produced a confident wrong answer.

=== APPLICATION ===
Under the ruling, the record-shaped field rows become landable: 3 in a04, 3 in a05, 16 in a19 by my
census. I have NOT landed them, because appendix-regenerate is currently blocked tree-wide by the
bead-provenance orphans (see fgdb-uug4 and the a19 bead) — no catalog increment by any pane can be
proven byte-exact until that clears.

The comment above says the a10:1912 body is UNATTRIBUTED, so binding it would "AUTHOR an
attribution the source does not make", forcing (A). The source makes that attribution TWICE.

source-manifest re-pin is needed to discharge H1.

=== AND IT IS A POPULATION OF FOUR, NOT ONE ===
I swept the whole census region for the shape "bold heading, then an anonymous `<phrase> is {`".
26 bold-headed paragraphs, 13 with multi-name headings, exactly 4 with an anonymous first body:

  plan 1912  heading[0]=CommitCommand         "A transaction order unit is {"
  plan 1924  heading[0]=LogicalDeltaTemplate  "A template is {"
  plan 1964  heading[0]=RecoveryCheckpoint    "A checkpoint is {"
  plan 2000  heading[0]=BranchManifest        "A branch manifest is {"

In all four the anonymous body is body 0 and heading[0] is a type name. Baseline census on all
four: CommitCommand = ProseDefinitionNoBody @1530 with 0 fields; the other three have NO SCHEMA
CANDIDATE ANYWHERE and 0 fields.

TWO OF THESE ARE 8kzt'S OWN "OWES NOTHING" SUBJECTS. 8kzt closed ruling CommitCommand "one of 202
definition-without-structural-body, the census owes nothing" and LogicalDeltaTemplate "never bound
at all, owes nothing". Both have spelled bodies in the appendix. THE OTHER TWO WERE NEVER ON

ever examined a10 subjects. RecoveryCheckpoint is the a12 one and BranchManifest is the a13 one.
The title was right and the partition was two slices short.

=== WHAT THE REPAIR COSTS, MEASURED BOTH DIRECTIONS ===
ONE READER, EXTENDED -- not a new one. `bold_schema_links` already binds `**Name**: {...}`; it
misses this shape only because the heading ends in `.` inside the bold and carries several names.
I factored its name-finding into one `bold_owner_name_range` with two spellings and no second
stack. Patch + probe preserved at ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/p3-ihtt/.

  BASELINE (HEAD)  schemas 1231  fields 11712  unions 575  arms 1697  ambiguities 8439
  WITH THE RULE    schemas 1234  fields 11771  unions 578  arms 1703  ambiguities 8468
                          (+3)         (+59)         (+3)       (+6)              (+29)

  THE OTHER 18 SLICES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL.

WRONG-NAME CONTROL, AND IT FIRES. Same patch with HEADING_NAME_INDEX = 1 (bind the heading's
SECOND name): fields 11752 -- different from baseline 11712 AND from the rule's 11771 -- a10=174,
a12=213, a13=228, and NONE of the four subjects recover. So the +59 is sensitive to choosing the

A GUARD OF MINE THAT IS VACUOUS, REPORTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED AS EARNED. I wrote a guard rejecting

title: Freeze the Appendix A annotation, semantic-binding, and evidence layer
description:
CATALOG-SCALE, binds all 21 slices. Today the catalog has ZERO annotation, semantic_binding, expansion_binding and evidence rows, with all four EXPECTED_*_COUNT consts pinned at 0. No slice can flip definition_status=complete until this exists, so it gates the whole Appendix A epic, not one slice.

THE LAW IS PER-TARGET, not per-slice. Every complete target requires exactly one annotation, exactly one semantic binding, at least one static evidence row covering G0, at least one runtime evidence row (planned or live), and a source-reconciled top|/field|/union|/arm| contract. That is ~4 rows per target.

CURRENT COST at 536 targets: a01 219, a16 170, g0 35, a15 29, a04 16, a10 16, a06 11, a20 10, a19 8, a03 6, a02 5, a11 4, a17 4, a07 1 -> roughly 2140 rows, growing with every target any lane lands.

PROPOSED SHAPE (see the full proposal on the a01 and a04 bead trails):
(a) Freeze the four row schemas and their pin mechanics ONCE, before any slice authors a row - fixing this after 2000 rows exist is a mass migration.
(b) GENERATE annotations from the census the way projections are generated, with a sanctioned writer and a byte-diff law. Annotations are source-checked (source_annotation_contract_mismatch requires byte-matching the census exact_type and cardinality; top-level annotations must discharge the generic signature through concrete expansions), so they are derivable and must not be hand-authored 2140 times.
(c) Semantic bindings and evidence rows are NOT derivable - they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs and gate. Author per slice, by that slice's owner.
(d) Sequence AFTER each slice's residual field/union/arm coverage, never before: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so targets minted later need their own four rows anyway.
(e) Nobody flips definition_status=complete until (a)-(d) are done for that slice; the flip arms all these laws at once plus source_complete_census_uncovered and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved.
close_reason: Schema and pin mechanics frozen with no completion data rows in a5b3048; exact clean-snapshot composite is green, and the bead records the proven generation boundary and all attributable gate evidence.

title: Bead-provenance violation codes still say count/expected after the floor rename
description:
## What

fgdb-hcvx (landed a4d60fc) renamed every bead-provenance PIN so its name states
a floor. Three names it deliberately did not touch still say "count"/"expected":

  tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs
    violation code  "bead_count_pin"              -> the declared-vs-code-pin
                                                     equality; both sides are
                                                     now *_floor
    violation code  "bead_family_expected_total"  -> fires when the
                                                     min_match_count values do
                                                     not sum to family_rule_floor
    local           expected_family_total         -> that sum

## Why it was deferred, not an oversight

A violation code is not prose. It is the `code` field of the NDJSON
contradiction stream, and tests/architecture_decisions.rs asserts on both
strings literally (`codes.contains("bead_count_pin")` twice,
`!codes.contains("bead_family_expected_total")` once). Renaming one is a change
to a machine-read contract and belongs in its own commit with its own sweep, not
bundled into a rename whose whole claim was "no behaviour moved".

## What must be measured first, before renaming anything

The fgdb-hcvx sweep found no consumer of these two codes outside
architecture.rs and its test file -- but that sweep was `grep` over the repo,
which is exactly the instrument that misses a code assembled at runtime or read
from a registry row. Before renaming, check registries/claims_lint.toml,
registries/invariants.toml and the other g0 e2e scripts for the literal, and
re-run the grep including .beads/ (10 bead records mention `bead_count`).

## Cost

Small: 2 codes x (1 emit site + 1-2 test assertions), plus a 3-line local
rename. Needs the catalog token; the compiler covers the local, nothing covers
the string literals, so the test assertions are the only guard and they must be
edited in the same commit.

## Judgement call this bead is asking for

It may be correct to leave them. `bead_count_pin` describes a pin over counts
and both operands really are equal-compared; the misleading word is "expected"
in `bead_family_expected_total`, which is the one fgdb-hcvx called "the worst of
them" in the TOML. A partial rename -- just `bead_family_expected_total` ->
`bead_family_floor_total` -- may be the whole fix.

Found while landing fgdb-hcvx (a4d60fc).

title: Field rows carry no source path: the owner law already fails closed (0 of 923), but 117 landed rows sit inside union arms with no mechanism that can tell
notes:
Filed by pane4 2026-07-27 ~04:3x at HEAD ccae08d, at the orchestrator's request
after pane3 surfaced the symptom on a05. Re-derived before filing, and the
reported defect does not reproduce — but the investigation that falsified it
found the real one.

=== THE REPORTED DEFECT IS FALSIFIED AT HEAD ===

Reported: "validate_identity ACCEPTS a [[field]] row on a UNION owner, so an arm
payload member lands silently as a field."

It does not. `field_unresolved_schema` (identity.rs:1762-1800) resolves a field's
`containing_schema`, by generic-free family, against an ALLOWLIST:

    resolves = logical || bootstrap || physical || prebootstrap

An allowlist fails CLOSED by construction: an unrecognised owner kind is a
violation, not a skip. That is exactly the property the law was to be built for,
and it is already there — including a dedicated message for the wire sub-case,
which the code comments say was added because "resolves in no identity class"
read as a missing mint and invited authors to re-mint the owner as a logical
kind.

CENSUS, denominator = EVERY landed [[field]] identity row, 923 of them:

    logical       849
    bootstrap      48
    physical       26
    ---------------------
    total         923      union owners: 0   wire owners: 0   unresolved: 0

Zero counterexamples, and the partition is total.

WITNESS — planted rows, both directions, positive control PASSES:

    baseline                                          0 violations
    ordinary-union owner  ActivatedRetentionCutSet...  REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    reference-union owner MandatoryInventoryRef        REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    wire-type owner       StrongRef                    REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
                                                       (with the wire-specific message)
    nonsense owner        ZzNoSuchOwnerZz              REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    logical owner         CommitMarker                 ACCEPTED   <- control passes

Without that last line the four rejections would only prove the probe rejects
everything. Building the requested law again would duplicate a live mechanism.

=== THE REAL GAP, WHICH IS WHAT pane3 ACTUALLY HIT ===

pane3's report was "the PATH rejected what the CHECKER could not — 49 dropped to
42 only because a human noticed", and that is precise. The owner is not the
problem; the PATH is, and a durable_fields row does not have one.

A [[field]] identity row carries `containing_schema` + `stable_name` and nothing
else about where the member sits in the source. The source path survives only in
the sibling `[[target]].source_key`
(`field|Owner|Owner.state.Arm.member|member`), and NO law reads it for depth.

Joining every landed field row to its target source_key:

    depth 1   762    a direct member,  Owner.member
    depth 2    62 )  an INTERIOR: Owner.state.Arm.member and deeper
    depth 3    54 )
    depth 5     1 )
    ------------------
    joinable  879    (44 of the 923 rows have no field target to join, itself
                      worth a look and NOT covered by this bead)

**117 landed rows are at depth >= 2.** Examples, all live today:

    AttemptFamilyState.latest_state.Active.registration_ref
    AuditTerminalFreezeRecord.state.Armed.scaffolding_applied_ref
    CommitMarker.effect_source.Local.capsule_ref
    DistributedSerializationCertificate.lifecycle_basis.ReadWrite.routing_certificate_ref
    GlobalBeginIdempotencyIndex.Reserved.reservation_ref

Whether each of those 117 is legitimate is exactly the question NOTHING in the
checker can answer, and that is the defect: the catalog relies on a rule with no
mechanism that can fail. The only governing artifact is
`STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES` (identity.rs:203), a hard-coded table of
exactly TWO named shapes with a completeness guard. Two, against 117.

=== WHAT A FIX HAS TO DECIDE FIRST, AND WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINER ===

The 117 are not obviously wrong. A union arm whose payload is a single StrongRef
is precisely the shape `STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES` licenses, and most of
the 117 look like exactly that. So the law cannot be "depth >= 2 is a violation";
it has to be "depth >= 2 is a violation UNLESS the arm it sits in is licensed",
and licensing is currently a two-row hand-written table.

Sequence I would follow, and did not because the ruling is the owner's:
  1. Partition the 117 by the arm they sit in and by whether that arm is a
     StrongRef-only payload. That is a census, no ruling needed, and it turns
     "117 unknown" into "N licensed by the existing rule, M needing one".
  2. Only then choose the mechanism. If M is small the table grows and gains a
     completeness guard over the whole 117. If M is large the table is the wrong
     instrument and the law belongs on the path itself.
  3. Either way the enforcement point has to be a law that READS
     `[[target]].source_key`, because that is the only place the path exists.
     identity.rs cannot see it at all — it never receives the targets.

That last point is the structural finding: `validate_identity` takes
`&IdentityRegistries` and the catalog's targets are not in it, so this law CANNOT
live where the sibling field laws live. It has to be an appendix_a.rs law, or
identity.rs has to be given the path. Grepped both artifacts first, as instructed:
appendix_a.rs has `field_owner_and_name` (:12014) keyed by owner+name and drops
the path, so neither artifact currently retains what the law needs.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===

pane3's second finding — field_tag has no derivable law (flat census rank agrees
774/837, depth-1 rank 668/720; only range and per-owner uniqueness enforced) —
stays on fgdb-uug4 and is deliberately not duplicated here.

Nothing deleted. Census and witness are standalone-rustc probes under
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law; no cargo, no catalog token was needed or
taken for any of the above.

=== THE 117, CENSUSED BY ARM. THE POPULATION IS HETEROGENEOUS — NO LAW YET ===

Denominator 117. Partition is TOTAL and splits into two shapes that share no
mechanism, so a single law over 117 would be exactly the thing we keep catching:

  106  ARM INTERIOR, backed by a landed [[union_arm]] row at that exact path,
       and EVERY ONE has payload_kind = "inline-record". SOURCE-FORCED: the
       source spells an arm whose payload is an inline record, the arm row is
       landed, and these field rows ARE that record's members. Nothing invented.
   11  NOT AN ARM AT ALL. Every one has `.record.` as the segment before the
       member — the collection-element marker of a repeated field:
         KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots.record.source_root_digest
         LocalConstraintReservationRecord.owner.record.registration_ref            (x3)
         NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof.raft_nonorder_evidence.record.configuration_ref
         PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role>.sorted_*_imports.record.*_ref  (x4)
         RemoteGrantRetirementPlan.sorted_entries.record.old_grant_evidence_ref
         KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots.record.source_root_ciphertext_digest
       11 of 11, no exceptions. Depth >= 2 here means "element of a repeated
       field", which is a different question from "member of a union arm".
  ---
  117

  depth 2  62   depth 3  54   depth 5  1
  86 distinct (owner, union_path, arm) keys: 62 carry 1 member, 17 carry 2,
  7 carry 3  (62 + 34 + 21 = 117).
  102 of 117 are strong/conditional StrongRef; the other 15 spread over
  AppliedControlRef 6, AppliedAbortRef 2, digest256 2, and one each of
  Operational, RemoteObjectIdentity, RestoreAbandonmentTombstoneRef<Role>,
  WeakDigest, u64.

THE TWO-ENTRY TABLE NAMES 0 OF THE 117, AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE TABLE.
STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES governs the COMPLEMENT: arms whose payload is
a single StrongRef and NO inline record, i.e. arms that correctly have no field
rows at all. It licenses an ABSENCE. Reading it as an under-populated licensing
table for these 117 is the wrong model and would grow it in the wrong direction.

A CONTROL THAT CAUGHT MY OWN PROBE. The first run of this census reported
117 of 117 "no landed union arm at that path" — a clean, alarming, and FALSE
result. `OrdinaryUnion.union_path` is the FULL dotted path INCLUDING the owner
("AttemptFamilyState.latest_state"); my key used the tail only, so nothing ever
matched. Caught by dumping four real landed union rows before believing a
near-total negative. The corrected join is 106/11.

=== THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP ===

THIS IS A DATA-FLOW CHANGE BEFORE IT IS A LAW.

  identity.rs   validate_identity(&IdentityRegistries). The registries DO carry
                paths — OrdinaryUnion.union_path and OrdinaryUnionArm.union_path
                are full dotted paths, and OrdinaryUnionArm.source_arm_name is
                the arm. The UNION side has everything. The FIELD side has none
                of it: FieldRow is containing_schema + stable_name and no path.
  appendix_a.rs has the path, in [[target]].source_key, and drops it —
                field_owner_and_name (:12014) keys by owner+name only.

So neither artifact retains what the law needs, but they fail differently, and
that decides the fix. It does NOT need a third place. The asymmetry is the
defect: [[union_arm]] rows carry union_path + source_arm_name and [[field]] rows
do not, though both are members of the same source tree. Give the [[field]]
projection row the same two columns the arm row already has, and the law becomes
a local check inside validate_identity with no cross-artifact plumbing at all:

    a field row whose union_path/arm_name are set must match a landed
    [[union_arm]] at that path whose payload_kind is inline-record;
    a field row with them unset must be a direct member.

That is a durable-format change to durable_fields.toml — additive-minor under
§16.6, which is the one exception to the no-compat-shim rule — and it is the
reason this is not a one-turn fix. 117 rows would need the two columns
backfilled from their [[target]].source_key, which is mechanical and verifiable
(the join above is exactly it, and it is already written).

WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY: author the law. The population is two shapes,
not one; the 11 repeated-record rows need their own ruling (is `.record.` depth
even in scope?), and a law written over the mixed 117 would be wrong for 11 of
them by construction.

Census: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law/arms.rs, standalone rustc, no cargo,
no catalog token taken.

=== THE 11 `.record.` ROWS, ASKED OF THE CHECKER. MOSTLY FORCED; ONE RULING LEFT ===

STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHERE ANY FIX GOES:
validate_identity takes &IdentityRegistries and the catalog's targets are not in
it, while appendix_a.rs keys field_owner_and_name at :12014 by owner+name and
DROPS the path — so neither artifact retains what a path law would need, which
makes this a data-flow change before it is a law. The right home is NOT a third
place: [[union_arm]] rows already carry union_path + source_arm_name, so giving
the [[field]] projection row those same two columns puts the law inside
validate_identity with no cross-artifact plumbing at all.

Shape of the 11, uniform: the REPEATED FIELD ITSELF has no landed row anywhere —
inherited_roots, owner, raft_nonorder_evidence, sorted_issuer_fence_imports,
sorted_expired_cohort_imports, sorted_revoked_cohort_imports, sorted_entries are
each unlanded — and only their element members are landed, every one at
cardinality = "one" on the top-level owner.

READINGS, run through validate_identity on the representative row
RemoteGrantRetirementPlan.sorted_entries.record.old_grant_evidence_ref:

  A  flatten the element member onto the owner   (what is landed)   0 violations
  B1 mint the element type as a WIRE type        REJECTED
       field_unresolved_schema: "resolves as a WIRE type, which can never own a
       field row" — this is reference_semantics being forced by the source: the
       member is StrongRef, and a StrongRef member cannot hang off a wire host.
  B2 mint the element type as a LOGICAL kind     0 attributable violations
  CONTROL unminted element host                  REJECTED (control fires)

So the checker forbids B1 and admits both A and B2. Applying that across the 11:

   9 rows are StrongRef with a real target (LocalAttemptRegistration,
     LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec, ConfigurationState,
     PriorIncarnationLeaseIssuerFenceReceipt, PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow,
     PreBootstrapPortableTimeExpiryAttestation,
     PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortRevocationReceipt, RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence,
     plus LocalConstraintReservationRecord.owner.record.admission_generation
     which is u64/inline in the same three-member element).
     For these B1 is FORBIDDEN. Two readings remain.
   2 rows are the KeyEnvelopeNode digests — source_root_digest and
     source_root_ciphertext_digest, digest256 with digest_class = "target",
     reference_semantics = none. These are ALREADY the correct resolution of a
     plan-named digest: digest256 plus digest_class on the carrying field, not a
     minted wire type, so that half is source-forced and settled. But because
     they carry no reference, B1 is not forbidden for them, so their option set
     is WIDER than the other nine, not narrower.

WHAT IS UNDECIDED, AND IT IS ONE QUESTION, NOT ELEVEN:

  Does the durable format record that these seven fields are COLLECTIONS at all?
  Under reading A — what is landed and green today — the repeated field has no
  row in any registry and its members are scalar `cardinality = "one"` rows on
  the owner, so nothing in the format says there are N of them. Under B2 the
  element becomes a logical kind and the owner carries one repeated field
  pointing at it, which records the repetition but costs 7 new logical kinds for
  element types that nothing references — and since none of them is a StrongRef
  target, the reservation bijection law forbids reserving them, so each would
  need a fresh code above the live frontier.

  That is a durable-format question about representation, not a checker question,
  and the checker has said everything it can: it accepts both. Naming it to you
  rather than inferring it.

  (The two KeyEnvelopeNode digest rows ride on the same answer for their parent
  `inherited_roots`; their own digest resolution is already correct either way.)

=== OWNER RULING: B2, RECORD THE COLLECTIONS. DESIGN DERIVED, NOT LANDED ===

Ruled by the owner (/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/OWNER_RULINGS.md): mint the 7 element
types as LOGICAL kinds at fresh codes and land the repeated field rows with
their true cardinality. Grounds are on the ruling; the decisive one is that
under A the repeated field is not in the durable format AT ALL, so every walker
plan 5.1 generates from durable_fields.toml reads "one" where the source says
"many".

EVERYTHING BELOW IS DERIVED AT HEAD b7effc2, TOKEN-FREE. Nothing is landed: the
catalog lease was held by pane3-bw2x throughout.

CARDINALITY VOCABULARY (measured, 923 rows): one 885, many 26, optional 12.
So the repeated field takes cardinality = "many".

PRECEDENT FOR THE SHAPE, from the corpus, two forms already in use:
  ConstraintValidationEvidence.owner_reservation_refs
    card=many wire=StrongRef sem=strong target=LocalConstraintReservationRecord
      -> a repeated StrongRef to a LOGICAL kind. This is our form.
  ConstraintMutationBatch.sorted_mutations
    card=many wire=ConstraintStateMutation sem=none target=None
      -> a repeated inline record whose element is a registered WIRE type. NOT
         our form, and the checker already said why: a wire host can never own a
         field row, and 6 of our 7 elements carry StrongRef members.

FRESH CODES: max landed logical is 0x0570; the next ten free of BOTH landed and
reserved are 0x0571..0x057a. Take 0x0571..0x0577 for the seven, in the order
listed below. Re-derive the frontier at the moment of the edit — other panes are
minting.

THE SEVEN, WITH THEIR ORDER WINDOWS — EVERY ONE SATISFIABLE, AND EVERY ONE
ADMITS THE OWNER'S OWN ORDER, which is the tightest defensible choice (the upper
bound IS the owner's order, and it clears every lower bound):

  owner (order)                                    repeated field                     window        take
  KeyEnvelopeNode (50) 0x02e1                      inherited_roots                    (-inf, 50]    50
  LocalConstraintReservationRecord (30) 0x056d     owner                              [20, 30]      30
  NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof (6) 0x0373       raft_nonorder_evidence             [5, 6]        6
  PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> (30) 0x039a
                                                   sorted_expired_cohort_imports      [27, 30]      30
                                                   sorted_issuer_fence_imports        [20, 30]      30
                                                   sorted_revoked_cohort_imports      [20, 30]      30
  RemoteGrantRetirementPlan (40) 0x03af            sorted_entries                     [24, 40]      40

  Lower bound = max construction_order over that element's member targets; upper
  bound = the owner's order, because the owner's new repeated field references
  the element and target.order <= containing.order. Equality is legal — the law
  fires only on `>`.

WHAT LANDS, PER ELEMENT TYPE (x7):
  1. [[logical_kind]] <Owner><Field>Record at its fresh code, status "reserved",
     construction_order per the table, role_predicate and max_size_bytes copied
     from the owner.
  2. [[field]] on the OWNER for the repeated field itself — the row that is
     missing today and is the whole point of the ruling:
       cardinality = "many", exact_wire_type = "StrongRef",
       reference_semantics = "strong", target_schema_id = the new element kind,
       identity_class = "logical", construction_order = the OWNER's order.
  3. RE-KEY the existing element-member rows from the owner to the new element
     kind: containing_schema becomes <Owner><Field>Record and construction_order
     becomes the element kind's order (the field-order-equals-kind-order law).
     Their field_tags are free to restart at the element, but re-keying moves
     released names, so check the append-only assignment pin before assuming.
  4. One [[target]] row per new [[field]], plus re-pointed source_keys for the
     re-keyed members.

SCOPE LIMIT HELD: the two KeyEnvelopeNode members keep digest256 + digest_class
= "target". A plan-named digest never becomes a minted wire type; B2 governs the
CONTAINING field row, not those element resolutions.

PIN COST — SPLIT THE INCREMENT. This adds 7 logical kinds + 7 field rows + 7
targets and re-keys 11 rows, so it moves at least: [target_manifest] target_count
and target_source_assignment_sha256, EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT and
EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_IDS_SHA256, the durable_fields assignment pin, and — new
this time, because kinds are minted — the LOGICAL assignment pin
(identity.rs:1211) and very likely the logical registry_epoch and its e2e drift
fixture at g0_identity_e2e.sh:637. BASE-DERIVE EVERY ONE from the loader's own
drift at the moment of the edit; do not copy a value from this note. Suggested
split: (i) the 7 kinds alone, (ii) the 7 repeated field rows, (iii) the 11
re-keys — each a separate pin round, each verifiable on its own.

AND CHECK refs.rs BEFORE COMMITTING: minting at status "reserved" does not trip
the fgdb-types compile-time assert, but ACTIVATING would. These land reserved.

=== INCREMENT (i) PROVEN TOKEN-FREE, WITH (ii) SYNTHESIZED ON TOP TO VALIDATE
    THE ORDER CHOICE, AND A CONTROL THAT FIRES ===

Script: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law/inc1.rs — re-runnable, derives the
frontier and PARSES the drift every run rather than restating one.

  baseline validate_identity                              0 violations
  frontier re-derived                 max landed 0x0570 -> 0x0571..0x0577
  name collisions across all 7 namespaces + 813 reservations   0
  (i) 7 logical kinds minted          1 violation, 0 ATTRIBUTABLE
  (i)+(ii) + 7 repeated field rows    2 violations, 0 ATTRIBUTABLE
  CONTROL element order 99 > owner order 40
      -> dag_future_result FIRED on RemoteGrantRetirementPlan#sorted_entries

WHY (ii) IS SYNTHESIZED HERE THOUGH IT LANDS SEPARATELY: increment (i) alone
CANNOT validate the order values, because nothing references the new kinds until
the owner's repeated field row exists — the DAG law has no edge to check. Proving
(i)+(ii) together and landing them separately is the only way the orders in (i)
are anything but assertions. The control at order 99 is what shows the check is
live rather than vacuous.

A DEFECT THE PROBE CAUGHT IN MY OWN SYNTHESIS, worth carrying into the edit:
three of the seven repeated fields share one owner
(PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>), and my
first pass allocated each one `max existing tag + 1` from the pristine catalog,
so all three took tag 26 and the checker returned two code_duplicate rows. They
need three CONSECUTIVE distinct tags. Allocate from the accumulating set, not
from the base.

ALSO NOTE THE PIN ALREADY MOVED UNDER ME: identity.rs:1211 read
LOGICAL = "fnv1a64:9853f4c21f65ce17" when I first opened it; the loader now
reports the released pin as "fnv1a64:5bf6e0e768c4d939". Other panes minted in
between. That is the whole argument for parsing the drift instead of copying a
value, and it is why the script re-derives rather than restates.

THE SEVEN ROWS TO AUTHOR (codes re-derived at edit time):
  a13:logical-kind:key-envelope-node-inherited-roots-record                  0x0571 order 50 role true
  a12:logical-kind:local-constraint-reservation-record-owner-record          0x0572 order 30 role role-local
  a08:logical-kind:no-terminal-signature-or-order-proof-raft-nonorder-evidence-record
                                                                            0x0573 order  6 role true
  a19:logical-kind:prior-incarnation-lease-barrier-bootstrap-import-sorted-expired-cohort-imports-record
                                                                            0x0574 order 30 role true
  a19:...-sorted-issuer-fence-imports-record                                0x0575 order 30 role true
  a19:...-sorted-revoked-cohort-imports-record                              0x0576 order 30 role true
  a08:logical-kind:remote-grant-retirement-plan-sorted-entries-record       0x0577 order 40 role true
All status "reserved", max_size_bytes copied from the owner, golden_corpus
corpus/logical/<snake_name>/. Reserved status does not trip the fgdb-types
compile-time assert; activating would.

NOT LANDED YET: pane3-bw2x holds the catalog lease fixing red main, which
outranks this. Ready to apply the moment it frees.

=== INCREMENT (iii) IS PARKED, DESIGNED, WITH ITS OPEN RISK NAMED ===

(i) landed at 8fb4cfb (7 element kinds), (ii) at c8438a2 (the 7 repeated field
rows with true cardinality). The B2 ruling is real: the collections are in the
durable format. (iii), the 11 re-keys of the `.record.` member rows onto their
element kinds, is DESIGNED AND NOT STARTED, parked on disk pressure rather than
on any open question of design.

Proven token-free already: validate_identity accepts all 11 re-keys — 2
violations, both assignment-pin drift, zero content violations.

THE OPEN RISK, and it must be checked FIRST inside the lease, before any edit:
appendix_a.rs:12014 keys `field_owner_and_name` by owner + name. Re-keying a
member's `containing_schema` onto the element kind while its
[[target]].source_key still names the OWNER-based census path breaks exactly
that join. validate_identity cannot see it — the catalog's targets are not in

0ee737f -- 100% MINE, and gate-verified. numstat is exactly the five files I edited:
  registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml      57/57   the 22 rows + target_manifest pins
  registries/durable_fields.toml         120/120  regenerated, a pure row move
  tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs  40/3    4 hunks: line 40 pin consts, and 7965/7972/7979 all inside covered_interior_keys
  tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs     1/1    the FIELDS assignment pin
  tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs  89/5    7 hunks, all in the 3 fns I edited
It has NO hunk anywhere near line 7518 or 7526, and it added ZERO expect(dead_code) lines. pane2's dead-code region is untouched by it.

8b38752 -- MY MESSAGE, MOSTLY NOT MY CODE. I intended a beads-only commit. It carries:
  .beads/issues.jsonl                       2/2   mine
  registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml       13/13  NOT mine
  registries/durable_fields.toml           12/12  NOT mine
  registries/logical_object_kinds.toml      1/1   NOT mine -- I never opened this file
  tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs  195/10  NOT mine -- hunks at CensusDagVerdict 7515, verify_census_construction_dag, and a Probe fixture at 15361
  tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs   27/5   NOT mine
Everything marked NOT mine is pane2's h1al work: the CensusDagWaiver dead-code fix and its waiver-contract test. It is committed under my message and my Co-Authored-By trailer. I did not review it and ran no gate over it.

MECHANISM, and it is a swarm-wide hazard rather than one pane's slip: THE GIT INDEX IS SHARED WORKTREE STATE. My command was a scoped add of .beads/ followed by a bare commit. A bare commit commits THE INDEX, so pane2's own staging of its files put them in that same index and my commit took them. There is no pre-commit hook and no commit.all setting; this is plain shared-index semantics. A scoped add does NOT protect you. The protection is a PATHSPEC-LIMITED commit -- pass the paths to git commit itself -- which ignores everything else staged. This generalises the already-known beads JSONL export hazard from one file to every tracked file in the repo.

NOT AMENDED, NOT RESET, NOT REVERTED. Those are forbidden and would compound it. The swept code looks fine on its face; the ATTRIBUTION is the defect, because a wrong attribution on a durable-format commit means the next reader cannot tell who verified what. This comment is the repair.
