THE HONEST CAVEAT, which is the real risk the sweep created: HEAD AS IT NOW STANDS HAS NOT BEEN GATE-RUN BY ANYONE. My 130/0 predates pane2's 195 lines; those reached HEAD through my beads commit afterwards, and I have run nothing since. Whoever picks this up should treat HEAD as unverified until a full suite runs over the combined tree.

title: Gate evidence dirs are 9.84GB of the tmp pool — same lifetime defect, different producer
description:
## The half of the pool fgdb-1j16 does not cover

fgdb-1j16 attributes 18.01 GB across 113 `/data/tmp/tmp.*` dirs to
scripts/lib/private_subject.sh. Partitioning each dir into `bin/` (what that
library writes) versus everything else (what the SOURCING GATE writes), measured
2026-07-27 02:3x:

  bin/  -- the subject private_subject.sh builds     8.17 GB   45.4%
  rest  -- gate evidence                             9.84 GB   54.6%

So fixing private_subject.sh at the source, even perfectly, leaves 9.84 GB of
the same defect standing. This bead is that remainder.

## Shape of it

Per-dir totals: min 72.3 MB, median 88.4 MB, mean 163.2 MB, max 627.5 MB. The
subject is a flat 75 MB, so everything above ~75 MB is gate output. The mean dir
carries 88 MB of it.

The largest single occupants are whole-registry COPIES made for negative
controls. /data/tmp/tmp.Q9JWAqKb1p alone holds five at 17.2 MB each:

  neg-appendix-unrelated-bindings   17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-unknown-key          17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-semantic-owner       17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-maintenance          17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-annotation-reference 17.2 MB

That is the appendix-baseline harness pattern: copy the registry tree, mutate one
row, run the checker, assert it fires. Correct as a method; the copies just never
had a lifetime. registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml is 4.0 MB and
registries/durable_fields.toml is 1.0 MB, so each control copy is dominated by
registry bytes that are identical across all five.

## Why it is a separate bead and not part of 1j16

Different producer, and a different fix. private_subject.sh writes ONE artifact
that is a pure function of the checker sources, so it can be content-keyed and
shared -- that is 1j16's fix. Gate evidence is per-run BY CONSTRUCTION: it is the
output being asserted on, and two runs must not share it or the gate stops
measuring its own run. Content-keying is the wrong instrument here.

## What to measure before choosing a fix

1. How much of the 9.84 GB is registry COPIES versus genuine per-run output.
   A copy that differs from the shipped registry in one row could be a
   copy-on-write clone, a symlink farm with one real file, or an in-memory
   mutation -- the checker already accepts a synthesised registry (see how
   tests/architecture_decisions.rs mutates a parsed ArchitectureRegistry rather
   than copying files). If most of the 9.84 GB is near-duplicate registry bytes,
   the fix is to stop copying, not to reap.
2. Which gates produce the biggest dirs. The 627.5 MB maximum is 8x the mean and
   is worth naming on its own.
3. Whether any of it is EVIDENCE someone is relying on. /data/tmp/tmp.G5czm7QFIs
   is already flagged on fgdb-1j16 as the recorded evidence for fgdb-ia2b and
   must not be reaped.

## Constraint inherited from 1j16

No external sweeper, and nothing in a gate deletes a file (RULE 1). If the answer
turns out to be retention rather than not-writing, it needs an owner with delete
authority -- 1j16 option 2 -- and this bead should be merged into that decision
rather than growing its own reaper.

Found while working fgdb-1j16 (pane2, 2026-07-27). Nothing has been deleted.
notes:
pane4, 2026-07-27 ~03:2x. Pool measured at HEAD 6c379ed with 7.1G free; written
up at HEAD 47a8c00, by which point fgdb-1j16 had landed (3668d69). MEASURED AND
DESIGNED; the code change is NOT LANDED and the reason is stated at the end.

=== THE CLAIM IN THIS BEAD THAT COLLAPSES ===

This bead says: "Gate evidence is per-run BY CONSTRUCTION: it is the output being
asserted on, and two runs must not share it or the gate stops measuring its own
run. Content-keying is the wrong instrument here."

Genuine per-run output is 0.272 GB of the 9.84 GB -- 2.8%. MEASURED: 2443 loose
files (.jsonl/.err/.sha256) sitting directly in the 113 marker dirs. Everything
else is INPUT, copied per fixture. 4.10 GB of it (41.7%) is four file classes
that no fixture and no checker code path ever writes.

Content-keying is indeed the wrong instrument. So is reaping. The instrument is
`cp -l`.

=== THE PARTITION OF THE 9.84 GB (measured, sums to 9.83) ===

  class                                       copies      GB      %   disposition
  registries/*.toml                              837    4.75   48.3%  MUST COPY
  .beads/issues.jsonl                            441    3.08   31.3%  LINKABLE
  tools/registry-check/src/*.rs                  441    0.93    9.4%  LINKABLE
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md                       453    0.71    7.2%  MUST COPY
  per-run evidence (.jsonl/.err/.sha256)        2443    0.27    2.8%  irreducible
  crates/ + scripts/ + Cargo.toml                441    0.09    0.9%  LINKABLE
                                                       -----
                                                        9.83

Cross-check on 1j16's half from the same census: libregistry_check.rlib 113
copies = 7.151 GB, registry-check 113 copies = 1.033 GB, total 8.18 GB -- 1j16
says 8.17 GB. The two halves are measured by one reader and agree.

Also from the same pass, unrelated to either bead: the /data/tmp pool is 10719
entries, not 165. 165 are directories (22.16 GB); 10554 are stray `tmp.*` FILES
totalling 0.04 GB. Negligible bytes, 10554 inodes, different producer.

=== Q1 (this bead's first question): copies vs genuine per-run output ===

87.1% of the 9.84 GB is copies (8.57 GB), 2.8% is genuine per-run output. The
three hypotheses this bead offered for the copies:

  - copy-on-write clone: FALSIFIED ON THIS MACHINE. / is ext4 on /dev/nvme0n1p4.
    `cp --reflink=always` -> "Operation not supported" (probed in scratchpad).
  - symlink farm: unnecessary. Repo and /data/tmp are the same device (st_dev
    66308 both), so HARD links work and are invisible to the checker's laws.
  - in-memory synthesis: correct in principle (that is what
    tests/architecture_decisions.rs does) but it is a rewrite of a 72 KB gate
    script, not a fix.

=== Q2: which gates produce the biggest dirs ===

The 113 marker dirs attributed by positive child marker:

  gate           dirs      GB   mean      max
  g0_identity      17    9.98  601.3MB  627.5MB (tmp.Q9JWAqKb1p)
  g0_spine         61    5.12   86.0MB   92.4MB
  g0_claims        22    1.97   91.7MB   93.1MB
  unattributed     13    0.94   73.8MB   81.8MB

Subtracting each dir's 75 MB subject (1j16's half) leaves 8.71 GB of evidence in
g0_identity and 1.01 GB in everything else. **88.5% of this bead is one script,
scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, and the 627.5 MB maximum is simply one run of it.**
The other three producers are ~zero evidence and ~all subject: they are 1j16.

Per run, that script stages 26 complete roots (23 stage_appendix + 3
stage_appendix_except) at 17.61 MB each = 458 MB, plus 14 registries-only roots
(3 stage + 11 stage_except) at 6.07 MB each = 85 MB, plus 0.27 GB/17 of evidence
and the 75 MB subject. 627 MB predicted, 627.5 MB observed.

AND IT GROWS. The two dominant copied files are the two files the swarm itself
appends to. MEASURED from git history:

  .beads/issues.jsonl          5.02 MB (07-22) -> 7.86 MB (now)   +57% in 5 days
  registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml
                               1.59 MB (07-24) -> 4.32 MB (now)  +171% in 3 days

Those two are copied 26x per identity run: 317 MB today, 172 MB five days ago.
The gate's disk cost is a linear function of the beads export size times 26, and
every bead any pane files raises it.

=== Q3: is any of it evidence someone relies on ===

9 distinct pool dirs are cited by name in .beads/issues.jsonl. 6 are PRESENT
(AJuYPC46f4, ECFKRWvum9, G5czm7QFIs, Q9JWAqKb1p, Z33uC7OtE5, qIVyqY2uko); 3 are
ALREADY ABSENT (04yme8fWMO, 1mDaWQL5Za, CB9K3IaRcE) and all three are cited by
one bead, fgdb-a15-key-backup-n77c, whose recorded evidence has therefore already
evaporated. G5czm7QFIs (89 MB, fgdb-ia2b) is present and must not be reaped.

That is the honest answer to "does anything rely on it": the citation practice
has a 33% dangling rate after one day, so a sweep must be checked against this
list, and citing a tmp path is not a durable record.

=== THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS SAFE ===

One function, scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:551 stage_appendix_support(). Change
`cp` to `cp -l` for the four never-written classes; leave registries/ and the
plan md as real copies:

  cp -l   .beads/issues.jsonl                  7676 KB   never written
  cp -l   tools/registry-check/src/*.rs        2308 KB   never written
  cp -l   scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh             76 KB   never written
  cp -l   Cargo.toml + crate/tool manifests      60 KB   never written
  ------------------------------------------- 10120 KB = 56.1% of a root
  cp      registries/*.toml                    6220 KB   36 mutation sites + law
  cp      COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md             1696 KB   2 mutation sites

Saves 26 x 9.88 MB = 257 MB per identity run, 41.0% of a 627 MB run. Retroactively
4.10 GB of this bead's 9.84 GB, 41.7%. Two independent derivations of the same
fraction: today's source sizes give 56.1% of a root linkable, and the historical
depth-2 census of a real fixture gives 9716/17396 KB = 55.9%.

Four propositions, all closed statically, no build:

1. THE GATE NEVER REFERENCES A LINKED FILE AGAIN, READ OR WRITE. Exhaustive
   census of every `$WORK/<fixture>/...` path in the script, by tail:

     registries/logical_object_kinds.toml        19
     registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml          18
     registries/durable_fields.toml              13
     registries/{wire_types,prebootstrap_artifact_kinds,
                 physical_record_kinds,bootstrap_frames}.toml  6 each
     COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md                     2   (both writes: 1120, 1532)
     registries, registries/                      8   (staging dests)
     .beads, .beads/, scripts, scripts/,
       tools/registry-check/src{,/}               6   (all inside
                                                      stage_appendix_support
                                                      itself, lines 551-568)

   Nothing outside registries/ and the plan md is touched after staging. This
   covers every write form, not just truncating `>`: there are appending `>>`
   writers (1126, 1144, 1221, 1328), an `ln -s` (1350), a bare `ln` (1378) and a
   `mkdir -p` (1401), and all six land on registries/logical_object_kinds.toml
   or registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml. An earlier same-line-only grep of mine
   reported "zero ln/mv/mkdir writers", which was wrong -- those six are
   line-continued. The conclusion is unchanged and stronger: the linkable set has
   zero post-staging references of any kind.

2. NO CHECKER WRITE CAN LAND OUTSIDE registries/. The whole production write
   surface of tools/registry-check is main.rs:808 (create a
   .appendix-regenerate-*.prepared inside registries/), main.rs:819 (write_all to
   it) and main.rs:1009 (rename it onto a projection destination inside
   registries/). main.rs:725 opens the catalog READ-ONLY for an advisory lock.
   Every other fs::write in the tool is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
   (unsafe_ledger.rs:2415).

3. THE CHECKER'S HARD-LINK LAW DOES NOT REACH THE LINKED SET. main.rs:638
   metadata_has_one_link is called at main.rs:746 (projection destination) and
   main.rs:846-847 (prepared projection). PROJECTION_FILES (appendix_a.rs:5058)
   is 6 files, all in registries/, which stays a copy. The gate's own
   neg-appendix-regenerate-hardlink fixture (line 1371) proves that law fires
   with exit 2 / code 6 -- linking a projection would break the POSITIVE
   appendix-regenerate fixture, which is exactly why registries/ is excluded.
   snapshot_nonprojection_tree (line 583) records %y|%m|%p|%l and sha256, none of
   which move under a hard link.

4. WRITE-THROUGH IS DETECTABLE AND DOES NOT HAPPEN. Probe (scratchpad, no repo
   file touched, no build, runs in under a second) builds a stand-in ROOT, stages
   it, applies all five write forms the census found, and digests the source:
     A today, all copies      -> source intact,  0 of 10 staged inodes shared
     B proposed               -> source intact,  5 of 10 shared
     C control: ALSO link the plan md, then truncate it
                              -> source CORRUPT, 6 of 10 shared
        136311807998a261 -> 6750d368e7325049; source plan reads "MUTATED plan"
     D control: append `>>` through the linked .beads/issues.jsonl
                              -> source CORRUPT, 5 of 10 shared
        136311807998a261 -> dea1c2313f0632e8; source reads
        "SENTINEL beads APPENDED beads"
   Both controls FIRE. Without C and D, A and B would prove only that the probe
   is blind. D exists because the gate has four `>>` appenders and a truncation-
   only probe cannot see them.

   The probe's own per-file reporter had this bug and it was caught by D: it
   classified a file as intact if its content still STARTED with the sentinel,
   which is true after an append. Fixed to a byte compare against a pristine
   rebuild. The case verdict was always driven by the tree digest and was correct
   throughout; the per-file line was the thing that lied.

THE FOOT-GUN THIS EXPOSES, INDEPENDENT OF THE FIX: two fixtures
(neg-appendix-source at line 1120, neg-appendix-reference-source at line 1532)
truncate-redirect into COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md
inside a staged root. It is the repo's single source of truth. Anyone who reaches
for the obvious `cp -l` across the whole staging function -- which is what both
this bead and 1j16 gesture at -- destroys it. That is case C above, and it is not
hypothetical: it is the first thing a reader of these two beads would try.

=== THE SECOND INCREMENT, AND THE GUARD IT NEEDS FIRST ===

registries/ is 4.75 GB, half this bead, and it is "MUST COPY" only in aggregate.
Distinct fixtures that write each registry file, over the 40 roots one run stages
(26 full + 14 registries-only):

  appendix_a_catalog.toml    4192 KB  18 writers  -> 22 roots never touch it
  logical_object_kinds.toml   120 KB  12 writers  ) all six are PROJECTION_FILES;
  durable_fields.toml        1072 KB   7 writers  ) the nlink==1 law reaches them
  wire_types.toml             204 KB   0 writers  ) so they stay copies whatever
  physical_record_kinds.toml    4 KB   0 writers  ) their writer count says
  bootstrap_frames.toml         4 KB   0 writers  )
  prebootstrap_artifact_...     4 KB   0 writers  )

appendix_a_catalog.toml is NOT a projection (appendix_a.rs:5058 lists six files

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FILED BY ORCHESTRATOR at pane2's request; pane2 surfaced it and declined to file unilaterally, correctly, since it is a design question rather than a defect in any one increment.

THE DEFECT. The bead-provenance pins are a COUNT over .beads/issues.jsonl -- a file every pane writes. So the pin is a global assertion about shared mutable state, and any pane running 'br create' invalidates every other pane's just-frozen pins. pane2 hit this TWICE in one session. It is not a bug in any pane's behaviour; correct panes racing correctly still break it.

OBSERVED COST TONIGHT, all from this one root cause:
  - repeated 'chore(beads): re-freeze provenance' commits that carry no product change
  - a 398->399 re-freeze sitting in one pane's tree while another pane's closed bead depended on it
  - seven CREATED records stranded in local .beads/beads.db, exposed to deletion by any 'br sync --import-only' (relayed swarm-wide 23:12Z; closed by a flush at 23:20Z)
  - the standing rule that a bead CREATION costs a pin re-freeze while an equal-insert/delete MODIFIED sweep does not -- a rule every pane must be told, because nothing enforces it

WHY IT IS A DESIGN FIX, NOT A REPAIR. Each occurrence is individually cheap to fix and collectively unbounded: the repair is O(number of concurrent creators) forever. A pin that quantifies over a file with N writers cannot be stable under N>1 by construction.

DIRECTIONS WORTH COSTING (do not assume one): make the pin per-record or content-addressed rather than a count; scope it to the records the freezing commit actually owns; derive it from committed HEAD rather than the working-tree export; or serialise creation behind the existing beads token and make that mandatory rather than advisory.

Related: the bead-provenance re-pin cycle is already known to break 5 tests on any creation. This bead is the root cause of that tax.

Fixture symlinks every path from that snapshot and materialises only `.beads/issues.jsonl`, so a difference in the report is attributable to the corpus mutation and nothing else. Checkers driven lock-free by plain rustc against `validate_architecture`. Base is 0 violations under both checkers, so the instrument is not vacuous.

=== 1. THE DEFECT STATEMENT NEEDS SHARPENING ===

The bead says the pin is a COUNT. That is true but it is not the defect, and taking it literally sends you to a fix that does not work. `binding_hash` is ALREADY content-addressed and it breaks exactly as hard:

  mutation create1 (one bead, resolves via an existing bet label -- legal under every provenance law):
    bead_source_count, bead_resolution_class_count, bead_binding_hash_mismatch, independent_bead_binding_hash_mismatch   = 4 violations

The problem is not count-vs-hash. It is the QUANTIFICATION DOMAIN: the change-detector quantifies over a set the freezing commit does not own. Any equality over corpus-derived data is unstable under insertion, whatever its form.

The second half of the sharpening: the provenance machinery is TWO things fused, and only one of them is broken.

  (A) PER-RECORD LAWS -- orphan, not_total, family_ambiguous, bet_label_unknown, decision_unresolved/superseded, override_shadowed, override_target_missing, owner_bead_unresolved. Every one is a predicate over a single record. They are ALREADY stable under N writers. A pane creating a bead with a home does not move any other bead's resolution. These are not the defect and must not be touched.

  (B) CORPUS-CARDINALITY CHANGE-DETECTOR -- bead_count, 4 class counts, 14 expected_match_counts, binding_hash, each pinned twice (TOML + code const). This is the whole of the tax.

=== 2. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS MOST: THE PINS DESTROYED THE SIGNAL THEY RIDE ON ===

`recompute_semantic_contract_hash` takes `&ArchitectureRegistry` and no `&Path` -- it CANNOT read the bead file. It is the registry's "did the ADR contract move" tripwire. But the corpus counts and `binding_hash` are laundered into its transcript, so every `br create` moves it.

Walking all 49 commits that touch architecture.rs:

  PINNED_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_HASH moved in                45 commits
    ...of which ALSO moved PINNED_BEAD_COUNT            44   <- bead churn, not a semantic edit
    ...genuine semantic-only edits                       1
  PINNED_BEAD_COUNT moved without the semantic hash      0   <- 100% laundering

44:1 noise-to-signal on the registry's most load-bearing tripwire. Independent confirmation: the rule-side content of the registry is BYTE-IDENTICAL between 60439d7 and HEAD (rule hash fnv1a64:c4e66b12a1e31d91 at both) -- every registry edit in that window was corpus-pin churn wearing a semantic-hash change as a disguise.

Rate: 44 re-freezes over 2026-07-22..07-26 (~9/day); 26 commits whose SUBJECT LINE is nothing but pin churn.

=== 3. DIRECTION VERDICTS ===

D1 per-record / content-addressed pins -- FALSIFIED. Content-addressing over the whole set is what `binding_hash` already is (4-violation result above). Making it genuinely per-record means a ~400-row table in the TOML that `br create` must append to, which converts a one-line conflict into a shared-table conflict and still costs a registry edit per create. Strictly worse; moves the race one hop.

D2 scope the pin to records the freezing commit owns -- COLLAPSES INTO D1. There is no "freezing commit" at check time; the checker runs on a working tree. Expressing ownership requires per-record attribution, i.e. D1. The useful CONTENT of this direction survives inside D5.

D3 derive from committed HEAD -- FALSIFIED, and strictly worse. HEAD moves too, so the race is unchanged; but the red now appears in a tree the pane never touched, with no local reproduction, and it puts a git dependency inside a checker that is deliberately git-free and cargo-free (that property is what makes `bead_provenance_preflight.sh` work while the workspace is mid-repair).

D4 mandatory beads token -- ALREADY DEPLOYED, ALREADY MEASURED AS INSUFFICIENT. token.sh's own header records that the `beads` token was added 2026-07-24 for exactly this failure. Since then:

  re-freeze commits before 2026-07-24    9
  re-freeze commits on/after             40
  growth transitions since               47

The token removes SWEEP collisions, which is what it was built for. It removes none of the tax, because the tax is per-create, not per-collision. Serialising a cost does not eliminate it. Keep the token for what it does; it is not this fix.

=== 4. D5 -- THE RECOMMENDATION: MAKE THE CORPUS PINS MONOTONE, MOVE THE EQUALITY TO THE RULES ===

Rules are not shared-mutable; the corpus is. Pin each with the form that suits it.

  (a) corpus cardinality: every `!=` becomes `<`. bead_count, the 4 class counts and the 14 family counts become FLOORS. Creation can never trip a floor; loss always does.
  (b) `binding_hash` stops being H(every bead's binding) and becomes H(rule_id -> sorted decision_ids) over direct owners, the six labels, every override and every family. Pure function of the registry; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is never read.
  (c) the floors and the rule hash come OUT of the semantic-contract transcript. That hash goes back to meaning what its name says.
  (d) per-record laws unchanged.
  (e) a ratchet (raise floors to observed) is available but never required for green -- raising a floor to the current count is arithmetic, not a judgement call, unlike assigning provenance.

The corpus/registry boundary turns out to be exactly three comparisons plus one hash function. One reader, no second implementation of the family rules.

MUTATION MATRIX (records; violations TODAY -> violations FLOOR):

  base                    398   0 -> 0     control, both green
  create1                 399   4 -> 0     THE TAX, gone
  create2                 400   4 -> 0
  create10                408   4 -> 0
  delete1  (bead loss)    397   4 -> 2     distinct *_below_floor codes
  delowner (owner lost)   397   8 -> 6
  swap     (equal +1/-1)  398   2 -> 0     MISSED by the fix
  grow10_del1 (stale)     407   4 -> 0     MISSED by the fix
  grow10_delowner         407   9 -> 5
  wipe     (198 lost)     200 180 -> 178

The line that indicts today's design: create1 and delete1 produce THE SAME FOUR CODES. A pane filing a bead and the corpus silently losing a bead are indistinguishable to the checker. That is why the alarm gets re-frozen reflexively -- it carries no information about which happened. Under floors they are different codes, and only one of them fires.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS ON THE PROTOTYPE -- all four FIRE:

  raise a family floor 7->8        -> bead_family_match_count_below_floor + bead_family_expected_total

That last one is the control I ran against my own recommendation, and it is the one that matters: a pure re-binding that changes no count and leaves every bead resolvable. It is precisely what the corpus hash was for. The rule-keyed hash catches it. So (b) is not a weakening on that hazard class.

The existing negative tests survive: `direct_owner_count += 1` and `expected_match_count += 1` both still fire (renamed codes).

wrong. Those are floors now; the exact assertion is the rule hash (newly
emitted as bead_rule_binding_hash); and a closure assert plus a sum check stop
a fifth resolution class hiding behind the per-class floors.

=== LIVE MEASUREMENT AT CLOSE ===

Filing the follow-up bead fgdb-hcvx was itself the test. The corpus is now 404
records against a floor of 401 -- my create plus two more from other panes
since the commit, i.e. the N>1 case unstaged and unsimulated:

  under the landed floor checker      0 violations   GREEN
  under the pre-change equality one   5 violations

Before 4a01ce8 that state cost a 7-value re-freeze across two files and redded
five tests for every pane. It now costs nothing.

=== GATES ===

scripts/check.sh: CORE 6 of 7 -- fmt, check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings,
test --workspace, file-coverage closure, shell lint ALL PASS; the one core red
is the whole-tree UBS scan (pre-existing false-positive class). REGISTERED LIVE
GATES 18 of 19, up from 17: w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh now passes,
confirming its earlier red was the shared-target-dir race. The single remaining
red is scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, unchanged cause and not mine -- the
reservation split from e7b6f09 (a20, fgdb-5cgb), observed existing=434
reserved=379 against pinned 431/382; repair is scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:210
-> 434 and :211 -> 379, left for pane5 because those numbers ratify their
adjudication.

=== HANDOFF ===

OPEN, filed: fgdb-hcvx -- rename the pins so their names stop claiming
equality (bead_count -> bead_count_floor, expected_match_count ->
min_match_count, binding_hash -> rule_binding_hash, and the matching consts).
Mechanical, compiler-checked, no semantics; wants the catalog token at a quiet
point. Nothing breaks mechanically if it waits -- the risk is a pane re-reading
"count" as equality and re-freezing a floor by hand.

FOR THE NEXT AUTHOR, two traps this turn hit:
  - Under floors, a negative test written as `declared + 1` goes VACUOUS the
    moment the corpus grows past the floor. The staged tree at 401-vs-401
    passed; the real tree at 402-vs-401 silently stopped firing it. Derive
    every floor mutation from the OBSERVED count. Staging alone cannot catch
    this, because the staged copy is exactly the state where observed ==
    declared.
  - When converting an equality pin anywhere, grep the GATES as well as the
    checker. The e2e carried an independent copy and would have kept the race
    alive on its own.

Evidence, both prototypes and the race harness survive in this session's
scratchpad; the permanent artefacts are the new test and the floor negatives.

title: check.sh reports 6 red cargo-test artifacts from 1 compile error, and the other 5 binaries are never run
close_reason: Masked count measured on two real runs: 67 of 67 suites masked by a compile error, 36 of 67 by a mid-run failure, with 6 artifacts reported RED both times and one of them actually passing. check.sh now attributes each cargo-test artifact from its own binary (pass/red/unrun); 6 false reds removed on a live run. My proposed --keep-going fix was measured NOT to work. 43f7907.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED (pane4, 2026-07-26) from a real scripts/check.sh run at HEAD 4710fd6, while closing fgdb-su5y. Log retained.

ONE compile error produced SIX red artifact rows:

  RED registered cargo-test crates/fgdb-codec/tests/generated_durable_roundtrip.rs — cargo test --workspace exited 101
  RED registered cargo-test tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs   — cargo test --workspace exited 101
  RED registered cargo-test tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs                   — cargo test --workspace exited 101
  RED registered cargo-test tools/registry-check/tests/threat_model.rs             — cargo test --workspace exited 101
  RED registered cargo-test tools/registry-check/tests/unsafe_ledger.rs            — cargo test --workspace exited 101
  RED registered cargo-test tools/registry-check/tests/workspace_topology.rs       — cargo test --workspace exited 101

The actual cause was a single error in ONE of them:

  error[E0599]: no method named `is_empty` found for tuple `(Vec<LintHit>, LintCensus)`
     --> tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs:544:14
  error: could not compile `registry-check` (test "claims")

BOTH FAILURE DIRECTIONS ARE PRESENT IN THIS ONE PLACE.

  CASCADE. Five artifacts are reported red on evidence that says nothing about
  them. A pane reading this concludes six things are broken and sizes the work
  accordingly; one thing is broken.

  MASKING, which is worse. `cargo test --workspace` has no --no-fail-fast, so
  those five test binaries were never built or run. Their real status is
  UNKNOWN and the report states it as RED. If one of them is also broken,
  clearing claims.rs turns the row green for everyone without the second defect
  ever having been measured -- which is exactly what dd7749b already recorded
  one gate over: "clippy aborted at the first error, so anything behind it is
  still unmeasured."

The same shape applies to the other three core cargo gates. `cargo check
--all-targets` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` both stop at the first crate
that fails to compile; only `cargo fmt --check` reports every file.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. scripts/check.sh's own harness is already fail-slow and
correct: it executed 7 of 7 core gates and 19 of 19 registered gates in that
same run, reported "2 passed; 5 red" and "12 passed; 7 red; 0 unrun", and
printed the unrun count explicitly. The defect is entirely in what one cargo
invocation can tell it. Do not rewrite the harness.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, for whoever takes it:
  - `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` so every test binary runs and each
    registered cargo-test artifact gets its own verdict;
  - `--keep-going` on check/clippy for the same reason;
  - attribute per-artifact rather than stamping one exit code onto every row --
    an artifact whose binary never ran should read UNRUN, not RED, since
    check.sh already has an "unrun" concept and already prints its count.

WATCH FOR: --no-fail-fast changes wall-clock on a broken tree (it builds and
runs everything rather than stopping), and it must not weaken the exit code --
the run must still exit nonzero. Mutation-prove that two independently broken
test binaries are BOTH named, and that one broken binary still reds the gate.

NOT MEASURED HERE: whether the other five binaries actually pass at that commit.
That is the point -- nothing in the tree knows.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, ~1 hour later, from a DIFFERENT root cause (pane4, 2026-07-26, HEAD 9c0d3c1). A full scripts/check.sh run again stamped one `cargo test --workspace exited 101` onto the same six artifact rows:

  crates/fgdb-codec/tests/generated_durable_roundtrip.rs
  tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs
  tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs
  tools/registry-check/tests/threat_model.rs
  tools/registry-check/tests/unsafe_ledger.rs
  tools/registry-check/tests/workspace_topology.rs

This time the cause was an in-flight architecture.rs / tests/architecture_decisions.rs change, not the claims-lint tuple. Same six rows, same message, different defect -- which is the point: the row set carries no information about WHICH artifact is broken, so it cannot distinguish the two occurrences. In the same run all 7 registered SCRIPT artifacts and all 6 registered BINARY artifacts reported individually and correctly (7/7 and 6/6 pass), so the defect is specific to how one cargo invocation's exit code is fanned out.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSED. Landed 43f7907.

THE MASKED COUNT, WHICH IS THE FINDING, measured on two REAL runs rather than
from the possibility of masking:

  4710fd6  compile error in tools/registry-check/tests/claims.rs
           0 of 67 suites ran -- 67 masked, 100%
           six artifacts reported RED on zero test evidence
  9c0d3c1  a test binary vanished from the shared /data/tmp/cargo-target
           mid-run ("could not execute process ... (never executed)")
           31 of 67 suites ran and ALL 31 PASSED; 36 masked, 54%
           six artifacts reported RED, five of whose binaries never ran, and
           one -- crates/fgdb-codec/tests/generated_durable_roundtrip.rs --
           which had just reported "ok. 12 passed; 0 failed" in that same run

So the old rule was wrong in BOTH directions at once: it called a passing
artifact red, and it called five unmeasured artifacts red rather than unrun.

CONTROLLED, on -p registry-check (10 test targets, 5 of the 6 registered
artifacts), two planted failures in two independent targets:

  fail-fast      exit 101, 12 binaries run, 12 suites reported, 1 of 2 named
  --no-fail-fast exit 101, 16 binaries run, 17 suites reported, 2 of 2 named
  green control  exit 0,   16 binaries run, 17 suites reported (both variants)

THE FIX I PROPOSED ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. I wrote
"--keep-going on check/clippy for the same reason". It does not work. With a
parse error planted in ONE test target:

  plain                        0 of 16 binaries run, exit 101
  --no-fail-fast               0 of 16, exit 101
  --keep-going                 0 of 16, exit 1
  --no-fail-fast --keep-going  0 of 16, exit 1
  and with a second, DEPENDENCY-FREE package named on the same command line,
  --keep-going still ran 0 of its tests

No cargo flag recovers a compile failure. --no-fail-fast governs whether cargo
keeps RUNNING binaries after one fails; it cannot make one that failed to
COMPILE exist. That is why the fix is attribution plus an UNRUN verdict rather
than a second flag, and why I left clippy and check alone -- adding a flag there
would have been cargo-cult, and I would have shipped it on my own say-so if I
had not run the experiment.

WHAT LANDED. scripts/check.sh now runs `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`,
keeps that run's output, and gives each registered cargo-test artifact a verdict
derived from ITS OWN test binary: pass when its "test result: ok" line is
present, red when its own line says FAILED, unrun when its binary never ran or
when the artifact is not individually attributable. UNRUN already reds the
overall gate (print_registered_summary counts REGISTERED_UNRUN != 0 as red), so
this is strictly more truthful and not one bit more permissive.

LIVE END TO END, on a genuinely red tree at HEAD 60cb545, where
tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs fails 12 tests (that is fgdb-un4g, not
mine, and I corroborated its count there):

  RED  core: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast (exit 101)
  PASS cargo-test generated_durable_roundtrip.rs  ok. 12 passed
  PASS cargo-test architecture_decisions.rs       ok. 39 passed
  PASS cargo-test claims.rs                       ok. 31 passed
  PASS cargo-test threat_model.rs                 ok. 40 passed
  PASS cargo-test unsafe_ledger.rs                ok. 43 passed
  PASS cargo-test workspace_topology.rs           ok. 56 passed
  REGISTERED LIVE GATES: 19 of 19 executed; 18 passed; 1 red; 0 unrun
  QUALITY GATE RED (exit 1)

Six false reds removed on one run, from a failure in a target that is not even
a registered artifact. The gate still exits 1.

CONTROLS, BOTH FIRE. --self-test gains four attribution cases off a fixture log
(pass / red / never-ran / ambiguous same-named target in two packages), a
missing-log case, an unattributable-artifact case, and one end-to-end
run_registered_gates case asserting UNRUN plus a nonzero exit.
  mutant 1, restore the old all-or-nothing rule
     -> self-test exit 1: "a cargo-test artifact whose own binary passed
        attributed 'red', expected 'pass'"
  mutant 2, keep pass/red but call a never-run binary red
     -> self-test exit 1: "attributed 'red', expected 'unrun'"
  shipped -> exit 0
So a future author cannot quietly restore either half.

WHAT I DID NOT DO:
  - cargo check and cargo clippy still stop at the first error. dd7749b's
    warning stands for them and I did NOT measure how many diagnostics they
    mask; that needs its own bead and its own experiment, and I did not want to
    guess a second time on this one.
  - I did not add --locked to the workspace test invocation. It would be a
    separate policy change (it fails when Cargo.lock would move) and it is not
    what this bead is about.
  - The registry covers 6 cargo-test artifacts; the workspace has 27 integration
    test targets. The other 21 have no registered row at all, so nothing in
    check.sh reports on them individually. That is a coverage question, not an
    attribution one, and I did not open it.
  - I did not touch the shared-target-dir race that CAUSED 9c0d3c1's false red
    (a concurrent pane deleting binaries out of /data/tmp/cargo-target). It bit
    my own first measurement too. Worth its own bead.

DISK, as instructed: NO new target dir was minted per run. The controlled runs
reused ONE path, /data/tmp/cargo-target-m2c1, now 512M -- small because
registry-check is std-only. I did not create it lightly: the first attempt ran
against the shared /data/tmp/cargo-target (51G) and a concurrent pane deleted my
test binaries mid-run, which corrupted the numbers and is exactly the hazard
above. Free space fell from 33G to 24G during this bead, none of it mine beyond
that 512M. I have NOT deleted it -- say the word and I will.

BUILD SLOT: build-1 held for the controlled runs and the two full check.sh runs,
renewed explicitly six times, released at the end.

title: Merge-algebra suites do not constrain their kernel: any confusable operator pair passes (three families)
description:
START HERE: `label_counts` already contains the discriminator. `merge_is_deliberately_not_idempotent` (crates/fgdb-sketch/src/label_counts.rs) is the relation that separates an additive merge from an absorbing one, and it was written independently before this defect was known. A reader who finds that test does not need to re-derive anything — copy its shape.

THE GUARD, which is the durable part and survives any change in how many families are affected:
**Commutativity and associativity cannot distinguish sum from max, so an algebra suite asserting only those constrains nothing.** Max is itself commutative and associative, so a merge kernel that silently used max instead of addition satisfies both properties and every test built on them. Any mergeable sketch with an additive kernel therefore needs at least one relation that separates the operators:
  * NON-IDEMPOTENCE — merging a value with itself must double it; under max it is a no-op.
  * MASS CONSERVATION over a disjoint split — partitioning a stream and merging must equal accumulating it whole. Assert on canonical bytes, not on a total, or a merge that moves mass between buckets while preserving the sum still passes.
And verify it the only way that counts: MUTATE THE KERNEL TO MAX AND WATCH THE SUITE GO RED, then revert and watch it go green. A suite that has never been observed to fail is not evidence that it constrains anything.

WHAT WAS FOUND AND FIXED. Two families carried a counter-addition kernel where this confusion is expressible, and both are now fixed:
  * `count_min` — was unconstrained; fixed by d7c4ff1 (split/merge equivalence on canonical bytes plus monotone accumulation).
  * `degree_histogram` — was unconstrained; fixed by 1d75e8f (`merge_is_additive_and_not_idempotent`, asserting both relations above). Proven: GREEN at 113 with the real kernel, RED with the kernel mutated to max and exactly that test failing.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the survey behind the scope, so nobody re-derives it and nobody overstates it. All eight families were probed.
  * Targeted addition/max mutation, applicable only where the kernel is counter-additive: count_min RED (constrained), degree_histogram RED after the fix (was GREEN before), label_counts RED via its existing non-idempotence test, distinct RED under max->overwrite. `distinct`'s kernel IS max and that is correct — proposing otherwise would be a defect, not a fix.
  * `bottom_k`, `exact_quantiles`, `path_correlation` merge COLLECTIONS, not counters — their `checked_add` calls operate on lengths — and `zone_map` merges bounds. The addition/max confusion is not expressible in those kernels, so the targeted mutation does not apply to them.
  * UNIVERSAL BASELINE, run so that the four non-additive families were not merely classified by reading: making `try_merge` a no-op fails 2-4 tests in EVERY one of the eight. So every suite constrains merge at the coarsest level; the gap was specifically at the operator-identity level, and only in additive kernels.

STATUS: no family currently carries this defect. This record exists for the guard, not for outstanding remediation. The action it implies is forward-looking: any NEW mergeable sketch with an additive kernel must ship a discriminating relation and a witnessed red run, not a commutativity/associativity pair.

METHOD NOTE that made this affordable: fgdb-sketch modules depend only on `fgdb_collections::hash_table`, and fgdb-collections has zero dependencies, so it links as a REAL rlib under standalone `rustc --test` — no stubs, hashing stays faithful. That gives the whole eight-family suite in about a second against a ~15 minute remote gate, which is what made mutating eight kernels and re-running everything cheap enough to attempt. One trap worth repeating: DELETE THE PROBE BINARY BETWEEN RUNS. A stale binary once reported a green result for a mutation that had failed to apply, which would have entered this record as a false finding.
close_reason: All three affected families fixed and proven by witnessed red/green: count_min d7c4ff1, degree_histogram 1d75e8f, exact_quantiles 06f29ae. Guard recorded for future additive/confusable kernels.

comments.author: pane4-calibrate
comments.text:
GENERALISATION AND CORRECTED COUNT — the title and scope of this bead are now wider than when I filed it, because I measured further and my original scope was wrong. Three families, not two, and the guard is not about addition versus max specifically.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I probed every family with ONE mutation — counter addition to max — found it inapplicable to the families whose merge unions collections rather than adding counters, and concluded no further family was affected. That was a scope error, not a measurement error: the right question is not "does the addition/max confusion apply here" but "does this suite constrain ITS OWN kernel", and every kernel class has its own confusable pair. Asking the narrow question and generalising the negative is the mistake.

THE GENERALISED GUARD, which is the durable content of this bead:
**Commutativity, associativity and idempotence cannot distinguish between operators that all satisfy them. An algebra suite asserting only those properties constrains nothing about WHICH operator the kernel implements.**
Confusable pairs observed in this crate, each pair being commutative, associative and idempotent on both sides: sum vs max (counter kernels); min vs max (bounds kernels); keep-k-smallest vs keep-k-largest (selection kernels); ascending vs descending (ordered-merge kernels). A suite built only on the three algebraic properties admits either member of any of these pairs.
THE FIX SHAPE, per kernel: add at least one relation that SEPARATES the pair. Non-idempotence under self-merge separates sum from max. Mass conservation over a disjoint split separates sum from any absorbing operator. An explicit ordering assertion over INTERLEAVED runs separates ascending from descending — non-overlapping runs merge identically under both and cannot discriminate. Assert on canonical bytes rather than on a derived scalar, since two different internal states can agree at the value you sampled.
AND WITNESS IT: mutate the kernel to the confusable operator, watch the suite go RED, revert, watch it go GREEN. A suite never observed to fail is not evidence that it constrains anything. This is the step that found all three.

THE THREE AFFECTED FAMILIES, each fixed and each proven by that RED/GREEN cycle:
  * `count_min` — counter addition confusable with max. Fixed by d7c4ff1 (monotone accumulation plus split/merge equivalence on canonical bytes). Before the fix all thirty tests passed under the mutation.
  * `degree_histogram` — same counter-addition kernel, same confusion. Fixed by 1d75e8f (`merge_is_additive_and_not_idempotent`). Proven GREEN 113 / RED 112+1 with only the new test failing.
  * `exact_quantiles` — ordered-merge kernel confusable with descending. Fixed by the commit carrying this comment (`merge_preserves_sorted_order_and_is_split_exact`). Proven GREEN 114 / RED 113+1. Order is not cosmetic here: `select` and `quantile` index into the values array, so an unsorted merge silently returns the WRONG QUANTILE rather than failing.

FAMILIES PROVEN CONSTRAINED, so nobody re-derives them: `label_counts` via its pre-existing `merge_is_deliberately_not_idempotent` — still the best starting point for anyone writing one of these; `distinct`, whose kernel IS max and correctly so, caught under max-to-overwrite; `zone_map`, caught under min-bound-to-max; `path_correlation`, caught under reversed sample selection; `bottom_k`, caught under keep-k-smallest-to-largest.

TWO INVALID PROBES, recorded so the evidence is not overcounted. I first probed `exact_quantiles` and `path_correlation` with "return early when the other operand is empty". Both passed, and that proves NOTHING — merging an empty operand should be identity, so the mutation is semantically equivalent and passing is correct. A mutation that does not change behaviour is not evidence in either direction. The real `exact_quantiles` defect only surfaced under a mutation that genuinely changes the result. Same discipline as a compile_fail doctest needing a must-compile companion.

STATUS: all three fixed; no family currently unconstrained under a class-appropriate mutation. The forward-looking action is the guard: any NEW mergeable sketch must ship a discriminating relation for its kernel's confusable pair, with a witnessed red run — not a commutativity/associativity/idempotence triple, which is satisfied by the wrong operator too.

comments.author: pane4-calibrate
comments.text:
CLOSING — all three affected families fixed and each proven by a witnessed red/green cycle. Commits: d7c4ff1 (count_min), 1d75e8f (degree_histogram), 06f29ae (exact_quantiles). Author: pane4-calibrate.

PER-FAMILY PROOF. Each kernel mutated to ITS OWN confusable operator, run against the full eight-family harness, probe binary deleted between runs so a build failure cannot masquerade as a pass:
  count_min         counter addition -> max          MUTATED 111 passed 1 failed   REVERTED 112 passed
  degree_histogram  counter addition -> max          MUTATED 112 passed 1 failed   REVERTED 113 passed
  exact_quantiles   ordered merge -> descending      MUTATED 113 passed 1 failed   REVERTED 114 passed
In every case EXACTLY ONE test fails — the newly added discriminating relation — and no other, which is what makes each failure attributable rather than incidental. The counts step 112/113/114 because each fix adds one test; they are sequential snapshots of one harness, not independent runs.
BEFORE the fixes, for contrast: count_min passed all 30 under its mutation, degree_histogram all 112, exact_quantiles all 113. That is what "the suite does not constrain the kernel" means concretely.

FINAL GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-sketch --locked = 122 passed 0 failed. rustfmt --check clean, ubs exit 0. Run under an exclusive build-2 hold, released immediately after.

PROVEN ALREADY-CONSTRAINED, so the fix set is exactly three and nobody re-checks them: label_counts (via its pre-existing merge_is_deliberately_not_idempotent — still the best model to copy); distinct (kernel IS max, correctly, caught under max->overwrite); zone_map (caught under min-bound->max); path_correlation (caught under reversed sample selection); bottom_k (caught under keep-k-smallest->largest).

THE GUARD, restated as the durable output: commutativity, associativity and idempotence cannot distinguish operators that all satisfy them, so a suite asserting only those constrains nothing about WHICH operator the kernel implements. Confusable pairs in this crate: sum/max for counters, min/max for bounds, keep-k-smallest/largest for selection, ascending/descending for ordered merges. Any new mergeable sketch needs a relation that SEPARATES its pair — non-idempotence under self-merge, mass conservation over a disjoint split, or an ordering assertion over INTERLEAVED runs — asserted on canonical bytes rather than a derived scalar, and witnessed by a red run.

TWO METHOD NOTES worth carrying, both paid for here. (1) Ask the question per kernel, not per crate: my first sweep probed every family with ONE mutation (addition->max), found it inapplicable to the collection kernels, and concluded no family remained. That was a scope error and it hid exact_quantiles for several ticks. (2) A semantically-equivalent mutation is not evidence: I probed exact_quantiles and path_correlation with "return early when the other operand is empty", both passed, and that proved nothing, because merging an empty operand SHOULD be identity. The real defect only surfaced under a mutation that genuinely changes the result.

title: Extend Local backup to multi-member Aegis with configuration-fenced pins and release
description:
## What & scope
Extend the exact Local backup barrier/pin/copy/reopen/closure/publication/release machinery into a multi-member Aegis consensus group without changing its manifest, inventory, recovery-projection, or independent-reopen semantics. This task owns configuration-fenced distributed barrier acquisition, member source-inventory/payload receipts, joint-configuration coverage, donor/failure-domain recoverability, all-member pin/GC coordination, leader-loss adoption, multi-member publication/release/abort, and the reusable group-level basis consumed by W12's separate Meta-plus-shard global backup.

## Why
Gate G2 needs a complete Local backup and must not wait for multi-member Raft. G3 needs the same guarantee across storage members and joint configuration. Separating the extension prevents reserved Sharded rows from forcing Aegis into G2 while preserving one format and one proof vocabulary: distribution adds certified participants and obligations, never a second backup truth or weaker reopen standard.

## Design — normative detail
A `ConsensusGroupBackupBarrierSpec` binds the Local-format semantic barrier plus exact `ConfigurationState`, stable or joint voter/storage-member sets, `ConfigPayloadFloor`, applied/visible/durable indexes, prepared-root generation, certificate ledger, GC epoch, key-wrap/signing epochs, payload predicate, failure-domain map, and required member set. Ordering it creates one group barrier identity and per-storage-member `MemberBackupPinRequest`; each accepted request roots the exact local physical/logical inventory under that member's current writer fence and configuration and returns a signed `MemberBackupPinReceipt` with inventory digest, durable index, fsync generation, encoding/placement coverage, and failure domain.

The coordinator forms `GroupBackupPinCertificate` only from the exact required stable/joint member predicate and a recoverable union of authenticated receipts. Joint configuration requires the registered old/new quorum and storage predicates; a bare majority or same epoch/member list is invalid. Prepared payload ownership and base closures remain rooted. A leader change adopts the durable operation by backup ID/configuration/fence and cannot issue a second barrier or lose a pin. Reconfiguration cannot retire a required member/configuration/key/payload floor while the group operation is live; consensus GC sees every member pin and terminal operation state as typed roots.

Copy and independent reopen use the existing content inventory, `BackupRecoveryProjection`, manifest, closure, and publication objects. The group certificate adds certified source coverage but does not enter the content inventory as a future/self edge. Publication/receipt/archive grant is one external operation over the sealed group manifest. Ordered release first proves independent archive recoverability and durable archive hold, then imports publication completion, releases every member pin through idempotent typed receipts, advances GC floors, and records one terminal group completion. Abort is legal only before publication send or with exact provider no-effect/terminal evidence; it releases all pins or none logically, with partial physical progress recovered to convergence.

W12 consumes this as the per-group layer. Its Meta intent, exact global prefix P, one certificate per required shard, and Global seal/finalize remain owned by `fgdb-w12-backup-restore-msk`; this task never claims cross-group atomicity.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-01 structured ownership/adoption; FG-INV-02 exclusive live generation; FG-INV-07 acyclic construction; FG-INV-09 same-group configuration binding; FG-INV-14 pins remain roots; FG-INV-15/16 exact obligation bijection and no lost/duplicate release; FG-INV-18 derived inventories remain subordinate. Recoverability and failure-domain calculations are bounded/configuration evidence, not universal invariants.

## Interactions
Depends on the Local backup core/publication/release tasks, W11 multi-member Raft, payload availability, membership configuration, fenced GC/physical execution, anti-entropy, W9 key/audit/time authority, and W2 transparency. W11 epic and Gate G3 consume it. W12 backup consumes its group certificate/pin/release interface but supplies separate cross-group sequencing and verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover stable/joint required-member calculation, receipt signature/config/fence binding, recoverability union, certificate canonical order, adoption/idempotency, typed-root registration, release/abort state totality, and exact reuse of Local manifest/reopen formats.
- Property/model tests vary member/configuration/failure-domain/receipt sets and prove certificate formation exactly matches the independent quorum+payload predicate oracle.
- Simulation explores leader loss, donor loss, member crash/restart, joint reconfiguration, GC pressure, key/time rotation, external sent-unknown publication, partial physical pin release, and cancellation at every obligation boundary; all runs converge to one terminal state with no unrooted required bytes.
- Negative tests reject mixed configurations, stale fences, duplicate member/failure-domain evidence, incomplete old/new joint coverage, nonrecoverable receipt sets, release-before-hold, GC of live pins, and accidental cross-group/W12 claims.
- E2E runs a three-member Local group under writes, takes a backup across leader change and joint reconfiguration, independently reopens it after simulated donor loss, publishes it through a simulated archive authority, releases pins, and proves current-root GC can retire only then. A second campaign aborts safely at each prepublication boundary.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics emit backup/group/configuration IDs, barrier positions, required/received member sets, member fence/fsync/inventory public commitments, failure-domain/recoverability calculation, prepared/payload floors, leader/adoption transitions, pin/GC roots, external dispatch/receipt state, per-member release state, checker verdict, artifact refs, seed, and replay command. Logs contain no keys, credentials, plaintext, protected locators, or hidden tenant facts.
- W12 conformance fixture proves this group layer composes under a Meta barrier without claiming or implementing the global layer here.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: making Local backup depend on multi-member Raft, one-leader copy without member receipts, majority-only payload assumptions, release on socket/provider timeout, and a separate distributed manifest. Risk: long backup pins impede reconfiguration/GC; explicit SLOs, admission, abort, and resumable adoption bound the operational cost without weakening safety.

## Provenance
Plan §14/W11 multi-member ownership and GC, §16.6 backup, §19 W11/G3 boundary, Appendix A backup/configuration/payload/GC formats.

title: Mechanical safe-facing API check: no public raw pointers, no public unsafe fn in any island
description:
Today this is a REVIEW property, asserted in three crate-root doc comments and
checked by nobody. With three islands landed it is now checkable and worth
checking: the whole point of an island is that safe crates consume it through
safe APIs, so a `pub unsafe fn` or a raw pointer in a public signature silently
moves the boundary outward without touching the ledger — and every existing
gate stays green, because the ledger only enumerates `allow` sites.

Scope: for each crate rostered in registries/unsafe_boundary_ledger.toml, reject
`pub unsafe fn`, and reject `*const`/`*mut` appearing in the signature of any
`pub fn`, in a `pub` field, or in a `pub type` alias.

Do it structurally, not by prefix. The precedent is in this bead's history: the
site scanner's first version matched the spelling `allow(` and walked past every
`cfg_attr`-wrapped site, and the manifest inheritance check asked whether the
text contained `[lints]` and `workspace = true` anywhere and was satisfied by a
comment. A `pub fn` whose signature wraps across lines, or a doc comment naming
`*mut`, will defeat a line-wise matcher the same way.

Vacuity: the check must FAIL, not skip, when it cannot read a source file or
parses zero public items in a crate that has some. Add a fixture island that
carries one violation of each kind and assert the exact code fires, plus the
clean control.
close_reason: Landed in e917efc: public_api structural reader + island_public_unsafe_fn / island_public_raw_pointer / island_public_api_unparsed / island_api_unscannable, wired into check_workspace and unsafe-ledger-check. Mutation-proved both directions on the real islands and on 16 new fixtures; four checker mutations go red on the tests that name them. Real workspace: 3 islands, 6 files, 104 public items, 0 findings.

title: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, the AGENTS.md-designated memorial for every doctrine violation, does not exist - so the looks-like-a-pass family stays invisible
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #5.

## What it claims

AGENTS.md, immediately above the eight constitutional doctrine items:

> "These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan.
>  Violating any of them is a revert, **memorialized in
>  `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md`**."

## What exists

`docs/` contains exactly three files:
  - `ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md`
  - `THREAT_AND_TRUST_MODEL.md`
  - `WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md`

`docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` does not exist and is referenced by nothing but the
sentence above.

## Why this is not merely a missing doc

2026-07-26 alone produced at least seven defects of one family — code that
presented as passing while standing in for a check it did not perform:

  1. a silently-disabled concurrency guard
  2. a source pin failing to the CONSTANT sha256("") (SC2033 / `xargs` on a
     shell function)
  3. `scripts/` exempt from every quality gate
  4. `ubs` exiting 0 on `.jsonl` while printing "this is NOT a pass"
  5. a `cfg_attr`-wrapped scanner bypass
  6. an allow-prefix match standing in for exact matching
  7. a substring test standing in for section parsing

Each was found, fixed, and — where a bead exists — recorded per-incident. None
is memorialized in the one place AGENTS.md designates for exactly this, because
that place does not exist. The consequence is that the FAMILY is invisible: any
reader of the doctrine sees eight rules and no evidence that the project has
ever caught itself breaking them, and each new agent rediscovers the pattern
from scratch. The value of negative evidence is precisely that it is aggregated.

The findings filed alongside this bead
(fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw,
fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o,
fgdb-orphan-w1-e2e-gates-unregistered-unrun-vuq8) are members of the same
family and should be its first entries.

## Which gate catches this today

None. `registries/checker_index.toml` has no row for it; nothing asserts that
paths named in AGENTS.md resolve. Related: fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq ("Generate
README/AGENTS as checked artifacts and run G0 self-containment checks") is the
natural home for the general law "every repo path AGENTS.md names must exist".

## Fix

1. Create `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` with a row schema: date, doctrine item
   violated, what the code claimed, what it did, how it was caught, the commit
   that reverted/repaired it, and — most valuable — the GENERALIZED signature so
   the next instance is recognized rather than rediscovered.
2. Backfill the seven above.
3. Add the self-containment law under fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq: every
   repository-relative path AGENTS.md names must resolve. That closes the class
   rather than this one instance.
notes:
LANDED: 37c28c0 (ledger + gate + registration), a3a5f8c (self-entries, floor 44). pane4.

VERIFIED, not assumed. docs/ held exactly three files; docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md did
not exist and AGENTS.md:86 was its ONLY reference in the tree. No ledger existed
under another name -- violation_witnesses.rs is about validator laws firing, an
unrelated artifact. The bead title held up.

MEASUREMENT (the part that reshapes the bead). Over all 705 commits: 1 produced by
`git revert`, 3 with any revert semantics, and ZERO of them a doctrine violation --
all three are beads bookkeeping (46e654e, 3a7248f, 1994b8e). AGENTS.md forbids the
mechanism its own clause requires: Backwards Compatibility mandates "just fix the
code directly". So a ledger keyed to REVERTS is empty forever while violations keep
happening -- decorative by construction. The real population is doctrine/enforcement
claims found FALSE: 44 now ledgered, every one previously recorded per-incident in a
bead and aggregated NOWHERE. Closest prior art was metamorphic.rs's header (ed70996),
which generalised 4 of one session's 7 and is invisible to any doctrine reader.

WHAT FAILS NOW. scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh, registered live (36->37 live
rows), and check.sh runs every live script row. Five laws: (0) the memorial exists;
(1) every repository path AGENTS.md names resolves, and the three named under "NEVER
create" must NOT -- the naive form would mandate plannerV2.rs; (2) well-formedness,
unique ids, seven fields, monotone floor 44; (3) every doctrine id / bead / repair
commit resolves (5/42/29 checked); (4) every revert-semantics commit has a structural
disposition. registry-check validate: 0 violations, checker_index 79 rows, liveness
licensed. shellcheck/bash -n clean.

RED-PROVED 13 of 13 mutations vs a green control on a depth-matched copy. The harness
paid for itself twice: the CONTROL caught a fail-open in law 1 (a tracked-but-deleted
file "resolved" via git ls-files), and law 4 DID NOT FIRE -- it was a whole-file
substring search that found the sha in the ledger's own preamble prose. That is
NE-0001..0004 (substring standing in for structural parsing) a FIFTH time, committed
inside the gate that memorializes the class. Review missed it; mutation found it.
Both fixed, both now fire. Ledgered as NE-0044.

LAW 1 WAS NON-VACUOUS ON ARRIVAL -- it found a SECOND dangling path: AGENTS.md said
bv computes over `.beads/beads.jsonl`, which has NEVER been tracked here (bv reads
the beads DB; the export is issues.jsonl). Corrected to `.beads/`. Ledgered NE-0043.

RESIDUE / NEXT STEP, in priority order:
1. The AGENTS.md sentence should be re-keyed from "is a revert" to "is memorialized",
   because the measurement above shows the revert-keyed reading can never populate.
   I did NOT edit the doctrine sentence -- that is a constitutional edit and is the
   orchestrator's call. This is the single highest-value follow-up.
2. NOT ENFORCED, and said so in both the ledger and the gate rather than left looking
   like coverage: a violation found, repaired and closed with NO entry added is
   invisible to all five laws. Total accounting over closed beads WOULD catch it and
   would also red main every few minutes in a 7-pane swarm and make the ledger a
   contended write for every agent (the closed count moved 105->108 while I worked --
   the churn is measured, not hypothetical). A text classifier over bead prose fails
   open, which is the very class this ledger records. Gate reports the residue as a
   count instead. Revisit when the swarm quiesces.
3. coverage_of() in check.sh maps `registries/*.toml` to "registry-check all", but
   there is NO registries/ directory closure law (validate.rs's read_dir is
   scripts-closure only). A NEW registry file would inherit a coverage claim nobody
   backs. Same family as tl0o/u7mw. Not filed as a bead -- creating one moves the
   provenance pins.

NO BEAD CREATED for any residue above, deliberately: a br create breaks the
provenance pins for every pane.

title: Normative source edit required: self-referencing predecessor_ref on thirteen plan lines
description:
## What & scope
The normative plan spells a lineage predecessor as a self-referencing retaining wrapper on THIRTEEN Appendix A lines. No such member can be modelled as a durable field row in any shape, so every slice holding one is permanently blocked at its last mile. Resolving this requires editing `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md`, which is the project's single source of truth and the repo owner's decision under the AGENTS.md spec-first workflow. This bead exists so that decision can be made without re-deriving any of the analysis. No agent should make this edit unilaterally.

## Why this cannot be resolved in the catalog
`source_complete_census_uncovered` names its own three discharge routes for an uncovered census field key: a TARGET, an approved ADJUDICATION, or a covering ARM/WIRE INTERIOR contract. All three were measured against HEAD, read-only.

ROUTE 1 — A TARGET ROW. BLOCKED, established on fgdb-u3gr. `catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch` derives the legal `reference_semantics` from the concrete wrapper in the census `exact_type`, so a `StrongRef<Self>` source FORCES `strong` — probed across all five candidate values, `strong` is the only one that does not fire. `dag_self_edge` forbids exactly that, and its filter covers strong, conditional and weak_digest alike. Strong is forced by one law and forbidden by the other; every alternative is rejected by the first before reaching the second. Order-independent: the self-edge check returns before `construction_order` is compared, and equal orders are legal anyway.

ROUTE 2 — AN APPROVED ADJUDICATION. CLOSED, and this is the measurement that settles it. An adjudication is keyed to a RAW CENSUS AMBIGUITY. Searching every raw ambiguity in the appendix:
    raw ambiguities touching TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref ....... 0
    raw ambiguities touching PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref ...................... 0
    CONTROL: total raw ambiguities across the whole appendix ....................... 8,423
A `StrongRef<Self>?` member is perfectly unambiguous — the census parses it exactly, which is precisely why it yields nothing to adjudicate. An adjudication row without a matching raw ambiguity is not merely inert: `source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved` requires one approved final adjudication per raw ambiguity "and no extras", so the row would itself fire and the slice ambiguity census pin would move against it. Adding a new `erratum` resolution VALUE does not help either, because the blocker is not which value the row carries — it is that there is no ambiguity for the row to key against. That would be a vocabulary widening that admits nothing.

ROUTE 3 — A COVERING ARM/WIRE INTERIOR CONTRACT. The only route that remains, and it requires the SOURCE to spell the member as a closed union, because an arm payload digest creates no DAG edge. That is the plan edit this bead requests.

## Measurement instrument, and a gap it closed
The two source-pass laws had been recorded on the trail as "read, not measured", because `load_and_verify` runs the source pass only when `validate_catalog` returns empty, and flipping any slice to `complete` makes `validate_catalog` return hundreds of violations — so `appendix_a_catalog_source` never ran. Fix: arm the slices IN MEMORY on a loaded `Catalog` and call `appendix_a::appendix_a_catalog_source(&cat, &source)` directly, bypassing the metadata gate. Both are `pub`.
    CONTROL, nothing armed .......... 0 violations
    a10 + a16 armed ................. 1,014 violations
                                      (1,012 source_complete_census_uncovered
                                       + 2 source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved)
Emitted verbatim for the a16 host:
    source_complete_census_uncovered  a16
      complete slice census field key "field|TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>|
      TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref|predecessor_ref"
      has no target, approved adjudication, or covering arm/wire interior contract
NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-MEASURING: through the ORDINARY loader, arming a10+a16 names `predecessor_ref` NOWHERE. The completion battery iterates landed targets, and these members have no field row and no target row, so nothing iterates over them. The armed-catalog recipe alone reads this defect as clean when it is not.

## The exact edit requested — 13 lines, current text and proposed replacement
Each line's EXACT current fragment (verified to match byte-for-byte, 13 of 13) and its proposed replacement:

    line 1486  LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>?
    line 1524  TxnOutcomeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>?
    line 1698  MetaPreparedCommandRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaPreparedCommandRecord>?
    line 1700  ShardPreparedPayloadRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPreparedPayloadRecord>?
    line 1720  GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>?
    line 1782  GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>?
    line 1832  AuditTerminalFreezeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>?
    line 1850  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalAttemptRecord>?
    line 1854  ShardPrepareRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPrepareRecord>?
    line 1856  ConstraintReservationRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ConstraintReservationRecord>?
    line 1858  MetaConstraintReservationRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConstraintReservationRecord>?
    line 1922  PreparedCommitRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>?
    line 2191  TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>?

    PROPOSED REPLACEMENT, identical in form for every one of the 13:
      predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest}

    PLUS, stated normatively adjacent to each:
      "Its predecessor digest authenticates generation adjacency but is comparison-only
       and is never traversed by reachability/GC, checkpoint, or backup walkers."

    PLUS, main body line 392 (outside the Appendix slice manifest):
      "record_generation, predecessor_ref, ..."  ->  "record_generation, predecessor, ..."
      "its typed references and predecessor are strong."
        ->  "its typed references are strong; its predecessor digest is nonretaining and
             comparison-only."

    PLUS, for line 2191 only, to preserve target ownership: tighten the existing index
    sentence to say TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role> strongly owns each current
    generation via StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>. Without this the
    reference census loses the schema as a target and its already-issued
    reservation/source disposition orphans; with it, target count and hash stay stable.

## Why this shape, not a shorter one
A direct `nonretaining_predecessor_digest:WeakDigest?` is NOT a complete source-only fix: the annotation law correctly derives `weak_digest`, but the construction-DAG loop also rejects a weak_digest self target, so omitting the target would make the annotation incomplete rather than fix the law. A closed union whose `Prior` arm carries an untraversed WeakDigest is the form that discharges via route 3.
Three landed precedents in these same families are already spelled non-retaining, which is exactly why they were landable — the 13 are the outliers against their own families:
  * `PreparedRootHeader<Role>` (a01:1694) carries `nonretaining_predecessor_digest` — the same prepared-root family as the a10 host.
  * `LocalCommandOrigin.Prior` uses `ConditionalCommandRef`, landed as "conditional (cuttable) reference to the predecessor LogicalCommandRecord; retention governed by checkpoint cuts (FG-INV-14)".
  * `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord.predecessor` (a16:2237) is a source-level closed union `Genesis|Prior` landed as `reference_semantics="none"` with the Prior arm weak-digest-bound.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness
`durable_fields.toml` is, per plan:292, "the sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure, construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers." A retaining predecessor edge makes every ancestor in an append-only generational chain permanently reachable — precisely what checkpoint cuts and retention floors exist to prevent. The three precedents avoid this deliberately.

## Costed blast radius (from the fgdb-u3gr 09:59 analysis, for the narrow a10+a16 pair)
Census movement for two fields: remove 2 field keys; add 4 field keys (two union anchors plus two nested `.Prior.record_digest`); add 2 union keys and 4 arm keys; re-key 1 a16 ambiguity adjudication; no schema keys move and no target keys move; reference-source occurrences 2458 -> 2457 with target count stable at 813. Slice blast radius: source bytes change in the affected slices only; the global Appendix source manifest sha changes; affected `[[slice]]` byte/hash and structural-census pins change; line ranges do not change and every other `[[slice]]` row stays byte-valid. Extending from 2 lines to 13 scales the field/union/arm movement proportionally and widens the set of slices whose pins must be re-frozen.

## A DISCREPANCY I AM DISCLOSING RATHER THAN RESOLVING
fgdb-u3gr's own population figure is "10 members across 7 slices", naming a03 LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration; a06 MetaPreparedCommandRecord, ShardPreparedPayloadRecord; a08 MetaConstraintReservationRecord, ShardPrepareRecord, TopologyTransitionRecord; a10 PreparedCommitRecord; a13 KeyEnvelopeNode; a16 TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>; a21 WitnessPolicy. My count is 13, on a different basis: I counted RAW SOURCE LINES carrying the literal `predecessor_ref:StrongRef<Self>?` spelling, whereas that figure was a measured MEMBER population. The two lists are not nested — mine adds TxnOutcomeRecord, GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration, GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord, AuditTerminalFreezeRecord, AuditTerminalAttemptRecord and ConstraintReservationRecord; theirs adds TopologyTransitionRecord, KeyEnvelopeNode and WitnessPolicy, which self-reference under DIFFERENT member names (`copy_record_ref`, `child_ref`, `predecessor_policy_ref`) and are therefore the same hazard class but outside the `predecessor_ref` spelling this bead is scoped to. Someone should reconcile the two before the edit is made; I did not, and the ruling should cover whichever population the owner intends. I also ran a broader scan for all self-referencing StrongRef members and got 163 hits, but that scan is OVER-BROAD and must not be used — its line-level heuristic cannot distinguish a genuine self-edge from a sibling reference sharing one dense definition line. The 13 are sound because a member named `predecessor_ref:StrongRef<X>` inside X's own definition is unambiguous.

## Success Criteria
- The repo owner rules on whether to amend the plan, and over which population (the 13 `predecessor_ref` lines, the 10-member measured set, or the union of both).
- If amended: source edited, the adjacent normative comparison-only sentence added, main-body line 392 amended, the a16 index-ownership sentence tightened, the global source manifest and all affected slice pins re-frozen in the same commit.
- `appendix_a_catalog_source` with the affected slices armed no longer reports `source_complete_census_uncovered` for any `predecessor_ref` key.
- fgdb-u3gr closes, unblocking fgdb-a16-time-authority-ytub and fgdb-a10-command-delta-ooy1.

## Provenance
Measured read-only against HEAD by cc_2/pane3-u3gr. Full derivation, probe recipe and controls are on the fgdb-u3gr trail. No remedy is authorized by this bead; it records a decision request.
