title: historical witness removal set is incomplete w.r.t. its own transcript; the A10 pin was already re-pinned once
description:
Found while fixing fgdb-bw2x (68661aa). The repair there was correct but narrow; this is the general defect underneath it, and it WILL recur.

THE GAP. identity::assignment_pins builds the durable_fields transcript from FOUR
components: field rows, reference unions (r.unions) with their arms, and ordinary
unions (r.ordinary_unions) with their arms. The historical witness in
idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen only ever retains two of them --
pre_erratum.fields and pre_erratum.ordinary_unions -- and its two cohort asserts
count fields and count unions.

Consequences, both measured:
 - r.unions (reference unions) is NEVER filtered and NEVER counted. It happens to
   be identical green-vs-HEAD today (13 transcript lines each side), so nothing has
   tripped it yet. That is luck, not a guard.
 - An ordinary union's ARMS are hashed but not counted. A post-erratum union left
   in the reconstruction moves the pin through its arm lines while the union count
   moves by one and the field count does not move at all. That is exactly how
   81ccbce went unnoticed: three arms of LocalConstraintReservationRecordState.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE RED. The failure surfaces only as an opaque
fnv1a64 mismatch with no indication of which component drifted. Diagnosing it cost
a full per-commit bisect (build each commit's own lib+test, ~12s each) because no
assert narrows it. 68661aa added an inline NOTE to the assert message naming the
four components and saying do-not-re-pin, which makes the next occurrence
diagnosable but does not make it DETECTABLE at the right place.

THE PRIOR RE-PIN, which is the reason to treat this as P1.
A10_COMMAND_REF_ERRATUM_PREVIOUS_FIELDS_PIN has already been moved once:
  5b76722  introduced  fnv1a64:bdbcdc27ccd92518
  8a704c2  changed to  fnv1a64:236efa5babe190fe
8a704c2 is 'fix(a02): register filesystem cipher physical fields' -- a landing
commit, not a witness-maintenance commit. So the first occurrence of this defect
class was closed by moving the pin to the observed value instead of extending the
removal set, which is precisely what the witness exists to prevent. I did NOT
unwind it in 68661aa: the current pin is load-bearing for the current
reconstruction and unwinding it is a separate, evidence-heavy job.

PROPOSED WORK, in order:
 1. Add a cohort assert for r.unions (count + a named removal filter) so a landed
    reference union fails LOUDLY at the count rather than silently in the hash.
 2. Add an arm-level cohort assert for ordinary unions, so arm drift is separable
    from union drift.
 3. Decide, on evidence, whether 236efa5b can be re-derived from the true
    pre-erratum namespace or whether bdbcdc27 was the last honest value. Until (3)
    is settled, treat 236efa5b as a floor that must not move again.
Controls for (1) and (2) must FIRE: land a throwaway reference union / arm in a
scratch copy and confirm the new assert names it.

title: Implement fgdb doctor + online ops verbs: verification probes and model-qualified reports
description:
## What & scope
Implement the §16.4 ops verbs — online `COMPACT`, `SCRUB`, `REBUILD INDEX`, `ANALYZE` — and the `fgdb doctor` verification tool with its full check list, filesystem-profile probes, configuration-model reporting, support bundles, and cancellation-progress surfaces.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: doctor is the operator-facing edge of the evidence system — it verifies exactly what the registries claim and labels every model-derived judgment as such, so an operator can distinguish "this store violates an invariant" from "this deployment profile fails its modeled durability target". Market: embedded/single-binary databases live or die by their doctor story (SQLite's integrity_check precedent); an agent-native database needs it machine-consumable (B6).

## Design — normative detail
Doctor check list (§16.4, exact): `fgdb doctor` verifies root slots, closure, full digests/encodings, marker/branch continuity, constraint state, key wraps, payload availability, GC epoch, and model-qualified configuration reports. Ops verbs run online: `COMPACT`/`SCRUB`/`REBUILD INDEX`/`ANALYZE` are admission-controlled maintenance, never stop-the-world.

Filesystem-profile probes (§5.1/w2 contract, exact): `fgdb doctor --write-profile` performs a scratch-directory conformance probe against the registered profile's allowed kernel/filesystem/mount/device assumptions and probe-suite version, while ordinary open repeats the mount, stable-inode, and option checks — doctor is the *full* probe, open is the fast recheck. Configuration-model gating (exact): `fgdb doctor` may reject a deployment profile below its modeled MTTDL target (`FG-CFG-01`), but the result is labeled a configuration-model gate rather than an invariant — the report must carry the CTMC/model version, fitted failure rates, failure domains, sensitivity bounds, repair/backup assumptions, and per-tier `fec_profile` reconstruction and checkpoint-fold recode paths per the FG-CFG-01 disclosure row. Resource-leak surfacing (§13): a result whose retention expires unconsumed surfaces as a debug-mode `ResourceWarning` and a doctor/metrics counter rather than a silent leak.

Support bundles carry replay-completeness/redaction grades. Cancellation exposes phase and deterministic drain progress; any probabilistic remaining-work/stall estimate names its model and is not a quiescence proof — quiescence is asserted only when obligations and resource ledgers reach their exact terminal state. Doctor output is dual-mode: human text and machine-readable JSON with one record per check `{check_id, claim_class: invariant|registry|slo|config-model|evidence, verdict, model_disclosure?}` so agents can consume it (B6).

## Invariants & claim types
Doctor *checks* invariants but its own novel judgments are never invariants. Claim classes it must label: invariant-class verdicts (root slots, closure, digests/encodings, marker/branch continuity, constraint state, key wraps — exact pass/fail against registered obligations); registry-class (format/identity registry conformance); config-model class (`FG-CFG-01` modeled MTTDL >= declared target with sensitivity bounds for every shipped profile — crash/restore tests remain separate empirical evidence; `FG-CFG-02` controller-stability default checks); evidence class (`FG-EVID-02` scrub/corpus-health: population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position and observed corruption).

## Interactions
Probes and profile registry from `w2-filesystem-profiles`; root-slot/closure verification against `w2-root-bootstrap`; scrub + MTTDL model from `w2-fec-scrub`; constraint state from `w4-constraints`; key wraps/epochs from `w9-key-lifecycle`; payload availability from `w11-payload-availability`; counters/bundles via `obs-observatory`. `verif-torture` reuses doctor as its post-crash validity oracle; `obs-slo` consumes doctor counters; deployment gates (§16.6) invoke doctor in drills.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Seeded-corruption matrix: for each check domain (root slot torn, closure gap, digest mismatch, marker discontinuity, branch-continuity break, constraint-state divergence, bad key wrap, missing payload symbol, stale GC epoch) doctor must fail exactly that check with actionable location detail; a healthy store passes all. (2) Probe tests: `--write-profile` on a conforming and a nonconforming mount (wrong options, unstable inodes) — accept/reject respectively; open-path recheck catches a profile change since last open. (3) FG-CFG-01 rejection test: profile below modeled target is rejected with the full disclosure set and labeled config-model, not invariant. (4) Ops-verb tests: each verb runs online under load; foreground latency impact recorded (feeds law 3); cancellation mid-verb exposes phase + drain progress and resumes/aborts cleanly. (5) JSON-mode schema tests + one e2e script that crashes a store, runs doctor, collects a support bundle, and verifies replay-completeness/redaction grades — all steps logged with check ids and timings.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: doctor drift from registry evolution — checks are generated from the registries where possible, mirroring the projection discipline. Risk: config-model verdicts read as invariants — mandatory claim-class labels in both output modes. Rejected: offline-only maintenance verbs; a doctor that "repairs" silently (verify + report; repair is an explicit separate verb path); quiescence/stall estimates as proofs.

## Provenance
§16.4 (1192); filesystem-profile probe clause (line 362 context); FG-CFG-01 doctor clause (line 484 context); §13 ResourceWarning clause (line 992 context); Appendix F FG-CFG-01/FG-EVID-02.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build fgdb-observatory: metrics/traces/crashpacks, early-warning monitors, redaction
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-observatory` and the `ObservatoryRegion` (metrics export, task inspector, spectral health, deadline monitor): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN`/`SHOW` surfaces, the §16.3 early-warning monitor suite, crashpacks/support bundles, and the secret-hygiene redaction contract across all telemetry outputs.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: observability is where evidence discipline either holds or leaks — every estimate here is model-qualified, every claim class respected, every secret redacted. Operationally this is the difference between a database operators trust under incident pressure and one that lies with averages. The Observatory also underwrites the perf program: law 3 (never hide compaction) and law 4 (memory census) need these counters, and support bundles feed replay-based debugging (B5's replayability).

## Design — normative detail
`ObservatoryRegion` sits under `FgdbRootRegion` beside the eight subsystem regions (Chronicle/Strata/Ripple/Beacon/Prism/Warden/Aegis/Fabric), Spork-supervised with declared restart topology. Telemetry (§16.2, exact): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN`, and `SHOW` surfaces cover transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, and commit phases. Little's-law checks and shadow prices are diagnostics under stationarity/model assumptions and live in evidence/SLO registries, not the safety-invariant registry.

Early warning (§16.3, exact): wait-graph, futurelock, autocorrelation/variance, and coupled-controller monitors provide model-qualified alerts. `FG-CFG-02` rejects defaults predicted unstable by a versioned fluid model with sensitivity analysis; it does not claim every real workload lies in that model. Hard safety comes from bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls — never from monitors. The early-warning wait-cycle probe is owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check, so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead (`fgdb-prism`) for an alerting primitive.

Crashpacks & support bundles: support bundles carry replay-completeness/redaction grades. Cancellation exposes phase and deterministic drain progress; any probabilistic remaining-work/stall estimate names its model and is not a quiescence proof — quiescence is asserted only when obligations and resource ledgers reach their exact terminal state. Secret hygiene (binding contract from §8.6/§12): production `seed_bytes` and equivalent secrets are redacted from debug formatting, metrics, audit payloads, errors, crashpacks, core-dump profiles, and decision cards, and synchronously overwritten on every success/error/cancel/panic ownership path. Trace context crosses process boundaries only in authorized/redacted form per capability (§12.6). Telemetry is never authority: "neither local session counters nor telemetry are quota authority" (§16.6) — Observatory reads ledgers, it never substitutes for them.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created; the binding rule is classification: monitor outputs are diagnostics; `FG-CFG-02` (modeled controller stability — must disclose model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards and soak results) is an `slo.toml` configuration-model claim; scrub/corpus-health surfacing follows `FG-EVID-02` (population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position and observed corruption). Any output that could be mistaken for a safety claim must carry its claim class in the schema.

## Interactions
Substrate for `obs-system-graph` (which materializes these domains as a graph), `obs-doctor` (verification reports), `obs-slo` (alert wiring). Consumes claim classes from `g0-claim-registries`, core types from `w1-foundation-types`, sketches/e-process primitives for spectral/autocorrelation monitors from `w1-sketch-calibrate`, redaction/authorization enforcement from `w9-enforcement` and `w9-redaction-erasure`. Every subsystem region exports into it; `perf-bench-*` consume its compaction/memory counters; `verif-replay-products` consumes support-bundle grades.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) `SHOW` surface integration tests cover all nine enumerated §16.2 domains — transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, commit phases — with stable schemas. (2) Redaction property tests: a corpus of secret-bearing states formatted through every output path (metrics, errors, crashpacks, traces, decision cards) never leaks a seed byte — fuzzed with `w1-crypto`-style secret markers; leak = release-blocking. (3) Wait-cycle probe unit tests: bounded cycle check finds seeded cycles within its bound and degrades declared (bound exhaustion is reported, not silent); proven to have no `fgdb-prism` dependency by crate-graph CI check. (4) Monitor model-qualification tests: every alert payload names rule id, model version, assumptions, sensitivity; an unqualified alert is a schema failure. (5) Quiescence tests: probabilistic drain estimator output cannot flip a quiescence flag; only exact terminal ledger state can — asserted under cancellation torture. (6) Support-bundle e2e: crash a workload, collect bundle, verify replay-completeness and redaction grades present and correct.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: telemetry overhead perturbs the benches — sampled under load with bounded cardinality. Risk: monitors ossify into implicit SLAs — claim-class stamping prevents promotion. Rejected: importing Prism for alerting-path analytics (bulkhead violation, registered rejection); global unredacted debug modes; quiescence from estimators.

## Provenance
§16.1-16.4 (1177-1192), §16.5 probe-ownership clause (1193), §16.6 authority clause (1194), secret-hygiene clause (line 924 context), Appendix F FG-CFG-02/FG-EVID-02 (3159, 3161).

title: Wire slo.toml into Observatory: keyed SLO rows, model-qualified alerts, attribution
description:
## What & scope
Wire the `slo.toml` registry into the running system: load keyed SLO rows, evaluate them against Observatory telemetry, raise model-qualified alerts, and attribute every breach to its operation class, plane segment, authority, or maintenance-stream cause. This bead owns the runtime SLO plane; the registry files themselves are `g0-claim-registries` artifacts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the claim-type constitution says every microsecond/throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}` — this bead makes those rows operational instead of documentary, closing the loop between §17's gates (CI-time) and production alerting (run-time) over the *same* rows. Attribution is the agent-native (B6) requirement: an alert that names its breached row, its Appendix G class, and its causal segment is actionable by an agent; a bare threshold ping is not.

## Design — normative detail
Registry split (exact, from §15.0/G0): `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets. SLO rows this bead must wire: (a) every §17 gate value, keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; (b) §16.8's per-posture availability numbers for the three lines — apply-durability, visibility, delivery — which are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants, tracked by the §20 authority-availability risk row; (c) §9.5's delivery-latency bound, claim-typed `slo` because delivery is hostage to the audit-visibility pipeline, external resolution RTT, and time-evidence activation, none of which the delivery plane may bypass; (d) per-tenant ticket-resolution SLOs at the external audit authority — an `slo.toml` surface, not a pipeline change (the audit-stall isolation unit is the database; intra-database per-tenant audit-visibility domains are a registered rejection); (e) `FG-CFG-03` view/index staleness feasibility (arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark and fallback policy) and `FG-CFG-04` head-of-line budgets; (f) `FG-EVID-04` derived-state freshness rows with typed `FreshnessBreach` rates.

Alerting rules: every alert names its row key, claim class, model (if model-derived: version + assumptions + sensitivity, per §16.3's model-qualified alert doctrine), and current fallback state. Attribution: latency breaches decompose along the Appendix G barrier chain of the row's operation class (which plane, which barrier, which external authority); Required-class breaches decompose into the two governance plane segments (order-accepted->released vs released->first-byte) mirroring `perf-bench-governance`'s additive decomposition; maintenance-interference breaches attribute user-commit p99 degradation to (N,M,R,k,tau) via the FG-CFG-04 model; freshness breaches name their audit-pipeline/time-evidence dependencies per FG-EVID-04; alerts link to system-graph node ids (`obs-system-graph`) so the breach's live waits/jobs are one query away. SLO evaluation is diagnostic-plane only: it can never gate admission, shed load, or assert safety — hard behavior stays with bounded queues, reservations, and deterministic backpressure.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row; the constitutional rule enforced here is the negative one: nothing evaluated by this bead may be represented, logged, or exported as an invariant, and an `slo.toml` row can never migrate into `invariants.toml` via alert config. FG-CFG-03/04 disclosure text as above; FG-EVID-04 (slo-class, never an invariant): bound in watermark/commit-sequence units, audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies named, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy.

## Interactions
Rows/claim classes from `g0-claim-registries`; operation classes + barrier chains for attribution from `g0-cost-registry`; telemetry substrate from `obs-observatory`; three-line availability doctrine and footprint table from `w9-authority-surface`; `FreshnessBreach` events from `w6-freshness`; breach->graph links into `obs-system-graph`. `perf-bench-*` beads and this bead share row definitions — CI baseline and production alert must reference the same row id, so a gate change automatically retunes alerting.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Loader round-trip: every `slo.toml` row parses to a typed key `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; unknown operation classes fail startup (registry coherence). (2) Alert e2e: inject latency at a named barrier (fault-injection via the sim harness); alert fires naming row, class, barrier-level attribution; logs carry row id, measured vs budget, decomposition table. (3) Governance decomposition test: stall the simulated audit authority; visibility-line alert fires attributed to the audit authority while the apply-durability line stays green — verifying the three-lines-never-one-product rule. (4) Freshness test: induce watermark lag; FG-EVID-04 alert carries realized lag distribution and FreshnessBreach rate. (5) Negative test: SLO evaluator provably cannot trigger admission/shedding paths (no such dependency edge, CI crate check) and its outputs are stamped diagnostic. (6) Head-of-line test: raise N x M until the FG-CFG-04 budget breaches; alert attributes to maintenance-stream parameters.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: alert storms under correlated breaches — attribution collapses correlated child alerts under their common cause. Risk: silent divergence between CI gate rows and alert rows — single row-id source. Rejected: SLO-driven automatic remediation (safety stays deterministic); availability as one multiplied product (three lines mandated); per-tenant audit-visibility pipelines (registered rejection — W12-scale redesign, not an additive registry change; the mitigation is per-tenant ticket-resolution SLOs at the authority plus §12.8's reserved capacity and pipeline limits).

## Provenance
§15.0 registry split (line 1118 context); §16.2-16.3 (1190-1191); §16.8 (1222-1228); §9.5 slo clause (line 802 context); §17 gate values; Appendix F FG-CFG-03/04, FG-EVID-04; §20 authority-availability row (line 1378 context).

title: Expose the system graph: queryable ops surface + Prism FeatureDisabled degraded mode
description:
## What & scope
Implement §16.5 as the dedicated `fgdb-system-graph` crate (§18.1, Surface/operations layer): the database's own runtime exposed as a read-only, access-controlled *temporal property graph* queryable in GQL, with Prism-powered analyses over it, the declared `FeatureDisabled` degraded mode, and the Observatory-owned wait-cycle probe kept independent of the analytics bulkhead.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 made concrete: the database dogfoods its data model as its ops surface. Agents and operators debug FrankenGraphDB with FrankenGraphDB — `MATCH (q:Query)-[:WAITS_FOR]->(x) WHERE q.elapsed_ms > 250 RETURN q, x` — instead of learning a bespoke admin API. B4/B1: incidents become subgraphs you can diff across time because the graph is temporal. B5: the degraded mode is typed and registered, never silent, preserving evidence discipline even when features are off.

## Design — normative detail
Graph contents (exact): sessions, transactions, queries, plans, operators, snapshots + leases, obligations, segments, compaction jobs, subscriptions, replication streams, repairs, decision cards — a read-only, access-controlled temporal property graph, queryable in GQL like any other graph. The wait-for graph is literally a graph: deadlock and contention analysis run Prism's own cycle detection and centrality over it, and incidents become subgraphs diffable across time. Cardinality is bounded, sampled under load, redacted per capability (§12.6).

Degraded mode (exact, normative): with `fgdb-prism` disabled by its posture/feature activation predicate, the system graph remains a queryable read-only temporal property graph, while the fnx-backed analyses over it — wait-for cycle detection, centrality, incident diffing — return a typed `FeatureDisabled` error rather than degrading silently, with the corresponding feature-disable registry row recorded per G0's per-clause rule. Nothing safety-bearing degrades with them: deadlock and starvation safety come from §16.3's bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls, and the §16.3 early-warning wait-cycle probe is owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check, so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead for an alerting primitive.

Separation of duties: `fgdb-system-graph` is a *projection* of Observatory state (`fgdb-observatory` is the substrate; the crate holds no second bookkeeping system); queries run through the ordinary Loom path under ordinary authorization, so plan certificates, decision cards, and redaction apply to ops queries exactly as to user queries. Prism analyses run inside the `PrismRegion` bulkhead (`w8-scheduling`) so an expensive centrality run over a huge wait graph cannot starve user work.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created. Binding rules restated: (a) safety never depends on this surface — deadlock/starvation safety is carried by bounded queues, reservations, cancellation checkpoints, deterministic fallbacks; (b) the `FeatureDisabled` behavior plus its feature-disable registry row is claim-typed under G0's per-clause activation contract (each disabled clause records which registered claims deactivate with it); (c) all exposed quantities inherit their source claim classes (diagnostics stay diagnostics even when rendered as graph properties).

## Interactions
Deliverable crate: `fgdb-system-graph` (§18.1). Builds on `obs-observatory` (source domains, wait-cycle probe stays there); GQL execution via `w5-executor`; Prism analyses gated by `w8-scheduling`'s bulkhead; access control and capability-scoped redaction from `w9-enforcement`; feature-disable registry rows per `g0-claim-registries`' clause-activation contract. `obs-slo` links alerts to system-graph node ids for attribution; incident tooling and `verif-replay-products` consume incident subgraphs.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) E2E: run a contended workload, execute the canonical wait-for GQL query, verify returned waits match ground truth from the scheduler's own records; logs include query text, capability, redactions applied. (2) Degraded-mode e2e: disable `fgdb-prism` via its activation predicate; plain GQL over the system graph still answers; cycle-detection/centrality/incident-diff calls return typed `FeatureDisabled` (assert error type, not a generic failure); the feature-disable registry row is present; re-enabling restores analyses. (3) Crate-graph CI: `fgdb-observatory` has no dependency edge to `fgdb-prism`; the wait-cycle probe passes its bounded-cycle unit tests independently. (4) Redaction tests: a low-capability session sees redacted query text/parameters in the graph; property fuzzing for leak paths. (5) Temporal diff test: capture incident subgraph at t1/t2, diff, verify changed edges. (6) Bulkhead test: a deliberately expensive centrality run is admission-bounded and cannot degrade user-commit p99 beyond the declared budget (logged both sides).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ops-surface cardinality explosion under incident load — bounded cardinality with declared sampling, so the graph degrades by disclosure rather than by OOM. Risk: the surface becomes a privilege-escalation channel — ordinary authorization path, capability redaction, read-only. Rejected: bespoke admin RPCs instead of the graph (violates B6 dogfooding); silent no-op when Prism is off (must be typed `FeatureDisabled` + registry row); Observatory importing Prism for its probe (registered rejection).

## Provenance
§16.5 (line 1193); §16.3 hard-safety clause (1191); §12.6 redaction; §18.1 `fgdb-system-graph` crate row (1293); G0 per-clause feature-disable rule.

title: Wire RegionAlloc into ART/succinct/hash storage and run the collections_e2e matrix
description:
fgdb-unsafe-arena landed with `RegionAlloc` as the seam ART, succinct, and hash
storage are meant to be parameterized over. NOTHING is wired to it. The site's
no_claim_boundary says so explicitly, so the trait's existence must not be read
as an integration — this bead is that integration.

Scope, from the parent's remainder item 9: allocator-parameterize the three
consumers, then run the original collections_e2e matrix — ART plus the
edit-distance oracle, target-vector hash join plus an independent map oracle,
succinct rank/select, scalar/target dispatch parity across two seeds, and the
region cancellation/reclamation logs.

Two constraints that are easy to lose:

* The named probe-latency and ART point/range benchmark rows stay CONSUMER
  benchmark-class claims. An island microbenchmark must not be presented as
  proving them, and the arena's ledger row attaches no benchmark at all.
* `bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated` must hold on the CANCELLATION path as
  well as on close, under the consumers' real allocation patterns rather than
  the island's unit fixtures. An arena that balances only on the happy path
  leaks exactly when a query is cancelled mid-build.

title: Systemic: 42 symbols carry a jointly-unsatisfiable construction_order, 35 already frozen
description:
A sweep of every symbol the Appendix A source constrains in BOTH reference directions finds 42 whose
construction_order is jointly unsatisfiable: the maximum order among the targets its own body
StrongRefs exceeds the minimum order among the rows that StrongRef it. No value satisfies
`projection_dag_future_result` in both directions.

  42  total
   4  BIND TODAY — the loader already rejects every value
  38  LATENT — the loader accepts values today that the source forbids
  35  are ALREADY-LANDED logical kinds, so the contradiction is frozen behind the append-only
      assignment pin and cannot be corrected by choosing a different order

WHY LATENT IS THE DANGEROUS HALF. `projection_dag_future_result` evaluates the LANDED field-row
graph. A kind minted before its field rows exist has no outbound edges the checker can see, so any
order below its ceiling passes every gate. The contradiction only surfaces when someone lands that
kind's own body — at which point the order is pinned and the correction is expensive. Two beads were
already parked as individual errata for exactly this, fgdb-tuw1 (GlobalTxnCommand, floor 40 against
ceiling 30) and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x (CommittedEffectCapsule, floor 40 against
ceiling 15). They are instances 1 and 2 of the 42.

ROOT CAUSE, structural rather than careless: the established increment shape mints kinds with an
order first and lands their fields later, so the order is chosen against a reference graph the
checker cannot yet see. Every slice following that shape manufactures more instances, and each is
frozen on landing. Three kinds minted tonight by pane3 are in the list and passed every gate.

THE FOUR THAT BIND TODAY are the ones to look at first; the full list is reproducible in seconds
with the sweep at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p3-tuw1-probe.rs, which also carries a known-good control
(ShardingFreezeSpec, window 29..=29) so a broken harness cannot report a silent all-clear.

OPTIONS, costed on fgdb-tuw1's latest comment: rule each bead individually (leaves 40); require a
source-derived two-directional window at mint time (stops new instances, does not fix the 35);
extend the DAG check to source edges (makes the invariant true, but turns 42 red and needs a
remediation plan for the 35 frozen); or document that construction_order is a landed-graph invariant
only (free now, leaves the generated reachability/GC and checkpoint-vector walkers keyed on an order
the source contradicts).
close_reason: Mechanical class discharged (331862c, 109d21a, 5b484ec). Re-measured at 7f60e5f: 3 cycles -> fgdb-2lch; 16 source self-edges + the last 3-symbol/6-row entangled batch (AuditTerminalAttemptRecord/AuditEventRecord/AuditTicket, one weakly-connected component blocked by AuditTerminalAttemptRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<Self>) -> fgdb-suhb, recorded there with both bounds; mint-time latency and the applier window guard -> fgdb-owlp. RE-MEASURED AND RE-COSTED. From pane3, against HEAD d80c942, checker rebuilt from that same HEAD.
Three of this bead's load-bearing claims do not survive, and the cheapest option is not the one the
bead recommends.

=== CORRECTION 1: THE 42 IS 39 + 3, AND THE 3 ARE A WORSE CLASS ===
Reconciled my sweep against the original one, deliberately, because a harness disagreement is exactly
the "looks like a pass" family. My list is a STRICT SUBSET: 39 vs 42, with 0 symbols in mine that are
not in theirs. The 3 in theirs only:
  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord, GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration, RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence
All three are symbols with a source SELF-EDGE. The original sweep let the self-edge act as the
symbol's own inbound ceiling, so it reported an unsatisfiable order window. They are not order
defects -- they are dag_self_edge defects, which no integer can fix in any direction. Counting them
here understates their severity.

=== CORRECTION 2: THE ORDER LAW IS NON-STRICT, SO MOST OF THIS IS SATISFIABLE ===
dag_future_result fires on `target.order > containing.order`. Strictly greater. Equal orders are
legal, and 18 landed retaining edges in the live green catalog already sit at equal order (of 184
with both ends ordered). A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC graph is satisfiable by construction.
So "no value satisfies it in both directions" is only truly unfixable where the SOURCE GRAPH CYCLES.
Full Tarjan SCC over the source StrongRef graph (963 symbols, 532 owners):
   3 nontrivial SCCs trapping 7 symbols   <- genuinely unfixable by any assignment
       GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord@60
       AuditTerminalFreezeRecord@6   <-> NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof@6
       KeyEnvelopeNode@50            <-> KeyEnvelopeRoot@50
  18 source self-edges                    <- also unfixable by any assignment
Splitting the 39 by that test:
   2  trapped in a source cycle  -> a reference SPELLING must change; a real owner ruling
  37  source is satisfiable      -> the FROZEN INTEGERS are wrong; mechanical, no plan edit
Note all three SCCs currently sit at co-equal orders, which is why they are green: co-equality
satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy dag_cycle, which fires on the edge set alone. They
go red the moment their field rows land, and no order will save them.

=== CORRECTION 3, THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE DECISION: THE 35 ARE NOT EXPENSIVELY FROZEN ===
This bead says the contradiction is "frozen behind the append-only assignment pin and cannot be
corrected by choosing a different order". construction_order is NOT in the pin. The pin's own message
enumerates its scope: "released codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union arms".
Measured, not read: moving GlobalFinalCertificationReservation 40->30, TopologyState 40->30 and
TopologyState's 3 landed field rows, in appendix_a_catalog.toml plus both projections, gives
LOAD OK / 0 violations -- not even pin drift.
NEGATIVE CONTROL, same copy same harness: TopologyState status reserved->active fires
projection_registry_assignment_drift instantly. The harness is live; the orders simply are not pinned.
(Editing only the projection and not the catalog yields projection_byte_diff -- the catalog is the
source of truth and the projections regenerate from it.)

=== WHAT THAT DOES TO THE FOUR OPTIONS ===
Option C -- extend the DAG check to source edges -- was rejected as "highest cost, needs a
remediation plan for the 35 frozen". Remediation is row edits with no re-freeze. C is now the
cheapest option that makes the invariant TRUE rather than merely unviolated, and it is the only one
that catches the 2 cycles and 18 self-edges, which are the genuinely dangerous residue and which no
amount of B-style discipline at mint time will ever fix.
Recommended: C, scoped as
  1. fix the 37 assignment defects mechanically (each is a small verified edit; two are already
     verified green on fgdb-tuw1 and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x)
  2. rule the 2 cycle-trapped symbols and the 18 self-edges as source errata -- these are the only
     genuine owner decisions in the whole set
  3. then land the source-edge DAG rule, which can now go green
B remains worth doing to stop new instances, but B alone leaves every existing defect in place.

=== BLOCKING ===
This bead blocks fgdb-tuw1 and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x, so `br update --status
in_progress` refuses to claim either. Both are nonetheless fully measured and settled on their own
comments; tuw1's value is forced at 30 and needs no ruling at all.

a stale binary reported 24 against a clean HEAD for me):
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-satisfiability.rs
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-scc.rs
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-landing-plan.rs

REPAIRED, IN TWO TRANCHES, AND THE HEADLINE COUNT IS NOW 19. pane3, against 109d21a.
43 of the 60 symbols this bead's class covers are landed at corrected orders; 23 remain,
every one of them inside a slice another pane holds or entangled with a self-edge.

=== WHAT THE PREDECESSOR'S RULING GOT RIGHT, RE-CONFIRMED ===
construction_order is NOT inside the append-only assignment pin. Both tranches moved
landed kinds and their landed field rows with LOAD OK / 0 violations and no pin drift.
The negative control was run on a copy of each post-repair tree: flipping one lifecycle
status still fires projection_registry_assignment_drift AND registry_assignment_drift,
exit 1. The green is a real green, not a check that stopped looking.
dag_future_result is non-strict, witnessed by 71 landed equal-order edges.

=== WHAT WAS MISSING, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DELIVERABLE ===
Every prior probe on this bead MEASURED. None of them REPAIRED, and a per-edge patch is
not a repair: raising one referrer to clear one violated edge pushes it through its own
ceiling, and the contradiction moves one hop instead of dying. The constraint system is

    o(target) <= o(referrer)    for every retaining edge

over a totally ordered label set. That is a monotone labelling problem, so with a
per-symbol cost for changing a value the MINIMUM-COST consistent assignment is exactly a
min-cut in Ishikawa's construction -- solved, not approximated. Chain node (v,l) means
"o(v) >= L[l]"; an infinite arc (t,l) -> (a,l) encodes o(t) <= o(a). Lexicographic
objective in one scalar, which Ishikawa admits because only the PAIRWISE term must be
convex and a hard monotone constraint is:
    1. fewest symbols moved       (1_000_000 each)
    2. fewest catalog rows edited (1_000 per landed field row that moves with its kind)
    3. shortest distance moved    (|new-old|, <= 75, tie-break only)
Term 3 is not cosmetic. Without it the cut is indifferent between two legal values and
parks symbols at the bottom label -- formally optimal, semantically vandalism, since
construction_order names a construction phase. It is what turns "AuditTicket 40 -> 5"
into "AuditTicket 40 -> 6".

Constraints come from BOTH populations, deliberately:
  S1 every retaining source reference between two symbols that carry an order, INCLUDING
     paths whose interior is still unminted -- each interior is forced into the window
     when it lands, so repairing direct-only re-manufactures this bead;
  S2 every retaining edge already in the catalog's landed field rows. The landed graph is
     not a subset of the source graph, and an S1-only repair can turn the loader RED.

=== THE MATCHER DEFECT, WHICH COST ME ONE LANDED VALUE ===
Tranche 1 (331862c) read a reference with strip_prefix. A repeated member's census
exact_type is spelled `[StrongRef<T<Local>>]`, starts with `[`, fails the prefix test,
and its edge is dropped -- the same under-reading fgdb-suhb traces to a frozen violation
already in the tree (a12 minted ResourceLedgerTransition against a ceiling computed from
five of its six consumers). A matcher that misses an edge reports a WIDER window than
exists and looks exactly like a pass.
Tranche 2 (109d21a) scans for every retaining wrapper ANYWHERE in the type, requires the
preceding byte to be a non-identifier so CertifiedRemoteStrongRef< is never read as a
bare StrongRef<, and takes the inner type with a BALANCED angle scan. +50 constraint
edges, +5 symbols.
CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: 17 of tranche 1's 18 values survive the wider reading
unchanged. ONE did not -- GcDecisionRecord went 15 -> 25 and 25 was still below its
floor; it is now 40. Nothing was landed in a wrong direction; one value was an
under-correction, caught before its field body froze it.

=== MEASURED (balanced-scan reading throughout) ===
                          865ecfb   331862c   109d21a
  violated edges             81        68        28
  unsatisfiable windows      38        35        19
  symbols still to move      60        48        23
  catalog rows still to edit 118       99        49

=== THE RESIDUAL, EXACTLY, FOR ITS OWNERS ===
Five components. Every move below is verified consistent with the whole system; a

it can violate an edge that was fine before).

  a16 -- pane7's lane, 19 symbols across three components
    C1  RestoreSourceLeaseRecord            45 -> 30   (5 landed field rows)
    C2  ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection   50 -> 30

  a08 -- pane6's lane, 2 components
    C3  TopologyRetirementAck                6 -> 30   (demand 30 <- TopologyRetirementFloor)
    C4  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord           6 -> 40   AuditEventRecord 40 -> 6   AuditTicket 40 -> 6
        !! ENTANGLED: AuditTerminalAttemptRecord also carries a SOURCE SELF-EDGE, so the

=== NOT MECHANICALLY REPAIRABLE, AND NOT MINE TO RULE ===
No integer assignment can satisfy these; they need a reference SPELLING change.
  3 constraint cycles, 7 symbols
    GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord@60
    AuditTerminalFreezeRecord@6   <-> NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof@6

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
THE METHOD, WRITTEN OUT SO pane6 DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT. pane3 handing off the residual.
This is the whole reasoning chain behind 331862c and 109d21a. Everything below is measured on
this tree, not argued.

=== 0. WHY THE PROBLEM IS NOT WHAT THE BEAD TITLE SAYS ===
"N symbols carry a jointly-unsatisfiable construction_order" describes symptoms. There is one
system underneath, and once you write it down the whole class is solved at once instead of 60
times. Three facts turn it from an erratum pile into an assignment defect:

  (a) construction_order is NOT inside the append-only assignment pin. The pin's own violation
      message enumerates its scope: "released codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union
      arms". Orders are not in it. Both my tranches moved landed kinds AND their landed field
      rows with LOAD OK / 0 violations and no pin drift.
  (b) dag_future_result is NON-STRICT. It fires on `target.order > containing.order` -- strictly
      greater. EQUAL ORDERS ARE LEGAL, witnessed by 72 landed equal-order retaining edges in the
      live green catalog, not by reading the code. A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC graph is
      satisfiable by construction (give every symbol the same integer), so "no ordering exists"
      can only be true where the SOURCE GRAPH CYCLES.
  (c) therefore every non-cyclic instance is a MECHANICAL REPAIR: edit integers, no plan edit,
      no erratum, no owner ruling.

=== 1. WHY EDGE-AT-A-TIME PATCHING IS NOT A REPAIR ===
The obvious move -- find a violated edge, raise the referrer above its target -- is wrong, and it
is wrong in a way that looks like progress. Each symbol is bounded in BOTH directions:
    demand(v)  = max order among the targets v's own body retains   (its floor)
    ceiling(v) = min order among the rows that retain v             (its ceiling)
Raising the referrer to clear one edge pushes it through its OWN ceiling and manufactures a new
violation one hop up. Lowering the target pushes it under its own floor. You can chase this
around a component indefinitely. That is why 42 became 60 in a day.

=== 2. THE SYSTEM, AND THE FACT THAT MAKES IT SOLVABLE EXACTLY ===
Write down every constraint at once:

    o(target) <= o(referrer)      for every retaining edge

That is a MONOTONE LABELLING PROBLEM over a totally ordered label set (the existing
construction_order vocabulary, 59 distinct values). With a per-symbol cost for changing its
value, the MINIMUM-COST CONSISTENT ASSIGNMENT is exactly a MIN-CUT in Ishikawa's construction --
solved, not approximated, not heuristic.

Construction, concretely:
  * label set L = the sorted distinct existing orders. Chain node (v,l) means "o(v) >= L[l]".
  * chain per symbol: s -> (v,1) -> (v,2) -> ... -> (v,k-1) -> t. Cutting the arc entering
    level l sets o(v) = L[l-1]. Give that arc capacity = the unary cost of assigning L[l-1] to v.
    Add an INFINITE reverse arc (v,l+1) -> (v,l) so exactly one arc per chain is ever cut.
  * one constraint arc per edge, per level: for `o(b) <= o(a)`, an INFINITE arc
    (b,l) -> (a,l) for every l. It encodes "o(b) >= L[l] implies o(a) >= L[l]".
  * min-cut value = minimum total unary cost. Decode: o(v) = the largest L[l] whose chain node
    is still on the source side.

Ishikawa admits an ARBITRARY unary term -- only the PAIRWISE term must be convex, and a hard
monotone constraint is -- so the whole lexicographic objective rides in one scalar:
    1. fewest symbols moved        1_000_000 each
    2. fewest catalog rows edited  1_000 per landed field row that must move with its kind
                                   (field_construction_order_mismatch forces a field's order to
                                   EQUAL its containing kind's, so they move together)
    3. shortest distance moved     |new-old|, <= 75, tie-break only
TERM 3 IS NOT COSMETIC. Without it the cut is indifferent between two legal values and parks
symbols at the bottom label. Formally optimal, semantically vandalism -- construction_order names
a construction phase. It is exactly what turns "AuditTicket 40 -> 5" into "AuditTicket 40 -> 6".

=== 3. WHICH EDGES GO IN. BOTH POPULATIONS, DELIBERATELY ===
  S1 every retaining reference the Appendix A SOURCE spells between two symbols that already
     carry an order -- INCLUDING paths whose interior is still unminted. Contract the unminted
     interior out and keep the endpoint constraint: that interior is forced into the window when
     it lands, so a direct-only repair re-manufactures this bead's next generation.
  S2 every retaining edge already in the catalog's LANDED field rows. The landed graph is NOT a
     subset of the source graph, and an S1-only repair can turn the loader RED.

=== 4. THE BALANCED-SCAN FLOOR, WHICH COST ME A LANDED VALUE ===
Tranche 1 read a reference with `strip_prefix("StrongRef<")`. A repeated member's census
exact_type is spelled `[StrongRef<T<Local>>]` -- it starts with `[`, fails the prefix test, and
its edge is DROPPED. fgdb-suhb traces exactly that under-reading to a violation already frozen in
the tree (a12 minted ResourceLedgerTransition against a ceiling computed from five of its six
consumers). A MATCHER THAT MISSES AN EDGE REPORTS A WIDER WINDOW THAN EXISTS, AND IT LOOKS
EXACTLY LIKE A PASS.
The floor, use nothing weaker:
  * scan for a retaining wrapper ANYWHERE in the type string, not as a prefix;
  * require the preceding byte to be a NON-IDENTIFIER, so `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<` is never
    read as a bare `StrongRef<`;
  * take the inner type with a BALANCED ANGLE SCAN, so `StrongRef<T<Local>>` yields `T<Local>`
    and not `T<Local`;
  * the nine RETAINING wrappers (from fgdb-owlp, not re-derived): StrongRef,
    CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, StrongCommandRef, StrongMarkerRef, StrongCiphertextRef,
    StrongGlobalCommandRef, StrongShardCommandRef, ConditionalCoordinateRef, ConditionalMarkerRef.
    MarkerRef, CommandRef, WeakDigest and the *Identity wrappers are EXCLUDED -- bare identity
    imposes no ordering obligation (the a01 identity-is-not-reachability law).
Consequence, measured: widening the matcher added 50 constraint edges and 5 symbols. 17 of
tranche 1's 18 landed values survived it unchanged; ONE did not. GcDecisionRecord went 15 -> 25
under the narrow reading and 25 was still below its floor of 40. Nothing landed in a wrong
direction; one value was an under-correction, caught before its field body froze it.

=== 5. THE BATCHING LAW: WHOLE COMPONENTS, NEVER PART OF ONE ===
Batch = weakly connected component of the constraint graph restricted to the moved symbols. Any
SUBSET OF COMPONENTS is safe, and here is the proof, because it is what lets you defer another
pane's slice without deferring the whole repair:
  * an edge between two moved symbols is INSIDE one component, so both ends move together;
  * an edge from a moved symbol to an unmoved one still holds -- the unmoved value is unchanged
    and the full solution satisfied it;
  * two unmoved symbols cannot be on a violated edge, since a violated edge forces at least one
    end to move.
PARTIAL-WITHIN-A-COMPONENT IS NOT SAFE: it can violate an edge that was fine before, and if that
edge is landed the loader goes RED.

=== 6. WHAT NO INTEGER CAN FIX ===
Tarjan the source graph. Symbols in a NONTRIVIAL SCC and symbols with a SOURCE SELF-EDGE are not
assignment defects -- a reference SPELLING must change, which is an owner ruling. Note the trap:
all three current cycles sit at CO-EQUAL orders and are therefore GREEN, because co-equality
satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy dag_cycle, which walks the EDGE SET alone. They
go red the moment their field rows land and no order will save them. Do not "fix" them with
integers.

=== 7. VERIFY LIKE THIS, AND KEEP THE NEGATIVE CONTROL ===
Rebuild the lib FROM THE TREE YOU ARE MEASURING -- a stale rlib silently passed and then failed
on byte-identical inputs for me today, and reported 7 phantom pin drifts against a clean HEAD.
    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check -O \
        tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o lib.rlib            (~15s)
    <build src/main.rs against it> ; ck all --root <tree>       (~0.6s, covers every projection)
    rustc --edition=2024 --test tests/identity.rs --extern registry_check=lib.rlib   (~9s)
    rustc --edition=2024 --test src/lib.rs                      (~2.5s -- the aNN binding-contract
                                                                 tests hard-assert orders and fire
                                                                 ONLY here)
NEGATIVE CONTROL IN EVERY BATCH, non-negotiable: on a COPY of the exact post-repair tree, flip one
released lifecycle status. projection_registry_assignment_drift and registry_assignment_drift must
fire, exit 1. A batch that passes because the check stopped looking is the failure mode this
codebase produced repeatedly. `order-repair-apply.py --negative-control <Kind>` does it.

title: OWNER RULING: tag_wire_type is u8 on 340/340 landed unions, including two the source calls u16
description:
A systematic divergence between the source spelling and the registry, surfaced
by landing 19 a21 unions. I followed precedent and am flagging it rather than
settling it silently in either direction.

## The measurement

* Landed ordinary unions with `tag_wire_type = "u8"`: 340. With `"u16"`: 0.
  The checker admits both (`bad_field` rejects anything else), so the u16
  vocabulary exists and has never been used.
* Ten of the nineteen unions landed in 3f34b52 are spelled `u16` in the source:
  AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis,
  DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget,
  DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof, DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis,
  DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof, DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef,
  DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef, DurableCapabilityStatusClassification,
  DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,
  TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence.
* The divergence PREDATES this landing. Two a05 symbols the source also spells
  `u16` -- `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject` ("the exact
  creation-only `u16` union") and `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec` ("the
  disjoint outer `u16` union") -- are landed at u8.

## Why I landed at u8

`PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject` embeds
`prebuilt_successor_replay:DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` by value. Landing
the embedded union at u16 while its embedder is u8 would have made an object
disagree with the object it contains, on a field inside the append-only
durable_fields assignment pin. Every arm tag in the tranche fits u8 (max 0x000c),
so u8 is not lossy today.

## The ruling needed

Either (a) `tag_wire_type` on an ordinary-union row denotes the CATALOG's tag
encoding for a closed-tagged union and the source's `u16` describes the object's
own tag field elsewhere -- in which case 340/340 u8 is correct and this bead
closes with that sentence written down; or (b) it is the wire tag width, in which
case 12 landed rows (2 a05 + 10 a21) are a durable-format defect and need
re-tagging together, with the a05 embedder/embedded pair moving as one.

## Cost of (b)

`tag_wire_type` IS inside the durable_fields assignment pin
(`ordinary-union|...|{tag_wire_type}|...`), so re-tagging is a 12-row edit plus
one pin re-freeze -- cheap while all 12 rows are `status = "reserved"`, and it
only gets expensive after activation. Deciding this before any of them activates
is the whole point of filing it now.

Filed by pane4 from fgdb-a21-residue-union-shapes-afpl.

  A METHOD CORRECTION, because I got this wrong first and it matters. My initial
  read of four symbols found them as `field:Symbol` payload references inside an
  enclosing u16 union, and I was about to report that the source's `u16` always
  belongs to the ENCLOSING union — which would have argued for (a). That was a
  sampling error: those were later, nested occurrences. Each of those symbols
  ALSO has its own dedicated declaring sentence, quoted above. Checking the
  matched windows instead of trusting the first hit reversed the conclusion.

THE RESULT: in all 11 cases where the source states a width, the registry
contradicts it. And the single row that uses the u16 vocabulary is one of the two
where the source states NO width. Source and registry agree in ZERO of the 13
cases where either speaks.

That is very hard to read as (a). Under (a) — "tag_wire_type denotes the
catalog's tag encoding, and the source's u16 describes something else" — one
would expect the source's u16 to attach to a different subject. It does not; it
attaches to these symbols by name, in the copula, eleven times.

--- 4. THE OBJECTION THAT MOTIVATED u8 DISSOLVES UNDER (b) ---

pane4 landed at u8 partly because `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject`
embeds `DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` by value, and landing the embedded
union at u16 under a u8 embedder would make an object disagree with the object it
contains. Under (b) that mismatch does not arise: the source declares BOTH at u16
(L1642 and L2633). Consistency and source-fidelity point the same way.

--- 5. COST, RESTATED AT TODAY'S TREE ---

  (a) u8 is correct, source `u16` means something else:
      0 rows change. Cost is one sentence written down — PLUS a decision about
      BoltBookmarkRequestKind, which is now u16 and would become the only row
      violating the sentence. So (a) is no longer free: it is 1 row + 1 pin
      re-freeze.

  (b) `u16` is the wire tag width:
      11 rows u8 -> u16 (the list above), and BoltBookmarkRequestKind is the
      open question in the other direction — the source states no width for it
      and its tags are 0x0001..0x0002, so it either stays u16 by author's choice
      or moves to u8 for consistency with every other width-silent union.
      Either way: 11 or 12 rows + one durable_fields pin re-freeze.
      All rows are `status = "reserved"`, so this is still cheap. It stops being
      cheap at activation.

  Either ruling costs a pin re-freeze now. Doing nothing costs the next pane a
  third arbitrary choice.

--- 6. WHAT I DID NOT DO ---

I did not re-tag anything and did not add a width law. Both would settle the
ruling, and the ruling is not mine. I also did not "fix" BoltBookmarkRequestKind:
pane7 landed it deliberately under xfrc and it is defensible under (a).

title: Five scripts/ deliverables present as gates but are in no runner and no registry, carrying hard-pinned counts that silently rot
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #3.

## What they claim

Five shell deliverables under `scripts/` present as gates. They carry every
signal of one: `set -euo pipefail`, a banner comment describing what they prove,
`mktemp -d` evidence directories, PASS/FAIL counters, and hard-pinned expected
counts. Reading the directory, they look like the W1 half of the gate suite.

## What they actually are

Nothing runs them and nothing registers them. Cross-referencing every tracked
`scripts/*.sh` against all in-repo references (excluding the file itself):

  - `scripts/w1_bigint_e2e.sh`                  -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_codec_scalar_e2e.sh`            -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh`   -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh`      -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_foundation_types_e2e.sh`        -> referenced only by
        `crates/fgdb-delta-types/examples/foundation_transcript.rs` (a doc
        mention, not an invocation)

None of the five appears in `scripts/check.sh`. None has a row in
`registries/checker_index.toml` — unlike the seven registered script artifacts,
these are absent from the registry entirely, so they are not even covered by
the (weak) file-existence liveness proof.

## Why this is worse than dead code

They carry hard-pinned magic numbers that silently rot as the crates they
"gate" evolve, and nothing will ever notice:

  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:62`  `wc -l` must equal 67
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:71`  `grep -c` must equal 64
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:79`  `grep -c` must equal 2
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:103` `wc -l` must equal 68
  - `w1_codec_scalar_e2e.sh:55`           `wc -l` must equal 5
  - `w1_bigint_e2e.sh:18`  `cargo tree ... | wc -l` must equal 1

A pinned count in a script nobody runs is not a gate, it is a comment that
looks like a gate. When someone eventually wires these up, they will fail for
reasons unrelated to the change under review, and the likely response will be to
re-pin the numbers rather than investigate — which converts the whole file into
decoration permanently.

`scripts/check.sh` DOES lint all five (`bash -n` + `shellcheck --severity=warning`
over `git ls-files '*.sh'`), so they are syntactically valid and shellcheck-clean.
That is exactly what makes this hard to see: they are maintained, they are
linted, they are green — and they have no gate role.

Note also that the lint step enumerates via `git ls-files`, so an UNTRACKED
script is exempt from even that.

## Which gate catches this today

None. There is no law that a `scripts/*_e2e.sh` must be registered in
`checker_index.toml`, and no law that a registered checker must be invoked (see
fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o).

## Fix

Decide per script, explicitly, and record the decision:
  - If it is a gate: register it in `checker_index.toml` and wire it into
    `check.sh` (or the slower lane).
  - If it is a one-shot bring-up transcript that has served its purpose: say so
    in its banner, drop the pinned counts that imply ongoing enforcement, and
    move it out of `scripts/` into a clearly-labelled evidence directory.
Then add the missing law: every tracked `scripts/*_e2e.sh` must resolve to a
`checker_index.toml` row. That law is cheap and closes the class.

It predicted the pinned counts "silently rot". Measured at 0ada651 — nothing has rotted. Every
assertion in all four w1 scripts holds TODAY. Verified lock-free by running the prebuilt example
binaries out of /data/tmp/cargo-target/debug/examples (all rebuilt Jul 26 14:28, newer than every
source they depend on), so no cargo and no build slot:

  scalar_transcript            5 evidence rows (pin 5), byte-identical across two runs
  codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e    67 evidence / 64 stream-vbyte / 1 block / 2 identity / 68 lines

The cargo-tree dependency assertions hold structurally: all six foundation crates declare ZERO
dependencies of any kind (normal, dev, build), so both the depth-1 count pin and the
"nothing outside fgdb-/asupersync" loop are satisfied.

CONTROLS, because "0 of 16 missing" is a zero result. (a) the 16 extracted patterns are real,
shortest 31 chars, not empty strings that match anything; (b) a known-absent string reports
MISSING; (c) mutating the transcript flips exactly 1 pattern to missing. Without those three the
loop proves nothing.

So these are not decoration. They are working, deterministic gates nobody wired up.

## The count is 6, not 5

Re-derived structurally — the registry parsed by the checker's own loader, not grepped, with a
control asserting the reader resolves a known-registered script before any zero was believed.
13 scripts on disk, 7 registered, 6 absent. The sixth is scripts/check.sh, which is correctly
not a gate: it is the runner.

## What landed

The missing direction. validate_checker_index closes ROW -> FILE (a live row's artifact must
exist). Nothing closed FILE -> ROW. Now validate_script_closure does: every scripts/*.sh must be
a registered [[checker]] artifact or a [[script_disposition]] row saying why it is not a gate.

  script_undeclared             neither registered nor declared
  script_disposition_conflict   both at once
  script_disposition_dangling   declares a script that does not exist
  script_scan_empty             CONTROL — an empty scan is a violation, not a pass,
                                because check.sh is itself a script so zero is never correct

It scans the FILESYSTEM, not `git ls-files`: an untracked script is already exempt from the shell
lint and must not be exempt twice.

Mutation audit, all four fire: the live repo before the table reported exactly the 6 undeclared
scripts by name; conflict and dangling each fire on their own probe; the staged tree is clean.

## THE RESIDUE, COSTED — this is the ruling I owe you

Promoting the four candidates to registered gates is NOT free any more, because pane6 made
check.sh registry-derived in 0ada651: registration is now what makes a script RUN. So promotion
is a claim about the swarm's whole gate chain, not a bookkeeping edit.

  cost to promote all four:  +4 [[checker]] rows, -4 [[script_disposition]] rows
                             net registry delta 0 rows; no pin moves (checker_index has no
                             count or transcript pin — worth fixing separately, cf. a7c8)
  what check.sh then gains:  2 x `cargo run --locked --offline --example` (verified to pass)
                             2 x `cargo test --all-targets` over 6 foundation crates (UNVERIFIED
                             here — cargo is unreliable in this environment, asupersync git
                             refresh is rate-limited)
                             2 x `cargo tree --locked` (holds structurally, unverified live)
  blocking law:              a candidate may be promoted only when its cargo half has been seen
                             to pass end-to-end, because check.sh now executes what it registers

Anyone with a working cargo can discharge this in one run of the four scripts. If they pass,
flip role="candidate" rows to [[checker]] rows and delete them from the disposition table.

## For a successor

- checker_index.toml has NO count or transcript pin, so rows can be added, removed, or swapped
  with nothing noticing. Same class as fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8.
- scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh is declared advisory AND is defective: it exits 0 on the
  pin-drift case it exists to catch (fgdb-bead-provenance-preflight-misses-pin-drift-a5kb).
- registering a script as status="live" today only asserts the file exists
  (fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o, pane2). Once that bead lands, these
  candidates will correctly go red until they are actually run — which is the desired sequencing,
  not a regression.

CORRECTION AND SHARPENING OF THE ORDER-WINDOW FINDING, now measured catalog-wide instead of owner-by-owner.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING. I reported TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence as "a second unsatisfiable order window". That was wrong. IssuanceFence is not the owner of a violating edge — it is a TARGET of one. Its apparent "consumers demand <= 21" bound comes entirely from TimeAuthorityRegistry@21 strong-referencing it through .profiles.Draining.issuance_fence_ref. The Registry-side constraint (>= 27) and the Fence-side constraint (<= 21) are the SAME EDGE seen from its two ends, not two independent problems. One root cause.

THE CATALOG-WIDE MEASUREMENT: 14 latent construction-order violations, over exactly TWO owners. A latent violation is a census strong reference whose target order already exceeds its owner's order but which has NO field row yet — so dag_future_result sees no edge and the checker is silent. Every one becomes a hard violation the moment its field body is modelled.

  OWNER TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> @21 — six distinct violating targets, all reached through the .profiles indexed-map interiors: TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence@27, RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>@40, RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure<Role>@41, TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>@55, TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>@60, TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>@65. Modelling those interiors as strong field rows would demand order >= 65 while the Registry's own six consumers demand <= 23. No order satisfies both, so the interiors CANNOT become flat or nested strong field rows at any order. They must either be covered by union arms (no DAG edge is created by an arm payload digest) or held indirectly.

  OWNER ControlCommand @10 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20. This one is NOT a16 and NOT mine. It is an independent instance of the same class in another slice, and it is the evidence that the hazard is structural rather than an a16 quirk — whoever owns ControlCommand should be told before they model its body. I am not touching it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND a16: the checker cannot warn about any of these today. The DAG law is enforced over field ROWS, and a census key with no row contributes no edge, so a slice can look completely clean while carrying an unsatisfiable ordering that only detonates when someone does the honest modelling work. A cheap standing guard would be to run this latent-violation probe as a checker law over census strong references rather than only over landed rows — that would surface the contradiction at mint time, when the order is still free to choose, instead of at field-body time when it is frozen. I would file that as its own bead, but bead creation needs the pin re-freeze and therefore the catalog token.

THE RESOLUTION SPACE IS UNCHANGED but the preferred option is now clearer. (a) Teach the census the `field[key -> A|B]` indexed-map union spelling so .profiles yields a union plus six arms, whose payload digests cover the interiors and create no DAG edges; the Registry stays at 21 and no new kind is minted. This is the most faithful to the source and it reuses the exact mechanism I2a/I6a/I6b already rely on, but it perturbs the frozen census and therefore every slice's candidate counts and sha pins. (b) Mint the map value as its own entry schema at order >= 65, held INLINE by the Registry and committed by its body digest — no parser change, no DAG edge, Registry stays at 21. Holding entries by StrongRef instead would reintroduce the contradiction, so inline is the only workable form. (c) Weakening the interior refs is wrong: a registry administering live profiles plainly means to retain them, and that would be identity-is-not-reachability applied backwards. I recommend (a), with (b) as the fallback if the census change is judged too expensive, and I am still not deciding it — it is either a catalog-wide parser change or a change to a released kind's object graph.

SCOPE OF THE BLOCK, unchanged: all 29 of TimeAuthorityRegistry's uncovered field keys (6 flat plus 23 interior) wait on this ruling. It is the second-largest uncovered owner in a16.
