**SessionReplayBundle (the customer-facing agent-replay product)**: the ordered per-statement `ReplayManifest`s of a session plus its FGP frame transcript, graded with the existing `ReplayCompleteness` vocabulary — `Replayable | StructuralReplay{reproduced_classes[], omitted_classes[]} | VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied{missing_classes[]} | AuditOnly{missing_or_redacted_classes[]}` — time-travel debugging of the database's recorded work for that agent. Whole-agent byte-identity is NEVER claimed for customer code not threaded through the lab.

**ReplayManifest substrate (§8.6, consumed from w5-replay)**: pins database/security namespace/incarnation, logical-command and commit sequences, topology/policy/revocation epochs, the execution `AnswerRequirement`, realized `AnswerContract`, `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId`, result-encoding version, and canonical result digest. Every evidence slot is `ReplayEvidenceRef<T> = Present{object: ReplayObjectRef<T>} | Unavailable{class, expected_logical_object_id?, expected_canonical_digest?, reason_code} | Redacted{class, commitment?, redaction_policy_oid}`. A versioned `ReplaySlotSchema` derives — not trusts — structural completeness from slot states and the recorded execution's actual semantic dependencies; at access time the verifier separately derives `effective_completeness` from live availability/lease/trust/resolver/authorization state, which can only stay equal or weaken. An encoded structural grade that disagrees with the generated slot matrix is invalid.

**Chaos packaging row (registered G0 decision)**: any customer-facing surface over `fgdb-sim`'s fault machinery ships behind an fgdb-owned facade crate with its own stability classification, never as a direct dependency on the foundation lab runtime; its reports are claim-typed falsification-only — structurally incapable of asserting "verified fault-free" — and chaos/fault-injection capabilities are absent from production `Cx` profiles BY CONSTRUCTION, a lab-only capability rather than a runtime flag.

Production incident bundles keep their fail-closed redaction contract; crypto entropy is never recorded; customer-safe bundles never overclaim byte identity.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19 (restated): a registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix, and its effective grade may only weaken as leases, resolution, trust, configuration, or authority change. `Replayable` requires every semantic slot — answer requirement, realized contract, authority, external inputs, executable artifacts, decisions, workspace-affecting statements, exact approximate generations — to resolve through exactly LocalStrong, live CertifiedRemote, or active Archived evidence and reproduce canonical logical output. Sharded replay is no stronger than its weakest required group. Erased subjects downgrade replay through the `Redacted` arm with the erasure tombstone as typed evidence; an `ErasureCutSpec` never silently breaks a byte-identity claim — the effective grade weakens attributably. FG-INV-20 applies to resolution: reading or resolving any replay item requires explicit `Replay` authority scoped to the complete evidence/artifact closure. Exposure/stability classifications are registry (`SafetyInvariant`-adjacent contract) rows; chaos reports are structurally falsification-only claims.

## Interactions
Consumes w5-replay (ReplayManifest, grades, FG-INV-19 machinery) and verif-sim (crashpacks/seeds, fault machinery, ReplayCompleteness vocabulary); g0-format-arms freezes both decision rows and the stability classifications; w10-fgp-core supplies the FGP frame transcript and the delivery surface; w9-redaction-erasure supplies `ErasureCutSpec` and the erasure-tombstone evidence the `Redacted` slot cites (the `Redacted` arm itself is defined by w5-replay’s `ReplayEvidenceRef` schema, §8.6); obs-observatory shares the fail-closed redaction contract for crashpacks.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Bundle builder assembles ordered per-statement ReplayManifests plus the FGP transcript; the bundle grade is computed by the generated slot matrix, never hand-encoded; an invalid-manifest test proves an encoded grade disagreeing with the matrix is rejected.
- Grade-weakening tests: expiring a lease, revoking trust, and erasing a subject each weaken the effective grade attributably; no code path re-strengthens a grade without new evidence.
- Redaction: fail-closed contract tests; an entropy-scan negative over emitted bundles; a customer-safe fixture proves no byte-identity claim appears for omitted classes and whole-agent byte identity is never claimed.
- Chaos facade: CI dependency check — no customer-visible crate depends directly on the lab runtime; the report type makes "verified fault-free" unrepresentable (type-level test); a production `Cx` profile compile check proves fault-injection capability is absent.
- E2E with logging: record an agent session, build the bundle, replay it; the Replayable case reproduces canonical logical output exactly; the AuditOnly case refuses byte-replay claims; every step emits §15.1 structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: implicit publicness of seeds/crashpacks; exposing the lab runtime directly (foundation coupling + capability leak into production); claiming whole-agent byte identity for un-labbed customer code. Risk: commercial pressure to overclaim grades — structurally prevented by derived-not-trusted grading and the falsification-only report type.

## Provenance
§15.1 final paragraph (1136), §8.6 (713-717), FG-INV-19/20, §19 G0 decision batch.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build Sextant calibration plane: e-processes, conformal, SPRT/OPE, claim typing
description:
## What & scope
Build the Sextant calibration plane (§15.0): e-processes, conformal predictors, sequential tests (SPRT), robust estimators, regime/change detectors (one versioned BOCPD+SR signal), and propensity/OPE tooling — all as deterministic transformations of logged inputs over asupersync's e-process core — plus the claim-class constitution wiring, the FG-CAL/FG-EVID/FG-CFG registry rows, decision-card binding, the deterministic-fallback law, and the never-mislabel-statistics law. This is the runtime stratum of B5: the calibration discipline that governs the LIVE system, not a test suite.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's third leg is calibrated adaptivity: the system tunes itself, but every adaptive choice is inspectable, evidence-typed, and reversible to a deterministic fallback — "this is how B5 makes adaptation inspectable without confusing 'well measured' with 'proved safe'." §15.7 paper 6 ("Calibrated adaptivity: anytime-valid statistical governance of a self-tuning DBMS") is the receipt. §3.5 fixes the verdicts: conformal prediction adopted as assumption-bearing evidence, never semantic enforcement; e-processes adopted for policy trials and health sentinels, kept in `evidence.toml`; SPRT adopted conditionally (may add evidence to migration cards, never replaces hard dwell/hysteresis guards); OPE adopted conditionally (logged probabilities, support exclusions, effective sample size, deterministic fallback, and explicit deployment evidence); CVaR/EVT as model-qualified control evidence (never call a fitted extreme quantile "certified"); empirical Bayes/Good-Turing/robust estimators to Evaluate per fixture.

## Design — normative detail
Sextant supplies its estimators as deterministic transformations of logged inputs; it governs performance and operational choices; it NEVER upgrades assumption-bearing evidence into exact correctness. Every evidence envelope carries a `ClaimClass`: `SafetyInvariant` | `FormalModelClaim` | `StatisticalClaim` | `ConfigurationModelClaim` | `EmpiricalGate` (with their §15.0-mandated disclosure fields). Registry split: `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets.

Validity laws (all normative): e-processes may be anytime-valid only under their named filtration/null assumptions; conformal coverage is marginal under its named exchangeability or online-validity conditions; drift alarms do not retroactively preserve a broken assumption; OPE requires positivity/overlap and sufficient effective sample size. Dead-code law: a monitor that drives no named decision is dead code, but binding it to a decision does not make it an invariant. Fallback law: every adaptive policy retains a deterministic fallback valid without the statistical model. Binding laws: answer-affecting execution policies are bound to the `AnswerRequirement`, plan, result contract, and replay closure; canonical-state-affecting promotions are logical-command-sequenced and replay-pinned; only proved answer-preserving physical policies may remain local. Immutable evidence identity: calibration windows, selection policy, strata, propensity support, regime epochs, fallback, and failure behavior are immutable identities of the evidence. Decision-card binding: an SPRT may add evidence to §6.6 migration cards but never replaces the hard dwell/hysteresis guards; one versioned BOCPD+SR regime signal feeds controllers without being treated as ground truth.

## Invariants & claim types
The statistical/configuration gate rows this bead materializes and enforces (restated from App F): FG-CAL-01 adaptive-policy evidence vs pinned fallback — null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only. FG-CAL-02 cardinality/risk interval coverage — population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage and drift. FG-CAL-03 ANN recall/drift — authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval and rebuild action. FG-EVID-01 decision-card/OPE completeness — state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback. FG-EVID-02 scrub/corpus-health — population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position, observed corruption. FG-EVID-03 endurance-gate evidence; FG-EVID-04 derived-state freshness (slo-class, never an invariant). FG-CFG-01 modeled durability (MTTDL); FG-CFG-02 controller stability; FG-CFG-03 staleness SLO feasibility; FG-CFG-04 maintenance-stream capacity model. None of these may ever appear in `invariants.toml` — the never-mislabel law is itself CI-checked.

## Interactions
Consumes w1-sketch-calibrate (`fgdb-sketch` + `fgdb-calibrate` over the asupersync e-process core) and g0-claim-registries (the three tomls). Serves: w3-write-amp decision cards (§6.6 SPRT/dwell), w5-planner optimizer intervals (§8.5, FG-CAL-02), w6-maintainers approximate-maintainer risk (§9.6), w7-vector recall evidence (FG-CAL-03), w2-fec-scrub (FG-EVID-02, FG-CFG-01), obs-slo production sentinels, perf-freshness-vector calibration rows, and verif-perf-apparatus evidence typing.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Determinism: identical logged inputs produce bit-identical scores/ledgers across runs and platforms under the pinned numeric profile.
- E-process validity harness: simulated null streams show Ville-bound violation rate within alpha; a filtration-violation fixture invalidates the claim rather than silently continuing.
- Conformal harness: synthetic exchangeable and nonexchangeable streams; realized marginal coverage reported per FG-CAL-02 fields; drift alarm fires and reverts to conservative costing.
- OPE: a positivity-violation fixture is excluded with a recorded zero-support exclusion; effective sample size below threshold blocks promotion; promotion is stream-sequenced.
- Registry CI: every FG-CAL/FG-EVID row lives in `evidence.toml`, every FG-CFG row in `slo.toml`, none in `invariants.toml`; a dead-monitor detector flags monitors bound to no named decision; every adaptive policy registers a deterministic fallback and a pulled-model test proves failover.
- Decision-card binding test: SPRT evidence present but dwell guard unsatisfied results in no migration.
- E2E script: replay one pinned decision-card episode end-to-end — logged inputs -> e-process/conformal/OPE scores -> FG-CAL-01 evidence row -> promotion decision -> forced assumption failure -> deterministic fallback engagement — asserting bit-identical scores across two runs and a fallback that operates without the statistical model.
- Detailed logging: every score/ledger update logs {estimator id, immutable evidence identity (window/selection policy/strata/propensity support/regime epoch/fallback/failure behavior), input digest, score, ClaimClass, decision binding}; promotion/rollback events log the named decision, policy epoch, and evidence refs; the dead-monitor detector logs every monitor-to-decision binding — calibration behavior must be fully reconstructible from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected per §3.5: conformal coverage as semantic enforcement; e-processes in the invariant registry; SPRT replacing dwell/hysteresis; context-free CALM "no coordination" labels; calling fitted extreme quantiles certified; graph-workload slogans substituting for fixture-specific risk evidence. Risk: assumption drift silently invalidating evidence — mitigated by immutable evidence identities and drift alarms that block claims instead of patching them; risk: adaptive-policy sprawl — every policy needs a registered fallback and named decision, or it is dead code.

## Provenance
§15.0 (1106-1120), §3.5 (159-183), App F statistical gates (3151-3165), §2.1 statistical-governance row.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build fgdb-sim: lab-runtime simulation harness with LDFI, shrinking, dual runs
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-sim` (§15.1): the simulation-first development harness that runs the ENTIRE database under asupersync's lab runtime — virtual time, virtual network, virtual disk, seeded deterministic scheduling, chaos injection, and deterministic pressure models — plus the five force multipliers (LDFI, model-qualified stopping, self-shrinking failures, lab-vs-live dual runs, graded production incident replay) and the mandatory structured failure artifact. Scope: harness integration, declared bounded scenario/state models, the LDFI campaign registry, and the artifact contract tests. Customer-facing exposure of sim artifacts is verif-replay-products' scope. Deliverable interface: the `fgdb-sim` crate exporting the scenario/state-model registration API, the campaign registry, the structured-artifact emitter, the shrinker, and the dual-run driver — plus a representative multi-component fixture state machine (virtual time/disk/network, chaos, seeded scheduling) that this bead's own acceptance runs against and that later campaign beads import as the harness smoke target.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: determinism as a bet means every failure is a replayable seed, never a flake. Per §2.1 the lab runtime is "the verification substrate for B5"; a query is an asupersync region, so MVCC interleaving bugs become seed-replayable test failures. §18.2 explicitly does not build the deterministic lab, LDFI, delta-debug, dual-run, or trace-export tooling — those are foundation assets; this bead wires the database into them. Simulation-first is the FoundationDB lesson; the lab-vs-live dual run closes the classic simulation-testing loophole ("we verified the simulator, not the system"). §3.5 adopts LDFI/delta-debugging/record-replay "with replay-completeness grades".

## Design — normative detail
The database runs entirely under the lab runtime. DPOR/Mazurkiewicz exploration is exhaustive only within the declared bounded scenario/state model and the soundness of its independence relation; broader campaigns remain falsification, never proof of bug absence. Every failure becomes a replayable seed/crashpack.

Five force multipliers, all normative. (1) **Targeted falsification (LDFI)**: derives minimal fault hypotheses from successful-run dependencies. Fixed target list: every file/directory action in D1/D2; every ordered, certificate, external-CAS, or physical side-effect boundary in dual-root publication; attempt generation/ticket claim/statement-workspace publication and delivery; checkpoint install/provisional-cut activation; prepared ownership and Raft; remote release; key stage/activate/zero/destroy/physical completion; GC preflight/authorization/quarantine/member completion; backup pin/copy/reopen/publish/release; restore reservation/transform/reconciliation/hidden activation/visibility/service preparation/continuity-plus-catalog receipt/finalize/open/reopen/completion; and Local-to-W12 seal/activation/authority-transfer/retirement. Residual random chaos guards lineage blind spots. (2) **Model-qualified stopping**: novelty estimates and coverage maximization prioritize finite CI time under a named sampling model; they may stop a campaign per policy but never certify that no unexplored bug remains; deterministic bounded-state completion is reported separately from statistical/heuristic stopping. (3) **Self-shrinking failures**: hierarchical delta debugging + replay minimization reduce every failing seed (schedule + workload trace) to a minimal reproducer before filing; divergence diagnostics explain exactly where a replay departed from its recording; crashpacks arrive pre-shrunk. (4) **Lab-vs-live dual runs**: the same scenario, same seed, runs under the lab and against the live build, and the traces are diffed — the runtime-behavior counterpart of the fgdb-reference semantics differential. (5) **Graded production incident replay**: production retains bounded mediated-nondeterminism records under a fail-closed redaction contract; each bundle carries `ReplayCompleteness = Replayable | StructuralReplay{reproduced_classes[], omitted_classes[]} | VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied{missing_classes[]} | AuditOnly{missing_or_redacted_classes[]}`. Crypto entropy is never recorded. Full internal forensic bundles may be exact when policy permits; customer-safe bundles never overclaim byte identity.

**Structured failure artifact (mandatory)**: every failing sim, live differential, integration, or E2E run emits ONE secret-redacted structured artifact containing `{seed, schedule, crashpoint, role, group, configuration, topology, incarnation, service_visibility_epoch, logical/commit/Raft/applied/visible/audit-visible positions, attempt/generation/statement/workspace/backup/restore/GC/key identifiers, object/spec/result/certificate/grant/floor identities, expected, actual, replay_command}`. Human prose is supplemental, never the record.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 enforcement runs here: "no structured task, ownership lease, begin/allocation/finalization reservation, pin, scratch object, result/workspace/cursor/output lease, prepared closure, privacy charge/seed/result, audit freeze/plan/per-signer lock/share/pipeline entry, escrow/resource hold, backup pin, remote transition, GC quarantine, restore-source lease, or TerminalPending postcondition is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated ... under declared quorum/storage/network/time/continuity/resource fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state" — checked by the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle inside every campaign. Claim typing: a fired checker is `SafetyInvariant` evidence; campaign summaries are falsification-only; stopping heuristics are `StatisticalClaim` under a named sampling model; DPOR bounded completion is a bounded `FormalModelClaim` reported separately; no sim output may ever claim "verified fault-free".

## Interactions
Hosts verif-oracles' checkers and verif-torture's crash campaigns; verif-differential's model-generated histories run here; verif-replay-products packages crashpacks/seeds under the G0 decision rows (g0-format-arms); perf-bench-governance uses its pinned deterministic simulated audit authority; every w2/w4/w9/w10/w11/w12 bead registers matrices on this harness. Consumes w1-foundation-types (claim/evidence types) and g0-claim-registries (ClaimClass constitution).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Determinism gate, phased by build order (this bead's dep closure is only foundation types + claim registries — no server exists yet): the exported fixture state machine boots under the lab with virtual time/disk/network and a pinned seed, and two runs at the same seed produce byte-identical traces; the identical two-run gate re-executes over the whole server at gate-genesis, which consumes this bead.
- Artifact contract tests, phased: the artifact schema, per-class field-presence assertions, and `replay_command` execution (requiring the identical failure) are implemented and exercised NOW against harness-native synthetic failure classes injected into the fixture state machine. The §15.1 lifecycle coverage list — lost `BEGIN_ACCEPTED`; duplicate/conflicting begin keys; denial/abandonment before registration; workspace-zero recovery; successor Registered-outcome rooting; cancel with prior results/workspace/grants; terminal/autocommit ACK/release races; every TerminalPending missing-postcondition combination; status before/during/after compaction and detail reclamation — is delivered here as a registered machine-readable coverage matrix whose rows activate as their owning beads land (w2-txn-lifecycle, w2-prepare-terminal, w2-outcome-tokens, w2-compaction); a CI check fails when an owning bead is complete but its rows have no passing campaign; full-list enforcement binds at gate-genesis and verif-torture, not at this bead's position.
- LDFI campaign registry enumerates the full normative target list now (rows registered even for machinery not yet built); CI proves each target class has at least one campaign once its owning workstream's beads are complete — before that the row is explicitly `pending(owning_bead)`, never silently absent; injected-fault failures shrink to minimal reproducers automatically, with divergence diagnostics on replay mismatch (demonstrated now on fixture-state-machine faults).
- Lab-vs-live dual run: the dual-run driver and trace-diff machinery are delivered and demonstrated NOW by running the fixture state machine under the lab and under the live (real-clock/real-scheduler) runtime with the same seed and diffing traces; the first whole-database end-to-end dual-run scenario binds at gate-genesis and is re-asserted by later campaigns.
- ReplayCompleteness grading fixtures for all four grades; a redacted bundle downgrades rather than claiming byte identity; scan-based negative proves crypto entropy never appears in any bundle.
- Detailed logging: every sim run logs {scenario_id, seed, virtual-clock epoch, injected faults with injection points, artifact fields asserted, shrink iterations, final reproducer path}; the lab-vs-live dual run logs both trace digests side by side; determinism-gate failures log the first diverging trace offset — every campaign verdict must be reconstructable from these logs without rerunning.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: random-only chaos (LDFI targets causal fault hypotheses; random remains only as blind-spot guard); treating DPOR as proof of bug absence; unstructured text logs as failure records; building a lab runtime in-house. Risks: sim/live semantic drift — mitigated by dual runs; heuristic stopping hiding bugs — mitigated by the separate deterministic-completion report.

## Provenance
§15.1 (1122-1136), §2.1 lab rows, §3.5 LDFI row, §18.2.


## Authoritative phase boundary (supersedes any broader reading above)
This bead delivers the reusable simulation substrate, fixture-level proof that the substrate works, registration APIs, and machine-readable future campaign rows. Its implementation dependency closure is G0/W1, so references above to W9, W10, W11, or W12 boundaries mean **registry vocabulary and pending owner rows only**, not executed implementation coverage and not gate evidence. Live G3 protocol/authority/member campaigns are owned by `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` and `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`. Live Meta/Shard/global-certification campaigns are owned only by `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl` and `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0` under `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`. A pending row cannot satisfy an invariant or gate, and G4 cannot acquire W12 evidence through this substrate.

Phase-boundary tests: unit-test owner/gate metadata on every registry row; property-test that activation before the owning implementation/feature clause is rejected; E2E exercise one G3 and one W12 row through their dedicated campaign entrypoints and prove the base harness reports them as delegated rather than covered. Structured JSONL adds `{phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,implementation_enabled,row_state:pending|live|disabled,coverage_evidence_ref}`; missing or mismatched ownership is a hard failure.

title: Build fault & recovery torture: crash matrices at every durability boundary
description:
## What & scope
Implement the phase-correct Local/W1-G1 portion of §15.3's fault-and-recovery torture program: exhaustive generated crash matrices for the W2 root, commit, prepared ownership, checkpoint, suffix recovery, FEC/scrub, and stale-writer boundaries in this bead's dependency closure; model-declaration lint; additional Local format/corruption campaigns; and real multiprocess takeover tests. Later G3 network/authority/member and post-1.0 W12 campaigns have dedicated owners and are not evidence from this bead.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's One Version Universe rests on a commit stream that survives arbitrary crashes at arbitrary points; the crash matrices are the empirical leg standing beside FG-INV-07/08/10's formal models. The model-declaration law prevents the classic vagueness of "we tested crashes" — every scenario states exactly which filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, and fairness model it assumes, so a green matrix is a bounded, honest claim.

## Design — normative detail
**Local crash matrix** kills at every W2 D1/D2 file and directory barrier, both RootSlots, inode/incarnation takeover check, post-rebase capsule, marker/root publication, prepared ownership, payload receipt/one-member order/apply, checkpoint install/provisional-cut/activation, retained-suffix reconstruction, and Local statement/workspace/result/status transition already implemented in the W2 closure. Rows for later audit/network/restore/distributed machines may be registered as pending but cannot execute or count here.

**Delegated W12 campaigns**: the registry reserves owner-tagged rows for begin reservation, Meta/Shard prepare/decision/audit/global-delta, TerminalPending, remote release, distributed keys, GC, backup/restore, topology, and Local-to-W12 activation. Those rows remain `pending(fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0)` and only that task may execute or satisfy them.

**Delegated G3 campaigns**: W9 audit/DP/key, W10 wire/adapters/protected outputs, W11 multi-member/backup/restore/service/reopen, external-authority, leader-loss, joint-reconfiguration, and donor campaigns remain `pending(fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4)`. This base bead supplies reusable generator/hooks but no G3 green evidence.

**Activation scope**: this bead executes only W2 checkpoint/provisional-cut activation. Local-to-Sharded freeze/seal/certificate/projection/first-entry/authority-transfer/RetiredLocal/finalize/reclamation executes exclusively in the W12 formal/torture task.

**Model-declaration law**: every scenario declares filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models. Inapplicable dimensions are explicitly `not_applicable(reason)`, never silently omitted.

**Additional Local campaigns**: partial marker tails; full-digest locator collisions; mixed `EncodingId` symbols; erasures within and beyond each W2 source-block budget; stale Local writers; and idempotent Local Unknown/status recovery. Uncertain multi-member membership, donor poisoning, distributed key loss, and remote-authority failures are G3/W12 tasks.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10's Local two-slot/root/recovery and stale-writer claims, FG-INV-07's Local prepared/ownership no-timeout-release claims, and FG-INV-08's Local logical/transaction sequence and checkpoint-suffix claims are falsified here. Each matrix row is `SafetyInvariant` falsification evidence under its declared model. This bead does not claim the distributed/restore/key/GC/role-transition arms of those invariants; their owning phases must emit separate evidence.

## Interactions
Runs on verif-sim, asserts through the Local verif-oracles, and consumes only W2 root/commit/recovery/checkpoint subjects plus their generated command contracts. Gate G1 consumes this Local matrix. `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4` extends it over live W9-W11; `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0` extends it over live W12. A registered pending row never satisfies Gate G3 or Gate W12.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Local matrix-completeness CI: generated from activated W2 publication modes/barriers; every Local command in this bead's closure has a campaign row. G3/W12 rows must carry their different owner and pending state.
- Each live Local campaign: post-crash recovery converges to a Local oracle-legal state; root/capsule/sequence/visibility checks pass; every failure emits the §15.1 artifact and executable replay command.
- fsync-lie and path-replacement variants exist for every Local matrix row; rollback (block-level snapshot restore) variants per the declared threat-model scoping.
- Erasure campaigns: reconstruction succeeds within each source-block budget and fails cleanly beyond it with the correct typed error — never silent corruption.
- Multiprocess kill tests for takeover: a stale writer is fenced by the inode/incarnation check at every interleaving of lease->recover->fence-root->enable.
- Scenario lint: a scenario file missing any of the six model declarations is rejected.
- E2E campaign script: generate active Local rows, execute one row per W2 durable command class plus fsync-lie, over-budget erasure, and real multiprocess takeover, recover and oracle-check, then assert all G3/W12 rows remain delegated/pending. Publish one machine-readable Local campaign summary.
- Detailed logging: every row emits JSONL `{campaign_id,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,crash_point_id,command_class,seed,model_profile_digest,kill_phase,recovery_verdict,oracle_results,artifact_ref,verdict}`. Passing and failing rows share the schema; phase misattribution or counting a pending row is a hard failure. CI executes a sampled failure's replay command and requires the same divergence identity.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: sampled Local durability boundaries, trusting fsync, clean-shutdown-only recovery, undeclared models, or treating a pending future row as coverage. Later matrix growth is owned by explicit G3/W12 tasks; each uses registry enumeration, LDFI, self-shrinking failures, and separately reported deterministic/statistical stopping.

## Provenance
§15.3 Local/W1-G1 lanes, Appendix F Local clauses of FG-INV-07/08/10, §19 Gate G1. G3 and W12 rows are delegated to their dedicated tasks.


## Authoritative phase boundary
Any earlier broad §15.3 inventory is retained only as registry vocabulary. This bead's executable evidence ends at Local/G1. G3 lives in `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4`; W12 lives in `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0`. This boundary supersedes any broader interpretation.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Freeze the universal verification, E2E, evidence, and diagnostic-event contract
description:
## What & scope
Freeze and enforce the repository-wide implementation verification, end-to-end scenario, evidence-artifact, and diagnostic-event contract. This is not a substitute for task-specific acceptance tests: it is the generated completeness schema that every implementation, protocol, format, operator, gate, benchmark, and operations bead must instantiate with concrete rows. It owns `verification_contracts.toml`, stable test/scenario/event IDs, the unit-to-E2E coverage matrix, failure-bundle rules, replay commands, fixture isolation rules, and CI lints that reject untested or unobservable normative clauses.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The plan makes verification a design pillar and the user requires comprehensive unit tests, E2E scripts, and detailed logging. A prose promise is insufficient at this scale. A generated, closed registry makes missing coverage visible before implementation, prevents a broad E2E test from disguising missing local semantics, and ensures every failure is diagnosable and replayable under B5 without leaking protected state under B6. It also turns future-self knowledge into executable metadata instead of relying on the source plan or institutional memory.

## Design — normative contract
`verification_contracts.toml` contains one stable `VerificationSubjectId` per durable schema, state-machine transition, algebra/operator law, invariant checker, protocol frame/state pair, recovery boundary, authorization noninterference surface, benchmark claim, and gate clause. Each subject declares: owning bead/workstream; normative clause IDs; applicable roles/postures/configuration epochs; unit/vector/property/model/fuzz/simulation/conformance/formal/benchmark test IDs; at least one E2E scenario ID unless the subject is proven compile-time-only with a registered justification; required fault and cancellation points; oracle independence class; required structured event IDs; secret/redaction classification; artifact retention class; replay command template; and the exact gate that consumes the evidence.

Every implementation bead must name task-specific tests for its owned clauses. Unit tests cover local totality, canonicalization, invalid tags/fields, arithmetic bounds, state preconditions, and error mapping. Property/model/fuzz tests cover generated inputs and mutation rejection. Simulation tests cover concurrency, cancellation, crash/restart, authority changes, virtual time, and deterministic seeds where applicable. E2E scripts exercise the public embedded/server/CLI robot surfaces through real subsystem composition, including success, refusal, degraded, retry, cancel, crash/recovery, and upgrade/restore paths appropriate to the subject. An E2E script cannot replace a missing unit/property oracle; a unit suite cannot satisfy the public composition row.

All E2E scripts are deterministic, noninteractive, bounded, and safe. They create isolated disposable fixture directories, use synthetic capabilities/keys and simulated donor/member loss, record exact inputs and toolchain/profile hashes, never target a pre-existing database, and never require deletion of user data. Cleanup is explicit best-effort fixture retirement; retained failure bundles are never silently removed. Robot output is versioned NDJSON and human decoration never contaminates it.

`DiagnosticEventId` rows define an exact versioned JSONL schema per transition/boundary: `event_version,event_id,subject_id,run_id,scenario_id,seed,virtual_time,role,posture,configuration_epoch,security_state_public_commitment,operation_id,state_before,state_after,decision_or_certificate_digest,oracle_id,verdict,failure_class,artifact_refs,replay_command`, with subject-specific typed extensions. Event ordering/cardinality and correlation are assertions, not merely debugging output. Secrets, capability bytes, plaintext protected values, DP seed material, hidden graph facts, raw tenant/principal identity, and nonpublic topology are forbidden; redaction/noninterference tests compare authorized and unauthorized runs including errors, sizes, timing class, and event presence. Logs use bounded cardinality and registered digest/public-commitment projections.

On any failure, the harness emits a content-addressed `VerificationFailureBundle` containing the minimal fixture manifest, exact binary/toolchain/profile hashes, seed and schedule, virtual-time trace, fault/cancellation plan, redacted ordered events, expected/observed oracle outputs, artifact refs, and one copy-paste replay command. Shrinking preserves the violated subject and authority posture. Successful gate evidence stores registry coverage summaries and digests rather than unbounded raw logs.

CI generation checks bijection and closure: every owned normative clause has a live subject; every subject has an owner, oracle, applicable unit/property layer, E2E row or approved compile-time-only justification, diagnostic schema, replay recipe, and consuming gate; every referenced test/scenario/event exists; every invariant/evidence/SLO/cost/command/frame row maps to verification subjects; stale tests and orphan logs fail. The same-change rule requires registry changes with any new normative schema, state arm, operation, frame, invariant, claim, or gate clause.

## Invariants & claims
Supports all FG-INV rows by making checker existence and coverage executable, especially FG-INV-01 structural concurrency, FG-INV-17 deterministic replay evaluation, FG-INV-19 byte replay, and FG-INV-20 authorization-before-observation. Test completion proves only the registered clause under the named configurations and oracle class; it never upgrades statistical evidence into proof or a partial model into a system-wide theorem.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes G0 invariant/evidence/SLO/cost/command/durable-field/frame registries and the threat model. `fgdb-sim`, `fgdb-reference`, subsystem test crates, protocol conformance suites, formal lanes, performance apparatus, and Observatory instantiate its rows. Every workstream epic and gate consumes the generated coverage report transitively through G0. Observatory owns production event transport; this task owns semantic event schemas and verification assertions. The wire/log taint checkers share redaction classifications but neither bypasses the other.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Registry schema, generators, stable IDs, versioning rules, and same-change CI lint are specified with no wildcard subject classes.
- A generated clause-to-test-to-event-to-gate matrix covers every current invariant, durable schema/state transition, command, GLA operator, FGP frame/state pair, recovery boundary, benchmark claim, and gate clause; omissions, duplicates, orphan tests, and orphan events fail fixtures.
- Unit tests validate registry parsing, referential closure, role/posture/configuration expansion, compile-time-only justification rules, event cardinality/order, redaction classification, and deterministic failure-bundle encoding.
- Property/mutation tests delete or corrupt each required field/link and prove CI rejects the manifest; fuzzing covers unknown IDs, cyclic aliases, incompatible oracle claims, and hostile diagnostic payloads.
- Simulation tests exercise crash/cancel/retry/virtual-time/authority-change event sequences and prove identical seed/profile inputs yield byte-identical redacted evidence bundles.
- E2E harness scripts run representative embedded, server, FGP, and CLI robot scenarios through success, refusal, crash/recovery, and replay; they use isolated synthetic fixtures, never pre-existing data, and emit a single machine-readable summary plus content-addressed artifacts.
- Noninterference tests compare authorized/unauthorized and before/after-revocation runs across result, error, timing class, event presence, sizes, and artifact metadata; forbidden secrets never appear in logs or bundles.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics conform to registered schemas; tests fail on missing, duplicate, out-of-order, uncorrelated, unbounded-cardinality, or secret-bearing events.
- Gate reports enumerate exact covered/missing/waived subject IDs, configuration coverage, oracle independence, artifact digests, and replay commands; no gate passes on an aggregate green bar with uncovered rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one generic “tests pass” checkbox, E2E-only coverage, snapshot logs without schemas, free-form debug strings as evidence, and production logging that reveals hidden state. Risk: registry overhead. Mitigation: generate boilerplate and matrices from the same normative registries while keeping task-specific assertions hand-authored and independently reviewed.

## Provenance
Plan §15 verification doctrine, §16 observability/operations, Appendix F live-checker closure, Appendix G same-change law, and the explicit project requirement for comprehensive unit tests, E2E scripts, and detailed logging.

title: Implement fgdb-authz-types nonconstructible permits and fgdb-policy verifier IR
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-authz-types` — the nonconstructible authorization permit family, centrally `AuthorizedMutationPermit` — and `fgdb-policy` — the restricted, versioned policy IR (`PolicyIr`) plus its deterministic evaluator and the trusted policy verifier that is the sole permit constructor in the codebase. Includes the fail-closed revocation interface. Warden (W9) administers issuance later; the verifier, permit type, and revocation interface are W1/W2 dependencies, not optional server middleware.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native): agents receive scoped, attenuable capabilities, so authorization must be a value the type system can carry, not a request-path filter. B1: permits bind branch/snapshot scope, so the One Version Universe's branches are security boundaries by construction. Market: every incumbent graph database treats security as server middleware that embedded mode silently loses; FrankenGraphDB makes enforcement a mandatory access type (§12.3) that even a forged internal call cannot bypass, because the coordinator independently re-verifies permits over FINAL effects. The restricted IR exists because the obvious alternative — evaluating policy as GQL — imports arbitrary recursion, procedure calls, and nondeterminism into the security boundary.

## Design — normative detail
No caller can submit bare mutation intents. `AuthorizedMutationPermit` is nonconstructible outside the trusted policy verifier (Rust type privacy: no public constructor, no Default, no deserialize-into-forgery; clients present credentials/token bytes, the verifier persists the record, and only a nonconstructible verified typed value crosses into database code). The permit binds, exactly: database security namespace/incarnation; tenant/principal/issuer; authority digest and a non-widenable operation ceiling; policy-semantics ObjectId; policy and revocation indices; root/snapshot and branch scope; exact read `GraphReferenceBinding[]` and write `CoordinateSchemaBinding[]`; topology epoch; expiry; channel/session binding where applicable; and a unique nonce. The coordinator (W4) verifies the permit's provenance and scope, recomputes authorization over the FINAL effects and any `CoordinateSchemaTransition[]`, and orders the authorization decision against revocation/policy changes.

`PolicyIr`: graph caveats compile to a versioned, deterministic, total, resource-bounded IR — never arbitrary GQL. Expressible: bounded label/type/property/system-field masks, scalar predicates, branch/time bounds, operation/resource limits, and finite allow-lists of procedure/UDF/module ObjectIds and invocation modes. Excluded: arbitrary recursion, procedure calls (policy evaluation never invokes those modules), nondeterministic functions, and unbounded path evaluation. A policy-version ObjectId identifies semantics permanently; old evaluators remain available for retained tokens or issuance is explicitly migrated/revoked — CI cannot enumerate hypothetical offline macaroons and pretend to prove semantic compatibility. The evaluator is packaged per `PolicySemantics {policy_id, version, policy_ir_ref, policy_ir_semantics_oid, evaluator_artifact_ref, scalar_profile_oid, unicode_and_collation_profile_oids, allowed_operation_classes, resource_ceiling_semantics, disclosure_contract_set, body_digest}`: deterministic, total, fuel/memory bounded, byte-matched to its semantics OID.

Revocation is fail-closed: an unavailable or stale revocation index denies; revocation is monotone (restored access requires a fresh subject/epoch — the full `RevocationSubject` machinery is W9, but the verifier-side check interface and its fail-closed contract land here). Downstream, `fgdb-secure-view` (W4) is the sole crate that can construct `AuthorizedSnapshot`/`AuthorizedCursor`/`AuthorizedGraphView`/`AuthorizedMutation`/`AuthorizedDerivedState`, with W1's verifier as the sole permit constructor behind that facade — planner pushdown is an optimization atop this boundary, never the authorization root.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (binding clauses): "Authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability." "Every authority-bearing durable schema binds one complete `SecurityStateBinding`; equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute." "Capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure." All invariant-class; no statistical claim may substantiate an authorization property.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-threat-model (authority lattice, per-posture footprint), w1-foundation-types (binding/reference types), w1-crypto (MAC/signature verification for token bytes and body digests). Produces the verifier consumed by: w4-secure-view and w4-coordinator (permit verification + independent final-effect re-verification), w9-threat-tokens (macaroon caveats compile to `PolicyIr`; issuance/revocation administration), w2-commit-protocol (authorization decision ordering against revocation/policy changes), w10-fgp-core (credential presentation path).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Compile-fail tests proving `AuthorizedMutationPermit` is unconstructible and unforgeable outside the verifier module. Mutation tests: flip each bound permit field (namespace, incarnation, ceiling, scope binding, topology epoch, nonce, expiry) — verification must fail per field, with a distinct typed error that is uniformly nonrevealing at the client surface. IR determinism: same IR + same inputs ⇒ identical decision and identical fuel consumption, under the lab runtime across seeds. Fuel/memory-bound tests: adversarial IR programs (deep masks, wide allow-lists) hit typed resource rejection, never unbounded evaluation. Fail-closed revocation: unavailable index, stale index, and concurrent-advance interleavings all deny. Evaluator artifact byte-match: modified evaluator with unchanged OID is rejected. Differential: IR evaluator vs. an independent naive evaluator over generated policy/graph corpora — delivered NOW as a minimal dependency-free naive interpreter beside the tests (this bead's dep closure does not include `fgdb-reference`), then re-hosted verbatim inside `fgdb-reference` under its allowlist when verif-reference lands (verif-reference depends on this bead, so a dep here would cycle) with the fgdb-reference leg validated at gate-genesis; the corpora and the differential harness are this bead's deliverables either way. Fuzz the IR decoder under App A length-before-allocation rules. Logging: every denial in tests records decision inputs (policy OID, indices, epochs) — never secret material. E2E: `authz_policy_e2e` — a scripted lab-runtime scenario that registers a `PolicySemantics` version with its pinned evaluator artifact, issues credentials, presents token bytes to the verifier, obtains an `AuthorizedMutationPermit`, drives a mutation through a stub coordinator that independently re-verifies over FINAL effects, then revokes and asserts fail-closed denial on the next presentation; the script restarts the harness mid-sequence to prove the revocation-check interface consults durable state, and finishes with an unavailable-revocation-index injection that must deny. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): the implementation logs every verification attempt with {policy_semantics_oid, policy version, security_policy_epoch, revocation_index, decision, typed denial class, fuel consumed} — never token bytes or secret material (asserted by a log-redaction test); tests assert one log record exists per denial and that its typed class matches the returned error; the e2e asserts the revoked presentation's decision log records a fail-closed denial naming the stale/unavailable-index reason.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: GQL as the policy language (recursion/nondeterminism/procedures in the security boundary); post-filter authorization (constitutionally a G1 gate failure); trusting a serialized permit across a process boundary (permits are process-local typed values; only credentials/tokens cross the wire); ambient "admin mode" bypass. Risk: IR expressiveness gaps discovered late force policy-version proliferation — mitigated by the permanent policy-version ObjectId design, which makes coexisting evaluator versions a supported state rather than a migration crisis.

## Provenance
§5.2 step 2 (permit definition); §12.2 (PolicyIr, PolicySemantics); §12.3 (mandatory access types, secure-view facade); §18.1; §19 W1/W4 rows.
acceptance_criteria:
### A21 exact durable permit and session-authorization format ownership

This bead is the unique implementation owner for the shared Appendix A permit format/type family: MutationPermitRecord<Local|Meta>, the distinct no-write ReadPermitRecord<Local|Meta>, AuthorityPermitRef<Local|Meta>, MutationPermitReadProjection<Local|Meta>, ReadCapablePermitRef<Local|Meta>, ImportedReadCapablePermitEvidence, and SessionAuthorizationRecord<Local|Meta> as frozen by fgdb-g0-authority-bindings-1xrl. It owns concrete role expansions, stable fields/tags, canonical codecs, body/transcript recipes, nonwidening and session-refresh validators, nonconstructible verified Rust wrappers, role/session/process/cross-group substitution negatives, golden/cross-version/mutation/fuzz corpus, and redacted diagnostics. AuthorizedMutationPermit remains a process-local verified wrapper over the exact persisted record; it is not a second durable schema or compatibility alias. W2/W12 own command-specific use and imported execution, W9 time authority owns TimeValidationEvidence, and W10/FGP/embedded surfaces own credential presentation and session issuance calls; those consumers may not duplicate or abbreviate these formats.

title: Build fgdb-codec: EF, varint, bitpack, snappy-class, roaring-like, identity-column codecs
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-codec`, the in-house compression/encoding library the closed universe requires: Elias–Fano monotone-sequence coding, delta-varint (canonical unsigned LEB128), bitpacking/FOR, a snappy-class block compressor, roaring-like compressed bitmaps, the registered identity-column codecs, and the `NeighborCodec` family — each with SIMD kernels (in `fgdb-unsafe-simd`) behind traits with scalar fallbacks.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B2 (Strata): the 2025 "Revisiting DGS" headline — 4–9× CSR space overhead across the dynamic-graph-store field — is the disease Strata's tiering cures: the hot minority pays delta overhead while the cold majority sits BELOW CSR via compression, and that compression is this crate. WCOJ machinery (§3.2 adopt row) is honest only if codec capabilities are honest: Elias–Fano neighbors support direct rank/select; other codecs get skip/decode paths — there is no pretending. Compression-ratio numbers are benchmark results tied to named corpora and encodings, never universal facts. Closed universe: no external codec crate exists in the allowlist, so every byte Strata stores flows through code owned here.

## Design — normative detail
`NeighborCodec` is the closed union `EliasFano | StreamVByte { skip_table } | DenseIntervals`. The intersection contract is normative: Elias–Fano neighbor lists support rank/select directly; StreamVByte lists use skip/fence metadata and bounded blockwise decode; dense intervals use interval arithmetic; Loom intersects without FULL-LIST decompression where the codec permits it — and there is explicitly no claim that Elias–Fano offsets provide rank/select over a separate varint stream. Sealed-run layout consumers rely on Elias–Fano offsets for O(1) list location. The identity-column codec (a G0-frozen decision, normative for `dst_VId`/`EId`/`stable_eids`/`OriginBirthOrder` columns): a registered order-preserving shared-prefix layout in which a block-header dictionary carries the `allocation_epoch`+`partition_id` components and the `monotone_slot` suffix is fixed-width or delta/FOR-coded; binary search and SIMD lower-bound operate on the fixed-width suffix under the header-extracted prefix, preserving canonical big-endian epoch‖partition‖slot order exactly; reverse-family blocks (destination-grouped, carrying source-partition EIds) may require multi-entry dictionaries and degrade gracefully toward raw width under adversarial prefix diversity. This encoding is what makes the ~4 KiB / ≤256-entry delta-block law hold (≤16 B per entry; raw 128-bit identities would cap a 4 KiB block near 95 entries). The layouts are registered as codecs in the run/block codec tables and, like every codec choice, are covered by the logical-digest validator over stable IDs — so encodings evolve without a format-identity change. Roaring-like bitmaps serve label bitmaps (§6.5) and hole/visibility metadata. The snappy-class compressor is deterministic under `CodecProfile` (canonical plaintext is deterministically compressed before AEAD — same input, same profile, same bytes). Encoding baseline for everything durable (App A): declared format major/minor, little-endian fixed integers, canonical unsigned LEB128 only where the field says varint, length-before-allocation, checked arithmetic, per-kind maximum sizes. Portable-SIMD is isolated behind `fgdb-codec`/kernel traits with scalar fallbacks; STRICT-mode kernels must be bit-identical across supported dispatch paths.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (binding clause): "Every claimed answer-equivalent ... codec/format rewrite ... preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract" — codec substitution is legal only under the logical-digest validator. Performance targets are `benchmark`/`slo` class, never invariants (constraints 11/12): §17 gate "Neighbor scans, sealed runs (decoded-cache path): ≥ 500M edges/s per core; ≥ 10B edges/s node aggregate (memory-bandwidth-bound: EF+varint decode ≥ 4 B/edge effective)". Decode-safety bounds (length-before-allocation, checked arithmetic) are invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-format-arms (identity-column codec definitions are a frozen G0 decision batch item), g0-identity-registries (codec-table registry rows), w1-foundation-types, w1-unsafe-ledger (SIMD islands). Produces codecs consumed by: w3-tier-r (per-list `NeighborCodec`, EF offsets), w3-tier-d + w3-identity-encoding (identity-column layout; w3 owns the 4KiB/256 block law built on it), w3-vertex-directory (roaring-like label bitmaps), w3-properties (columnar encodings), w7-fts/w7-btree (postings/keys), w1-generated-parsers (varint/framing primitives), w5-executor (decoded-cache path), perf-bench-core (gate rows).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Round-trip property + fuzz tests per codec (arbitrary monotone sequences for EF, adversarial gap distributions, malformed-input decode fuzz under allocation bounds); rank/select correctness differential vs. a naive oracle over randomized universes; identity-codec order-preservation property (decoded comparison order equals canonical big-endian epoch‖partition‖slot order — exhaustive small-domain enumeration plus randomized large-domain checks) and prefix-dictionary degradation tests under adversarial prefix diversity (must degrade toward raw width, never corrupt order); ≤16 B/entry accounting checks on representative corpora; snappy-class determinism (byte-identical output across runs/platforms for fixed profile); SIMD-vs-scalar bit-identity on every dispatch path (CI matrix across target features); compression-ratio benchmarks tied to named fnx-generator corpora with results recorded as benchmark-class rows; §17 neighbor-scan bench wiring with logged per-run manifests (corpus, codec table, machine profile). E2E: `codec_pipeline_e2e` — generate a named fnx-generator graph (the pinned Barabási–Albert fixture), build neighbor lists, encode every list under all three `NeighborCodec` arms plus the identity-column codec, run a seal -> scan -> intersect cycle (rank/select intersections checked against the naive oracle), decode, and assert logical-digest equality over stable IDs; the whole script repeats under SIMD and scalar dispatch with byte-identical encodings and identical scan results, under the lab runtime with a pinned seed. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): every encode/decode run emits structured rows {codec_id, corpus_id, entry_count, encoded_bytes, bytes_per_entry, dispatch_path, output_checksum}; the ≤16 B/entry accounting test asserts directly from the logged bytes_per_entry rows; fuzz harnesses log minimized failing inputs with seeds; bench runs log the full per-run manifest (corpus, codec table, machine profile) as stated above.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: LZ4/zstd/roaring-rs/other external crates (closed universe); raw 128-bit identity storage in blocks (space law fails); claiming rank/select capability for varint streams (the honest-contract rule exists precisely to forbid this); making codec choice part of format identity (the logical-digest validator decouples them so encodings can evolve). Risk: SIMD kernels drifting from scalar semantics — bit-identity CI is the guard; nightly portable-SIMD churn — isolation behind traits per §20.

## Provenance
§3.2 WCOJ row; §3.5 (Dostoevsky/S3-FIFO adapt context); §6.2 (identity-column law), §6.3 (run layout, NeighborCodec, intersection contract), §6.5; §17 scan gate; §18.2; App A.

title: Build fgdb-collections: ART/radix structures, succinct rank/select, vectorized hash tables
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-collections`: adaptive radix trees (ART) with path compression and lazy expansion, succinct bitvectors with rank/select support structures, and vectorized (SIMD-probed) hash tables. In-memory data structures only — nothing here is a durable format; durable bytes exist only through registry-generated encoders.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Closed universe (§18.2): ART/radix structures, succinct rank/select, and vectorized hash tables are on the explicit build-it-ourselves inventory. The SOTA context fixes their roles: Teseo (§3.1) is REJECTED as a primary store (PMA rebalance storms conflict with p99 goals) but its lesson — the vertex table must not be a straitjacket — makes the vertex directory an index, for which radix structures serve; GTX/Spruce/RapidStore/RadixGraph (§3.1 adapt row) contribute ART-indexed buffers and latch-free append lessons for Strata's write path. The FTS term dictionary is an ART over which Levenshtein automata walk for fuzzy(edit≤2) search (§10.3). Vectorized hash tables serve Loom's join/group-by kernels and the FreeJoin family (B3). Mechanical sympathy is inherited doctrine from frankensqlite (§2.3): cache-line-padded sharded tables, prefetch on descent.

## Design — normative detail
ART: byte-keyed adaptive nodes (the classical Node4/16/48/256 progression), path compression, lazy expansion; ordered iteration in key order (required for the term dictionary and any surface where iteration order can reach results); explicit interface for automaton-product traversal (Levenshtein automata over the term ART). Succinct rank/select: bitvector with o(n) directory supporting O(1) rank and select queries — the support structure under Elias–Fano high-bits queries (w1-codecs) and label/existence bitmaps. Vectorized hash tables: open-addressing layout with SIMD group probing (islanded in `fgdb-unsafe-simd` with scalar fallback), cache-line-conscious buckets, and an explicit determinism posture per B5/CGSE: any hash-table iteration order that can affect an answer or a canonical result encoding must either be canonically re-sorted by the caller or use a deterministic seed/iteration contract — hash seeds are never ambient entropy in strict execution; they come from the pinned execution context. All crates `forbid(unsafe_code)`; the only raw-pointer/SIMD code sits in ledgered islands behind safe traits with scalar fallbacks (constraint 2). Memory for query-scoped structures comes from asupersync region heaps with generational handles, so cancellation reclaims collection memory structurally (§2.1) — the collection types must be arena-compatible (allocator-parameterized) rather than hard-wired to the global allocator.

## Invariants & claim types
Constraint 2's ledger discipline binds every unsafe site used by these structures. FG-INV-12's coherence clause applies transitively: a collection whose iteration order leaks nondeterminism into a canonical result violates the determinism contract (constraint 4) — deterministic-iteration contracts are invariant-class where exposed. Throughput/probe-cost numbers are `benchmark` class on named fixtures only.

## Interactions
Consumes: w1-foundation-types (key/value types, canonical ordering), w1-codecs (rank/select shared with EF; bitmap interop), w1-unsafe-ledger (SIMD probe kernels). Produces structures consumed by: w7-fts (term-dictionary ART + Levenshtein automata), w3-buffer/w3-tier-d (buffer indexing per the RadixGraph/GTX lessons), w5-executor (vectorized hash join/aggregation, FreeJoin), w2-id-allocator (range bookkeeping), w8-kernels (masked-semiring workspaces).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property tests differential against `BTreeMap`/`HashMap` reference models (insert/delete/lookup/range/iteration over randomized operation sequences, including adversarial shared-prefix key sets for ART); ordered-iteration correctness (ART iteration equals sorted key order); rank/select exhaustive small-case verification plus randomized differential vs. naive scan; hash-table determinism test: fixed seed ⇒ identical iteration across runs and across SIMD/scalar dispatch; SIMD-vs-scalar bit-identical probe results; arena-compatibility test: structures allocate exclusively from a provided region heap and full reclamation occurs on region close (leak oracle from asupersync's suite); Miri/ASAN over island code paths; microbenchmarks (probe latency, ART point/range throughput) recorded as benchmark-class rows with machine profiles. E2E: `collections_e2e` — inside one lab-runtime region: build an ART term dictionary from a generated token corpus, run Levenshtein-automaton (edit≤2) product walks against a naive edit-distance oracle, execute a vectorized hash join of two generated relations against a BTreeMap-join oracle, answer rank/select queries over an EF high-bits bitvector, then cancel the region and assert full arena reclamation via the leak oracle; the script repeats across SIMD/scalar dispatch and two seeds with identical results. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): test-mode instrumentation logs {structure_kind, op_count, ART node-type histogram, probe-length distribution, iteration seed, dispatch_path, arena_id, bytes_allocated, bytes_reclaimed}; property tests log the failing operation sequence and seed on any counterexample; the e2e asserts the reclamation log shows bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated at region close and that iteration-order logs are identical across dispatch paths.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: PMA-based structures as primary (Teseo rebalance-storm lesson); external crates (im, hashbrown-as-dependency — note std's hasher is available but seed discipline is ours); pointer-chasing B-trees for in-memory dictionaries where radix wins on graph key distributions (the durable B-tree is w7-btree, a different artifact). Risk: ART worst-case memory on adversarial keys — bounded by resource accounting and documented degradation, never a correctness issue.

## Provenance
§2.1 (region heaps), §2.3 (mechanical sympathy row); §3.1 Teseo/GTX rows; §8.7 (executor kernels); §10.3 (FTS ART); §18.2.
