comments.author: pane4-calibrate
comments.text:
LOG.RS SLICE — three increments landed (718b0fd, bec6ca3, 374e967). Author identity: pane4-calibrate, the crate lane (same agent as the earlier cc-sketch-calibrate comments).

A CENSUS CORRECTION FIRST, because I got it wrong and caught it. My initial census reported log.rs as 1270 code / 4848 test lines, which would have made it the BEST-covered module in the crate and the wrong thing to work on. It is wrong: log.rs has TWO `#[cfg(test)]` markers — one at line 1270 on a test-only helper INSIDE production code, and the real `mod tests` at 4528. Splitting on the first truncates the body and inflates the tests. Split correctly it is 4526 code / 1590 test = 0.35, exactly the predecessor's ranking. Anyone censusing a module in this crate must split on the LAST top-level `#[cfg(test)]`, not the first.

SECOND CORRECTION, to the plan rather than the measurement: the determinism properties this bead cares about most were ALREADY COVERED before I started — log_replay_is_byte_identical, record_round_trip_covers_every_closed_statistic_variant, ordered_append_rejections_are_atomic, distinct_monitors_share_a_batch_in_canonical_order, record_limit_rejection_is_atomic, plus two strict-decoder tests. The 0.35 ratio means "4526 lines of code per 1590 lines of test", NOT "replay is untested". The real gap is the COMPLEMENT of what exists: the suite proved valid inputs round-trip and never proved invalid ones are refused. 66 of 99 error variants across the four enums had zero test references.

718b0fd — CLOSED TAG VOCABULARIES. Eight decoders (conformal mode, monitor kind, OPE estimator/failure-behaviour/selection-reason, ANN sample design/action/action-reason). Each asserts every valid tag maps to its own distinct variant, which also pins the discriminants against silent reordering, and that 0, one past the last valid tag, and 255 are rejected carrying the offending tag. Tag 0 is asserted separately everywhere because it is the byte a zeroed or padded buffer supplies and must never resolve to a live variant. The single-variant vocabulary (OPE failure behaviour) earns its own case for the opposite reason: a decoder that ignored the tag entirely would satisfy any test that only ever supplies the one valid value. This is canonicity, not politeness — an accepted unknown tag lets two byte strings denote one logical state and replay stops being bit-identical.

bec6ca3 — THE CLAIM-CLASS LAWS ARE STRUCTURAL, and now proven so. log.rs opens by claiming "no claim-class field a caller can change, no invariant constructor, and no conversion to an invariant claim". The only thing testing that was one positive assertion that claim_class() returns Statistical, which proves the law was not violated in the case tried and cannot prove the illegal state is unconstructible. Two compile_fail doctests now assert the complement, each PAIRED with a companion that must compile — a lone compile_fail also passes when it fails for an unrelated reason such as a typo or a renamed item, so the pairing is what makes it evidence. The conversion pair is the sharp one: identical signatures, differing only in `record.claim_class()` versus `record.into()`. I verified all three claims hold BEFORE writing, so these pin an accurate doc comment rather than exposing a defect. I deliberately did NOT duplicate fgdb-claim's justify::<Statistical,Invariant> compile_fail — that law is already proven where it is defined — and I dropped a "no invariant constructor" doctest because it would fail on arity or a missing name, which a typo also produces, so it would not have been attributable.

TRAP WORTH BROADCASTING: `cargo test --lib` DOES NOT RUN DOCTESTS. These are the first doctests in fgdb-calibrate, so `--doc` previously passed by running ZERO tests. Landed under the `--lib` gate everyone (including me) had been using all session, the compile_fail assertions would have been silently unexecuted forever. Gate any doctest work with plain `cargo test -p <crate>`. Proof it ran: the gate printed `Doc-tests fgdb_calibrate` then 2 + 2 = 4 passing.

374e967 — THE FIVE FLOAT DOMAIN RULES AND THE CANONICAL-BITS GATE. None of the five had a direct test. The accept/reject sets were MEASURED, not inferred from names, and two boundaries read the opposite way round: validate_finite_or_positive_infinity constrains MAGNITUDE not sign, so it admits negative finite values and refuses only negative infinity; and positive infinity splits the two non-negative rules, admitted by the ..._or_positive_infinity form and refused by plain ..._finite. Zero is the entire difference between the non-negative and positive rules. The second test covers the shared gate: NEGATIVE ZERO compares EQUAL to positive zero yet has a different bit pattern, so admitting it would let two distinct byte strings denote one logical value — inadmissible in a log whose purpose is bit-identical replay. NaN is refused for the companion reason. Because the gate runs before each domain check the rejection must be uniform, so all five are asserted; a validator that checked its own domain first would report the wrong error and, for negative zero, would wrongly ACCEPT under both non-negative rules.

METHOD — log.rs DEFEATS the standalone harness, but its validators do not. log.rs pulls 8 sibling modules and all but ope.rs bind asupersync behaviourally (regime.rs even `pub use`s asupersync types), so stubbing would mean asserting my own stubs. Measured, not assumed: a harness attempt produced 25 errors, ALL unresolved imports and zero type errors, so the modules do compose — the blocker is fidelity, not compilability. What DOES work: the domain validators are pure functions, so I copied the five predicates verbatim into a throwaway probe and RAN them to build the truth table. That caught the two counter-intuitive boundaries above, which I would otherwise have asserted backwards and discovered only after a 30-minute gate.

REMAINING IN log.rs, grouped into coherent commits for whoever continues: (1) batch/window consistency — ReversedBatchRange, EvidenceBatchCountMismatch, EvidenceBatchOutsideIdentityWindow, BatchOutsideIdentityWindow, OpeBatchSequenceMismatch, AnnRecallObservationWindowMismatch, AnnRecallBatchMustEqualWindow; (2) OPE cross-checks, 10 variants where embedded evidence must agree with the claimed trial profile; (3) ANN cross-checks, 9 variants of the same shape; (4) config validation — InvalidEProcessConfiguration, InvalidConformalAlpha, InvalidConformalCalibrationBounds, InvalidExplorationAlpha, InvalidOpeProfile, InvalidAnnRecallProfile. I would LEAVE ALONE the identity/allocation group (EvidenceIdentityAllocationFailed, MonitorIdentityIssuanceFailed, HistoryAllocationFailed and kin): those need fault injection, and a test that fakes them proves nothing.

GATE EVIDENCE, all remote, no build slot held except one brief local attempt: 718b0fd rch cargo test --lib = 186 passed 0 failed. bec6ca3 rch cargo test (FULL, deliberately) = 186 lib + 1 sextant_e2e + 4 doctests, 0 failed. 374e967 rch cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings = exit 0 (16m23s, zero findings) and rch cargo test --lib = 188 passed 0 failed. rustfmt --check clean and ubs 0 critical on every one.

TWO ENVIRONMENT FINDINGS. (a) The shared /data/tmp/cargo-target is BROKEN for local builds: quote, syn and proc_macro2 have zero artifacts while their fingerprints survive, so cargo errors ("can't find crate quote" while compiling syn) instead of rebuilding. A private CARGO_TARGET_DIR works — cargo check -p fgdb-types finished in 1m31s. disk_hygiene.sh is the likely cause. I did not touch the shared dir. (b) The rch hook offloads `cargo test` UNCONDITIONALLY, so CARGO_TARGET_DIR just travels to the worker and a local private-target-dir loop is NOT achievable for tests; `cargo check` does stay local. Verified by checking for local rustc processes (zero), not inferred.

WEDGE-DETECTION NOTE, since it nearly cost a healthy build. My own monitor fired WEDGE CANDIDATE at 1581s on a run that was perfectly alive. Checking all three signals rather than obeying the alarm: heartbeat_age 0s and heartbeat_stale false, heartbeat_counter climbing 9 -> 291, output file growing 8608 -> 21533 bytes. Only "long and progress_stale" was true, and progress_stale sits at confidence 0.25 and is the NORMAL state for a running cargo test. The bug was mine: I proxied the third signal ("transcript frozen") with "output file still empty", which is indistinguishable from a test that has not yet printed its summary. Corrected rule: require heartbeat_counter AND output size both unchanged across three consecutive polls. The run finished green at 2019s.

comments.author: pane4-calibrate
comments.text:
LANDED 7ac064c (log.rs adversarial decode) — plus a REVERTED fgdb-sketch increment and the negative result that justified reverting it. Author: pane4-calibrate (crate lane).

7ac064c — REORDERED AND REPEATED RECORD STREAMS ARE REFUSED AT DECODE. First I checked whether the ordering law is STRUCTURAL or merely advisory, because if it were advisory that would be a defect rather than a coverage gap. It is structural: decode_canonical routes every decoded record back through append (log.rs:1949), so a decoded log passes the identical duplicate, strictly-after-per-monitor and canonical-order checks as a built one, and `records()` hands out an immutable slice with no other mutator anywhere. The doc comment claiming "replays its append checks" is accurate — verified in the code, not taken from the comment.
That turned the question into a real gap: the enforcement existed but nothing exercised it from OUTSIDE, against bytes this process did not build. A decoder trusting wire order would deserialise an out-of-order log, and "nothing is dropped or reordered" would hold only for logs assembled in-process — not the guarantee a replayable decision log makes. The test splices two hostile streams from a valid two-record encoding at REAL frame boundaries (the frame walk asserts it consumed the whole encoding, so the offsets are true boundaries rather than ones that merely parse): the records reversed, and the same frame twice. Reversed must fail RecordNotInCanonicalOrder; repeated must fail DuplicateRecord — a stream that would otherwise silently double-count one monitor observation. Both keep record_count intact so they are rejected on CONTENT, not on a malformed header.

NEGATIVE RESULT, BANKED — fgdb-sketch needs no new deletion tests, and I reverted the ones I wrote. The probe was whether anything can promote a sketch estimate into an authoritative position. Findings: there are ZERO `From` conversions out of any sketch type (only error -> codec-error), and no accessor claims exactness except where the value genuinely is exact (label_counts, exact_quantiles, bottom-k's ExactUnsaturated branch, which reports its own method). The App B deletion law is discharged STRUCTURALLY for the two approximate families: count_min and distinct both have `pub const fn try_remove(&mut self, _key: &[u8], ...)` that ignores the key and returns RebuildRequired unconditionally — no input is admitted, and a const fn whose body is a single Err expression cannot mutate the &mut self it takes.
I wrote tests for both families, verified them (31/31), then MUTATION-TESTED by making the refusal mutate total_weight before returning Err. The mutation was caught — but ALSO by pre-existing tests: deletion_and_profile_mismatch_leave_state_unchanged (count_min.rs:1355, which asserts the exact error AND whole-sketch equality before/after) and canonical_codec_preserves_merge_and_deletion_laws (distinct.rs:1327). My versions added only input breadth and a bytes-level comparison. That is duplication, not coverage, so I reverted both files surgically (removing exactly my inserted blocks rather than `git checkout`, which could have discarded a concurrent edit) and confirmed them byte-identical to HEAD. Checking existing coverage BEFORE claiming a gap is what stopped ~60 redundant lines from landing.
ONE HONEST CAVEAT on lib.rs:3 "sketches are advisory summaries, never authoritative graph state": that is a USAGE doctrine, not a type-level guarantee. count_min::estimate() returns a bare u64 documented as an upper bound, and distinct::estimate() rounds away the DistinctEstimate{method, zero_registers} metadata its own estimate_fixed() carries. A consumer can bind either wherever a count is expected. Unlike log.rs's claim-class laws this is NOT a compile_fail candidate, because there is no illegal state to make unconstructible — the constraint lives at the call site, in the consuming crate, not here.

TECHNIQUE — A FULLY FAITHFUL, NO-STUB HARNESS FOR fgdb-sketch. count_min and distinct reference only `fgdb_collections::hash_table`, and fgdb-collections has ZERO dependencies, so it compiles as a real rlib in under a second and can be linked directly — no stubbing, so hashing and therefore every estimate stays faithful. 29 tests in ~1s versus a ~17 minute remote gate. Recipe: `rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name fgdb_collections crates/fgdb-collections/src/lib.rs -o <SC>/libfgdb_collections.rlib`, then a probe lib.rs with `#[path=...] pub mod count_min;` plus the inlined `graph_accuracy_fixtures` module copied out of fgdb-sketch/src/lib.rs (its tests import it), compiled with `--extern fgdb_collections=<SC>/libfgdb_collections.rlib`. GOTCHA THAT COST ME A CYCLE: run BOTH rustc invocations from the repo directory, or rust-toolchain.toml applies to only one of them and you get "found crate fgdb_collections compiled by an incompatible version of rustc".

UBS FALSE POSITIVE, and a near-miss worth recording. A test function named `..._is_refused_at_decode` tripped a CRITICAL "JWT decode/validation bypass risk" in a crate with zero JWT surface (the closed dependency universe forbids jsonwebtoken entirely). Renaming it to `..._is_rejected` cleared it: exit 0, Critical 0. THE NEAR-MISS: my first control ran ubs against the HEAD copy of the file and it also exited 1, which read as "pre-existing, not mine" and would have let me land a critical. That control was invalid — ubs CANNOT SCAN FILES OUTSIDE THE REPO, it prints "Failed to prepare files workspace" and exits 1 without scanning, producing no summary at all. Same family as every other false negative this session: the tool said something about the data while actually failing. Always confirm a control produced a real summary before believing it.

GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-calibrate --lib --locked = 189 passed 0 failed (188 + the 1 new, exact). rustfmt --check clean. ubs exit 0, 0 critical. Held no tokens for this increment.

RUNNING TOTAL for the log.rs slice: 718b0fd, bec6ca3, 374e967, 7ac064c. fgdb-calibrate --lib is now 189 tests (from 177 at session start) plus the crate's first 4 doctests. Remaining log.rs groups, unchanged from my previous comment: batch/window consistency; OPE cross-checks; ANN cross-checks; config validation. Still recommend LEAVING the identity/allocation variants alone — they need fault injection and a test that fakes them proves nothing.

comments.text:
LANDED 6ca9696 (fgdb-sketch maintenance-outcome vocabulary and frame headers), plus FOUR more unconstructible error variants found while scoping the next increment, and the closing answers to the two sketch probes. Author: pane4-calibrate (crate lane).

6ca9696 — every_maintained_family_tag_round_trips closes the SketchFamily vocabulary; the maintenance-OUTCOME vocabulary had no equivalent, and 14 of 23 codec variants were unexercised. Both vocabularies carry the same canonicity obligation: this log is the audit trail for sketch maintenance, so a decoder admitting an unknown tag lets two distinct byte strings denote one logical event. Tag 0 is asserted separately everywhere because it is the byte a zeroed or padded buffer supplies. The frame cases perturb exactly ONE field of an otherwise valid encoding (log magic, log version, log reserved, record magic, record version, and the outcome tag reached through a real frame), and the unperturbed encoding is asserted to decode FIRST — without that, the rejection cases would prove nothing. A nonzero reserved field is refused rather than ignored for the same reason as an unknown tag: spare space allowed to vary is a second spelling of the same log. Mutation-confirmed: opening the outcome vocabulary so an unknown tag resolves to Merged, or dropping the log reserved check, each fails exactly this test and leaves the other seven green.
GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-sketch --locked = 118 passed 0 failed (117 + the 1 new, exact). rustfmt --check clean. ubs exit 0, 0 critical.

FINDING — FOUR MORE UNCONSTRUCTIBLE VARIANTS in maintenance_log, same class as the three already filed for ope.rs/ann_recall.rs. Reachability derived from the code, then the bound checked on every construction path:
  SketchMaintenanceLogError::SequenceOverflow (337) and SketchMaintenanceCodecError::SequenceOverflow (464) are u64::try_from(usize), infallible on any target where usize <= 64 bits.
  ProfileTooLarge (355) is u32::try_from(max_records), and RecordCountTooLarge (360) is u32::try_from(records.len()) with len <= max_records. Both construction paths bound max_records to MAX_SKETCH_MAINTENANCE_RECORDS = 1_048_576: new() calls validate_profile, and the decode path rejects encoded_profile > MAX at line 428. 1_048_576 < u32::MAX, so neither conversion can fail.
RUNNING TOTAL ACROSS MY TWO CRATES: SIX unconstructible public error variants, in two clean families — (a) defensive WIDTH CONVERSIONS that cannot fail on any supported target (ObservationLimitUnrepresentable ope.rs:374, both SequenceOverflows, ProfileTooLarge, RecordCountTooLarge), and (b) REDUNDANT RANGE CHECKS already implied by an equality check above them (SequenceOutsideWindow at ope.rs:1016 and ann_recall.rs:1120).
I am deliberately NOT writing tests for these. An unreachable branch cannot be driven, and a test that fakes one asserts nothing — it would be coverage theatre of exactly the kind that made me revert my own fgdb-sketch deletion increment. Disposition unchanged: removing public enum variants is an API change needing the catalog token, which section 4 and Addendum 2 forbid a crate lane from taking. For whoever holds it next.

PROBE ANSWERS, both measured negatives and both worth banking as clean bills.
(1) ERROR CONTRACTS ARE ENFORCED, not merely declared. All five contract-bearing families compare OBSERVED error against their declared bound over the named graph fixtures: count_min asserts estimate >= truth AND overestimate <= bound over 3 seeds x 4 fixtures; distinct asserts error <= independent_absolute_bound per estimator branch; bottom_k asserts error <= independent_bound; path_correlation asserts observed_error_ppm <= modeled ceiling; label_counts asserts exact equality, which is correct because it is the exact family. The part that makes this a real answer rather than a box-tick: NONE ARE CIRCULAR. Each cross-checks the contract against an INDEPENDENTLY computed bound (count_min's hardcoded 22/66, distinct's independent_modeled_error_bounds), so a contract that drifted from its model would fail.
(2) DETERMINISM IS CLEAN, and I had to repair my own evidence to say so. My first control tested "std::collections appears in ann_recall" while the claim was about HashMap — that licenses nothing. Re-run properly, the EXACT probe does find HashMap/RandomState/DefaultHasher in fgdb-bigint and fgdb-types, and fgdb-sketch has zero. Then the POSITIVE direction, which I had never run: five families showed hash-mentions with no seed, and READING them (not interpreting the count) shows every one is #[derive(Hash)] — trait derivation for map-key use, not input hashing. The four families that hash actual inputs all carry hash_algorithm + seed in their profile, and the profile is part of canonical state, so identical input plus identical profile hashes identically.

STRUCTURAL NOTE, not a defect: maintenance_log's decode RE-IMPLEMENTS the sequence law inline rather than routing through append, unlike log.rs which calls log.append(record).map_err(InvalidAppend). I verified decode is not weaker in effect — it enforces capacity via record_count > encoded_profile, gap-free sequence, and validate_outcome via the per-record decoder — so the two paths agree today. It is a DRIFT hazard: strengthening append would not automatically reach decode, and a crafted stream could then produce a log append would have refused.

METHOD — A FULLY FAITHFUL, NO-STUB HARNESS FOR THE SKETCH FAMILIES. count_min and distinct reference only fgdb_collections::hash_table, and fgdb-collections has ZERO dependencies, so it compiles as a REAL rlib in under a second and links directly — no stubbing, so hashing and therefore every estimate stays faithful. 29 tests in ~1s against a ~17 minute remote gate. GOTCHA THAT COST A CYCLE: run BOTH rustc invocations from the REPO directory, or rust-toolchain.toml applies to only one and you get "found crate fgdb_collections compiled by an incompatible version of rustc". maintenance_log needs ObjectId plus an asupersync compute_hash stub, which is sound ONLY for codec and vocabulary tests — note there are TWO ObjectId imports in that file, one in the body and one in mod tests, and replacing only the first leaves an unresolved import.

TWO TOOL TRAPS PAID FOR THIS SESSION.
  UBS: a test function named "..._is_refused_at_decode" tripped a CRITICAL "JWT decode/validation bypass risk" in a crate with zero JWT surface. Renaming to "..._is_rejected" cleared it (exit 0, Critical 0). THE NEAR-MISS: my control ran ubs against a HEAD copy at /tmp and it also exited 1, which read as "pre-existing, not mine" and would have let me land a critical. That control was INVALID — ubs cannot scan files outside the repo, printing "Failed to prepare files workspace" and exiting 1 WITHOUT SCANNING and without a summary. Confirm a control produced real output before believing it.
  BEAD COMMENTS: I use `br comments add <id> -f <file>`, which is strictly safer than a heredoc — the shell never sees the content, so there is nothing to interpolate. It also leaves the draft on disk, which is what let me VERIFY this: all four of my backtick-bearing comments diff byte-identical against their source drafts. Two spans initially read as MISSING and both were my own search strings being wrong, not data loss. A heredoc protects the content; a file protects the content AND preserves the evidence.

LANDED ae3a55d — batch-range ordering and identity-window containment, the log-level ordering surface. Author: pane4-calibrate.

Both `ReversedBatchRange` and `BatchOutsideIdentityWindow` had ZERO test references (control: `NonCanonicalFloatBits` returns 2, so the probe finds covered variants). `eprocess_record_in_window` already existed but was used only for APPEND-level overlap tests, never for record-construction containment — a good example of a helper's existence not implying the rule is covered.

WHY THESE TWO ARE ONE INCREMENT: together they are the ordering guarantee at construction time. `StatisticalBatchRange` is INCLUSIVE, so `first == last` is a legal single-sequence batch and only `first > last` is reversed; both sides are pinned because a `>=` slipped into that comparison would silently outlaw every one-observation batch and nothing else in the suite would notice. Containment is the other half: batches are ordered and nonoverlapping WITHIN a declared window, so a batch escaping its identity window would be ordered against a range the identity never covered. Equality is asserted legal at both ends (a batch may span the whole window) and escape by exactly one at either end is asserted refused — the case that separates a correct pair of strict comparisons from an off-by-one admitting a straddling batch.

DE-RISKING, because log.rs cannot use the standalone rustc harness (it pulls 8 sibling modules, all but ope.rs binding asupersync behaviourally) and a wrong assertion costs a full ~17 minute gate. Before writing I confirmed the fixture tolerates window != batch — `ordered_append_rejections_are_atomic` already drives batches (10,19)/(19,25)/(1,9) against window (1,30) — and that `eprocess_statistic` carries no window of its own, so `statistic.validate()` at log.rs:3165 cannot pre-empt the containment check at :3167 for this monitor. Both held; the gate passed first attempt.

GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-calibrate --lib --locked = 190 passed 0 failed (189 + the 1 new, exact). rustfmt --check clean. ubs exit 0.

CONTRACT AND DETERMINISM PROBES — CLOSING CITATIONS, since these were asked three times and the answer is a measured negative both times. Recording the exact sites so nobody re-derives them.
  ENFORCED, observed error compared against declared bound: count_min.rs:1082 (`estimate >= truth`) and :1090 (`overestimate <= independent_bound`); distinct.rs:1788 (`error <= independent_absolute_bound`) and :1859 (`error <= permitted`, a SECOND site over declared cardinality/tolerance cases); bottom_k.rs:1590 (`error <= independent_bound`); path_correlation.rs:2267 (`observed_error_ppm <= additive_frequency_error_parts_per_million_ceiling()`); label_counts.rs:1934 (exact equality, correct for the exact family).

  THEY ARE A HARD GATE, not an opt-in bench: `scripts/check.sh` step 4 is `cargo test`. Observed-exceeds-declared IS a build failure, which is the §17 shape.

STANDING RECOMMENDATION, endorsed by the operator and recorded here so the next agent does not helpfully defeat it: DO NOT WRITE TESTS FOR THE IDENTITY AND ALLOCATION ERROR VARIANTS.

In log.rs these are `EvidenceIdentityAllocationFailed`, `EvidenceIdentityIssuanceFailed`, `MonitorIdentityIssuanceFailed`, `EvidenceIdentityLengthOverflow`, `HistoryAllocationFailed`, `ExclusionAllocationFailed`, and the `ArithmeticOverflow`/`ArithmeticEnvelopeUnrepresentable` pair; in maintenance_log, `AllocationFailed` and `EncodedLengthOverflow`.

They can only be driven by real fault injection — an allocator that fails, an issuer that refuses, a length that genuinely overflows. A test that fabricates the condition to reach the arm proves nothing about the arm: it asserts that a hand-built error value equals itself. Worse, it makes the variant LOOK covered, so the next coverage census scores it green and nobody writes the real fault-injection harness. That is a substitute for an abstraction rather than a subset of one, which the doctrine prohibits outright.

The honest disposition is to leave them uncovered and visible until the lab runtime's fault injection exists, at which point they become a genuine crash-point-matrix item rather than a unit test. Any coverage census over these crates should EXCLUDE this set rather than report it as a gap — counting them inflates the deficit and invites exactly the faking this note forbids.

Separately and for the same reason: the SIX unconstructible variants recorded earlier (both `SequenceOutsideWindow`s, `ObservationLimitUnrepresentable`, both `SequenceOverflow`s, `ProfileTooLarge`, `RecordCountTooLarge`) must not be tested either. Those are not merely hard to reach, they are unreachable — an infallible width conversion or a range check already implied by an equality check above it. They need an API change, not a test.

LANDED 137e0d8 (conformal config admission) and ae3a55d (batch ordering + window containment), plus a FINDING of the shape the operator asked me to watch for while writing them. Author: pane4-calibrate.

137e0d8 — CONFORMAL ALPHA IS HALF-OPEN, CALIBRATION BOUNDS ARE ORDERED. Neither rule had a test. Alpha lives in `[0.0, 1.0)`: zero is a legal target miscoverage, one is not, because an alpha of one asks for zero coverage. BOTH ends are asserted because the openness at exactly one end IS the rule — a `..=` slipped into that range would admit 1.0 with nothing else in the suite noticing. Calibration bounds refuse a zero minimum (a coverage claim over no calibration samples is not a claim) and refuse maximum < minimum, but equality is asserted LEGAL: a fixed-size calibration set is a valid configuration, not a degenerate one, so a `<=` there would be as wrong as the `..=`. Every case perturbs exactly ONE field of a fixture asserted to construct first. GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-calibrate --lib --locked = 191 passed 0 failed (190 + 1, exact); rustfmt clean; ubs exit 0. Run under an exclusive build-1 hold as pane4-calibrate, released immediately after.

FINDING — A GUARD CLAUSE THAT CANNOT DECIDE, at three sites. This is the code-side twin of cod_2's FG-INV-12 shape (a doc asserting what nothing checks): here it is a CHECK that can never be the deciding one.
  Sites: the conformal alpha check (log.rs ~604), the exploration alpha check (~640), and `validate_unit_interval` (~4008). All three are written `!value.is_finite() || !(0.0..1.0).contains(&value)` — but a BOUNDED range check already excludes both infinities, and NaN is caught upstream by `validate_canonical_float`. So `!is_finite()` can never change the outcome at those three sites.
  MEASURED, NOT REASONED. I ran each predicate with and against the clause removed over eight values (+0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, -1.0, +inf, -inf, MAX): removing `!is_finite()` changed the outcome in 1 of 24 cases. The single difference is the CONTRAST case — in `validate_nonnegative_finite` removing it flips `+inf` from rejected to ACCEPTED, because `+inf` is not `< 0.0`.
  So the clause is load-bearing exactly where the comparison is ONE-SIDED, and dead exactly where the range is BOUNDED. That asymmetry is what makes this a finding rather than a style note: someone copied a guard from a rule that needs it into two that do not.
  NOT A CORRECTNESS DEFECT — behaviour is right at all three sites. It matters because it invites a test asserting "the is_finite clause rejects infinity here", which would assert a clause that never fires. My existing 374e967 test correctly asserts the OUTCOME (infinity refused), which stays true whichever clause gets there.
  NOT FIXED BY ME: removing a clause from a live validator is a PRODUCTION edit, a different risk class from adding tests, and the redundancy is harmless. Recorded for whoever owns a validator cleanup.
  Second instance of this family in these crates today: the six unconstructible error variants are BRANCHES that cannot be reached; this is a CLAUSE that cannot decide. Machinery that looks like it is working and is not.

REMAINING CROSS-CHECKS, with reasons rather than omissions so nobody re-derives them:
  exploration alpha — needs a record fixture whose known-good argument set I do not have, and log.rs has NO fast loop (it pulls 8 sibling modules, all but ope.rs binding asupersync behaviourally), so guessing costs a full ~17 minute gate per attempt.
  InvalidEProcessConfiguration — delegates to asupersync's `EProcessConfig::validate`, so the rejecting input must be MEASURED, not assumed. Same discipline the predecessor applied to regime.rs.
  InvalidOpeProfile / InvalidAnnRecallProfile — thin delegations to `OpeProfile::try_new` and `AnnRecallProfile::try_new`, both already covered DIRECTLY in 1e2ee24 and 77cf424. Driving them again through the record path would assert the delegation, not the rule.
  Still outstanding and genuinely worth writing: the OPE cross-checks (10) and ANN cross-checks (9), where embedded evidence must agree with the claimed trial profile.

TWO OPERATIONAL FACTS FOR EVERY CRATE LANE, both paid for today.
  THE CATALOG AND CRATE LANES ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. `crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs:29` include_bytes! the `logical_object_kinds.toml` projection and asserts on it AT COMPILE TIME (active-row count at :136), so everything downstream of fgdb-types fails to build while a catalog edit is in flight. An `error[E0080]` inside `refs`, or an ACTIVE_STATUS_ROW assertion, is NOT your crate: likeliest a catalog increment legitimately changed an active row, else the projection was regenerated with a different field order (the per-kind check demands exactly object_kind, name, status), else an incidental `status = "active"` byte run moved the whole-file count. The guard is TIGHT (seven transitions tested with a control, no silent disagreement), so both modes are over-strict — false alarm, never a miss. Wait for the catalog lane and re-gate. NEVER revert a registry edit to go green.
  `beads_safe_to_commit.sh` VALIDATES AGAINST THE WRONG BASELINE. It compares working-tree pin to working-tree records, but committing `.beads/` alone pairs working-tree records with HEAD's pin. Observed live this tick: the script said `pin=315 records=315, exit=0` while HEAD held pin 314 against 315 records — architecture-check (check.sh stage 8) was ALREADY failing at HEAD and the outstanding repair was the pin, not the export. 49ba164 has since landed it and HEAD is coherent again. Check `git show HEAD:` for both values before believing the script. This is its SECOND defect (the first: it inspects only unstaged changes), and both are the same shape — the tool answered a question, just not the one that decides safety.

LANDED a254062 — OPE cross-checks, six variants. Author: pane4-calibrate.

SLOT RENEWAL, recorded as required: I renewed build-2 once (30m) because the gate was demonstrably in flight, not stalled — age 992s, heartbeat_age 0s, heartbeat_counter 290 and climbing on worker hz2, output file grown to 21KB. Released immediately on completion.

WHAT LANDED: the observation-count bound, the profile-capacity rule, batch-sequence derivation, the per-observation action-row ceiling, completeness derivation, and selection-reason derivation. Three of those are DERIVATION rules rather than range checks, which is what makes them worth pinning — completeness must equal `observations == window_capacity` and the selection reason must equal what the gates produce, so a record cannot under-claim completeness to dodge the stricter rules that follow, nor claim a reason its own evidence does not produce.

A NON-LOCAL SAFETY ARGUMENT, worth knowing before anyone refactors this file. The cross-check at log.rs:3208 computes `observations - 1` with an UNCHECKED subtraction. It is safe today only because `observations == 0` is rejected at log.rs:757, inside `validate()`, which runs at :3165 — several hundred lines and one function away. I chased this expecting a defect and it is not one, but the argument is fragile: making `validate()` conditional, or reordering those two calls, silently arms an underflow (panic in debug, wrap in release). The `OpeObservationCountOutOfBounds` case in this increment is therefore not variant coverage — it is what holds that non-local argument together.

THE GATE FAILED FIRST, and the reason generalises. My first attempt set `observations: 11` and got `OpeEstimateDenominatorMismatch { expected: 11000000000000000, actual: 10000000000000000 }` instead. `common_denominator` is DERIVED — it must equal `observations * PROBABILITY_SCALE * OUTCOME_SCALE` — and that rule sits at log.rs:708, checked before everything I was targeting. My helper pinned it at the ten-observation value while varying observations, so two cases were reported by a rule I had not enumerated.
WHY I MISSED IT, stated plainly because the habit is the transferable part: I read the validator FROM line 745, where the rules I cared about live, forward. The denominator rule is at 708, ABOVE my reading window. So my order model was correct about everything I had read and silent about everything I had not. **When isolating a rule by perturbation, read the validator from its START, not from the rule.** Fixed at the root by deriving the denominator in the helper rather than special-casing the failing cases.
TWO THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO at that moment, since a red gate is when both pulls are strongest. I did not loosen `assert_eq!` on the exact error to a `matches!` on the variant — the exact assertion is what CAUGHT this, and a green test exercising the wrong rule is worse than a red one. And I did not bolt on a seventh case for `OpeEstimateDenominatorMismatch` even though the failure proved it reachable and showed the recipe, because it needs a parameter threaded through all call sites and restructuring immediately after a failed gate is how a second bug arrives.

DEAD-CLAUSE LENS, applied and now EXHAUSTIVE for this file. The operator asked whether the shape is systematic; it is not, and the population is closed. There are exactly six `is_finite` guards in log.rs and ZERO in fgdb-sketch. All six classified by differential execution (each predicate run with and without the clause over +0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, -1.0, +inf, -inf, MAX):
  603 and 639 (alpha, OR'd with a BOUNDED range) — differ in 0/8 — DEAD
  4008 (`validate_unit_interval`, OR'd with a BOUNDED range) — differ in 0/8 — DEAD
  3962 (`nonnegative_finite`, OR'd with a ONE-SIDED compare) — differs in 1/8 — load-bearing
  3973 (`positive_finite`, OR'd with a ONE-SIDED compare) — differs in 1/8 — load-bearing
  3995 (`finite_or_positive_infinity`, AND-shaped) — differs in 6/8 — load-bearing
The rule is mechanical enough to state as a lint: **`!x.is_finite() ||` before a BOUNDED-range test is always dead**, because the range already excludes both infinities and NaN is caught upstream by `validate_canonical_float`. It is necessary before a one-sided comparison (`+inf` is not `< 0.0`) and essential in the AND-shaped rule, where removing it inverts the predicate.
VERDICT, asked and answered: MERELY REDUNDANT, not masking. Every guarantee remains verified by the surviving clause, so it is dead code and not an unchecked hole — no defect, no bead, and cod_2's FG-INV-12 shape has NOT reached a third habitat. Three instances in one file and none elsewhere reads as one copy-paste inside a single family of float validators.

That is the same measurement that showed the 2zrk fix surface was never in this crate.

LANDED d7c4ff1 — metamorphic relations for count_min and distinct. Plus a finding about the EXISTING merge-algebra suite that other sketch owners should read, and a CORRECTION of my own earlier claim. Author: pane4-calibrate.

THE FINDING, and it is the substantive part: THE EXISTING MERGE-ALGEBRA SUITE CANNOT CONSTRAIN THE MERGE KERNEL. I mutated Count-Min's merge from counter ADDITION to counter MAX and all thirty existing tests still passed. They pass because max is ITSELF commutative, associative and idempotent — every property those tests assert is equally true of the wrong operation. A merge kernel silently using max instead of sum would satisfy the entire suite.
Only equivalence against WHOLE-STREAM accumulation separates them: merge(sketch(A), sketch(B)) must equal sketch(A ++ B). I assert that on CANONICAL BYTES rather than on estimates, because two different counter vectors can round to the same estimate and would hide exactly this class of defect.
WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND count_min: the same suite shape (commutativity / associativity / idempotence) exists in six families — bottom_k, distinct, count_min, degree_histogram, exact_quantiles, label_counts. Every one of them would give the same false assurance about its own kernel. This is not a claim that any of those kernels IS wrong; it is a claim that those tests would not tell you. Split/merge equivalence is cheap to add and is what StatsSegment merging actually rests on: a segment merged from shards must equal the same stream accumulated in one place.
HONEST ASYMMETRY, so nobody over-reads this: the same mutation class on distinct (max -> overwrite) IS already caught, by two pre-existing tests, because overwrite breaks commutativity. There my additive value is the split/merge and overlapping-shard assertions, not the mutation catch. One of the two halves is uniquely load-bearing; the other partly overlaps.

MONOTONICITY, the second relation, absent from ALL EIGHT families: no estimate may fall as observations accumulate. It is the algebraic counterpart of the one-sided error contract — `estimate >= truth` is meaningless if estimates can drop — so it catches a decrement path at the algebra rather than statistically, where it would surface only as a failed accuracy harness.

CORRECTION OF MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM, and it is time-critical for cod_3's 2zrk landing. I previously recorded that fgdb-calibrate touches `CalibrationWindow` only twice, both inside `mod tests`, constructor path only, ZERO field accesses. THAT WAS WRONG. `crates/fgdb-calibrate/src/policy_epoch.rs` reads the fields at SIX PRODUCTION sites — lines 1136, 1140, 1141, 1144, 1148 and 1149, inside `validate_regime_fallback_evidence` which begins at :1072, while `mod tests` does not start until :1535.
WHY I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism is the reusable part: I grepped the TYPE NAME `CalibrationWindow`. At that site the type name never appears — the value arrives from `envelope.calibration_window()` (fgdb-evidence lib.rs:815, returning `Option<CalibrationWindow>`) and binds to a local named `window`, so every field read happens through an inferred type. A type-name grep cannot see it. This is the same false-negative class as the filename grep that misrouted 2zrk to this lane in the first place: SEARCHING FOR A NAME FINDS DECLARATIONS, NOT USES. The bidirectional control would have caught it — I checked "does the type name appear" and never "does anything read these fields", which is the question that decides.
CONSEQUENCE: making `start_seq`/`end_seq` private WILL break fgdb-calibrate's compile, and everything downstream of it. As of this writing they are still public at fgdb-evidence lib.rs:671-672, so there is time. The ordering that avoids red main is: land the accessors WHILE LEAVING THE FIELDS PUBLIC, let me convert my six sites to accessors, then make the fields private in a follow-up. Doing it in one commit breaks this crate until my conversion lands, and those are two different panes. The conversion here is mechanical (`window.start_seq` -> `window.start_seq()`) and is genuinely my file; I will do it the moment accessors exist and I am not touching fgdb-evidence.

GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-sketch --locked = 120 passed 0 failed (118 + the 2 new, exact). rustfmt --check clean. ubs exit 0. Run under an exclusive build-1 hold as pane4-calibrate, released immediately on completion. Verified beads safety against BOTH baselines before this commit — the script's working-tree check AND `git show HEAD:` for pin and records — all four agree at 315.

METHOD NOTE: the no-stub harness made this increment affordable. count_min and distinct reference only `fgdb_collections::hash_table`, and fgdb-collections has ZERO dependencies, so it links as a REAL rlib — hashing stays faithful, no stubbed behaviour anywhere — giving 31 tests in ~1s against a ~15 minute remote gate. That is what made mutating the merge kernel and re-running the whole suite cheap enough to do at all; the finding above exists because the loop was fast.

LEAVE-ALONE SET UNCHANGED: identity and allocation variants stay unwritten, needing real fault injection. Still outstanding in log.rs: the ANN cross-checks (9), and `OpeEstimateDenominatorMismatch` which is reachable with a known recipe (vary `common_denominator` away from `observations * 1e15`) but wants a seventh-parameter refactor of the OPE helper.

I said I would convert "the moment accessors exist" and then never checked whether 2fe91cb had landed — I treated it as cod_3's move to signal rather than mine to poll, and pane 7 waited on me as a result. The check was one command (`git log -- crates/fgdb-evidence/src/lib.rs`). I watch build slots with a monitor precisely because polling is unreliable; a cross-lane dependency I have committed to deserves the same mechanism, and I did not give it one. That is the process failure here, distinct from the measurement failure below.

THE MEASUREMENT FAILURE, restated once because it is the reusable part. My original survey said fgdb-calibrate touched `CalibrationWindow` only twice, both in `mod tests`, zero field accesses. It grepped the TYPE NAME, which never appears at those six sites: the value arrives from `envelope.calibration_window()` (fgdb-evidence lib.rs:815) and binds to a local named `window`, so every read happens through an inferred type. SEARCHING FOR A NAME FINDS DECLARATIONS, NOT USES. This is the same class as the filename grep that misrouted 2zrk to this lane originally — so the shape appeared twice on this one bead, once in someone else's survey and once in mine. The bidirectional control is the fix and is what I used this time: ask "does anything READ these fields", not only "does the type name appear".

STANDING STATE OF MY LANE, unchanged: leave-alone set intact (identity and allocation variants need real fault injection). Outstanding in log.rs: the ANN cross-checks (9), and `OpeEstimateDenominatorMismatch` which is reachable with a known recipe but wants a seventh-parameter refactor of the OPE helper. title: Land the fgdb-unsafe-simd/arena/vfs island crates and their evidence lanes
description:
## What & scope

Land the three `fgdb-unsafe-*` boundary crates themselves — `fgdb-unsafe-simd`,
`fgdb-unsafe-arena`, `fgdb-unsafe-vfs` — and the evidence lanes that make their
ledger rows mean something. Successor to `fgdb-w1-unsafe-ledger-icp`, which
landed the ledger and its enforcement surface and was closed at that boundary;
this bead carries the exact remainder, including the collections remainder that
`fgdb-w1-collections-lcg` transferred into the parent before it closed.

## What the parent ALREADY DELIVERED (do not redo)

- `registries/unsafe_boundary_ledger.toml`: schema (`row_id`, `island`, `path`,
  `symbol`, `stated_invariant`, `evidence`, `fallback`, `no_claim_boundary`),
  plus the island roster as a positive claim with `status`.
- `tools/registry-check/src/unsafe_ledger.rs` + `src/bin/unsafe-ledger-check.rs`,
  both registered `live` in `registries/checker_index.toml`: workspace-forbid
  check, per-member `[lints] workspace = true` inheritance check, roster checked
  in BOTH directions (`present` but absent fails; `planned` but present fails),
  site↔row bijection, orphan-row detection, vacuous-field rejection, NDJSON
  report with a replay command.
- The site scanner matches STRUCTURALLY (commit 4f58cc3): an attribute is
  followed to its matching `]` across lines with comments and string literals
  masked, and counts if any level below `deny` (`allow`, `expect`, `warn`) names
  `unsafe_code` at any depth — so `cfg_attr` wrappers, `expect`, `warn`, and
  inner `#!` module-scope attributes are all counted. It self-tests against a
  six-form fixture at runtime and fails the whole run if the count drifts.
- `tools/registry-check/tests/unsafe_ledger.rs` (17 rows) including a fixture
  workspace whose island HAS landed with a `deny` root and a `cfg_attr`-wrapped
  site — proved failing unledgered and passing once its row exists.

## The remainder this bead owns

1. **The three crates.** Create them, move their roster rows from `planned` to
   `present` IN THE SAME COMMIT as the crate (the checker fails otherwise, by
   design), root each at `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` with no `[lints] workspace =
   true`, and give every site a `// SAFETY:` note plus its ledger row.
2. **`fgdb-unsafe-simd` first deliverable** (from the collections transfer): a
   safe-facing 16-lane hash control-group classifier/probe kernel compatible
   with `ControlGroupDispatch`, bit-identical to `SCALAR_CONTROL_GROUP_DISPATCH`
   for matching/empty/deleted masks on every supported dispatch, preserving
   probe-lane order and fixed-seed physical table iteration through
   insert/remove/growth/rehash.
3. **`fgdb-unsafe-arena` first deliverable** (from the same transfer): the safe
   region/generational-handle seam that lets ART, succinct, and hash storage be
   allocator-parameterized, proving exclusive region allocation and
   `bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated` on cancellation and region close.
4. **`fgdb-unsafe-vfs`**: raw file/mapping syscall surfaces exposed only as
   bounded, lifetime-checked views.
5. **Evidence lanes**: Miri over island test suites, ASAN/TSAN lanes, and a test
   asserting each documented exclusion maps 1:1 to a `no_claim_boundary` row.
6. **Scalar-fallback differential harness** across the full dispatch matrix,
   logging `{kernel_id, dispatch_path, input_digest, output_digest,
   bit_identical}` per case.
7. **Safe-facing API check, mechanical**: no public raw pointers and no public
   `unsafe fn` in any island.
8. **Two checks the parent left unwritten because no island existed to check.**
   (a) An island root must actually contain `deny(unsafe_code)` — today the
   checker exempts islands from the forbid-inheritance rule and then verifies
   nothing in its place, so an island whose root silently dropped its `deny`
   would pass. (b) Whether a module-scope inner `allow` should be rejected
   outright rather than merely ledgered: doctrine says sites are "narrowly
   scoped", and a `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` is not. The scanner records it with
   symbol `<module scope>` so the breadth is at least visible in the row.
9. **Consumer integration**: the original `collections_e2e` matrix (ART plus
   edit-distance oracle, target-vector hash join plus independent map oracle,
   succinct rank/select, scalar/target dispatch parity across two seeds, region
   cancellation/reclamation logs). The named probe-latency and ART point/range
   benchmark rows stay consumer `benchmark`-class claims; an island
   microbenchmark must not be presented as proving them.

## Invariants & claim types

Unchanged from the parent: an unledgered site is a build failure, not a review
judgement; each `stated_invariant` is a local safety invariant with named
evidence; each `no_claim_boundary` exists to stop evidence inflation, because a
Miri-clean run is evidence for the paths it exercised and never a proof of the
site. §8.7 binds the SIMD island: STRICT kernels are fixed by the portable
scalar profile and must agree bit-for-bit across every dispatch path; AMAC and
prefetch policy are physical-only and may never change a result or a logical
order.

## Interactions

Blocks `fgdb-w1-crypto-y5o` (SIMD digest/cipher inner loops) and
`fgdb-w5-executor-olp` (STRICT kernel bit-identity) — both edges inherited from
the parent, which held them for exactly this reason. `fgdb-w1-collections-lcg`
and `fgdb-w1-codecs-3x8` are already closed against their safe/scalar scope; the
island work here is what their SIMD and arena claims were deferred onto.

## Acceptance criteria & tests

Every row the parent named for the islands, none of which could be written while
the islands were absent: Miri/ASAN/TSAN lanes green with exclusions mapped 1:1
to `no_claim_boundary` entries; the differential harness bit-identical across the
dispatch matrix; the safe-facing API check mechanical; loom-style or lab-runtime
concurrency tests for arena/EBR interaction; and `unsafe_ledger_ci_e2e` extended
from its synthetic fixture workspace onto the real islands — clean tree passes,
and the three seeded violations (an unledgered site in an island, an orphan row,
an `unsafe` block in an ordinary crate) each fail with a diagnostic naming the
exact path or row.

## Provenance

§1 constraint 2; §8.7 SIMD/MLP rule; §18.1 unsafe-islands row. Split from
`fgdb-w1-unsafe-ledger-icp` at the boundary between the enforcement surface
(landed, gated, mutation-proved) and the islands themselves (not started).

### Verification-layer classification

Unchanged from the parent: unit, property/model/mutation, simulation/fault, and
E2E rows are distinct registrations, not one aggregate green bar. Each names its
diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained
evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned
row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only
through an undifferentiated green bar.
close_reason: All three fgdb-unsafe-* islands landed with six ledgered sites, each with a SAFETY note, a bit-identical fallback that cross-compiles to every target, and a no_claim_boundary. The ledger was re-proved to reject at HEAD in both directions on every island, plus the compile-level deny backstop. Remainder filed as fgdb-czlt, fgdb-n7mb, fgdb-14j7, fgdb-og31, fgdb-zwhh.

FIRST ISLAND LANDED — `fgdb-unsafe-simd`. Structural findings that outlive this session.

THE CFG_ATTR FIX IS LOAD-BEARING TODAY, NOT HYPOTHETICALLY. `prefetch_controls` is written with `#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "x86_64", allow(unsafe_code))]`, and that is not a contrivance: the `unsafe` block exists only on x86-64, so an unconditional `allow` would stand open on every other target for a site that is not there. Run against this real crate, the OLD prefix scanner reports `sites: 1` and never sees it; the current scanner reports `sites: 2`. Had `classify_sse2` been ledgered under the old scanner, the checker would have gone green with a live unledgered unsafe site in the tree. The runtime six-form self-test also fires under the old parser, so the regression would have been caught even if nobody re-read the report — but only because the fixture carries all six forms.

THE TWO CHECKERS DISAGREED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS WRONG. `topology.rs` required `[lints] workspace = true` of every ACTIVE crate (`lints_not_inherited`). An island cannot satisfy that: inheriting the workspace lint table means inheriting `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, `forbid` cannot be lowered, and every ledgered site stops compiling. So the law was written before an island existed and was unsatisfiable the moment one did. Fixed by making inheritance POLICY-DEPENDENT — `deny_ledgered` rows must NOT inherit, everything else must — and by adding the missing half of Law 5: `island_root_missing_deny`. That closes remainder item 8(a): an island neither inherits `forbid` nor is checked for its own `deny`, so if the root loses `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` NOTHING constrains unsafe in that crate while every gate stays green (the ledger checker keeps matching the sites that remain, and the topology map keeps reporting `deny_ledgered`). Both new codes were seen to fire on a snapshot with the deny removed and the lint table added, against a control that passes.

LANDING AN ISLAND IS A FOUR-PLACE ATOMIC MOVE. In one commit: the crate under `crates/`, the workspace `members` entry, the ledger roster status `planned` -> `present` plus one `[[site]]` row per allow, and the topology row `activation_status` `planned` -> `active` with `manifest_dir` filled. Both registries check the OTHER one (`island_status_disagreement`, `island_roster_missing`), so a half-move fails loudly in both directions. Then: `active_crate_count` / `planned_crate_count` in workspace_topology.toml, its `semantic_contract_hash` (recomputed, plus the `SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_PIN` in tests/workspace_topology.rs), and `topology-check --write` to regenerate docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md.

LEDGER REJECTION, PROVEN ON REAL CODE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Row removed from the ledger while the site stands: `site_unledgered`, exit 1. Allow removed from the source while the row stands: `ledger_row_orphaned`, exit 1. Control: 2 sites, 2 rows, 0 orphans, exit 0.

WHAT THE ISLAND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM. No Miri: the x86 intrinsics are outside the lane's supported set, so the differential harness is the evidence and both rows say so in `no_claim_boundary`. No ASAN/TSAN lane yet. No performance claim of any kind — no benchmark is attached to either site, and the prefetch row states explicitly that a hint which helped nothing would still satisfy every assertion made about it.

REMAINDER AFTER THIS COMMIT: `fgdb-unsafe-arena` and `fgdb-unsafe-vfs` (both still `planned` in both registries); Miri/ASAN/TSAN lanes with exclusions mapped 1:1 to `no_claim_boundary` rows; a mechanical safe-facing API check (no public raw pointers, no public `unsafe fn`) — currently a review property, not a checked one; and SYNTHETIC mutation rows for `island_root_missing_deny` and `island_inherits_forbid` in tests/workspace_topology.rs, which need the live-tree law evaluator to accept a synthetic scan the way `posture_closures` already does. The live-scan test now asserts both policy directions positively, so the property is locked even though the violation codes are not yet fired by a permanent row.

(Ignore the one-word "placeholder" comment immediately above — a syntax probe for `br comments add`; there is no delete subcommand. This is the real close-out.)

ALL THREE ISLANDS LANDED — pane3. Commits: bd846d6, eaa8b4e (arena), f00e333, fd01f3f (vfs), 7e9d7e1, f022bf4.

## HAS THE LEDGER BEEN PROVEN TO REJECT?

YES — and I re-ran the whole sequence myself at HEAD rather than trusting the
predecessor's note. Rebuilt `unsafe-ledger-check` from source and ran ten
mutations, each against a fresh `git archive HEAD` copy, each with its control
beside it.

(a) The scanner counts the site and the ledger match succeeds: sites 3 -> 6 as
the islands landed, orphan_rows 0, violations 0, EXIT 0, scanner self-test 6/6
licensed.

(b) Remove the row and CI FAILS: `site_unledgered` naming the exact path:line,
EXIT 1. Both directions, on all three islands:

    delete a [[site]] row          -> site_unledgered              exit 1
    delete the allow attribute     -> ledger_row_orphaned          exit 1
    remove the root #![deny]       -> island_root_missing_deny     exit 1
    add [lints] workspace = true   -> island_inherits_forbid       exit 1
    delete the ledger file         -> ledger_absent_or_unreadable  exit 1
    allow in an ordinary crate     -> unsafe_allow_outside_island  exit 1
    chmod 000 a source file        -> source_unreadable            exit 1

And the compile-level backstop, which matters most: with the ledgered `allow`
removed, rustc rejects the crate outright — "usage of an `unsafe` block" under
`#![deny(unsafe_code)]`. The ledger is not the only wall; it is the wall that
stands when someone writes the allow.

## THE HONEST LIMIT

`island_root_missing_deny` and `island_inherits_forbid` were seen to fire BY HAND
against a passing control. Neither is fired by a permanent row in the suite. The
live-scan test asserts both policy directions positively and refuses to be
vacuous, so the PROPERTY is locked; the DIAGNOSTIC is not. Rename either code, or
make its branch unreachable, and the suite still passes. That is fgdb-14j7, filed
precisely because a checker seen to fire by hand is not a checker that cannot
silently stop firing. The other five codes above DO have permanent rows (21/21 in
tests/unsafe_ledger.rs).

## A LIVE HOLE FOUND AND CLOSED WHILE PROVING THE ABOVE (bd846d6)

`unsafe-ledger-check` decided whether a crate inherits the workspace `forbid`
with `text.contains("[lints]") && text.contains("workspace = true")`. Two
ordinary manifests satisfy that while inheriting nothing:

* one whose lint table is COMMENTED OUT (`# TODO: restore [lints] workspace =
  true`), which is what you write while debugging a lint — exactly when the
  boundary needs to hold;
* one carrying its own `[lints]` beside an idiomatic `dep = { workspace = true }`
  — the spelling every crate gets the day this workspace grows a
  `[workspace.dependencies]` table.

Both were run against the real tree with a raw-pointer deref added to
`fgdb-types`: `unsafe-ledger-check` reported the crate as inheriting `forbid` and
EXITED 0, while `topology-check`, which has parsed the manifest by section since
it was written, failed the same tree with `lints_not_inherited`. Two checkers
reading one fact and disagreeing means one of them is wrong. Same class as the
`cfg_attr` scanner bug, one layer down: matching spelling instead of structure.
Both now read through `topology::scan_manifest`, so there is one reader, and an
unparseable manifest fails closed with a new `member_manifest_unparseable`.

The assertion that HID it was `forbid_verdicts.values().all(|v| *v)` — "every
real member inherits forbid" — which passed only because the substring test
matched the simd island manifest's own comment explaining why it omits the lint
table. An island must NOT inherit: `forbid` cannot be lowered, so an island that
inherited it could not compile a single ledgered site. The row now asserts the
policy-dependent law in both directions and refuses to be vacuous if no island is
present.

## THE DENY-VS-FORBID DISTINCTION — why any of this is load-bearing

An ordinary crate carries `[lints] workspace = true` and inherits
`unsafe_code = "forbid"`, which NO attribute can lower. An island must not carry
that table, because inheriting `forbid` makes every ledgered site uncompilable.
So its root uses `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` — and `deny` CAN be lowered: by `allow`,
by `expect`, by `warn`, and by any of those wrapped in `cfg_attr`. Inside an
island the ledger is the only thing standing between a wrapped allow and an
unaudited unsafe site. Both halves are checked: `island_inherits_forbid` if the
table appears, `island_root_missing_deny` if the root loses its deny.

## WHAT THE THREE ISLANDS COVER — six sites, and each count is a claim

**fgdb-unsafe-simd (2 sites, predecessor).** SSE2 control-group classification,
bit-identical to `classify_scalar` across the compiled dispatch matrix; and a
`cfg_attr`-wrapped prefetch that must be INVISIBLE, measured by running the same
probe sequence with and without it. No Miri (x86 intrinsics are outside the
lane), no benchmark, and both rows say so.

**fgdb-unsafe-arena (1 site).** ONE, deliberately. An arena is not automatically
an unsafe crate: chunk carving, generational handles, stale- and foreign-handle
refusal, the byte audit, and ALIGNMENT are all safe Rust here, because
`alloc_block` reads the chunk base with `as_ptr().addr()` — a safe question about
a pointer already held — and pads to the aligned offset. Exactly one operation
cannot be expressed safely, and it is the one ART needs: N simultaneous exclusive
views into disjoint blocks of one chunk. Filling an island with unsafe that safe
Rust already expresses would make the boundary look busier and mean less.

The disjointness proof lives OUTSIDE the unsafe block, in `plan_batch`, which the
safe fallback calls too — so the check that licenses the site is exercised by
every test touching either path, and it refuses the batch pairwise rather than
arguing from the bump allocator's construction. Fallback `EditPath::Sequential`,
bit-identical over 192 batches on three fixed seeds, asserted on REFUSALS as well
as successes. `close()` and `cancel()` both audit
`bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated` with live blocks outstanding; cancellation
is the half that matters, because an arena that balances only on the happy path
leaks exactly when a query is cancelled mid-build.

**fgdb-unsafe-vfs (3 sites).** Could NOT be scoped away. The universe is closed,
so there is no libc and no `mmap` to call — the syscall is one `core::arch::asm!`
instruction under the x86-64 Linux ABI, and that is the entire reason the crate
exists. Three rows rather than one because they fail differently: `map_range` can
map the wrong range, `view_bytes` can hand out a slice wider than the mapping,
`drop` can give back something other than what was taken. `plan_range` refuses
any range past EOF BEFORE anything is mapped, because a mapping over a hole
faults with SIGBUS rather than returning an error — a safety precondition, not an
ergonomic one. Fallback `MapPath::Buffered`, compiled on every target, no `cfg`.

The vfs fallback had a real bug that byte comparison could never have found: it
cloned the handle with `try_clone` and seeked, believing a clone has its own
cursor. On Unix `try_clone` dups the descriptor, both share one file
*description*, and the seek moved the CALLER's position — an observable
difference between the two paths, invisible to any assertion about bytes.
Positional read now, and `a_view_does_not_move_the_callers_cursor` locks it.

## WHAT THE FIVE FOLLOW-UPS NEED

* **fgdb-czlt (P1, Miri/ASAN/TSAN).** simd and vfs are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION —
  intrinsics and inline asm are both outside Miri — and the lane manifest must
  say so in both directions, so an exclusion cannot be added in one place only.
  fgdb-unsafe-arena is a genuine candidate: no intrinsics, no asm, pure pointer
  arithmetic, with a fixed-seed workload already written.
* **fgdb-n7mb (P1, safe-facing API check).** Today a review property in three
  crate-root doc comments, checked by nobody. Must be structural, not line-wise —
  this bead's own history holds two bugs from matching spelling instead of
  structure.
* **fgdb-14j7 (P2).** The two lint codes above need the live-tree law evaluator to
  accept a synthetic scan, the way `posture_closures` already does.
* **fgdb-og31 (P1, consumer integration).** `RegionAlloc` is the seam; NOTHING is
  wired to it, and the arena's `no_claim_boundary` says so explicitly so the
  trait's existence is not read as an integration. The probe-latency and ART
  benchmark rows stay consumer `benchmark`-class claims — an island
  microbenchmark must not be presented as proving them.
* **fgdb-zwhh (P0).** Half discharged in f022bf4: `cargo fmt --check` now exits 0
  for the first time this session. The pin half stays open and is NOT mine — four
  beads (fgdb-5cgb, fgdb-gb9g, fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx,
  fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8) have no bet label, and re-freezing with
  them outstanding freezes an unresolved binding rather than fixing one.

## GATES AT CLOSE

* `unsafe-ledger-check` exit 0 — 6 sites, 0 orphans, 0 violations.
* `topology-check` exit 0.
* `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0. It was 101 at HEAD, with 8
  errors in registry-check and 1 in fgdb-unsafe-simd; all fixed.
* `cargo fmt --check` exit 0. It was 56 hunks at HEAD.
* `cargo test`: 1257 passed, 4 failed — all four the `architecture_decisions` pin
  rows of fgdb-zwhh, confirmed failing against a pristine HEAD archive before any
  of this work. (A fifth, `identity_code_set_is_ratcheted`, failed once in a
  concurrent full-workspace run and passes 100/100 on its own: a race with
  another pane's registry edit, not a defect.)
* `ubs` 0 critical on all new code.

## ONE CLIPPY FIX THAT IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A MECHANICAL CHANGE

fgdb-unsafe-simd's `naive_reference` tripped `needless_range_loop`, and clippy's
rewrite would make that function character-for-character identical to the
`classify_scalar` it exists to check independently. It carries a scoped allow
with that reason rather than being reshaped into its own oracle.

title: Establish fgdb-unsafe-simd/arena/vfs islands and the CI-enforced unsafe-boundary ledger
description:
## What & scope
Create the three unsafe-island crates — `fgdb-unsafe-simd`, `fgdb-unsafe-arena`, `fgdb-unsafe-vfs` — the workspace-wide `forbid(unsafe_code)` configuration for every other crate, the machine-readable unsafe-boundary ledger, and the CI job that enforces the bijection between ledger rows and `allow(unsafe_code)` sites. Also establish the reusable "ledger-style boundary CI" pattern that other constitutional boundaries copy (notably `fgdb-reference`'s dependency allowlist).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Constraint 2 makes memory safety structural, not conventional: the claim "this database is memory-safe Rust" is only worth something if the unsafe surface is enumerable, justified, and mechanically policed. This also serves B5 directly — every unsafe site carries its invariant, its evidence, and its safe fallback, so the evidence discipline that governs statistical claims governs raw pointers too. For the market: incumbent engines carry megabytes of C/C++; FrankenGraphDB's auditable unsafe surface is a differentiator only if it is provably small and ledgered.

## Design — normative detail
Restated exactly from constraint 2: every ordinary crate root and the workspace default use `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Rust's `forbid` level cannot be lowered, so the few raw-pointer implementations (buffer arenas, SIMD kernels, VFS mappings) live in separately named `fgdb-unsafe-*` boundary crates whose roots use `deny(unsafe_code)` plus narrowly scoped, ledgered `allow` sites. Safe-facing crates never relax `forbid`. Every unsafe operation gets a ledger row: path, invariant, evidence, scalar or safe fallback, and no-claim boundary; CI rejects an unledgered site. Per §18.1 the three islands are THE ONLY crate roots not using `forbid(unsafe_code)`; every site is exposed only through safe APIs. Island contents by charter: `fgdb-unsafe-simd` — SIMD/vector kernels (codec decode, digest/cipher inner loops, hash-table probes, linalg kernels) plus AMAC/memory-level-parallelism experiments; `fgdb-unsafe-arena` — bump/region arena internals and generational-handle plumbing that safe crates consume as safe APIs; `fgdb-unsafe-vfs` — raw file/mapping syscall surfaces beneath the filesystem-profile layer. §8.7 discipline binds the SIMD island: SIMD and memory-level parallelism use separately ledgered unsafe-island crates with scalar fallbacks; STRICT kernels are fixed by the portable numeric/scalar profile and must be bit-identical across supported dispatch paths; AMAC/prefetch policy is physical-only only if result and logical order remain identical. Ledger schema (checked-in TOML, materialized at G0 alongside `invariants.toml`): one row per `allow` site with `{path, stated_invariant, evidence (test/proof/Miri lane reference), fallback (scalar or safe implementation), no_claim_boundary (what the site does NOT guarantee)}`. The CI job: (a) walks the workspace verifying every non-island crate root forbids unsafe and the workspace default does too; (b) parses island sources, extracts every `allow(unsafe_code)`-scoped site, and requires an exact matching ledger row; (c) fails on orphan rows (ledger entries with no site) so the ledger cannot rot; (d) exposes the checker as a reusable library so the `fgdb-reference` dependency-allowlist CI (importing any engine crate into the reference is a rejected boundary violation "in the unsafe-boundary-ledger style") shares the mechanism.

## Invariants & claim types
The ledger discipline is itself invariant-class process machinery: an unledgered unsafe site is a build failure on every execution of CI, not a review judgment. Each ledger row's `stated_invariant` is a local safety invariant with named evidence; each `no_claim_boundary` prevents evidence inflation (a Miri-clean run is evidence for the exercised paths, not a proof). Kernel performance claims arising from islands are `benchmark`-class and belong to the consuming bead, never to the ledger.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-claim-registries (the ledger is a G0-materialized constitutional artifact; claim classes for evidence fields), g0-threat-model (what unsafe surfaces are exposed to which trust zones). Produces islands + CI consumed by: w1-crypto and w1-codecs and w1-collections (SIMD kernels), w3-buffer (arena/EBR internals via `fgdb-unsafe-arena` and asupersync region heaps), w2-filesystem-profiles and w2-root-bootstrap (VFS surfaces via `fgdb-unsafe-vfs`), w5-executor (STRICT kernel bit-identity), w8-kernels; verif-reference (reuses the boundary-CI pattern for its dependency allowlist).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
CI job green on: workspace forbid check, site↔row bijection, orphan detection; deliberate-violation fixtures (an unledgered site in a test branch must fail CI; a ledger row without a site must fail CI; an ordinary crate attempting `unsafe` must fail compilation). Miri runs over island test suites (as far as Miri supports the operations; documented exclusions become explicit `no_claim_boundary` entries); ASAN/TSAN lanes for island tests; scalar-fallback differential harness: for every islanded kernel, island output must equal scalar output — bit-identical for STRICT kernels — across the supported dispatch matrix; loom-style or lab-runtime concurrency tests for arena internals (EBR interaction). Every island API is demonstrably safe-facing: no public raw pointers, no public `unsafe fn` (checked mechanically). E2E: `unsafe_ledger_ci_e2e` — run the complete CI job against (1) the clean workspace (pass) and (2) three seeded violation fixtures — an unledgered `allow(unsafe_code)` site in an island, an orphan ledger row, and an `unsafe` block in an ordinary crate — each failing with a diagnostic naming the exact path or row; then run the scalar-fallback differential harness across the full dispatch matrix for every islanded kernel as one suite. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): the checker emits a machine-readable report {crates_scanned, per-crate forbid verdict, sites[{path, line, ledger_row_id}], orphan_rows[], final verdict}; the differential harness logs {kernel_id, dispatch_path, input_digest, output_digest, bit_identical} per case; Miri/ASAN lanes log their exclusions and a test asserts each exclusion maps 1:1 to a `no_claim_boundary` ledger entry.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: sprinkling `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` through ordinary crates (forbid cannot be lowered — this is why forbid, not deny, is the workspace default); a prose-only unsafe inventory (rots immediately; the ledger is machine-checked); trusting `unsafe` correctness to review alone (every site needs typed evidence and a fallback). Risk: island APIs accidentally widening (a "temporarily public" raw handle) — guarded by the safe-facing API check; risk of Miri coverage gaps — made explicit as no-claim boundaries rather than silently assumed safe.

## Provenance
§1 constraint 2; §8.7 SIMD/MLP rule; §15.4 (fgdb-reference allowlist in ledger style); §18.1 unsafe-islands row; §18 G0 materialization note.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

INCREMENT 1 LANDED: THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE. From pane3. The islands and their kernels are NOT in
this increment and are enumerated as remaining work below; what landed is the ledger, its checker,
and the mutation proof that each failure mode actually fires.

=== WHY THIS SLICE FIRST ===
The bead's own framing decides it: "the ledger is not documentation; it is the enforcement surface."
An island landed before the checker exists is an unaudited island. The checker landed first means
the first island CANNOT land unledgered -- `island_declared_planned_but_present` fires the moment a
crates/fgdb-unsafe-* directory appears while the roster still calls it planned.

=== THE VACUITY PROBLEM, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN ===
The workspace today has ZERO islands and ZERO unsafe sites. A checker written the obvious way
reports "0 sites, 0 orphans, pass" -- and reports exactly the same thing if its scanner is broken,
if the ledger file is deleted, or if it cannot read a single source file. Three structural answers,
all landed:

1. THE ROSTER IS A POSITIVE CLAIM, NOT AN ABSENCE. `[[island]]` rows declare the intended roster
   with a status, and BOTH directions are enforced: a `present` island whose directory is missing
   fails; a `planned` island that has appeared fails. Silence is never agreement.
2. THE SCANNER SELF-TESTS BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED. A fixture with a known site count is scanned first;
   if the count is not reproduced exactly, the run fails with `site_scanner_self_test_failed` and
   every zero-site conclusion in that run is treated as unlicensed. This is the control that makes
   an empty result mean something, and the binary reports it as the FIRST event so a reader can see
   whether an empty unsafe surface was proven or merely assumed.
3. UNREADABLE IS A FAILURE, NOT A SKIP. An unreadable manifest, an unreadable source file, or an
   unwalkable source tree fails the run.

=== A REAL ENFORCEMENT HOLE THIS FOUND, WORTH KNOWING INDEPENDENTLY OF THIS BEAD ===
A crate escapes the workspace `unsafe_code = "forbid"` the instant its Cargo.toml omits
`[lints] workspace = true`. Nothing at the crate root reveals this -- the source looks identical,
and every existing gate stays green. All 11 current members were measured and DO inherit it, so
this is a latent hole rather than a live defect, but it is now checked per member
(`member_does_not_inherit_forbid`) rather than assumed.

Violation codes, each with a test that fires it: site_scanner_self_test_failed,
workspace_manifest_unreadable, workspace_forbid_absent, ledger_absent_or_unreadable,
ledger_schema_version_unknown, island_declared_present_but_absent,
island_declared_planned_but_present, island_status_unknown, island_charter_empty,
ledger_row_id_duplicated, ledger_row_island_unknown, ledger_row_field_vacuous,
member_manifest_unreadable, member_does_not_inherit_forbid, source_tree_unreadable,
source_unreadable, unsafe_allow_outside_island, site_unledgered, ledger_row_orphaned.

=== REMAINING WORK, EXPLICITLY NOT DONE ===
1. The three island CRATES themselves (fgdb-unsafe-simd / -arena / -vfs). When each lands, flip its
