title: Build HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket adapters preserving full FGP semantics
description:
## What & scope
Build the HTTP/2 + gRPC + WebSocket adapters over asupersync's http stack: query endpoint, subscription streams, health/metrics, and bulk import/export endpoints (multipart or ATP bonded pull), all dispatching into the one FGP connection machine.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents arrive over whatever transport their framework speaks; the moat is that every transport gets the same durable semantics, not a degraded HTTP-flavored subset. §1's closed universe supplies TLS/HTTP/gRPC from asupersync — Fabric adds no new protocol stack, only mappings.

## Design — normative detail
Adapters are mappings, not machines: each adapter session resolves to the same `TransportEstablished -> ... -> Ready` machine, the same three-header discipline (transport framing may differ, binding semantics may not), and the same typed children. Normative rule (App D): HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt adapters preserve the same idempotency, posture, explicit release, output-guard, cancellation, result-resume, and cutover semantics; adapters cannot weaken Appendix D's state, frame, retry, privacy, and posture rules. Every protected byte still consumes a fresh `PublicFrameSendGuard` arm before write; `TransportSendObligation` states and poisoning apply per adapter connection. Endpoints: query (unary + streaming), subscription streams (server-streaming with cursor ACK verbs mapped to SUBSCRIBE_*/ACK semantics), health/metrics (public-mechanics surfaces carrying no protected content and exposing no database-existence signal pre-auth; note that Appendix D's `NoTimeNeeded` registry admits only payload-free protocol-mechanics frames, so metrics payloads cannot ride `NoTimeNeeded` rows — these endpoints stay outside the protected-frame matrix entirely), bulk import/export as multipart upload or ATP bonded pull attached to the durable artifact-output registry. Idempotency keys, capabilities, and opaque projections are carried verbatim in adapter encodings — no adapter-local identifier scheme may replace `PublicHandle`/`PublicStateToken` values, and no adapter may synthesize ACK/release from transport-level success (an HTTP 200 is not an ACK, mirroring the Bolt rule).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: adapter disconnects cannot release independently retained output. FG-INV-20: adapter routes perform the same authorization-before-observation; health/metrics endpoints expose no database-existence signal pre-auth. Adapter parity transcripts are FG-EVID artifacts; per-adapter connection limits are configuration rows.

## Interactions
Consumes `w10-fgp-core` (machine), `w10-result-machines` (delivery), `w10-capabilities` (presentation), `w10-qos` (admission combinators). Composed by `w10-server`; parity-tested with `w10-bolt` under `verif-differential`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Adapter parity matrix in CI: the App D conformance corpus (idempotent retry, resume/ACK/release, cancellation, revocation-between-chunks, protected-error silence) executed over FGP, HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket with equivalent outcomes and release-evidence classes; divergences fail the build. Fuzz adapter framing (chunked/multipart edge cases, WS fragmentation) — no partial protected frame ever surfaces. Load test: bulk export via ATP bonded pull resumes across connection loss from the canonical chunk boundary, with structured logs correlating adapter stream IDs to obligation states.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: impedance mismatch (gRPC deadline vs. FGP budgets) — deadlines map to cancellation requests, never to silent release. Rejected: REST-flavored simplified semantics (splits the contract); adapter-local retry with new idempotency keys (duplicates work); treating transport ACKs as delivery ACKs.

## Provenance
§13.4 (1049), Appendix D 3116, §18.2 (asupersync boundary).


## Comprehensive adapter verification and diagnostics
- Unit tests cover every adapter-to-FGP mapping, header/binding preservation, deadline-to-cancel conversion, stream/flow-credit translation, canonical public-handle/token encoding, health/metrics pre-auth nonobservation, send-guard acquisition, and the rule that transport success cannot synthesize semantic ACK/release.
- Property/fuzz tests generate fragmentation, chunking, multipart, cancellation, deadline, disconnect, retry, resume, revocation, and backpressure traces. The same abstract operation trace must produce equivalent public outcomes and retained-owner states over native FGP, HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket; malformed/partial protected frames never surface bytes.
- Real-server E2E: boot `fgdbd`; authenticate independent clients over all four transports; run unary/streaming query, subscription baseline/ACK/delta/resume, protected result lost-response/resume/release, health/metrics before and after auth, bulk multipart import, ATP bonded export with connection loss, revocation between chunks, deadline/cancel, and server restart. Assert canonical wire/public outcome equivalence, exact durable owner retention and terminal evidence, no pre-auth database-existence signal, no protected bytes after revocation, and recovery from canonical chunk/cursor boundaries.
- Detailed JSONL per adapter step: `{run_id,scenario_id,seed,adapter,connection_id,stream_id,abstract_operation_id,fgp_frame_or_mapping_id,protocol_state,public_handle_or_token_digest,capability_epoch,flow_credit_before_after,send_guard_arm,transport_obligation_state,result_owner_arm,cursor_frontier,deadline_cancel_state,expected,actual,verdict}`. Failures include both adapter/native trace digests, first divergent transition/byte, minimized input, all obligation/evidence IDs, and §15.1 replay command. Passing rows use the same schema; G3 parity evidence is regenerated from these logs.

title: Implement ArchiveReadOnlyOpen for single-file .fgdb dataset distribution
description:
## What & scope
Implement the registered `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` open class: `fgdb::Database::open_archive(path)` and the equivalent `fgdbd` mount that serve a `.fgdb` archive directly, strictly read-only, with full verification and honest posture labeling.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Dataset distribution is an agent-era use case (share a graph as one signed file, query it immediately — the SQLite distribution model, B6). Doing it as a first-class registered open class, instead of an improvised reader, keeps the security and audit story intact: an archive can never impersonate an Operational database.

## Design — normative detail
The open path verifies the signed `BackupManifest`, object inventory, and transparency checkpoint with the same independent verifying-reader machinery that backs `BackupArtifactReopenProof`, reusing the restore staging/validation machinery in read-only mode rather than introducing a second opener. It then exposes the archived root strictly read-only: no incarnation takeover, no writer, no service promotion, and no service-promotion receipt is minted, so the posture is explicitly labeled in READY/status surfaces and structurally cannot impersonate an Operational database. Decryption rides the archive's recipient key wraps under the archive's own escrow policy. The audit classification of archive reads is explicit under FG-INV-20/FG-INV-04 — never inherited by analogy from the Operational read classes. Anything outside the archived closure fails closed with a typed `HistoryUnavailable`-class refusal, never a partial result. Because read-only media cannot create lease inodes, the §5.3 snapshot-lease machinery runs under a registered read-only filesystem-profile variant whose pinning discipline is profile-registered rather than improvised per open. The open-class, posture, and filesystem-profile-variant registry rows are reserved in the §19 G0 decision batch (`g0-format-arms`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04: restore/role-transition state remains unobservable; the archive posture is a distinct labeled state, and hidden-restore rejection of ordinary open is preserved (archive open is the only legal path to archived bytes). FG-INV-20: authorization precedes observation for archive reads under their explicit audit classification. FG-INV-10 alignment: the archive opener never writes; there is no root-slot publication, takeover token, or format activation from this path. Verification transcripts (manifest signature, inventory, transparency checkpoint) are FG-EVID artifacts; the read-only filesystem-profile variant is a registered configuration row.

## Interactions
Consumes `w11-backup` (`BackupManifest`, `BackupArtifactReopenProof` machinery), `w11-restore` (staging/validation reuse), `w2-filesystem-profiles` (read-only variant registration), `w2-snapshots-leases` (profile-registered pinning), `w9-enforcement` (archive read authorization), `g0-format-arms` (reserved registry rows). Surfaces through `w10-embedded` and `w10-server` mounts; `.fgdb` container from `w10-formats`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Open matrix: valid archive opens read-only and labels posture in READY/status (golden fixture); tampered manifest/inventory/checkpoint, missing objects, wrong recipient wrap all fail closed before any data observation (log assertion). Impersonation negatives: attempt writer takeover, service promotion, root-slot write, ordinary `open()` on an archive — all structurally rejected. Closure tests: query touching an object outside the archived closure returns typed `HistoryUnavailable`, never partial rows. Read-only-media suite: open from an actually read-only mount (no lease-inode creation attempted; profile variant logged). Differential: same dataset served from Operational database vs. archive yields identical canonical results for in-closure queries. e2e script: back up an Operational database to a signed `.fgdb`, transfer it, `open_archive` on an actually read-only mount, run in-closure and out-of-closure queries plus attempted write/subscription verbs, and diff results against the source database; structured logs record each manifest/inventory/transparency-checkpoint verification event with digests, the posture label emitted in READY/status, the selected read-only filesystem-profile variant, and every typed refusal (`HistoryUnavailable`-class, write/subscription/promotion attempts), so log inspection alone proves no write or promotion path was ever invoked.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: users treating archives as live replicas — READY posture labeling plus refusal of all write/subscription verbs. Rejected: a second lightweight opener (divergent validation paths); minting a pseudo service receipt (impersonation vector); silently degrading out-of-closure queries to partial results.

## Provenance
§13.7 (1057), §5.3, §16, §19 G0 batch.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement the durable artifact-output request and delivery state machine
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact durable artifact-output request, manifest, policy, resource escrow, Protocol delivery, activation, resume, ACK/release/expiry, index and compaction formats for Export, public replay-manifest projection, and proof bundles.

## Why
Artifacts can outlive a socket and may pin history, proof inputs, disclosure authority and durable charges. Treating export as streaming loses idempotency and retention on disconnect; treating it as a query result obscures its different request key, source pins, format contract and output digest.

## Design — exact normative contract
   **Durable artifact outputs and replay execution.** Export, public replay-manifest retrieval, and proof bundles are not socket-owned streams. `DurableArtifactOutputKind=Export|ReplayManifestProjection|ProofBundle`; `DurableArtifactOutputRequestKey` is `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,posture,tenant,principal,non_widenable_authority_digest,kind,scoped_idempotency_key,canonical_request_digest}`. Reusing the scoped key with any body/domain/authority drift fails before source observation or charge. `DurableArtifactOutputManifest` is `{format_version,kind,public_format_contract_oid,public_scope_projection,disclosure_contract_digest,canonical_encoding_version,byte_count,ordered_chunks[CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor],canonical_output_digest,source_retention_refs[TypedArtifactSourceRetentionRef],resource_charge_ref,body_digest}`; its public digest covers kind/public contracts/encoding/count and exact concatenated bytes, excluding internal identities/refs/charges/placements and itself.

   Semantic `ArtifactOutputRequestRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is state-shaped `Reserved{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,source_pins,resource_reservations}|MaterializedDetached{authority_bound_header,manifest_ref:StrongRef<DurableArtifactOutputManifest>,output_delivery_id,delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryPolicy<Role>>,audit_gate_commitment,detachment_commitment}|FailedDetached{terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,protected_error_key,public_error_commitment,audit_gate_commitment}` and never stores a delivery lease, capability, ACK, release, or protocol-record ref. The terminal arm is nonrevivable and payload-free; a failed request that still owns an error manifest uses the separate live ProtectedError lifecycle below. `DurableArtifactOutputRequestRegistry<Role>` owns request idempotency and compacted semantic floors. Materialization atomically transfers the charge to `ArtifactOutputResourceEscrow<Role>` and creates Protocol `ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>::PendingVisibility{common,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_gate_commitment}` unless same-apply visibility creates ReleasedAwaitingActivation or a legal inline fresh recipe selects ActiveDeliverable. Pending/released states have no time window/capability and emit neither READY nor bytes.

   `ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,request_key_digest,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,canonical_output_digest,semantic_detachment_identity,nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`; `ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>` replaces the header with `terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>` and retains only terminal/public identities. `ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the exact Protocol state union `PendingVisibility{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_gate_commitment}|ReleasedAwaitingActivation{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_release_evidence,release_maintenance_ref}|ActiveDeliverable{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,lease_time_basis_ref,lease_generation,capability_lineage_ref,escrow_ref,sender_generation}|Acknowledged{common:ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>,ack_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}|ReleasedUnacked{common:ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>,release_or_expiry_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}`; terminal arms retain no strong authority, manifest, lease, payload, capability replay, escrow, or predecessor edge. `ArtifactOutputDeliveryIndex<Role>` maps request and output-delivery keys to the one current record plus a compacted disposition floor. Audit visibility changes PendingVisibility only to ReleasedAwaitingActivation; independent activation supplies a fresh `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, exact time evidence, and prebuilt generation-zero `ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord`. Resume/ACK/authenticated explicit release/profiled expiry are maintenance transitions with the same full-header/nonwidening receipt, sender fencing, send-completion bridge, capability-lineage, resource-conservation, and lost-response rules as query results. Checkpoint/protocol snapshot, backup, restore, GC, and posture transitions walk both the semantic request registry and Protocol delivery index. Local/Meta payloads root only the semantic registry; `RootManifest`'s protocol state roots only the delivery index.

## Invariants & interactions
Consumes result-owner lifecycle patterns, authority bindings, audit release/activation, resource ledger, time evidence, capabilities and wire projections. fgdb-w10-result-machines retains shared machinery while this task owns artifact-specific schemas and tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact rows/codecs cover all request, manifest, common, record/index, policy/time-basis/lease, escrow/disposition, capability and transition types.
- Unit/golden tests freeze idempotency keys, authorized public digest transcript, source-retention refs, state arms and terminal edge removal.
- Property/model/DPOR proves one output per key/body, no source observation or charge on conflict, pending/released no clock/capability, active exact retention, and ACK/release/expiry one-winner conservation.
- Fuzz rejects body/domain/authority drift, cross-result/artifact arms, internal refs in public digest, stale state/capability, missing source pin and terminal strong edges.
- Crash/restart E2E exports multi-chunk artifacts, loses requests/responses/connections, resumes, ACKs/releases/expires, checkpoints/restores/GCs and reproduces canonical_output_digest.
- JSONL emits {event_version,artifact_kind,request_key_digest,output_delivery_id,from_state,to_state,state_version,manifest_digest,public_format_contract,source_pin_count,resource_escrow_state,capability_generation?,sender_generation?,terminal_evidence?,recovery_action,replay_command}; no artifact bytes or protected refs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: socket ownership, ad-hoc export cache, query-result owner reuse without an artifact arm, time window before audit release, and terminal records retaining source pins.

## Provenance
Plan section 13.2 lines 1017-1021 and Appendix D.

### Detailed diagnostic-event contract
Artifact output emits versioned redacted JSONL at request, authorization, reservation, build/seal, ownership publication, visibility, activation, send-guard, write-start, ACK/release, retry, cancellation, expiry, and terminal cleanup: `event_version,event_id,run_id,artifact_output_id_public_commitment,request_idempotency_commitment,artifact_kind,owner_generation,state_before,state_after,manifest_and_public_digest,answer_disclosure_contract_commitment,authority_binding_public_commitment,audit_gate_public_state,resource_reservation_public_commitment,send_guard_arm,transport_obligation_state,frame_transcript_digest?,durable_disposition,checker_id,verdict,failure_class,artifact_refs,replay_command`. Unit tests assert schema, ordering, cardinality, redaction, and byte-identical retry; E2E crash/cancel/resume/release reconstructs ownership and proves no socket event implicitly releases durable bytes. Logs never expose artifact payload, capability bytes, raw tenant/principal identity, local locator, encryption key, or unauthorized existence/size metadata.

Audit visibility changes PendingVisibility only to ReleasedAwaitingActivation; independent activation supplies a fresh `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, exact time evidence, and prebuilt generation-zero `ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord`.
   `ArtifactOutputEndSendCompletionRecord<Role>` is the channel-only `{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_binding,server_process_incarnation,sender_generation,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,resume_capability_commitment,surface_terminal_frame_and_canonical_fgp_end_digest,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_output_digest,flow_reservation_identity,transport_sent_obligation_commitment,sent_completion_nonce,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. `EmbeddedArtifactOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>` is the embedded-only `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,output_owner_token_commitment,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_output_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Their construction rules are the exact channel-Sent and complete-consumption rules above; neither partial read, Drop, EOF inference, release, nor cross-surface substitution can build one.
   `ArtifactOutputDispositionAuthority<Role>` is the closed union `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment}|ReadyChannelManagementHandle{validated_management_handle_commitment}|EmbeddedOutputOwner{output_owner_token_commitment,host_session_generation}`. `ArtifactOutputDispositionCompletion<Role>` is `ChannelSent{record_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputEndSendCompletionRecord<Role>>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedArtifactOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}|NotApplicable`. `AuthenticatedClientArtifactOutputDispositionReceipt<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,authority:ArtifactOutputDispositionAuthority<Role>,completion:ArtifactOutputDispositionCompletion<Role>,output_delivery_id,expected_delivery_state_version,canonical_output_digest,action:Acknowledge|Release,canonical_request_digest,request_nonce,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Each transition retains its direct or nested validation ref through successor acknowledgement or terminal receipt/tombstone resolution. Checkpoint/protocol snapshot, backup, restore, GC, and posture transitions walk both the semantic request registry and Protocol delivery index. Local/Meta payloads root only the semantic registry; `RootManifest`'s protocol state roots only the delivery index.

title: Implement BoltCompatProfileV1 read-only subset and register the V2 write roadmap
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-bolt`: the `BoltCompatProfileV1` explicit read-only downgrade for 1.0, and the registered-but-post-1.0 `BoltCompatProfileV2` write profile shape, divergence registry, and conformance gate definition.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Market adoption: the Neo4j driver ecosystem is the largest graph client base; a bounded compatibility surface lets teams point existing drivers at FGDB without FGDB inheriting Bolt's semantic holes. The profile is a negotiated downgrade with documented divergences — never a drop-in-Neo4j claim.

## Design — normative detail
V1 (sole 1.0 profile): read-only autocommit and read-only explicit transactions only; every RUN is server-classified ProvenReadOnly before graph access; no writes, subscriptions, CDC, export, replay, proof, FEC, factorized frames, capability presentation, or authority refresh. Bolt RECORD bytes use the ordinary read/audit/send guards and independent result retention. Socket success and final SUCCESS are not ACKs. Authenticated DISCARD or RESET creates one exact Bolt-source client-release receipt per addressed published result (`ClientResultReleaseAuthority::Bolt{bolt_session_binding,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}`); transport loss creates none, so otherwise output survives to profiled expiry even though Bolt cannot resume it. Unsupported semantics fail with stable documented divergence. Adapter conformance compares only the common supported surface; the negotiated profile is published in READY/metadata.

V2 (registered 1.x post-G4 write profile — normative now in shape, its implementation is its own registered workstream in §19's platform/compatibility roadmap): openCypher write clauses admitted through ordinary bind-time mutation classification — every RUN resolves a server-derived `CanonicalStatementClassification` at bind, like every other surface, instead of proving ProvenReadOnly. Bolt explicit and autocommit write transactions map onto the W10 transaction machines with no Bolt-private lifecycle. Bolt bookmarks are realized as §14.3 `ReadYourWritesCapability` values — issued at commit, accepted as visibility floors — so bookmark causality is honored semantically rather than imitated. COMMIT SUCCESS for Required-audit work is ordered after the audit-visibility advance, never before. Documented stable divergences: a lost COMMIT response is an unknown outcome (the Bolt surface carries no reattach, resume, or outcome re-query — matching official drivers' behavior); no procedure surface beyond the registered UDF/module set; no APOC. Server error causes map through `protected_error_classes.toml` to `Neo.ClientError` codes so hidden constraint/existence/authorization causes do not leak through the compatibility surface. V2's conformance gate: openCypher TCK write scenarios plus the §15.4 differential corpus.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: Bolt transport loss cannot release retained output; only the authenticated DISCARD/RESET receipt or expiry does. FG-INV-20: hidden causes surface only as mapped opaque `Neo.ClientError` codes; classification precedes graph access. The divergence registry is a documentation-contract artifact; TCK/differential results are FG-EVID; profile negotiation strings are configuration rows.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-parsers`/`w5-binder` (openCypher classification), `w10-result-machines` (retention/release), `w10-capabilities` (V2 bookmarks-as-RYW), `w10-fgp-core` (machine + guards). V2 gate depends on `verif-differential`'s corpus. Composed by `w10-server`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
V1: official Neo4j drivers (Python/JS/Java) run the read-only corpus successfully; write attempts, subscriptions, and procedure calls fail with the registered stable divergences (golden error fixtures). Classification negative: crafted RUN that mutates via subquery is rejected before any graph access (log assertion: zero storage observations). DISCARD/RESET produce exactly one release receipt per addressed result (idempotent duplicates); kill-socket-instead leaves retention until expiry (doctor counter). Error-mapping noninterference: constraint-violation vs. authorization-denial produce the same mapped code class where the disclosure contract requires opacity, byte/timing uniform. V2 (spec-only now): divergence registry and gate definition merged into §19 roadmap docs; shape types compile behind a feature flag with V1 negotiation refusing them. E2E script: launch fgdbd with the Bolt adapter and run the pinned read-only corpus end-to-end from stock Python/JS/Java driver environments — connect, authenticate, query, DISCARD/RESET, then a mid-result socket kill — diffing every response against the golden fixtures. Detailed logging: the adapter logs {connection_id, bolt message type, mapped command, classification verdict, release-receipt id, divergence-registry ref} per message; classification rejections log the zero-storage-observation proof; the e2e asserts receipt-per-result and expiry-retention behavior from adapter logs plus the doctor counter alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: driver-version drift in Bolt handshake details — pin tested driver versions, conformance compares the common surface only. Rejected: full Bolt server emulation with APOC (unbounded surface, leaks); write support in 1.0 (would ship without the audit-ordering machinery hardened); Bolt-private transaction lifecycle (splits the ownership model); treating final SUCCESS as ACK.

## Provenance
§13.5 (1050-1052), Appendix D 3116, App D 2796 (Bolt release arm).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

## Authoritative post-d96bf0f contract reconciliation

Bolt release authority is versioned as distinct BoltV1 and BoltV2 arms; neither arm fabricates capability-validation evidence, and only authenticated DISCARD/RESET can release a retained result.

The following current plan text is authoritative and supersedes any older rendering in this Bead:

**Authoritative v1 delivery and control corrections.** `QUERY_CANCEL` controls computation and the current sender only. Before publication it may select the role-valid no-result/abort path; after independent retention it can only durably pause that session's sender after joining queued/writing transport obligations. It never ACKs/releases a result, changes capability lineage, or frees durable charge. `ClientResultReleaseAuthority` is the closed source union `ReadyChannel{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,presented_authority:ResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,capability_commitment}|ManagementHandle{validated_management_handle_commitment},session_binding,auth_context_generation,surface_request_digest,canonical_fgp_request_digest}|Embedded{stream_release_token_commitment,host_session_generation,explicit_release_call_digest}|BoltV1{bolt_session_binding,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}|BoltV2{bolt_session_binding,negotiated_profile_oid:BoltCompatProfileV2,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}`. Only ReadyChannel ResumeCapability validation selects the exact ResumeBufferedResult/ResultReleaseUnacked row and byte-matches the capability commitment, surface/canonical request pair, current result lineage, role, header, and session. The ReadyChannel management-handle arm, embedded stream token, and Bolt V1/V2 authenticated DISCARD/RESET arms cannot populate a capability-validation ref. `AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>` binds the complete role/domain/service/principal/authority/result ID/state version/digest/release nonce/source/authentication attestation and thereby strongly retains validation evidence only in the ReadyChannel ResumeCapability source arm. `ResultReleaseEvidence` is exactly `ClientRelease{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>>}|LeaseExpired{expiry_evidence_ref}`. Rust Drop, transport loss, QUERY_CANCEL, drain, and process/session death cannot construct it.

Implementation, tests, retained evidence, and public-surface behavior must use this exact corrected contract. No Markdown plan edit is required or authorized by this reconciliation.

title: Implement the four durable capabilities: header, bodies, lineage, and tombstone family
description:
## What & scope
Implement the durable capability plane: the shared `DurableCapabilityHeader`, the exactly-four durable authority-bearing capabilities that survive connection loss — §9.5's `ResumeCapability`, §5.6's `MergeOutcomeCapability`, §14.3's `ReadYourWritesCapability`, and `TxnOutcomeCapability` — plus their replay records, lineage roots, rotation rules, and the generated terminal tombstone family. Also the contrasting ephemeral handle regime and the shape of `CAPABILITY_MIGRATE` (exercised by W12).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: a disconnected agent must be able to learn its transaction's outcome, resume a buffered result, complete a merge, and read its own writes — with cryptographic proof, without a session, and without the server ever revealing anything to a wrong-principal presenter. Exactly four kinds, closed bodies, and generated tombstones keep the survival surface auditable; everything else is deliberately ephemeral.

## Design — normative detail
Ephemeral regime: `stmt_id`, `stream_id`, delivery cursor, open-query, active-transaction, and transient-reservation handles are server-minted random or MACed capabilities scoped to protocol version, database security namespace, cluster incarnation, service visibility epoch, tenant, principal, non-widenable authority digest, session, and creation policy/revocation epochs. Prepared statements bind the `PreparedQueryTemplate` digest, language/catalog/schema compatibility contracts, and authority ceiling; each execution resolves a fresh `BoundQuery` and reauthorizes it.

All four durable kinds use the exact wire-safe `DurableCapabilityHeader {capability_format_version,capability_kind,issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,projection_domain_commitment,security_state_binding_public_commitment,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expiry,capability_nonce:PublicHandle<CapabilityNonce>}`; namespace/incarnation/service/posture/principal/authority are committed by the projection domain and retained in the replay object's complete binding — never repeated as correlation-friendly scalars. No local ref or policy/revocation counter. A capability is `{header,kind_specific_body,mac}` with a domain-separated MAC over the complete header/body. Every live, replayable, or byte-owning durable issuance/replay object carries `authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>` and proves its complete binding derives both public commitments; only a nonrevivable, nonpayload terminal tombstone may replace it with `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>`. Presentation validates current same-or-narrower complete binding and fresh time evidence; bad MAC/domain/binding/profile returns uniform `NotVisibleOrUnknown`. Rotation/expiry respect promised floors.

Bodies. Txn: exactly `{request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,scoped_request_commitment,txn_handle:PublicTxnHandle,outcome_lookup_handle:PublicHandle<TxnOutcomeLookup>,capability_lineage_token:PublicStateToken<TxnCapabilityLineage>}`; permits lookup plus narrowly scoped Reattach/Renew, never direct statement/commit/rollback. `ResumeCapabilityBody` is the closed union `SubscriptionCursor{cursor_handle,issuance_cursor_state_token,capability_lineage_token,public_derived_identity_commitment,baseline_handle,public_state_commitment}|BufferedResult{posture,owner_commitment,delivery_handle,issuance_lease_token,issuance_delivery_state_token,capability_lineage_token,canonical_result_digest}|DurableArtifactOutput{posture,output_kind,request_key_commitment,delivery_handle,issuance_lease_token,issuance_delivery_state_token,capability_lineage_token,canonical_output_digest}`; `resume_capability_arms.toml` is the single source for body and `ResumeCapabilitySubjectBasis`, and generation rejects arm drift; no mutable state hint or numeric internal generation is encoded — the rooted Protocol index alone determines state, and PendingVisibility/ReleasedAwaitingActivation cannot have a Resume capability at all. `MergeOutcomeCapabilityBody` is exactly `{merge_handle:PublicMergeHandle,target:WireGraphReferenceSpec,canonical_request_commitment,capability_lineage_token:PublicStateToken<MergeCapabilityLineage>}` with `MergeOutcomeSubjectBasis<Role>` `{merge_token,target_internal_binding,target_basis:StrongMarkerRef,source_heads[],merge_bases[],resolution_policy_oid,authority_bound_header,lookup_and_retention_floor,public_body_digest}`; a public marker selector resolves only through its authenticated retained mapping — never decoded as an internal marker identity. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord` body is `{posture,txn_outcome_capability_commitment,registration_handle,floors:PublicRywFloorSet,capability_lineage_token}`; issued only with TerminalReady; permits waiting/reading at an authorized subset of the opaque committed floor set under current same-or-narrower authority; contains no WeakMarkerIdentity, raw Raft/logical/commit/audit counter, or local ref on wire; `ReadYourWritesSubjectBasis<Role>` (Local|Meta) supplies the exact marker/branch/visibility/retention map byte-matching `floors`.

Replay records store canonical capability bytes plus commitment plus complete binding (e.g. `TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord {public_fields,canonical_capability_bytes,capability_commitment,authority_bound_header,canonical_request_digest,request_kind,scoped_request_idempotency_key_digest,internal_txn_token,internal_outcome_capability_key,internal_capability_generation,lineage_nonce,issuer_and_verifier_key_epoch,verifier_key_ref,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expiry,minimum_begin_retry_floor,body_digest}`); stored bytes decode and byte-match every public projection/MAC/commitment; a server-side index maps opaque handles to internal subjects; internal generation zero precedes reservation and successors precede Reattach/Renew. `TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Role>` maps each key to `Current{current_replay_ref}|CurrentWithConsumedPredecessor{current_replay_ref,predecessor_replay_ref,consuming_request_digest,recovery_until:SuccessorAcknowledgedOrSuccessorTerminal}|TerminalCurrent{current_replay_ref,terminal_subject_commitment}|ExpiredTombstone{tombstone_ref}`. There is no independent short recovery deadline: the predecessor remains recoverable until the successor is acknowledged/consumed or terminally ends; consumed-predecessor recovery reproduces only the installed successor while it remains live and exposes no outcome. TerminalCurrent stays a live replayable capability; only ExpiredTombstone drops the replay object.

`DurableCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role,Kind>` is a generated finite family (named members for TxnOutcome, Resume, MergeOutcome, ReadYourWrites — noninterchangeable) with exact common fields `{role,capability_kind=Kind,capability_commitment,projection_domain_commitment,subject_key_commitment,lineage_token_commitment,last_generation,terminal_disposition:Acknowledged|ExplicitlyReleased|SubjectTerminal|Expired|MigratedConsumed,terminal_subject_or_successor_commitment,expiry_or_terminal_evidence_commitment,issuer_and_verifier_epoch_commitment,terminal_authority_commitment,minimum_nonreuse_lookup_and_replay_floor,body_digest}`. Tombstones contain no canonical capability bytes, verifier-key ref, replay object, protected payload, lease, live subject, or predecessor edge, and cannot authorize lookup, replay, delivery, migration, or successor issuance. `ResultCapabilityTombstone`, subscription/artifact tombstones, begin/outcome-index expiry leaves, merge expiry leaves, and capability-migration consumed leaves are exact generated members or exact wrappers; an informal `{capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}` tuple is not a durable schema. `CAPABILITY_MIGRATE` (legal only under a fresh Sharded E2 Ready binding, six-arm `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec`) is shaped here; W12 exercises it.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-01: each durable token maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome; matching retries return the recorded lineage. FG-INV-16: ownership is durably reattachable/renewable only under the capability lineage. FG-INV-20: capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, uniformly nonrevealing. FG-INV-14: capability lineage and replay records are GC roots until exact terminal transfer/release. Restart/rotation/lost-response/expiry/substitution byte tests are FG-EVID artifacts; expiry-profile durations are configuration rows.

## Interactions
Subjects come from `w2-txn-lifecycle` (TxnOutcomeIndex), `w6-subscriptions` (cursor state), `w2-branch-merge` (MergeRecord/tokens), `w11-read-contracts` (RYW floors). Consumes `w10-wire-projections` types and `w9-time-authority` evidence. Consumed by `w10-txn-ownership`, `w10-result-machines`, `w10-embedded`, `w10-bolt` (V2 bookmarks), `w12-backup-restore` (migration).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
All capability kinds pass exact restart/rotation/lost-response/expiry/substitution byte tests: rotate under load, crash, present predecessor -> same prebuilt successor bytes; present grandparent -> capability-safe failure. Negative suite: wrong principal/domain/epoch/profile all return byte-identical `NotVisibleOrUnknown` with uniform timing class. Generation CI: `resume_capability_arms.toml` drift rejection; tombstone family completeness (one named member per kind, no generic member). Property: header `not_before`/`expiry` window floors honored across rotation (the durable capability header and replay records use App D's field name `expiry`, not the generated window schemas' `expires_at`); tombstone can never revive (fuzz attempted transitions). e2e: kill-connection-mid-delivery script, reconnect with each capability kind, log every lineage transition and assert single-successor CAS.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: lineage state growth — bounded by evidence-bound expiry installing permanent tombstones. Rejected: a fifth durable capability for errors (replay rides the scoped request key instead); short fixed recovery deadlines (stranded agents); encoding internal generations in bodies (correlation and staleness lies).

## Provenance
§13.3 (996-1002, 1010-1014), Appendix D 2788, 2798, 3023-3028, 3112.

## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

This ownership, retention, status-classification, and lifecycle integration contract is part of the durable-capability implementation unit. It supersedes any implication that generic Lifecycle rotation or status-by-handle is sufficient.

W10's durable-capability slice is the unique schema/Bead integration owner. Implementation ownership is intentionally split: W9's `fgdb-warden` boundary owns canonical decode, key selection, MAC verification, and current authority/security/time/lineage validation and constructs the evidence; W10 owns the exact lifecycle/protocol/admission/receipt consumers of the resulting nonconstructible ref. Exact crate/path consumers are `fgdb-formats`, `fgdb-protocol`, `fgdb-bolt`, `fgdb-txn`, `fgdb-chronicle`, `fgdb-branch`, `fgdb-subs`, `fgdb-audit`, `fgdb-secure-view`/read admission, embedded `fgdb`, `fgdb-server`, `fgdb-reference`, `fgdb-sim`/fuzz/format verification, and the W12 role-transition/migration path. Static G0 checker IDs are `durable_capability_validation_schema_exactness`, `durable_capability_validation_compatibility_matrix`, `durable_capability_validation_construction_dag`, and `durable_capability_validation_diagnostic_redaction`. Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, lifecycle/race, migration, adapter parity, and public-noninterference checker rows are planned rather than live until their named W9/W10/W12 owners provide executable evidence.

Any action-specific receipt constructed from a presented durable capability strongly retains this validation ref; management-handle, authenticated-session/embedded-owner, and Bolt V1/V2 release alternatives are distinct authority arms and do not fabricate one. ACK/release/status receipts remain the later action authority objects rather than being replaced by generic validation evidence. Every concrete matrix row pins subject/subkind, presented role, current authority role, consumer schema and action tag, allowed presentation arm, lineage relation, exact `TimeBoundSubject`, required `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, authority relation, current-state predicate, outcome, and retention class. Cross-kind/subkind/role/presentation substitution, stale service or security state, equal scalar under a different security root, NotYetValid/Expired evidence in a validation row, wrong verifier/key epoch/format, lineage drift, widening, action/scope substitution, use after retirement, and any unregistered row fail uniformly.

Construction is acyclic and fixed: current replay/key plus current authority/security/session request plus `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` plus the fresh same-process linear time-use guard plus any nonwidening proof and current lineage membership -> `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` -> exact lifecycle/transition/admission/receipt spec -> command -> applied result/successor/root. A durable Usable record surviving restart is not authority; each process must revalidate current state and acquire a fresh linear guard. A successor ref appears only in ConsumedImmediatePredecessor or MigratedConsumedExactRetry evidence after that successor already exists; the migration form also points backward to its initial validation generation and never forward to a later one. While its consumer or retry floor remains rooted, the object strongly retains the replay record, verifier key, time evidence and its profile/import basis, complete current authority/security basis, session authorization, and any nonwidening proof. Rejected input constructs no durable validation record. Diagnostics and events emit only a validated catalog row ID, context/action tag, and public outcome class; they never emit raw or committed capability/header/body/MAC values, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/handles, or attacker-controlled row/value text. The G0 schema, compatibility, construction-DAG, and sentinel-redaction checkers may be live once exact; codec/golden/fuzz, key/time rotation, restart/replay, race, migration, and public-noninterference evidence remain explicitly planned under W9/W10/W12 until their real checkers run.

Negative-time status classification is deliberately not another validation object and cannot authorize lookup or effect. `DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0003 LocalMergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|0x0004 MetaMergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}`, with each arm's decoded authority-header role and capability-kind predicate registered in its wire row; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis` is the embedded role-closed `u16` union `0x0001 Local{current_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Local,presented_replay:DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,presentation_binding:DurableCapabilityPresentationBinding,presented_capability_commitment,presented_header_digest,presented_kind_body_digest,verified_mac_transcript_digest,verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,verifier_key_identity,capability_format_version,time_subject_digest:TargetDigest<TimeBoundSubjectBody>,action_scope_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,authority_relation:0x0001 Exact|0x0002 Narrowed{proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>},action:TxnStatusLookup|MergeStatusLookup,canonical_status_request_digest}|0x0002 Meta{current_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta,presented_replay:DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,presentation_binding:DurableCapabilityPresentationBinding,presented_capability_commitment,presented_header_digest,presented_kind_body_digest,verified_mac_transcript_digest,verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,verifier_key_identity,capability_format_version,time_subject_digest:TargetDigest<TimeBoundSubjectBody>,action_scope_digest:TranscriptDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope>,authority_relation:0x0001 Exact|0x0002 Narrowed{proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>},action:TxnStatusLookup|MergeStatusLookup,canonical_status_request_digest}`; every other outer or authority-relation tag is reserved-invalid. The Local basis requires one of the two Local replay arms and ReadyChannelLocal or EmbeddedLocal; the Meta basis requires the corresponding Meta arms. `authority_relation` compares the complete current header/session authority with the replay's issuance header: Exact requires byte equality, while Narrowed requires the named proof over those exact two commitments; widening is uninhabited even when time cannot be classified. The status action-scope digest is recomputed from the exact `TxnStatusLookup` or `MergeStatusLookup` selector, canonical request, presentation-binding digest, capability commitment, and requested scope; its action, request digest, and time-subject digest must byte-match the other basis fields. It is constructible only after header/body/MAC, key, domain, current security, role, session, presentation, kind, request, action scope, time subject, and same-or-narrower authority authentication succeeds; it contains commitments, not raw token/MAC bytes.

`TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence` is the embedded closed `u16` failure union `0x0001 BoundaryOverlap{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,possible_time_interval,not_before,expires_at}|0x0002 CheckedArithmeticFailure{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,operation,operands_commitment}|0x0003 ProfileOrEpochUnavailable{profile_oid,required_domain_and_epoch,current_registry_commitment,time_subject_digest,intended_use_digest,stable_failure_class}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `DurableCapabilityStatusClassification` is the inline `u16` union `0x0001 Usable{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>}|0x0002 NotYetValid{authenticated_basis:AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:NotYetValid}|0x0003 Expired{authenticated_basis,time_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:Expired}|0x0004 TimeAuthorityUnavailable{authenticated_basis,failure:TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. In every negative arm, the evidence/failure `time_subject_digest` equals the authenticated basis's typed subject digest and `intended_use_digest` equals its exact action-scope digest; profile/window/request/presentation/capability fields must also agree, so another subject or request cannot supply the classification. It is legal only inside `StatusLookup`; the three negative arms cannot read the outcome/merge index, distinguish existence/current state, rotate a capability, or authorize any effect, and may emit only their named public time class. Invalid MAC/domain/security/role/presentation/kind/request produces `NotVisibleOrUnknown` with no classification object. `TokenExpired` additionally requires the existing durable expired requirement arm before send; the inline classifier does not invent expiry or retire bytes.

`LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>` is a generated associated type: Local contains only `AuthorityPermitRef<Local>`, Meta only `AuthorityPermitRef<Meta>`, and Shard is uninhabited. `LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>` is the generated closed union `PresentedPermit{permit_ref:LifecyclePresentedPermitRef<Role>}|RegisteredAuthority{registration_ref:RoleExactRegistrationRef,current_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,nonwidening_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>}|PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus{classification:DurableCapabilityStatusClassification}|AuthenticatedSession{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,request_digest}`; only role-valid arms inhabit each operation row. `PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus` is mandatory for a capability-bearing StatusLookup; its Usable arm owns the positive `DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence` ref and may proceed to the exact protected lookup, while its negative arms may only select the matching public time class. That source is forbidden for every non-status operation, and no ordinary PresentedDurableCapability Lifecycle arm exists. The durable capability kind/subkind is derived from the validation record or authenticated status basis, never repeated as an independently forgeable scalar. `LifecycleOperation` is exactly `RegisterAttempt|PrepareAdmissionScaffolding|RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active|PrepareAdmitted}|StatusLookup{registered_status_kind}|CapabilityManagement{registered_kind,action}`, where the generated associated action type is the disjoint union `Durable{Revoke}|Macaroon{Attenuate|Revoke}`; no generic Rotate or durable Attenuate arm exists. Client-authorized durable rotation is performed only by the exact typed transition surfaces and validation rows `TxnReattach|TxnRenew|ResultRotateResume|SubscriptionPause|SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect|SubscriptionAckBaseline|SubscriptionAckDelta|SubscriptionAckResetOrGap|ArtifactOutputResume|ReadYourWritesWait`; their own authorization/spec/receipt records retain positive validation evidence, and Lifecycle cannot add a second generic rotation path. The separately registered `SubscriptionDeliveryTransitionSpec::RotateCapability` is system-authorized Protocol maintenance with no presented client capability or DCVE compatibility row; it is distinct from Lifecycle rotation and uses only its structural authority arm. The `GlobalControlCommand(kind=CancelActiveAttempt)` and Local `TxnAbortSpec` both require `RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active}`; admitted Local/Meta abort requires `stage:PrepareAdmitted`. `LifecycleEffectClass<Operation>` is a generated associated closed tag: registration and preparation use their exact scaffolding classes; terminal abort uses `TerminalAbortNoEffectReleaseOnly{stage,registered_result_workspace_conflict_and_hold_disposition_schema}`; status is read-only projection; and capability management uses only the exact kind/action class above. There is no nullable permit, catch-all maintenance class, or wildcard rotate/attenuate/revoke row. `LifecycleAuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>` is the pre-result form `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,operation:LifecycleOperation,authority_source:LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>,sequence_neutral_spec_body_digest,requested_snapshot_or_scope_commitment,effect_class:LifecycleEffectClass<operation>,operation_audit_admission_commitment?,decision,authorization_audit_gate:AuthorizationAuditGate}`. The generated Role/operation matrix fixes every authority/source/effect arm, and the source, requested scope, audit evidence, lifecycle stage, and containing command must byte-match. RegisterAttempt uses a PresentedPermit; PrepareAdmission uses `PrepareAdmissionScaffolding` with exact NotRequired proof while its spec embeds the one GlobalMutation decision for complete effects; RequestTerminalAbort uses RegisteredAuthority plus the exact authenticated client request or the distinct administrative record. Capability-bearing status uses PresentedDurableCapabilityStatus; administrative durable revocation requires RegisteredAuthority or AuthenticatedSession, and macaroon attenuation remains in the macaroon/permit family. Protocol/system maintenance uses its registered structural system-authority command arm, never Lifecycle. ReadClose uses GlobalRead; each shard basis uses its own Read decision. A mutation/read/status decision, scalar epoch pair, fabricated zero effect, wrong-stage abort, or `StatusOrMaintenance` alias cannot substitute.

`TerminalAuditGate` is the same-group-only union `StructurallyInapplicable{exemption:StructuralAuditExemption}|NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|Required{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,terminal_resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>}`. A required gate is encodable only in the ticket-owning consensus domain and only when all three objects and the earlier authorization gate agree on namespace/domain/profile/principal/request; the resolution owns the event and its typed outcome matches the command/spec. The sole Local `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord` body is the PrepareAdmitted CAS schema in the Local transaction section; `Absent` and `Submitted` tags are unregistered. W12 exclusively uses the separate gate-free `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord`; no object is reinterpreted or wrapped as the other kind, and only the later `GlobalTxnCommand` carries W12's terminal gate. `DurableCapabilityVerifierKey {issuer_id,key_id,key_epoch,algorithm,public_or_protected_verifier_material,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,verify_through,format_versions[],rotation_predecessor?,status}` is Chronicle-sequenced and strongly retained until no live capability can require it; retirement requires exact Expired evidence for its registered subject/action. Each capability uses the exact common header/body/MAC format, names this key, and is never reinterpreted across versions or visibility epochs.
