title: Compose fgdbd: multi-tenant admission, drain choreography, and child terminality
description:
## What & scope
Compose `fgdbd` (`fgdb-server` crate): multi-database, multi-tenant serving by capability, connection admission, the full graceful-drain choreography with the closed child-terminality union, and GOODBYE discipline.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents cannot tolerate a server restart that loses admitted work or fabricates acknowledgements. Drain is a structural property (asupersync region close = no dropped in-flight commits) rather than a timeout heuristic; independently retained owners make restarts invisible to disconnected agents. Operationally this is the difference between "rolling deploy" and "incident."

## Design — normative detail
`fgdbd` is multi-database, multi-tenant by capability; connection admission composes semaphore + rate-limit combinators (`w10-qos`) ahead of session creation; the top-level composition wires Fabric + Warden + Aegis (§18.1 `fgdb-server`). Drain: `Draining{cause,cutoff_child_generation}` admits no later child. Each existing child must become exactly one of `EphemeralCancelledBeforeRegistration|TransactionOwnershipDetached|SemanticTerminalDurable|AdmittedRecoveryRooted|ResultDurablyDetached|ArtifactOutputDurablyDetached|SubscriptionDurablyDetached|ProtectedErrorDurablyOwned`, and every transport obligation must become Sent, CancelledBeforeWrite, or Failed. Drain never fabricates ACK/release/expiry and never waits for an offline client; independent result/output/cursor owners remain rooted after connection/process close. Draining waits only for: queued/writing transport obligations to become Sent/Failed, required audit publications, prepublication cancellations, admitted-decision recovery, terminal records, and durable detach/pause of senders. GOODBYE is emitted only after durable handoff; transport failure closes without another protected frame. Region-structured concurrency makes "no dropped in-flight commits" a type-level property: an admitted semantic decision either completes under its durable rules or is recovery-rooted before the region closes. Per-tenant/per-database authority surfaces, availability lines, and isolation-unit doctrine follow `w9-authority-surface` (§16); shutdown ordering: stop admission -> drain adapters -> drain FGP children per the union -> close regions -> flush observability.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: no admitted obligation is lost or duplicated across drain/restart; under declared fairness every child reaches one legal terminal or recovery-rooted state. FG-INV-15: drain cannot release retained output. FG-INV-01: admitted decisions complete exactly once across restart (recovery joins, never re-executes). Drain-time bounds and admission limits are configuration/`slo.toml` rows; drain choreography transcripts and crash-restart corpora are FG-EVID artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w10-fgp-core` (child machines), `w10-adapters` (transport endpoints), `w10-qos` (admission), `w10-result-machines` (detached owners), `w9-authority-surface` (per-posture authority footprint, succession). Feeds `obs-observatory`/`obs-slo` (drain metrics), `verif-torture` (multiprocess crash campaigns), `w11-*` (the same drain law under cluster membership changes).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Drain matrix: for every child type in every state, initiate drain and assert the reached terminal class is in the closed union — no fabricated ACK/release/expiry (evidence-absence assertion), no wait on a deliberately offline client (bounded drain with owners left IndependentlyRetained). Crash-during-drain: kill at each choreography step; restart shows admitted decisions recovery-rooted, obligations reconciled, zero duplicate effects. In-flight commit test: SIGTERM storm during sustained writes — every accepted COMMIT reaches a durable terminal; every unaccepted one is cleanly absent. GOODBYE ordering fixture: no protected frame after transport failure. Multi-tenant isolation: one tenant's admission saturation cannot starve another's emergency/maintenance reserves (logged admission decisions per tenant). e2e rolling-restart script under agent load with structured logs: cause, cutoff generation, per-child terminal class, drain duration histogram.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: drain latency under large retained-owner populations — owners detach durably rather than being awaited, keeping drain bounded. Rejected: timeout-and-kill drain (fabricates outcomes); waiting for client ACKs during shutdown (offline clients block forever); a separate lifecycle for embedded vs. server (one child-terminality union serves both).

## Provenance
§13.2 (993), §13.3 (994), Appendix D 2770, §18.1, §16.

title: Implement the SnapshotQuery ephemeral read class end-to-end with its oracle
description:
## What & scope
Implement the `SnapshotQuery` class end-to-end: bind-time eligibility, the `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` execution-scope arm, visible-endpoint pinning, the `SNAPSHOT_RESULT_CHUNK`/`SNAPSHOT_RESULT_END` frame family, the `SnapshotEphemeralOutput` send-guard path, registry citizenship, and the strict-serializability differential oracle.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is the fast read class that §17's point-read and 1-hop latency gates measure: the durable class's begin/registration/publication machinery prices every read like a transaction. `SnapshotQuery` keeps authorization-before-observation, visible-endpoint pinning, fresh send guards, and strict serializability while shedding durable cost — and states honestly, as a declared class contract, what it gives up. B6: agents get a typed, data-independent steer to the durable class when policy demands it; B5: sampled Sextant evidence keeps calibration coverage on the hottest surface.

## Design — normative detail
`SnapshotQuery` is the registered second honest result class beside the durable classes: a single-envelope, permit-validated, visible-endpoint-pinned, session-owned ephemeral result stream that consumes zero sequenced semantic commands and zero Protocol-plane maintenance transitions — no begin reservation, no attempt registration, no statement records, no durable result retention, no delivery lease, and no resume capability. Output is dropped on disconnect, explicitly non-resumable, and audit-NotRequired by construction. Class selection is bind-time and policy-driven, never a client verb: a statement is eligible exactly when (a) its `CanonicalStatementClassification` proves ProvenReadOnly single-statement autocommit within the class's declared output/row/time bounds; (b) the effective `AuditCompletenessProfile` does not name the operation class Required; (c) the classification carries no DP or Warden-classified operation class (`required_warden_operation_classes` empty and an ordinary `output_class`); and (d) the namespace's registered class policy permits the class — a governed namespace may force every read onto the durable path. Under a Required-read profile, eligibility fails closed with a typed, data-independent rejection steering the statement to the durable class; a silent upgrade is forbidden. While `security_barrier_state=AppliedHidden`, admission returns the same bounded, data-independent audit-backpressure class as every other admission (§12.8).

Admission is a new registered `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` execution-scope arm (Appendix A): coordinator-local and non-ordered, with authorization preceding every observation (FG-INV-20), pinning the pipeline's visible candidate root (FG-INV-04) through the ordinary `AuthorizedSnapshot`/`fgdb-secure-view` boundary under an ordinary snapshot retention lease. The arm is exactly `LocalSnapshotQuery{common:ReadAccessCommon<Local>,execution_scope:ReadExecutionScope::LocalSnapshotQuery,permit_ref:ReadCapablePermitRef<Local>,class_policy_ref:StrongRef<SnapshotQueryClassPolicy>,classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>,declared_output_bounds:SnapshotQueryOutputBounds,session_binding_digest,visible_endpoint_binding_commitment}`: session-owned and never durably persisted — no durable object may strongly reference it — and it carries no audit admission or audit-gate field, so a Required-profile operation is unencodable in this arm; it is not substitutable for a Local terminal/statement arm. Results stream through the ordinary canonical-chunk encoding and a fresh `PublicFrameSendGuard::SnapshotEphemeralOutput{admission_record_commitment,visible_endpoint_binding_commitment,read_release_authorization_digest}` immediately before every frame write — output-side revocation fencing preserved unchanged — under session-scoped ephemeral resource reservations, never durable charge. Wire: an eligible request rides the ordinary EXECUTE surface (no client verb); the response is BEGIN-less `SNAPSHOT_RESULT_CHUNK{stream_ordinal,chunk_ordinal,canonical_offset,chunk_digest,payload}` frames carrying the ordinary canonical-chunk encoding fields with no result owner projection, resume capability, delivery lease, or delivery state token, then `SNAPSHOT_RESULT_END{stream_ordinal,chunk_count,effective_snapshots:PublicEffectiveSnapshotSet}` with no durable-outcome projection; frames obey ordinary flow control under the `SnapshotStream{admission_commitment,stream_ordinal}` subject arm; ineligibility, revocation, and security-barrier backpressure return uniform NotVisibleOrUnknown/audit-backpressure classes with no data-dependent shape. After disconnect nothing is resumable and no durable record exists — no ACK, release, retry-join, replay, or outcome lookup. The class's `AnswerContract` behavior row records non-resumable, no-replay, no-durable-outcome semantics: giving up durable outcome lookup, idempotent retry joining, result resume, replay evidence, and exactly-once delivery is part of the declared class contract, not an implementation weakness. The class is strict-serializable by construction — a visible-endpoint read whose acknowledgement discipline satisfies §7.1's real-time condition — and that claim carries its own differential oracle against the durable read path, never inherited by analogy. Sampled Sextant decision-card/propensity evidence is emitted under a registered sampling policy. Registry citizenship is complete: `command_type_classification.toml` rows for the non-ordered admission types, the Appendix D `SnapshotQuery` frame family joined once in `wire_types.toml`, the `AnswerContract` behavior row, and the amended FG-INV-04/FG-INV-20 clauses in Appendix F; §17's point-read and 1-hop gate rows measure exactly this class while the durable classes carry their own Appendix G command/entry/barrier budget rows.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (amended clause, restated): applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline; a `SnapshotQuery` admission reads only the pipeline's visible candidate root and can never observe applied-hidden state. FG-INV-20 (amended clause, restated): `SnapshotQuery` admission obeys the identical authorization-before-observation rule — coordinator-local admission verifies the complete capability and policy binding before any statement or storage observation — with the same oracle coverage as the durable read classes. The point-read/1-hop latency numbers are §17 `slo.toml` benchmark-class gates; strict-serializability is an invariant-class claim with a named oracle; Sextant sampling coverage is a calibration (FG-CAL) row.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-binder` (`CanonicalStatementClassification`, class selection), `w4-secure-view` (`AuthorizedSnapshot` boundary), `w2-snapshots-leases` (retention lease), `w9-enforcement` (permit validation), `w9-audit-pipeline` (visible candidate root, AppliedHidden backpressure), `w5-answer-contracts` (behavior row), `w10-fgp-core` (frames/guards), `verif-sextant` (sampling policy). Measured by `perf-bench-core`; oracle lives with `verif-oracles`/`verif-differential`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Differential oracle: randomized ProvenReadOnly workloads via both classes — byte-identical canonical results plus a strict-serializability (real-time condition) check over mixed durable-write/SnapshotQuery histories. Eligibility matrix tests: each of the four conditions independently violated yields the typed data-independent rejection (byte/timing uniform); Required-read profile never silently upgrades. Negative golden fixture: `LocalSnapshotQuery` is not substitutable for a Local terminal/statement admission arm, and a Required-profile operation is unencodable in it (encoding attempt fails at type/decode level, logged with the rejected arm tag). Visible-endpoint negatives: applied-hidden commits invisible to admission under interleaved visibility advances. Fuzz: SNAPSHOT_RESULT frames rejected outside `SnapshotEphemeralOutput` arm; disconnect mid-stream leaves zero durable records (GC oracle sweep). Bench gate: §17 point-read/1-hop rows measured on this class in CI with logged latency anatomy per Appendix G. Sextant sampling e2e: decision cards emitted at configured rate, verified in the calibration ledger.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: class-selection policy complexity leaking data-dependence — all rejections are typed and data-independent by test. Rejected: a client-requested fast-read verb (policy bypass); silent upgrade to durable class (cost surprise, audit hole); inheriting strict-serializability by analogy (oracle required); making the fast class resumable (recreates durable retention by the back door).

## Provenance
§13.3 (1025-1029), Appendix D 2794, 2898-2902; FG-INV-04/20 (Appendix F).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement TxnOwnershipLease reattach/renew/expiry and the ownership directory
description:
## What & scope
Implement durable active-transaction ownership: `TxnOwnershipLease<Role>`, `TxnOwnershipDirectory<Role>`, the closed `TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec<Role>` (Reattach/Renew), lease-expiry abort, and the TXN_REATTACH/TXN_REATTACHED/TXN_RENEW/TXN_RENEWED frames.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: session binding must be an ordered, generation-fenced lease — never an in-memory connection pointer — so an agent process can die mid-statement and a successor can take over the same transaction with the old process provably fenced before it can order another effect.

## Design — normative detail
`TxnOwnershipLease<Role>` (closed Local/Meta specialization) is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,registration_ref:StrongRef<RoleAttemptRegistration>,ownership_generation,owner_session_binding_digest,owner_auth_generation,current_outcome_capability_replay_ref,current_capability_commitment,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,open_statement_state:Idle|Open{statement_identity,statement_state_version,detached_sender_state},control_mode:FullControl|RollbackAndStatusOnly,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,weak_prior_lease_identity,body_digest}`; it never strongly names a predecessor. `TxnOwnershipDirectory<Role>` maps each registered nonterminal attempt to exactly `Owned{lease_ref}|PrepareFenced{prepare_admission_ref,last_ownership_generation,capability_lineage_ref}|Terminal{terminal_lookup_key}`. Registration atomically installs generation zero; every statement registration/publication/abort, commit, rollback, and ownership transition must present an ephemeral handle whose `{registration,ownership_generation,session_binding,authority_binding}` byte-matches the current Owned leaf — a later generation fences every old process/session/handle. `TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec<Role>` has no shared ambiguous body: `Reattach {expected_owned_lease_ref,presented_capability_validation_ref,presented_replay_ref,expected_capability_lineage_ref,canonical_request_idempotency_key,new_session_binding_digest,new_auth_generation,current_authority_bound_header,requested_control_mode,open_statement_disposition:NoOpen|TransferRecoverableExecution{old_compute_owner_fence_ref,new_compute_owner_recipe,complete_task_and_sender_handoff_proof_ref}|CancelAndTerminalize{structured_cancel_completion_ref,statement_terminalization_ref,result_detachment_proofs[]},prebuilt_successor_capability_replay_ref,successor_lease_body_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}` may change session only through one exact open-statement disposition. `Renew {expected_owned_lease_ref,presented_current_capability_validation_ref,expected_capability_lineage_ref,canonical_request_idempotency_key,required_same_session_binding_digest,required_same_auth_generation,current_authority_bound_header,requested_not_before,requested_expires_at,time_validation_evidence_ref,prebuilt_successor_capability_replay_ref,successor_lease_body_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}` cannot transfer session/control mode and requires Usable evidence for the exact successor window/action. Both validate domain/principal/generation and CAS one successor; an open statement can never be left without a compute owner or terminalization path. PrepareFenced permits status only. Expiry cannot strand: every active lease satisfies `expires_at <= current_outcome_capability.expiry`; `TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec<Role>` references `time_validation_evidence_ref` whose decoded tag/classification must be Expired for the exact lease/action (a ref to an inline enum variant is illegal), requires complete structured cancellation/open-statement terminalization/result detachment/workspace-resource/conflict evidence, and is legal only before PrepareFenced. Renewal lost-response recovery uses the capability lineage rule.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (verbatim core): transaction ownership is generation-fenced, durably reattachable/renewable only under the capability lineage, and becomes PrepareFenced atomically before finalization; expiry can only order the registered rollback/status-safe path. FG-INV-01: reattach/renew idempotency keys map to one outcome. Model/crash coverage of every boundary and no-stranding condition is an explicit FG-EVID deliverable.

## Interactions
Consumes `w10-capabilities` (TxnOutcome lineage, prebuilt successors), `w2-txn-lifecycle` (attempt registration, terminal completion), `w4-coordinator` (prepare fencing), `w9-time-authority` (`TimeValidationEvidence`). Consumed by `w10-embedded` (ownership renewal/reattachment), `w10-python` (GC-abandoned txn abort), `w10-server` (drain: TransactionOwnershipDetached).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Model checking: no interleaving of {statement publication, reattach, renew, expiry abort, prepare admission} lets two generations order effects, leaves an open statement ownerless, or aborts after PrepareFenced. Crash matrix: kill at each of lease install, transition CAS, successor prebuild, frame send; recovery presents predecessor capability and receives the exact successor. Negative fixtures: renew with changed session binding; reattach with stale lineage ref; expiry abort with non-Expired evidence — all fail closed. e2e: two-process handover script logging generations, dispositions, and fence proofs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: transfer-of-open-statement complexity — the `TransferRecoverableExecution` proof bundle is mandatory, not best-effort. Rejected: connection-pointer ownership (unfenceable); server-side rollback on disconnect (destroys agent recovery); an ambiguous shared transition body (aliasing bugs).

## Provenance
§13.3 (1004-1008), Appendix D 2807-2816.

### Verification-layer classification

The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. title: Build the deterministic UDF bytecode VM and native-procedure boundary rules
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-udf-vm`: the fuel/memory/stack-bounded deterministic bytecode VM with mediated authority and pinned arithmetic, the validated-Datalog admission path, and the categorical boundary rules for native Rust procedures.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: extensibility is where determinism usually dies. FGDB draws a hard line — anything replicated, replayed, or merged must run inside a machine whose every step is deterministic and fuel-bounded; native code stays an embedded-host convenience that can never contaminate replicated state. This preserves replay grades (FG-INV-19) and rebase determinism (FG-INV-17) under user extensibility, which competitors cannot claim for their procedure surfaces.

## Design — normative detail
Replicated/apply/merge logic is limited to validated Datalog or the fuel/memory/stack-bounded deterministic bytecode VM with mediated authority and pinned arithmetic (numeric profiles from §8.6 — no host-float drift, no platform-dependent intrinsics). The VM meters fuel per instruction, bounds stack depth and heap bytes at admission, and exposes authority only through mediated host calls that check permits per invocation — no ambient capability. No mutable clock, entropy, filesystem, network, or policy lookup is reachable from replayed execution. Native Rust procedures remain embedded-host extensions and are categorically barred from replicated logical effects, merge/apply, constraints, and replay-guaranteed queries; a conformance test cannot prove arbitrary native code deterministic — the bar is categorical, not empirical. Native read procedures receive authorized views (through `fgdb-secure-view`-derived projections) and are labeled external nondeterminism unless their outputs are excluded from strict replay. Datalog admission validates the registered subset (see `w6-recursion` for incremental fixpoints); UDF registration is a transactional SchemaOp with pinned `IntentSemanticsOid` so merge/rebase replays the exact semantics version. Built in-house per §18.2.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-17 (verbatim core): rebase and branch merge execute under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`; no mutable clock, entropy, filesystem, network, or policy lookup enters replay. FG-INV-19: native-procedure outputs not excluded from replay downgrade the manifest grade attributably. FG-INV-20: mediated host calls authorize before observation. Fuel/memory/stack bounds are configuration rows; determinism differential corpora (same program, N platforms/runs, byte-identical traces) are FG-EVID artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-determinism` (numeric profiles, CGSE contracts), `w9-enforcement` (mediated authority permits), `w5-executor` (invocation from query execution), `w1-foundation-types` (value types). Consumed by `w10-bolt` V2 (registered UDF/module set is the only procedure surface), `w4-merge-ladder`/`w2-branch-merge` consumers for deterministic merge logic, `w10-embedded` (native procedure host).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Determinism differential: randomized bytecode programs executed across platforms and repeated runs produce byte-identical outputs and fuel counts. Bounds: fuel exhaustion, stack overflow, heap cap each yield typed deterministic aborts at the exact same instruction index across runs. Authority: fuzz host-call sequences — every observation preceded by a permit check (taint assertion); ambient-capability escape attempts fail compile/validation. Boundary negatives: attempt to register a native procedure for merge/apply/constraints/replay-guaranteed queries — rejected at registration with typed error. Replay: a query using a VM UDF replays byte-identically; the same query using a non-excluded native read procedure is labeled external nondeterminism and downgrades the manifest grade (assert grade computation). e2e: register a VM UDF through a transactional SchemaOp with pinned `IntentSemanticsOid`, invoke it via query on at least two platforms, then replay — byte-identical outputs, fuel counts, and manifest grades; the implementation and tests log per-invocation fuel consumed, instruction count, abort instruction index (if any), every mediated host-call permit check (subject, permit, decision), and the determinism-boundary label attached to any native-procedure output, so replay-grade computation is verifiable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: VM performance for hot UDFs — mitigate with fuel-priced fast paths, never JIT-with-host-float. Rejected: WASM runtime dependency (closed universe; determinism caveats around NaN/SIMD); conformance-testing native code into replicated paths (unsound); trusting procedure authors with ambient authority.

## Provenance
§13.8 (1059), §18.2, §8.6; FG-INV-17/19.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement wire-safe public projections, handles, receipts, and the wire taint checker
description:
## What & scope
Implement the wire-safe public type system every FGP frame is built from: projection domains, handles, state tokens, opaque commitments, disclosure receipts, the closed posture-tagged projections, and the generated taint checker proving no internal identity ever crosses the wire.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/B5: agents correlate everything; opaque-by-construction wire types prevent cross-principal/cross-epoch correlation oracles and offline dictionaries while still letting authorized clients compare positions through registered comparison domains. This is the "no ObjectId on wire" doctrine that makes the whole security story checkable.

## Design — normative detail
Every opaque value is built under `PublicProjectionDomain {database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,posture,principal_scope_commitment,non_widenable_authority_commitment,projection_key_epoch}`. `PublicHandle<Kind>` is a pre-minted random 128-bit nonce plus a domain-separated MAC over domain/kind/nonce — never derived from an ObjectId, marker, counter, name, or low-entropy hidden fact. `PublicStateToken<Kind>` is a separately pre-minted random CAS nonce plus the same scoped MAC for one externally addressable state transition — not a serialized internal generation. `OpaquePublicCommitment<Kind>` is `PRF(projection_key, "fgdb:opaque:" || domain || kind || per_subject_random_salt || canonical_internal_subject_commitment)`. Key rotation never recomputes a live public token; replay retains exact bytes and the verifier-key floor. The sole portable field-declassification proof is `PortablePublicDisclosureReceipt {receipt_version,projection_domain_commitment,disclosure_profile_oid,stable_projection_subject_commitment,allowed_public_field_bitmap,receipt_free_projection_digest,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_epoch,signature}`; the signature covers every preceding field plus the receipt-free projection digest, never itself, and contains no session binding, local reference, state root, topology identity, policy/revocation counter, or internal position — frozen bytes survive reconnect and compaction; the later `PublicFrameSendGuard` separately binds them to the current Ready/session/auth generation.

Closed posture-tagged projections (each `Local|Sharded`, noninterchangeable): `PublicMarkerProjection{handle,commitment,disclosure:Opaque|Disclosed{public_comparison_domain,public_ordinal,receipt}}`; `PublicLogicalPositionProjection` (Disclosed adds `axis:LocalLogical|GlobalLogical`); `PublicSnapshotProjection{snapshot_handle,snapshot_commitment,logical_position,normalized_valid_time_projection,selector_echo_commitment,receipt:None|Some}`; `PublicResultOwnerProjection{owner_handle,owner_commitment,disclosure:Opaque|Disclosed{owner_class:TerminalRead|AutocommitWriteTerminal|Statement|DpResult|ReplayExecution,receipt}}`. Digest projections `PublicEffectProjection|PublicPublicationProjection|PublicResultDigestProjection|PublicOutputDigestProjection` are each `Omitted{commitment}|Disclosed{digest_of_authorized_public_bytes,receipt}` — a disclosed digest is recomputed from the registered authorized public transcript, never copied from an internal digest; cross-kind substitution fails decoding. `PublicReasonProjection` is `Opaque{coarse_class:OperationDidNotComplete,reason_commitment}|Disclosed{public_reason_code:RegisteredPublicReasonCode,reason_commitment,receipt}`. `StablePublicReasonClass` and generic `PublicDigestProjection` are invalid types. Sets: `PublicEffectiveSnapshotSet{set_handle,sorted_bindings[{client_binding_ordinal,graph_binding_handle,branch_handle,effective_snapshot}],set_commitment}` and `PublicRywFloorSet{set_handle,visibility_floor,sorted_branch_floors[],set_commitment}` (unique, sorted by client binding ordinal). Incoming selection is `WireGraphReferenceSpec {client_binding_ordinal,graph_selector,branch_selector,system_time_selector,valid_time_selector,required_public_schema_contract}`; `PublicMarkerSelector` is handle+expected commitment backed by the server's retained mapping/floor — a display commitment alone cannot select a merge basis. Release evidence projections: `AuditReleaseEvidence` is exactly `NotRequired{release_subject_commitment,nonrequired_evidence_projection,visibility:Opaque|Declassified}|RequiredVisible{release_subject_commitment,audit_outcome_and_visibility_commitment,visibility:Opaque|Declassified}` (no nullable fields; a raw position only in the authorized declassification arm); `ReadReleaseAuthorizationEvidence` never serializes an internal policy epoch, revocation index, authority digest, root identity, or decision-record reference. `wire_types.toml` materializes the noninterchangeable aliases (`PublicTxnHandle`, `PublicRegistrationHandle`, `PublicResultDeliveryHandle`, `PublicArtifactOutputHandle`, `PublicCursorHandle`, `PublicBaselineHandle`, `PublicDeliveryLeaseHandle`, `PublicMergeHandle`, `PublicAuditSubjectHandle`, `PublicErrorDeliveryHandle`, matching `PublicStateToken` kinds). `ProofBody` is the closed union `RawCommitMembership|RawContiguousRange|FilteredMembership|FilteredCompleteness|ReplayProjectionVerification|OutputDigestVerification` — no generic payload arm. Forbidden wire types: at-rest `SymbolRecord`, `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, `PlacementDescriptor`, object DEKs, placement metadata; G0 rejects any protected frame containing `ObjectId`, any reference tag, `WeakMarkerIdentity`, `GraphReferenceBinding`, `CoordinateSchemaBinding`, `DerivedIdentity`, raw internal counter/frontier/generation, or `ReplayManifest`. The generated taint checker proves every wire path passes an exact projection constructor and fresh send guard.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 clause: equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute; uniform `NotVisibleOrUnknown` on failure. FG-INV-15 clause: public digests cover exact authorized canonical bytes, never keyed object IDs. The taint-checker output and golden projection vectors are FG-EVID artifacts; the PRF/MAC constructions inherit `w1-crypto` review-gate claims.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-identity-registries` (wire_types.toml), `w1-crypto` (PRF/MAC profiles), `w9-enforcement`/`w9-audit-release` (release-decision inputs). Produces every opaque type consumed by `w10-fgp-core`, `w10-capabilities`, `w10-result-machines`, `w10-snapshotquery`, `w10-cdc`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Taint checker in CI: zero wire paths bypassing projection constructors (negative fixture per forbidden type). Property tests: handle/token/commitment unlinkability across principals and projection-key epochs; cross-kind decode substitution fails; disclosed ordinals only inside a registered comparison domain/epoch with retention floor (v1 otherwise emits Opaque). Golden vectors for every projection and the receipt signature transcript (signature excludes itself). Fuzz decoders for all closed unions rejecting unknown arms. e2e: drive a live FGP session across every projection-emitting frame family, capture the full wire transcript, and run the taint checker over both source paths and the captured transcript — zero internal identities anywhere; the implementation logs every projection construction (projection-domain commitment, kind, projection key epoch, handle nonce lifecycle) and every send-guard binding of frozen receipt bytes to a Ready/session/auth generation, so cross-principal/cross-epoch unlinkability and receipt-signature transcripts are auditable from logs after implementation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: projection sprawl — bounded by the generated alias registry. Rejected: deriving handles from internal IDs (dictionary/correlation oracle); nullable release-evidence fields (ambiguity); a generic digest projection (cross-kind substitution).

## Provenance
§13.3 (1033-1047), Appendix D 2772-2774.

title: Build ATP multi-donor transfer, symbol authentication, and Merkle anti-entropy
description:
## What & scope
Implement §14.5's transfer and repair plane: ATP (fountain-coded transfer protocol) multi-donor symbol fetch, per-symbol authentication against logical/encoding identity and the §5.1 MAC transcript, Merkle anti-entropy for divergence location, and the CRDT position-gossip cache — plus new-replica seeding.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Replicas diverge physically by design (repair ESIs, ciphertext encodings, placement need not be byte-identical), so repair must be defined at the logical/encoding-identity layer, not byte mirroring. Fountain-coded multi-donor fetch (ATP) makes repair bandwidth-efficient and donor-failure-tolerant. B5: authentication is per-symbol and transcript-bound — **donor agreement alone creates no authority**; two lying donors are still lies.

## Design — normative detail
ATP may fetch compatible symbols from multiple donors concurrently. Every symbol is authenticated against the exact logical/encoding identity and the §5.1 MAC transcript (symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; `EncodingId` fixes the FEC profile/parameters so incompatible encodings never combine — a symbol from encoding A cannot help decode encoding B even for the same logical object). A fetched object is accepted only when its `ObjectId`/`CiphertextId`/`EncodingId` recompute from the registered descriptors and bytes (FG-INV-09); the receiver then realizes its own placement (possibly a different `PlacementId`) — physical divergence is fine, logical-digest divergence is an incident.

Merkle anti-entropy locates two distinct classes: missing encodings (a replica lacks a durable realization it should hold under the placement policy) and logical-digest divergence (replicas disagree on canonical semantic content at the same role/prefix — which the Aegis doctrine forbids (§14: canonical logical effects/digests agree across replicas; checked by the replica logical-digest oracle under FG-INV-19); it is surfaced as fatal evidence, not silently repaired). Tree ranges are computed over registry-typed identity keyspaces so comparisons are role/namespace-scoped.

Applied/durable positions may gossip through a CRDT cache (monotone max-merge, advisory only), but **branch heads derive only from committed head CAS records** — the gossip cache can route repair and tune scheduling, never define state. Donor selection uses SWIM/Lifeguard evidence plus the position cache; donor authority for serving symbols is checked against the donor's fenced member identity and current `ConfigurationState` (a retired or fenced member is not a legal donor). Seeding a new replica is the same machinery pointed at the full closure: snapshot cut + suffix + prepared/protocol closures per `w11-raft-multi` formats, with reconstructibility tiering from `w2-fec-scrub` deciding what is decoded vs. copied.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 (excerpt): `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory; child-key AAD and symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; collision buckets verify full identity and incompatible encodings never combine. Repair throughput/latency and scrub cadence are `slo.toml`/`FG-EVID-02` (scrub/corpus-health evidence) claim classes; MTTDL impact feeds `FG-CFG-01`.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-object-identity` (§5.1 SymbolRecord/MAC transcripts, identity pipeline), `w2-fec-scrub` (RaptorQ profiles, dynamic reconstructibility tiering, scrubber), `w1-crypto` (MAC/AEAD profiles), `w11-payload-availability` (prepared-payload donor duties share the donor service), `w11-membership-config` (donor legality against current configuration; SWIM evidence). Produces the repair path consumed by `w11-fenced-gc` (repair must respect quarantine no-new-reference rules) and W12 (`w12-*` anti-entropy across groups uses certified wrappers instead).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/fuzz: symbol MAC verification with bit-flips, wrong-key, wrong-namespace, mixed-encoding symbol sets (FG-INV-09 fuzz campaign rows); truncated/duplicated/reordered symbol streams decode correctly or fail typed. Property: multi-donor decode with adversarial donors (one honest donor sufficient given enough symbols; poisoned symbols detected per-symbol, never accepted by majority). Merkle: injected missing-encoding and injected logical-divergence both located within the expected probe count; divergence raises fatal evidence, never auto-overwrite. CRDT cache: gossip stale/forged positions — assert zero effect on branch heads or repair authority (heads only from committed CAS records). Seeding e2e with logs: add a member to a 2-node cluster under write load; logs record symbols fetched per donor, verification failures, decode campaigns; final state passes the log-to-state verifier and full digest doctor.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: rsync-style byte mirroring (breaks under legal physical divergence); quorum-attested symbol validity (donor agreement is not authority); gossip-derived heads (would let a partitioned minority resurrect state). Risk: anti-entropy traffic competing with foreground load — bounded by the repair budget tiering from `w2-fec-scrub` and ResourceVector admission.

## Provenance
§14.5 (line 1078, first half), §5.1, §5.7, App F FG-INV-09, FG-EVID-02, FG-CFG-01.

title: Implement Local backup barriers, pins, closure certificates, and manifest construction
description:
## What & scope
Implement the source side of §16.6 backup: ordered barriers, durable source pins, copy + independent content reopen, closure certificates, and acyclic `BackupManifest` construction — for Local posture, with the Sharded (Meta intent / shard pin / global seal) generalization implemented as the reserved schemas. Publication, transparency, archive grants, and the external authorize/dispatch/import machinery live in `w11-backup-publication`; source-release holds, pin release, completion import, and abort live in `w11-backup-release`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Backup uses **ordered source pins, not a manifest that permanently retains the live database**: pinning is a typed, ordered lease on the source closure that is dropped only after the published artifact is independently proved recoverable and the archive authority durably holds a release. This gives B5-grade evidence (a backup you cannot independently reopen is not a backup) without B1-violating retention leaks. Agent-native ops (B6): every backup phase is a typed registry state, queryable and resumable.

## Design — normative detail
A **Local barrier** fixes one published root/checkpoint/vector/configuration/floor/prepared/certificate/remote/history closure: `LocalBackupBarrierSpec {backup_id,authorized_request_digest,expected_source_root_manifest_ref,expected_logical_state_root_ref,expected_logical_command_seq,expected_commit_seq,expected_raft_index,expected_checkpoint_ref,expected_checkpoint_vector_digest,expected_configuration_ref,expected_config_payload_floor_ref,expected_prepared_root_generation,expected_certificate_ledger_digest,expected_retained_history_interval,archive_profile_ref,recipient_and_key_recovery_profile_ref,format_matrix_ref,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply requires `Operational` and exact equality, then creates `LocalBackupPinRecord {backup_id,source_domain,barrier_logical_command_seq,barrier_commit_seq,barrier_raft_index,source_root_manifest_ref,source_logical_state_root_ref,pinned_closure_refs[BackupPinnedClosureRef<Local>],pinned_closure_coverage_bitmap,complete_logical_and_physical_inventory_root_ref:StrongRef<BackupSourceInventory>,pin_generation}`. **This ordered record, not the manifest, is the source retention lease.** `BackupPinnedClosureRef<Role>` is a generated tagged union of `RegisteredStrongRef` arms legal for the exact role payload schema; every value carries its `source_slot_tag`, and the coverage bitmap must equal every live mandatory-inventory class at the barrier exactly once — role-invalid, untyped, duplicate, missing, or ambient strong edges are unencodable.

Content identity classes: `BackupSourceIdentity<T> {source_authority_domain,source_cluster_incarnation,object_kind,object_id,canonical_digest}` is nonretaining evidence, never accepted by mark traversal. `BackupContentSubject<T>` is `SourceObject{expected_source}|RecoveryProjection{backup_id,projection_digest}` (RecoveryProjection legal only for `T=BackupRecoveryProjection`). Root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>` `{backup_id,archive_authority_id,inventory_key,subject,archived_byte_digest,archived_length,protection_profile,required_recovery_proof_class}` can be embedded before the final inventory root exists; rooted `BackupArchiveRef<T>` `{entry,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,inventory_leaf_index,inventory_inclusion_proof}` is constructed only after, and must authenticate under a current matching archive-retention grant.

Portable recovery is one plane-complete object: `RecoverySlotDisposition` is `TransformCurrent|CarryPriorEvidence|RecreateCurrentAuthority|ReconcileExternal|SuspendProtocolOwner|DiscardReplicaLocal{registered_law_id}|Reject`. `PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Role>` carries semantic cut (applied+visible states/positions), protocol cut (protocol state, maintenance generation/index, audit pipeline + pending queue inventory, result/cursor/artifact/error/escrow inventory, security barrier state), prepared cut, consensus cut (applied-cut snapshot, retained suffix, configuration, certificate/attempt ledgers, remote obligation floors), checkpoint/floor cut, external continuity inputs, bootstrap reconstruction inputs, sorted slot dispositions, and a complete durable-state-slot coverage proof. `BackupRecoveryProjection` is `Local{common,local_cut}|Sharded{common,meta_cut,sorted_shard_cuts,exact_global_barrier_and_partition_bijection_proof}`; every activated `durable_state_slots.toml` row and mandatory inventory class has exactly one disposition; same-identity recovery preserves applied/visible divergence, the exact pending audit queue, independent output owners, prepared owners, and maintenance suffix. Clone projections require either a certified `CloneExportReady` cut with no applied-hidden barrier or an explicit exclude/transfer/reissue disposition for every hidden entry — a clone may never make source hidden state target-visible; old transport leases/capabilities restore as suspended/no-send until fresh target authorization and time evidence, and source Raft hard state crosses as historical evidence, never as current target consensus state.

`BackupManifestBody` construction order is exact and acyclic: archive every source object + root-free entry -> build/archive `BackupRecoveryProjection` from only those entries -> add its entry -> compute the final content-inventory root + inclusion proofs -> construct rooted `BackupArchiveRef`s -> construct the body `{backup_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,source_cluster_incarnation,source_posture,barrier,backup_state,exact_logical_commit_base_and_anti_rollback_ranges,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,content_archive_inventory_count,recovery_projection_ref,recovery_projection_digest,branch_checkpoint_history_prepared_certificate_key_derived_trust_continuity_cursor_delivery_replay_inventories,object_id_key_escrow_policy,recipient_policy,format_matrix,canonical_semantic_digest,trust_policy,transparency_policy:NotRequired{policy_digest}|Required{log_id,minimum_checkpoint_policy_oid},prior_transparency_checkpoint?}`. Publication-envelope objects are excluded from the content inventory. `BackupManifestSignatureSet` binds complete body bytes/digest and signer identities/keys/epochs; `BackupManifest` is exactly `{body_ref,signature_set_ref,body_digest,signature_set_digest,manifest_format_major,manifest_format_minor}` — **no self digest, receipt, inclusion, grant, or reopen proof** (its acyclic Body -> SignatureSet -> Manifest construction is the registered exception to the BodyDigest convention).

Verification objects: `BackupInventoryBijectionProof` (no missing source, no extra archive, no duplicate target, per-entry length/digest), `BackupRecoverabilityProof` (protection profile, failure-domain predicate vs observed inventory, deterministic decode campaign, key-escrow recovery), and pre-seal `BackupContentReopenProof` by an **independent fresh reader** that decodes the projection and verifies every role cut/disposition/inventory edge but names no future manifest/receipt/grant. `LocalBackupCopyVerification` + `LocalBackupClosureCertificate` (quorum-signed, contains no retaining source edge) commit their digests. Closure publication is the only Pinned->Certified path; seal cannot skip it.

Sharded reservation: `GlobalBackupIntentSpec` fixes one Meta-issued global prefix `P`, exact Meta closure/topology/configurations, and every required shard; `ShardBackupPinSpec.barrier_state` is `ExactCurrentPrefix{global_applied_prefix=P}|ExactHistoricalCut{...,ExactHistoricalPrefixProof}` — **there is no `LatestAtLeastP` tag**; `latest >= P` is not a legal proof, and an irrelevance proof is accepted only inside a contiguous authenticated Global-command coverage proof that reconstructs exact state at `P`. `GlobalBackupSealSpec` accepts one closure certificate from every and only required shard, all at exact `P`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14 (excerpt): backup pins are independent obligations that remain roots until their exact terminal release. FG-INV-16 (excerpt): no backup pin is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-07: manifest construction is acyclic; no object contains its own digest or a future object. Backup duration/size/RPO are slo class; recoverability decode campaigns feed FG-CFG-01.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-retention-checkpoints` (checkpoints/floors in the pinned closure), `w11-membership-config` (floors retain nonterminal backup states), `w9-key-lifecycle` (recipient/escrow wraps; `BackupKeyReleaseAck` gating key destruction), `w11-fenced-gc` (pins block GC), `w2-transparency` (prior checkpoint field). `w11-backup-publication` continues the lifecycle from Sealed; `w11-restore`/`w11-restore-lease` consume manifests/projections/archive refs; `w10-archive-open` reuses the verifying-reader machinery.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Barrier: any drift between expected and current values rejects apply (one negative per field). Pin coverage: bitmap-vs-mandatory-inventory bijection enforced; deleting any class is a generated negative. Construction-order tests: attempt to embed a rooted ref before inventory finalization, or a publication object in the content inventory — unencodable/rejected. Independent reopen: fresh-process reader with precommitted challenges decodes the projection and recomputes the semantic digest; corrupt one archived entry and assert reopen fails with the exact entry named. Bijection proof negatives: missing source, extra archive, duplicate target. Sharded: `latest>=P` proof shape rejected; historical-cut path proves exact state at `P`; a bare irrelevance proof outside a contiguous authenticated Global-command coverage proof rejected. Clone-projection negatives: a hidden entry with no exclude/transfer/reissue disposition and a clone cut carrying an applied-hidden barrier are both rejected; restored old transport leases/capabilities assert suspended/no-send until fresh target authorization and time evidence. Crash rows at barrier apply, pin, copy, reopen, closure publish, seal. E2e with logs: full Local backup to Sealed under write load; logs record barrier coordinates, pin generation, inventory counts, decode-campaign summary, semantic digest.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: manifest-as-retention (permanently pins the live DB); decode-proof shortcut instead of §16 pins; `LatestAtLeastP` shard barriers (not a proof of state at P); trusting the writing process to verify its own copy (independent fresh reader is mandatory). Risk: pin lifetime under slow archives inflates retention — bounded by abort (pre-publication) and the publication SLOs.

## Provenance
§16.6 (lines 1196-1199), App A lines 2035, 2065-2079, 2105-2115, 2121-2125; App F FG-INV-07/14/16.

### Fidelity addendum — complete backup identity/manifest schema group
The backup content plane and publication-envelope plane are disjoint and generated as such. `BackupSourceIdentity<T>={source_authority_domain,source_cluster_incarnation,object_kind,object_id,canonical_digest}` is nonretaining evidence. Root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>={backup_id,archive_authority_id,inventory_key,subject:SourceObject{expected_source}|RecoveryProjection{backup_id,projection_digest},archived_byte_digest,archived_length,protection_profile,required_recovery_proof_class}` is legal before the final inventory root. Rooted `BackupArchiveRef<T>={entry,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,inventory_leaf_index,inventory_inclusion_proof}` is legal only afterward and must verify under the matching grant. Publication-only `BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T>={backup_id,publication_bundle_id,archive_authority_id,artifact_kind:ManifestBody|ManifestSignatureSet|Manifest,expected_canonical_digest,expected_length,authenticated_locator,publication_receipt_digest,receipt_artifact_index}` is never a content leaf.

`PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Role>` covers every semantic, Protocol, Prepared, Consensus, checkpoint/floor, continuity, bootstrap, and activated `durable_state_slots.toml` row exactly once through `RecoverySlotDisposition=TransformCurrent|CarryPriorEvidence|RecreateCurrentAuthority|ReconcileExternal|SuspendProtocolOwner|DiscardReplicaLocal{registered_law_id}|Reject`. `BackupRecoveryProjection` is exactly Local or Sharded{Meta plus sorted Shard cuts and the global barrier/partition bijection}. `BackupManifestBody` then freezes the complete content inventory, recovery projection, barrier/anti-rollback ranges, role inventories, key escrow/recipient policy, format/trust/transparency policy, and semantic digest. Construction is acyclic: source entries -> projection entry -> final inventory/proofs -> rooted refs -> body -> `BackupManifestSignatureSet` -> `BackupManifest={body_ref,signature_set_ref,body_digest,signature_set_digest,manifest_format_major,manifest_format_minor}`. The manifest contains no self digest, receipt, inclusion, grant, or reopen proof.

Registry/golden tests assert the identity-class split and complete slot bitmap; mutation tests attempt content/publication substitution, final-root use inside the projection, missing/duplicate slot dispositions, self/future edges, and manifest-policy drift. The full E2E uses only an isolated disposable lab fixture and simulated archive/KMS/escrow providers; logs record barrier, source/inventory/projection/body/signature/manifest commitments, slot-disposition counts, proof verdicts, and reader identity, never plaintext, keys, provider credentials, or protected locators.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

### Phase boundary correction — Local implementation versus distributed extension
This bead implements the complete Local quorum-one backup and freezes the reserved Sharded field/tag rows; it does not wait for or claim multi-member barrier/receipt/GC behavior. Its live dependencies are W2 quorum-one ordering, retention, Local typed-root GC, Chronicle publication, key wrapping, and transparency. `fgdb-multi-member-backup-nhpk` consumes this exact format/state machine and adds configuration-fenced member receipts, joint coverage, payload recoverability, leader adoption, consensus GC, and distributed release for G3. W12 adds the separate cross-group Meta/shard barrier and seal. Local tests set `distribution_profile=QuorumOne` and reject evidence from later profiles.

title: Implement backup publication, transparency, archive grants, holds, and release
description:
## What & scope
Implement the external half of the backup lifecycle: the acyclic publication order `BackupManifestBody -> BackupManifestSignatureSet -> BackupManifest -> BackupPublicationReceipt -> BackupTransparencyInclusion? -> ArchiveRetentionGrant -> BackupArtifactReopenProof`, the six external authorize/dispatch/import operations, and grant-authority CAS heads, observations, and use guards. Source-release holds, release finalization, and abort live in `w11-backup-release`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
A backup only counts once it is externally published, transparency-logged (when required), and covered by a durable, externally linearized archive grant. B5: every external effect is rooted before transport (authorize -> Armed -> SentUnknown -> byte-identical send -> status-first recovery -> receipt import), so provider interactions are idempotent and evidence-complete.

## Design — normative detail
Registry lifecycle (Local): `Absent -> Pinned -> ClosureCertified -> Sealed -> PublicationAuthorizedUndispatched -> PublicationReceiptedPendingTransparency|PublicationReceiptedPendingGrant -> (TransparencyAuthorizedUndispatched -> TransparencyIncludedPendingGrant ->)? GrantIssueAuthorizedUndispatched -> Published -> ArtifactVerified -> HoldPrepareAuthorizedUndispatched -> HoldPrepared -> HoldActivateAuthorizedUndispatched -> HoldActivated -> ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion -> Released`. The NotRequired transparency policy skips only the transparency operation, never publication or grant issuance. No intermediate state is reopenable, servable, or pin-releasable except the named Published/ArtifactVerified states, and no pin release begins before HoldActivated.

External operations: `BackupExternalOperationKind` is the closed union `PublishEnvelope|AppendTransparency|IssueArchiveGrant|RenewArchiveGrant|PrepareSourceReleaseHold|ActivateSourceReleaseHold` (hold completion is the separately typed `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionOperationRecord`). Each has an exact authorize spec (binding current manifest/receipt/inclusion/grant/head inputs, expected predecessor CAS/head, immutable action-body recipe, resource reservation, terminal audit gate — never future evidence), producing an immutable Semantic `BackupExternalOperationRecord<Role>` in state `AuthorizedUndispatchedRecipe`. Only the authorizing candidate's role-valid `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Role>` may initialize Protocol dispatch; the full request digest lives in `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<ExactBackupAction>::Armed|SentUnknown`, never in the Semantic record. Universal rules: mark-SentUnknown before transport, fresh authority/time/continuity/registry guard, byte-identical send, authenticated status-first recovery, receipt import, action-typed portable terminal evidence. A timeout, unavailable status, or signed NotRegistered after SentUnknown permits only exact retry — not abort or substitution.

Publication: `BackupPublicationRequestBinding` binds backup/bundle/authority IDs, manifest digests, content-inventory root/count, prebuilt `BackupRecoveryBootstrapDescriptor` digest (bounded public descriptor with deterministic preallocated `PortableRecoveryLocator` bytes — a provider that cannot honor them refuses without effect), durability profile, and service visibility epoch. `BackupPublicationReceipt` must return byte-equal descriptor/locators; exact retry returns the same generation/bytes; a different request under the same idempotency token is a permanent conflict. `BackupTransparencyInclusion` carries log_id/leaf_index/tree_size/root_hash/inclusion_path/checkpoint bytes+signatures and verifies the body-declared policy and prior checkpoint; a NotRequired body makes it illegal, a Required body makes it mandatory before the grant.

`ArchiveRetentionGrant` is the immutable successor record whose subject set fixes content root/count, manifest digests, receipt digest, descriptor digest, and transparency arm — excluding the grant itself; generation one has no predecessor; renewal preserves every subject and increments generation/counter with checked arithmetic; early revoke before `minimum_retain_through` requires the manifest-declared exceptional authority and cannot claim deletion. Freshness is externally linearized via `ArchiveGrantAuthorityHead` (CAS chain with `active_source_release_hold:None|Prepared|Activated|Completed`; no skip/fork; while Activated, revoke/expire/subject-removal are rejected). Reads of the head are challenged `PortableArchiveGrantAuthorityObservation`s (with `intended_action` from the closed action list) imported role-locally via `ArchiveGrantAuthorityObservationImport<Role>`; presentation creates a linear `ArchiveGrantUseGuard<Role>`; every pin-releasing order needs a **new current observation under the Activated hold**. `ArchiveGrantAuthorityProjection<Role>` records the selected head with `continuity_status:DirectSuccessor|PermanentGap` (gap only via separately audited reconciliation).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (excerpt): backup obligations and TerminalPending postconditions are never lost/duplicated/released while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state. FG-INV-08 (excerpt): transparency claim grades remain distinct; non-equivocation requires the declared intersection/durable-witness/rotation/freshness premises. FG-INV-07 (acyclic publication order: no object contains its own digest or a future receipt/signature/inclusion/grant/proof). Archive-authority availability sits on the backup path only (§16.8 footprint table) — slo class.

## Interactions
Continues `w11-backup` (from Sealed); consumes `w2-transparency` (witnessed checkpoints), `w9-audit-release` (`PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate` gating every dispatch initialize), `w9-time-authority` (observation time guards). `w11-backup-release` continues with holds/release/abort and consumes the grant/observation machinery built here. Shares the universal irreversible-dispatch pattern with `w11-gc-physical` and key destruction. `w11-restore-lease` consumes grants, receipts, and bootstrap descriptors.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
State machine: exhaustive transition tests — every skip (seal without closure publication, grant before required inclusion, transparency on a NotRequired body) rejected. Dispatch: lost-response after SentUnknown permits only byte-identical retry; different-request-same-idempotency-token is a permanent-conflict fixture; provider locator substitution rejected by byte-equality with the prebuilt descriptor. Grant head: fork/skip/rollback CAS chains rejected; stale generation fails every consumer closed; renewal preserves the identical subject set (mutation negatives). Observation/use guard: wrong intended_action, wrong subject, non-Active status, and stale head each reject guard creation. Crash rows at every authorize/dispatch/import boundary through Published/ArtifactVerified. E2e with logs: Sealed -> Published -> ArtifactVerified against a simulated archive authority with injected timeouts; logs record operation IDs, attempt states, head CAS versions, and the reopen proof identity.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: provider substitution of locators (byte-equality with the request-bound descriptor is mandatory); inferring transparency policy from absence (policy is signed in the manifest); a single reopen proof serving both content and publication equivalence (the two-stage `BackupContentReopenProof` / `BackupArtifactReopenProof` split is deliberate — only the artifact proof establishes content/publication equivalence). Risk: archive-authority unavailability stalls publication — pins are retained and every step resumes idempotently.

## Provenance
§16.6 (lines 1196-1199), App A lines 2069, 2081-2093, 2103-2109, 2115-2117, 2127; App F FG-INV-07/08/16.

### Fidelity addendum — exact bootstrap descriptor and rooted external-operation family
`BackupRecoveryBootstrapDescriptor` is the bounded portable public object `{backup_id,publication_bundle_id,leakage_class:RestoreBootstrapMetadata,manifest_artifacts[{artifact_kind,canonical_digest,length,ciphertext_id,encoding_id,archive_locator:PortableRecoveryLocator::ArchiveObject,key_opener_locators[KmsWrap|HsmObject|ThresholdEscrow],decoder_profile_oid}],recovery_projection_bootstrap:{content_inventory_entry_identity_and_digest,archived_byte_digest,length,ciphertext_id,encoding_id,archive_locator,key_opener_locators,decoder_profile_oid},content_archive_inventory_root_digest,descriptor_digest}`. Locator bytes are deterministic and preallocated before Armed; provider substitution is a permanent failure. `BackupPublicationRequestBinding` binds external request, backup/bundle/authority, manifest/body/signature/inventory/descriptor digests, durability profile, authority commitment, and service epoch. `BackupPublicationReceipt` returns the exact three artifact rows plus the byte-equal descriptor, inventory durability commitment, generation/counter/time/signer/signature and contains no local ref.

`BackupExternalOperationKind` is exactly `PublishEnvelope|AppendTransparency|IssueArchiveGrant|RenewArchiveGrant|PrepareSourceReleaseHold|ActivateSourceReleaseHold`; hold completion has its distinct record. `BackupExternalOperationRecord<Role>` is immutable Semantic `AuthorizedUndispatchedRecipe` with exact source spec, predecessor/subject commitment, request-body recipe, resource reservation, and terminal audit gate. Only `BackupExternalDispatchInitializeSpec<Role>` after role-valid visibility may create the exact Protocol Armed attempt; universal mark-SentUnknown, status-first recovery, typed receipt import, and portable terminal evidence apply. The six authorize input types are noninterchangeable and each owns only already-built inputs.

Golden/E2E tests cover descriptor bounds and signatures, byte-for-byte provider locator equality, all six action tags, wrong action/spec/receipt substitution, Required versus NotRequired transparency, lost responses, exact retry, and direct CAS successor relations. Logs join backup/bundle IDs, action/contract/operation IDs, Semantic recipe, publication certificate, Protocol attempt generation/state, request/descriptor commitments, provider counter/CAS version, typed receipt/import, and resulting backup state; locators are commitment-only in ordinary logs.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement source-release holds, backup pin release, completion import, and abort
description:
## What & scope
Implement the terminal third of the backup lifecycle: `BackupArtifactReopenProof`-gated verification, `ArchiveSourceReleaseHold` prepare/activate/complete, Local and Sharded source-pin release, `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionImportSpec` to final `Released`, and the exact `BackupNoPublicationProof` abort machinery.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The source pin may drop only when the published artifact is independently proved recoverable AND the archive authority durably holds an **Activated release hold with no time-based escape hatch** — Activated holds complete only against presented release evidence, so crash, timeout, or partial release retains the artifact while recovery completes the same release generation. Abort is symmetric evidence, not a timeout shortcut. This closes the classic backup failure: a "successful" backup whose artifact quietly lapsed before the source discarded history (B5 evidence-first; agent-resumable typed states for B6).

## Design — normative detail
Reopen and release: `BackupArtifactReopenProof<Role>` (a different independent fresh reader) opens the actually published portable artifact via the rooted operation/request/status/receipt lineage, verifies manifest bytes/signatures, projection completeness, transparency, grant/current head, inventory, key material, and all recovery recipes, consuming an action-bound use guard — the artifact proof, not the earlier content proof, establishes content/publication equivalence. `ArchiveSourceReleaseHold`: Prepared may expire only before activation and before any pin release; **Activated completes only after the exact release evidence is presented**. `LocalBackupReleaseSpec` (sole pin-removing transition; requires artifact proof, Activated hold, fresh observation, expected HoldActivated) installs `ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion`; the Semantic release also mints `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionOperationRecord`; after dispatch and the authority's CAS to Completed, `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionImportSpec<Role>` alone installs compact final `Released` (heavy closure retained until then; replaced only by a later activated cut). Sharded: `GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizeSpec` (Meta, ArtifactVerified -> Releasing) -> per-shard `ShardBackupReleaseSpec::Authorize|Finalize` (Certified -> ReleaseAuthorized -> Released with `BackupPinAbsenceProof` and signed `ShardBackupReleaseAck`) -> `GlobalBackupReleaseFinalizeSpec` (every and only shard ack under the still-current Activated hold) -> completion import. Meta participant set is Meta-plus-shards, activated externally durable before any shard sees authorization.

Abort: `BackupNoPublicationProof<Role>` is `PreSeal{...}|SealedPublicationNeverEscaped{...,publication_operation_disposition:NoOperationAuthorized|AuthorizedUndispatched{dispatch_never_initialized_proof}|ArmedAbandonedBeforeSend{DispatchNeverSentProof}|ProviderCancelledBeforePublication{provider_linearizable_cancellation_tombstone},zero_transparency_and_grant_operation_proof,publication_receipt_nonmembership_proof,...}` — bare local absence, timeout, unavailable status, provider Requested, or unresolved SentUnknown cannot inhabit any disposition; any successful receipt or ambiguous external state permanently makes abort illegal and forces roll-forward. `LocalBackupAbortSpec` (plus cleanup plan/completion and `BackupPinAbsenceProof`) installs compact `AbortedBeforePublication`; W12 abort is two-phase (`GlobalBackupAbortBeginSpec` -> shard aborts/acks -> `GlobalBackupAbortFinalizeSpec`). Disconnect, timeout, grant renewal, or a stale Active generation never drops a pin.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (excerpt): no backup pin is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-14 (excerpt): backup pins remain GC roots until their exact terminal release; heavy release closure retires only after visibility and an activated cut. FG-INV-07: the completion receipt/head chain is acyclic (the Completed head contains no future receipt ref).

## Interactions
Blocked by `w11-backup-publication` (grants, heads, observations, use guards, dispatch pattern); consumes `w9-audit-release` (visibility certificates gating release dispatch) and `w9-time-authority`. Releasing unblocks `w11-fenced-gc` reclamation of the pinned closure; `w12-backup-restore` generalizes the sharded authorize/ack/finalize ladder.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Hold laws: Prepared expiry legal only pre-activation and pre-release; Activated hold rejects revoke/expire/subject removal at the simulated authority; time-based completion of an Activated hold is unencodable. Release ordering: pin release before HoldActivated rejected; `LocalBackupReleaseSpec` requires artifact proof + fresh observation under the Activated hold; final `Released` only via completion import after the authority CAS. Sharded: missing/duplicate/wrong-shard `ShardBackupReleaseAck` blocks `GlobalBackupReleaseFinalizeSpec`; Meta activation externally durable before any shard sees authorization. Abort: positive fixture per disposition arm (`NoOperationAuthorized`, `AuthorizedUndispatched`, `ArmedAbandonedBeforeSend`, `ProviderCancelledBeforePublication`); timeout/SentUnknown/provider-Requested cannot inhabit any arm; abort after any publication receipt permanently illegal with forced roll-forward; W12 two-phase abort crash rows (proof, begin, cleanup dispatch/receipt, shard apply/ack, finalize, lost response). E2e with logs: full run ArtifactVerified -> HoldPrepared -> HoldActivated -> ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion -> Released with one crash injected per hold transition; logs record hold state, release generation, completion CAS version.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: time-based release of Activated holds (crash windows would silently drop artifacts); local absence or timeout as abort evidence; dropping pins on disconnect/timeout/grant-renewal/stale-generation (never legal). Risk: a permanently dead archive authority strands `ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion` — the §16.8 threshold-authorized authority-succession transition is the only exit, never local override.

## Provenance
§16.6, App A lines 2095-2101, 2109, 2117-2119, 2129-2139; App F FG-INV-07/14/16.

### Fidelity addendum — exact hold, release, and abort proof group
Source-pin release is guarded by the current direct-successor `ArchiveGrantAuthorityHead` and action-bound `PortableArchiveGrantAuthorityObservation` imported locally as `ArchiveGrantAuthorityObservationImport<Role>`. The head's hold state is exactly `None|Prepared{hold_id,backup_id,release_generation,participant_set_digest,expires_at}|Activated{hold_id,backup_id,release_generation,participant_set_digest,activated_counter}|Completed{hold_id,backup_id,release_generation,participant_set_digest,source_release_evidence_digest,completion_counter}`. Activated prevents revoke/expire/subject removal until exact completion. `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionImportSpec<Role>` is the only transition from `ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion` to compact `Released` and byte-matches operation record, Activated hold, dispatch terminal evidence, completion receipt, Completed head/hold, observation action, and direct predecessor.

Abort evidence is exact and state-shaped: `BackupNoPublicationProof<Role>=PreSeal{...}|SealedPublicationNeverEscaped{...,publication_operation_disposition:NoOperationAuthorized|AuthorizedUndispatched{dispatch_never_initialized_proof}|ArmedAbandonedBeforeSend{attempt_identity,DispatchNeverSentProof}|ProviderCancelledBeforePublication{attempt_identity,canonical_full_request_digest,provider_linearizable_cancellation_tombstone},...}`. A timeout, local absence, provider Requested, unavailable status, signed NotRegistered after SentUnknown, or unresolved external state cannot prove abort. `BackupStagingCleanupPlan<Role>` enumerates every staging object/realization/key opener/upload and pre-mints one idempotent cleanup operation per owner; `BackupStagingCleanupCompletion` proves the exact terminal receipt bijection and post-cleanup inventory. Any successful or ambiguous publication forces roll-forward through verification and hold-backed release.

Crash/model/E2E tests race grant renew/revoke/expiry, hold prepare/activate/complete, every pin release, abort proof construction, cleanup dispatch/receipt, and completion import. All tests use disposable archive fixtures and simulated authorities. Logs emit grant/head/hold generations and commitments, observation intended action, pin set, abort disposition arm, cleanup target/receipt bijection, release acknowledgements, completion CAS/import, and remaining owners; no cleanup target outside the fixture can be configured.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement consensus GC: typed-root collection, safe points, quarantine, retention cuts
description:
## What & scope
Implement the replicated, fenced GC semantic plane of §14.5 + App A: the pipeline `CollectTypedRoots(stable_membership_epoch,config_payload_floor) -> ResolveMarkedPhysicalRealizations -> ProposeSafePoint -> ValidateAllTypedRootsAndCuts(prepared,commands,leases,pins,merge,privacy,replay,keys,backups,audit,transparency) -> CommitGcEpochThroughRaft -> Reclaim`, with `GcProposal`/`GcDecisionRecord`, quarantine installation, the no-new-reference rule, and the provisional/activated retention-cut distinction. Physical execution/dispatch is split into `w11-gc-physical`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
In a replicated system, reclamation is the most dangerous operation: reclaiming bytes another member, an in-flight prepared owner, a backup pin, or a privacy obligation still needs is unrecoverable. The design makes GC a consensus decision over recomputed proofs — every follower re-derives the candidate set — and inserts an audit-visible quarantine between authorization and physical action. B5: reclaim authority is proof-carrying and crash-replayable; B1: one GC epoch history inside the Raft order.

## Design — normative detail
**What stops reclamation** (§14.5): uncertain membership, incomplete new-configuration payload closure, partition, missing root/prepared-owner acknowledgement, external privacy-continuity mismatch, or unavailable key wrap. Backup/restore follows §16, never a decode-proof shortcut.

`GcProposal` is the Local pre-order bounded-set authorization `{gc_id,basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_logical_command_seq,basis_commit_seq,basis_raft_index,configuration_ref,checkpoint_ref,config_payload_floor_ref,activated_retention_cut_ref,retention_map_digest,complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>,candidate_derivation_profile_oid,sorted_reclaim_objects_and_realizations,exact_reclaim_set_digest,required_storage_profile_and_member_set,completed_remote_release_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],excluded_live_prepared_certificate_remote_key_backup_legal_hold_replay_audit_capability_restore_result_workspace_and_delivery_obligation_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}` — weak basis identities, strong current floors/inventories.
