FG-INV-04: restore/role-transition state remains unobservable while reconciliation, activation, pipeline release, service preparation, or independent reopen is pending; every request/cursor/capability matches the current incarnation/service epoch. FG-INV-10: only typed takeover, fresh-creation, or guarded restore publication may precede the ordinary token; irreversible seals recheck both authorities. Invariant-class throughout; conversion downtime is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes root/slot machinery from `w2-root-bootstrap`, format activation from `w11-format-activation`, audit continuity from `w9-audit-continuity`; produces the activated Meta/shard planes for every other w12 bead; legacy artifacts feed `w12-backup-restore` capability migration; the `LocalActivationBridge` origin is validated by `w12-meta-clock`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "fresh Sharded Genesis and audited Local freeze/seal/activation/authority transfer/RetiredLocal finalization/reclamation pass every crash point." Crash/model tests stop at every reservation, staging write, readiness signature, freeze/mirror, seal acknowledgement, Begin commit/apply, signature lock, continuity-reserved CAS, shard hidden root/barrier, Meta hidden root, transfer finalize, service manifest, continuity/catalog split, Meta finalize/reopen, shard open/reopen/ack, completion, legacy transition, and floor release — proving one certificate, E-to-E2 exclusivity, one-way rollback, old-writer/old-credential rejection, exact legacy status/replay/cursor behavior, and no mixed-role visibility. DPOR races on prepare/certificate/receipt/finalize/seal/reopen/ack orderings; hidden-phase traffic negatives. E2E: convert a populated Local database under a scripted drill; assert `Lf+1/Cf` bridge exactness, legacy outcome lookup byte-identity through `CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef`, and RetiredLocal manifest rejects every semantic operation. DETAILED LOGGING (required): every ladder stage (freeze, Begin, shard barrier, ShardingActivationSpec apply, transfer finalize, service prepare, each promotion-catalog stage, finalize, shard open, seal install, independent reopen, reopen confirms, shard operational acks, completion, legacy retirement/floor release) emits a structured record `{migration_nonce, stage, role, shard_id?, applied ref/assigned seq, resulting bootstrap phase/activation phase, service_gate}`; the crash/DPOR harnesses log every injected stop point and the recovery decision (exact roll-forward step taken or refusal), and the drill fails if any stage transition is missing from the log or observed out of order relative to the ladder.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: conversion is a full-stop freeze (accepted; agents drain first; duration benchmarked). Rejected: online trickle migration of live transactions; reusing G4 evidence for the W12 gate; unfreezing a sealed Local after catalog conflict.

## Provenance
App A 1584-1642 (activation contract), 1616-1638; RootManifest RetiredLocal (1538); §19 Gate W12 (1350); §14.6 scope/exit (1097).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement GlobalTxnCommand apply, decision certificates, shard acks, and delta batches
description:
## What & scope
The terminal half of the W12 write path: `GlobalTxnCommand` (Commit / AbortAfterAdmission), Meta apply and the applied-hidden candidate, `GlobalDecisionCertificate` publication, shard decision apply with typed audit-visibility projection, post-visibility `ShardAppliedAck`, `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch` publication, and `GlobalTerminalCompletionSpec`/`TerminalReady`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: the Meta record alone decides outcome; shards install decisions, never make them. B4: Ripple's global frontier advances only through one Meta control over a complete, acyclic delta batch. B6: clients get `TerminalReady` with byte-stable public outcomes or capability-scoped `Unknown` — never partial delta visibility.

## Design — normative detail
**Command.** `GlobalTxnCommand` common fields: header, registration, admission record, `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence` (required Armed), `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` (required Active), admission generation, `MetaPreCommandBaseAvailabilityCertificate` (pre-command availability covers only already-built inputs and excludes itself/the future command; a stable prepared-owner successor adds the completed command), order attempt input + availability certificate, topology/policy/revocation. `Commit` adds routing certificate, one valid `ShardPrepareCertificate` CRSR per admitted participant, the DSC, complete `ConstraintReservationRef` set, authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, terminal audit gate, expected branch heads/key epochs, `global_final_effect_digest` (excludes wrapper/audit objects). Apply assigns exact next `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq` and, commit-only, `GlobalCommitSeq` from the supplement, marks Ordered, consumes the reservation, selects the unique `TerminalOrdered` fence successor, builds marker (commit only), heads, outcome/conflict/constraint state, payload, `GlobalTxnRecord`, and candidate `GlobalStateRoot` — never future shard batches. `AbortAfterAdmission` is constructible even with no prepare (typed `TerminalAbortAuthority<Meta>`, complete no-effect/release proof, known certificates retained only for deterministic release); it adopts no effect, creates no marker/delta, releases exactly the proved holds. Active-but-unadmitted cancellation is exclusively `GlobalAttemptCancelSpec`, so the two abort paths cannot race.

**Visibility & decision.** A required terminal audit gate keeps the candidate root fenced until the external batch CAS and the exact gap-free Protocol visibility advance publish it; only after the releasing slot is durable does the group build `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>`. `GlobalDecisionCertificate` quorum-signs {txn record, resulting root, visibility certificate, admission, exact participants, term/index, assigned sequences/HLC, decision, marker/effect digest, topology epoch, retention floor}; `GlobalDecisionCertificatePublishSpec` installs it in the global registry — only the published certificate is exportable. **Shard side.** `ShardDecisionApplyCommand` (authority projection byte-matched; commit requires `Prepared`; abort accepts Prepared or proven absence, installing `ShardAbortTombstone`) applies decision N strictly `N-1 -> N`, consumes/releases reservations, materializes hidden fragment effects/batch for commit, creates `ShardDecisionInstallRecord`. The shard must next apply the exact audit-visibility `MetaControlProjectionCertificate` at `N+1`; only that projection makes `audit_visible_global_prefix >= N`, and only the post-visibility root can produce `ShardAppliedAck` {decision/publish/visibility identities, prepare_key, terminal_result:Prepared|NoPrepare{abort_tombstone_ref}, post-visibility state root, fragment batch ref?, `audit_visible_prefix>=N`, quorum signatures}. No pre-visibility ack is exportable. Shard acks are post-decision cleanup gates, never command inputs.

**Delta & completion.** After every committed participant's batch + ack, Meta constructs `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch {global_txn_record_ref,marker_identity,global_commit_seq,sorted_fragment_batches[{shard_id,fragment_batch_ref:CRSR<LogicalDeltaBatch>,fragment_digest}],sorted_apply_ack_refs,complete_participant_commitment,resulting_global_frontier,batch_digest}` (the txn record points to no batch — acyclic) and orders `GlobalDeltaPublishSpec` (verifies exact prepare-set equality and contiguous frontier; atomically installs batch/index/frontier). This one Meta control alone advances the global Ripple frontier; delivery/CDC names the Global batch, never a shard fragment. Client acknowledgement waits for delta publication, participant durability/apply, audit visibility, and durable outcome; loss returns scoped `Unknown`. `GlobalTerminalCompletionSpec` CASes the pending outcome, verifies the generated postcondition bitmap (decision publication evidence, exact sorted post-visibility acks, delta completion or `NoDeltaApplicable`, durability evidence, result disposition, `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate`), and selects `TerminalReady` only when required equals satisfied; `PublicTxnStatusProjection` exposes only `FinalizingOpaque` before release.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: W12 transaction records never name future batches; only complete post-visibility shard acknowledgements form one acyclic Global batch and its contiguous Meta publication advances Ripple. FG-INV-04: applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline; visibility never decreases. FG-INV-07 (write order tail): Meta command/applied-hidden candidate -> external audit batch/visibility advance -> decision publication -> shard decision and typed visibility projection -> post-visibility acknowledgements -> Global delta publication -> TerminalReady. FG-INV-01: TerminalReady only after exact postcondition bitmap, audit visibility, independent result detachment; no shard creates or reverses the semantic decision. Commit-visible latency is benchmark-class; freshness of downstream views is FG-EVID-04 slo-class.

## Interactions
Consumes certified terminals from `w12-certification`, audit release from `w9-audit-release`, delta-batch format from `w2-delta-batches`. Produces `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch` for `w6-delta-consumption`/`w10-cdc`; acks/floors for `w12-recovery-gc`; completion state for `w10-capabilities` status.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "decision-certificate publication, shard decision, typed visibility projection, post-visibility acknowledgements, complete GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch publication, and TerminalReady status pass exact DAG/crash proofs." Tests: crash at every arrow of the write-order chain; abort-with-no-prepare; late prepare after abort tombstone; pre-visibility ack export attempt (unrepresentable/rejected); delta publish with missing participant ack blocked; frontier contiguity property tests; `Unknown` on leader loss is capability-scoped. E2E: 3-shard commit storm with induced ack loss and shard restart; log per-shard decision/visibility/ack prefixes; assert Ripple frontier equals published batches exactly and no client observes partial deltas.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ack fan-in adds commit-visible latency (measured; batched acks legal). Rejected: shard-fragment delivery to Ripple/CDC; decision-by-timeout; semantic "mirror" records substituting for ledgered decision bytes.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullets "Global certification and decision"/"Apply, visibility, and Ripple" (1085,1091); App A 1856-1864, 1784; §19:1350/1354.

### Fidelity addendum — exact Shard/Meta delta indexes and cuts
Shard decision apply that materializes `LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>` must atomically update `ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex {format,shard_id,retained_after_global_commit_seq,observed_through_global_prefix,entries[participating committed global_txn_id/global_commit_seq -> StrongRef<LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>>],nonparticipant_or_noncommit_coverage_commitment,retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Shard>>?}` in the same shard transition. The index is a complete participant-decision bijection over its retained interval, not a dense global-commit map. Abort/nonparticipant coverage advances the authenticated coverage commitment and never invents a fragment.

`GlobalDeltaPublishSpec` alone atomically updates `GlobalDeltaBatchIndex {format,retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier,entries[every global_commit_seq in (retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier] -> StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>],retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Meta>>?}` and `global_delta_frontier`; the retained interval is dense and gap-free. `ShardFragmentDeltaRetentionCutSpec` and `GlobalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec` require exact `DeltaRetentionCutEvidence` plus paired checkpoint/floor coverage before removing old strong entries. Crash recovery proves fragment/index atomicity, global batch/index/frontier atomicity, and byte-identical retry. Negatives cover missing/extra participant fragment, invented nonparticipant fragment, missing post-visibility ACK, global frontier gap, stale cut, and a live obligation omitted from cut evidence. Logs emit shard decision/prefix, fragment ID, participant coverage verdict, Global batch/commit/frontier, index roots before/after, cut evidence root, and each retained obligation disposition.

title: Implement W12 distributed-GC cancellation, progress, and aggregate completion
description:
## What & scope
Implement W12 distributed GC coordination over the exact Appendix A formats: bounded preflight, typed-root current-basis inventory, Meta authorization, Shard/member requested operations, the asymmetric CancelAllowed versus CompletionRequired mode, durable progress, exact participant terminal acknowledgements, aggregate completion, quarantine retirement, and successor operation generations.

## Why
Distributed GC cannot use timeout-based best effort. Before any participant starts, Meta may authorize all-member cancellation; after any Started receipt, cancellation is globally impossible and every planned participant must reach Completed. Losing that mode transition can reclaim live data on one member while another believes the operation was cancelled.

## Design — normative detail
- GlobalGcAuthorization selects one immutable current-root basis, complete target/quarantine set, exact topology/configuration and planned Meta/Shard/member participants.
- Preflight proves bounded work, no current-root edge, no prepared/backup/restore/result/replay/grant/key obligation, and installs a nonresurrectable quarantine before physical start.
- Each participant state is Requested, Started(receipt), Completed(receipt), or CancelledBeforeStart(receipt). Meta derives mode CancelAllowed iff every participant is Requested; the first authenticated Started receipt irreversibly selects CompletionRequired.
- GlobalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec names all Requested participants and their zero-start proofs. GlobalGcCompletionRequiredSpec names the first-start evidence and complete remaining plan. GlobalGcProgressSpec monotonically imports signed participant progress without changing semantic authority.
- Aggregate completion requires exact bijection over every planned participant and matching operation generation/configuration. Missing, replaced, or reconfigured participants remain blocking through an explicit transfer protocol.
- Retry is byte-identical; a successor generation is legal only after the predecessor is terminal and its quarantine/floors are transferred or released.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-14 and FG-INV-16 are binding. No resurrection, no cancellation after any start, no aggregate completion from progress alone, and no physical deletion before current-root/quarantine/publication guards.

## Interactions
Depends on W11 fenced/physical GC and membership, W12 recovery/remote trust/core/compaction formats, topology/configuration and exact backup/restore/result/replay/key floors. Topology movement and sharded backup/restore cannot retire/move participants while an untransferred operation is live.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit/golden tests cover all modes/specs/receipts/progress/participant roles and operation-generation transitions.
- Property/model tests enumerate every participant state vector and prove mode selection, cancel/completion exclusivity, complete terminal bijection, no resurrection and current-root safety.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects stale roots/configuration, omitted/duplicate participant, forged zero-start, progress-as-completion, mixed generations, unsigned member receipt and cancel-after-start.
- DPOR/crash E2E races every member start against cancellation across Meta and multiple Shards, partitions/reconfigures/loses leaders, restarts at every publication/import boundary, and converges only to all-cancelled or all-completed.
- Physical E2E uses isolated harness-owned objects, proves bytes remain while blocked, verifies authenticated retirement after aggregate completion, and never deletes user/repository files.
- JSONL emits {event_version,gc_operation_id,generation,root_basis_digest,configuration_digest,mode,participant_id,participant_role,from_state,to_state,start_receipt_digest?,progress_digest?,terminal_receipt_digest?,quarantine_digest,aggregate_state,reconfiguration_transfer?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Tests fail on missing, duplicate, nonmonotone or cross-generation events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: timeout cancellation, majority completion, unsigned worker status, restart-from-scratch generation reuse, and topology retirement that forgets a participant. Conservative blocking is correct when evidence is unavailable.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1812-1816; FG-INV-14; W12 gate.

title: Implement W12 escrow custody, Meta-owned DP execution, and certified shard allocation
description:
## What & scope
The three sharded resource-authority arms: escrow custody (Meta canonical, shard grants), differential-privacy execution (Meta-only seed/noise, clipped shard fragments), and ID allocation (meta-fenced ranges, shard leases, first-escape reservations).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: conserved quantities (escrow rights, privacy budget, ID ranges) have exactly one authority; shards hold only certified, staged-then-activated projections. B5: conservation bijections and permanent spent commitments are provable at every transition. Rejected: shard-minted rights, shard-local noise, allocator reuse after crash/restore.

## Design — normative detail
**Escrow (§4.7 W12 arms).** Canonical custody lives in Meta; shards hold certified projections. `GlobalEscrowTransferPrepareSpec` moves source custody to `InTransit`. `ShardEscrowGrantInstallSpec` installs unusable `Staged` bytes and emits a certified ack. `GlobalEscrowTransferActivateSpec` consumes the complete ack set, moves `InTransit -> Delegated`, and emits an activation certificate; `ShardEscrowGrantActivateSpec` alone makes the matching generation `Active`. Shard prepare reserves only Active rights and returns a certified reservation/contribution. Meta final certification requires a bijection over every participant reservation and holds the canonical bases; global apply consumes/produces rights once and shard decision apply mirrors the exact successor. Reallocation first freezes the grant, obtains certified shard quiescence and complete reservation disposition, then moves `Delegated -> InTransit`; an Active final-certification hold blocks the freeze. Topology movement retains old grants and reservations until every prepared decision terminates. Shards cannot mint, transfer, relabel, or double-project rights. Every quiescence-proof-bearing escrow transition is a batch singleton under the §14.6 certification law.

**DP (§12.7 W12).** In W12 Meta alone owns seed/noise. `GlobalDpExecutionGrant` and `DpShardAggregateFragment` have exact registered certificate schemas binding request/charge/generation/profile/mechanism, clipped shape, shard/configuration, security projection, and idempotency digest — and NO seed/public-output authority. Meta verifies the complete participant set and applies one seed. Shards execute clipped DP fragments only under a Meta-certified `DpExecutionGrant` through the shard prepare/decision protocol; they never own a privacy-ledger or DP-charge control arm. Gate wording: "DP clipped fragments with one Meta charge/noise/result owner."

**Allocation.** `AllocationContinuityProfile::ExternalCas` is mandatory for W12/Meta/Sharded postures (the `DirectoryBound` local-journal arm is Local-only); `IdentityContinuityRecord` external CAS is the anti-rollback authority. Roles hold `IdRangeLease<Role>` (header, lease_id, graph/element_kind/allocation_epoch/partition, half-open range, applied control ref, profiled time window, `permanent_spent_commitment`); shards hold the distinct `ShardIdRangeLease` bound to a `MetaIdRangeGrantCertificate` CRSR — allocation ranges are meta-fenced before use (§14.6 topology bullet). First-escape doctrine: an identity becomes externally stable at its first escape (`EscapingAllocationCause = PublishedStatementResult|LaterStatementWorkspace|ProcedureOrUdfBoundary|DurableProvenanceOrAudit|TerminalResultPreparation`). Sharded flow: the owning shard orders `ShardEscapingAllocationReserveSpec` (marks offsets consumed, installs `ShardEscapingAllocationReservationRecord`), its quorum exports `ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence`, then Meta orders `GlobalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec` (complete tmp-ref-to-permanent-value bijection; rejects missing/duplicate/overlapping/foreign-range/wrong-workspace/nonparticipant bindings) making the global workspace mapping authoritative. Shard holds remain independently rooted until Meta publication and the ordinary two-sided retention release; a Meta failure cannot make a certified slot reusable. `TxnAllocationBindingRoot` maps every escaped slot to exactly one binding; rebase preserves leaves and appends only; disappearance/conflict/abort records `AbandonedAllocationTombstone`; `AllocationBindingCompactionSpec` never returns capacity. Finalization (confined values, App A 1896-1900): confined temporary references also require durable allocation before their permanent values enter a capsule or shard effect basis — each allocation-owner shard orders `ShardFinalizationAllocationReserveSpec` before constructing `ShardEffectBasis`, consumes exact offsets in its authoritative leased-range ledger, and exports certified `ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader, reservation_record_ref:StrongRef<FinalizationAllocationReservationRecord<Shard>>, sorted_mappings, permanent_spent_extension_commitment, topology_and_configuration_basis, one_digest_signer_lock_ref, quorum_signatures}`; the effect basis and routing certificate bind the exact certified evidence; `GlobalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` (`w12-final-reservation`) requires a canonical bijection over all such evidence and every remaining temporary reference, holds those reservations, and cannot remap them; global commit/abort disposition is projected back to every shard, participant loss retains the spent reservation until recovery applies that disposition, and Meta never guesses a shard's next slot while a shard never uses an uncertified Meta mapping.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: escrow custody is a disjoint exhaustive partition, finite-side conservation equations hold at every transition, values stay in bounds, and only registered transitions with exact before/after proof may mint or burn rights. FG-INV-11: allocation epochs/leases/spent commitments are externally monotonic under `ExternalCas` (mandatory for W12/Meta) and prevent alias/overlap/reuse across crash, branch, merge, restore, topology movement, and role activation; any value is durably reserved no later than first escape; rebase appends only. FG-INV-16: DP has one external charge request/tombstone/receipt lineage and noise is generated only by Meta after the charge is mirrored. Escrow conservation has a Lean lane (verification-class); allocator throughput is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes escrow semantics from `w4-escrow`, DP machinery from `w9-dp`, allocator core from `w2-id-allocator`, continuity postures from `w2-continuity-profiles`. Feeds reservations into `w12-prepare`/`w12-certification` (batch singletons); certified `ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence` into `w12-final-reservation`'s reserve-spec bijection; spent commitments consumed by `w12-topology` and `w12-backup-restore`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "certified shard allocation reservations with permanent spent commitments; Meta escrow custody with staged/active shard grants and conservation bijection; ... DP clipped fragments with one Meta charge/noise/result owner." Tests: escrow conservation property across install/activate/freeze/reallocate/topology-move with crash at each stage; Staged rights unusable in prepare (negative); double-project/mint rejection; DP fragment without grant rejected, seed never present in shard state (scan assertion); allocation: crash/lost response before and after every Local/shard/Meta publication, expose-then-rebase, abort-after-exposure, lease expiry, restore-old-backup, partition move — visible value stable, no offset issued twice; finalization rows: a `ShardEffectBasis` naming confined permanent values without a prior `ShardFinalizationAllocationReserveSpec` is unencodable, crash between shard finalization reserve and Meta reserve retains the spent reservation, and a Meta reserve with a missing or duplicated `ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence` member fails the bijection. E2E: 3-shard escrow-bounded counter under contention plus a DP aggregate query; log per-shard reservations and Meta folds; assert conservation equation and single noise application.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: escrow freeze vs. hot final-certification holds can stall reallocation (by design; Active hold blocks freeze). Rejected: shard noise generation; DirectoryBound continuity in sharded posture; capacity reclamation from abandoned bindings.

## Provenance
§4.7 (258); §12.7 (938); §14.6 (1089,1095); App A 1886-1900, 2535/2553; §19:1352.

### Fidelity addendum — DP continuity is a hard W12 authority prerequisite
Meta may execute distributed DP only after the exact current `PrivacyContinuityRecord` has been imported and every relevant `DpRequestRecord<Meta>` state is reconciled by `fgdb-w9-dp-continuity-import-bhtn`. Meta alone owns `PrivacyLedgerState<Meta>`, `DpRequestIndex<Meta>`, seed material, one noise application, result detachment, and external charge lineage. Shards own only certified clipped `GlobalDpExecutionGrant`/`DpShardAggregateFragment` inputs and retention floors; they never own a ledger, seed, noise generator, charge, or public-output authority.

Admission/restore/role-transition tests remove, stale, fork, or permanently gap the continuity head and require fail-closed DP while non-DP work follows its declared profile. Fragment tests prove one complete participant set, no shard noise, no duplicate fragment, and exact charge/request/generation/profile binding. Logs join continuity head/CAS commitment, Meta request state/generation, grant and fragment commitments, participant bitmap, one-noise verdict, and result owner/detachment; privacy principal, query, seed, and raw fragment contents are redacted.

title: Implement the final-certification reservation (single and batch arm) and cancel path
description:
## What & scope
The ordered final-certification reservation for W12 terminals: `GlobalFinalCertificationReserveSpec`, `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` (single-candidate and registered batch arm), `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Meta>`, and the pre-signature cancellation path. Split from `w12-certification` for size; the batching semantics of the batch arm are defined by that bead's law.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: final terminal certification is a distinct ordered reservation AFTER final rebase/authorization/serialization and BEFORE any terminal audit lock or signature, so the terminal command never revalidates mutable heads/key/policy/revocation/conflict/resource bases — it verifies the Active reservation and the exact selected terminal. Rejected: reason-string aborts (aborts are authorized by typed `TerminalAbortAuthority<Meta>` objects only).

## Design — normative detail
`GlobalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` binds header, registration, `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence` (Armed), admission + certification generations, `selection:FinalCertificationSelection::MetaCommit{global_final_effect_directory_ref,global_final_effect_digest,distributed_serialization_certificate_ref,participant_prepare_and_constraint_certificate_commitment,global_authorization_decision_ref,resource_and_constraint_hold_commitment,outcome_preparation_body_digest,terminal_write_result:None|Prepared{preparation_ref,required_posture:Sharded}}|MetaAbort{terminal_abort_authority_ref,stable_public_reason_class,complete_no_effect_and_release_proof_ref,known_prepare_and_reservation_release_basis_commitment}`, expected current branch heads/key epochs/policy epoch/revocation index/conflict basis/topology and Meta configuration, complete participant write-coordinate set, complete resource/constraint/remote-grant/ID hold set, authorization ceiling digest, and expected reservation-index absence or cancelled predecessor. Apply reruns every named validation against current state and atomically installs the Active `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` — validated head/key-epoch, policy/revocation/authority, conflict/serialization, and topology/configuration commitments plus `exclusive_coordinate_head_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<MetaTerminalCoordinateHoldRoot>` and `resource_constraint_id_remote_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<MetaTerminalObligationHoldRoot>`; states `Active|CancelledBeforeSignature{cancel_applied_ref,release_commitment}|Consumed{terminal_input_identity,assigned_global_logical_command_seq}`. The ID-hold half of the spec is App A's finalization-allocation law: the reserve requires a canonical bijection over all certified `ShardFinalizationAllocationEvidence` (exported by allocation-owner shards per `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`) and every remaining temporary reference, holds those allocation reservations, and cannot remap them; global commit/abort disposition is projected back to every shard, and participant loss retains the spent reservation until recovery applies that disposition. The registered **batch arm** binds the shared basis commitments once and carries a canonically sorted member set of per-candidate sub-holds — each with its own registration, selection, held roots, and Consumed state, consumed only by its member's terminal command; the single-candidate schema is exactly the degenerate one-member batch. `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Meta>` maps `(registration,admission_generation,certification_generation)` to the latest reservation with a unique-active selector per registration; reserve CASes absence/cancelled-predecessor to Active; terminal apply or cancel replaces exactly that value. Every state transition that can affect a held predicate is generated with a mandatory reservation-conflict check — a conflicting commit/head change, key retirement, policy/revocation reclamation, topology retirement, resource release, or GC must wait, transfer the reservation exactly, or reject. `GlobalFinalCertificationCancelSpec` names the exact Active reservation, complete hold-release recipe, and `NoTerminalPlanLockShareOrOrderProof` (built from one linearizable barrier; invalid if any terminal semantic plan, signing attempt, terminal command, Ordered supplement, candidate, or external audit CAS exists); apply moves to `CancelledBeforeSignature` and releases exactly its holds; the admission fence remains Armed so recovery can take a higher certification generation or a certified abort. Once a signing plan or any lock exists, cancellation is permanently illegal and the selected terminal must finish.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: the (batch-scoped) reservation is the single legal live owner of the shared final-certification basis; exclusivity is per generation, not per candidate. FG-INV-17: once an Active reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift must use the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path, while any terminal audit plan/lock/share requires completion of that selected basis. Invariant-class; checkpoint/configuration/backup/restore/GC inventories must include the root, every Active record, both hold roots, and all audit/order maintenance evidence.

## Interactions
Consumes admission fences from `w12-prepare` and audit-plan sequencing from `w9-audit-release`; the certifier (`w12-certification`) selects into it; `GlobalTxnCommand` apply (`w12-decision-visibility`) consumes it; hold checks constrain `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`, `w12-topology`, `w12-recovery-gc`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Deleting any generated reservation-conflict check is a G0 negative fixture. Tests: CAS forbids two successors; cancel-after-lock permanently illegal; reservation survives crash/reconfiguration with holds transferred exactly; batch arm: per-candidate sub-hold consumed only by its member's terminal; abort reservation with `MetaAbort` selection byte-matches the admitted abort command. Reserve/sign/cancel ordering model per FG-INV-17. E2E: scripted Meta group under concurrent terminals — reserve -> sign -> consume for both MetaCommit and MetaAbort selections, plus reserve -> cancel-before-signature -> higher-certification-generation re-reserve, while injected conflicting maintenance (branch-head change, key retirement, policy/revocation reclamation, topology retirement, resource release, GC) runs against held predicates and must wait, transfer exactly, or reject; include one batch-arm run proving per-candidate sub-holds are consumed only by their members' terminal commands and the one-member batch byte-matches the single-candidate schema. DETAILED LOGGING (required): every reservation state transition logs `{registration identity, admission_generation, certification_generation, selection kind, state Active|CancelledBeforeSignature|Consumed, coordinate/obligation hold-root ids, conflicting-transition verdict wait|transfer|reject}`; every cancel logs its `NoTerminalPlanLockShareOrOrderProof` quiescence barrier id; tests assert the log stream reconstructs the exact CAS history of `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Meta>`.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: long-held reservations block conflicting maintenance (by design). Rejected: terminal-command revalidation of mutable bases; timeout-released holds.

## Provenance
App A 1736-1750, 1896-1900; §14.6 (1087); App F FG-INV-02/17 (3131/3146).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Prove and torture W12 formal, crash, recovery, and format contracts
description:
## What & scope
Deliver W12's separate bounded formal models, durable-format/protocol fuzzing, and exhaustive fault/recovery torture over Meta, every shard, and Local-to-Sharded activation. This task owns the post-1.0 formal/torture evidence that the 1.0 formal and Local crash beads must not claim.

## Why
Sharding adds new authorities and multi-phase ownership transfers whose safety is not a corollary of Local proofs: pre-response begin reservation, global certification, distributed visibility, remote trust/release, distributed key destruction and GC, Sharded backup/restore, topology transitions, and irreversible Local retirement. The plan names ten separate W12 TLA+/TLC models and requires crash proofs at every phase. They need explicit bounds, refinement bridges, live format readers, real-process campaigns, and negative evidence.

## Formal lanes (scoped and honest)
Create separate TLA+/TLC models for: (a) begin reservation, attempt generation, ticket claim, statement/workspace publication, terminal/autocommit delivery, status, cancellation, read close; (b) admission, shard prepare, signer-locked terminal candidate, external CAS/mirror, decision publication, shard audit projection/post-visibility acknowledgement/global-delta publication; (c) provisional-cut replacement with inherited absent bytes and later activation; (d) closed-attempt build/attest/publish plus detailed/compacted status equivalence; (e) six-stage remote release; (f) staged distributed key activation and physical destruction; (g) GC quarantine/no-resurrection and physical completion; (h) exact backup publication/release; (i) restore reservation, leaves-first transformation, hidden activation/visibility/service preparation, receipt-first finalize/open/reopen/completion; (j) Local-to-W12 activation, authority transfer, RetiredLocal finalization, reclamation. Include partitions, Meta/shard joint reconfiguration, conflict-index lifetime, constraint reservations, topology moves, and declared fairness.

Each proof-lane manifest names exact abstraction, role/posture/feature activation predicate, state/participant bounds, crash/failure assumptions, fairness, checked properties, checker command and digest, implementation trace schema, refinement/conformance status, and everything not proved. Trace export demonstrates captured executions are allowed by the model; it is not called a full implementation-refinement proof. Runtime monitors do not inherit model-check completeness.

## Fault, recovery, and fuzz campaigns
- Crash/partition at every Sharded Genesis and Local freeze/seal/certificate/projection/first-entry/authority-transfer/RetiredLocal/finalize/reclamation point.
- Crash at every begin reservation, ticket/statement/workspace/delivery, prepare/certification/availability, Meta audit candidate/external batch CAS/mirror/visibility, decision, shard projection/ack, global-delta, TerminalPending/compaction, remote-release, key, GC, backup, restore, and topology boundary.
- Per Meta/shard matrices for payload/certificate loss, checkpoint+suffix recovery, donor loss/poisoning, leader loss, current/joint configuration floors, rolling upgrade/downgrade refusal, exact status, backup, restore, service-open, and no-resurrection.
- Fuzz every new W12 durable reader/decoder, role-tagged command/frame, cut/proof, remote-ref trust envelope, manifest, certificate, and transition registry row. Cross-role substitution, mixed encoding, truncated/duplicate/reordered arrays, stale epochs, invalid sorted bijections, and strong-reference cycles fail closed.
- LDFI uses the full dependency lineage; residual random chaos guards blind spots. Every scenario declares filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests for model translators, invariant predicates, trace exporters/importers, durable reader validation, fault-hook placement, campaign generation, and manifest/schema lint; mutation tests prove each property/checker catches a seeded violation.
- Property/metamorphic tests verify encode/decode stability, cross-role rejection, batch/order invariance only where registered, idempotent retry, no premature release/reclaim, no timeout fracture, and recovery convergence to a global-oracle-legal state.
- Model checks complete at every registered bound with counterexample replay tests; at least one intentionally weakened model per lane produces the expected counterexample, preventing vacuous properties.
- Simulation torture executes every generated active crash row with the W12 global/protocol oracles attached; matrix completeness fails for any activated transition with no row.
- Real-process E2E boots Meta and at least three shards, then performs Local conversion, multi-statement cross-shard commit, membership and topology transition, remote release, key rotation/destruction, GC, exact backup, and receipt-first restore while killing/partitioning processes at selected phases; it independently reopens the archive/target and proves no stale endpoint/capability/role or old ObjectId is accepted.
- A final evidence audit proves every live W12 invariant clause maps to a unit/property/model/simulation/E2E result and structured diagnostic ancestry. Otherwise `sharding=true` remains absent.

## Detailed structured diagnostics
Every model run and campaign row emits JSONL `{run_id,phase:"W12",lane_id,model_digest,bounds,fairness_profile,scenario_id,seed,role,group_id,configuration_topology_service_epochs,command_transition,crash_point_id,fault_hypothesis_id,logical_txn_meta_shard_positions,attempt_statement_workspace_decision_remote_key_gc_backup_restore_ids,expected_property,actual,oracle_verdicts,recovery_verdict,verdict}`. Model counterexamples include complete state traces and the exact checker command. Runtime failures include the complete secret-redacted §15.1 artifact, minimized workload/schedule/input, first divergence, all evidence identities, and executable replay command; sampled commands run in CI. Passing rows use the same schema, and the W12 gate report is rebuilt from logs alone.

## Dependencies and phase boundary
Consumes the completed W12 implementation, the W12 simulation/global-oracle task, and the reusable 1.0 formal/torture engines. Feeds only the W12 verification epic and W12 gate. It must never become a dependency of G4 or retroactively expand a G1-G4 claim.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one monolithic unbounded model; calling trace conformance refinement proof; sampling durability boundaries; clean-shutdown-only distributed tests; reusing Local model results; weakening semantics to avoid Meta sequencing. State explosion is managed with separate bounded models and refinement manifests, never hidden scope.

## Provenance
Plan §15.3, §15.5 and §19 Gate W12; Appendix F W12 clauses; Appendix A W12 role/public formats.

title: Implement the one scalar semantic clock: Meta sequences, HLC, and the record chain
description:
## What & scope
Build the Meta consensus group's semantic clock and command-record chain: Meta-issued `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq`, transaction-only `GlobalCommitSeq`, global logical HLC, the `GlobalTxnRecord`/`GlobalControlRecord`/`GlobalStateRoot`/`GlobalStatePayload` chain, the order-attempt supplement machinery, and the W12 history-reference wrappers. Shard Raft order is deliberately nonsemantic.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: in sharded posture the three counters are Meta-issued global *aliases*, not vector clocks; Chronicle, branches, Ripple, and replay keep one scalar time. B5: order/HLC freshness is deliberately outside stable semantic prepared ownership and signed audit bytes, so evidence never has to be re-signed when an order race is lost. Rejected at §3.4/§14.6: vector time, federated shard histories, shard-local semantic bypass.

## Design — normative detail
**Clock rules.** Every canonical mutation passes through Meta; shard Raft indices order durability/apply only and never move time or heads. Meta computes HLC from the previous persisted value and normalized proposal observations. I/O batching of already-certified entries is allowed; same-basis certification only under the virtual-serial law (`w12-certification`).

**Order supplements.** `MetaOrderSubject = Terminal{final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_state:Active,selected_terminal_digest} | Control{typed_payload_ref:StrongRef<GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec>,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_audit_freeze_commitment}`. The proposer builds `MetaOrderAttemptInput {order_attempt_id,subject,semantic_prepared_ownership_id,hlc_proposal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<MetaHlcProposalEvidence>,expected_next_global_logical_command_seq,expected_next_global_commit_seq:NotApplicable|Commit{value},configuration_ref,body_digest}` plus a `MetaOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate`. Commit applicability derives from the immutable selected terminal/control kind — abort/read/control cannot smuggle a commit-sequence assignment. Voters derive next sequence/HLC only from that input and current persisted HLC; if the observation ages out or the expected sequence loses a race, the supplement is retired with a linearizable nonorder proof (`OrderAttemptRetirementEvidence`) and a fresh attempt is certified without changing semantic ownership, reservations, or audit bytes. `PreparedOrderAttemptRoot<Meta>` entries are `Available{input_ref,availability_certificate_ref,maintenance_install_index}|Ordered{role_order,commit_order:None|Some,semantic_command_identity,semantic_raft_index}|RetiredStale{retirement_evidence_ref,successor_attempt_id}`. A terminal reservation CAS, or a control spec's exact idempotency/expected-state CAS, admits at most one ordered semantic command across all supplements.

**Record chain.** `GlobalTxnRecord {predecessor:ConditionalGlobalCommandRef,command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>,decision:Committed|Aborted,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,assigned_global_commit_seq?,global_logical_hlc,marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef?,final_effect_digest,resulting_global_state_payload_digest:WeakDigest}`. `GlobalControlOrigin = Prior{predecessor}|LocalActivationBridge{transition_ref,frozen_local_head,Lf,Cf,Hf,local_chain_mmr_checkpoint_projection_digests}|RecoveryBridge{bridge_spec_ref,source_manifest_identity,transform_and_projection_digest}` — only the first activation record may use `LocalActivationBridge`, only the first guarded restore record `RecoveryBridge`. `GlobalStateRoot {payload_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStatePayload>,global_command_head:StrongGlobalCommandRef?}`. Every registration, statement publication, admission/cancel/read-close, policy/key/topology/GC/remote-retention transition, directory publication, decision/delta publication, activation, and restore bridge enters this one contiguous Meta chain. `GlobalStatePayload` is the generated Meta Semantic-plane schema (branch head/manifest/key-epoch roots, topology, conflict index, begin/attempt/statement/outcome indexes, constraint/reservation roots, resource/privacy/DP, policy/revocation, audit/transparency, retention/derived/replay/backup/restore, decision-certificate and delta-batch registries, compaction floors); audit continuity and delivery owners live only in `AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Meta>` under the RootManifest Protocol slot — a payload alias field is illegal.

**History wrappers (within-group only):** `StrongGlobalCommandRef/ConditionalGlobalCommandRef(axis=GlobalLogical)/WeakGlobalCommandIdentity` target `GlobalTxnRecord|GlobalControlRecord`; `ConditionalGlobalTxnInputRef` targets an already-built `GlobalTxnCommand`, valid only when the record at that sequence names the same input; `StrongShardCommandRef/ConditionalShardCommandRef(axis=ShardRaft)/WeakShardCommandIdentity` target `ShardCommandRecord`. Cross-group carriage always requires `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`. Shard state: `ShardCommandRecord {origin:Prior|RecoveryBridge,shard_raft_index,command,result_refs,resulting_shard_payload_digest}`; shard order cannot move branch heads or semantic time.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08: logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their sequences; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise visible cut/root/configuration/positions; fresh Sharded Genesis/Local activation never mix role histories. FG-INV-07: the durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm. FG-INV-01: matching retries return the recorded lineage. Sequencer throughput/latency numbers are benchmark-class (Appendix G/§17), disclosed as serial + batched ceilings.

## Interactions
Consumes quorum machinery from `w2-order-raft`/`w11-raft-multi` and the D1/D2 commit discipline from `w2-commit-protocol`. Produces the ordering substrate for `w12-registration-snapshot`, `w12-certification`, `w12-decision-visibility`; `GlobalStatePayload` roots consumed by `w12-constraints-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: checked counter mismatch, duplicate subject, self-staleness, retirement-after-order, command/supplement substitution all fail closed. Crash tests: stale HLC evidence before/during signing, intervening commands, leader/configuration change, multiple fresh supplements — exactly one semantic application ever. Generated log-to-state verifier proves exact role-specific root/config/prefix at every cut; cross-role command injection rejected (gate requirement). E2E script: 10k mixed txn/control commands across leader failovers; assert contiguous `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq`, commit-seq increments only on committed transactions, HLC monotone; log every retired supplement with its nonorder proof id.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: per-command Meta apply chain is the residual ceiling (stated honestly at the gate). Rejected: vector clocks; shard-local sequence assignment; signing order/HLC into audit bodies (would force re-signing on order races).

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 1 (1081); App A 1402-1404, 1644-1656, 1752-1754; §19:1350.

title: Implement exact Meta/Shard roots, keys, checkpoints, prepared, and certificate formats
description:
## What & scope
Implement exact Meta/Shard canonical payload, root, command, key-distribution/destruction, checkpoint/floor, prepared-root, certificate-ledger, and projection formats. This task is the durable schema prerequisite for W12 meta clock, preparation, certification, constraints, decision, recovery and key lifecycle.

## Why
W12 cannot be a role-erased extension of Local Chronicle. Meta owns global semantic order; Shards own nonsemantic partition state. Their roots, logs, checkpoints, prepared ownership, keys and certificates require disjoint tags and complete generated inventories so cross-role bytes and omitted state are rejected.

## Design — exact normative contract
Shard canonical state is parallel but deliberately nonsemantic. The following brace list is a compact navigation projection of generated `ShardLogicalStatePayload`, not its field registry: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,bootstrap_phase:Genesis|CheckpointInstalled|Operational|OperationalPendingIndependentReopen|RecoveryReconciling|RecoveryAbandoned|RoleTransitionPreparedHidden,role_transition_activation_state_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionActivationState>?,shard_id,topology_epoch,partition_state_roots,shard_constraint_state_root,constraint_reservation_index_root,prepared_attempt_root,applied_decision_index_root,terminal_abort_tombstone_root,fragment_delta_batch_index_root:StrongRef<ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex>,shard_derived_component_registry_root,shard_key_material_registry_root,active_meta_projection_root:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,global_applied_logical_command_seq,global_applied_commit_seq,meta_policy_epoch,meta_revocation_index,meta_key_epoch_commitment,audit_visible_global_prefix,retention_map_root:StrongRef<RetentionMap>,backup_registry_root,restore_state_ref:StrongRef<RestoreState>?,restore_retention_anchor:RestoreRetentionAnchor<Shard>,remote_retention_authority_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionObligationRoot>,remote_retention_consumer_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot>,remote_configuration_trust_root:StrongRef<RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot>,shard_recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<ShardRecoveryCheckpoint>?,shard_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardConfigPayloadFloor>?}`; it has fresh three-state bootstrap, hidden role-transition preparation, and restore reconciliation/abandonment. During restore it remains `RecoveryReconciling` through activation, visibility apply, and `ShardRestoreServicePrepareSpec`; those produce hidden `ActivationAppliedHidden`, `VisibilityApplied`, and `ServicePreparedHidden`. `ShardRestoreAbandonApplySpec` alone selects RecoveryAbandoned with no restore-state ref, payload `RestoreRetentionAnchor::AbandonmentPinPending`, and registry `AbandonedAwaitingTerminalPin`; that phase admits only certified Meta abandonment recovery, exact abandonment-pin installation, source-lease projection refresh, and terminal controls and can never serve. After that root is durable, `ShardRestoreAbandonmentPinInstallSpec` alone replaces the pending anchor with `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` and enters `AbandonedParticipantComplete`; only then may the Shard issue its abandon acknowledgement. The exact `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec` for the same restore, final Meta certificate, and already-issued promotion receipt clears restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`; seal installation and `ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec` with a fresh independent proof alone reach Operational, and request admission rejects every pending phase. `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot` is keyed by the generated exhaustive `MetaProjectionSlot` registry, not a five-slot hand list. Every slot value has exactly one source: `Genesis{certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardedGenesisCertificate>,payload_ref:StrongRef<GenesisMetaProjectionPayload>,projection_digest}|Activation{transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,projection_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedTransitionArtifactRef<LocalToShardProjection>>,payload_ref:StrongRef<ActivationMetaProjectionPayload>,projection_digest}|Control{source_global_control_identity,source_global_prefix,payload:TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload,projection_digest}`. The registry includes every shard-relevant topology, catalog/schema, constraint/owner, branch/head/key/grant, ID-allocation, policy/revocation/audit, retention/trust, derived-generation, backup/restore, GC/reconfiguration, and delivery/frontier effect; each Global control kind has exactly one generated `NoShardEffect{proof rule}` or typed targeted slot-update row. Genesis/activation payloads are typed consumer-local closures constructed after their certificate and contain no raw remote edge. Aggregate scalars byte-match rooted values and are cross-checks only. `ShardConstraintStateRoot` contains aggregate contributions and prepare-keyed reservation refs; prepare installs and decision consumes/releases them. `ShardCommandOrigin` is the closed union `Prior{predecessor:ConditionalShardCommandRef}|RecoveryBridge{bridge_spec_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryBridgeSpec<Shard>>,source_manifest_identity:WeakDigest,transform_and_projection_digest}`. `ShardCommandRecord` is `{origin:ShardCommandOrigin,shard_raft_index,command:StrongRef<ShardPrepareCommand|ShardDecisionApplyCommand|ShardControlCommand>,result_refs[StrongRef],resulting_shard_payload_digest:WeakDigest}`; only the first guarded restore record uses `RecoveryBridge`, while fresh Genesis has no head and all later records use `Prior`. `ShardLogicalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStatePayload>,shard_command_head:StrongShardCommandRef?}`. Shard order cannot move branch heads or semantic time. Generated checkpoint/floor/backup/GC coverage includes every root above.

For Shard, generated activated slots additionally include `shard_security_state_projection_ref`, `shard_allocation_lease_and_reservation_root`, `shard_escrow_grant_and_reservation_root`, `shard_valid_time_projection_ref`, `shard_result_transport_projection_root`, `shard_format_compatibility_projection_ref`, `shard_bulk_staging_root`, `shard_derived_build_registry_root`, `shard_gc_operation_root`, `shard_backup_protocol_root`, `shard_restore_registry_root`, and `shard_capability_migration_root`. Each is either shard-owned protocol state or a certified Meta projection selected through `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot`; none is a second semantic authority. The scalar `meta_policy_epoch` and `meta_revocation_index` are cross-checks of `shard_security_state_projection_ref`, not authorization inputs by themselves.

Key authority is Meta-owned but ciphertext/envelope material follows its data shard, using an acyclic four-phase protocol. First, `GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan {plan_id,operation:Fork|Grant|Rotate,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_prior_branch_head_and_key_registry_digests,new_branch_and_epoch_record_refs[StrongRef],sorted_per_shard_recipes[{shard_domain:ConsensusDomain,assigned_partition_ranges,expected_envelope_write_key_epochs,material_commitment,recipient_and_wrap_policy,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}],complete_shard_range_and_material_commitment,activation_cas,policy_epoch}` is prebuilt without any shard certificate. `GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlanSpec` orders it and changes only the plan registry to `Distributing`; the new epoch is nonqueryable.

Second, each shard imports a certified-remote plan/typed recipe and orders `ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec {plan_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan>,own_recipe_index,expected_topology_epoch,expected_shard_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_prior_key_registry_entry,local_envelope_wrap_opener_root_refs[StrongRef],complete_local_material_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyMaterialInventory>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>}`. Apply installs `ShardKeyMaterialProjection {plan_identity,graph,branch,envelope_epoch,write_key_epoch,assigned_partition_ranges,local_envelope_wrap_opener_root_refs,availability_floor,status:Staged}`. Staged material cannot satisfy a read, effect basis, prepare, backup-as-active, or current key lookup. The shard then creates purpose-specific `ShardKeyMaterialAvailabilityCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,purpose:StagedAvailability,plan_identity,shard_id,topology_epoch,configuration_identity,staged_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardKeyMaterialProjection>,exact_partition_and_material_commitment,inventory_root_ref:StrongRef<KeyMaterialInventory>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`.

Third, Meta builds `GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest {plan_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,branch_epoch_registry_candidate_ref:StrongRef,sorted_shard_availability_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardKeyMaterialAvailabilityCertificate>],complete_shard_range_and_material_commitment,meta_grant_root_ref:StrongRef,body_digest:BodyDigest<GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest>}` and orders `GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec {plan_ref,manifest_ref:StrongRef<GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest>,expected_plan_state:Distributing,expected_prior_branch_head_and_key_registry_digests,activation_cas,terminal_audit_gate}`. The registered body transcript excludes only `body_digest`. Apply verifies one matching certificate for every and only planned shard/range, atomically activates the branch/key epoch, and moves the replaced epoch to `Retiring`; it never creates material. Fourth, each shard consumes the generated typed Meta projection through `ShardKeyMaterialActivateSpec`, byte-matches plan/manifest/material commitment, and changes only its matching `Staged -> Active` entry. Reads/effects/prepares require both the Active local entry and an active-Meta-projection prefix at or beyond activation. Old material remains Active/Retiring and retained until every dependent operation and replacement acknowledgement closes.

Zero-reference is a different certificate kind, never an availability flag. `GlobalKeyDestroyAckRef` is the closed union `Backup{ack_ref:StrongRef<BackupKeyReleaseAck>}|LegalHold{ack_ref:StrongRef<LegalHoldReleaseAck>}|RemoteConsumer{ack_ref:StrongRef<RemoteKeyConsumerReleaseAck>}`. `GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec` is `{destruction_id,key_epoch_and_material_set,expected_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_branch_key_envelope_and_grant_registry_digests,exact_target_plan:{meta_local:None|Some{material_set,generated_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,zero_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,external_operation_plan},sorted_shards[{shard_id,authority_domain,assigned_ranges,material_set,expected_active_or_retiring_projection_digest,external_operation_plan}],complete_meta_shard_range_and_material_coverage_digest},backup_legal_hold_remote_consumer_ack_refs[GlobalKeyDestroyAckRef],expected_state_conditions,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply atomically changes the global lifecycle `Retiring -> DestroyAuthorized`, installs a global no-new-reference quarantine, and, for Meta-local material, durably creates one immutable `MetaExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord::AuthorizedUndispatchedRecipe` per target. Those Semantic records authorize no call. After the authorization's audit visibility advance, `MetaKeyDestructionDispatchInitializeSpec` creates the matching Protocol Armed attempts; the universal mark-SentUnknown/guard/status/receipt-import protocol is the only Meta-local physical path. Meta then creates `GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,destruction_id,authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,key_epoch_and_material_set,topology_and_configuration_identity,exact_target_commitment,global_quarantine_generation,meta_zero_reference_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`.

Each planned shard orders `ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec {authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationCertificate>,expected_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_epoch,expected_local_key_registry_state:Active|Retiring,exact_material_and_range_set,current_complete_generated_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,current_zero_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,quarantine_body_recipe}`. Apply byte-matches the plan, atomically installs the local no-new-reference quarantine and `DestroyAuthorized`, and creates a local record. Only afterward may its quorum create `ShardKeyZeroReferenceCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,purpose:ZeroReference,destruction_authorization_identity,key_epoch_and_material_set,not_before_global_prefix,basis_shard_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,basis_checkpoint_floor_and_history_digests,basis_prepared_certificate_backup_replay_cursor_grant_topology_gc_root_digests,complete_scanned_root_set_commitment,zero_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,quarantine_generation,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. The certificate is valid only while every named current root, configuration, prefix, and quarantine generation remains byte-identical.

`ShardKeyDestroyApplySpec` is `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationCertificate>,zero_reference_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardKeyZeroReferenceCertificate>,expected_current_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_epoch,expected_quarantine_generation,current_inventory_equality_and_no_new_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoNewKeyReferenceProof>,sorted_external_operation_plans[{operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target:KeyDestructionTarget,canonical_request_transcript_digest}],post_apply_registry_body_recipe}`. Only after this candidate is audit-visible does `ShardKeyDestructionDispatchInitializeSpec` create matching Protocol Armed attempts; every target call then uses the registered mark-SentUnknown, fresh `KeyDestructionDispatchGuard`, status-first recovery, and target-typed receipt-import transitions. `ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionSpec` is `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationCertificate>,destroy_apply_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardCommandRecord>,expected_destroying_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_quarantine_generation,operation_record_refs[StrongRef<ShardExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord>],dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence>,typed_terminal_receipt_refs[KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef],target_completion_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TargetCompletionBijectionProof>,current_inventory_equality_and_no_new_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoNewKeyReferenceProof>,replicated_wrap_key_inventory_erasure_verification_ref:StrongRef<KeyErasureVerification>,storage_member_completion_quorum_ref:StrongRef<StorageMemberPhysicalCompletionQuorum>,post_destroy_registry_body_recipe}`. `GlobalKeyDestructionCompletionSpec` is `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,authorization_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationCertificate>,expected_global_destroy_authorized_state:WeakStateIdentity,current_meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,current_topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,current_global_inventory_and_no_new_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoNewKeyReferenceProof>,meta_operation_record_and_receipt_refs[MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence],exact_sorted_shard_completion_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionCertificate>],complete_planned_target_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TargetCompletionBijectionProof>,terminal_audit_gate}`. `MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence` is the closed `{operation_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord>,dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence>,terminal_receipt:KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef,erasure_verification_ref:StrongRef<KeyErasureVerification>}`. Apply reaches global Destroyed only when every and only planned Meta target and shard/range has physical completion evidence under the current topology/configuration and the global quarantine still forbids references. A new retaining edge or owner, a changed target/material/topology/current-or-prospective configuration set, or a failed current-root zero-reference proof invalidates the authorization and forces a new generation. Ordinary checkpoint, RootManifest/RootSlot, protocol, compaction, or configuration-progress publication that preserves the exact quarantine, target set, material set, no-new-reference rule, and zero-reference truth does not invalidate merely because its scalar position advanced; the completion proof authenticates the allowed successor chain. Floors retain every Staged, Active, Retiring, DestroyAuthorized, Destroying, Semantic authorization recipe, Protocol dispatch attempt, receipt, and certificate state. Crash tests stop at every quarantine visibility, dispatch arm, SentUnknown publication, guard recheck, pre-send crash, call, authenticated status result, target Started fence, receipt import, semantic completion apply, signature, and global completion boundary, including partial KMS/member failure and ambiguous replies.

`CheckpointStateVector` is one top-level content-addressed role-tagged object `{schema_version,payload_schema_oid,role:Local{entries[LocalPayloadFieldTag->CheckpointFieldRecipe]}|Meta{entries[GlobalPayloadFieldTag->CheckpointFieldRecipe]}|Shard{shard_id,entries[ShardPayloadFieldTag->CheckpointFieldRecipe]},coverage_bitmap,projection_digest}`; field tags come from the generated payload schema and cannot cross roles. `CheckpointFieldRecipe` is the closed union `CopiedStrong|ProjectedSnapshot|ResetByCheckpointInstall|SelfExcluded|InstallProvisionalCut|ApplyActivationProjection` with the exact per-tag literals defined below. `GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint` is `{basis:Genesis|Global{basis_global_logical_command_seq,basis_global_commit_seq,covered_global_command:WeakGlobalCommandIdentity?,covered_global_marker:StrongMarkerRef?}|LocalActivation{transition_commitment,frozen_local_head:WeakCommandIdentity,Lf,Cf,Hf,local_projection_digest},basis_payload_digest:WeakDigest,basis_projection_digest,global_logical_hlc_state,topology_epoch,global_checkpoint_state_vector_ref:StrongRef<CheckpointStateVector>,nonretaining_predecessor_checkpoint_digest}`. `ShardRecoveryCheckpoint` is `{shard_id,basis:Genesis|Shard{basis_shard_raft_index,basis_global_logical_command_seq,basis_global_commit_seq,covered_shard_command:WeakShardCommandIdentity?}|LocalActivationProjection{transition_commitment,local_to_shard_projection_digest,Lf,Cf,Hf},topology_epoch,basis_shard_payload_digest,basis_projection_digest,shard_checkpoint_state_vector_ref:StrongRef<CheckpointStateVector>,nonretaining_predecessor_checkpoint_digest}`. Each vector has exactly one entry per field of its matching payload schema. The provisional tag is required exactly for operational replacement retention maps; `ApplyActivationProjection` is legal only under the matching activation basis and classifies every destination field from the pre-certified body recipe without a future result OID. Fresh Genesis forbids both. Checkpoint/floor fields use exact literals. Generated coverage and DAG checkers reject any role mismatch, mixed basis, omitted field, future ref, or result recipe mismatch.

Recovery treats every checkpoint as the **post-install** payload. Ordinary Local/Meta basis `(L0,C0)` reconstructs sequence `L0+1`, commit `C0`, deterministic install HLC, literals/resets/provisional cut, verifies the unique retained install input/record, then replays `L0+2..head`; ordinary Shard basis `R0` analogously reconstructs `R0+1`. LocalActivation reconstructs the first Meta activation at `Lf+1/Cf`; LocalActivationProjection reconstructs the first shard projection-install result at its declared shard index and `Lf/Cf`. In each case the transition certificate/projection recipe and retained input/record are the unique witness; recovery never reapplies it. Double apply, missing/duplicate install, mixed basis, scalar/reset/projection mismatch, or pairing with another root fails closed.

The Meta protocol floors are closed projections, not category bags. `MetaBeginStatusFloor` covers every Reserved/Bound/Detailed/Compacted begin-key entry, outcome-capability directory value, staging resource, terminal-pending postcondition set, and public-status proof through its advertised lookup floor. `MetaAttemptFamilyFloor` covers the family/generation/token/attempt/outcome directory and every Active or PrepareAdmitted attempt. `MetaStatementResultFloor` covers the statement index, cumulative witness roots, buffered spill manifests, delivery leases, publication chain, and statement summaries. `MetaConflictOverlapFloor` covers every live dependency edge and overlap-close proof. `MetaAttemptCompactionProtocolFloor` covers the terminal summary, `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot`, authoritative floor, build closure, signer lock, attestation, publication, audit visibility advance, and independent obligations. `MetaAuditClaimSignerFloor` covers pending/claimed tickets, owners, terminal-attempt records, signer locks, candidate fences, external-CAS receipts, and mirrors. `MetaDecisionPublicationFloor` covers decision construction, signer lock, certificate, publication, shard audit projection, and post-visibility ack directory; `MetaDeltaPublicationFloor` covers each committed `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch`, its index, publication record, and contiguous frontier. The remaining exact floors respectively cover provisional plus activated cuts; remote trust/grants/all six release stages; key plan/staged-certificate imports/active manifest/zero-reference/durable destruction/physical completion; distributed derived generations; GC preflights/authorization/quarantine/member receipts/Meta and shard physical completion/`PartialBlocking`; backup intent/pins/shard closures/manifest publication/release authorization/acks/finalize; `RestoreSourceLease`, reconciliation, activation/visibility acks, service promotion and catalog receipt; fresh-sharded Genesis or LocalActivation, migration authority transfer, retirement authorization/certificate/acks/finalize; incarnation continuity and service-visibility state; and configuration/prepared transfer/topology movement. Imported entries are consumer-local CRSR/evidence only.

Those floors respectively retain prepared attempts/reservations/ownership transfers; imported registration/statement/read bases and cumulative-witness obligations through publication/close; fragment batches, decision-publication input, audit projection and post-visibility ack; the exhaustive active Meta projection; provisional/activated cuts; every `Staged|Active|Retiring|DestroyAuthorized|Destroying` key object plus zero/physical receipts; derived components; GC preflight/quarantine/member physical receipts/completion; backup pin/closure/release; restore hidden activation/visibility/service promotion/operational ack; remote trust/grants/release; topology copy/configuration/prepared transfer; complete history needed by the advertised interval; and incarnation/service epoch.
