`MetaCheckpointCertificate` is a meta-group object `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,global_recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,basis_global_prefix:{logical,commit},install_global_prefix:{logical=basis.logical+1,commit=basis.commit},install_meta_raft_index,checkpoint_install_record_ref:StrongGlobalCommandRef,installed_global_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>?,log_to_state_proof_digest,certificate_ledger_floor,quorum_signatures}`. Header configuration/predicate are the sole configuration fields. `ShardHistoryInventory` is `{shard_id,topology_epoch,queryable_global_prefix_interval,partition_version_roots[StrongRef],key_epoch_roots[StrongRef],tombstone_and_hole_roots[StrongRef],retention_lease_roots[StrongRef],body_digest:BodyDigest<ShardHistoryInventory>}`; its registered transcript excludes only `body_digest`. `ShardCheckpointCertificate` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,shard_id,topology_epoch,basis_shard_raft_index,install_shard_raft_index=basis+1,basis_global_prefix,install_global_prefix,checkpoint_install_record_ref:StrongShardCommandRef,queryable_global_prefix_interval,installed_shard_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,shard_recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<ShardRecoveryCheckpoint>,shard_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardConfigPayloadFloor>?,retained_history_inventory_ref:StrongRef<ShardHistoryInventory>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,log_to_state_proof_digest,certificate_ledger_floor,quorum_signatures}`. Genesis certificates require the optional floor `None`; Operational certificates require `Some`. The interval is valid only when the inventory proves every MVCC version/key needed for each included prefix. A database snapshot at `P` requires the meta root at `P` and, for every routed shard, a certified checkpoint whose queryable interval contains `P`; “checkpoint at or beyond P” alone is insufficient.

`MetaRelevanceRangeProof` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,target_shard_id,prior_global_prefix:{logical,commit},resulting_global_prefix:{logical,commit},sorted_command_entries[{global_logical_seq,command_kind,terminal_kind:Control|CommittedTxn|AbortedTxn,assigned_global_commit_seq?,routing_or_scope_commitment,generated_meta_effect_class,affected_projection_slots,topology_epoch,policy_epoch,revocation_index,key_epoch_commitment,audit_fence_effect}],irrelevance_checker_version,result:Irrelevant,quorum_signatures}`. Entries are contiguous and exhaustive from `prior.logical+1` through `resulting.logical`; commit sequence increments exactly on `CommittedTxn` and is unchanged on controls/aborts. The generated `MetaControlEffect` registry must classify every entry, and Irrelevant is legal only when every row is `NoShardEffect` for this target and no transaction data, topology/catalog/schema/constraint/branch/key/ID/security/audit/retention/trust/derived/backup/restore/GC/reconfiguration/delivery effect applies. Any targeted slot or data effect requires its typed apply command.

`MetaCertificateLedger` and `ShardCertificateLedger` are replica-local immutable maps rooted by the role's `RaftStateRoot`. Each entry is `{certificate_kind,certificate_ref:StrongRef,authority_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,subject_identity,base_closure_inventory_digest,first_required_index,release_condition,successor_or_publication_status}`; a successor may strengthen but never shorten its closure or release condition. Meta ledgers retain un-published global decisions and remote-reference availability promises; shard ledgers retain prepare/checkpoint/applied-ack certificates. A certificate may leave the ledger only after its canonical publication/replacement is rooted and every named consumer/configuration/GC floor has acknowledged that transfer. The matching config floor and Raft snapshot carry the ledger floor, so log truncation cannot orphan a certificate between creation and publication.

Prepared roots are three distinct top-level kinds sharing a generated header but no cross-role entry union. `PreparedRootHeader<Role> = {database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Role,group_id,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,published_under_fence_epoch,root_generation,nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`. `LocalPreparedRootEntry = Owned{ownership_id,record_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>}|Transferring{transfer_record_ref:StrongRef<LocalPreparedOwnershipTransferRecord>}|Transferred{new_ownership_id,new_record_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>,transfer_identity:WeakDigest}`; Meta and Shard specialize every record/transfer ref to `MetaPreparedCommandRecord`/`MetaPreparedOwnershipTransferRecord` and `ShardPreparedPayloadRecord`/`ShardPreparedOwnershipTransferRecord`. `LocalPreparedPayloadRoot {header:PreparedRootHeader<Local>,entries[stable_command_identity->LocalPreparedRootEntry]}`, `MetaPreparedPayloadRoot {header:PreparedRootHeader<Meta>,entries[attempt_or_control_identity->MetaPreparedRootEntry]}`, and `ShardPreparedPayloadRoot {header:PreparedRootHeader<Shard{shard_id}>,entries[ShardCommandIdentity->ShardPreparedRootEntry]}` are separate object kinds; a cross-role key, record, or transfer tag is unencodable.

Each role-specific `PreparedOwnershipTransferRecord<Role>` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,old_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,new_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,old_ownership_id,new_ownership_id,old_record_ref:StrongRef<RoleRecord>,new_record_ref:StrongRef<RoleRecord>,identical_base_closure_inventory_digest,old_current_closure_inventory_digest,new_superset_closure_inventory_digest,old/new availability_certificate_refs[StrongRef],command_status:Preparing|Receipted|Ordered{raft_index}|CommittedUnapplied|AppliedVisibilityPending,transition_phase:Joint|New|RetirementAcknowledged,transition_floor_ref:StrongRef,raft_snapshot_acknowledgement,transfer_digest}`. Reconfiguration atomically changes `Owned(old)` to `Transferring` only after the new owner exists and has the same base plus superset closure, then to `Transferred/Owned(new)` after the exact transition floor and Raft/snapshot acknowledgement. Old ownership releases only after canonical applied/certificate state or completed transfer owns everything; abandonment requires fenced proof of non-order. Ordinarily the root fence epoch equals the manifest. The sole takeover exception preserves the exact epoch-E root OID/entries under E+1 via the takeover proof, then the first ordinary successor reheaders unchanged entries at E+1 before mutation. New records/receipts require E+1; old records remain obligations. Crash tests cover every role and transfer phase for Preparing/Receipted/Ordered/committed-unapplied/applied-visibility-pending states.

Replica-local `MetaPreparedCommandRecord` is `{prepared_ownership_id,record_generation,predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaPreparedCommandRecord>?,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Meta,group_id,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,local_writer_fence_epoch,attempt_or_control_identity,base_closure_inventory_digest,current_closure_inventory_digest,strong_local_refs[StrongRef],certified_remote_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef],exact_realizations[],command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand|GlobalControlCommand>?,status:Preparing|Receipted|Ordered{raft_index}|Applied{global_logical_command_seq}|Abandoned{fence_and_nonorder_proof}}`; ownership IDs, receipts, and successors bind the full domain/config/predicate header, preserve the base, and strengthen current closure. `MetaPreCommandBaseAvailabilityCertificate` begins `SameGroupCertificateHeader` and carries `{prepared_ownership_id,attempt_or_control_identity,base_closure_inventory_digest,sorted_payload_receipts,covered_object_kinds,exclusion_rule:Exactly{ThisCertificate,FutureMetaCommand,OrderAttemptSupplement}}`. It covers only already-built stable semantic evidence/base closure and excludes itself, the future command, and repeatable order/HLC supplements. Each proposal separately builds `MetaOrderAttemptInput` plus `MetaOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate`; voters revalidate its source signatures/set epoch, quorum, age, uncertainty, normalization, expected next sequence, and forward-jump policy against current state. Stale or sequence-losing evidence retires only that provably unordered supplement and may be replaced without changing semantic prepared ownership or audit bytes. After command construction, every proposer root-publishes the stable-owner successor that adds it.

Replica-local `ShardPreparedPayloadRecord` is `{prepared_ownership_id,record_generation,predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPreparedPayloadRecord>?,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Shard{shard_id},group_id,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,local_writer_fence_epoch,shard_command_identity:ShardCommandIdentity,base_closure_inventory_digest,current_closure_inventory_digest,strong_local_refs[StrongRef],certified_remote_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef],exact_realizations[],command_ref:StrongRef<ShardPrepareCommand|ShardDecisionApplyCommand|ShardControlCommand>?,status:Preparing|Receipted|Ordered{raft_index}|Applied{shard_raft_index}|Abandoned{fence_and_nonorder_proof}}`. Ownership IDs and receipts bind the entire domain/config/predicate header. `ShardPreCommandBaseAvailabilityCertificate` begins `SameGroupCertificateHeader` and carries `{prepared_ownership_id,shard_command_identity,base_closure_inventory_digest,sorted_payload_receipts,covered_object_kinds,exclusion_rule:Exactly{ThisCertificate,FutureShardCommand}}`. For prepare, generated coverage includes exact basis/fragment/admission closure formerly called `ShardPayloadAvailabilityCertificate`; that name is an alias, not a second certificate. Decision-apply and every payload-bearing shard control use the same exact-configuration D1 barrier. A stable-owner successor adds the completed command before proposal. Replica fence epochs never enter canonical semantic objects.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-01, FG-INV-08 through FG-INV-16, and FG-INV-20 for W12. Consumes G0 identity/command/state-slot/authority contracts, W11 Raft/configuration/payload/format/key contracts, role-transition formats and certified remote trust. All W12 semantic/protocol tasks depend on it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every field/root/command/ref/checkpoint/floor/prepared/key/certificate/projection type has stable role-specific registry rows, reference strengths, construction DAG, exact-cut and inventory coverage.
- Unit/golden tests freeze fresh Genesis and operational vectors, role tags, command origins, RootSlot closure, key stages, certificate ledgers, prepared transfers, checkpoint vectors and every floor field.
- Property/model tests prove Meta-only semantic time, Shard nonsemantic order, exact payload/root/log agreement, pre-order ownership before consensus, staged keys unusable until projection activation, destruction only after zero/completion, and complete floors.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects Local/Meta/Shard substitution, omitted/duplicate slot, wrong group/config/prefix, future applied/certificate ref, missing prepared closure, incomplete key stage, stale projection, raw remote edge, and checkpoint/suffix mismatch.
- Crash/DPOR E2E boots Meta plus multiple Shards, prepares/transfers/applies, rotates keys/configuration, checkpoints and recovers with loss at every log/root/slot/certificate/receipt boundary.
- JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,command_kind,role_prefix,root_kind,root_digest,slot_generation,checkpoint_digest?,floor_digest?,prepared_owner_id?,certificate_kind?,certificate_digest?,key_generation?,key_state?,projection_slot?,configuration_digest,recovery_action,replay_command}; secrets and raw key material excluded.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: generic role parameter accepted on wire, digest-only floors, Shard semantic clocks, keys active by local convention, certificate logs outside rooted closure, and hand-maintained projection slot lists. Missing coverage disables W12.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1654-1694.

title: Implement GlobalPrepareAdmission, effect bases/fragments, and fence-free shard prepares
description:
## What & scope
The write path from finalized workspaces to durable shard prepares: `ShardEffectBasis`, deterministic participant routing, the single union authorization decision, `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord`, `GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec` + `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence`, `ShardEffectFragment`, and `ShardPrepareCommand/Record/Certificate`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: one admission, one immutable participant/reservation set, one final-effect digest — Meta alone decides. B5: every shard input is a certified-remote wrapper; nothing is ambient. Rejected: per-shard authorization approvals substituting for the union decision; coordinator-fenced prepares (prepares are deliberately fence-free — replica fence epochs never enter canonical semantic objects).

## Design — normative detail
**Effect bases.** Post-rebase, each shard builds `ShardEffectBasis {global_txn_id,registration_generation,shard_id,registered_snapshot,topology_epoch,active_meta_projection_root_ref,authority_projection,operation_audit_admission_commitment,sorted_coordinate_bindings,write_key_material_projection_refs,final_effect_refs[ConditionalCoordinateRef],logical_delta_fragment_template_ref,read_witness_refs,final_write_summary,constraint_requests_and_deltas,resource_charge_basis,intent_semantics_oid,basis_effect_digest}`. `basis_effect_digest` hashes the effect-only projection through `intent_semantics_oid`; it excludes authorization/audit/outcome/resource/fragment/prepare/certificate objects but includes the authority-projection commitment. Every basis must deterministically finalize the certified workspace overlay — never re-execute or omit a prior statement.

**Routing fixed point.** `ParticipantRoutingDerivationProof` records ordered fixed-point rounds (cross-partition effects, cascades, constraint owners). Meta builds `ParticipantRoutingCertificate` with sorted bases/participants/constraint owners and `global_final_effect_digest = H("fgdb:global-effect:v1", sorted(shard_id,basis_effect_digest))`. Missing/extra bases, mixed authority projections, non-fixed-point cascades fail closed. Then exactly one `GlobalAuthorizationDecisionRecord` — the global validator replays the permit across the union including hidden cascades and disclosure contracts; per-shard approvals cannot substitute. Meta then creates resource transitions plus `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord` (terminal compare contract, `terminal_domain:CommitIfCertifiedElseAbort{global_final_effect_digest,allowed_stable_abort_reason_classes}`, optional Sharded `TerminalWriteResultPreparation`) — but no outcome event/resolution/terminal gate yet.

**Admission.** `GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec` names expected published-statement frontier, delivery-terminal frontier, statement-index digest, workspace generation, cumulative read-witness and logical-effect roots, routing certificate, sorted participants/constraint owners/bases, meta constraint reservation requests, the authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, audit admission (`Claimed|NotRequired`, ticket stays unresolved), `global_final_effect_digest`, expected branch heads/key epochs/topology/policy/revocation/conflict basis. Apply requires ReadWrite, exact fixed-point equality, a contiguous frontier with every statement terminally `Published|Failed|Abandoned`, every Buffered output delivery-terminal or independently retained, no Open statement, no prior admission — then atomically installs `PrepareAdmitted`, creates Meta reservations, and constructs `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence::Armed` freezing branch heads, key epochs, write coordinates, constraint-reservation/resource sets, statement/delivery/workspace/witness/effect commitment, topology/policy/revocation/conflict basis. The fence deliberately contains no assigned future sequence or HLC. Any drift afterwards requires admitted abort/release plus a NEW registration generation; digest substitution never recertifies stale work.

**Fragments & prepares.** Only after admission is visible may shards build `ShardEffectFragment` (every Meta object an exact CRSR bound to Meta domain/configuration, this consumer domain, availability, and two-sided grant; only `basis_ref` is shard-local; envelope digest excluded from the global effect digest) and order fence-free `ShardPrepareCommand` keyed `prepare_key:{global_txn_id,registration_generation,admission_generation}`: the shard first applies every Meta command through the admission (typed projection or exhaustive irrelevance proof), then byte-verifies authority projection, active Meta projection, topology/policy/revocation/key/audit, configuration, admission, basis, fragment, and the D1 `ShardPreCommandBaseAvailabilityCertificate`. Apply builds `ShardPrepareRecord` (states `Prepared|GloballyCommitted|GloballyAborted|Applied|GcEligible`), installs canonical constraint reservations atomically, then the quorum signs `ShardPrepareCertificate` (followers recompute all fields). Late prepare after an abort tombstone, a second admission generation under one registration, or any stale projection rejects.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (W12 write order): registration/workspace -> effect bases/routing -> authorization/resource/outcome/admission -> shard fragments/prepares -> constraints/serialization -> final-certification holds -> Meta command; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; timeout releases no prepared owner. FG-INV-02: at most one legal live generation owns each reservation/hold. FG-INV-06: routing/coarsening and workspace overlays preserve witness contracts — missing routing or prior-touched-shard overlay causes conservative failure, never a dropped edge. Invariant-class; prepare fan-out latency benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes workspaces/witnesses from `w12-statement-machine`, coordinator choreography shape from `w4-coordinator`, availability certificates from `w11-payload-availability`. Produces prepares/reservations for `w12-certification` and `w12-decision-visibility`; constraint requests for `w12-constraints-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "Fence-free prepares... pass exact DAG/crash proofs"; "every participant prepare has durable availability and one terminal decision; no timeout fractures atomicity under crash/partition/leader loss/reconfiguration." Tests: substitution matrices (wrong role/group/incarnation/configuration/grant, locally-encoded Meta StrongRef unrepresentable); admission with an Open statement or undetached result rejected; drift-after-admission forces new generation; crash at every prepare state (Preparing/Receipted/Ordered/committed-unapplied/applied-visibility-pending) across reconfiguration transfer phases. E2E: 3-shard write with induced shard lag; assert prepare waits for admission-prefix apply, logging per-shard applied prefix at prepare time.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: exhaustive irrelevance proofs on quiet shards add work (mitigated by `MetaRelevanceRangeProof` contiguity). Rejected: fenced prepares; re-execution at prepare time; catch-all basis commitments replacing typed refs.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 2 (1083); App A 1734, 1818-1822, 1848; §19:1350/1354.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement W12 recovery: prepared pinning, compaction, six-stage release, distributed GC
description:
## What & scope
Everything that keeps W12 safe over time: prepared-closure pinning and the nonblocking-impossibility stance, `NeverRegisteredFloor` and three-phase `ClosedAttemptCompaction`, the `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef` trust/retention system with the six-stage release handshake, reconfiguration ownership transfer, and the distributed GC protocol with fenced cancellation.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B5: partitions may block but can never reverse decisions or reclaim uncertain state; every release is an explicit typed handshake, never inferred from time or a missing client. Rejected: presumed-abort timeouts; inferring release from absence; cross-group raw strong references.

## Design — normative detail
**Prepared pinning.** Prepared closures remain pinned through terminal decision, post-visibility participant acks, overlap/retention floors, and staged GC. No prepared participant times out or guesses; it recovers Meta's decision. `MetaConfigPayloadFloor`/`ShardConfigPayloadFloor` are exact closed schemas whose typed subfloors cover begin status, attempt families, statements/results, conflict overlap, attempt compaction, audit claim/signer, prepared owners, certificate ledger, decision and delta publication, retention cuts, remote trust/release, key lifecycle, derived generations, GC, backup, restore, activation/retirement, continuity/service, reconfiguration/topology; missing/duplicate/wrong-role/raw-cross-group coverage fails G0.

**Attempt compaction.** `NeverRegisteredFloorSpec` removes only proved staging: `NeverRegisteredEvidence` + `NoReservationBindingProof` (reservation never consumed by registration nor exported), rewrites Detailed -> Compacted preserving the same replay ref and byte-identical public bytes. `ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec` has three separately ordered phases and neither decides Prepared work: **build** verifies every selected attempt is TerminalReady and audit-visible with complete decision/certificate publication, every admitted shard post-visibility ack, committed Global-delta publication/frontier (or no-delta proof), all statements terminal, all results Acknowledged/ReleasedUnacked/independently retained, workspace/remote-grant release evidence, overlap closed — creating an unsigned compact `ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord` in `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot` (build does NOT advance the authoritative floor); **attest** — only after the record and its audit visibility advance are durable does the quorum create `AttemptCompactionAttestation` (no strong edge to the build command/prior floor/heavy evidence); **publish** — `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec` rewrites selected entries to `CompactedTerminal`, installs `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor` (no strong/CRSR path to the previous floor), and only then, after visibility and an activated checkpoint cut, is heavy evidence reclaimable. Detailed/compacted NeverRegistered and terminal outcomes are byte-identical (gate). `GlobalOutcomeExpirySpec` alone drops replay/bundle edges via permanent `ExpiredTombstone`s.

**Remote trust & six-stage release.** W12's one cross-consensus edge is `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>` over `ExportLeaf<T>`, `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence` (trust transition `Genesis{root artifact}|Successor|ValidatedCheckpointSuccessor`; current-member signatures alone never a trust root), `RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence`, and `RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence` (`grant_id = H("fgdb:remote-grant:v1",...)`). Release is the explicit six-transition handshake: (1) consumer orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec` -> `ReleaseRequested` (type state cannot acquire new refs under the old grant); (2) consumer quorum certificate + portable leaf -> `ReleaseCertified`; (3) authority imports and orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseApplySpec` -> `RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone` (no strong edge to the released target); (4) authority ack certificate + portable leaf; (5) authority publish -> `RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry` under the permanent release-proof floor; (6) consumer `ConsumeReleaseAck` with current no-old-grant-ref proof. Meta/Shard reconfiguration uses explicit `PreparedOwnershipTransferRecord<Role>` (Owned -> Transferring -> Transferred only after new owner holds base+superset closure and the transition floor plus Raft/snapshot acknowledgement) and remote-config trust adoption (`ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationSpec`, `ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence/Spec`, `RemoteGrantRetirementPlan`) before old retirement.

**Distributed GC.** Certified preflight (`ShardGcPreflightSpec/Record/Evidence`, `MetaGcPreflightRecord`) -> `GlobalGcAuthorizationSpec/Record` (bounded candidate sets; an Active/ReleaseRequested grant target is never a candidate; a planned remote release is not completion — `GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef` accepts only stage-5/6 or imported permanent evidence) -> per-role Semantic quarantine (`ShardGcApplySpec`/`MetaGcApplyQuarantineSpec`: followers recompute from CURRENT state; require `reclaim ⊆ authorized ∩ preflight`, disjointness from the reachable set, exact family/plan bijection; every encoder/dedupe/validator rejects new edges to quarantined identities) -> Protocol physical machine -> `PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence` -> Semantic disposition import -> four noninterchangeable acks (`MetaGcCompletedAck|ShardGcCompletedAck|MetaGcCancelledAck|ShardGcCancelledAck`) -> `GlobalGcCompletionSpec`. Cancellation is fenced and monotone: `Executing -> CancellationPreparing -> CancellationAuthorized|CompletionRequired -> CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart|Completed`; any Started observation permanently forces roll-forward.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14: W12 requires bounded preflight, Meta authorization, current-root disjoint quarantine, no resurrection, exact member completion, progress, and aggregate completion; missing participants remain blocking; heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut. FG-INV-07: timeout releases no prepared, certificate, audit, result, allocation, escrow, or retention owner. FG-INV-01: detailed and compacted proofs return byte-identical public outcomes. FG-INV-16: no obligation is lost/duplicated/refunded while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal. Invariant-class; MTTDL modeling stays FG-CFG-01.

## Interactions
Consumes acks/floors from `w12-decision-visibility`, GC core from `w2-gc-core`/`w11-fenced-gc`, checkpoints from `w2-retention-checkpoints`. Produces compaction floors consumed by status surfaces (`w10-capabilities`) and the retirement predicates for `w12-topology`/`w12-backup-restore`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "Meta/Shard GC must pass Requested/Started/Completed-or-all-cancelled state machines before aggregate completion"; "attempt compaction's build/attest/publish protocol proves every result/workspace/remote-grant/public-status obligation before release"; "remote configuration trust and the six-stage grant release... pass models and physical evidence gates"; "every cross-group edge passes two-sided CertifiedRemoteStrongRef trust/retention/GC tests." Tests: status race matrix (build/visibility/attestation/publish/expiry/post-cut reclamation) requiring identical validated-capability response bytes; six-stage crash at every transition leaving target root/permanent proof/replayable pending state; GC tests covering every start position, all-no-start, ambiguous status, prepare/fence/start races, successor exhaustion, mixed ack substitution, configuration/topology change; dedupe-resurrection storms. E2E: scripted 1-Meta/3-shard cluster — prepared transactions pinned through an induced partition and leader loss with zero timeout decisions (recovery fetches Meta's decision), a full six-stage remote-grant release drill, NeverRegistered plus build/attest/publish closed-attempt compaction under concurrent status lookups (byte-identical public responses before, during, and after), and two distributed GC runs: one cancelled mid-flight with all-participants-no-start (CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart) and one forced to CompletionRequired by a first Started observation. DETAILED LOGGING (required): every six-stage release transition logs `{grant_id, release_nonce, stage 1-6, role, applied ref}`; every GC participant logs `{operation family/generation, fence generation, participant state Pending|FenceInstalled|NoStartFenced|StartedObserved|RollForwardPending|Completed|Cancelled, evidence/ack ids}`; compaction logs `{compaction_id, phase build|attest|publish, selected attempt keys, prior/new floor digests}`; prepared-ownership transfers log `{ownership ids, command_status, transition_phase}`; tests replay the logs against the registered state machines and fail on any missing or out-of-order transition.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: blocking GC under partition accumulates debt (accepted — safety over reclamation). Rejected: timeout-terminated prepares; stage-4 certificate as release completion; floors that decide Prepared work.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet "Recovery and nonblocking impossibility" (1093); App A 1396-1400, 1676-1690, 1788-1816; §19:1352-1354.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement W12 BEGIN/ticket/registration and the ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot
description:
## What & scope
Build the W12 transaction front door: durable BEGIN reservation, operation-ticket admission, Meta attempt registration with workspace generation zero, the registered ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot, and the shard-read witness basis discipline. Statements/publication live in `w12-statement-machine`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B6: an agent's BEGIN gets a durable, idempotent, capability-visible lineage *before* any attempt exists, and every read observes one exact global prefix — no shard ever serves data ahead of ticket visibility or registration. B5: authorization and audit admission precede observation, evidence-first. Rejected: optimistic shard-first reads reconciled later ("local SSI plus hope", §14.6), and overloading a claimed operation ticket for lifecycle scaffolding.

## Design — normative detail
**Ticket-first.** When the audit profile requires it, Meta first mirrors one pending operation ticket; only then may it order the `ReadOnly|ReadWrite` registration with matching read/mutation permit and `OperationAuditAdmission` (`NotRequired{evidence}|PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref,ticket_admission_record_ref,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref,claim_record_ref,owner:{global_txn_id,registration_generation},operation_request_basis_commitment}`). The registration's own control gate is a validated lifecycle-scaffolding `NotRequired` proof and cannot consume the operation ticket. The claim remains unresolved until the one terminal read-close/commit/abort event.

**BEGIN lineage.** `TxnOutcomeCapabilityFields` (header/body/MAC bytes exist before ordering; `capability_commitment` is their domain-separated digest). `GlobalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(namespace,incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved|BoundDetailed|BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredDetailed|NeverRegisteredCompacted|ExpiredTombstone`. `GlobalBeginReservationSpec` (sequence-neutral: header, key, request digest, operation class/isolation/`TransactionErrorPolicy`, capability replay ref, audit admission, absence proof, staging resource reservation) applies to `GlobalBeginReservationRecord` + atomic `Reserved` + `GlobalOutcomeDirectoryValue::BeginStaging`; only then may Fabric emit `BEGIN_ACCEPTED`. Byte-identical retry returns identical canonical capability bytes even after key rotation; any drift fails. `BeginTerminalEvidence = Denied|AuthenticatedAbandon|RegionClosed{BeginRegionClosedReceipt}|Superseded`; time passage, socket suspicion, process death inhabit no arm; `GlobalBeginTerminalSpec` resolves the exact pending ticket and creates the compactable NeverRegistered record — never an attempt/family/burn.

**Registration.** `GlobalAttemptRegistrationSpec` binds header, `global_txn_id`, begin binding (`BindReserved|IdempotentBound`), token, `TxnOperationCeiling`, autocommit classification (required exactly for AutocommitExecute, forbidden for ExplicitBegin), requested snapshot + minimum acceptable, permit, error policy (`AbortTransactionOnStatementError|ContinueOnDeclaredRecoverable{recoverable_error_class_table_oid}`; savepoints rejected at BEGIN), initial workspace recipe, audit admission, topology basis, `registration_generation`, and family expectation `First{authenticated_absence_proof}|Successor{prior_generation,prior_terminal_outcome_proof_ref,prior_release_and_overlap_floor_ref}|IdempotentRetry`. Applied only via `GlobalControlCommand(kind=RegisterAttempt)`: binding claims the operation ticket, checks the conflict safe-snapshot frontier, inserts Active family/attempt/conflict entries, flips the outcome directory to `W12`, constructs `GlobalAttemptRegistration` and workspace generation zero (exact same header, ProvenReadOnly cumulative potential) plus the `Registered` outcome. `AttemptFamilyState` enforces one active registered generation; parallel generations, gaps, token rebinding, ceiling drift fail closed.

**Global snapshot & shard reads.** The registered ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot follows registration; no shard read precedes ticket visibility or registration. A shard read proves its active Meta topology/policy/revocation/key/audit projection covers the registration prefix and binds the operation-audit commitment; before any shard read, operation and applicable statement tickets are imported/claimed through the two certified registrations; the shard rechecks revocation. `ShardReadWitnessBasis` binds execution scope (`ReadExecutionScope::ShardTerminal|ShardStatement`), the complete `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` (not a digest), registered snapshot, workspace overlay root, `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot`, read state root + checkpoint certificate + `ShardHistoryInventory`, `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` (exists before the first cursor/storage/statistics observation), witness refs, answer contract, result fragment digest, and the after-the-fact `ReadResultReleaseDecisionRecord`. Reads evaluate registered snapshot plus the exact ordered local workspace overlay certified by the imported global generation; a missing prior-touched-shard delta or false empty-overlay proof fails. Meta aggregates via `ReadParticipantRoutingCertificate` (fixed point over every routed read/expansion/constraint-disclosure and previously touched workspace shard). Queries choose one global prefix and wait/fail until every routed shard has applied/proved it and retained that history.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation or effect; W12 registration claims operation/statement tickets before observation; shard work carries only exact certified projections; equal epoch scalars with different roots never substitute. FG-INV-01: W12 reserves the begin key and outcome-capability bytes before response; `AttemptFamilyState` admits only generation-zero First, exact prior+1 Successor after a registered Terminal with proved release/overlap floor, or byte-identical IdempotentRetry; NeverRegistered creates no family/generation/burn. FG-INV-04: every read begins at the visible endpoint of the audit pipeline. All are invariant-class clauses in `invariants.toml`; begin-path latency is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w12-meta-clock` (control ordering), `w9-audit-pipeline` (tickets), `w11-read-contracts` (ReadIndex fencing), `w4-ssi-witnesses` (witness types). Produces registrations/workspaces for `w12-statement-machine` and `w12-prepare`; begin/outcome directories consumed by `w12-recovery-gc` compaction.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate lines: "BEGIN durably reserves its key/outcome capability before response; registration atomically claims the operation ticket and roots workspace zero before every serializable read." Tests: lost-response BEGIN retry returns byte-identical capability; concurrent First/Successor/IdempotentRetry races; NeverRegistered-no-family negatives; shard read attempted before registration visibility must fail (oracle-checked); stale Meta projection at shard read rejected; crash at every point between reservation, registration, and first shard read with recovery to a single lineage. E2E: scripted 3-shard cluster, 1k concurrent BEGINs with induced duplicate delivery, log reservation/registration/first-read prefixes and assert monotone coverage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ticket-first adds an external round trip on Required audit profiles (amortized via batching, priced in §16/§17). Rejected: reading before registration; consuming the operation ticket for scaffolding; fabricating attempt identities for denied BEGINs.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 2 (1083); App A 1696-1721; §19:1350.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement certified-remote trust, retention grants, and six-stage release formats
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact W12 certified-remote trust, reference, retention-grant, consumer/authority release, configuration adoption, and six-stage retirement formats. This task owns the two-sided cross-group edge contract and prevents a remote ObjectId or signature from masquerading as a local strong reference.

## Why
Cross-group data is safe only while the consumer can prove both authority trust and retention. Reconfiguration/topology cannot drop old grants or verification evidence until replacement/release is acknowledged on both sides; otherwise GC can reclaim live data or stale configurations can authorize work.

## Design — exact normative contract
`ConsensusDomain {database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id},group_id}` is the indivisible authority/consumer identity in every signed, MACed, indexed, or retained cross-group transcript. `group_id` is also a random 256-bit database-global unique identifier, but no validator relies on uniqueness without matching the complete domain. Later shorthand `authority_group_id`, `consumer_group_id`, or `group_id` in a cross-group schema means the corresponding full `ConsensusDomain`; wire encoders never serialize the scalar alone. `RemoteObjectIdentity {authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,object_oid,object_kind,canonical_digest}` is comparison-only and never a local reachability edge.

`RootAuthorityTrustBody` is the signature-free immutable `{authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,artifact_kind:FreshShardedGenesis|CertifiedLocalRoleTransition,canonical_genesis_or_transition_bytes,target_configuration_oid,target_configuration_canonical_digest,externally_pinned_root_policy_id,expected_root_verification_key_set_digest,threshold,source_identity_or_transition_continuity_commitment,body_digest:BodyDigest<RootAuthorityTrustBody>}`; its registered body transcript includes every preceding field and excludes exactly `body_digest`. `RootAuthorityTrustArtifact` is `{body_ref:StrongRef<RootAuthorityTrustBody>,body_digest:BodyDigest<RootAuthorityTrustBody>,canonical_root_authority_signature_set,signed_transcript_digest:TranscriptDigest<RootAuthorityTrustArtifact>}`. Each root signature signs the domain-separated tuple `{schema/tag,authority_domain,artifact_kind,body_digest,externally_pinned_root_policy_id}`; the artifact transcript includes the body digest and canonically sorted signatures and excludes exactly `signed_transcript_digest`. Validation first resolves the deployment's externally pinned policy, key set, and threshold and byte-matches their IDs/digest to the body, then verifies signatures and transcript; keys merely embedded in the object can never select their own trust root. The canonical genesis/transition bytes and policy evidence remain strongly retained and independently reverified. `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence` is the nonrecursive imported leaf `{authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,configuration_oid,configuration_canonical_digest,canonical_configuration_bytes,configuration_adoption_raft_index,adoption_log_prefix_digest,member_verification_key_set,payload_predicate_digest,trust_transition:Genesis{root_authority_trust_artifact_ref:StrongRef<RootAuthorityTrustArtifact>}|Successor{predecessor_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,joint_transition_transcript,old_configuration_quorum_signatures,new_configuration_quorum_signatures,final_retirement_floor_digest}|ValidatedCheckpointSuccessor{predecessor_anchor_ref:StrongRef<ValidatedRemoteConfigurationAnchor>,joint_transition_transcript,old_configuration_quorum_signatures,new_configuration_quorum_signatures,final_retirement_floor_digest},minimum_configuration_retention_floor,signer_epoch,configuration_quorum_signatures}`. Current-member signatures alone are never a trust root. Embedded canonical configuration bytes recompute the OID/digest and self-bind the complete domain; the transition proves adoption from an already trusted root artifact, predecessor, or anchor. `RemoteConfigurationRef` means a consumer-local `StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>`.

Authority-local certificate object `T` and its imported representation are deliberately different schemas. `ExportLeaf<T> {domain:ImportedCertificateDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,export_projection_version,object_specific_scalar_projection,local_strong_ref_projection[RemoteObjectIdentity],target_closure_inventory_digest,authority_ledger_floor,quorum_signatures}` replaces every authority-local strong reference with a typed remote identity/closure commitment while preserving every verifier-relevant scalar. Its generated projector is injectively bound to the canonical digest of `T`; a consumer never decodes an authority-local `StrongRef` as local. `RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence` is the consumer-local leaf `{authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,certificate_export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>>,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_predicate_digest,receipt_set_commitment,encoding_placement_coverage,failure_domains,authority_retention_floor,signer_epoch,authority_quorum_signatures}`; the authority ledger separately roots the real certificate/receipts.

W12's one cross-consensus edge is `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T> {authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,export_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<T>>,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence>,retention_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}`. Every `StrongRef` inside it targets a complete consumer-local leaf; none targets `T` in the authority group. The generated `T -> ExportLeaf<T>` verifier and field-level schema registry define exactly which refs become remote identities. `grant_id = H("fgdb:remote-grant:v1", authority_domain, consumer_domain, target_identity, grant_nonce)`; consumer and authority maps are keyed by `(authority_domain,grant_id)`, and any collision with nonidentical bytes fails closed. `RemoteGrantTargetRef` is the containing-schema-generated closed union with one typed strong-reference arm per exportable authority-local target kind; it has no generic target arm. `RemoteRetentionGrantSpec` is authority-group input `{grant_id,authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,authority_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_ref:RemoteGrantTargetRef,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,minimum_authority_checkpoint_floor,grant_nonce}`. The target ref and identity must be the exact registered pair. Authority apply creates `RemoteRetentionGrantRecord {spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantSpec>,authority_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,state:Active}` in `RemoteRetentionObligationRoot`, which roots the exact target closure. Its quorum exports `RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence {authority_configuration_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,grant_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,grant_id,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,target_closure_inventory_digest,payload_availability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence>,authority_order_index,minimum_authority_checkpoint_floor,grant_nonce,signer_epoch,authority_quorum_signatures}`. The consumer may publish the wrapper only after authenticating all leaves and byte-matching both complete domains; the authority ledger, not the evidence, owns the remote target.

Release is an explicit six-transition handshake, never inferred from time or a missing client. (1) After canonically removing/replacing every reference while retaining the grant leaf, the consumer orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec {grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,consumer_release_state_identity:WeakDigest,complete_consumer_root_digest,consumer_checkpoint_floor,successor_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>?,release_nonce}`; apply rechecks the complete consumer root, constructs `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord {spec_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec>,consumer_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,consumer_no_reference_floor_digest}`, and installs `ReleaseRequested`. That type state cannot acquire or create another local ref under the old grant; any concurrent/new use must first acquire and publish a distinct successor grant. (2) Only afterward does the consumer quorum create authority-local `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,request_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestRecord>,complete_consumer_root_digest,consumer_no_reference_floor_digest,successor_grant_identity?,release_nonce,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}` after rechecking the root. A generated specialized `ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>` replaces its local refs with remote identities; the later consumer publish control installs this portable leaf as `ReleaseCertified`. (3) The authority imports that leaf and orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseApplySpec {active_grant_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantRecord>,release_request_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestCertificate>>,expected_active_grant_digest,verified_consumer_no_reference_floor,successor_transfer_proof?}`. Apply rechecks every stronger authority root, removes the active grant, and creates `RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone {grant_record_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,grant_spec_digest:WeakDigest,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,request_certificate_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,release_nonce,authority_command_input_digest:WeakDigest,authority_order_index}` with no strong edge to the active record, spec, target, or apply command. The release command/log retains those inputs only until its verified cut. (4) Only after that applied root does the authority quorum create local `RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,tombstone_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone>,grant_id,consumer_domain:ConsensusDomain,target_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,release_nonce,authority_order_index,authority_state_root_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}` and its specialized portable ExportLeaf. (5) A later authority publish control atomically creates `RemoteRetentionAckPublishRecord {ack_certificate_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,authority_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,summary_key}` and installs `RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry {authority_domain,consumer_domain,grant_id,target_identity,release_nonce,ack_leaf_identity,ack_digest,authority_order_index,published_at_order_index,permanent_release_proof_floor}` in `RemoteReleaseSummaryRoot`. The summary and nonrecursive archive-backed ack leaf remain available through the database's capability-safe permanent release-proof floor and require no new releasable grant merely to prove the old grant released. (6) The consumer imports the portable leaf without a CRSR, rechecks that its current complete root still contains no old-grant ref, orders `ConsumeReleaseAck`, and creates `RemoteRetentionConsumeAckRecord {ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,consumer_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,current_no_old_grant_ref_proof_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionNoOldGrantProof>,summary_key}`; only then may it retire request/grant evidence after its checkpoint floor. `AuthorityAppliedRef = Local{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq}|Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}|Shard{command_ref:StrongRef<ShardControlCommand>,shard_raft_index}` is used only inside its owning group and prevents role ambiguity. A crash at any point leaves an authority target root, permanent release proof, or replayable pending transition; no imported leaf contains an ordinary strong edge into its source group.

W12 history wrappers are distinct rather than overloading the local `LogicalCommandRecord` tag: `StrongGlobalCommandRef{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq}`, `ConditionalGlobalCommandRef{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq,axis=GlobalLogical}`, and `WeakGlobalCommandIdentity{record_oid,global_logical_command_seq}` target `GlobalTxnRecord|GlobalControlRecord`; `ConditionalGlobalTxnInputRef{command_oid,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,axis=GlobalLogical}` targets the already-built `GlobalTxnCommand` and is valid only when the record at that sequence names the same input; `StrongShardCommandRef{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index}`, `ConditionalShardCommandRef{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index,axis=ShardRaft}`, and `WeakShardCommandIdentity{record_oid,shard_id,shard_raft_index}` target `ShardCommandRecord`. Strong variants retain, conditional variants stop only at a verified matching meta/shard checkpoint cut, and weak variants compare only. Cross-group carriage of any target still requires `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`; these wrappers are only within the owning consensus group.

Canonical result objects that can be produced in either posture use closed role tags rather than pretending every input is local: `AppliedControlRef = Local{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq} | Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}`; `AppliedAbortRef = LocalControl{command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,logical_command_seq} | LocalTxn{command_ref:StrongRef<AdmittedTxnAbortCommand>,logical_command_seq} | MetaControl{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,global_logical_command_seq} | MetaTxn{command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>,global_logical_command_seq}`; and `AuditCandidateRef = Local{blocked_after_logical_command_seq,candidate_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>} | Meta{blocked_after_global_logical_command_seq,candidate_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>}`. The group-role and lifecycle-stage validator accepts only the matching tag: active/unadmitted Local cancellation uses LocalControl, admitted Local abort uses LocalTxn, active/unadmitted Meta cancellation uses MetaControl, and admitted Meta abort uses MetaTxn. These tags are part of the v1 durable schema and the generated spec/result compatibility matrix; no decoder infers posture from ambient configuration.

Key-envelope openers use the separate retaining physical edge `StrongCiphertextRef<T> { logical_oid, ciphertext_id, dek_id, ciphertext_digest, protected_length, key_opener_ref:KeyOpenerRef<T>, recoverability_profile, selected_realizations[CiphertextRealizationRef<T>],payload_availability_certificate_ref:PayloadAvailabilityCertificateRef<T> }`. `KeyOpenerRef<T>`, `CiphertextRealizationRef<T>`, and `PayloadAvailabilityCertificateRef<T>` are generated exact unions whose arms are legal for that ciphertext class and owning role; no bare `StrongRef` or cross-role certificate decodes. Its target ciphertext, complete authenticated realization inventory, opener, and certificate exist before the referring envelope object, and the certificate must prove that the selected set satisfies the named profile under the exact configuration. It pins that `CiphertextId` and the selected recoverable `EncodingId`/`PlacementId` set; recoding or movement first creates a successor envelope/grant edge with a newly certified set before the old set can retire, while re-encryption cannot substitute a new ciphertext under a live reference. This is intentionally stronger than ordinary logical reachability and is included in GC, reconfiguration, backup, and key-destruction floors.

The schemas below use a flattened prose rendering, but **names and suffixes never imply reference strength**. Every field's exact type, cardinality, identity class, target, role/posture predicate, retention/cut behavior, and `PriorObject` construction annotation come from §5.1's generated `durable_fields.toml`; the rendering checker rejects any brace field that lacks or disagrees with its row. A compact phrase such as “typed mandatory inventory” is a named closed sub-schema, never an open bag or slash-separated set of ambient refs. Bootstrap-slot root identity is an external GC root and is followed as strong. Pending/prepared traversal treats a registered `ConditionalCoordinateRef` as strong because no committed-marker cut context exists. Archive and prior-incarnation identities are separate nonlocal classes and can never enter the current local ObjectId mark set. Every concrete target of a strong or currently followed conditional edge must exist before the parent encoder runs. Recursive persistent nodes are legal only in that child-before-parent direction. Generated schema/reference/DAG checkers compare the field table, Appendix rendering, Rust encoders, and registry rows; they reject unresolved, untyped, role-invalid, self, mutual, or future-result cycles and fail G0 on drift. Unknown tags or context fail closed.
Shard membership is Meta-authorized and later Meta-adopted. `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationSpec` is `{shard_id,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,old_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_meta_remote_trust_generation,expected_meta_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,joint_and_final_canonical_configuration_bytes_and_digests,transition_nonce,payload_predicates,required_checkpoint_floor_remote_prepared_certificate_obligations,successor_evidence_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`; its applied `ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationRecord` fixes the one permitted transition and current trust selector. Each `ShardConfigurationTransitionSpec` consumes the certified record and transfers every old-configuration owner. After `CommitRetirementFloor`, old and new quorums create `ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,authorization_identity,old/joint/new configuration identities,final_floor,through_shard_index/global_prefix,remote_obligation_commitment,predecessor_remote_configuration_evidence_identity,old_and_new_quorum_signatures,one_digest_signer_lock_ref}`. The successor `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence::Successor` is authenticated from the currently trusted predecessor and both quorums; new members alone cannot bootstrap it.

`RemoteGrantRetirementPlan` is the Meta-local pre-order object `{plan_id,basis_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,basis_remote_trust_generation,retired_authority_domain,retired_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,sorted_entries[{old_grant_id,old_grant_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,target_identity,consumer_domain,target_closure_commitment,disposition:ReplaceWithSuccessorGrant{successor_grant_body_recipe,required_consumer_adoption_predicate}|Release{release_request_body_recipe},required_six_stage_transition:RequestConsumerRelease->PublishConsumerReleaseEvidence->ApplyAuthorityRelease->PublishAuthorityReleaseAck->ConsumeReleaseAck->Acknowledged,completion_predicate}],complete_old_grant_set_and_target_coverage_digest,expected_consumer_root_digest,completion_floor_body_recipe}`. It names no future request, tombstone, ack, applied record, or result; adoption verifies the exhaustive old-grant set before selecting it. `ShardConfigurationAdoptionSpec` is Meta input `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,adoption_evidence_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_old_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_remote_trust_generation,expected_selected_old_evidence_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,successor_configuration_evidence_ref:StrongRef<RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence>,expected_successor_evidence_digest,old_grant_retirement_plan_ref:StrongRef<RemoteGrantRetirementPlan>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies the direct trust transition and atomically CASes both the topology shard entry and `RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot` selector/generation; neither may advance alone. Only then may the six-stage handshake release old-configuration grants and membership. Stale trust generation, anchor, topology, old/new signature domain, or successor bytes reject with no partial adoption.

Distributed GC separates preflight, semantic authorization/quarantine, physical completion, and aggregate completion. A stage-4 certificate is not release completion. `PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection` is the reference-free `{authority_domain,configuration_oid,configuration_digest,canonical_configuration_bytes,payload_predicate_digest,trust_transition_proof_bytes,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence` is `{authority_domain,consumer_domain,grant_id,target_identity,release_nonce,ack_leaf_bytes_and_identity,authority_configuration_evidence:PortableRemoteAuthorityConfigurationProjection,summary_entry_key,summary_inclusion_proof,permanent_release_proof_floor,authority_signatures}` and contains no CRSR, new retention grant, or cross-group strong edge. `GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef` is the closed role-checked union `AuthorityPublished{publish_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionAckPublishRecord>,summary_entry_ref:StrongRef<RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>}|ConsumerAcknowledged{consume_record_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumeAckRecord>,ack_leaf_ref:StrongRef<ExportLeaf<RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate>>,current_no_old_grant_ref_proof_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionNoOldGrantProof>}|ImportedPermanent{evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableRemoteReleaseAckEvidence>}`. The candidate's ownership/consumer role selects the one legal arm; every arm proves stage 5 or stage 6 plus the permanent summary floor. A request, stage-4 certificate, tombstone, plan, unsigned identity, or a newly granted CRSR cannot inhabit it. A shard first orders `ShardGcPreflightSpec {basis_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_shard_raft_index,basis_global_prefix,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_epoch,complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>,candidate_derivation_profile,excluded_obligation_commitment}`. Apply creates `ShardGcPreflightRecord {source_spec_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightSpec>,basis identities,generated current/cut/prepared/certificate/lease/key/derived/backup/replay/restore/remote inventories,exact_candidate_local_reclaim_set,excluded_obligations,candidate_set_digest}`; only afterward does the quorum create `ShardGcPreflightEvidence {SameGroupCertificateHeader,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,candidate_set_digest,root_inventory_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. Meta likewise builds `MetaGcPreflightRecord` for its local physical universe before ordering `GlobalGcAuthorizationSpec {basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_prefix,meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,exact_meta_candidate_set,sorted_shard_preflight_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardGcPreflightEvidence>],exact_per_shard_candidate_commitments,excluded_global_obligation_commitment,completed_remote_release_proof_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply creates `GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord` authorizing only those bounded sets; a planned remote release is not completion, and an active/ReleaseRequested grant target is never a reclaim candidate.

Each participant next orders a role-specific **Semantic quarantine** command. `GcMemberOperationPlan` is the exact `{generation,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,storage_member_id,storage_profile_oid,target_inventory_digest,canonical_action_body_recipe_and_digest}`. `GcOperationFamily` is `{family_id,base_target_set_commitment,base_generation_zero_plan_set_commitment,successor_operation_id_recipe,max_generations,body_digest}`. `ShardGcApplySpec` is `{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_shard_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_epoch,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_local_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest}`. `MetaGcApplyQuarantineSpec` is the exact Meta-local `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,authorization_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,meta_preflight_record_ref:StrongRef<MetaGcPreflightRecord>,expected_current_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_meta_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_root_inventory_digest,exact_authorized_meta_reclaim_set,completed_remote_release_ack_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],current_reachability_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<GcReachabilityProof>,newly_reachable_disjoint_proof_ref:StrongRef<GcDisjointnessProof>,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,sorted_generation_zero_plans[GcMemberOperationPlan],complete_member_target_plan_and_family_bijection_digest,terminal_audit_gate}`. Followers recompute from the **current** Semantic state, both RootSlots, Protocol/Prepared/Consensus state, and the candidate result. They require `reclaim_set ⊆ authorized_set ∩ preflight_set`, disjointness from the current reachable set, and exact family/base-plan coverage; “unchanged or stronger” is not a relation. Apply creates the role-specific reclaim-authorization record and `GcSemanticState::Quarantined` only. Every object encoder, dedupe lookup, prepared receipt, command validator, and root publisher rejects a new retaining edge or realization selection to a quarantined identity. All floors retain the family, every generation, and all cancellation/abandonment/status receipts through aggregate terminality.

After each quarantine is visibly certified, that group's Protocol plane uses the common physical machine defined for Local GC. Neither Shard nor Meta quarantine apply creates a Protocol Requested record, and no maintenance transition mutates Semantic quarantine. `PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence` binds role/group, authorization/quarantine/family/all-generation commitments, complete receipt bijection, pre/post physical-root set, configuration/fence/slot ancestry, and terminal kind. A role-specific `GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec` then imports that evidence into Semantic state. Only after the resulting Semantic disposition is applied, role-validly published, and audit-visible may a signer-locked certificate attempt create one of four noninterchangeable acks: `MetaGcCompletedAck`, `ShardGcCompletedAck`, `MetaGcCancelledAck`, or `ShardGcCancelledAck`. Completed acks bind reclaimed inventory/post-physical roots; cancelled acks bind global cancellation authority, exact participant no-start evidence, unchanged/no-reclaim physical-root proof, and cancelled-disposition visibility. No apply handler emits an ack or certificate directly.

Distributed cancellation is a fenced protocol, never an independent per-group choice. Global coordination is monotone `Executing -> CancellationPreparing -> CancellationAuthorized|CompletionRequired -> CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart|Completed`. `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareSpec {authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalGcAuthorizationRecord>,expected_global_gc_state:Executing,cancellation_nonce,exact_required_participant_commitment,expected_latest_progress_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` creates `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareRecord`; only after that record is applied and audit-visible may the quorum create `GlobalGcCancellationPrepareCertificate`.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-08, FG-INV-13, FG-INV-14, FG-INV-16, and FG-INV-20. Consumes root trust, current/joint/final configurations, payload availability, remote grant universal dispatch, W11 membership/GC, and exact authority projections. W12 registration/prepare/recovery/topology/backup consume these types.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows cover ConsensusDomain, RemoteObjectIdentity, root trust, configuration evidence/anchors, certified remote refs, grant specs/records/evidence, consumer roots, release requests/evidence/tombstones/acks, retirement plans, adoption and floors.
- Golden/unit tests freeze trust transcripts, signature domains, grant targets/closures, configuration succession, reference tags, six-stage transition and nonretaining terminal summaries.
- Property/model tests prove no raw cross-group edge, trust rooted externally then successor-verified, grant before use, retention until both sides finish, no early old-config retirement, and one complete target/grant bijection.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects scalar-only group IDs, embedded self-selected keys, wrong authority/consumer/config/topology, stale grant generation, closure substitution, missing release stage, cross-role refs, and current signatures without predecessor trust.
- Partition/crash/DPOR E2E rotates Shard configurations while prepares/results/backups/replay hold remote objects, loses every message/leader, and proves exact continued availability then six-stage release and GC eligibility.
- JSONL emits {event_version,authority_domain,consumer_domain,remote_object_digest?,configuration_digest,trust_generation,grant_id,grant_generation,closure_digest,release_stage,request_id?,consumer_evidence_digest?,authority_tombstone_digest?,ack_digest?,floor_state,recovery_action,replay_command}; no remote payload/protected identity leakage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: raw ObjectIds, signature-only trust, current-member self-rooting, lease timeout as release, one-sided tombstones, and topology removal before grant retirement. Missing evidence retains data conservatively.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1392-1408 and 1800-1810.
