## Authoritative post-d96bf0f contract reconciliation

Meta authority projection is a registered portable trust/export leaf. This Bead owns certified-remote retention, agreement, and export traversal for its exact identity and transcript.

The following current plan text is authoritative and supersedes any older rendering in this Bead:

`MetaAuthorityBindingProjection` is the independently addressable portable logical object with registered `ObjectKind=0x0108`, schema major 1, role predicate Meta, and `canonical_max_size_bytes=65536`: `{source_authority_binding_public_commitment,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,tenant_commitment,principal_commitment,non_widenable_authority_ceiling_commitment,purpose_class,exact_clipped_operation_read_write_disclosure_and_resource_scopes,security_policy_epoch,revocation_index,source_meta_prefix,source_configuration_and_retention_grant_evidence,projection_digest:BodyDigest<MetaAuthorityBindingProjection>,signatures}`. Its body transcript is `BLAKE3("fgdb:body:meta-authority-binding-projection:v1" || canonical(schema_major=1, every field through source_configuration_and_retention_grant_evidence))`; the field row explicitly excludes `projection_digest` and `signatures`, and the signatures cover that digest plus the exact authority/configuration domain. Its logical-kind row, field rows, encoder/decoder, retention owner, export leaf, and golden/fuzz corpus are mandatory before status advances from reserved. `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` is the shard-local exact `{security_state_projection:ShardSecurityStateProjection,certified_source_authority_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaAuthorityBindingProjection>,source_authority_binding_public_commitment,tenant_commitment,principal_commitment,non_widenable_authority_ceiling_commitment,purpose_class,exact_clipped_operation_read_write_disclosure_and_resource_scopes,source_meta_prefix,source_configuration_and_grant_commitment,projection_digest}`. The certified source projection and local security projection must agree on namespace/incarnation/service epoch/policy/revocation and cannot be recombined from different Meta prefixes or principals. `AuthorityBindingFor<Role>` is the generated closed role family `Local{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>}|Meta{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>}|Shard{projection:ShardAuthorityBindingProjection}`; exactly one arm is inhabitable for a given containing role. Every durable field set marked `authority_bearing=true` must contain exactly one inline complete binding, one `AuthorityBoundHeader`, or—only for a shard consumer—the exact `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection`; scalar epochs/digests, a permit reference alone, the narrower `ShardSecurityStateProjection`, or an opaque “authority projection digest” alone fail G0. Public wire values cannot carry local refs, so their signed/MACed header contains `security_state_binding_public_commitment`; the durable issuance/replay record strongly retains the complete AuthorityBindingRecord and proves that commitment. The generated matrix covers permits, admissions/releases, audit-requirement decisions, prepared/final owners, intents/batches/effects, constraints/resources/escrow, derived identities/builds, plans/replay, result/cursor/output promises, DP, backup/export, descriptor views, cache keys, dispatch attempts, and every command authorization. Every Local/Meta outer command carries exactly one complete `AuthorityBoundHeader` that byte-matches its authorization object and frozen reservation; a Shard command instead carries the exact `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` named by its imported authorization. Equal-scalar/different-root/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/role/purpose substitution is a mandatory negative fixture.

Implementation, tests, retained evidence, and public-surface behavior must use this exact corrected contract. No Markdown plan edit is required or authorized by this reconciliation.

title: Implement exact W12 role-transition, Genesis, activation, and RetiredLocal formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze and implement the exact W12 role-transition, fresh Sharded Genesis, Local activation, RetiredLocal, and role-specific state/root/bootstrap phase formats. This is the schema prerequisite for conversion; it does not permit W12 implementation to reuse Local durable transaction objects or invent compact phase aliases.

## Why
Posture transition changes which consensus domain owns semantic authority. Every hidden, sealed, reopened, acknowledged, complete, retired, and reclaimable phase must be durable and role-tagged so crashes cannot serve two postures or reclaim the Local source early.

## Design — exact normative contract
`RoleTransitionActivationState` is the closed role union `Meta{migration_nonce,transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,continuity_reservation_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,target_service_visibility_epoch,phase:ProjectionPreparedHidden{activation_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|ServicePrepareApplied{prepare_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|FinalizedPendingIndependentReopen{finalize_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_state:Unsealed|Sealed{seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Meta>>}}|MetaReopenedAwaitingShardAcks{reopen_confirm_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Meta>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionIndependentReopenProof<Meta>>}|Complete{completion_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_release_state}}|Shard{migration_nonce,transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,shard_id,continuity_reservation_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionContinuityReservationReceipt>,target_service_visibility_epoch,phase:ProjectionPreparedHidden{install_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}|OpenedPendingIndependentReopen{open_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_state:Unsealed|Sealed{seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Shard>>}}|ShardOperationalAwaitingMetaCompletion{reopen_confirm_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionPromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionIndependentReopenProof<Shard>>}|Complete{completion_apply_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef,seal_release_state}}`. This exact schema supersedes any earlier compact navigation rendering. The state object, reached by the payload's existing strong field, is the canonical owner of role-transition seals/proofs; `None` is legal only outside a role transition. Post-publication visibility/state certificates live in the certificate ledger and are supplied separately to later pin-release/service consumers as `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>`; the Complete root cannot embed the certificate that certifies itself. Generated construction-DAG negatives reject that future back-edge. Generated phase/bootstrap/admission rows require `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` through prepare, `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen` through Unsealed/Sealed, `Operational` plus an awaiting phase after reopen, and ordinary service only in `Complete`.
`InitialProtocolStateRecipe<Role>` is the generated pre-order contract that makes that requirement executable: `{role_and_group,target_incarnation,target_service_visibility_epoch,source_kind:FreshGenesis|Restore|RoleTransition|Takeover,source_recovery_or_transition_projection_commitment?,semantic_applied_and_visible_endpoint_recipes,inherited_or_empty_audit_queue_recipe:LocalMetaOnly{pipeline_recipe,visible_outcome_index_recipe,external_continuity_recipe}|ShardInapplicable,independent_result_cursor_artifact_error_delivery_recipes,protocol_resource_escrow_recipes,capability_invalidation_suspension_or_transfer_recipes,physical_recovery_progress_recipe,security_barrier_recipe,complete_protocol_slot_bitmap,cross_plane_conservation_commitment,body_digest}`. Every active `protocol_state_fields.toml` slot appears exactly once; a source-kind/role matrix rejects missing, extra, or semantically impossible recipes. Pending/released output recipes retain bytes, policy, escrow, and release evidence but no target-era lease or send capability. Takeover preserves the exact prior Protocol state through its adoption record rather than reconstructing it from semantic state.

The universal first-manifest construction order is `semantic payload/command record/state root -> role-valid Protocol state from InitialProtocolStateRecipe -> PreparedOwnership root -> Consensus/Raft hard state, log, snapshot, configuration, and state root -> create/authenticate/fsync generation-lease inode and fsync its directory -> construct PhysicalGenerationLeaseDescriptor -> RootManifest -> RootSlot`. Every later publication uses the same lease-inode-before-manifest tail. A first-manifest builder may hold body recipes for later objects but no earlier object contains a future ObjectId. `PendingCreationGuard`, `PendingRestoreCreationGuard`, and `PendingRoleTransitionCreationGuard` each carry the exact role-valid Semantic/Protocol/Prepared/Consensus/bootstrap/physical-lease recipe commitments and complete slot bitmaps; their encoders accept only the registered source-kind closure. Genesis creates an empty Local/Meta audit pipeline with applied=visible and no barrier, or a Shard Protocol state with its genesis Meta projection. Restore reconstructs the projection's applied/visible split and pending queue. Role transition creates Meta `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` and Shard `RoleTransitionPreparedHidden` Protocol arms; migrated owners are suspended or transferred without E-era send authority. Mandatory closure, backup/restore, checkpoint/snapshot, GC, format, role-transition, and orphan-cleanup walkers include the exact lease descriptor/inode proof class. Negative first-manifest fixtures delete, duplicate, substitute, or cross-role every plane root and lease field and must fail before write mode or service exposure.

A RetiredLocal manifest is authenticated and recoverable only as a compact terminal proof posture: ordinary open, resurrection, Raft participation, receipt issuance, and service advertisement fail before any logical object is exposed. A `MetadataTreeBootstrap` embeds `{tree_kind,tree_generation,tree_key_id,root_oid,cipher_descriptor,ciphertext_id,encoding_descriptor,placement_records,tree_key_opener,closure_digest}`; generated exact role-specific bootstrap unions replace erased lists. Each authenticated internal edge carries the exact child identity/cipher/encoding/placement/wrap/AAD fields defined in `durable_fields.toml`; parent ObjectId is absent because it is not known before parent encoding. Tree-root bootstrap edges are strong, ordinary locator entries are nonretaining, and semantic/protocol/prepared/terminal-proof marking decides liveness before realization resolution. RetiredLocal trees may locate only their compact proof closure. The predecessor is weak, and independently hashed markers use authenticated nonretaining subobject locators.

The preceding role union is the sole authoritative RootManifest schema; the obsolete `logical_state_root_oid`, `global_state_root_oid`, direct `audit_visibility_pipeline_ref`, and duplicate visible-root fields are unregistered. Generated field fixtures require exactly one applied semantic root and one role-valid protocol root, with the latter's authenticated pipeline selecting the visible root.

`MetadataTreeBootstrap.closure_digest` commits only the already-built metadata-tree closure. That same generation MUST NOT contain any entry—strong, weak, or physical-locator—for its current `RootManifest`, `RootSlot`, or bootstrap bytes; the slot bootstrap is the current manifest's sole opener. This is a construction rule in the generated DAG checker, not merely a GC classification.

Each shard orders `ShardRoleTransitionCompletionApplySpec` under that certificate, changes its phase to `Complete`, RootSlot-publishes the result, and only after `ShardStatePublicationCertificate` may direct shard service or Meta routing target it. Meta admits/routs only after its own completion visibility certificate. Crash/DPOR tests cut and race prepare, certificate creation, receipt, finalize/open, seal/pin publication, fresh reopen, confirmations, all acknowledgements, completion, projection, and pin release; no hidden or awaiting phase serves traffic.

Old-E sessions, frames, permits, authorization/result leases, and durable capabilities fail before routing or disclosure once RoleTransitionReserved is published, but retained promises cannot be stranded. title: Build W12 simulation and independent global protocol oracles
description:
## What & scope
Build and execute the dedicated post-1.0 W12 deterministic simulation, independent global serializability/history oracle, and canonical Meta/Shard protocol-state oracles. This is the only bead that may turn the generic checker schemas for sharding into live W12 evidence. It consumes the completed W12 implementation and does not back-propagate W12 obligations into G1-G4.

## Why
W12 changes the semantic authority from Local to Meta, introduces role-tagged logs and roots, global registration/statement/workspace machines, cross-shard observations, distributed prepare/certification/constraints/DP/audit, remote strong-reference trust, and Meta-coordinated GC/backup/restore/topology. Local strict-serializability and protocol campaigns cannot validate those state spaces by inheritance. The plan explicitly requires separate bounded W12 models and an independent global SCC/history oracle.

## Normative oracle inventory
- Independent global dependency oracle reconstructs every local, cross-shard, positive, negative, gap, path, read-only, statement-workspace, and batch `wr`/`ww`/`rw` edge from traces. It uses a deliberately independent SCC implementation; production fnx algorithms are secondary differentials only.
- The registered virtual-serial batch-certification law is checked for every generated batch. Same-basis two-writer, rw-cycle, aggregate-overflow, same-head, constraint-owner, and escrow cases are evaluated both batched and in canonical submission-order serial replay; admitted set, abort set, terminal evidence, committed history, state digest, constraint outcome, and resource/escrow conservation must be identical.
- Deterministic constraint-owner and reservation results are compared with the single-threaded reference semantics; complete effect-only authorization bases must produce one union-wide decision, while terminal audit remains a distinct signer-locked event/resolution.
- Canonical-map state machines cover Sharded Genesis; Local freeze/seal/activation/authority transfer/RetiredLocal retirement; begin reservation and Attempt First/Successor/idempotent/burn; ticket claim and workspace-zero rooting; statement registration/routing/publication/delivery; overlay/witness/effect roots; read close/cancel; prepare/availability/certification; Meta applied-hidden audit candidate, external batch CAS/mirror/visibility; decision publication, shard decision/projection/post-visibility acknowledgement/global-delta publication; TerminalPending/Ready and compaction; remote grant/trust/release; distributed key, GC, backup, restore, and topology transitions.
- Cross-role/domain/incarnation/configuration/security projection substitutions, observation before mirror/open, stale service epochs, ambient remote evidence, old ObjectId reinterpretation, shard-local semantic bypass, premature reclaim/release, and incorrect Local/W12 coexistence are mandatory fail-closed negatives.
- Every role-tagged durable command, root, floor, snapshot, and payload closure is checked against generated registries; every compiled-and-negotiated subordinate W12 clause of FG-INV-01-20 must name a live oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover every canonical transition, global-edge constructor, batch virtual-serial replay step, rejection class, and role/authority validator. Mutation tests demonstrate that each oracle fires on a seeded defect.
- Property tests generate cross-shard histories and protocol traces; after every step optimized and canonical state, resource ownership, retention floors, public outcome bytes, and global dependency edges agree. Shrinking preserves the first semantic divergence.
- Simulation campaigns exercise partitions, leader changes, Meta/shard joint reconfiguration, conflicting prepares, same-basis batches, statement workspace overlays, visibility lag, cancellation, remote release, key loss, GC quarantine, restore hidden/service/open, and topology epoch straddles with all oracles attached.
- E2E: boot Meta plus at least three shards; perform cross-shard read/write and read-only transactions, multiple statements with overlays, a same-basis batch containing an injected cycle, constraint and escrow operations, DP fragments, branch operation, protected result resume, and topology movement while injecting a partition and leader loss. Assert exactly the reference/virtual-serial admitted and abort sets, no committed cycle, one Meta order, complete global delta, legal terminal outcomes, and no unauthorized/hidden observation.
- Gate coverage audit rejects `sharding=true` if any activated W12 clause lacks a checker, negative test, replay artifact, or complete structured-log ancestry.

## Detailed structured diagnostics
Every unit/property/simulation/E2E verdict emits JSONL `{run_id,scenario_id,phase:"W12",seed,model_bounds,role,group_id,configuration_epoch,topology_epoch,service_visibility_epoch,global_logical_txn_hlc_meta_index,shard_applied_visible_audit_positions,attempt_generation_statement_workspace_ids,certification_basis,batch_id,candidate_submission_order,dependency_edges,admitted_set,abort_set,constraint_owner,escrow_before_after,remote_grant_key_gc_backup_restore_topology_ids,oracle_id,clause_id,expected,actual,verdict}`. On failure, emit the complete §15.1 secret-redacted artifact, minimized history/schedule, first divergent transition/edge, canonical and optimized digests, and executable replay command. CI executes sampled replay commands and regenerates the W12 verification report from JSONL only.

## Claim discipline
Oracle failures are correctness defects. A passing bounded campaign is falsification evidence; DPOR completion is reported only for its declared model/bounds. Batch-equivalence results apply only to the registered submission-order law. No result from this task is reusable as G4 evidence and no G4 result substitutes for this task.

## Provenance
Plan §14.6, §15.1-§15.5, §19 Gate W12; Appendix F W12 clauses and the virtual-serial batch-certification law.

title: Implement Meta statement registration/publication, workspace generations, and read close
description:
## What & scope
The per-statement Meta machine for explicit W12 transactions: statement registration, shard workspace deltas, Meta publication, statement abort, cancellation, and the read-only terminal `GlobalReadCloseSpec`. Split out of `w12-registration-snapshot` for size.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents run multi-statement transactions with read-your-own-writes across shards without exposing unaudited or SSI-untracked observations. B3/B5: every statement is one registered, classified, deterministic unit whose publication atomically advances witness/effect state.

## Design — normative detail
`GlobalStatementRegistrationSpec` requires attempt Active, checked next `statement_seq`, statement idempotency key, `CanonicalStatementClassification` within the attempt ceiling, canonical statement + parameter digests, requested answer contract, expected prior statement frontier + workspace generation, byte-identical `TransactionErrorPolicy`, and a distinct statement ticket (`StatementAuditAdmission::NotRequired|PendingUnclaimed`); apply claims the ticket, creates `GlobalStatementRegistration`, inserts `Open`. Exact retry returns the record; any drift fails. No shard read/effect precedes visible registration.

Shards produce immutable `ShardStatementWorkspaceDelta` (authority projection, classification CRSR, routed intent-batch projection, base snapshot root, ordered prior-overlay commitment, witnesses, `statement_effect:Write{delta_ref:StrongRef<LogicalDeltaTemplate>}|ReadOnly{no_write_effect_proof_ref}`, result fragment digest, successor overlay root, deterministic recompute digest) certified by `ShardStatementWorkspaceCertificate`. Meta folds them into `GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration` (monotone potential join, same-or-proved-narrower authority, cumulative effect and read-witness roots); generation zero is the canonical empty overlay.

`GlobalStatementPublicationSpec` byte-matches published-output tag/manifest owner, statement class, exact prior/successor workspace, routed shard set, read witnesses, `DistributedSerializationCertificate` for the statement, and audit owner; its event/resolution commits the result and workspace/effect transition WITHOUT resolving the operation ticket. `StatementPublishedOutput = NoResult{no_result_proof_ref,...}|Buffered{manifest_ref:StrongRef<BufferedResultManifest>,initial_retention_recipe}`; Buffered results are atomically detached (`AtomicProtocolDetach`) into the independent retention machine — semantic state keeps only `BufferedDetached{delivery_id,result_digest,detachment_commitment}`. The same RootManifest generation constructs the succeeding `GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord::Registered` with all frontiers advanced. `GlobalStatementAbortSpec` resolves the statement ticket, marks `Failed|Abandoned`, leaves workspace/cumulative witnesses unchanged; the pinned error policy uniquely determines `continuation_action:ContinueAttempt|AbortAttempt`. `GlobalAttemptCancelSpec` (pre-admission only) requires every Open statement terminal, every published result detached with a `ResultDeliveryDispositionProof`, workspace release evidence, a typed `TerminalAbortAuthority<Meta>`, and installs `Aborted` via `AppliedAbortRef::MetaControl` — client death/timeout/suspicion is never a transition.

`GlobalReadCloseSpec` is the read-only terminal: `AutocommitResult` (routing cert, global read authorization decision, buffered manifest, retention recipe) or `ExplicitClose` (complete publication/detachment chain, zero-cumulative-write-effect proof, no-open-statement proof); both rerun serialization over cumulative witnesses, resolve the operation ticket, install `ReadClosed`, and advance `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq`/HLC but not `GlobalCommitSeq`. Read close is a Global control (gate). Write-then-read executes against the certified workspace overlay, preserving RYW; ACK latency is outside transaction correctness.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-05: each statement publication atomically extends the cumulative witness/conflict state; ReadWrite admission and ReadOnly close name the exact statement/delivery/workspace frontier and independently recheck the complete graph. FG-INV-15: result owners are generated noninterchangeable arms of the state-shaped independent-retention machine; QUERY_CANCEL/Drop/disconnect cannot release them. FG-INV-20: no result streams before its distinct statement/read-close audit visibility release and typed delivery lease (gate text). Invariant-class throughout; statement latency is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes registrations from `w12-registration-snapshot`; publishes into `w12-prepare` (admission names statement/delivery frontiers) and `w12-certification` (cumulative witnesses); delivery machinery shape shared with `w10-result-machines`; audit release from `w9-audit-release`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "every explicit statement is Meta-registered against one sequence/key/class/error policy and workspace generation; every routed shard reads registered snapshot plus the exact certified overlay for every previously touched shard; Meta publication atomically advances statement/delivery/workspace/witness/effect state and constructs the successor Registered outcome... Cancellation proves open-statement, result, overlay, and remote-grant discharge. Read close is a Global control." Tests: statement retry idempotency; sequence-gap and workspace-drift rejection; false empty-overlay proof rejection; publication crash before/after AtomicProtocolDetach; cancel racing publication; read-close vs commit-seq assertion (no commit-seq movement). E2E: multi-statement RYW script across 3 shards with mid-transaction shard leader failover; log every workspace generation and assert extensional equality with a single-shard replay.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: per-statement Meta ordering costs a control command per statement (priced; batched under the certification law where legal). Rejected: shard-local statement visibility; savepoint/partial-rollback semantics (rejected at BEGIN); resolving the operation ticket per statement.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 2 (1083); App A 1714-1732, 1756-1760; §19:1350.

title: Implement three-phase topology movement (copy/cutover/retire) and the vertex-cut option
description:
## What & scope
Repartitioning: source-range base partitioning, optional hub vertex-cut, and the three separately ordered evidence-complete movement commands `TopologyCopyBeginSpec` / `TopologyCutoverSpec` / `TopologyRetireOldSpec` with their typed evidence objects.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: no transaction ever straddles topology epochs; ownership changes are single Meta-ordered facts with exhaustive attempt closure — no ambient evidence, no racing writers. B2: source-range partitioning keeps Strata locality; the hub vertex-cut arm addresses supernode fan-out with a single canonical edge owner. Rejected: consistent-hash implicit movement, apply-time evidence discovery ("apply records only evidence already named by its command").

## Design — normative detail
**Partitioning.** Source-range partitioning is the base edge-cut/vertex-owner scheme; optional hub vertex-cut uses separately versioned replicated-vertex metadata and a single canonical edge owner. Allocation ranges are meta-fenced before use.

**Phase 1 — copy.** `TopologyCopyBeginSpec {move_id,old/new_joint/new_final_topology_refs,affected_ranges,copy_basis_global_prefix,old/new_shard_configuration_refs,source_checkpoint_certificate_refs[CRSR<ShardCheckpointCertificate>],transfer_plan_ref:StrongRef<TopologyTransferPlan>,expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs,terminal_audit_gate}` fixes copy basis `F`, source checkpoint/suffix inventory, joint configurations, and the transfer plan while the old owner remains sole write authority. `TopologyTransferPlan` carries affected ranges, copy basis, sorted source checkpoint identities, object-and-suffix inventory, destination assignments, copy crypto profile, completion predicate; destinations answer with `TopologyTransferAck` (received inventory digest, applied-through prefix, destination checkpoint certificate).

**Phase 2 — cutover.** `TopologyCutoverSpec` names canonical transfer/catch-up certificates plus the exact active-attempt closure at prefix `S` via `TopologyAttemptClosureProof`: sorted, exhaustive-against-old-epoch-indexes evidence per `(global_txn_id,registration_generation)` — `Terminal{outcome_ref,published_decision_ref?,old_owner_ack_refs}` or `AbortForPostCutoverRetry{abort_outcome_ref,published_abort_ref,old_owner_release_ack_refs,retry_request_nonce,intent_commitment,old_to_future_attempt_mapping_commitment}`. It stops old-epoch admission and switches ownership only at `S+1`. No new-epoch registration can preexist cutover; a registration racing the cutover basis is either included/terminalized under the old epoch or rejected for later retry, and only a later meta command after ownership switches may create the new generation linked to the recorded retry intent.

**Phase 3 — retire.** `TopologyRetireOldSpec` names every new-owner/meta/backup/key/retention acknowledgement and the final `TopologyRetirementFloor` (old-owner inventory, remaining certified-remote obligations, backup/key/retention/prepare floors, external receipts, required Meta and shard ack sets); `TopologyRetirementAck` uses `LocalMeta` (Meta only) or `RemoteMeta` CRSR arms. Old bytes/keys cannot retire before this third command; source bytes/keys remain live through final retirement and its two-sided remote floors. Each apply constructs one `TopologyTransitionRecord {move_id,phase:CopyInProgress|CutoverCommitted|OldOwnersRetired,command_ref,phase_predecessor,copy_basis_global_prefix,cutover_global_prefix?,affected_ranges,evidence_commitment,resulting_topology_ref,assigned_global_logical_command_seq}`; completed moves do not form an unbounded strong chain. Shards consume movement via `ShardTopologyCopyApplySpec` (copy record + transfer plan + source checkpoints CRSRs, received inventory digest, through-prefix). Topology-changing controls are batch singletons under the certification law.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: no dual write authority — old owner is sole authority through copy; ownership switches atomically at `S+1`. FG-INV-11: allocation epochs/spent commitments survive topology movement with no alias/overlap/reuse. FG-INV-14: topology retirement retains every in-flight family/evidence until aggregate terminality; premature byte/key retirement impossible before phase 3. Gate text: "Three-phase topology copy/cutover/retire proves no ambient evidence, straddled epoch, or premature byte/key retirement." Movement throughput/pause metrics are benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes decision/ack machinery from `w12-decision-visibility`, retirement predicates and six-stage release from `w12-recovery-gc`, configuration ladders from `w11-membership-config`, checkpoint certificates from `w2-retention-checkpoints`. Constrains `w12-escrow-dp-alloc` (grants/reservations retained across moves) and `w12-backup-restore` (barrier interaction).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Tests: crash at every phase boundary and inside copy (donor loss mid-transfer); attempt racing cutover lands exactly once (old-epoch terminal or typed retry — never both); straddled-epoch injection unrepresentable; retire blocked by one missing shard ack; vertex-cut: replicated-vertex metadata version skew rejected, single canonical edge owner enforced under concurrent edge writes; checkpoint-interval sufficiency (`queryable interval contains P`) verified for snapshot routing during moves. E2E: move a hot range under sustained write load across 3 shards; log per-phase `TopologyTransitionRecord`s, old/new admission counts around `S`/`S+1`; assert zero straddled transactions and byte-identical range digests source-vs-destination at `F` plus replayed suffix.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: exhaustive attempt-closure proofs delay cutover under heavy load (bounded by registration-generation range). Rejected: live migration with dual-write windows; hash-ring implicit ownership; retiring source data on content-proof alone.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet "Topology and repartitioning" (1095); App A 1868, 1880-1882; §19:1354.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement exact W12 transaction, statement, result, outcome, and public-status formats
description:
## What & scope
Implement exact W12 begin/registration/statement/workspace/result/outcome/public-status/read-close/terminal-completion formats and ownership transitions. This task freezes the durable contract shared by the W12 registration, statement, prepare, decision and Fabric delivery implementations without sharing Local object schemas.

## Why
Explicit multi-statement transactions need byte-stable lost-response and restart behavior. Begin reservation must exist before response, registration/statement publication must atomically root workspace and audit ownership, and public status must remain identical across detailed/compacted states without exposing internal TerminalPending descriptors.

## Design — exact normative contract
The sole permit schemas are Appendix A's generic `AuthorityPermitRef<Role>`, `MutationPermitReadProjection<Role>`, `ReadCapablePermitRef<Role>`, and `ImportedReadCapablePermitEvidence`; no unparameterized duplicate permit union or digest-only mutation-read projection exists here. `AuditTicketOwner` is the closed tag `Operation{global_txn_id,registration_generation,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Statement{global_txn_id,registration_generation,statement_seq,statement_idempotency_key,statement_request_basis_commitment}|Control{control_request_identity}`. `AuditResolutionOrigin` is `Unclaimed{admission_record_ref:AppliedControlRef,request_basis_commitment,terminal_class:DeniedBeforeClaim|AbandonedBeforeClaim}|Claimed{claim_record_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketClaimRecord>,owner:AuditTicketOwner,request_basis_commitment}`.

The Semantic `AuditTicketIndexValue` is the monotone state machine `PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,admission_record_ref:AppliedControlRef,request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketClaimRecord>,owner:AuditTicketOwner,request_basis_commitment}|TerminalPrepared{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,origin:AuditResolutionOrigin,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>,terminal_gate_commitment,candidate_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,pipeline_order}`. Only `PendingUnclaimed -> Claimed -> TerminalPrepared(origin=Claimed)` or the no-effect pre-claim `PendingUnclaimed -> TerminalPrepared(origin=Unclaimed)` is legal. The Semantic index never contains an external CAS receipt or visibility result because those facts arise later in the Protocol plane. `VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex` is the sole join from a TerminalPrepared ticket/candidate to its exact external batch receipt/member ordinal, `AuditOutcomeRecord`, and releasing maintenance transition. Byte-identical retry returns the same value; mismatched admission/claim/owner/origin fails, and a ticket can never be claimed by two attempts/statements, prepared for another owner, or released by a nonmatching Protocol outcome.

`OperationAuditAdmission` is `NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,ticket_admission_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketClaimRecord>,owner:{global_txn_id,registration_generation},operation_request_basis_commitment}`. `GlobalAttemptRegistrationSpec` accepts only `NotRequired` or `PendingUnclaimed`; registration apply atomically transforms the latter into `Claimed` and creates `AuditTicketClaimRecord {ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:AuditTicketOwner::Operation,request_basis_commitment,claiming_control_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,claimed_at_global_logical_command_seq}` before constructing the registration/payload. Every later read, statement publication, admission, cancel, commit, abort, or read-close must carry or derive the exact Claimed value from that registration. The claim remains unresolved until the one terminal attempt read-close/commit/abort event. A pre-registration denial or abandoned BEGIN is one semantic mutation—creation of the capability-visible NeverRegistered outcome—so only `GlobalBeginTerminalSpec` may resolve its exact `PendingUnclaimed` ticket and publish that candidate; `AuditTerminalSpec` remains reserved for terminal paths that create no other durable semantic mutation.

Registration and prepare admission are distinct lifecycle-scaffolding rows. A `GlobalBeginReservationSpec`, `GlobalAttemptRegistrationSpec`, or `AuditTerminalFreezeSpec::Arm` exists before the operation claim it may atomically create, so its wrapper is exactly `NotRequired{evidence:LifecycleScaffolding{decision_ref,registered_scaffolding_spec_tag,scaffolding_body_digest,parent_operation_claim_commitment?,compatibility_row_id}}`; the decision is prebuilt against the pending-ticket/request basis and the registered atomic-claim recipe and never points to the future claim. After registration has produced a claim, `GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec` may use `NotRequired{evidence:CoveredByParentClaim{claim_ref,coverage_rule_id=LifecycleScaffoldingCoveredByOperationTicket,covered_body_digest}}`. Neither form resolves the operation ticket. The typed evidence byte-matches operation tag, pending admission or claim owner, request/body basis, audit epoch, policy, and revocation state. Arm/claim substitution and any pre-order reference to a future claim are G0-invalid and have negative DAG fixtures. Nonterminal statement results use distinct statement tickets below, never the operation ticket. A completeness profile that requires separate registration/admission events supplies distinct tickets and registered lifecycle tags; negotiation fails rather than overloading a claimed ticket.

BEGIN has its own durable, idempotent lineage before an attempt exists. `TxnOutcomeCapabilityFields` is the shared exact inline value `{header:DurableCapabilityHeader{capability_kind=TxnOutcome},body:{request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,scoped_request_idempotency_key_digest,txn_token,outcome_capability_key},mac}`; the body key is pre-minted, every header/body field and MAC byte exists before ordering, and `capability_commitment` is the domain-separated digest of those canonical bytes. `GlobalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved{reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundDetailed{registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>,reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredDetailed{terminal_record_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredTerminalRecord>,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,audit_terminal_commitment}|NeverRegisteredCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptSummaryRoot>,summary_leaf_key_digest,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|ExpiredTombstone{scoped_key_digest,txn_token_digest,capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}`. `GlobalBeginReservationSpec` is the sequence-neutral pre-order body `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,scoped_begin_idempotency_key,canonical_begin_request_digest,operation_class,isolation,transaction_error_policy,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,operation_audit_admission:OperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,expected_begin_index_absence_proof,staging_resource_reservation_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The header is the sole namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation source. The replay object's capability header/body/request kind/key/domain/authority/profile/window, resource reservation, and audit admission byte-match it; no command trusts a duplicate inline encoding. Apply creates `GlobalBeginReservationRecord {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,source_spec_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationSpec>,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,canonical_begin_request_digest,txn_token,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,capability_commitment,operation_audit_admission:OperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,reserved_at_global_prefix,staging_generation}` and atomically installs `Reserved` plus `GlobalOutcomeDirectoryValue::BeginStaging` with that same replay ref; only then may Fabric emit `BEGIN_ACCEPTED`. A byte-identical retry returns the replay object's identical canonical capability bytes even after key rotation, while a same key with any request, admission, authority, epoch, profile/window, or policy drift fails. Verifier key and accepted time profile remain rooted through the capability lookup/expiry floor.

Registration must consume the exact reservation and atomically change `Reserved -> BoundDetailed`; no later command may return it to staging. `BeginRegionClosedReceipt` is the authenticated runtime record `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_binding,session_region_id,reservation_identity,canonical_request_digest,observed_region_close_generation,no_registration_worker_or_acceptance_response_obligation_proof_digest,issuer_id,key_epoch,signature}` and is distinct from result-delivery `SessionRegionCloseReceipt`. `BeginTerminalEvidence` is the role-checked closed union `Denied{authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord>,stable_denial_class}|AuthenticatedAbandon{request_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedBeginAbandonRequest>,request_idempotency_key}|RegionClosed{receipt_ref:StrongRef<BeginRegionClosedReceipt>}|Superseded{request_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedBeginSupersedeRequest>,request_idempotency_key,new_request_commitment}`. Its generated compatibility table maps exactly Denied->DeniedBeforeRegistration, RegionClosed->BeginDisconnected, AuthenticatedAbandon->AbandonedStaging, and Superseded->SupersededRetry; every arm binds the same session/principal/authority/reservation/request and includes a typed no-registration/effect/response proof. Time passage, socket suspicion, process death, or a result-delivery receipt inhabits no arm.

`LocalBeginTerminalSpec` is `{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,expected_index_value:Reserved,evidence:BeginTerminalEvidence::Local,internal_reason_class,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,staging_resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>],terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<LocalBeginTerminal>,terminal_audit_gate}`. `GlobalBeginTerminalSpec` is `{reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,expected_index_value:Reserved,evidence:BeginTerminalEvidence::Meta,internal_reason_class,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,operation_audit_admission:OperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,staging_resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>],terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<MetaBeginTerminal>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Admission, evidence, internal reason, bundle subject/domain/request, and freeze must byte-match the reservation exactly. Apply resolves that exact ticket when present and creates the role's compactable NeverRegistered record; Meta creates `NeverRegisteredTerminalRecord {reservation_identity:WeakDigest,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,capability_commitment,internal_reason_class,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,terminal_global_prefix,audit_terminal_commitment}` plus detailed index/directory entries carrying that same bundle. Deterministic apply never mints a public handle, maps a reason, signs a disclosure receipt, or recomputes response bytes. Neither role creates an attempt, attempt family/key, conflict, prepared, statement, or shard entry. `NeverRegisteredFloorSpec` later rewrites Meta Detailed to Compacted after proving that this reservation never bound or escaped and copies the bundle's exact frozen public bytes into the authenticated summary leaf; both compacted indexes retain the same bundle ref. `GlobalOutcomeExpirySpec` then atomically rewrites both outcome-directory and begin-index leaves to permanent capability/key `ExpiredTombstone` only with matching `TimeValidationEvidence::Expired`, verifier/profile floors, terminal proof, and retention cut; only expiry drops the bundle/replay edges. Neither step requires the index being rewritten to be absent, and neither fabricates an attempt identity.

`AttemptFamilyState` is the authenticated Meta map value `{global_txn_id,latest_generation,latest_state:Active{registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>}|PrepareAdmitted{outcome_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>}|Terminal{outcome_or_summary_ref:StrongRef},active_generation:None|Some{generation},latest_token_digest,successor_eligibility_floor}`. NeverRegistered is exclusively a terminal begin-key/outcome-directory state and never creates or advances an attempt family. `TransactionErrorPolicy` is the closed v1 union `AbortTransactionOnStatementError|ContinueOnDeclaredRecoverable{recoverable_error_class_table_oid}`; unsupported savepoint/partial-rollback semantics are rejected at BEGIN. `GlobalAttemptRegistrationSpec` is sequence-neutral `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,global_txn_id,begin_idempotency_key,begin_binding:BindReserved{reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,expected_index_value:Reserved}|IdempotentBound{reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,existing_registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>,expected_index_value:BoundDetailed},txn_token,txn_operation_ceiling:TxnOperationCeiling,autocommit_classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>?,requested_snapshot_selector,minimum_acceptable_snapshot,authority_permit_ref:AuthorityPermitRef<Meta>,transaction_error_policy:TransactionErrorPolicy,initial_workspace_body_recipe,operation_audit_admission:OperationAuditAdmission::NotRequired|PendingUnclaimed,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,registration_generation,expected_attempt_family_state:First{authenticated_absence_proof}|Successor{prior_generation,prior_terminal_outcome_proof_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAttemptOutcomeProof>,prior_release_and_overlap_floor_ref:StrongRef<AttemptReleaseAndOverlapFloor>}|IdempotentRetry{existing_registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>,existing_registration_body_digest},expected_outcome_capability_state:ReservedForThisBegin|IdempotentSameRegistration,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The full header, permit, replay object, reservation, audit admission, requested snapshot, and topology basis must byte-match one complete Meta binding. The optional classification is required exactly for AutocommitExecute and must be within the ceiling; it is forbidden for ExplicitBegin. Apply decodes the replay object, byte-matches it to the reservation/request/classification, atomically installs BoundDetailed with that same replay ref, and stores it in the first registered outcome lineage. `BoundCompacted` is terminal lookup state, never an idempotent-registration input.

It is applied only through `GlobalControlCommand(kind=RegisterAttempt)`. `First` requires an absent family and generation zero; `Successor` requires checked generation increment, no active generation, an exact terminal predecessor, every required release/overlap floor, and a fresh token. `IdempotentRetry` byte-matches the complete registration. `BindReserved` atomically changes Reserved to BoundDetailed; `IdempotentBound` returns the exact existing registration. Only binding claims the operation ticket, checks the conflict safe-snapshot frontier, inserts Active family/attempt/conflict entries, changes the outcome directory to W12, and constructs `GlobalAttemptRegistration {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,command_ref,global_txn_id,begin_idempotency_key,capability_replay_ref,request_kind,txn_token,txn_operation_ceiling,autocommit_classification_ref?,registered_snapshot,registered_at_global_logical_command_seq,topology_state_ref,authority_permit_ref,permit_scope_digest,transaction_error_policy,operation_audit_admission,registration_generation}`. Apply then constructs workspace generation zero with the exact same header and ProvenReadOnly cumulative potential plus the Registered outcome. Parallel generations, gaps, token rebinding, classification/ceiling/authority drift, or reuse fail closed. Every transaction registers before its first participant read; denial before registration uses only `GlobalBeginTerminalSpec`.

`{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,global_txn_id,registration_generation,txn_token,predecessor_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>?,state:Registered{registration_ref:StrongRef<GlobalAttemptRegistration>,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,published_statement_frontier,delivery_terminal_frontier,latest_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<CumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,cumulative_logical_effect_root_ref:StrongRef<CumulativeTxnEffectRoot>,statement_index_digest}|PrepareAdmitted{admission_spec_ref:StrongRef<GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec>,terminal_admission_fence_ref:StrongRef<MetaTerminalAdmissionFence>,admission_generation,published_statement_frontier,delivery_terminal_frontier,workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<CumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,cumulative_logical_effect_root_ref:StrongRef<CumulativeTxnEffectRoot>,operation_audit_admission:OperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired,audit_basis_commitment,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef}|CommittedPendingPostconditions{marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef,final_effect_digest,global_txn_command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>,applied_global_logical_seq,applied_global_commit_seq}|Committed{marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef,final_effect_digest,applied_global_logical_seq,applied_global_commit_seq,global_delta_publish_command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>,delta_publish_applied_prefix,published_delta_frontier,public_outcome:TerminalPublicOutcome::Sharded}|Aborted{reason_class,applied_abort_ref:AppliedAbortRef,public_outcome:TerminalPublicOutcome::Sharded}|ReadClosed{read_close_spec_ref:StrongRef<GlobalReadCloseSpec>,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,publication_chain_digest,final_result_digest?,public_outcome:TerminalPublicOutcome::Sharded},audit_state:NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|ClaimedPending{ticket_digest,claim_identity}|TerminalGateCommitted{ticket_digest,terminal_gate_commitment,candidate_pipeline_order},completion_state:TxnCompletionState,minimum_lookup_retention_floor}`. The header is the sole namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation source, and every successor is equal or registered-narrower. Detailed terminal records retain the full header because they own markers, public outcomes, and lifecycle refs; only the final payload-free expiry tombstone may use `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Meta>`. Its predecessor is the immediately prior attempt-lifecycle value; registration creates the first Registered value and thereby roots workspace generation zero, and every statement publication atomically constructs the immediately succeeding Registered value with all frontiers/roots advanced and makes GlobalOutcomeDirectoryValue::W12 point to it. No semantic state strongly owns a protocol-plane `AuditOutcomeRecord`. A committed write is semantically decided at CommittedPendingPostconditions but ordinary success and ReadYourWritesCapability are unavailable until all typed postconditions yield TerminalReady and the current protocol state proves its terminal gate released; only the matching terminal transition resolves the operation claim.

`GlobalAttemptIndex` maps only an actually registered `(global_txn_id,registration_generation)` to `Active|PrepareAdmitted|Terminalizing{semantic_terminal_kind,missing_postcondition_bitmap}|Terminal`; `AttemptFamilyState` enforces one active registered generation and exact successor rules. A pre-registration `NeverRegistered` outcome has no attempt identity and therefore exists only in the begin-key/outcome-capability directories and their permanent tombstones; no attempt-index row or fabricated attempt burn is legal. `GlobalStatementIndex` maps `(global_txn_id,registration_generation,statement_seq)` and the statement idempotency key to `Open|Published|Failed|Abandoned`, including the immutable result manifest, workspace successor, delivery state, and statement-ticket terminal evidence where applicable. `GlobalTxnOutcomeIndex` maps the scoped outcome token to the latest completion state or the separate begin/never-registered directory value. Family, attempt, statement, begin-key, token, audit-ticket, conflict, workspace, and publication/delivery-frontier entries transition atomically in the command that owns them. Matching retries return the original value; conflicting bodies or owners fail. Capability-safe status resolves the role-tagged directory/summary proof rather than a local-only outcome and reports `TerminalPending` instead of fabricating success while any required postcondition remains incomplete.

`GlobalCheckpointInstallSpec` is `{basis_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_global_logical_command_seq,basis_global_commit_seq,basis_payload_digest:WeakDigest,basis_projection_digest,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,checkpoint_state_vector_digest,paired_meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>?,retention_cut_body_ref:StrongRef<RetentionCutBody>?,reset_field_tags[],terminal_audit_gate}`. Genesis alone uses no cut body and produces `CheckpointInstalled`; an operational replacement requires the body and paired floor, atomically installs the matching provisional cut, and preserves `Operational`. The single exact `ShardOperationalBootstrapBarrier` schema is the origin-tagged, strongly retaining definition in the activation/genesis contract above; no digest-only alternate encoding exists. `MetaInitialFloorInstallSpec` is `{checkpoint_installed_global_state:WeakStateIdentity,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,checkpoint_state_vector_digest,initial_meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,initial_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,sorted_active_shard_barrier_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardOperationalBootstrapBarrier>],expected_global_logical_command_seq,terminal_audit_gate}` and is the sole fresh `CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` transition. The barrier set equals every and only `Active` topology entry, all at one global prefix; `Joining` shards are unroutable. `GlobalHistoryCutActivationSpec` is `{provisional_cut_ref:StrongRef<ProvisionalRetentionCutSet>,checkpoint_install_record_ref:StrongGlobalCommandRef,expected_retention_map_basis:WeakStateIdentity,verified_contiguous_suffix_start,terminal_audit_gate}` and only strengthens that exact provisional set to `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`.

Meta-owned directories change only through typed CAS controls. `PublishShardCheckpointCertificateSpec` is `{checkpoint_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardCheckpointCertificate>,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_prior_directory_value:WeakDigest?,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,terminal_audit_gate}`; apply byte-matches shard/config/topology/prefix/history interval and installs the exact CRSR. `PublishShardAppliedAckSpec` similarly binds `{ack_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>,prepare_key,decision_record_identity,decision_publish_record_identity,expected_topology_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_shard_configuration_ref:RemoteConfigurationRef,expected_prior_directory_value:WeakDigest?,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>,terminal_audit_gate}` and is required for commit and abort acknowledgements.

`GlobalTerminalCompletionSpec` is the sole W12 postcondition transition `{pending_outcome_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>,semantic_outcome:SemanticTerminalDescriptor::Sharded,terminal_public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<TerminalPublicProjectionBundle<Meta>>,prebuilt_read_your_writes_issuance_ref:None|Some{StrongRef<ReadYourWritesIssuanceBundle<Meta>>},expected_required_postcondition_bitmap,observed_satisfied_postcondition_bitmap,decision_publication_evidence:Committed{decision_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>}|NoDecisionApplicable{terminal_kind:ReadClosed},exact_sorted_post_visibility_shard_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardAppliedAck>],shard_ack_coverage_commitment,delta_completion:Committed{global_delta_batch_ref:StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>,global_delta_publish_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,published_frontier_proof_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDeltaFrontierProof>}|NoDeltaApplicable{terminal_kind:Aborted|ReadClosed,proof_ref:StrongRef<NoDeltaProof>},configured_durability_evidence_ref:StrongRef<GlobalDurabilityEvidence>,result_disposition:NoTerminalResult|ReadTerminalResult{delivery_disposition_proof_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>}|AutocommitWriteReturning{preparation_ref:StrongRef<TerminalWriteResultPreparation>,required_posture:Sharded,initial_retention_recipe:ResultInitialRetentionRecipe<Meta>},resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition<Meta>>],terminal_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,expected_conflict_overlap_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConflictOverlapCloseProof>,terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<MetaControl>,terminal_audit_gate}`. The portable visibility certificate, not a Protocol-plane `AuditOutcomeRecord` edge, proves that the terminal candidate and audit release are public. Every evidence arm and required bit is generated from terminal kind, participants, result class, and durability policy; arrays are canonical bijections. Apply CASes the exact pending predecessor, monotonically adds only verified bits, validates rather than manufactures the frozen public/capability artifacts, constructs the succeeding outcome, and selects `TerminalReady` only when required equals satisfied.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-02 through FG-INV-06, FG-INV-12, FG-INV-15 through FG-INV-20. Consumes Meta/Shard core formats, result-owner registry, audit terminal contracts, authority bindings, answer/replay contracts, resource/escrow, constraints and certified workspace projections. W12 registration/statement/prepare/decision/terminal tasks depend on it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact rows/codecs exist for every begin key/reservation/never-registered, attempt/claim, statement/index/workspace, read admission/release, result owner, outcome/directory/summary, status/capability, terminal completion and visibility type.
- Unit/golden tests freeze initial/retry/conflict/terminal/compacted public bytes, role-exclusive encodings, workspace generations, owner arms, response commitments and construction order.
- Property/model tests prove response only after reservation, no observation before registration/statement claim, one active family generation, statement sequence/idempotency, workspace RYW, no stream before audit release/lease, exact result disposition, and detailed/compacted equivalence.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects Local object substitution, wrong authority/claim/ticket/key/body, stale workspace/frontier, missing participant/effect/witness, future result ref, internal descriptor on wire, incomplete postconditions and status leakage.
- Crash/DPOR E2E covers lost BEGIN/EXECUTE/ACK/release responses, multi-statement RYW across shards, statement failure policy, cancel/read close/write commit, result resume, compaction and status lookup with restart at each publication.
- JSONL emits {event_version,global_txn_id?,registration_generation?,begin_key_digest,attempt_state,statement_seq?,statement_state?,workspace_generation?,delivery_frontier?,owner_arm?,result_state?,outcome_state,completion_bitmap?,public_status_class?,audit_ticket_state?,role_prefix,recovery_action,replay_command}; no internal keyed IDs or hidden reasons on public channels.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: response-before-reservation, Local/Global shared durable unions, parser-interpreted statements, implicit RYW, result streaming at semantic commit, cancel as durable release, and status reconstructed from unrooted process state.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1696-1784; W12 gate.

title: Implement branch fork: boundary reservation, epoch records, key-envelope DAG, fork bundle
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch creation and forking as one canonical command: `BranchManifest`, `BranchEpochBoundaryReserveSpec`/`BranchEpochBoundaryReservation`, `BranchKeyEpochRecord`, the `KeyEnvelopeNode`/`KeyEnvelopeRoot` DAG with its four AAD domains, `BranchForkBundle`/`BranchForkSpec` build-and-apply, the fork-time double rotation, and the cancel/abandon paths. Grant issuance/revocation surfaces are split to w2-branch-grants; merge to w2-branch-merge; retirement to w2-branch-retire.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1+B6: branches are "git for graphs" — what-if analysis, agent isolation, schema experiments, reproducible feature snapshots. §3.1's Aspen verdict: adopt the spirit of immutable structural sharing (free snapshots) at run granularity. §3.3's 2026 market synthesis flags governance/access control as the field's gap: FrankenGraphDB's fork isolation is cryptographic (key epochs + envelope DAG), not ACL-only, so a fork is a security boundary a hostile reader cannot cross even with stolen storage bytes. frankensqlite's ECS lesson adapted: fork is a canonical ordered command, never an out-of-band KMS effect.

## Design — normative detail
`BranchManifest {graph, branch_id, origin:Genesis{creation_checkpoint_or_genesis_basis:GenesisBranchBasis}|Fork{parent_branch, parent_head:StrongMarkerRef, fork_boundary_logical_command_seq, boundary_reservation_identity}, base_checkpoint_ref?, key_envelope_root_ref:StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeRoot>, current_envelope_epoch, current_write_key_epoch, policy}`. Genesis forbids parent/head/boundary fields; Fork requires all four and verifies parent ancestry/head/epochs at the exact already-assigned boundary. The boundary sequence is `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation.boundary_logical_command_seq`, NEVER the later bundle-install sequence; install provenance lives only in the applied control record/registry projection. Branch creation adds only metadata and key wraps — data-copy complexity O(1); metadata is proportional to the bounded envelope-root fanout, not falsely O(1) for arbitrary recipient lists; durable creation still pays ordered root-publication latency and is never promised below an fsync-independent microsecond constant. Reads select the branch head and follow explicit branch-parent links atop structurally shared objects.

Ordered first: `BranchEpochBoundaryReserveSpec {reservation_id, operation:Fork|SnapshotGrant|StartOrContinueAdvancingGrant|RevokeAdvancingGrant|Rotate, graph, branch, parent_or_target_scope, expected_head:WeakMarkerIdentity, expected_envelope_epoch, expected_write_epoch, transition_nonce, complete_affected_coordinate_set, expected_boundary_index_absence, terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply validates current state and creates immutable `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation {source_spec_ref, reservation_id, operation, graph_branch_scope, frozen_head_and_epoch_commitment, boundary_logical_command_seq, transition_nonce, exclusive_branch_head_and_epoch_hold_root_ref, state:Active}`; every branch mutation/key transition consults the hold root — conflicting work waits or rejects, disjoint commands proceed. `ObjectCreationBoundary` is the exact tag `CommittedExisting{creation_marker_identity, creation_commit_seq}|TransactionReserved{final_certification_reservation_identity, permanent_object_ordinal}|BranchEpochReserved{boundary_reservation_ref, permanent_object_ordinal}`, supplying stable AAD identity before ordering.

`BranchKeyEpochRecord {database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, graph, branch, kind:Envelope|Write, epoch, key_id, predecessor:Genesis|SameEpochLifecycle{ref:StrongRef<BranchKeyEpochRecord>}|PriorEpoch{identity:WeakEpochIdentity}, transition_nonce, boundary_reservation_ref, state:Active{opened_at_boundary}|Closed{opened_at_boundary, closed_through_boundary, close_reason}}`; both boundary fields carry the reservation identity/sequence. Closing uses the strong same-epoch predecessor; opening a successor uses only the weak prior-epoch identity/rotation-chain digest — the current epoch never retains every old key forever; old envelope roots/nodes/grants/backups are the strong owners that keep an old key decryptable, and when they disappear two-stage destruction can prove zero references.

`KeyEnvelopeNode` carries `children[{range, child_ref, child_ciphertext_ref, wrapped_child_dek, wrap_profile, aad_bytes, aad_digest}]`, `inherited_roots[{source graph/branch/epoch, source_root_ref + ciphertext_ref, maximum_logical_command_seq, maximum_marker?, wrapped_source_envelope_key, wrapped_source_root_dek, wrap_profile, aad}]` (every inherited edge carries a maximum logical-command/marker cut), and `write_epochs[{write_epoch_record_ref, allowed_creation_range, wrapped_write_epoch_key, wrap_profile, aad}]`. `KeyEnvelopeRoot {namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, envelope_epoch_record_ref, current_write_epoch_record_ref, root_node_ref, root_node_ciphertext_ref, coverage_cut, profile_oid}`. This is a constructively verified immutable DAG, not an opaque closure. Four exact AAD domains: `"fgdb:key-envelope-child:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, parent_node_kind, child_range, child_oid, canonical child_ciphertext_ref, wrap_profile, envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:key-envelope-inherit:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, target_graph, target_branch, target_envelope_epoch, source_graph, source_branch, source_envelope_epoch, source_root_oid, canonical source_root_ciphertext_ref, maximum_logical_command_seq, maximum_marker, wrap_profile, target_envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:key-envelope-write:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, write_epoch_record_oid, allowed_creation_range, wrap_profile, envelope_key_id); `"fgdb:branch-object-dek-wrap:v1"` (namespace, incarnation, logical_oid, ciphertext_id, dek_id, graph, branch, write_epoch, canonical object_creation_boundary, wrap_profile, write_key_id). Stored AAD bytes must equal the canonical transcript; a digest alone is not usable AAD.

`BranchForkBundle<Role>` is built bottom-up under a stable prepared owner: epoch records -> ciphertexts/encodings/placements/openers -> typed `StrongCiphertextRef<T>` availability certificates -> envelope nodes/roots -> portable grant bytes -> local grant records/registry successor -> manifests -> bundle; fields include the reservation ref, closed parent envelope+write epoch records (through boundary L-1), frozen path-copied parent root + ciphertext, disjoint parent-successor and child epoch records/roots/manifests at boundary L, grant records/bytes, resulting `KeyGrantRegistry`, bijection proof, complete object-wrap ciphertext-realization inventory, and closure_digest; one payload-availability certificate covers that exact closed inventory, excluding only the future install control/order supplement. `BranchForkSpec<Role> {boundary_reservation_ref, required_reservation_state:Active, bundle_ref, bundle_payload_availability_certificate_ref, expected_parent_head, expected_parent_envelope_epoch, expected_parent_write_epoch, transition_nonce, terminal_audit_gate}`: deterministic apply creates NO key/ciphertext/node/record/grant/manifest — it byte-validates bundle, certificate, reservation, held head/epochs, nonce, closure disjointness, and isolation laws, atomically installs the already-known manifests/registries, consumes the reservation, and releases holds. The double rotation is the isolation boundary: the child receives the now-closed parent envelope key, never a key under which post-fork parent grants or ciphertexts may be created; parent writes admitted after the boundary use only the successor; the child opens frozen history but no successor/sibling epoch; a prepared old-epoch parent write must be revalidated and rewrapped/re-encoded or abort before order. Epoch material is never reused after crash, restore, or merge. `BranchEpochBoundaryCancelSpec` is legal before any bundle/prepared owner/certificate/wrap exists (requires `NoBoundaryClosureProof`); `BranchEpochBoundaryAbandonSpec` after construction requires complete signer/prepared closure, no install order/candidate/external grant publication, and typed cleanup/zeroization evidence. Once a grant or revocation is externally published, recovery must complete the matching install; timeout cannot release the hold.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-13 (invariant, restated): commits are immutable and branch heads move only by atomic expected-head updates; fork closes the parent envelope/write epochs before opening independent parent/child successors; every envelope, object-DEK, grant, and wrap is bound to one authenticated root/cut/epoch. FG-INV-07 (invariant): every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. FG-INV-16 (invariant): no boundary hold is lost, duplicated, or released while obligated. Fork latency/metadata cost is an Appendix G latency-anatomy + benchmark-class claim, never an invariant.

## Interactions
Boundary reservation and bundle install ride w2-commit-protocol's D1/order path with prepared ownership; manifests/registries publish via w2-txn-lifecycle state roots; identities from w2-object-identity; key lifecycle states and destruction pipeline from w9-key-lifecycle; crypto profiles/entropy from w1-crypto; command rows from g0-command-contracts. w2-branch-grants, w2-branch-merge, w2-branch-retire, and w11-payload-availability all build on the reservation/bundle idiom defined here.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Mandatory suites from the plan: Genesis/no-fake-parent, cross-branch/head substitution, boundary substitution, unrelated-command interleaving, and reproposal tests; fork/handoff/rotation coverage over sibling, post-fork-parent, post-snapshot, post-revocation, expired-grant, stale-prepared-wrap, merge overbreadth, cancel/abandon, restore, every reserve/build/order/apply crash boundary, and collected-key decryption (child cannot decrypt post-fork parent ciphertext and vice versa). AAD mutation tests independently perturb every transcript field per domain. Microbench: O(1) data-copy verified; durable-creation latency reported against the Appendix G anatomy row with fsync attribution logged. E2e script: genesis-create a branch, write, reserve+fork, write divergent data on parent and child, verify cross-branch decryption denial both ways, then exercise the cancel-before-closure and abandon-after-construction paths end-to-end. DETAILED LOGGING (required of implementation and tests): every reserve/build/order/apply/cancel/abandon step logs reservation_id, operation, boundary_logical_command_seq, transition_nonce, hold-root acquisition/release, closed/opened epoch-record identities (kind, epoch, key_id), bundle closure_digest, availability-certificate identity, per-check apply validation verdicts, and cleanup/zeroization evidence identities; the crash-boundary suites assert post-recovery state from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: out-of-band KMS fork effects (unauditable, unrecoverable); deriving boundary identity from the install order (future-OID cycle); opaque key closures (unverifiable). Risk: envelope fanout blowup for wide grants — costed as metadata proportional to fanout, never hidden behind an O(1) claim.

## Provenance
§5.6 (451-453, 461), App A branch/envelope rows (~1994-2025), §3.1, §3.3.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement branch key grants: portable bytes, local records, grant bundles, registry
description:
## What & scope
Implement branch sharing/handoff: `KeyEnvelopeGrantBytes` (portable), `KeyEnvelopeGrantRecord<Role>` (local authority/retention owner), `KeyGrantRegistry<Role>`, `BranchGrantBundle<Role>`/`BranchGrantTransitionRef<Role>`/`BranchGrantSpec<Role>`, and the snapshot/advancing/revocation semantics. Split from w2-branch-fork to keep each bead within budget; the reservation/bundle/apply idiom is inherited from there.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: cross-organization branch sharing (agent memory handoff, regulated data rooms) needs a portable cryptographic artifact whose authority is still locally owned, revocable, and time-bounded. The market's governance gap (§3.3) is answered by grants that are keys plus policy, not ACL rows: a snapshot recipient physically cannot open post-grant writes.

## Design — normative detail
`KeyEnvelopeGrantBytes` is the portable signed `{format_version, grant_id, generation, predecessor_grant_digest:WeakDigest?, authority_binding_public_commitment, security_state_binding_public_commitment, tenant_principal_ceiling_purpose_commitment, graph, branch, envelope_root_identity_and_digest, root_ciphertext_identity_and_digest, envelope_epoch, write_epoch?, coverage_cut, mode:SnapshotAtHead|AdvancingBranch, recipient_id, recipient_public_key_id, wrapped_root_object_dek, wrapped_envelope_key, wrap_profile, time_authority_profile_oid, not_before:AuthorityInstant, expires_at:AuthorityInstant, issuer_id, grant_aad_bytes, grant_aad_digest, signer_set_epoch, signature}` with no local `StrongRef`. Its AAD is exactly `canonical("fgdb:key-envelope-recipient:v1", every unsigned field except wrapped_root_object_dek, wrapped_envelope_key, grant_aad_bytes, grant_aad_digest, and signature)` — excluding the ciphertexts avoids a circular encryption input; the outer signature covers the entire portable body including both wrapped ciphertexts and the exact AAD bytes/digest, excluding only the signature. `KeyEnvelopeGrantRecord<Role>` binds those exact bytes to current roots/ciphertexts/policy/time evidence: `{authority_bound_header, grant_id, generation, predecessor_record_ref?, portable_grant_bytes_ref, portable_grant_digest, graph, branch, envelope_root_ref, root_ciphertext_ref, envelope_epoch, write_epoch?, coverage_cut, mode, recipient_id, recipient_public_key_id, time_basis_ref:StrongRef<KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role>>, issuance_time_validation_evidence_ref, state:Current|Revoked{revocation_evidence_ref}|Expired{time_validation_evidence_ref}, body_digest}`. Generation one has no predecessor; renewal is the exact prior+1 direct successor preserving authority/subject/recipient/mode/coverage and wrapped-key identities, advancing only the profiled window and issuance fields, with checked arithmetic. `KeyGrantRegistry<Role>` is the sole CAS-linear owner `{generation, entries[grant_id -> current_record_ref | Terminal{terminal_authority_commitment, grant_identity, terminal_portable_digest, status:Revoked|Expired}], recipient_and_subject_indexes, nonreuse_floor, body_digest}`; exact retry joins one generation; competing renew/revoke/expire transitions race one current leaf.

A snapshot/revocation `BranchGrantBundle` prebuilds the same close/freeze/double-rotation as fork, grants only the frozen root through boundary `L-1`, carries both portable bytes and local record, and provides the successor manifest before ordering; `BranchGrantTransitionRef` is `IssueOrRenew{record_ref, portable_bytes_ref}|Revoke{current_record_ref, revocation_evidence_ref, terminal_registry_body_recipe}`; `BranchGrantSpec` apply only validates/installs the bundle and registry successor. Semantics: a snapshot grant names only a frozen closed root, so a snapshot/revoked recipient never retains a key under which later wraps are legal; an advancing grant intentionally binds the exact current root/epoch and covers new wraps under that named active epoch until rotation — every later epoch needs another ordered grant. Revocation claims only prevention of future access, never erasure of plaintext/keys already received; expiry without ordered revocation/rotation does not claim cryptographic cutoff — the ordered `Expired` successor ends new use and releases retention only after every independent promise floor closes. Handoff wraps metadata/keys, not graph data, and reports metadata and recipient cost. GC/backup/restore/key destruction follow every live LOCAL record/registry edge; portable grant bytes never become a local reachability edge by themselves; a live local record pins its exact named root/ciphertext even if compaction creates another realization; an equal-scalar portable grant under another authority binding is noninterchangeable and cannot be imported without its matching local record.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-13 (invariant): every envelope, object-DEK, grant, and wrap is bound to one authenticated root/cut/epoch. FG-INV-16 window class: `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role> {authority_bound_header, grant_id, generation, recipient_id, graph, branch, envelope_epoch, coverage_cut, grant_record_digest}` rides the common profiled prefix `{subject_kind, time_authority_profile_oid, not_before, expires_at, subject_body_digest, intended_use_set, owner_plane_and_slot, body_digest}` with `not_before < expires_at`; ambient wall time never substitutes. FG-INV-20 (invariant): authorization precedes every observation; grant lookup failure is uniformly nonrevealing.

## Interactions
