title: Implement the keyed identity pipeline: ObjectId, CiphertextId, EncodingId, SymbolRecord
description:
## What & scope
Implement §5.1's complete noncircular identity pipeline for every durable logical object: keyed `ObjectId`, deterministic compression, one object-level AEAD under a per-ciphertext DEK, `CiphertextId`, `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`/`EncodingId`, `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId`/`PlacementId`, RaptorQ symbolization, and per-symbol MACs over the exact `SymbolRecord` transcript — plus collision-bucket verification, dedup/namespace laws, and the non-self-referential construction rules.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's promise — logical identity that survives recompression, re-encryption, and RaptorQ re-encoding within one keyed security namespace — requires identity layers separating *what an object is* (ObjectId), *how it is protected* (CiphertextId), *how it is coded* (EncodingId), and *where it lives* (PlacementId). That is what lets branches, dedup, replication, backup, recoding, and KMS rewrap each change exactly one layer. Keying the ObjectId prevents honest-but-curious storage from running an offline plaintext dictionary against the public slot (`g0-threat-model`); frankensqlite's Argon2id/encrypt-then-code design is the starting point (§2.3), but nonce, AAD, per-encoding DEK, symbol-MAC, rewrap, and KMS/HSM details are respecified here — no correctness inherited.

## Design — normative detail
`ObjectId = BLAKE3_keyed(K_oid, "fgdb:logical:v1" ‖ DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId ‖ canonical_plaintext_header ‖ canonical_plaintext_payload)`, full 256-bit. `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId` is an immutable random 256-bit database-creation identity distinct from the human/catalog `DatabaseId`; `K_oid` is an immutable random database identity key shared only with authorized replicas/restore principals and wrapped through the root/bootstrap/key-escrow chain; both exist before any ObjectId is verified. A 128-bit prefix is only a lookup accelerator; collision buckets always verify full digest, object kind, length, and canonical plaintext before deduplication or substitution. Same-identity restore preserves namespace and key; clone restore creates both anew and must re-address and re-encrypt the complete logical closure. Dedup never crosses security namespaces unless a deployment policy explicitly accepts equality leakage via a separately specified shared namespace/key domain.

Pipeline: canonical plaintext is deterministically compressed under `CodecProfile`; a random per-ciphertext DEK performs **one** object-level AEAD with AAD `("fgdb:object-aead:v1", ObjectId, CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest)`. `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest = { logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len }` — it excludes FEC and placement. `CiphertextId` hashes descriptor + ciphertext + profile-sized object tag; `CiphertextRecord = { descriptor, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, object_tag_digest, protected_length }`. `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId = { ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile }` holds every parameter changing RaptorQ decoding or symbol authentication; `EncodingId = BLAKE3("fgdb:encoding:v1" ‖ canonical(EncodingDescriptorWithoutId))`. The same authenticated ciphertext may be recoded under another complete encoding descriptor without re-encryption. `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId = { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }` where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`; `PlacementId = BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" ‖ canonical(...))` — neither the ID nor a digest of the record is an input to itself. Adding/moving symbols creates a new placement record, never a new encoding identity.

RaptorQ encodes the complete ciphertext-plus-object-tag. `K_symbol = KDF(DEK, "fgdb:symbol-auth:v1" ‖ EncodingId)` MACs the exact canonical `SymbolRecord` transcript: domain/version plus every serialized header field except the MAC bytes, then the payload — framing lengths, identities, object kind, source block, ESI, transfer length, OTI, flags, auth profile, payload length; no shorter competing transcript. Wire format: `SymbolRecord { magic="FGEC", format_version:u16, header_len:u16, record_len:u32, logical_oid:[u8;32], ciphertext_id:[u8;32], encoding_id:[u8;32], object_kind:u16, source_block:u32, esi:u32, symbol_len:u32, transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32, flags:u32, symbol_mac_profile:u16, symbol_mac_len:u16, payload, symbol_mac }`. Symbols never reuse an object AEAD nonce as per-symbol nonces; symbols from different `EncodingId`s never mix; a decoder obtains the complete descriptor/OTI/auth profile from an authenticated `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` (or FGP's authenticated encoding prelude) before accepting any symbol — a bare SymbolRecord is never self-authorizing. DEK/ciphertext identity is separate from `wrap_key_epoch`: KEK/KMS rewrap changes only immutable `KeyWrap` records, never `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`. RaptorQ protects erasures only within the declared source-block/placement model; replication/backup protects failure-domain loss. Truncated/noncanonical tails are ignored only in proved-unreferenced staging; a reachable sealed tail triggers authenticated repair or fail-closed recovery. Every stored digest declares one class — `TargetDigest`, `TranscriptDigest` (registered recipe), `WeakIdentityDigest`, or `BodyDigest<T>` with `{domain_separator, schema_major, included/excluded field tags}`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 (verbatim): `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory; root bootstrap reconstructs all identities without indexes; child-key AAD and symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; collision buckets verify full identity and incompatible encodings never combine; every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe. Golden vectors and profile bounds are FG-EVID-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-identity-registries` (five registries, BodyDigest transcripts, acyclic construction checks), `w1-crypto` (BLAKE3-keyed, AEAD profiles, KDF), `w1-codecs` (compression), `w1-generated-parsers` (registry-generated encoders/golden vectors). Produces the identity substrate for `w2-object-packing`, `w2-root-bootstrap` (RootBootstrap reproduces these descriptors byte-for-byte), `w2-fec-scrub` (recode law), `w2-commit-protocol` (capsule closures), all `w3-*` objects, and `w9-key-lifecycle` (KeyWrap/rewrap separation).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Full keyed-identity/descriptor/AAD recompute oracle: encode → decode → recompute all four identities from bytes alone. Property tests: recode under a new `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` preserves `ObjectId`/`CiphertextId` and changes `EncodingId`; move/add symbols changes only `PlacementId`; KEK rewrap changes only `KeyWrap`. Negative fixtures: wrong `K_oid`, wrong namespace, mixed-`EncodingId` symbol sets, truncated MAC, competing shorter transcript, self-referential placement — all fail closed. Mutation, golden, and cross-version corpora per registry row; FEC-wire fuzz over `SymbolRecord` framing; collision-bucket test with engineered 128-bit prefix collisions verifying full-digest/kind/length/plaintext checks. CI: the generated digest/field checker rejects unknown exclusions, two body-digest fields, implicit zero placeholders, digest-over-self. E2E: a pipeline-lifecycle script builds a randomized multi-kind object corpus and drives encode → store → recode under a new `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` → KEK/KMS rewrap → symbol move/add → decode, then recomputes all four identities from the stored bytes alone and byte-compares them against the originals across a process restart. DETAILED LOGGING: the implementation and tests must emit structured events for every identity computation/verification `{object_kind, namespace_id, profile_ids, computed_identity, expected_identity, verdict}`, every AEAD seal/open with its AAD transcript digest, every symbol-MAC accept/reject with `{encoding_id, source_block, esi, symbol_mac_profile}`, every collision-bucket candidate with its full-digest/kind/length/plaintext check results, and every dedup/substitution decision; the e2e verifier replays the log stream and fails on any missing event or identity/verdict mismatch, so post-implementation verification is possible from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: unkeyed content addressing (offline dictionary attack); placement inside encoding identity (every move would re-identify); self/future-referential descriptor digests (bootstrap cycles); per-symbol reuse of the object AEAD nonce; cross-namespace dedup by default (equality leakage). Risk: profile drift between Appendix A and code — mitigated by registry-generated encoders and golden vectors as the single source.

## Provenance
§5.1 (278-280), App A (1445-1458), §2.3 encryption row, FG-INV-09 (App F).

title: Implement PackedObjectGroup with the pack-homogeneity law and D1-boundary packing
description:
## What & scope
Implement `PackedObjectGroup`, the registered `physical_record_kinds.toml` class that packs the length-delimited canonical plaintext bytes of many small logical objects into one physical record paying **one** compress/AEAD/FEC/placement pipeline, plus its mandatory homogeneity law, subobject locator indexing, reclamation coarsening, and byte-economy reporting. `MarkerBatch` is respecified as exactly such a pack.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 makes every commit produce several small control-plane objects (capsule, effect set, delta template, authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome-preparation record). Paying a full pipeline (compression header + AEAD tag + FEC symbolization + placement record) per tiny object multiplies metadata bytes per user commit — a direct threat to the §17 byte-economy targets and §6.6 write-amplification model (B2's economics). Packing generalizes the `MarkerBatch` trade the plan already accepts: one pipeline per group, members keep logical identity. The saving is priced, never assumed (B5 discipline).

## Design — normative detail
The pack, not the member, owns the `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`/`PlacementId` chain. Every member keeps its keyed `ObjectId`, computed and verified over its own canonical plaintext exactly per `w2-object-identity`. The object-location index maps each member OID to an authenticated `(pack_encoding, offset, length)` subobject locator in the same registered metadata-tree locator class marker batches already use; entries remain nonretaining locators. `PreparedCommitRecord.exact_realizations` already carries `object_or_subobject_id`, so prepared ownership names packed members without new schema surface. `StrongRef` semantics, generated reachability/GC walkers, and content addressing are unchanged because references target logical ObjectIds, never placements; a pack never acquires an `ObjectKind`; a packed member deduplicates against any other realization only through the full-digest/kind/length/plaintext verification every collision candidate already pays.

**Mandatory homogeneity law**: a pack is homogeneous in (a) key domain — every member belongs to exactly one write-key domain: the branch envelope/write-key epoch for branch-scoped payloads, or the database-scoped commit-stream key domain for commit-mechanism objects (markers, capsules, command records); (b) tenant/authority domain — one `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId` and one tenant; (c) retention/floor class. Thus the pack DEK's wrap binds a single source epoch and creation boundary under §12.5's envelope rules, and crypto-erasure granularity never coarsens across epochs, tenants, or floors. A mixed pack fails closed at build time. Reclamation coarsens to the pack — a pack is reclaimable only when every member is — and compaction owns the rewrite of partially dead packs (the same trade marker batches accept).

**Packing boundary = existing D1 boundaries, no new ordering step**: the coordinator packs one ordered group's control-plane commit objects at the seal §5.2 step 5 already performs; each per-proposal order-attempt supplement and its availability certificate pack analogously at their own step-6 D1 boundary; later command/command-record/marker objects ride their existing publication boundaries under the same rule. Packing adds no new ordered durability barrier. Packs report through §17 byte-economy metrics — metadata bytes per small durable object and Chronicle stream bytes per user commit, by operation class — and §6.6's write/space-amplification component breakdown.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 applies unchanged to members: every member `ObjectId` recomputes from its own canonical plaintext; the pack's physical identities recompute from the pack descriptor/bytes. FG-INV-14 clause: subobject locator entries are registered nonretaining fields; GC reclaims the pack only when every member is unreachable and no independent obligation roots any member. The byte-economy saving is a benchmark/SLO-class claim (Appendix G / §17 rows), never an invariant; the homogeneity law is a G0 build-time format law with negative fixtures.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-object-identity` (member identity + pack pipeline), `g0-format-arms` (frozen `PackedObjectGroup` decision + homogeneity law), `g0-identity-registries` (physical-record row, locator class), `g0-cost-registry` (byte-economy rows). Produces packing used by `w2-commit-protocol` (step-5/step-6 D1 seals), `w2-group-commit` (group boundary = pack boundary), `w2-compaction` (partially-dead-pack rewrite), `w3-write-amp` (component breakdown), `perf-bench-core` (metadata-bytes gates).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: build/decode round-trip for packs of 1..N members; member OID verification from subobject locators; pack digest recompute. Negative: mixed key-domain pack, mixed tenant, mixed retention class — build fails closed with typed errors; a `StrongRef` targeting a pack (rather than a member OID) is unencodable. Property: dedup of a packed member against an unpacked realization requires full plaintext verification; GC never reclaims a pack with one live member; compaction rewrite of a partially dead pack preserves all live member ObjectIds and logical digests. Crash matrix, phased: at this bead, harness-level pack-seal atomicity — cut a simulated durability boundary before/after pack seal and assert a torn or partial pack is detected and treated as absent (no partial-member ambiguity); the step-5 and step-6 D1 integration rows (recovery sees either no pack or a complete sealed pack inside a real commit) are registered now as named matrix rows and executed at w2-commit-protocol's crash matrix and verif-torture. Bench: metadata bytes per small durable object with packing on/off, logged per operation class and checked against the Appendix G row; e2e script logs pack sizes, member counts, and reclamation coarsening events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: per-member pipelines (metadata blowup — the reason this exists); packs as logical objects with ObjectKind (would corrupt the reference model); heterogeneous packs (would coarsen crypto-erasure across epochs/tenants/floors, violating §12.5 granularity); a new pack-publication barrier (packing must ride existing D1 boundaries). Risk: pathological packs with one hot + many dead members inflating space-amp — mitigated by compaction rewrite policy and the §6.6 breakdown making it visible.

## Provenance
§5.1 (line 342), §19 G0 decision batch (1313), §12.5 envelope rules, §17/§6.6 metrics.

title: Implement fgdb-order: quorum-one Raft core, hard state, snapshots, log verifier
description:
## What & scope
Build the `fgdb-order` crate: the durable Raft log/state core and quorum-one driver that every durable FrankenGraphDB posture orders through. Scope: `RaftLogSegment`, `RaftHardState`, `RaftSnapshot` (applied-cut), `RaftConsensusCutProjection`, `RaftStateRoot`, `ConfigurationState` consumption, the role-tagged maintenance-command routing, the generated log-to-state verifier, and gap classification during log examination. Multi-member protocol (`fgdb-raft`) layers on top later (w11); this bead delivers the one-member/quorum-one specialization that single-node embedded and server postures run in production. Only `:memory:` runs the same state machine without a durability claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism/evidence): one commit state machine for single-node and replicated means single-node correctness evidence transfers to clusters instead of maintaining two recovery authorities. B1: the ordered log is the spine of the One Version Universe — `CommitSeq`/`LogicalCommandSeq` derive from it. Market: SQLite-class embedded durability with a story that scales to consensus without a rewrite; competitors (Neo4j, Kùzu) keep separate WAL vs replication machinery. The frankensqlite donor (§2.3) supplies the no-extra-mutable-file, root-publication architecture; Raft here is not middleware but the ordering substrate under it.

## Design — normative detail
`RaftLogSegment` carries the exact domain/index/term/entry fields and a generated closed command union over Local semantic txn/control, Meta semantic txn/control, Shard prepare/decision/control, and `Maintenance{command:RaftMaintenanceCommand}`. `RaftMaintenanceCommand` is the role-tagged outer union `Local{command_ref:StrongRef<LocalMaintenanceCommand>}|Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<MetaMaintenanceCommand>}|Shard{shard_id,command_ref:StrongRef<ShardMaintenanceCommand>}`; role/group validation rejects substitution. Maintenance commands advance Raft/maintenance indexes and their declared nonsemantic planes only; they never advance semantic sequences/HLC/heads or mutate a semantic payload. A self-staleness fixture must fail any maintenance handler that changes semantic order.

`RaftHardState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,current_term,voted_for?,log_first,log_last,commit_index,applied_index,visible_index,configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,snapshot_ref?,maintenance_applied_index,certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptLedger>,prepared_order_attempt_root_ref:StrongRef<PreparedOrderAttemptRoot>,audit_signer_journal_root_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerJournalRoot>,protocol_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity}`. `ConfigurationState` (`{database_id,...,configuration_epoch,form:Stable{voters[],storage_members[]}|Joint{old/new voters and storage members},sorted_member_descriptors[...],raft_quorum_rule,payload_recoverability_predicate,failure_domain_map,gc_ack_policy,predecessor:WeakConfigurationIdentity?,transition_nonce}`) has its ObjectId as identity, never stored inside itself; one-member is the ordinary Stable specialization; cross-group import only via `RemoteConfigurationRef` — equal member lists or bare config OIDs never authorize replay.

`RaftConsensusCutProjection<Role>` is the prebuilt snapshot-self-excluding projection (last_included_index K, term at K, vote/commit state at K, configuration-at-cut ref, prospective configs, log-prefix digest, retained_suffix_begin_index K+1, floors, format escape latch, takeover head projection, `snapshot_slot:SelfExcluded{InstallThisSnapshot}`); the construction-DAG generator rejects any path from it back to the snapshot under construction. `RaftSnapshot` is a role-tagged exact **applied-cut** union with the invariant `last_included_index = K = successor RaftHardState.applied_index_at_cut`; retained suffix begins exactly K+1; construction order is cut projection -> snapshot -> successor `RaftHardState{snapshot_ref}` -> successor `RaftStateRoot`, never a cycle; every semantic/protocol/prepared/consensus object through K is owned by the snapshot closure and none is double-owned as a suffix entry; an unresolved Local/Meta audit candidate may cross the visible sub-prefix because the snapshotted protocol state owns its complete queue. It is never a visible-only cut. `RaftStateRoot<Role>` is `{hard_state_ref,retained_log_segment_refs,configuration_state_refs,matching_applied_cut_snapshot_ref?,prepared_and_certificate_ledger_refs,remote_obligation_floor_refs,transition_lock_refs,format_first_target_escape_latch,takeover_adoption_head,role_protocol_state_ref,unresolved_candidate_closure_refs,body_digest}`; hard-state and snapshot refs must agree.

No-extra-mutable-file doctrine: a node syncs the new closure before vote/append/receipt/durability replies; every append reply or reply batch mints a fresh `RaftHardState`/`RaftStateRoot`/`RootManifest` closure plus one serialized `RootSlot` publication. Every reply follows a durable RootManifest publication of the appropriate semantic/protocol/consensus state. Local Raft publication may advance RootSlot without semantic change. Leader loss yields capability-scoped `Unknown`, never a guess.

The generated log-to-state verifier proves the exact role-specific root/config/prefix at a cut; no later root may pair with an earlier cut (`LogToAllPlanesProof` is a strong RaftSnapshot field). Gap classification: entries at or below snapshot cut K are benignly absent (owned by the applied-cut closure); a missing/damaged entry inside the retained suffix (K, durable tail] is corruption and fails closed (repairable only through the FEC/replica ladder, never partially interpreted); an unacknowledged torn tail above the durable commit point may be truncated, but truncation stops at visible audit-safe state and waits for the generated-complete floor covering prepared transfers, cursors, replay, external continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, and current/prospective configurations.

The `RaftHardFrame` bootstrap-frame spike (a G0 decision, owned by g0-format-arms) is consumed here: per-append scalars alone cannot stop closure re-minting because `certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref`, `prepared_order_attempt_root_ref`, and `audit_signer_journal_root_ref` churn per commit; skipping per-batch root publication makes the retained log tail a bootstrap input requiring new subordinate clauses under FG-INV-08/FG-INV-10, a changed log-to-state verifier, and takeover coverage, with the frame embedding the same database/security-namespace/incarnation/writer-fence tuple as `RootSlot`. Implement to the recorded spike outcome either way.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07: the concrete durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm/handler. FG-INV-08: logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their sequences; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise visible cut, root, configuration, maintenance state, and applied/visible positions; Raft indexes are contiguous. FG-INV-10: the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; every irreversible seal, receipt, Raft action, certificate, and slot write rechecks both authorities; closure failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back. Claim types: ordered sync operations per commit and per append batch (by posture and audit class) are §17 gated benchmark numbers derived from Appendix G `latency_anatomy.toml`; they are registry/slo rows, never invariants.

## Interactions
Consumed by w2-commit-protocol (orders `CommitCommand`), w2-hlc-order-attempt (order-attempt roots live in hard state), w2-group-commit (append/reply batching and fusion), w2-recovery (log reconciliation), w2-snapshots-leases (visible index), w9-audit-pipeline (maintenance command family), w11-raft-multi (`fgdb-raft` builds multi-member on `fgdb-order`). Consumes w2-object-identity (ObjectId/StrongRef machinery), w2-root-bootstrap (RootSlot/RootManifest publication), g0-command-contracts (generated command unions), g0-cost-registry (priced closure re-mint), w1-foundation-types, w1-crypto.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: role/group/incarnation substitution rejection for every command family; ConfigurationState one-member quorum math. Property: snapshot cut invariant (K equality, suffix begins K+1, no double ownership) under randomized snapshot/install schedules. Generated: log-to-state verifier runs in CI against every constructed cut; construction-DAG checker rejects projection-to-snapshot cycles. Crash matrix: torn-root/marker-tail/stale-writer/bootstrap/recovery rows; every-write/fsync-lie/path-replacement/rollback profiles (FG-INV-10 fixture set). Gap classification suite: benign below-cut absence, retained-suffix hole (must fail closed with typed corruption error and full logging of segment identity/index/digest), torn-tail truncation halting at the generated-complete floor. Self-staleness fixture over all maintenance handlers. Fuzz `RaftLogSegment` decode. Bench: one-member append-to-apply sync count measured and checked against the Appendix G derivability law. E2E (harness-level at this bead — the §5.2 commit stack is a dependent, not a dependency): scripted single-node durable session — open, drive a mixed stream of registered command-union entries (Maintenance commands plus generated fixture semantic entries from the G0 command unions) through the quorum-one append/apply/publication path, kill -9 at randomized points, restart, and assert the generated log-to-state verifier accepts the recovered cut and recovered state matches a reference replay of the same entry stream; the identical script re-runs with real committed writes through the full §5.2 stack once w2-commit-protocol lands, and again at gate-genesis. DETAILED LOGGING: every append/apply/snapshot-install event logs {role, group, term, index, cut K where applicable}; every RootSlot publication logs {slot generation, closure digest, trigger: append-reply|apply|maintenance}; gap-classification outcomes log {segment identity, index, digest, classification}; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: per-append closure re-minting cost in the embedded hot path — mitigated by the priced `RaftHardFrame` spike and group commit; the cost is gated, not hidden. Rejected: a separate mutable WAL file (second recovery authority, violates the no-extra-mutable-file doctrine); rejected: treating single-node as a WAL special case with Raft bolted on later (two commit state machines, non-transferable evidence); rejected: ambient abbreviated Raft schemas without database/namespace/incarnation/role/group domains (enables cross-group replay).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 (l.393, l.407), §14.W1 item 1 (l.1068–1070), App A l.1552–1562, App F FG-INV-07/08/10, App G, §18.1 (fgdb-order row).

title: Build TxnOutcomeRecord, TxnOutcomeIndex, token capabilities, compaction and expiry
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Local token/outcome authority: `TxnOutcomeRecord`, `TxnOutcomeIndex`, `LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex`, `txn_token`/`TxnOutcomeCapability` semantics, `LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot`, `LocalOutcomeCompactionSpec`, and `LocalOutcomeExpirySpec`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents need a durable, MAC-scoped answer to "what happened to my transaction?" that survives crashes, retries, compaction, and years of retention — this index is that answer, with byte-identical responses across detailed and compacted forms. B1: outcomes are part of the version universe, retained under explicit floors rather than evaporating with server memory.

## Design — normative detail
`txn_token` is the opaque durable idempotency identity inside §13's MACed `TxnOutcomeCapability`, scoped to database security namespace/incarnation/service-visibility epoch, tenant/principal, authority ceiling, and an issuance/expiry interval. `TxnOutcomeIndex` is the sole Local token/capability lookup and attempt-lifecycle authority, mapping each scoped token to `Detailed{outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>}|Compacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest}|ExpiredTombstone{token_digest}`. `TxnOutcomeRecord` is predecessor-linked `{header,txn_token,predecessor_ref?,state:BeginStaging|NeverRegistered|Registered|PrepareAdmitted|CommittedPendingPostconditions|Committed|Aborted|ReadClosed,audit_state:NotRequired{evidence}|ClaimedPending{ticket_digest,claim_identity}|TerminalGateCommitted{ticket_digest,event_digest,resolution_digest,gate_commitment,candidate_pipeline_order},completion_state,time_authority_profile_oid,issued_at,expires_at,minimum_lookup_retention_floor}`; it moves only through `BeginStaging -> Registered/StatementOpen -> PrepareAdmitted -> CommittedPendingPostconditions -> Committed` or the typed `Aborted`/`ReadClosed`/`NeverRegistered` terminals. Every successor header equals or is a registered nonwidening successor of the registration binding; scalars are never independently forgeable. Public terminal/audit state is the join of the immutable terminal-gate commitment with the current protocol `VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex`; a missing/mismatched release remains FinalizingOpaque. No Sharded arm is encodable. Detailed terminal records keep the full authority header because they retain semantic/result/public-projection state; only a later payload-free expired tombstone may use `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Local>`, and a record never acquires a strong `AuditOutcomeRecord` edge after its candidate bytes were built. `LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(namespace,incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved{reservation_ref,capability_replay_ref}|BoundDetailed{registration_ref,capability_replay_ref}|BoundCompacted{summary_root_ref,leaf_key_digest,capability_replay_ref}|NeverRegisteredDetailed{terminal_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref,capability_replay_ref}|NeverRegisteredCompacted{...}|ExpiredTombstone{scoped_key_digest,txn_token_digest,capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}`.

Laws: an identical retry joins and returns the original durable state; a mismatched request/authority/epoch/token/idempotency key/statement/expected predecessor fails closed. Before any terminal result returns, the exact semantic outcome and required durability/delta/result/audit/resource postconditions reach `TerminalReady`. Records, compact summaries, permanent token tombstones, and verifier keys remain through the advertised lookup/retry/retention floor. After expiry, a valid-MAC matching-domain capability returns `TokenExpired` — never treated as a new transaction. Cancellation after terminal ordering may return `Unknown(txn_token)` only when the caller lacks evidence to distinguish the durable state, and resolves solely through scoped status lookup — it never promises rollback of a possibly committed transaction. `LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot` stores the full authority header with exact wire-safe public outcome/commitments, time window, result disposition commitment, lookup floor, and protocol release proof identity needed to reproduce the same response; it cannot answer an in-progress state or retain the protocol root through a semantic back-edge. `LocalOutcomeCompactionSpec` (NeverRegistered and TerminalReady arms) requires the summary leaf to copy the exact frozen public bytes/receipt from the detailed bundle, writes the authenticated leaf, and atomically changes `TxnOutcomeIndex Detailed -> Compacted` together with the begin-index `NeverRegisteredDetailed -> NeverRegisteredCompacted` or `BoundDetailed -> BoundCompacted`; status/retry bytes remain identical. `LocalOutcomeExpirySpec` is the distinct ordered transition legal only from compacted state (`expected_outcome_index_entry:Compacted`, `expected_begin_index_entry:BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredCompacted`) and carries `terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<LocalControl>`; it requires `TimeValidationEvidence` classifying the replay record's exact window Expired for this action with every advertised retry/lookup floor closed; apply atomically installs `ExpiredTombstone` in both indexes (token/key/capability commitments plus evidence digest), drops replay/bundle edges only there, and permanently prevents key/token reuse; valid old bytes return TokenExpired while invalid/unauthorized input remains NotVisibleOrUnknown.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-01: at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome per scoped key/token; detailed and compacted proofs return byte-identical public outcomes; TerminalReady exposure conditions. FG-INV-20: capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure. Retention floors are registry configuration (advertised), not invariants.

## Interactions
Populated by w2-txn-lifecycle and w2-prepare-terminal transitions; read by w10-capabilities (durable capability lookup/status), w10-fgp-core (status frames), w9-audit-pipeline (VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex join), w2-recovery (outcome reconciliation), w9-time-authority (expiry evidence). Compaction interacts with w2-retention-checkpoints floors.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: state-machine legality (no skip, no reverse); byte-identity of status responses across Detailed/Compacted/replay. CAS tests: concurrent compaction vs lookup vs expiry — one winner, stable responses. Negative: forged-scalar header substitution; cross-domain capability (NotVisibleOrUnknown); expired valid MAC (TokenExpired). Crash: compaction mid dual-index swap (both-or-neither). Fuzz: capability decode. E2E: kill client mid-commit, reconnect, resolve via status lookup with logged evidence chain; verify Unknown resolves to a definite state. DETAILED LOGGING: every `TxnOutcomeIndex`/`LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex` transition logs {scoped token/key digest, prior arm -> new arm, applied command identity, evidence digests}; status/lookup paths log {capability-domain verdict, returned state class} while remaining uniformly nonrevealing on unauthorized input; compaction and expiry log the dual-index CAS outcome; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: unbounded outcome growth — answered by compaction+expiry with permanent tombstones, never silent deletion. Rejected: in-memory dedupe caches as idempotency authority; rejected: reusing expired tokens as fresh transactions (replay confusion); rejected: revealing existence on unauthorized lookup (breaks noninterference).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.403–405, App A l.1478, l.1518, l.1534; App F FG-INV-01/20.

title: Implement prepare admission, terminal admission fences, reservations, and admitted aborts
description:
## What & scope
Implement the terminal-fencing segment of the Local lifecycle: `LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec`, the `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence` state machine (`Armed -> TerminalOrdered | Released`), `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord`, `LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec`/`LocalFinalCertificationReservation`, `TerminalWriteResultPreparation`, `TxnAbortSpec`, and `AdmittedTxnAbortCommand`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the fence/reservation pattern is what lets §5.2 step 6 voters skip revalidating mutable state — everything was atomically validated and held before signing, so certification is evidence-based, not race-based. B6: aborts are first-class ordered commands with proofs, so an agent's ROLLBACK has the same durability/idempotency guarantees as COMMIT.

## Design — normative detail
`LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec` binds `{registration_ref,expected_registered_outcome_ref,admission_generation,expected_statement_frontier,expected_delivery_frontier,expected_statement_index_digest,expected_workspace_generation_ref,expected_cumulative_read_witness_root_ref,expected_cumulative_effect_root_ref,local_serialization_certificate_ref,global_authorization_decision_ref,resource_transition_refs[],operation_audit_admission:Claimed|NotRequired,transaction_audit_basis_commitment,finalization_basis_digest,expected_branch_heads[WeakMarkerIdentity],expected_branch_key_epochs,expected_policy_epoch,expected_revocation_index,expected_conflict_index_basis:WeakStateIdentity,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply requires ReadWrite, no Open statement, contiguous terminal statement/delivery frontiers, exact workspace/witness/effect/SSI/security bases, no prior admission; it constructs immutable `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::Armed {registration_ref,admission_generation,admission_applied_ref,frozen_statement_delivery_workspace_witness_effect_commitment,frozen_branch_heads,frozen_branch_key_epochs,frozen_resource_and_constraint_commitment,frozen_policy_epoch,frozen_revocation_index,frozen_conflict_basis,operation_audit_claim_commitment,transaction_audit_basis_commitment}` (no future sequence/HLC) and makes the succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::PrepareAdmitted` the unique canonical selector of that fence, atomically replacing the token's Detailed entry. Only then are the final rebased effect directory, optional `TerminalWriteResultPreparation`, and `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord {txn_token,expected_prior_state:PrepareAdmitted{outcome_ref,terminal_admission_fence_ref,admission_generation,state_digest},proposed_terminal_kind,final_effect_digest,terminal_write_result:None|Prepared{preparation_ref,required_posture:Local},authorization_decision_ref,resource_transition_refs,terminal_audit_gate}` constructed. Before any terminal audit lock, `LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` revalidates the final rebased selection and installs the Active reservation plus coordinate/obligation holds; the stable capsule/template/D1 closure includes the reservation but no HLC/order observation. Commit apply requires the exact Armed fence and Active reservation with selection LocalCommit, atomically consumes the reservation, constructs `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::TerminalOrdered {predecessor_ref,final_certification_reservation_ref,commit_command_ref,assigned_logical_command_seq,assigned_commit_seq}`. `TerminalWriteResultPreparation::Local` (autocommit ReadWrite WriteReturning only) binds registration/prepare-admission/final effect directory+digest/deterministic RETURNING plan+certificate/manifest/result digest+contract/delivery policy/prepared owner identity/closure digest; the certificate proves manifest bytes are exactly the RETURNING projection of the final effect set; completion cannot reevaluate or substitute RETURNING bytes.

Aborts: `TxnAbortSpec` is only the active/unadmitted path `{header,registration_ref,expected_prior:Registered{outcome_ref,state_digest},all_open_statement_abort_refs[],result_disposition_proof_refs[],workspace_release_evidence_refs[],conflict_close_evidence_ref,terminal_abort_authority_ref,required_abort_source:ClientRequested|Administrative,resource_release_refs[],operation_audit_admission,terminal_audit_gate}`; it uses `LifecycleOperation::RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active}` and can never consume a PrepareAdmitted fence or reservation. `AdmittedTxnAbortCommand` is the Local transaction-order peer of `CommitCommand` (never a generic ControlCommand): `{command_version,header,registration_ref,terminal_admission_fence_ref,required_fence_state:Armed,final_certification_reservation_ref,required_reservation_state:Active,required_selection:FinalCertificationSelection::LocalAbort,required_selected_terminal_digest,order_attempt_input_ref,required_order_subject:LocalOrderSubject::Terminal{...},order_attempt_availability_certificate_ref,terminal_abort_authority_ref,complete_no_effect_and_release_proof_ref,resource_release_refs[],txn_outcome_preparation_ref,payload_availability_certificate_ref,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply marks the supplement Ordered, consumes the Active reservation, constructs `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::Released {predecessor_ref,final_certification_reservation_ref,applied_abort_ref:AppliedAbortRef::LocalTxn,assigned_logical_command_seq}`, terminalizes outcome/conflict state, releases exactly the proved holds. It cannot race an ordered commit, create a marker/delta/effect, or be synthesized from timeout. The lifecycle matrix adds `RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active|PrepareAdmitted}` with exact effect classes; the PrepareAdmitted client/admin source feeds `TerminalAbortAuthority`, while correctness-required aborts use their structural reason-specific authority. All fence transitions are new immutable objects; the outcome/reservation index CAS forbids a second successor.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: at most one legal live generation owns each final-certification basis/hold; stale/cancelled/expired owners can neither mutate nor release. FG-INV-17: once an Active reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift uses the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path. FG-INV-01: PrepareAdmitted is exclusive; Abort can never later Commit.

## Interactions
Sits between w2-txn-lifecycle (statement machine feeds admission) and w2-commit-protocol (capsule/D1/command consume the fence/reservation); order subjects from w2-hlc-order-attempt; outcome lineage in w2-outcome-tokens; W4 (w4-coordinator) later owns the full final-certification reservation choreography — this bead delivers the Local schemas and apply semantics.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Model: fence state machine exhaustive transitions (Armed exactly-once; TerminalOrdered xor Released; no second successor). DPOR: commit vs admitted-abort race on one Active reservation — exactly one wins, loser gets typed rejection. Crash: after admission before reservation; after reservation before order; after order before completion — recovery resolves per §5.2 abandonment arms. Negative: TxnAbortSpec against PrepareAdmitted (rejected); AdmittedTxnAbortCommand with selection LocalCommit (rejected); RETURNING substitution (digest mismatch fails). Property: frozen commitments byte-stability across replay. E2E: two scripted explicit transactions through the full stack — one prepare-admission -> Active reservation -> `CommitCommand` -> completion, one prepare-admission -> Active reservation -> `AdmittedTxnAbortCommand` — asserting in logs the Armed -> TerminalOrdered and Armed -> Released fence paths, reservation consumption, and exact released holds; plus a client cancel of an active unadmitted txn via `TxnAbortSpec`. DETAILED LOGGING: every fence transition logs fence state, generation, consuming command identity, reservation ref/state, and released hold identities; abort paths additionally log `required_abort_source` and proof identities; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: reservation held across audit signing lengthens hold time — bounded by the pre-signature cancel/restart path. Rejected: mutating the Armed fence in place (destroys audit evidence); rejected: abort as coordinator flag or timeout inference (FG-INV-16 forbids losing obligations; timeout is never abandonment proof); rejected: generic ControlCommand for admitted abort (needs transaction-order peer semantics).

## Provenance
Plan App A l.1520–1524, l.1530–1532; §5.2 l.393; App F FG-INV-01/02/17.

title: Implement crash recovery: the recovery equation, prepared and pipeline reconciliation
description:
## What & scope
Implement single-node recovery for Chronicle: the authoritative §5.4 recovery equation, §5.2's recovery procedure (root-slot selection, `PreparedPayloadRoot` <-> Raft log reconciliation, completion of committed-but-unapplied work), audit-pipeline recovery, verification of applied/visible endpoints and marker contiguity, and the scope boundary of RaptorQ repair.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: recovery is a deterministic equation over authenticated artifacts, not heuristic log scanning — the same equation defines Chronicle-reconstructibility for FEC tiering and backup/restore, so one verified definition serves durability, scrub, and restore. B1: recovery preserves the full version universe including invisible (audit-hidden) suffixes, so compliance postures survive crashes without leaking or losing candidates.

## Design — normative detail
The recovery equation: `state(L, C) = reconstruct_and_verify_install(RecoveryCheckpointProjection(B0 at L0,C0), retained CheckpointInstall input+record at L0+1) + apply contiguous LogicalCommandRecord suffix (L0+1, L]` where `L` is `LogicalCommandSeq` and `C` is transaction-only `CommitSeq`; the interval deliberately begins at L0+2 — the install record at L0+1 is reconstructed/verified exactly once, never replayed twice. Later retained records are contiguous; transaction records form a subsequence whose markers advance contiguously from C0; control commands do not advance CommitSeq. (Checkpoint construction/install semantics are owned by w2-retention-checkpoints; recovery consumes them.)

Procedure (§5.2): recovery starts from the highest valid root slot, reconciles `PreparedPayloadRoot` with the one-member or multi-member Raft log, completes every committed-but-unapplied command, and only then considers fenced abandonment/collection of prepared records — under the two abandonment arms: a semantic prepared owner may abandon only an unreceipted, provably unordered attempt under a current writer/configuration fence, or a receipted attempt after consensus proves it cannot be ordered and every certificate/configuration retention floor has expired; once any terminal audit lock exists, neither semantic prepared ownership nor final certification may be abandoned — only a provably unordered stale supplement may be retired/replaced; timeout or process death alone is never abandonment proof. Recovery reconciles log ownership, validates the exact command/payload closure, and idempotently applies committed work. The complete Local/Meta audit pipeline is recovered from RootManifest and the Raft closure; its gap-free candidate chain remains retained and invisible beyond the visible endpoint while recovery reconciles external terminal records/batches and may order the exact visibility-advance command. Recovery verifies both applied and visible endpoints, the authoritative checkpoint, and the contiguous logical-command suffix; for transaction records it additionally verifies the contiguous transaction-marker subsequence, authenticates and decodes every referenced final capsule, and applies canonical effects. Order-attempt reconciliation (w2-hlc-order-attempt): classify each entry Available/Ordered/RetiredStale; a stale supplement is retired with `OrderAttemptRetirementEvidence` proving at a linearizable read barrier it was never a semantic log entry/candidate. Truncation stops at visible audit-safe state and waits for the generated-complete floor (prepared transfers, cursors, replay, external continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, current/prospective configs). Delta postcondition: the `LogicalDeltaBatch` for each recovered commit is reachable from the candidate root at the first crash point at which the commit exists; recovery owns the batch through `RaftStateRoot` and the pipeline. RaptorQ may repair damaged compatible symbols within the configured erasure model; it does not replace root redundancy, payload replication, or fail-closed recovery beyond that model — missing bytes without a matching authenticated cut are corruption; a proved cut returns `HistoryUnavailable`, not a partial result.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07: before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; timeout releases no prepared/certificate/audit/result/allocation/escrow/retention owner. FG-INV-08: command order and marker subsequence contiguous; retained checkpoint suffix begins with its exact install command; only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint; provisional cuts authenticate inherited absence but authorize no new release until activation. FG-INV-10: recovery always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; closure or capability failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back or partially interprets. FG-INV-16: no obligation is lost/duplicated/released while obligated; recovery reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state under declared fairness. MTTDL/repair modeling is FG-CFG-01 (configuration-model claim), owned by w2-fec-scrub.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-order-raft (log/snapshot/hard state, gap classification, log-to-state verifier), w2-commit-protocol (capsule/prepared/command semantics), w2-root-bootstrap (slot selection), w2-writer-takeover (fencing before recovery writes), w2-retention-checkpoints (checkpoint install artifacts), w2-fec-scrub (symbol repair, RebuildFromSuffix escalation), w2-hlc-order-attempt (supplement reconciliation). Consumed by w11-restore (restore is recovery plus continuity bridging), verif-torture (crash matrices), w2-gc-core (post-recovery collection gating).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash matrix: systematic kill points across all six §5.2 steps x fsync-lie/torn-write/path-replacement profiles; each row asserts the recovered state satisfies the equation and endpoint verification. Prepared reconciliation cases: receipted-unordered (retained until proof), unreceipted-unordered (fenced abandonment), ordered-unapplied (completed), applied-unpublished-RootSlot (republished), terminal-audit-locked (never abandoned). Idempotency: double-apply of a committed command is byte-neutral. Audit: recovery with pending Required candidates keeps them hidden and re-orders the exact visibility-advance; gap-free prefix property checked. Differential: recovered state vs fgdb-reference replay of the same command stream (a verif-differential hook — this bead delivers the hook and the recovery-report fields it consumes; the replay-differential itself executes in `verif-differential` once `verif-reference` lands, both outside this bead's closure, and is validated at gate-g3). Determinism: two recoveries of the same disk image produce byte-identical roots. Logging: every recovery emits a structured report (selected slot, K, suffix range, reconciled prepared records with dispositions, repaired symbols, truncation floor holds) — required for verif-torture triage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: recovery time on long suffixes — bounded by checkpoint cadence (w2-retention-checkpoints), measured in §17 endurance rows. Rejected: best-effort roll-forward with partial interpretation (FG-INV-10 forbids); rejected: treating timeout as abandonment proof (loses receipted attempts that consensus may still order); rejected: replaying the checkpoint-install record twice (double-install corruption — the (L0+1] boundary exists precisely for this); rejected: RaptorQ as a substitute for replication/root redundancy.

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.407, §5.4 l.423–429, §5.7 l.477, §14.W1 l.1070; App F FG-INV-07/08/10/16.

## Comprehensive recovery E2E and diagnostic evidence
- Unit tests cover highest-credible-slot selection, checkpoint-install single application, contiguous logical suffix and transaction-marker subsequence validation, each prepared disposition, audit applied/visible endpoint reconciliation, repair-within-budget versus fail-closed, and every typed `HistoryUnavailable`/corruption refusal.
- Property/model tests generate authenticated root/checkpoint/suffix/prepared/audit states, crash at every prefix, recover twice, and assert deterministic idempotence, no sequence gaps/double install, no timeout-only abandonment, no hidden-candidate exposure, and equality with canonical replay.
- Full E2E under the lab VFS: create an isolated database fixture, commit mixed transaction/control commands with statement/workspace/result and Required-audit states, install a checkpoint, leave receipted-unordered and ordered-unapplied records, inject torn write/fsync lie/bit flip/process death at every recovery phase, reopen through the public Database/server path, drive reconciliation to legal terminal/recoverable state, compare with `fgdb-reference`, then reopen a second time and require byte-identical roots and public status. A live-process companion kills only the isolated fixture process during writer takeover and proves the stale writer is fenced.
- Structured JSONL for every unit/property/matrix/E2E step: `{run_id,scenario_id,seed,filesystem_failure_profile,crash_point_id,recovery_phase,selected_root_slot,root_generation,checkpoint_id,L0,C0,target_L,target_C,suffix_range,transaction_marker_range,prepared_id,receipt_order_audit_lock_state,prepared_disposition,repaired_symbol_ids,retention_floor_holds,applied_visible_audit_visible_before_after,expected,actual,oracle_verdict,reference_digest,recovered_root_digest,reopen_digest,verdict}`. Failures include the complete secret-redacted §15.1 artifact, first divergent command/field, minimized disk image/workload reference, and executable replay command; sampled commands run in CI.
- Evidence completeness: passing rows use the same schema as failures; the G1/G3 consumers may count this recovery evidence only when its model profile and exact clause IDs match. Missing log ancestry or a nondeterministic second reopen is a hard failure.

title: Implement retention tiers, KEEP policies, and checkpoint authority transfer
description:
## What & scope
Implement Chronicle's One Version Universe retention machinery for the Local role: the three query-retention tiers, per-graph `KEEP` policies, the recovery-equation checkpoint discipline, `CheckpointInstallSpec` construction/apply, the `RetentionCutBody` -> `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet` -> `HistoryCutActivationSpec` -> `ActivatedRetentionCutSet` pipeline, the `RetentionMap`, conditional-reference traversal semantics, and the effective-floor set. Excludes the compaction actor (w2-compaction), delta-batch retention cuts (w2-delta-batches), and physical reclamation (w2-gc-core).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: retired MVCC versions ARE the temporal database — `AS OF`, PITR, and audit ride the same commit stream, not a bolted-on history store. §3.1's AeonG verdict is "adopt and unify": AeonG bolts anchor+delta temporal onto Memgraph (≈5.7x storage reduction); here anchors = sealed checkpoints and deltas = the durably ordered commit stream we already have, so temporal is a corollary of durability. frankensqlite's §2.3 lesson: temporal support rides the MVCC machinery, never duplicates it. History is queryable for the configured retention contract, never marketed as unbounded when policy permits reclamation.

## Design — normative detail
Recovery equation: `state(L, C) = reconstruct_and_verify_install(RecoveryCheckpointProjection(B0 at L0,C0), retained CheckpointInstall input+record at L0+1) + apply contiguous LogicalCommandRecord suffix (L0+1, L]` where `L` is `LogicalCommandSeq`, `C` is transaction-only `CommitSeq`. The suffix deliberately begins at `L0+2`: the install record at `L0+1` is reconstructed/verified exactly once, never replayed twice. Tiers: **Tier 0** live MVCC (current version chains + unsealed deltas); **Tier 1** warm columnar logical effects sorted by `(element_id, commit_seq)`, directly queryable for recent `AS OF`/`BETWEEN`; **Tier 2** historical checkpoints = full compressed partition snapshots plus a bounded logical-effect suffix; optional inter-object delta compression names an explicit base ObjectId, forms an acyclic bounded-depth dependency graph, and is applied BEFORE each payload is independently RaptorQ encoded — RaptorQ is never a delta codec. Retention is per graph `KEEP ALL | KEEP <duration|seqs> | KEEP NONE`; physical collection is governed by the conservative union of all roots.

`RecoveryCheckpoint {basis_logical_command_seq, basis_commit_seq, command_basis:Genesis{command_chain_genesis_seed}|Ordered{covered_basis_logical_command:WeakCommandIdentity, covered_command_chain_hash}, marker_basis:NoCommittedTransactionAtBasis{marker_chain_genesis_seed, proof_ref}|Committed{covered_global_marker:StrongMarkerRef, covered_marker_chain_hash}, basis_payload_digest:WeakDigest, basis_projection_digest, logical_hlc_state, checkpoint_state_vector_ref, nonretaining_predecessor_checkpoint_digest}`. `Genesis` legal iff seq=0; `NoCommittedTransactionAtBasis` legal iff commit_seq=0 (control-only databases checkpoint without inventing a marker). The weak command identity plus chain/payload/projection commitments authenticates the cut without retaining prior command/spec/checkpoint chains. `CheckpointStateVector` is role-tagged with exactly one typed entry per payload-schema field from the closed recipe union `CopiedStrong|ProjectedSnapshot|ResetByCheckpointInstall|SelfExcluded|InstallProvisionalCut{field_tag=retention_map_root, retention_cut_body_ref, checkpoint_binding=InstallThisCheckpoint, install_input_kind, assigned_order_literal}|ApplyActivationProjection`; `InstallProvisionalCut` is required exactly once for an operational basis, forbidden for Genesis; Local-activation Meta/Shard bases use `ApplyActivationProjection` only for fields covered by the certified projection recipe, and the generated role/basis matrix rejects either special tag anywhere else. `recovery_checkpoint_ref` uses `SelfExcluded{InstallThisCheckpoint}`; operational `config_payload_floor_ref` uses `SelfExcluded{InstallPairedConfigFloor}` — copying the old floor would recreate an unbounded floor -> checkpoint -> prior-floor retention chain; Genesis copies the absent floor as `None`. `basis_projection_digest = BLAKE3("fgdb:checkpoint-projection:v1" || canonical(vector reconstruction with exact literals))`; it never hashes a future checkpoint/floor/cut OID.

`CheckpointInstallSpec {basis:WeakStateIdentity, basis_logical_command_seq, basis_commit_seq, basis_payload_digest, basis_projection_digest, checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>, checkpoint_state_vector_digest, paired_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>?, retention_cut_body_ref:StrongRef<RetentionCutBody>?, reset_field_tags[]}` is the exact first retained command at `L0+1`. Acyclic construction: basis/projection + checkpoint-free cut recipes -> `RetentionCutBody` -> `CheckpointStateVector` -> `RecoveryCheckpoint` -> (operational) paired floor with weak checkpoint observation -> install spec. Genesis: both optionals `None`, no `InstallProvisionalCut` entry; operational: both `Some`, with body/vector/checkpoint/floor covering the same prefix and configuration. Apply verifies the current basis/projection, replaces `recovery_checkpoint_ref`, atomically swaps the floor, installs the deterministic provisional cut, performs only the listed `ResetByCheckpointInstall` values (each with its registered equivalence/semantic-transition proof), and changes no other field. `InitialConfigFloorInstallSpec` is the sole local `CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` transition. Authority becomes effective only after projection/equivalence/floor verification, install-command + payload durability, root publication, and the configured replica-durability gate — an explicit transfer of recovery and configuration-payload authority, not a derived cache silently becoming primary.

The cut pipeline (exact object schemas in w2-retention-cut-objects): the checkpoint-free `RetentionCutBody` — containing the role's one command-cut recipe plus every marker/effect recipe to be superseded, and naming NO checkpoint identity — is consumed by install-apply into a deterministic `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet`, which the later ordered `HistoryCutActivationSpec` strengthens into an `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`; the `RetentionMap` holds policy epochs plus exactly one `Provisional|Activated` entry per retained cut body. **Domination law**: a provisional cut may authenticate bytes already absent under inherited activated coverage but satisfies NO new-reclamation, key-destruction, backup-pin-release, remote-release, topology-retirement, or ownership-discharge predicate; a replacement provisional must dominate every absorbed activated absence until its own activation; only an `ActivatedRetentionCutSet` authorizes new physical release.

Conditional references: capsule effect directories and `LogicalDeltaTemplate` entries use `ConditionalCoordinateRef{oid, graph, branch}` — while a capsule is pending, traversal from `PreparedPayloadRoot` treats every conditional edge as strong; after commit the marker supplies the retention coordinate and a cut may stop only the matching coordinate at/below its verified boundary. Command/marker predecessor links use `ConditionalCommandRef`/`ConditionalMarkerRef`, cuttable only on the matching axis. Branch/fork/merge bases and all other strong roots always win. Missing bytes without a matching cut are corruption; a proved cut returns `HistoryUnavailable`, never a partial result. Effective floors include: stable prepared owners and consensus commands, transaction outcomes, branch manifests/key epochs/envelope roots/recipient+advancing grants/merge idempotency state, identity/privacy/audit external continuity, DP request+seed+result, audit ticket/event/resolution/receipt/gap state, replay registry/manifests/archives, resume cursors and baseline/delta/snapshot leases, backup/legal holds, current/prospective configuration floors, keys, and transparency policy. Floor checkpoint/vector observations are explicitly weak (`CurrentCheckpointObservation` is the sole weak-checkpoint exception, byte-matched against the separately strong current payload checkpoint). Checkpoint-fold FEC law (§5.7): an install that folds a reduced-repair (`fec_profile`) object into the authoritative closure must either recode it to the full-budget profile (changing only `EncodingId`, never `ObjectId`/`CiphertextId`) or materialize independent full-FEC checkpoint payloads; the cut activation permitting suffix reclamation fails closed until the chosen path is durable. Overrides, cuts, and retained bytes are observable. PITR, temporal queries, raw CDC, and compliance audit all reuse Chronicle ordering but are NOT identical retention products: PITR is bounded by retained checkpoints/effects, compliance audit rides its separate signed retention chain (§12.8), replay requires its evidence closure (§8.6), and derived subscriptions consume canonical `LogicalDeltaBatch` objects (§9), never unresolved intents.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08 (invariant): logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their respective sequences; every retained checkpoint suffix begins with its exact install command; provisional cuts authenticate inherited absence but authorize no new release until activation. FG-INV-07 (invariant): every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; timeout releases no retention owner. FG-INV-14 (invariant): GC follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim. FG-CFG-01 (configuration-model class, never an invariant): the CTMC MTTDL report must model per-tier `fec_profile` reconstruction and the checkpoint-fold recode path. Checkpoint cadence and space amplification are empirical/configuration gates (benchmark class).

## Interactions
Consumes the `LogicalCommandRecord`/marker stream and capsule closure from w2-commit-protocol; implements the recovery equation with w2-recovery; publishes through w2-root-bootstrap. w2-delta-batches' delta cuts require the paired ordinary activated cut installed here; w2-compaction traverses installed cuts; w2-gc-core requires `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`; w2-branch-retire activates the branch cut through this machinery; the fold-recode law binds w2-fec-scrub. Schemas/recipes are generated from g0-identity-registries; command rows from g0-command-contracts.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generated coverage/DAG checkers reject role mismatch, mixed basis, omitted field, future ref, or result-recipe mismatch. Unit: Genesis-vs-operational legality matrix (optionals, exactly-once `InstallProvisionalCut`). Property: install record verified exactly once, never replayed. Control-only checkpoint/cut/recovery fixtures cover every `(logical_seq>0, commit_seq=0)` crash point. Crash/recovery campaigns begin with bytes already reclaimed under the prior cut and interrupt every install/activation step. Oracles: query below a proved cut returns `HistoryUnavailable`; missing bytes without a matching cut are flagged corruption. Differential: KEEP-policy configurations vs conservative-union collection. E2e script: checkpoint install -> cut activation -> reclaim, logging basis digests, vector recipes, cut bodies, and activation records for post-hoc audit.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: self-referential checkpoints (solved by weak basis + `SelfExcluded`); copying the prior config floor (unbounded retention chain); replica positions/gossip as retention authority; "unbounded history" marketing. Risk: recipe/coverage drift between generated vector and payload schema — mitigated by G0 bijection CI. Risk: fold-recode cost spikes at install — priced via Appendix G, gated empirically, never skipped.

## Provenance
§5.4 (421-440), §5.7 fold law (477), App A checkpoint/cut rows (~1958-1966, 2037), §2.3, §3.1.

title: Specify retention cut objects: RetentionCutBody, provisional and activated cut sets
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact retention-cut object family split out of w2-retention-checkpoints: the pre-order cut-recipe union, `RetentionCutBody`, `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet`, `HistoryCutActivationSpec`, `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`, and the `RetentionMap` entry discipline. w2-retention-checkpoints owns the tiers/KEEP/install-authority semantics and the domination law; this bead owns the schemas, construction-order proofs, and their crash coverage.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: the entire One Version Universe rests on cuts that transfer authority to checkpoint+install+suffix without ever creating a forward reference to a not-yet-computed checkpoint. B5: every reclaimed byte must be attributable to a proved, ordered cut object — absence without a matching cut is corruption, never an excuse.

## Design — normative detail
The checkpoint-free pre-order cut-recipe union is `CommandCutRecipe {axis:Logical, stop_at:WeakCommandIdentity} | GlobalCommandCutRecipe {axis:GlobalLogical, stop_at:WeakGlobalCommandIdentity, exact_covered_global_prefix} | ShardCommandCutRecipe {axis:ShardRaft, stop_at:WeakShardCommandIdentity, exact_covered_shard_raft_index, exact_covered_global_prefix} | MarkerCutRecipe {axis, stop_at:WeakMarkerIdentity} | EffectCutRecipe {graph, branch, through_seq, effect_payload_digest_range}` (Local role uses the Logical/marker/effect arms; Global/Shard arms are generated here for W12 reuse). `RetentionCutBody {role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id}, basis_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity, command_cut_recipe, sorted_marker_cut_recipes[], sorted_effect_cut_recipes[], covered_policy_epoch, covered_coordinate_set_commitment, verified_first_retained_order, completeness_digest}` must contain the role's one command recipe plus every marker/effect recipe to be superseded. It contains NO checkpoint identity or reference and therefore exists before the vector/checkpoint that will consume it; construction is strictly `RetentionCutBody -> CheckpointStateVector -> RecoveryCheckpoint -> checkpoint-install input`. The vector's `InstallProvisionalCut` entry means "attach this body to `InstallThisCheckpoint` at the assigned install order"; it never points backward from the body to that checkpoint.

Apply deterministically constructs `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet {body_ref:StrongRef<RetentionCutBody>, checkpoint_ref:Local{StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>}|Meta{StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>}|Shard{StrongRef<ShardRecoveryCheckpoint>}, install_input_ref:Local{StrongRef<ControlCommand>, assigned_logical_command_seq}|Meta{StrongRef<GlobalControlCommand>, assigned_global_logical_command_seq}|Shard{StrongRef<ShardControlCommand>, assigned_shard_raft_index}, basis_projection_digest:WeakDigest}` BEFORE constructing the payload; role, basis, recipe, checkpoint/vector, assigned order, and install-input fields must match exactly. The checkpoint and input are already known at apply time; the future result root/record is not named — the outer state root and command head then prove the corresponding applied record. `HistoryCutActivationSpec {provisional_cut_ref, checkpoint_install_record_ref:StrongCommandRef, expected_retention_map_basis:WeakStateIdentity, verified_contiguous_suffix_start, terminal_audit_gate}` is the sole local strengthening path (Global/Shard use the matching record tags); apply creates `ActivatedRetentionCutSet {provisional_cut_ref, checkpoint_install_record_ref, activation_applied_ref:AuthorityAppliedRef}` and atomically replaces that provisional map entry. Operational checkpoint reset atomically drops superseded entries and installs the new provisional set; at every crash point, either the old activated authority or the new provisional authority authenticates already-missing bytes. Traversal may stop only when axis/group/checkpoint/body completeness and the provisional input+assigned-order or activated record proof all validate; strong roots always win. A cut transfers authority to checkpoint+install+suffix; it does not assert that pruned capsules or old delta ranges remain individually recoverable.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08 (invariant): provisional cuts authenticate inherited absence but authorize no new release until activation. FG-INV-07 (invariant): the body is a pre-order input that excludes its future checkpoint/result/root; self IDs and mutually strong cycles are unencodable. FG-INV-14 (invariant): reclamation predicates accept only `ActivatedRetentionCutSet`.

## Interactions
Consumed by w2-retention-checkpoints' install-apply and domination law; `HistoryCutActivationSpec` gates w2-gc-core reclamation, w2-branch-retire finalize, and w2-compaction retirement; ordering/apply via w2-commit-protocol; schemas and generated DAG/coverage checkers from g0-identity-registries; command rows from g0-command-contracts. W12 roles (w12-recovery-gc) reuse the Global/Shard arms.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generated checkers reject a body naming any checkpoint identity, a vector entry without exactly one operational `InstallProvisionalCut`, or a provisional set whose fields mismatch body/checkpoint/input. Property: construction-order fuzzing can never produce a forward reference. Crash tests interrupt every install/activation step for all three roles and begin with bytes already reclaimed under the prior cut; the old-activated-or-new-provisional authentication law is asserted at each point. Negative: traversal stop without completeness+proof validation is rejected; strong-root override verified. Golden vectors for each recipe arm and both cut-set unions. E2e script: body -> vector -> checkpoint -> install -> provisional set -> activation -> reclaim on a Local fixture, then the generated Global/Shard arms under the W12 test roles, verifying at each step that reclamation predicates accept only the activated set. DETAILED LOGGING (required of implementation and tests): every construction and transition logs role, body completeness_digest, covered_policy_epoch, checkpoint/vector identities, install-input assigned order, provisional-set and activated-set identities, RetentionMap entry replacement events (superseded entry -> successor entry), and each traversal-stop decision with its validating proof identities; the crash suites assert the old-activated-or-new-provisional authentication law from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a body that names its enclosing checkpoint (cycle); scalar-epoch cut authority (cannot authenticate absence); activation folded into install (would let a crash between install and activation authorize reclaim). Risk: recipe/coverage drift across roles — held by the generated role-tag matrix.

## Provenance
§5.4 (427-437), App A cut rows (~1962-1966, 2037).

title: Implement RootSlot dual-slot frames, RootBootstrap self-sufficient recovery, RootManifest
description:
## What & scope
Implement `manifest.root`: the fixed two-slot bootstrap file (the only published durable bytes updated in place), the exact `RootSlot`/`RootBootstrap` frames, self-sufficient root recovery, recovery slot selection, and the `RootManifest` four-posture union with its deliberate metadata-tree exclusion. The publication sequencer/permit/evidence machinery is the sibling subtask `w2-root-publication`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is B1's published-recovery-root constitution: one fixed-location, tear-validated, generation-alternating frame from which the entire database — semantic, protocol, prepared, and consensus planes — is reachable and authenticatable without any pre-existing index. Everything else being immutable is only safe because this one mutable thing has an exhaustively specified format and recovery rule. frankensqlite's root-publication design is the donor; Chronicle re-specifies it with self-sufficient bootstrap descriptors (the root carries its own complete cipher/encoding/placement description) so recovery never depends on an index the root itself must bootstrap.

## Design — normative detail
Each slot is exactly 4096 bytes at offsets 0 and 4096. `RootSlot { magic="FGRT", format_major:u16, format_minor:u16, slot_generation:u64, local_writer_fence_epoch:u64, database_id:[u8;16], database_security_namespace_id:[u8;32], cluster_incarnation:u64, incarnation_continuity_profile_id:u16, cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest:[u8;32], continuity_cas_version:u64, service_visibility_epoch:u64, root_manifest_oid:[u8;32], bootstrap:RootBootstrap, reserved_zeroes, tear_checksum:[u8;32] }`. `RootBootstrap` supplies everything needed **before** the object-location index exists: `{ root_encoding_id, root_placement_id, root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id, root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len, root_symbol_inventory_digest, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, nonce_len, nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, opener_kind, oid_key_id, opener_payload_len, opener_payload:[u8;1024], opener_digest }`; unused nonce/opener bytes are zero. Together with `root_manifest_oid` these reproduce the root's exact `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest`, complete `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`, and specialized ContiguousSpan `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` byte-for-byte. `opener_payload` is a versioned bundle of inline wraps or authenticated KMS/HSM locators sufficient to recover both the root DEK and immutable `K_oid` without consulting the object index; its digest covers kind, key IDs, locators/wraps, and namespace/incarnation.

Recovery: locate the declared span → scan and authenticate its exact `SymbolRecord` inventory → verify the sorted inventory commitment and recomputed `root_placement_id` → reconstruct the exact object AAD and encoding transcript → decode the root → verify its keyed `ObjectId` → only then consult its indexes. No descriptor or identity-key field comes from the object being opened; `ObjectId` is already the full logical digest (no redundant `root_full_digest`); recovery rejects a root whose authenticated namespace/database/incarnation/continuity/profile/visibility tuple disagrees with the slot. Slot selection: first discard slots whose fixed record fails structural/tear validation, then select the highest remaining generation; once a slot is structurally credible, authentication or mandatory-closure failure triggers symbol/replica repair and then **fails closed** — never silent rollback to an older authenticated state that may precede an acknowledged commit; an older generation requires §16's explicit restore protocol. Two structurally credible equal-highest generations are accepted for read recovery only when their complete authenticated slot bytes are identical; any difference fail-closes; write mode first normalizes an identical-equal pair through a specialized takeover/convergence permit or remains read-only.

**RootManifest**: the exact four-posture role-tagged union rendered authoritatively in Appendix A. Every active arm has one applied Semantic root, one role-valid Protocol root, one PreparedOwnership root, one Consensus/Raft root, and the exact position tuple those roots jointly prove; Local/Meta visible endpoints are selected only inside `AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Role>`, Shard visibility by `ShardProtocolState` plus its imported Meta projection; no direct audit-pipeline or visible-root field is encoded in RootManifest. `RetiredLocal` retains only its compact nonsemantic certified transition/retirement proof closure and rejects every semantic, protocol, prepared, Raft, or service root. Mutation/recovery starts from the applied Semantic root; ordinary/public reads start from the Protocol-selected visible endpoint; metadata-tree entries remain nonretaining locators resolved only after plane-aware liveness. **Metadata-tree exclusion**: the current RootManifest is deliberately absent from every metadata-tree generation it bootstraps — its slot's `RootBootstrap` is its sole opener, and a tree `closure_digest` covers only the already-constructed tree closure, excluding the slot, the current manifest, and the bootstrap bytes; a later generation may index an older manifest only as nonretaining history after that older identity is known. This prevents a future-root identity from entering the tree whose identity the root must already name.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10 (verbatim core): under the accepted filesystem/crash profile the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure with exact applied/visible/service positions; closure or capability failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back or partially interprets. FG-INV-09's root-bootstrap clause: root bootstrap reconstructs all identities without indexes. FG-INV-07: the manifest-exclusion rule keeps the durable graph acyclic. `bootstrap_frames.toml` fixes byte size, offsets, alternation/update protocol, tear-validation rule, opener fields, compatibility gate, and recovery test vectors (registry-class artifacts).

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-object-identity` (descriptor reconstruction, SymbolRecord auth), `w2-filesystem-profiles` (slot_write_rule, sync obligations), `g0-identity-registries` (`bootstrap_frames.toml` row), `g0-format-arms`. Produces the frames and recovery rule consumed by `w2-root-publication` (writes them), `w2-writer-takeover` (step-3 authentication), `w2-recovery`, `w2-snapshots-leases`, and every restore path; `w2-continuity-profiles` fields ride in the slot.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Golden recovery vectors from `bootstrap_frames.toml`. Crash/corruption matrix: torn slot bytes at arbitrary offsets (tear_checksum rejects); both-slots-torn fails closed; equal-generation identical pair readable, differing pair fail-closed; authentication failure after structural credibility triggers repair-then-fail-closed (no silent fallback to the older slot). Property: decode → re-encode of RootSlot/RootBootstrap is byte-identical; reconstructed descriptors byte-match originals for randomized roots. Negative: a root whose namespace/incarnation tuple disagrees with slot bytes is rejected before closure traversal; a manifest identity inside its own metadata-tree generation is a construction-DAG failure. E2E: bootstrap-from-cold-directory script logging span scan, symbol-authentication counts, inventory-digest checks, and each selection decision.
