Consumes w4-secure-view (disclosure contracts, authorization binding in evidence), w2-commit-protocol (constraint evidence rides `CommittedEffectCapsule.constraint_evidence`), w3-tier-d (before-image reads). Produces: the state the w4-merge-ladder reruns per rung 3; `TemporalConstraintStateRoot` machinery for w4-temporal-nonoverlap; owner reservations held by w4-coordinator's obligation hold root; branch overlay retirement consumed by w2-branch-retire dispositions; w4-bulk-ddl publishes through this state; w12-constraints-authority generalizes ownership to Meta.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Exhaustive per-body unit tests: each of the 11 bodies enforced synchronously at finalization, including cascade/endpoint/slice-set-driven net changes; checked-arithmetic overflow rejects, never wraps. (2) Property test: any generated effect set produces sorted, unique, no-op-free mutations whose composition equals the logical net change (differential vs reference evaluator). (3) Fork/merge tests: sibling branches resolving the same unique key to different elements do not conflict or leak until merge; merge rebuilds/revalidates affected entries into the target root. (4) Construction-DAG negative fixtures: any object naming its future marker/command fails the generated checker. (5) Concurrency: two concurrent writers claiming one equality key — exactly one commits, the other gets the disclosure-contract-conformant error (blind writer rejected pre-probe; verify zero probe I/O via trace logging). (6) Crash matrix: crash between mutation-batch construction and apply leaves before-root authoritative; retry is idempotent. (7) Restricted-IR fuzz: Check/Regex predicates fuzzed for fuel/memory-bound enforcement, no native escape. (8) Reservation tests: overlapping key/range acquisitions resolve to one deterministic winner in canonical coordinate/constraint/key order; injected delays never expire a Held reservation by clock; commit consumes exactly the held set and abort/cancel releases exactly it (coverage differencing). (9) e2e constraint script: two concurrent sessions race a Unique key, a Cardinality cap, and a Referential target end-to-end through commit, then a corrupt-root injection verifies fail-closed writes and a rebuild reproducing the expected ObjectId. DETAILED LOGGING: every `ConstraintStateTransition` logs {transition_id, before_root, after_root, mutation_count}; every reservation event logs {reservation_id, state, sorted_domain_keys}; every disclosure decision logs {contract_arm, rejected_pre_probe} with no identity/value payload; tests assert these structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: u128 aggregates and interval trees on hot paths — mitigated by map sharding and derived (rebuildable) interval structures. Rejected: index-backed asynchronous uniqueness (phantoms under concurrency); constraint state inside indexes (must survive index rebuild); per-label key scoping (keys belong to a declared constraint domain, §4.5).

## Provenance
Plan App A (1970-1978), §4.5 (227), §12.3 (888), §7.4 rung 3; Appendix F FG-INV-18/02/07.

title: Build the WriteCoordinator choreography and final-certification reservation/holds
description:
## What & scope
Implement the WriteCoordinator actor (§7.6) and the Local final-certification reservation machinery: `LocalFinalCertificationReservation`, `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Role>`, the two hold roots, the finalization-allocation half of reserve apply (the `FinalizationAllocationPlan<Local>` the reserve spec names and the `FinalizationAllocationReservationRecord<Local>` it installs), and the terminal-apply consumption rule. This is where validation results become an irreversible, held certification basis. The pre-signature cancellation path (`LocalFinalCertificationCancelSpec` + `NoTerminalPlanLockShareOrOrderProof`) is split into w4-cert-cancel.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the reservation converts "we validated X" into a durable, exclusively-owned, atomically-consumed object, so terminal signing never re-reads mutable state and no race can reinterpret an authorized terminal. B1: single ordered command stream; the coordinator is the funnel where FCW/SSI/merge-ladder/constraints/escrow all compose. Donor lesson (§2.3): frankensqlite's WriteCoordinator is a useful ordering shape, NOT a promise that final-effect regeneration, authorization, payload availability, or consensus is off the critical path — the complete D1/D2/Raft path is benchmarked and failure-tested.

## Design — normative detail
Actor choreography (§7.6): WriteCoordinator is a supervised actor. Commit requests arrive on a two-phase MPSC whose reserve/commit protocol prevents a cancelled producer from publishing a partial queue entry. Its response is a oneshot obligation whose unresolved terminal state is detected by the obligation/leak oracle; detection is not confused with impossibility. Group-commit batching uses bounded queues and the three-lane scheduler (cancel/EDF/ready) with an explicitly tested fairness/deadline policy, rather than claiming an EDF hint alone proves starvation freedom. These are typed runtime contracts plus lab-tested database state-machine obligations, not guarantees inherited without integration evidence.

Reservation schema (App A, exact): `LocalFinalCertificationReservation {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>, source_spec_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec>, registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>, terminal_admission_fence_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>, admission_generation, certification_generation, selection:FinalCertificationSelection::LocalCommit|LocalAbort, validated_branch_head_and_key_epoch_commitment, validated_policy_revocation_and_authority_commitment, validated_conflict_serialization_commitment, validated_local_configuration_commitment, exclusive_coordinate_head_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalCoordinateHoldRoot>, resource_constraint_id_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalObligationHoldRoot>, applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef, state:Active|CancelledBeforeSignature{cancel_applied_ref,release_commitment}|Consumed{terminal_input_identity, assigned_logical_command_seq}}`. An Active reservation additionally has a distinct `escrow_rights_hold_root_ref` beyond resource/constraint holds (§4.7). Selection, header, registration, terminal fence, authority decision or abort authority, and every held root must byte-match. Apply reruns every named validation against current state and atomically installs the Active record in `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot` with the two hold roots. Reserve apply is also §4.5/App A's allocation gate for confined values: `LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` names the `FinalizationAllocationPlan<Local>` built during finalization (schema and confined-tmp-ref bijection law owned by `w2-escape-bindings`), and its apply atomically updates `IdAllocatorState`, installs `FinalizationAllocationReservationRecord<Local> {plan_ref, registration_identity, finalization_generation, sorted_mappings, permanent_spent_extension_commitment, applied_control_ref, state:Active}`, and installs the Active final-certification/constraint/resource/escrow holds together; only afterward are final effects, terminal result preparation, capsule, and terminal audit bytes constructed, and each strongly names the reservation record. Terminal apply atomically replaces the allocation record with `Consumed{terminal_input_identity, marker_identity}`; cancel or abort replaces it with `AbandonedSpent{terminal_or_cancel_identity, tombstone_summary_ref}` — because durable plan/effect candidates may already name the values, capacity is never returned. A conflicting commit/head change, key retirement/destruction, policy/revocation reclamation, topology/configuration retirement, resource release, or GC must wait, transfer the reservation exactly, or reject; later revocation still fences new work and unsent output but cannot reinterpret this already authorized terminal.

`TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Role>`: authenticated map `(registration identity, admission generation, certification generation) -> latest StrongRef<RoleFinalCertificationReservation>` plus a unique-active selector per registration, hold-root coverage bitmap, nonretaining predecessor digest, and body digest. Reserve CASes absence/cancelled predecessor to Active; terminal apply or cancel replaces exactly that value with an immutable Consumed or Cancelled successor. Any state transition that can affect a held predicate is generated with a mandatory reservation-conflict check; deleting any such check is a G0 negative fixture.

Consumption: the final Local `CommitCommand`/admitted abort no longer revalidates mutable heads/key/policy/revocation/conflict/resource bases; it verifies the Active reservation, semantic prepared closure, and exact selected terminal, then atomically moves the reservation to `Consumed{terminal_input_identity, assigned_logical_command_seq}` and the admission fence to `TerminalOrdered|Released`. Unrelated commands may interleave; commands touching a reserved basis cannot. Crash/reconfiguration/checkpoint floors retain and transfer every Active reservation and hold.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: the final-certification basis has at most one legal live owner; stale/cancelled owners can neither mutate nor release. FG-INV-16: no reservation, hold, prepared closure, or oneshot obligation is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state. FG-INV-17's freeze clause: once Active, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift uses the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path. FG-INV-11 (finalization clause): confined values are reserved by the finalization plan before capsule/effect construction; the permanent spent-extension commitment survives commit, cancel, and abort — capacity is never returned. FG-INV-07: construction DAG — the reservation precedes and is named by the command; no pre-order input names its future applied record. Group-commit throughput/fairness results are `benchmark`-class.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-commit-protocol (capsules, D1 closure, order-attempt supplements the command names), w2-order-raft (ordering), w2-group-commit (batch/barrier fusion), w2-txn-lifecycle (`TxnOutcomePreparationRecord`, fences, admitted-abort command), w4-mvcc-locks (final lock-set acquisition feeding the holds), w4-merge-ladder (rebase before reservation), w2-escape-bindings (`FinalizationAllocationPlan<Local>` schema, escaped-binding preservation, and the confined-tmp-ref bijection law consumed at reserve apply). Produces: the Active-reservation discipline consumed by w4-cert-cancel (pre-signature cancellation), w4-escrow (escrow hold root), w9-audit-pipeline (audit plan binds the reservation), w12-certification (batch arm of the reservation generalizes this schema — the single-candidate schema is exactly the degenerate one-member batch).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) MPSC cancellation test: a producer cancelled between reserve and commit publishes nothing (DPOR exploration); obligation/leak oracle detects any unresolved oneshot. (2) Reservation lifecycle model: CAS absence/cancelled->Active; exactly one Consumed or Cancelled successor; double-consume and consume-after-cancel are negative fixtures. (3) Reservation-conflict check generation: for every state transition affecting a held predicate, CI verifies the generated conflict check exists; a fixture with the check deleted fails G0. (4) Freeze test: injected head drift after Active reservation forces cancel/restart, never in-place rebase (assert via ordered-event logs). (5) Crash matrix: crash between reserve-apply and terminal command; across reconfiguration — Active reservations and holds are retained/transferred exactly. (6) Fairness/deadline policy: three-lane scheduler soak with adversarial arrival; starvation bounds measured and published (benchmark-class), no starvation-freedom claim from EDF hints alone. (7) e2e commit script: full propose->validate->reserve->D1->order->apply->acknowledge path with structured logging at every barrier; logs must show zero mutable-base revalidation at terminal apply. (8) Finalization-allocation rows: reserve apply installs the allocation reservation record atomically with the holds and the `IdAllocatorState` update; commit yields `Consumed{terminal_input_identity, marker_identity}`; cancel/abort yields `AbandonedSpent` and never returns capacity; a `FinalizationAllocationPlan` containing a previously escaped slot or an incomplete confined-tmp-ref bijection fails apply (shared negative fixtures with `w2-escape-bindings`).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: reservation adds a command-latency step — amortized by group commit; Appendix G rows price the barrier chain. Risk: hold conflicts serialize hot coordinates — by design (correctness); merge ladder + escrow reduce the need. Rejected: revalidate-at-commit (races reinterpret authorized terminals); timeout-based abandonment (timeout or process death alone is never abandonment proof); treating donor WriteCoordinator behavior as inherited guarantees.

## Provenance
Plan §7.6 (647-649), App A (1744-1754, 1896-1898), §5.2 step 6 (393), §4.7 hold paragraph (254); Appendix F FG-INV-02/16/17/07/11.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement EscrowRightsTransitionSpec arms, branch seeds, and merge semantics
description:
## What & scope
Implement the closed `EscrowRightsTransitionSpec` union — the ONLY registered rights transitions — plus escrow branch fork/merge semantics: `EscrowBranchSeed` overlays, squash-merge replay, AuthorityGlobal single-consumption, and `RetireBranchOverlay` burning. Split from w4-escrow for size.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Conservation (FG-INV-02) is only as strong as the mint/burn discipline: if any code path can create or destroy rights outside registered, proof-carrying transitions, the Lean conservation lane proves nothing about production. B6: branch-per-agent workloads need branch-local escrow capacity that appears at fork and provably disappears at retire.

## Design — normative detail
`EscrowRightsTransitionSpec` is the closed Local union `TransferAtomic | ReconfigureDomain | AdvanceQuotaEpoch | RetireBranchOverlay | CompactTerminalEvidence` (a required Local semantic registry row; missing/extra/wrong-plane rows fail G0).

`TransferAtomic` CASes exact source/target generations and exact retry returns the same record (via `EscrowTransferRecord` idempotency keys; states `PreparedDebit|TargetStaged|Activated|CancelledBeforeStage`). `ReconfigureDomain` requires no unaccounted Held/InTransit custody or a complete migration mapping; tightening a bound fails unless burnable Available rights suffice. `AdvanceQuotaEpoch` is an ordered transition with subject-bound rollback-resistant `TimeValidationEvidence`; ambient time never mints rights, and old-epoch holds finish or block rollover. `RetireBranchOverlay` burns a retiring branch's CoordinateLocal `EscrowBranchSeed` overlay rights with an exact before/after conservation proof and is orderable ONLY from §5.6's `BranchRetireSpec` capsule (FG-INV-02 admits no silently dropped rights: overlay capacity is burned by a registered transition or not at all). `CompactTerminalEvidence` replaces fully terminal Consumed/Released reservation, transfer, and operation records with their permanent `EscrowOperationSummary` evidence under the ordinary compaction floors; it neither mints nor burns rights and never touches Held or InTransit custody.

Branching: CoordinateLocal domains fork as lazy `EscrowBranchSeed {child, parent, fork_head, parent_state_digest}` overlays and intentionally receive independent branch-local capacity. Squash merge never imports source rights: it replays unique operation-key deltas against target rights. AuthorityGlobal domains never fork; their global effect is consumed once at the source transaction and merge recognizes the permanent summary rather than charging it again; the effect envelope tag makes those scopes unambiguous. Depletion means `NeedsRights`/transfer/retry or failure; stream ordering cannot legalize an out-of-bound update.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (mint/burn clause, restated): only registered creation/reconfiguration/quota-epoch/branch-overlay-retirement transitions with exact before/after proof may mint or burn rights; escrow custody remains a disjoint exhaustive partition with finite-side conservation at every transition. FG-INV-16: transfer records are obligations with one terminal outcome. Quota-epoch time evidence follows w9-time-authority's rollback-resistance contract. All invariant-class.

## Interactions
Extends w4-escrow (ledger objects, conservation core). Consumes w2-branch-fork (the fork boundary/head and `parent_state_digest` that lazy `EscrowBranchSeed` overlays pin — the frozen `BranchForkBundle` field list carries no escrow objects; seeds materialize lazily on first use, per §4.7), w2-branch-retire (`BranchRetireSpec` capsule orders RetireBranchOverlay), w9-time-authority shape for `TimeValidationEvidence` (interaction, not a blocker: the evidence type contract is registered at G0). Produces: the transition arms consumed by w4-ladder-strengthenings (escrow rung transfers), w2c retirement dispositions, and w12-escrow-dp-alloc (Meta/Shard generalization).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Closed-union check: CI verifies exactly five arms with registry rows; an unregistered mint/burn path is a G0 negative fixture. (2) TransferAtomic: duplicate idempotency key returns the identical record; generation-CAS races leave exactly one Activated transfer (lab DPOR). (3) ReconfigureDomain: tightening with insufficient burnable Available rights fails; migration mapping must account for all custody (property tests). (4) AdvanceQuotaEpoch: stale/rolled-back time evidence rejects; old-epoch Held records block or finish before rollover (fixtures both ways). (5) RetireBranchOverlay: only orderable from a BranchRetireSpec capsule (direct order is a negative fixture); before/after conservation proof checked; ledger equality verified post-burn. (6) Merge replay: repeated/partial merges replay unique operation keys exactly once (differential against operation summaries); AuthorityGlobal effects charged once ever. (7) Lazy-fork tests: seed materialization on first use; parent_state_digest mismatch fails closed. (8) Crash rows across every transition phase with custody-total assertions in structured logs. (9) e2e transition script: fork a branch (lazy seed materialization), TransferAtomic between owners, ReconfigureDomain bound tightening, AdvanceQuotaEpoch with valid evidence, branch retire through a `BranchRetireSpec` capsule (RetireBranchOverlay burn), then CompactTerminalEvidence — asserting after every step that log-derived custody totals satisfy the conservation equations and equal the authoritative ledger. DETAILED LOGGING: every transition apply logs {transition_arm, domain_id, epoch, before_totals{available,reserved,in_transit}, after_totals, minted, burned, proof_ref}; TransferAtomic additionally logs {transfer_id, state, idempotency_key}; lab and e2e assertions run against these structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: quota-epoch rollover stalls under held old-epoch rights (by design — bounded by hold lifetimes; observable). Rejected: mint/burn via ordinary effects; importing source rights at merge (double-counting); counting staged shard projections (shadows are never counted); ambient-time epoch advance; eagerly materializing escrow seeds into the fork bundle (the bundle's closed field list carries no escrow objects — lazy overlays only).

## Provenance
Plan §4.7 (250, 256), §5.6 (465), App A registry row (1912), App A BranchForkBundle field list (2023); Appendix F FG-INV-02/16.

title: Implement the escrow conserved-rights algebra: domains, custody, transfers, retirement
description:
## What & scope
Implement §4.7's core: the escrow semantic ledger — `EscrowDomainDefinition`, custody unions and conservation equations, the `EscrowLedgerRoot` object family, reservation/transfer/operation records, final-certification escrow holds, and the workspace prefix law. Escrow is a separate semantic ledger, never an alias for the operational `ResourceLedger`. The registered rights transitions (`EscrowRightsTransitionSpec`, including `RetireBranchOverlay`) and branch fork/merge semantics are split into w4-escrow-transitions.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The purpose claim is exact and modest: escrow preserves registered numeric invariants without per-operation cross-branch/replica coordination by pre-distributing rights; within the single commit order the delivered property is abort/rebase-rate reduction and merge-order independence for counter-shaped invariants, with coordination amortized into explicit rights-transfer transitions rather than eliminated — every escrow commit still rides ordered final certification, and depletion escalates to the ordered path (§7.4). This is the merge ladder's "missing middle" for inventories, budgets, rate limits, degree caps — exactly what LWW mangles and aborts throttle (B6 agent swarms decrementing shared budgets; B1 single commit order preserved). SOTA basis: O'Neil escrow transactions + CALM scoping (§3.5), adopted with scoped proofs, never a context-free "no coordination" label.

## Design — normative detail
`EscrowNumericProfile` permits only checked integer or fixed-scale decimal quantities, never floating point. `EscrowDomainDefinition` is `{domain_id, scope:CoordinateLocal{graph,constraint_id,subject_key_profile}|AuthorityGlobal{database_or_tenant,constraint_id,subject_key_profile}, value_source:ExplicitProperty|DerivedCardinality|EpochQuota, quantity_profile, lower:Finite(q)|Unbounded, upper:Finite(q)|Unbounded, branch_policy:IndependentOverlay|SharedAuthority, epoch, overflow:Reject, schema_epoch}` and requires `L <= value <= U` under checked arithmetic.

Conservation equations: for each finite lower bound, `sum(AllCustody(Decrement)) = value - L`; for each finite upper bound, `sum(AllCustody(Increment)) = U - value`. Local `AllCustody` is the disjoint exhaustive union `Available(owner) | Reserved(reservation_id) | InTransit(transfer_id)`. Meta adds `Delegated(grant_id, target_consensus_domain, generation)`, whose amount must byte-equal the active shard projection's available-plus-held totals; staged projections are shadows and never counted; no grant generation has two Active projections. A positive delta consumes Increment rights and creates equal Decrement rights; a negative delta does the inverse. An unbounded side needs no consumed rights but still creates capacity on the finite opposite side. Reserve, abort, and transfer preserve totals; commit changes value and custody atomically. Domain creation, bound change, ordered quota-epoch transition, or branch-overlay retirement is the ONLY mint/burn path and requires an exact quiescence/before-after proof. Depletion means `NeedsRights`/transfer/retry or failure; stream ordering cannot legalize an out-of-bound update.

Canonical objects: `EscrowLedgerRoot {generation, domains[(domain_id,epoch)->StrongRef<EscrowDomainState>], active_reservation_index, transfer_index, operation_tombstone_root, body_digest}`; `EscrowDomainState {definition_ref, value, state_generation, owner_accounts_root, reservation_root, transfer_root, contribution_root, operation_index_root, conservation_digest}`; `EscrowOwner {consensus_domain, topology_epoch, partition, branch?, holder_generation}`; `EscrowAccount {owner, available_increment, available_decrement, generation}`. Immutable predecessor-linked `EscrowReservationRecord {reservation_id, generation, domain_id, epoch, owner, attempt_statement_intent_identity, right_kind, amount, basis_generation, state:Held|Consumed{terminal_identity}|Released{typed_proof}}`. `EscrowTransferRecord {transfer_id, generation, domain_id, epoch, source, target, right_kind, amount, basis_generations, idempotency_key, state:PreparedDebit|TargetStaged|Activated|CancelledBeforeStage}`. `EscrowOperationSummary {operation_key, domain_id, epoch, canonical_delta, terminal_effect_digest}` is permanent idempotency evidence; duplicate keys with different bytes fail closed.

Holds: an Active Local/Meta final-certification reservation has a distinct `escrow_rights_hold_root_ref` in addition to resource/constraint holds. Reservation atomically moves exact rights from Available (or Delegated projection) custody into Held records and freezes domain/value/operation/constraint generations. Commit consumes every Held record and creates the opposite rights in the same state transition as the graph effects and marker; admitted abort releases them. Cancellation before signing requires the existing no-plan/lock/share/order proof plus exact release successors. Timeout, client death, or crash NEVER releases Held or InTransit custody. Multi-statement workspaces carry `EscrowWorkspaceState`; produced rights are reusable only in that same workspace until terminal apply, and every published statement satisfies bounds; normalization proves every intermediate prefix, not merely a zero net effect.

Mint/burn discipline: domain creation, bound change, ordered quota-epoch transition, and branch-overlay retirement are the only mint/burn paths; each requires an exact quiescence/before-after proof. The five registered transition arms and the branch fork/merge semantics are specified in w4-escrow-transitions. The Local root is `escrow_ledger_root`; W12 adds `global_escrow_ledger_root` + transfer/grant registries (Meta) and `shard_escrow_grant_root`/`shard_escrow_reservation_root` (Shard) — the W12 delegation protocol is owned by w12-escrow-dp-alloc against this bead's Local semantics.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (restated, escrow clause): escrow custody is a disjoint exhaustive partition, finite-side conservation equations hold at every transition, values remain within bounds, and only registered creation/reconfiguration/quota-epoch/branch-overlay-retirement transitions with exact before/after proof may mint or burn rights — enforced by the Lean escrow conservation/bounds lane plus duplicate-consume/quota-rollover/topology-transfer oracles. FG-INV-16: escrow holds are obligations never lost/duplicated/refunded while obligated. Checkpoint/floor/prepared/backup/restore/role-transition/reconfiguration/GC/attempt-compaction inventories enumerate every Held, InTransit, Staged, Active/Delegated record and permanent summary. Abort-rate reduction is `benchmark`-class; the ledger itself is invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-txn-lifecycle (workspace state, terminal apply), w2-commit-protocol (same-transition commit semantics). Produces: the custody/conservation core extended by w4-escrow-transitions; the escrow rung consumed by w4-ladder-strengthenings; the `escrow_rights_hold_root_ref` consumed by w4-coordinator; Local semantics projected by w12-escrow-dp-alloc; Lean lane coordinated with verif-formal.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Lean proof obligations: conservation equations and bounds across reserve/abort/commit/transfer — registered as a `verif-formal` anchor lane (verif-formal depends on this bead, so a dep here would cycle); proved there with lane-green at gate-g4; in-bead, the same equations are checked as executable properties over randomized operation sequences. (2) Lab campaigns (the corresponding TLA+ model is likewise a verif-formal §15.5 anchor, model-checked there): concurrent reserve, duplicate transfer, every phase crash, lost ack, leader/config/topology change, participant loss, abort after prepare. (3) Exhaustive reference tests: lower/upper/both/unbounded domains, boundaries, signed values, overflow, multi-statement prefixes (every intermediate prefix within bounds), degree cascades, shared-global scope, same-identity restore/clone, hidden depletion/error noninterference, and exact ledger equality after every operation. (4) Idempotency: duplicate `operation_key` with identical bytes returns the summary; different bytes fail closed. (5) Custody-never-leaks: injected timeout/client-death/crash leaves Held/InTransit intact (lab assertions on custody totals, with per-transition ledger logging in the e2e script). (6) Benchmark: abort-rate reduction on counter-contended workloads vs escrow-off baseline, published as benchmark-class evidence. (7) e2e ledger script: a full workspace lifecycle — create bounded domains (finite lower, finite upper, both, unbounded), reserve rights across a multi-statement workspace, publish intermediate statements (every prefix proved within bounds), commit (every Held record consumed and the opposite rights created atomically with the graph effects and marker); a second run takes admitted abort after reservation (Held released exactly); a third crashes mid-commit and recovery proves Held/InTransit custody intact before the retry converges. DETAILED LOGGING: the implementation logs one structured ledger event per custody movement {domain_id, epoch, owner, right_kind, amount, custody_from, custody_to, reservation_id_or_transfer_id, basis_generation} and per value change {value_before, value_after, conservation_digest}; tests replay the event stream to reconstruct the ledger and assert exact equality with the authoritative `EscrowLedgerRoot` after every operation — this is the per-transition ledger logging that the custody-never-leaks assertions in (5) and the Lean-lane cross-checks consume.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: rights fragmentation across many branches starves writers (transfers + depletion escalation to ordered path are the designed response; measured). Rejected: aliasing escrow to the operational ResourceLedger (different semantics/lifecycles); floating-point quantities; LWW counters; claiming coordination is eliminated (it is amortized); mint/burn outside the registered transitions.

## Provenance
Plan §4.7 (246-260), §7.4 strengthening 3 (631), §5.6 (465); Appendix F FG-INV-02/16; §3.5 CALM/escrow row.

title: Milestone W4/G1: serializable transactions and Secure View core
description:
## What & scope
Aggregate the exact W4 transaction and Secure View subset required by Gate G1: block MVCC, canonical locking, SSI witness families and strict-serializability certification, constraint/resource/base escrow enforcement, coordinator/final-certification/cancellation, deterministic semantic rebase/merge ladder, schema/catalog and normalized valid-time/temporal semantics, and the sole authorized storage/query/mutation facade. It excludes G2 extensions whose correctness depends on later branch or derived-build surfaces: branch seed/transfer/retirement escrow transitions, multi-branch ladder strengthenings, transactional bulk staging/DDL, and shadow derived-index build/activation.

## Why
The full W4 epic crosses two convergence gates. Making G1 wait for branch and derived-build extensions hid the minimum complete serializable engine path and dragged G2 work into the earlier gate. This milestone is not a simplified transaction model: every included component is its final abstraction, and excluded registered operations remain unconstructible/disabled until the full W4 epic closes.

## Design and phase contract
The milestone publishes a generated `G1TxnCapabilityManifest` from command/state/invariant/checker rows. It admits Local authorized transactions over the exact schema/valid-time/constraint/resource/base-escrow model; produces final post-rebase capsules; proves witness lifetime/refinement and strict-serializable certification; and uses Secure View before storage observation. Base drift and commutative/exact intent re-evaluation are active. TTL/expiry execution remains disabled at G1 because Gate G1 requires normalized valid-time slices but does not activate the W9 time-authority dependency; TTL closes with the full W4 epic at G2. Branch-specific escrow custody and multi-branch order are disabled despite their frozen formats. Bulk/DDL and derived-build commands are disabled; ordinary schema transactions needed by G1 remain active through the core catalog/coordinator path.

## Success Criteria
- All child tasks' unit/property/model/fuzz/simulation/E2E and diagnostic-event rows pass.
- Independent history/oracle suites cover read/write, negative/gap/path/temporal witnesses, constraint conflicts, resource and base-escrow conservation, cancellation, ownership handoff, and forced rebase.
- A G1 E2E proves authorization-before-observation, canonical lock order, SSI/constraint validation, post-rebase final capsule, D1/D2 publication, recovery, and byte-identical strict result/replay.
- Compile/registry tests reject every excluded branch-escrow, multi-branch-strengthening, bulk-staging, and shadow-build command/capability while preserving its frozen schema row.
- Unit tests validate generated capability closure and ensure no Snapshot isolation claim is labeled serializable and no post-filter authorization path exists.
- Structured JSONL rollup names transaction/witness/constraint/resource/escrow/coordinator state, authority public commitment, capsule/command digests, checker/oracle, verdict, evidence refs, seed, and replay command with protected values redacted.
- Completion makes no claim for excluded G2 features; the full W4 epic remains their gate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: global-lock interim transactions, snapshot isolation mislabeled ACID, a reduced AST executor, or duplicating core types for the milestone. Risk: activation-row drift; generated closure and same-change checks make it explicit.

## Provenance
Plan §7, §19 W4 workstream, Gate G1 additional criteria, Gate G2 bulk/derived/branch criteria.

title: Implement DerivedBuildRegistry shadow-build, validation, and transactional activation
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact shadow lifecycle for derived generations (indexes, contract enablement, typed-column/schema migrations): `IndexDefinition` states, `DerivedBuildRegistry<Role>`, `DerivedBuildTransitionSpec<Role>`, `DerivedGenerationValidationCertificate`, and the transactional `SchemaOp::ActivateDerivedGeneration` switch.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The industry norm — index build progress implicitly changing query behavior — is a determinism and replay hazard. B5: a build NEVER changes query-visible schema; only an ordinary transaction activates a validated generation, so plans, certificates, and replay stay pinned. B4/market: "incremental reindexing" is a named 2026 buyer gap; the shadow->catch-up->validate->activate pattern with exact watermarks is the answer, and rebuilds are generations, not in-place mutations (B1).

## Design — normative detail
A committed `SchemaOp::DeclareIndex` creates a versioned `IndexDefinition` in `DeclaredBuilding`; it does NOT make any generation usable. `DerivedBuildRegistry<Role>` maps `(definition_oid, generation_id)` through `Reserved -> SnapshotBuilding{pin, watermark} -> CatchingUp{contiguous_delta_frontier} -> Validating{candidate_component_root} -> ReadyForSchemaActivation{validation_certificate_ref} -> Active`, or from any preactivation state to `Aborted{typed_reason, disposition}`. `DerivedBuildTransitionSpec<Role>` has exactly `Reserve`, `PublishSnapshotProgress`, `PublishCatchupProgress`, `BeginValidation`, `PublishReady`, and `Abort`; every progress update is monotone/idempotent, owns its bounded closure, and advertises its exact watermark.

`DerivedGenerationValidationCertificate` binds definition/identity/security/authority, pinned snapshot, complete delta interval, exact component root/content commitment, scalar/collation/approximation profiles, constraint and deletion semantics, validation oracle results, resource bounds, and signer/configuration evidence. It names no future activation.

Activation: only a later ordinary `SchemaOp::ActivateDerivedGeneration` transaction, strongly naming an already-built Ready certificate and rechecking the current definition/head/security state, atomically changes the definition/generation registry to Active. Rebuild creates a distinct generation; old Active remains usable until that transaction switches it, and retention floors protect old snapshots. Exact indexes prove answer equivalence or fall back; approximate generations carry their own semantic generation and `ApproximationProfile`, so a changed ANN topology cannot masquerade as the same definition. Contract enablement and typed-column/schema migrations use the same shadow/catch-up/validate/transactional-activate pattern. Cancellation/abort never changes schema, and GC cannot reclaim pins/components/certificates until abort/activation, audit visibility, and a covering cut.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated, relevant clauses): every claimed answer-equivalent exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract; approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation; no build progress or physical bulk/index artifact changes schema visibility before its ordinary transactional SchemaOp activation. FG-INV-18: rebuildable indexes can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. FG-INV-14/16: pins, components, and certificates are GC roots until abort/activation + audit visibility + covering cut. ANN recall evidence for approximate generations is FG-CAL-03-class, never an invariant.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-delta-batches (contiguous delta frontier for CatchingUp), w2-snapshots-leases (build pins), w4-constraints (constraint semantics bound into the certificate), w2-commit-protocol (SchemaOp transactions). Produces: the lifecycle that w7-index-core, w7-btree, w7-fts, w7-vector, w7-path-temporal all build under; the activation pattern reused by w4-valid-time and w4-ttl-expiry contract enablement; watermarks consumed by w6-freshness; `ApproximationProfile` generations consumed by w5-replay (exact approximate generations are replay slots).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) State-machine conformance: only the six transition specs move the registry; progress updates are monotone/idempotent (replayed updates are no-ops); any preactivation state can abort; Active cannot. (2) Visibility gate: while a build is in any pre-Active state, differential tests prove zero change in any read result, error, or statistics observable through the surfaces in this bead's dependency closure (authorized reads and registry/statistics state — shadow invisibility); the full query-answer/plan-choice form of the same gate (zero change in any query answer or plan choice visible in certificates) is instantiated by the per-index-kind suites of (6) in the w7-* beads once `w5-planner` lands — this bead ships the differential harness and its named CI rows, not the planner-level runs. (3) Activation races: activation transaction rechecking definition/head/security fails cleanly when the definition drifted after Ready (definition-drift fixture); old generation serves until the atomic switch; snapshots pinned pre-switch keep the old generation (retention floors). (4) Stale-tail test: a Ready certificate whose delta interval is no longer contiguous with the current frontier cannot activate. (5) Approximation-generation test: a rebuilt ANN topology under the same definition gets a new semantic generation; replay pinned to the old generation resolves the old one or degrades attributably. (6) Full differential/metamorphic/crash suite per §7.5: differential, metamorphic, crash, stale-tail, definition-drift, policy/revocation, branch-fork/merge, delete, approximation-generation, and rebuild-switch tests gate EVERY index kind (each is a named CI row; e2e scripts log registry state at every transition and assert the exact state path) — the per-kind battery hooks land with `w7-index-core`, which depends on this bead, so the every-kind battery executes there and is validated at gate-g2; this bead's own close-time CI covers the lifecycle machinery itself via (1)-(5) and (7). (7) GC negative: reclaiming a pinned component before abort/activation+visibility+cut fails the generated reachability checker.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: long catch-up on hot graphs delays Ready (bounded-closure progress + watermark advertising make lag observable; freshness is slo-class). Risk: certificate bloat (bounded closure, exact commitments). Rejected: `IndexDefinitionSpec`/`IndexActivationSpec` control-command shortcuts (forbidden; G0 negative fixture); build-progress-changes-visibility (replay hazard); in-place ANN topology swap under one generation (masquerade forbidden by FG-INV-12).

## Provenance
Plan §7.5 (643-645); Appendix F FG-INV-12/14/16/18; FG-CAL-03.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Prove merge-ladder eligibility context, multi-branch order, and the escrow rung
description:
## What & scope
Implement and prove the three formal strengthenings of §7.4's merge ladder: complete-context `ConsistencyClass` eligibility, explicit multi-branch order semantics, and the invariant-preserving escrow rung between commutative-replay and abort. Split from w4-merge-ladder for size.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
These strengthenings are what keep the ladder honest (B5): eligibility is a proof about a composed context, not a lookup table; order independence is an algebraic property with a registered proof, not a vibe; and the escrow rung is the designed middle path for the counter-shaped properties (inventories, budgets, rate limits, degree caps) that LWW mangles and aborts throttle — the B6 agent-swarm case.

## Design — normative detail
(i) Rung eligibility is proved for a COMPLETE context: `ConsistencyClass` is derived from the intent algebra only after composing schema constraints and read dependencies. CALM-style monotonicity is sufficient only within the declared lattice and authority domain; a context-free table is a cache of proved classifications, never the source of truth (an edge addition is not coordination-free when uniqueness or cardinality makes it non-monotone).

(ii) Multi-branch semantics are explicit: only registered associative, commutative, idempotent (ACI) joins are order-independent. Other resolvable intents use the pinned total order `(source_head_seq, source_branch_id, source_intent_ordinal, element_id)` recorded in the merge policy; unresolved cases return conflicts. Merge records carry the target visibility parent plus source heads as non-parent provenance, all bases/imported ranges, policy, and final digest (§5.6), so retries are idempotent and order is auditable without inventing multiple target ancestries. No general cocycle claim is made without a formal merge algebra and higher-order coherence proof.

(iii) The escrow rung: escrow merge modes preserve numeric invariants (x >= 0, quota ceilings, degree caps) without per-operation cross-branch/replica coordination by pre-distributing rights per branch/replica with an idempotent transfer ledger, under exactly §4.7's purpose claim — abort/rebase-rate reduction and merge-order independence within the single commit order, coordination amortized into rights transfers rather than eliminated, depletion escalating that intent to the ordered path. The model-checked transfer protocol lives in the sim lab's standing scenarios.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-17 binds all rung behavior (reuse legal iff extensionally equal to full re-evaluation). FG-INV-13's merge clauses bind (ii): effects obey proved ACI algebra or their recorded total order; merge tokens have one terminal outcome. FG-INV-02's escrow clause binds (iii). Rung hit rate and escrow benefit are `benchmark`-class; `ConsistencyClass` classifications are cached proofs (invariant-class provenance, never heuristics).

## Interactions
Extends w4-merge-ladder (rung structure, evaluator). Consumes w4-escrow (rights/ledger for the rung), w2-branch-merge (MergeRecord provenance, pinned policy order, ImportedRangeKey idempotency). Produces: `ConsistencyClass` registry consumed by w5-intent-log classification and w12 (CALM classes at global scope); escrow-rung escalation consumed by w4-coordinator's ordered path.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) CALM negatives: an edge-add under a uniqueness/cardinality constraint must NOT classify coordination-free in the composed context; the same intent without the constraint may. (2) Cache-vs-truth test: mutating schema constraints invalidates cached classifications (a stale-cache fixture must recompute, not reuse). (3) Multi-branch metamorphic: permuting source arrival order never changes results — via ACI proof for registered families, via pinned total order otherwise; unresolved cases return typed conflicts (never silent LWW). (4) Escrow-rung tests: concurrent branch decrements within pre-distributed rights merge order-independently; depletion escalates the intent to the ordered path (assert escalation event in logs); rung outcome equals ordered-path outcome extensionally (differential). (5) Sim-lab standing scenario: the model-checked transfer protocol runs in every CI lab batch. (6) Benchmark: escrow-rung abort/rebase-rate reduction on counter workloads, benchmark-class registered. (7) e2e strengthening script: three branches concurrently decrement one escrowed counter and add edges under a uniqueness constraint, then merge in permuted orders; the script asserts identical final state across permutations, typed conflicts for unresolved intents, and escrow-rung escalation on depletion. DETAILED LOGGING: eligibility decisions log {intent_ordinal, consistency_class, classification_source:cached_proof|composed_derivation, context_digest}; merge resolution logs {policy_oid, aci_family_or_pinned_order_key, conflict_count}; escrow-rung outcomes log {domain_id, rights_consumed, escalated}; the stale-cache fixture in (2) must observe a logged recompute event, never a cache-hit event, after schema mutation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: classification-context explosion (bounded by declared lattice/authority domains). Rejected: context-free eligibility tables as source of truth; general cocycle/commutativity claims without algebra + coherence proof; LWW resolution; per-operation cross-branch coordination.

## Provenance
Plan §7.4 (627-631), §5.6 (455-459), §4.7 purpose claim (248); Appendix F FG-INV-17/13/02.

title: Implement the semantic merge ladder with the incremental-rebase law (FG-INV-17)
description:
## What & scope
Implement the four-rung semantic merge ladder invoked on base-drift at commit (block changed since snapshot), the capability-stripped rebase evaluator `Cx`, and the incremental transitive-closure re-evaluation law with unchanged-observation certificates. One evaluator serves three consumers: transaction rebase, §5.6 branch merge, and §14.4 multi-writer preparation, through distinct typed policies. The three formal strengthenings (complete-context eligibility, multi-branch order, escrow rung) are specified in w4-ladder-strengthenings.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
frankensqlite built this ladder to rescue B-tree page conflicts; graphs love it more: selected graph intents have promising algebraic merge opportunities, but actual eligibility is constraint- and read-context-dependent, so hit rate and skew benefit are benchmark questions, not architectural facts. B6: agent swarms produce exactly the same-granule, semantically-independent conflicts the ladder rescues; B5: rung-1 replay determinism is enforced by construction, and the reuse law is a registered invariant clause with a differential oracle. This is the abort-rate lever that makes STRICT SERIALIZABLE affordable.

## Design — normative detail
On base-drift at commit, before aborting:

Rung 1 — semantic re-evaluation: evaluate the original intents against the current branch heads under a capability-stripped `Cx` — no clock, entropy, network, or filesystem — accepting every needed snapshot/constraint input explicitly, so ambient nondeterminism is inexpressible and missing inputs fail closed. Eligibility depends on operation semantics, active constraints, captured reads, property merge algebra, and branch policy; an edge addition is NOT coordination-free when uniqueness or cardinality makes it non-monotone. Re-evaluation is incremental BY LAW: rung 1 re-evaluates exactly the transitive closure of the intents whose captured observations drifted, together with every intent that depends — through procedure-output observations, workspace-generation reads, or escaped-allocation bindings — on a re-evaluated intent, evaluated in intent-ordinal order to a fixpoint against the rebased upstream state. A reused per-intent result carries an unchanged-observation certificate naming the exact `CapturedIntentObservation` set it was validated against; intents whose registered `ConsistencyClass` proves CALM-monotone eligibility in the composed context skip re-evaluation entirely.

Rung 2 — structured physical reuse: a disjoint physical patch may be retained only as an optional accelerator after the semantic result is fixed and only when its apply-basis digest still matches.

Rung 3 — final-effect regeneration: produce a new `CommittedEffectSet`, permanent IDs/keys, constraint reads, canonical logical deltas, write summary, and witnesses. Rerun FCW, SSI, and all affected constraints. Then build and persist a NEW capsule as §5.2 requires; no successful rung may publish the pre-rebase capsule or its stale availability receipts. Rung 3's revalidation is NOT a substitute for the rung-1 law: it reruns FCW/SSI/constraints over final effects but never re-derives effects from intents.

Rung 4 — abort/retry with a capability-redacted machine-readable conflict report when no safe resolution exists.

Re-evaluable intents bind `IntentSemanticsOid` (content digest of intent-schema version, `language_contract_oid`, semantic/scalar profiles, binder/normalizer version, every influencing procedure/UDF/module artifact); the ladder evaluates canonical typed intents under this object, never reparses source text; unavailable artifacts fail closed. Observation granularity is a decision-card question — coarse constraint or adjacency observations drift often and defeat reuse.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-17 (restated): rebase and branch merge execute under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`. Every semantic drift regenerates effects, workspace/read/write state, constraints, escrow/resource requirements, witnesses, logical deltas, allocation plan, RETURNING bytes, and capsule BEFORE final-certification reservation and terminal signing. Incremental rung-1 re-evaluation may reuse a prior intent's results only under unchanged-observation certificates closed transitively over the intra-transaction dependency DAG in intent-ordinal order, and such reuse is legal iff it is extensionally equal to full re-evaluation. Once an Active final-certification reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift must use the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path. No mutable clock, entropy, filesystem, network, or policy lookup enters replay. Hit rate/skew benefit: `benchmark`-class. Observation granularity: decision card (FG-EVID-01 disclosure).

## Interactions
Consumes w5-intent-log (Appendix B vocabulary, `CapturedIntentObservation`, net-effect normal form), w4-ssi-witnesses (rung-3 SSI rerun), w4-constraints (rung-3 constraint rerun + non-monotone eligibility), w2-commit-protocol (new-capsule requirement, D1 closure). Produces: the evaluator consumed by w2-branch-merge (squash merge) and w11/w12 multi-writer preparation; the rung structure w4-ladder-strengthenings extends; rung-4 conflict reports consumed by w10 surfaces; FG-INV-17's digest oracle consumed by verif-oracles.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Determinism-by-construction test: the rebase `Cx` type exposes no clock/entropy/network/fs capability (compile-time negative fixtures); a rebase requiring an unavailable input fails closed with a typed error. (2) Differential oracle (registered): on sampled conflicts, run incremental rung-1 AND full re-evaluation; final-effect/workspace/allocation/result digests must be equal (extensional equality); any divergence is a release blocker. (3) Certificate tests: a reused intent's unchanged-observation certificate names exactly the validated `CapturedIntentObservation` set; forced drift of any named observation invalidates reuse transitively through procedure-output/workspace/escaped-allocation dependencies (property tests over generated intent DAGs). (4) Capsule freshness: any successful rung publishes a new capsule; a fixture attempting to publish the pre-rebase capsule or stale availability receipts fails apply. (5) Interleaved-head property tests + reserve/sign/cancel ordering model rows (crash between drift detection and reservation; drift after Active reservation must take cancel/restart). (6) Benchmark: ladder hit-rate distribution on contended agent-swarm workloads, published as `benchmark`-class evidence. (7) e2e rebase script: drive two sessions into base-drift on one block and follow one transaction end-to-end through drift detection, rung-1 incremental re-evaluation, rung-3 regeneration, new-capsule publication, and commit; repeat with an ineligible conflict to exercise rung-4 abort and its capability-redacted conflict report. DETAILED LOGGING: every ladder attempt logs {txn_token, rung_entered, drifted_observation_count, reused_intent_count, reevaluated_intent_count, certificate_refs, fixpoint_iterations, final_effect_digest}; rung-4 logs {conflict_report_digest, redaction_applied}; the differential oracle in (2) and the e2e script assert extensional equality and rung decisions from these structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: coarse observations defeat reuse (decision card; measure granularity). Risk: fixpoint re-evaluation cost on dense intra-txn DAGs (bounded by intent-ordinal order; abort remains the floor). Rejected: physical patch reuse as primary (semantic result must be fixed first); reparsing source text at rebase; treating rung-3 revalidation as a substitute for the reuse law.

## Provenance
Plan §7.4 (616-631), §5.2 (386, 389), §5.6 (455-459); Appendix F FG-INV-17.

title: Implement block-granularity MVCC, canonical lock order, and SSI metadata lifetime
description:
## What & scope
Implement per-block MVCC over Strata `DeltaBlockVersion` chains, the canonical final lock protocol, the monotone transaction state machine, and the SSI metadata lifetime/coarsening rules. This bead owns FG-INV-02 (lock exclusivity) and FG-INV-03 (chain shape) for the transaction plane.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: the MVCC chain is the durable object chain — a published block head reaches an immutable predecessor chain; no durable bump-arena index or process pointer appears in canonical bytes, so time travel/branches/replication reuse the same versions. B2: the versioning granule equals the storage granule (frankensqlite's page-MVCC lesson re-instantiated for ~4KiB/256-entry graph blocks, §7.2). Granularity rationale: vertex-level false-conflicts on hubs, edge-level drowns in metadata; blocks keep lock/siread tables cache-resident; contended hubs escalate to delta-chains (commutative appends) — contention is handled by changing the data structure, not tuning locks.

## Design — normative detail
Visibility walk: readers continue down the predecessor chain until the first version satisfying ALL sequence, branch-ancestry, schema, retirement, and own-write visibility predicates; a newer sibling-branch version is skipped rather than terminating the search. The current-line fast path may collapse this to one compare only under a verified lineage token. Process-local `VersionArena`/`prev_idx` layouts are discardable decoded caches of immutable objects, never the authoritative chain. Giant hubs stripe the neighbor-ID space into independently locked/versioned candidate ranges; witness granularity follows the durable stripe identity. Eager block locks, latch-free transaction-private nodes, bump arenas, and EBR are strictly volatile staging machinery; abort drops only volatile staging; another transaction's staging is unobservable.

Lock protocol (§7.1): SIREAD witnesses never block. Mutations remain proposal-private until finalization computes the complete block/constraint/quota lock set. The coordinator acquires that set in canonical `(lock_class, graph, partition, object)` order; an implementation may instead use a proved no-wait abort protocol. It never waits while holding an unordered subset, and discovery of a missing lower-order lock releases without publication and restarts validation. Wait-for acyclicity and cancellation cleanup have separate model/oracle coverage from exclusivity.

Transaction state machine (monotone): `Active -> Validating -> FinalPrepared -> PayloadDurable -> OrderSubmitted -> CommandCommitted -> Applied(MarkerRef) -> Acknowledged`; `Aborted` is legal only before the irreversible ordering boundary; externally reported `Unknown` represents an unresolved observer outcome, not an internal rollback state. Single-node mode collapses consensus substates but not their ordering; cancellation and retries follow §5.2.

SSI metadata lifetime: SSI transaction records, rw-edge summaries, and SIREAD witnesses survive commit until every transaction that overlapped their lifetime has ended; reclamation is tied to an explicit overlap horizon, not the reader's commit. Coarsening under memory pressure is an atomic monotone replacement: the coarse superset becomes visible BEFORE fine entries are removed. Pressure may increase false aborts but never erases a possible dependency; admission returns `ResourceExhausted` rather than dropping correctness metadata.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (restated): for every exclusive block, constraint-owner reservation, resource hold, allocation offset, final-certification basis, and escrow custody unit, at most one legal live generation owns or may consume it; stale, cancelled, expired, or prior-configuration owners can neither mutate nor release it. FG-INV-03 (restated): every physical version chain is finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first by commit order, and every link remains within one owning object generation. Enforcement: lock/reservation/ownership-transfer models; independent lock-table, generation-reuse, duplicate-consume, cancellation oracles; Lean chain model plus arena decode, generation-substitution, debug, property, and fuzz oracles. Note explicitly: these local invariants alone do not prove SI or SSI — publication, branch visibility, deletes, own writes, witness soundness, and metadata lifetime are separate registry obligations.

## Interactions
Consumes w3-tier-d (block/partition-root objects, hub stripes, overflow), w2-snapshots-leases (`ReadSnapshot`/visibility predicates), w2-txn-lifecycle (outcome records the state machine reports into), w1-collections (sharded cache-line-padded lock/siread tables). Produces: the lock/visibility substrate for w4-ssi-witnesses (witness storage/lifetime), w4-coordinator (final lock-set acquisition), w4-merge-ladder (base-drift detection). w6-delta-consumption reads the same chains.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Property tests: chain walk returns the unique first version satisfying all predicates, across randomized branch DAGs and sibling-version interleavings; sibling skip never terminates a search. (2) Lineage-token test: fast path returns identical results to full walk on 10^6 randomized cases; forced token invalidation falls back correctly. (3) Lock-order model: DPOR/lab exploration of canonical-order acquisition proves no waiting-while-holding-unordered-subset; injected missing lower-order lock triggers release-without-publication + restart (assert via trace logs that no publication event precedes the restart). (4) Coarsening test: under injected memory pressure, verify the atomic monotone replacement (coarse visible before fine removal) and that a dependency deliberately covered only by a fine entry is still detected post-coarsening; admission returns `ResourceExhausted` under exhaustion. (5) Overlap-horizon test: metadata for a committed txn survives until the last overlapping txn ends (lab virtual time), then reclaims. (6) State-machine conformance: exhaustive transition fuzz rejects any non-monotone or post-boundary Abort transition. (7) Crash-matrix rows: crash at each state; recovery discards unrooted arenas and reconstructs from the Chronicle suffix. (8) e2e concurrency script: concurrent writers on shared and disjoint blocks plus a hub escalating to delta-chains run to commit/abort, exercising visibility walks, canonical lock acquisition, and SSI metadata reclamation end-to-end. DETAILED LOGGING: lock acquire/release logs {lock_class, graph, partition, object, txn_token, canonical_order_position}; state-machine transitions log {txn_token, from_state, to_state}; coarsening logs {before_entry_count, after_entry_count, coarse_visible_first}; the fast path logs {lineage_token_valid, fallback_taken}; tests (3), (4), and the e2e script assert ordering and monotone-replacement properties directly from these structured events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: no-wait protocol vs canonical-order choice affects tail latency — both admitted, but the choice is a decision card; correctness identical. Rejected: vertex- and edge-granularity locking (§7.2); durable overflow logs as a source of truth (§6.2.4 — volatile staging only); donor monotone-TxnId visibility rule (replaced by durable transaction idempotency + branch-ancestry semantic visibility).

## Provenance
Plan §7.1 (581-586), §7.2 (590), §6.2.2-6.2.4 (534-537); Appendix F FG-INV-02/03.

title: Implement the FrankenGraph model surface: schema gradient, catalog, coordinates, reserved system slots
description:
## What & scope
Implement §4.1–§4.4: the FrankenGraph data model surface — the `CanonicalPropertyValue` storage union and element-model laws, the three-posture schema gradient with online posture migration and typed-column promotion, the graph/branch catalog with versioned aliases and the role-free/role-bearing coordinate objects, and the reserved system property/edge-type surface. This bead owns the schema objects, catalog state, and coordinate types that most other beads reference but none defines: `CoordinateSchemaBinding`, `GraphReferenceBinding`, `CoordinateSchemaTransition`, the posture machine, and the reserved-slot registry rows. Build-order boundary: this bead's dep closure is only {g0-format-arms, g0-identity-registries, w1-foundation-types} — no commit protocol, snapshots, branches, plan cache, or shadow-build machinery exists yet. It therefore owns the posture state machine, transition/validation rules, catalog application logic, and the migration/promotion job *specifications*; every marker-, snapshot-, or shadow-build-dependent behavior is exercised here against fixture `MarkerRef`s and synthetic snapshot/catalog states, while executing an online shadow-build migration itself rides w4-index-lifecycle's machinery and Chronicle's write path, with the integration drills explicitly deferred as marked in Acceptance.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B6: the model is a bitemporal, schema-gradient, multi-label property multigraph. The gradient (Open→Shaped→Strict, changeable online per label/edge type) is the migration-friendly on-ramp for agent workloads that start schemaless and harden over time, and versioned schema-in-the-commit-stream makes schema changes transactional, time-travelable, and branchable — frankensqlite's schema-root/epoch design re-instantiated for graph objects (§4.2). Without one owner for the catalog/coordinate objects, every consumer (binder, permits, certificates, replay) would reinvent them and the per-coordinate schema-epoch law behind precise plan-cache invalidation would have no implementation home.

## Design — normative detail
Model (§4.1): vertices carry a label set (not a single label), properties, and identity. Edges are typed (exactly one edge type), directed — undirected exposed as a view/semantics flag per type — may be parallel, and carry properties; `EId` is the unconditional parallel-edge discriminator, and an optional user edge key participates only in a declared key/uniqueness constraint. Stored property values use `CanonicalPropertyValue`, exactly: `Null, Bool, Int64, UInt64, Float64, Decimal128, String, Bytes, Date, LocalTime, ZonedTime, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, Duration, Point(2D/3D geo), Uuid, List<T>, Map<String,T>, Struct, Embedding{dim, dtype: f32|f16|i8}` under the pinned scalar profile (`Point` is storable but not orderable/indexable in 1.0 per §3.4/§10.1). The bound-query type lattice is separate — it adds graph element/reference, path, binding/table, absence/`NOTHING`, and every required/optional GQL constructor/coercion named by the exact `LanguageContract` — and property storage never pretends to be a strict superset of query-only types. The fnx bridge is lossless only for the registered intersection with `CgseValue`; unsupported values require an explicit projection/coercion law. System time (bitemporal axis 1) is universal, automatic, and branch-aware: every vertex/edge/property version carries `created_by: MarkerRef` plus zero or more retirement/supersession `MarkerRef`s; at a selected branch head the effective interval is the creation followed by the earliest retirement visible in that ancestry — a sibling-branch deletion cannot retire the version elsewhere; linear trunk generations may cache `[created_seq, effective_retired_seq)` only as a projection whose lineage/head is explicit (§5.3–5.4). Valid time (axis 2) is opt-in per element type and owned by w4-valid-time. Provenance is first-class: any element can carry a `provenance` system property (source id, extraction confidence, agent/session id), and `DERIVED_FROM` is the reserved lineage system edge type — the GraphRAG lineage story is modeled, not improvised.

Schema gradient (§4.2): three enforcement postures per label/edge type, changeable online — (1) Open: any property, any value; types inferred and recorded as statistics; (2) Shaped: declared properties are typed and validated; extra properties are allowed into an overflow map column; (3) Strict: declared properties only; constraints active (existence, uniqueness/key, range/regex/check, edge endpoint label constraints, cardinality constraints like `AT MOST 1 :MOTHER edge out` — state owned by w4-constraints). Schema objects (labels, edge types, property defs, constraints, indexes) are versioned in the commit stream like data: a schema root/epoch for every bound coordinate. Migration between postures — and any typed-column promotion of a hot overflow property — is an online shadow-build job reusing §6.3's seal/publish protocol: build against a pinned snapshot, catch up deltas, validate, atomically publish the new schema epoch; old snapshots keep their epoch's interpretation. The per-coordinate schema binding is part of snapshot identity (§5.3) and of every plan-cache key, so prepared plans invalidate precisely rather than consulting one ambient epoch.

Catalog and coordinates (§4.3): a database has a stable `DatabaseId` and contains named graphs with stable `GraphId`s; each graph has a trunk branch plus arbitrary user branches (§5.6); a branch coordinate is `(GraphId, BranchId, head: MarkerRef)`; names are versioned catalog aliases, never identity. Queries address `graph@branch` or `graph@branch AS OF <time|seq>`; the default is `trunk@now`. A single-node transaction may touch several graph/branch coordinates and commits them atomically through one global marker carrying `head_updates[]` — this atomicity is a property of Chronicle's global commit protocol (w2-commit-protocol builds the marker), never inferred merely from sharing a sequence counter; the post-1.0 sharded posture must supply §14.6's distributed atomic-commit protocol before cross-shard atomicity is claimed. The role-free state coordinate is `CoordinateSchemaBinding { graph, branch, selected_head: MarkerRef, schema_root_oid, schema_epoch }`; there is no transaction-wide "current schema epoch." Query binding wraps it as `GraphReferenceBinding { binding_role_id, coordinate: CoordinateSchemaBinding }`, where the binder deterministically derives `BindingRoleId` from the canonical graph-reference occurrence; bindings are unique by role, so one statement may compare the same branch at two `AS OF` heads without conflating visibility, schema, retention leases, authorization, or witnesses. A schema mutation instead records `CoordinateSchemaTransition { graph, branch, apply_basis: MarkerRef, before_root_oid, before_epoch, after_root_oid, after_epoch }`; the newly created marker becomes the `selected_head` of the resulting coordinate binding, avoiding a capsule that recursively names its own future marker. Catalog, binder, cache, permit, certificate, and replay contracts use role-bearing bindings for query inputs and role-free bindings for state ownership; only genuinely database-global topology and policy epochs remain scalar.

Reserved system surface (§4.4): `_id`, `_labels`, `_type`, `_key`, `_created_seq`, `_retired_seq`, `_commit_time`, `_valid_from`, `_valid_to`, `_expires_at` (expiry instant under an enabled `ExpiryContract`; §4.8/w4-ttl-expiry), `_provenance`, `_embedding` (conventional default vector slot), `_score` (query-time). `_retired_seq` is the effective retirement in the selected snapshot ancestry, never a branch-global stored scalar. System edge types: `DERIVED_FROM` and `SAME_AS` (entity-resolution assertions with confidence — the agent-memory dedup primitive; created only through the `AssertSameAs` intent sugar, no second mechanism). These fields are ordinary protected data from Warden's perspective: a capability may mask provenance, embeddings, commit metadata, or selected properties even when it can see the element (§12).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 clause: the per-coordinate schema binding is part of snapshot identity and of every plan-cache key. FG-INV-18 linkage: Strict-posture constraints are synchronous authoritative pre-commit state (owned by w4-constraints; this bead owns the posture that activates them). The closed `CanonicalPropertyValue` union, the reserved-slot rows, the system edge-type rows, the posture-transition arms, and the coordinate-object schemas are G0-frozen format arms — implementation may trail the frozen rows, the arms may not (§19). Alias-resolution defaults and posture defaults are configuration-class; the coordinate-object and ancestry-visibility laws are invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-format-arms` (frozen unions/registry rows), `g0-identity-registries` (kind rows, BodyDigest transcripts), `w1-foundation-types` (scalar values, identity newtypes, `CanonicalScalarProfile`). Produces the coordinate/schema/catalog objects consumed by `w4-bulk-ddl` (`SchemaOp` is the only mutation vehicle for these objects), `w4-constraints` (constraint scoping by `(GraphId, BranchId/head, schema_epoch)`), `w5-binder` (graph-reference specs resolve to `GraphReferenceBinding`; classification names write coordinate sets), `w2-commit-protocol` (marker `head_updates[]` and `coordinate_schema_transition_digest`), `w2-snapshots-leases` (snapshot identity includes the schema binding), `w9-enforcement` (reserved-slot masking), `w4-ttl-expiry` (`_expires_at`), `w4-valid-time` (`_valid_from`/`_valid_to` projections), `w8-projection` (fnx `CgseValue` intersection law), `w5-branch-stats` (Open-posture inferred-type statistics). Posture migration and typed-column promotion reuse `w4-index-lifecycle`'s shadow-build/catch-up/validate/transactional-activate pattern.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property tests: `CanonicalPropertyValue` round-trip/equality/hash/order coherence for every arm — including `Embedding` dtypes, nested `List/Map/Struct`, and `Point` digest-equality-without-order — under the pinned scalar profile; parallel-edge `EId` discrimination under identical `(src, type, dst)`; user-edge-key rejection without a declared constraint; undirected-view flag semantics per edge type (named scenario: `undirected_view_roundtrip`). Posture machine: generated tests for every posture transition pair proving validate-then-atomic-epoch-publish, overflow-map admission in Shaped, extra-property rejection in Strict, and old-snapshot epoch-interpretation stability (named scenarios: `open_to_shaped_inference`, `shaped_overflow_admission`, `strict_rejects_undeclared`, `posture_downgrade_keeps_history`); typed-column promotion shadow-build drill with concurrent writers catching up deltas to the exact watermark and crash injection at pin/catch-up/validate/activate boundaries (deferred drill — registered here as named scenario `typed_column_promotion_drill`, executable only once w4-index-lifecycle's shadow-build and Chronicle's write path exist; executed at w4-index-lifecycle). Catalog: alias rename/re-point proves identity stability (`GraphId` unchanged) and time-travel resolution of the old alias at old snapshots; multi-coordinate transaction commits atomically via one marker's `head_updates[]` with crash injection between coordinate applies — recovery is all-or-nothing (at this bead: the `head_updates[]`/`CoordinateSchemaTransition` schemas and catalog application logic are tested with fixture markers; the crash-injection legs are registered rows executed at w2-commit-protocol integration and gate-genesis); binder-role property test: the same branch at two `AS OF` heads yields two distinct role bindings with independent schema epochs and no cross-role substitution. Reserved surface: every reserved slot readable via its defined projection; `_retired_seq` differs across sibling branch heads after a one-sided delete (named scenario: `sibling_branch_retirement_isolation`); Warden mask test — a capability masks `_provenance`/`_embedding` while the element remains visible; user writes to reserved slots outside their contracts reject; reserved-name squatting by user properties rejects at registry generation. Fuzz: catalog/schema-object decoders over the registered kind rows with mutation corpora. E2E script (integration-deferred: registered now with its step list frozen, executed at the gate-genesis slice and w4-bulk-ddl once Chronicle/branching/plan-cache machinery exists; at this bead a fixture-marker dry run drives the same catalog/posture/epoch transitions without durability): create graph → Open-posture ingest → declare Shaped schema with overflow → promote a hot overflow property to a typed column online under concurrent writes → tighten to Strict with constraints → fork a branch, diverge schema on both sides, time-travel both — asserting per-coordinate schema epochs, plan-cache invalidation of exactly the affected entries, and `AS OF` interpretation stability at every step. DETAILED LOGGING: the implementation logs every schema-epoch publication `{graph, branch, before_epoch, after_epoch, transition_digest, apply_basis}`, every posture transition with validation row counts, every catalog alias mutation `{alias, from_graph_or_branch, to, marker}`, and every promotion shadow-build phase (pin, catch-up watermark, validation counts, activation marker); tests assert the presence and field-completeness of these events, and the e2e script asserts exactly one `CoordinateSchemaTransition` log record per schema mutation whose before/after roots byte-match the committed transition.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a single ambient schema epoch per transaction (conflates coordinates; breaks two-`AS OF` self-joins — §4.3 forbids it explicitly); names as identity (breaks rename under history and branching); inferring multi-coordinate atomicity from the shared sequence counter (§4.3: atomicity is the commit protocol's property); a second entity-resolution mutation mechanism beside `SAME_AS`/`AssertSameAs`; treating property storage as a superset of the query type lattice; native hyperedges (§3.4 rejection (a), one of the four alternatives evaluated in depth and rejected with recorded reasons — the §4.1 element model is deliberately binary: vertices plus typed, directed, possibly parallel binary edges, with no hyperedge arm in the closed element-model unions, so n-ary relations are expressed through ordinary vertices and typed binary edges rather than a new element kind); RDF-first modeling (§3.4 — property graph first; RDF import/view is a later compatibility layer, never the primary model). Risk: posture-churn thrash — bounded because migration is an ordinary shadow-build job under decision-card discipline; risk: reserved-slot collisions with user schemas — prevented by registry-generated reserved-name rejection at G0.

## Provenance
Plan §4.1 (186–195), §4.2 (197–205), §4.3 (207–213), §4.4 (215–217); Appendix A `CommitMarker.head_updates[]` (1945–1953); §8.1 (664) and §13.3 for binding consumption; §3.4/§10.1 for the `Point` non-goal; §3.4 (lines 153–157) for the hyperedge and RDF-first rejections.

title: Build fgdb-secure-view as the sole authorized facade (mandatory access types)
description:
## What & scope
Implement the `fgdb-secure-view` crate: the single crate that may construct `AuthorizedSnapshot`, `AuthorizedCursor`, `AuthorizedGraphView`, `AuthorizedMutation`, `AuthorizedMutationPermit`, and `AuthorizedDerivedState`.
