Enforcement is a mandatory access type, not middleware: Fabric, Loom, Ripple, Beacon, Prism, UDFs, backup/export, observability, and constraint reporting cannot obtain raw Strata cursors or unscoped commit submission. Includes `DescriptorVisibilityProjection` and the `ConstraintDisclosureContract` union.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/governance is the market gap (§3.3): capability governance over agent memory is what buyers cannot get. Making authorization a Rust type-construction privilege (only this crate exports the constructors; W1's restricted verifier is the sole permit constructor behind the facade) means a forged internal call cannot bypass policy merely by reaching a lower crate — the coordinator independently re-verifies the permit and final-effect authorization as §5.2 requires. Planner pushdown is an optimization atop this boundary, never the authorization root.

## Design — normative detail
Authorization occurs before retrieval/statistics/ANN traversal/expansion and both before and after mutation. `AuthorizedMutationPermit` (defined in `fgdb-authz-types`, nonconstructible outside the trusted verifier) binds: database security namespace/incarnation, tenant/principal/issuer, authority digest and non-widenable operation ceiling, policy-semantics ObjectId, policy and revocation indices, root/snapshot and branch scope, exact read `GraphReferenceBinding[]` and write `CoordinateSchemaBinding[]`, topology epoch, expiry, channel/session binding where applicable, and a unique nonce.

Hidden-state constraints require an explicit `ConstraintDisclosureContract`, a closed three-arm union: `CompleteDomainAuthority` (the mutator may observe the entire constrained domain), `AuthorityPartitioned` (integrity defined independently inside a tenant/authority partition), or `ExplicitConflictDeclassification` (a narrowly scoped capability deliberately releases one padded conflict bit, with audit ticket, rate limit, and no conflicting identity/value). A blind writer without one of these contracts is rejected before probing; error redaction cannot make global uniqueness and zero-disclosure coexist.

Descriptor masking is an enforced object: only fgdb-secure-view may construct `DescriptorVisibilityProjection {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>, graph_reference_binding, snapshot_identity, canonical_visible_descriptor_keys, per_descriptor_predicate_digests, degree_mode:ExactAuthorityPartition{visible_count_index_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizedVisibleCountIndex>}|FilteredScanRequired, projection_digest}`. The permit, access admission, AuthorizedSnapshot, witness/routing basis, plan certificate, cache key, and release decision all bind that digest and exact authority record. An `ExactAuthorityPartition` count is usable only when authority partition/predicates match; otherwise degree uses authorized filtered scan. Hidden descriptors/rows affect no visible enumeration, cardinality, routing, plan/error/timing/statistics/cache fact.

The remaining contract surface covers hidden-edge cascades, property/provenance/embedding masks, invoker-versus-definer view rights, subscription reauthorization, capability-safe conflicts and certificates, branch merge, system graph, backup/restore, and descriptor masking so hidden edges cannot affect visible degree. Every API and operator declares its permitted declassifications.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated): authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability; `SnapshotQuery` admission obeys the identical authorization-before-observation rule with the same oracle coverage as the durable read classes; every authority-bearing durable schema binds one complete `SecurityStateBinding`; one union-wide authorization decision covers the complete effect set; capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure; hidden constraints follow one explicit disclosure contract and only named ticketed declassification is legal. All conformance here is invariant-class (proof/oracle), not statistical.

## Interactions
Consumes w1-authz-policy (verifier IR + permit types) and w2-snapshots-leases (`ReadSnapshot` the facade wraps into `AuthorizedSnapshot`), w3-tier-d (the raw cursors it fences). Produces the facade consumed by every reader/writer: w4-mvcc-locks and w4-coordinator (mutation path), w5-executor, w6 views, w7 indexes, w8 projections (`SnapshotGraphView` must come through here), w9-enforcement (which extends this boundary), w10 surfaces. w4-constraints consumes `ConstraintDisclosureContract`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Compile-time enforcement test: a crate outside fgdb-secure-view attempting to construct any Authorized* type fails to compile (trybuild negative fixtures). (2) Forged-internal-call negative: a synthetic lower-crate call with a fabricated permit is rejected by the coordinator's independent verification. (3) Differential hidden-vs-physically-removed databases: for a corpus of graphs, every query/plan/error/timing/statistics/cache observable is byte-identical between "element hidden by policy" and "element absent". (4) Noninterference rows for every API/operator, plus cross-capability differential tests. (5) Degree-mode test: ExactAuthorityPartition used only on exact authority match; fallback filtered scan produces identical counts. (6) Blind-writer rejection test: uniqueness probe without a disclosure contract is rejected before any probe I/O (verified by I/O trace logging in the e2e script; log must show zero storage reads before the typed rejection).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: facade becomes a performance choke point — mitigated because pushdown is allowed as optimization once authorization is bound into the plan certificate. Rejected: authorization as server middleware (bypassable by internal calls); per-cursor convention for descriptor masking (must be an enforced object); letting error/timing channels leak hidden-state conflicts (padded, ticketed declassification only).

## Provenance
Plan §12.3 (884-891), §5.2 step "Propose"/permit paragraph (384), §12.4 context; Appendix F FG-INV-20.

title: Implement the SSI witness algebra: all witness types, contracts, refinement, gating
description:
## What & scope
Implement phantom protection for pattern queries: the closed set of witness encodings, the three executable contracts every witness implementation supplies, the FG-INV-06 refinement law, gap registration, refinement-under-budget, and the reject-in-SERIALIZABLE-until-proved gate. Every physical access path declares an abstract logical-read domain plus a conservative witness encoding.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
SSI must protect observed elements AND observed absence — graph pattern queries (negative patterns, optional matches, path searches with early termination) read absences that a later write can invalidate. B5: witness soundness is a formal, per-family gated claim with oracles, never an assumption; the refine-vs-abort policy is a performance decision card that cannot change the conservative-abort fallback. This is the donor adaptation from frankensqlite's page-level Cahill/Fekete SSI: storage-granularity dangerous-structure detection is kept, but logical predicate witnesses are added because graph access paths are logical, not physical.

## Design — normative detail
Witness types (closed, verbatim):
`BlockRange {descriptor, stable_low_key, stable_high_key, generation, visible_version, routing_translation_epoch}`;
`AdjacencyRange {descriptor, low_key, high_key, gaps, descriptor_epoch}`;
`LabelPartition {label_expr, partition, predicate, gaps, scan_epoch}`;
`IndexRange {index_generation, low_key, high_key, gaps, early_stop_boundary}`;
`NegativePattern {canonical_predicate, quantified_domain}`;
`PathCut {path_semantics, automaton_state, mode_state_class, settled_domain, unexpanded_edge_domain, cost_boundary, feasible_time_domain, topology_epoch}`.

Each witness implementation supplies three executable contracts: `concretization(w)` — the set of logical positive and negative observations represented; `may_affect(final_write, w)`; and `refine(coarse, trace)`. A `BlockRange` is logical-keyed: split, seal, and compaction publish a mutation-routing translation from old generation/range to its covering descendants, retained until the SSI overlap horizon passes; an implementation unable to retain that translation emits `AdjacencyRange` directly. A bare physical block address is never a witness.

Refinement law (FG-INV-06 core): `concretization(refined) SUBSET-OF concretization(coarse)` AND preservation of every logically relevant positive read, gap, absence observation, early-stop boundary, and path cut. Refining a predicate to only elements returned or encountered is forbidden unless the binder proved it was a point predicate.

`WitnessTrace` is execution evidence, not automatically the predicate domain. `ORDER BY/LIMIT`, anti/semi joins, optional matches, negative patterns, uniqueness probes, and early-terminated scans register the gaps or remaining domains whose absence affected the result. Path witnesses use the same mode-aware product state and proved dominance relations as §8.2; `(NFA state, partition, cost)` alone is NOT accepted for TRAIL, SIMPLE/ACYCLIC, temporal, capture-sensitive, or negative-cost semantics.

Refinement-under-budget: an apparent overlap may be refined under a bounded resource reservation. If exact overlap survives, or the budget expires, validation conservatively aborts and reports whether refinement was truncated. That conservative abort is the disposition of the VALIDATING CANDIDATE whose witness overlap could not be refined away, not an edge-level law: dependency edges among committed transactions are legal and retained — they are the SSI serialization graph. The accept/reject law for a candidate is §7.1's certification law (cycle/dangerous-structure/real-time-edge test); refinement only shrinks the conservative edge set entering that test. Canonical predicate normalization improves witness reuse but is not itself a proof of semantic equivalence; every rewrite used for witness identity carries a law certificate.

Gate: the default SERIALIZABLE claim is gated on (a) formal soundness of every witness constructor and refinement; (b) preservation through every optimizer rewrite; (c) exhaustive small-graph differential histories against an independent reference dependency checker; (d) model-based tests inserting precisely the missing edges/vertices/index keys that could invalidate negative and path results. Until a witness family passes those gates, queries using it are REJECTED in SERIALIZABLE mode rather than silently downgraded.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-06 (restated): every witness conservatively represents all logically relevant positive, negative, gap, valid-time slice, early-stop, and path-cut observations, and refinement preserves their concretization and `may_affect` behavior; W12 routing/coarsening, workspace overlays, shard transport, cumulative statement union, and finalization preserve the same contracts; missing routing, prior-touched-shard overlay, time slice, support, or proof causes conservative failure, never a dropped edge. Enforcement: constructor/refinement/optimizer/partition/workspace/temporal transport proofs plus mutation-complete differential suites. The refine-vs-abort policy point is decision-card (FG-EVID-01-style disclosure); witness soundness itself is invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes w4-mvcc-locks (SIREAD storage, overlap horizon), w3-tier-r (index/run generations and early-stop metadata that IndexRange/BlockRange name), w2-snapshots-leases (snapshot identity in witness basis). Produces: the witness set consumed by w4-strict-serializability (edges entering the certification law), w4-merge-ladder (rung-3 SSI rerun), w5-planner (rewrite preservation obligations + law certificates), w5-executor (trace/gap registration), w4-temporal-nonoverlap (`ValidTimeRangeWitness` follows the same contracts), w12-certification (transport of the same contracts).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Per-family contract tests: for each of the six types, property tests that `concretization(refine(w, trace)) SUBSET-OF concretization(w)` and that `may_affect` is monotone under refinement (any write affecting the refined witness affects the coarse one). (2) Routing-translation test: after split/seal/compaction, `BlockRange` witnesses route to covering descendants; deleting the translation before horizon expiry is a negative fixture forcing AdjacencyRange emission. (3) Model-based phantom insertion: generated small graphs where exactly one missing edge/vertex/index key would change a negative/path/LIMIT result; the corresponding write must produce an rw edge (differential vs independent reference dependency checker). (4) Path-mode negatives: TRAIL/SIMPLE/ACYCLIC/temporal/capture-sensitive/negative-cost histories where `(NFA state, partition, cost)`-only dominance would drop a cut — must be rejected by the constructor gate. (5) Budget-expiry test: forced refinement truncation conservatively aborts the candidate and the report flags truncation (assert in logs). (6) Gate wiring: a witness family with an intentionally failing proof causes SERIALIZABLE queries using it to be rejected with a typed error, never downgraded (e2e script asserts the error class and that no result bytes were produced).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: over-coarse witnesses inflate false aborts (refinement + decision-carded granularity, benchmark-gated); witness tables grow under long transactions (overlap-horizon reclamation + monotone coarsening from w4-mvcc-locks). Rejected: physical block addresses as witnesses; trace-as-domain refinement (unsound for absences); silent isolation downgrade for unproved families.

## Provenance
Plan §7.3 (592-614), §8.2 cross-reference (610); Appendix F FG-INV-06.

title: Prove and enforce the Local strict-serializability certification law
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Local certifier's strictness law — the real-time-precedence-edge / Cahill-pivot certification rule — register the proof-class theorem that the Local default contract is STRICT SERIALIZABLE, wire the named carve-out read classes, and stand up the abort-rate benchmark obligation.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the difference between "serializable" and "strict serializable" is exactly the kind of claim that must be a registered theorem with explicit premises, not marketing. B6: agents chain observations across sessions ("read what I just committed elsewhere"); real-time order matters to tool-using agents more than to humans. SSI establishes an acyclic serialization-graph order; it does NOT assert that commit-marker order is the serialization order — exact acyclicity admits serializable-but-not-strict histories through long-lived read-write pivots, so an extra law is required and its abort cost is honestly priced.

## Design — normative detail
Premises (hold by construction in the Local posture): (P1) a single sequencer orders every semantic command; (P2) snapshot acquisition reads and revalidates the current published slot (§5.3), so every commit acknowledged before acquisition is included in the snapshot; (P3) acknowledgement follows gap-free visible publication (§5.2). These are necessary, not sufficient.

The strictness law (registered, two equivalent formulations): (a) real-time precedence edges — every transaction whose visible publication precedes the candidate's snapshot acquisition precedes it in the checked serialization graph; or (b) by the registered earliest-committer argument, any cycle in the union of the dependency graph and the real-time order must route through a long-lived concurrent pivot carrying an rw-in and an rw-out edge whose rw-out target commits first — hence a registered Cahill-style dangerous-structure rule suffices. With the law, the Local default contract is STRICT SERIALIZABLE, registered under §1.11 as a `proof`-class theorem whose premises are exactly P1-P3 plus the law; without the law, strictness is not claimable.

Carve-outs (named typed contracts, never silent weakening): `READ_ONLY_HISTORICAL`, `SNAPSHOT`, `SNAPSHOT_FOLLOWER(max_lag)`, `BRANCH_CAUSAL`, and explicit historical selectors (`AS OF`). Ordinary serializable read-only transactions may receive a serialization failure; `READ_ONLY DEFERRABLE` may wait for a safe snapshot and, once acquired, is immune to SSI abort. The server rejects rather than silently weakens a requested minimum.

Cost accounting: the added conservatism raises abort rates for long-lived writers — most under Required-audit visible-prefix lag, where writers validate against applied state while readers see the visible prefix and backward rw edges become more common. That cost is a registered `benchmark`-class distribution, never assumed free. W12 remains plain SERIALIZABLE unless the Meta certifier adopts the same real-time-edge rule; the oracle strengthening is registered in Appendix F's FG-INV-05 row.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-05 (restated): every committed SERIALIZABLE history has an acyclic logical dependency graph, and dependency metadata remains until no overlapping attempt can add an edge. For the Local SERIALIZABLE default the checked graph additionally contains real-time precedence edges — or applies the registered dangerous-structure rule proved to reject every DSG-union-real-time cycle — so the default Local contract is strict serializable; W12 Meta histories remain plain serializable unless Meta registers the same certification rule. Each statement publication atomically extends the cumulative witness/conflict state; ReadWrite admission and ReadOnly close name the exact statement/delivery/workspace frontier and independently recheck the complete graph; compaction removes detail only after overlap closure. Claim types: the strictness theorem is `proof`-class (premises P1-P3 + law); the abort-rate distribution is `benchmark`-class; the SCC/Elle oracle is the enforcement row.

## Interactions
Consumes w4-ssi-witnesses (the conservative edge set entering the test), w2-commit-protocol (visible publication/acknowledgement state machine supplying real-time order), w2-snapshots-leases (snapshot acquisition revalidation, P2). Produces: the certification predicate used by w4-coordinator at final certification; the oracle strengthening consumed by verif-oracles (Elle/SCC must check DSG-union-real-time acyclicity for Local histories); the decision point w12-certification must either adopt or leave Meta at plain SERIALIZABLE. perf-bench-core hosts the abort-rate benchmark.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Registered theorem artifact: the equivalence of formulations (a) and (b) under the earliest-committer argument is registered on the §15.5 anchor list with its premise list wired to §1.11 registration — this bead lands the registration, statement, and premise wiring; the machine-checked proof (Lean or TLA+) is discharged in `verif-formal`'s lanes with lane-green at gate-g4. (2) Independent history oracle: lab-generated concurrent histories checked by an SCC oracle over the union graph (dependency + real-time); any accepted history with a union cycle is a hard failure. (3) Pivot fixtures: constructed serializable-but-not-strict histories (long-lived read-write pivot, rw-out target commits first) must be rejected by the certifier and flagged by the oracle if admitted. (4) Carve-out conformance: each named read class returns its contract; a requested-but-unavailable minimum is rejected with a typed error (e2e script asserts rejection, not downgrade, with response-class logging). (5) DEFERRABLE test: waits for a safe snapshot then never aborts under adversarial concurrent write load (lab virtual time). (6) Benchmark gate: registered abort-rate distribution comparing law-on vs law-off across long-lived-writer workloads and Required-audit visible-prefix lag; published with the release, regressions block per Appendix G/perf gates.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: abort inflation for long-lived writers under Required-audit lag — priced, benchmarked, and mitigated by carve-out classes and the merge ladder. Rejected: claiming strictness from SSI acyclicity alone (admits non-strict histories); commit-marker order as serialization order (false in general); TrueTime-class infrastructure (§3.4 rejection h — HLC plus consensus-fenced read contracts supplies exactly the semantics specified); silently downgrading unprovable requests.

## Provenance
Plan §7.1 (581-582); Appendix F FG-INV-05 row; §3.4(h).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement TemporalNonOverlapConstraint and the temporal constraint state root
description:
## What & scope
Implement temporal nonoverlap as synchronous authoritative state: `TemporalNonOverlapConstraint`, `TemporalConstraintStateRoot`, `CanonicalTemporalEntry` sets, `ValidTimeRangeWitness`, atomic before/after contribution swaps at finalization, and branch fork/merge overlay behavior. Split from w4-valid-time to keep both under the size ceiling.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
"No two salary records for one employee overlap in valid time" is the canonical bitemporal integrity demand; making it an index promise (the industry norm) yields phantom overlaps under concurrency. Synchronous authoritative state + SSI temporal witnesses give an invariant, serving B1 (one authoritative state) and the governance market gap (constraints with explicit disclosure).

## Design — normative detail
`TemporalNonOverlapConstraint` is `{constraint_id, coordinate_and_element_type, valid_time_contract_ref:StrongRef<ValidTimeContract>, canonical_key_expression_oid, maximum_overlap_multiplicity, null_key_policy, same_element_policy, disclosure_contract, schema_epoch}`. `TemporalConstraintStateRoot` is `{coordinate, schema_epoch, generation, entries[(constraint_id, canonical_key) -> CanonicalTemporalEntrySet], root_digest}`, where `CanonicalTemporalEntry = {interval, element_id, slice_id, system_version_basis, contribution_key}` and each entry set is canonically sorted. Finalization atomically removes every before-slice contribution and adds every after-slice contribution; the interval-tree/range implementation is derived (rebuildable), never authoritative.

`ValidTimeRangeWitness` binds `{binding_role, contract_id, key_or_predicate_domain, query_interval_set, positive_entries[{element_id, slice_id, interval}], gaps, slice_set_and_index_generations, base_and_tail_frontiers}` — it follows w4-ssi-witnesses' three contracts (concretization/may_affect/refine) so temporal phantoms (a new overlapping slice invalidating an observed gap) produce rw edges.

Branching: fork structurally shares the parent's basis and creates a branch overlay; sibling overlays diverge; merge replays, splits/coalesces, and revalidates the target. Hidden overlap failures obey the constraint's `disclosure_contract` (three-arm union from w4-secure-view). In W12, deterministic Meta constraint ownership/reservations cover cross-shard keys and shards export certified contributions (owned by w12-constraints-authority; this bead keeps the Local machinery projection-ready). Branch retirement retires the overlay with the cut (w2-branch-retire disposition).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-18: synchronous constraints must hold before commit — temporal nonoverlap is authoritative state, not an index promise. FG-INV-02: constraint-owner reservations on `(constraint_id, canonical_key)` have one live owner. FG-INV-06: `ValidTimeRangeWitness` conservatively represents positive entries, gaps, and time slices; refinement preserves them. All invariant-class.

## Interactions
Consumes w4-valid-time (slice algebra, lineage, `CanonicalValidTimeSet`), w4-constraints (`ValidTimeNonOverlap` body, mutation batch machinery: `SetTemporalInterval` arm, `Temporal{canonical_partition_tuple}` domain key, `TemporalIntervalSet` state value), w4-ssi-witnesses (witness contracts). Produces: constraint contributions consumed by w4-coordinator holds, overlay dispositions consumed by w2-branch-retire, certified-contribution shape consumed by w12-constraints-authority.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Unit: multiplicity bounds, null-key policy arms, same-element policy arms; checked interval arithmetic at domain boundaries. (2) Property: for any slice-set mutation, before/after contribution swap is atomic and net (no intermediate visible state; differential vs recomputed-from-scratch entry sets). (3) Temporal phantom tests: transaction A observes a gap `[t1,t2)` for key K; concurrent B inserts an overlapping slice; certification must find the rw edge (model-based insertion per w4-ssi-witnesses gate). (4) Fork/merge: sibling overlays hold conflicting intervals without leaking; merge replay splits/coalesces and revalidates the target root (reference differential). (5) Disclosure: hidden-overlap failure emits only the contract-conformant error; cross-capability differential shows no identity/value leak. (6) Rebuild check: derived interval tree deleted and rebuilt equals authoritative entry sets byte-for-byte. (7) Crash rows: crash between mutation batch and apply; retry idempotent. (8) e2e bitemporal script: an employee/salary graph under a nonoverlap constraint runs concurrent overlapping-slice writers (exactly one commits), subinterval corrections, sibling-branch fork/merge with conflicting intervals, and a derived interval-tree rebuild, asserting final entry sets against the reference evaluator. DETAILED LOGGING: every contribution swap logs {constraint_id, canonical_key, removed_contribution_count, added_contribution_count, generation_before, generation_after}; violation rejections log {contract_arm, padded} and never an identity/value payload (the disclosure differential in (5) also asserts log-channel noninterference); witness registration logs {witness_kind, positive_entry_count, gap_count}; tests assert these structured fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: hot keys serialize on owner reservations (inherent to synchronous integrity; disclosure-partitioned scopes reduce domain width). Rejected: index-backed asynchronous overlap checking (phantoms); treating the interval tree as authoritative (must be derived/rebuildable); global-only scoping (authority-partitioned integrity is a first-class arm).

## Provenance
Plan §4.6 (242), App A (1970-1974), §5.6 (469), §12.3 (888).

title: Implement TemporalSlice/TemporalJoin operators and temporal path modes
description:
## What & scope
Implement §4.6's temporal evaluation surface: `TemporalSlice`, `TemporalJoin`, the output-coalescing law, the closed temporal path-mode union, and the exact feasible-time domains in path state and witnesses. Split from w4-valid-time for size.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3 (one execution model): temporal evaluation is ordinary Loom operators over slice-carrying rows, not a separate temporal engine. B5: path feasibility over time is exactly where competitors return wrong answers (a path valid edge-by-edge may be invalid as a journey); the Monotone witness with hop times and waiting-interval validity makes the semantics exact and checkable.

## Design — normative detail
`TemporalSlice(row, Q)` emits the intersection of the row period and `Q` and drops an empty result. `TemporalJoin` emits the intersection across every participating period and preserves ordinary multiplicity. Adjacent output periods coalesce ONLY when every nonperiod value, multiplicity, provenance, authorization projection, and deterministic ordering key is byte-identical.

Temporal path mode is the closed union `Concurrent{one_common_instant_required} | Monotone{order:Nondecreasing|Strict}`. A Monotone witness carries canonical hop times `t0..tn`; each edge and endpoint is valid at its hop, times obey the selected order, and an intermediate vertex remains valid over any waiting interval `[t_i, t_{i+1}]`. `DURING Q` first intersects every candidate period with `Q`. `PathStateKey.feasible_valid_time` and `PathCut.feasible_time_domain` are exact `CanonicalValidTimeSet`s; dominance, spill encoding, and coalescing are separately proved for each mode, and the deterministic tie break appends the canonical time-witness schedule after ordinary path keys. Rows denoting sliced elements retain the slice discriminator `{stable_element_ref, slice_id, period}` until a defined coalesce/projection boundary; ordinary `id()` returns the stable VId/EId.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04: distinct valid-time selectors never alias; operator outputs respect slice-set intersection and boundary normalization. FG-INV-06: path cuts carry `feasible_time_domain` exactly — a temporal path witness missing a time slice causes conservative failure, never a dropped edge; `(NFA state, partition, cost)` alone is not accepted for temporal semantics. FG-INV-12: coalescing is an answer-equivalence claim (byte-identity conditions). Registered `TemporalSlice`/`TemporalJoin` derivatives must equal batch evaluation (invariant-class, delta = batch).

## Interactions
Consumes w4-valid-time (interval/slice algebra, `CanonicalValidTimeSet`), w4-ssi-witnesses (PathCut contracts, dominance discipline shared with §8.2). Produces: operators consumed by w5-executor (path machinery, spill) and w5-gla-algebra (operator inventory rows); delta-equality obligation consumed by w6-zset-circuits; feasible-time domains consumed by w7-path-temporal.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Operator unit tests: intersection/empty-drop, multiplicity preservation, boundary equality at half-open endpoints, infinite bounds. (2) Coalesce metamorphic: permuting input order never changes coalesced output; any non-byte-identical nonperiod value blocks coalescing (negative fixtures per condition: multiplicity, provenance, authorization projection, ordering key). (3) Path-mode reference tests: every mode (Concurrent, Monotone Nondecreasing/Strict) against brute-force enumeration on small graphs, including waiting-interval validity violations and `DURING` pre-intersection; spill/restore round-trips preserve dominance decisions. (4) Dominance proofs: per-mode registered proof artifacts; a fixture using ordinary cost-only dominance under a temporal mode fails the constructor gate. (5) Determinism: tie-break with appended time-witness schedule yields byte-identical results across runs/replans (CGSE witness comparison). (6) Derivative-vs-batch differential for registered temporal derivatives across slice-set mutations. (7) e2e temporal query script: load a small bitemporal graph and run TemporalSlice/TemporalJoin/coalesce queries plus every path mode (Concurrent, Monotone Nondecreasing/Strict, with DURING) end-to-end via the query surface against brute-force results. DETAILED LOGGING: each operator execution logs {operator, input_rows, output_rows, coalesce_merges, coalesce_blocked_reason}; path search logs {mode, settled_count, dominance_prunes, spill_events, time_witness_schedule_digest}; the determinism test in (5) compares the logged digests across runs, and coalesce negative fixtures assert coalesce_blocked_reason names the exact blocking condition.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: temporal dominance state growth (exact `CanonicalValidTimeSet` domains with proved spill encodings; witness-only coarsening is allowed after a declared bound, results never coarsen). Rejected: edge-by-edge validity as path validity (journey semantics required); coalescing on value-equality alone (would merge rows with distinct provenance/authorization); a separate temporal executor.

## Provenance
Plan §4.6 (240), §8.2 cross-reference; Appendix F FG-INV-04/06/12.

title: Implement element expiry contracts (TTL): visibility predicate, epoch advance, decay
description:
## What & scope
Implement §4.8 completely: `ExpiryContract`, the `_expires_at` reserved slot, expiry as a visibility conjunct, the closure-captured evaluation instant, `ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec` (the sole sequencer-visible expiry artifact), lazy physical reclamation under retention floors, the closed Ripple expiry law, and the decay policy's claim-typing. The format arms land at G0; the mechanism may trail, the arms may not.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agent memory needs TTL (session scratch, cache-like facts) — but naive TTL-as-mutation floods the commit stream and breaks determinism. Expiry is a VISIBILITY PREDICATE, never a mutation: no stored byte changes, no retirement transaction exists, the sequencer never carries per-element expiry work. B5: the evaluation instant is closure-captured, so replay is byte-deterministic. B1: expiry composes with branches per head and with `AS OF` per pinned instant.

## Design — normative detail
`ExpiryContract` is the immutable schema object `{contract_id, element_kind_and_type, expiry_slot, domain:InstantUtcNanos, default_assignment:NoExpiry|RequireExplicit, visibility_semantics, permitted_selectors, canonical_scalar_profile_oid, schema_epoch, body_digest}`, mirroring `ValidTimeContract`'s shape. It declares the reserved `_expires_at` slot (§4.4) for one element kind and type; `domain` is exactly `InstantUtcNanos`; comparison, precision, overflow, and canonical encoding come only from the bound `CanonicalScalarProfile`; `default_assignment` fixes whether an absent instant means no expiry or a rejected write; `visibility_semantics`/`permitted_selectors` fix the at-or-before invisibility rule and the closed selector set naming the expiry axis.

Visibility: a version whose `_expires_at` instant is at or before the query's pinned evaluation instant is invisible to current-time reads as an additional §5.3 visibility conjunct — exactly as retirement/supersession markers make versions invisible. The evaluation instant is the closure-captured profiled authority-time observation of the binding (the same pattern §4.6 fixes for `CURRENT VALID_TIME`), never an ambient wall-clock read; it enters the authorization, plan-cache, certificate, and replay keys, so the same pinned closure yields the same bytes. Expired-but-within-retention versions remain visible to `AS OF` selectors pinned at pre-expiry instants. An expired instant never authorizes GC by itself. Expiry composes with branch selection per head: `_expires_at` writes are ordinary versioned property mutations, so sibling branches may carry different expiry updates and every binding evaluates expiry against its own selected ancestry and pinned instant.

Reclamation: lazy; the sequenced command stream observes expiry only as one registered `ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec` control command per configured epoch tick — the sole sequencer-visible expiry artifact. The epoch advance is an ordered transition carrying subject-bound rollback-resistant `TimeValidationEvidence`, mirroring §4.7's quota-epoch discipline; ambient time never advances an expiry epoch. Compaction drops fully expired versions under the ordinary §5.3/§5.4 retention floors and snapshot leases; a version still covered by a floor, lease, or backup pin is retained invisible bytes, and its later physical drop changes no visible answer.

Ripple law (closed): a registered derivation over expiry-bearing inputs must declare exactly one of `ExpiryInsensitive`, an explicit `AS OF` evaluation basis, or `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick`; the consumed tick emits one canonical retraction delta for every version newly expired at the epoch boundary, so every registered derivative equals batch evaluation at that boundary, silent time-varying view drift is inexpressible, and an undeclared derivation over an expiry-enabled input fails closed at registration.

Decay: salience-weighted retention priority is a named post-1.0 GC/compaction policy candidate, claim-typed FG-CFG for its policy model and FG-EVID for its statistical evidence, never an invariant: it may prioritize which already-reclaimable bytes compaction visits first and may NEVER shorten a retention floor, override a GC root, or claim any semantic effect.

Lifecycle: enabling/changing/disabling an `ExpiryContract` is an ordinary transactional schema effect under §4.6's pinned-snapshot shadow-build, delta catch-up, exact validation, and atomic schema-epoch publication; old snapshots keep their former contract; a type without an enabled contract rejects expiry syntax and `_expires_at` assignment rather than silently storing an inert instant. The `ExpiryContract` registry rows, `_expires_at` reserved-slot row, expiry selectors, and `ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec` command-contract and classification rows are decided at Gate G0.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (restated, expiry conjunct): visibility obeys the expiry predicate (§4.8) alongside snapshot/ancestry/valid-time/erasure conjuncts; distinct selectors never alias. FG-INV-19 (restated, relevant clause): the same pinned closure yields the same bytes — the pinned evaluation instant is part of the replay closure. Decay policy: FG-CFG (policy model) + FG-EVID (statistical evidence), explicitly not invariant-class. Epoch-tick cadence and reclamation lag are slo-class observations.

## Interactions
Consumes w4-valid-time (contract shape, closure-captured authority-time pattern, schema lifecycle), w9-time-authority (`TimeValidationEvidence` for epoch advance), w2-retention-checkpoints + w2-compaction (floors/leases governing physical drop), g0-format-arms (Expiry arms decided at G0). Produces: the expiry visibility conjunct consumed by every read path (w4-secure-view, w5-executor), the `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` retraction stream consumed by w6-views/w6-subscriptions/w6-freshness, replay-key fields consumed by w5-replay.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Visibility unit tests: at-boundary equality (expires exactly at pinned instant => invisible), pre-expiry `AS OF` visibility, per-branch divergent `_expires_at` values evaluated against each binding's own ancestry+instant. (2) Determinism: replays of one pinned closure across epoch ticks return byte-identical results; ambient-clock use in the expiry path is a negative fixture (runtime capability check). (3) Sequencer-load test: N expiring elements produce exactly one `ExpiryEpochAdvanceSpec` per tick and zero per-element commands (assert on the command stream log). (4) Epoch-advance evidence: rollback-resistant `TimeValidationEvidence` required; stale/rolled-back evidence rejects the advance (negative fixtures). (5) Reclamation: expired version under a floor/lease/backup pin is retained invisible; post-floor physical drop changes no visible answer (differential before/after compaction). (6) Ripple law: an undeclared derivation over an expiry-enabled input fails closed at registration; `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` derivatives equal batch evaluation at the boundary (differential); `ExpiryInsensitive` views never drift across ticks. (7) Contract lifecycle e2e with crash rows; a disabled type rejects `_expires_at` assignment with a typed, logged error.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: coarse epoch ticks delay derived-view retractions (cadence configured; freshness is slo-class FG-EVID-04). Rejected: TTL-as-mutation (sequencer flood, replay nondeterminism); ambient wall-clock evaluation (breaks FG-INV-19 and plan-cache keys); expiry authorizing GC (retention floors alone govern reclamation); decay as a semantic mechanism (visibility never depends on salience).

## Provenance
Plan §4.8 (262-268), §4.4 (217); Appendix F FG-INV-04/19; §19 Gate G0 reference (268).

title: Implement valid-time semantics: contracts, slice sets, selectors, temporal operators
description:
## What & scope
Implement the second temporal axis (§4.6): the valid-time interval algebra, `ValidTimeContract`, `ValidTimeSliceSet`/`ValidTimeSlice` with lineage, subinterval mutation semantics, selector algebra, and the storage/delta/authorization requirements. Temporal operators and path modes are split into w4-temporal-operators; TemporalNonOverlap constraint machinery into w4-temporal-nonoverlap.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: valid time rides the same version universe — the engine first resolves branch ancestry, system snapshot, coordinate schema, and the ONE system-visible slice-set generation, then applies the valid-time selector; no second temporal store (the AeonG §3.1 lesson: temporal as a corollary of durability, not a bolt-on). B4: canonical slice-keyed deltas make every registered temporal derivative equal batch evaluation. B6: agent memory is bitemporal (facts valid over intervals, corrected later); typed interval algebra with exact lineage beats nullable `_valid_from/_valid_to` properties, which every competitor mangles.

## Design — normative detail
Algebra: `ValidTimeDomain` is exactly `DateDay|InstantUtcNanos`; floating local dates/times are query inputs only, normalized under a pinned timezone/coercion profile before entering either domain. `ValidTimeBound<T>` is `NegInfinity|Finite(T)|PosInfinity`. A stored `ValidTimeInterval<T>` is one nonempty half-open `[start,end)` where start != PosInfinity, end != NegInfinity, finite start < finite end. `CanonicalValidTimeSet<T>` is a sorted, disjoint, nonadjacent sequence; adjacent intervals coalesce. Comparison, precision loss, overflow, and canonical encoding come only from the bound `CanonicalScalarProfile`. Witness-only approximations may conservatively coarsen after a declared bound; result and constraint state spill or fail and never coarsen.

`ValidTimeContract` is the immutable schema object `{contract_id, element_kind_and_type, domain, endpoint_precision, storage:ElementVersionSliceSet, default_assignment:RequireExplicit|AllTime, permitted_selectors, mutation_policy, temporal_constraint_ids[], path_policy_ids[], canonical_scalar_profile_oid, schema_epoch, body_digest}`. A system-time element version encodes exactly `NotApplicable{single_payload} | Sliced{contract_ref:StrongRef<ValidTimeContract>, slice_set_ref:StrongRef<ValidTimeSliceSet>}`. `ValidTimeSliceSet` is `{element_identity, contract_id, generation, sorted_slices[ValidTimeSlice], complete_domain_coverage_commitment?, root_digest}`; intervals disjoint but need not be adjacent or cover all time. `ValidTimeSlice` is `{slice_id:ValidTimeSliceId, interval, payload:Vertex{label_set,properties,provenance}|Edge{fixed_src_type_dst,properties,provenance}, lineage:Created{operation_key}|Carried{prior_slice_id}|Split{prior_slice_id,fragment_ordinal}|Coalesced{sorted_prior_slice_ids}, payload_digest}`. Slice IDs are stable for unchanged carried fragments and newly derived by a domain-separated hash of element identity, source operation key or sorted parent IDs, resulting interval, payload digest, and fragment ordinal. Two current slices may never overlap; coalescing is mandatory only for adjacent slices with byte-identical payload, provenance, authorization class, and lineage-safe ordering metadata. One stable VId/EId can simultaneously represent `[2020,2021)=A` and `[2021,2022)=B` without duplicating identity.

Mutation: properties and label membership are slice payloads for an enabled type; edge src/type/dst remain element identity attributes while edge properties/provenance vary by slice. `_valid_from`/`_valid_to` are protected projections of the currently enumerated slice, never separately mutable (row-level slice discriminators are specified in w4-temporal-operators). A subinterval mutation performs canonical interval subtraction, creates exact carried/split/replacement fragments, and leaves the untouched remainder visible; its effect records full before/after slice sets plus a total lineage map; overwriting one header interval is forbidden. Delete under `FOR VALID_TIME` retracts only selected slice intersections unless syntax explicitly requests the stable element across all valid time; full retirement records every current slice before-image. Enabling/changing/disabling a contract is an ordinary transactional schema effect with pinned-snapshot shadow build, delta catch-up, exact validation, atomic schema-epoch publication; old snapshots keep their former contract; a disabled type rejects valid-time syntax.

Selection: system and valid time are orthogonal. `ValidTimeSelector` is exactly `All | At{instant} | Overlaps{query_set} | ContainedIn{query_set} | Contains{query_set}`. Omitted valid-time syntax means `All`, never wall-clock "now". FQL: `FOR VALID_TIME ALL|AS OF <t>|OVERLAPS <interval>|CONTAINED IN <interval>|CONTAINS <interval>`; `graph@branch AS OF` is system-time-only. A future `CURRENT VALID_TIME` must capture a profiled authority-time observation into the query/certificate/replay closure. `PreparedQueryTemplate`/`BoundQuery` carry separate `system_selector` and normalized `{valid_selector, contract_id, domain, precision}` per graph-reference role; those values enter authorization, plan-cache, certificate, and replay keys. Valid time never changes `CommitSeq`, ancestry, or retention; an old valid endpoint never authorizes GC.

Storage/deltas: canonical rows, effects, and Ripple deltas carry contract, stable element identity, slice ID, and period. A slice-set change emits one retraction per removed/before fragment and one insertion per added/after fragment including split/coalesce lineage, so every registered `TemporalSlice`/`TemporalJoin` derivative equals batch evaluation. Tier D and sealed runs key temporal payloads by `(stable_element_id, valid_start, slice_id)`, store canonical endpoint tags/columns, preserve one canonical incidence identity per edge; Beacon temporal indexes are rebuildable watermarked generations; exact queries tail them or use the base fallback. `ValidTimeContract`, `ValidTimeSliceSet`/nodes, `TemporalConstraintStateRoot`/nodes, selectors, path modes, intents/effects, and witnesses have exact registry rows and generated Local/Meta/Shard payload, checkpoint, floor, backup, restore, GC, and role-transition coverage. Authorization temporal scopes are intersected before scan, index, expansion, path, constraint observation, error formation, or mutation; a mutation checks every before AND after slice.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (visibility obeys valid-time slice-set intersection and boundary normalization; distinct valid-time selectors never alias). FG-INV-18 (canonical committed effects equal logical before/after state over normalized valid-time slices). FG-INV-06 (valid-time slice observations are witness-relevant). Registered temporal derivatives are invariant-class (delta = batch); temporal index staleness is FG-CFG-03/slo-class, never an invariant.

## Interactions
Consumes w1-foundation-types (`CanonicalScalarProfile`), w3-tier-d (temporal payload keying), w2-delta-batches (canonical delta stream carrying slice IDs/periods), w4-constraints (temporal bodies), w2-commit-protocol (effects/capsules). Produces: slice algebra for w4-temporal-operators and w4-temporal-nonoverlap; selector/keys consumed by w5-binder and w5-replay; deltas consumed by w6-zset-circuits; temporal index basis for w7-path-temporal.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Unit/fuzz: exhaust infinities, empty/reversed intervals, boundary equality, precision/overflow, canonical set coalescing, split lineage, encodings. (2) Property: interval subtraction + fragment lineage reconstructs exact before/after sets; slice-ID stability for carried fragments and domain-separated derivation for new ones. (3) Reference/model matrix: system-time x valid-time x branch x schema visibility; simultaneous disjoint slices; subinterval correction/deletion with untouched remainder; workspace updates; sibling merge; derivative-vs-batch; compaction/seal/index-tail/backup/restore/activation equivalence; temporal-scope noninterference. (4) Selector-key test: plan-cache/certificate/replay keys differ whenever `{valid_selector, contract_id, domain, precision}` differ (negative: two selectors aliasing one cache entry fails). (5) Contract lifecycle e2e: enable->shadow-build->catch-up->validate->epoch-publish with crash rows at each phase; old snapshots keep the former contract; disabled type rejects syntax (logs assert typed rejection). (6) DETAILED LOGGING: slice-set mutations log {element_id, contract_id, generation_before, generation_after, removed_slice_ids, added_slice_ids, lineage_arms}; selector binding logs {valid_selector, contract_id, domain, precision, cache_key_digest}; the lifecycle e2e in (5) asserts shadow-build/catch-up/validate/publish phase events with exact watermarks, and the selector-key test in (4) asserts cache-key divergence from the logged digests.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: slice-set explosion under frequent subinterval corrections (compaction coalescing + payload-identical merge law bound it; measured). Rejected: two nullable properties as valid time (undefined algebra, no lineage, no constraint basis); closed intervals (half-open composes); wall-clock "now" defaults (nondeterministic replay, violates FG-INV-19); overwriting header intervals.

## Provenance
Plan §4.6 (230-244); Appendix F FG-INV-04/18/06; §3.1 AeonG row.

title: Specify AnswerRequirement/AnswerContract typing with freshness and transfer totality
description:
## What & scope
Define and implement the three deliberately different approximation phase types — execution-time `AnswerRequirement`, definition-time `ApproximationProfile`, and realized `AnswerContract` — plus the orthogonal freshness constraint and the transfer-totality law every GLA operator must satisfy. This is the semantic typing that makes every realized logical stream carry an honest exactness/approximation/freshness claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5/B6: agents must be able to demand exactness, permit qualified approximation, or bound derived-source staleness — and get a typed, replayable answer either way. The market failure this fixes: ANN/vector and stale-view systems that silently return approximate or lagging data as if exact. Freshness is expressed in watermark units precisely so no time-authority observation joins the hot read path (Appendix G cost discipline).

## Design — normative detail
`AnswerRequirement = Exact | AllowApproximate { permitted_kinds[], population_constraint?, minimum_quality?, evidence_floor, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }` is an execution-time demand and contains no chosen generation. Default is `Exact`; any query-language approximation clause narrows the requirement and an empty intersection is rejected at binding. An `AnswerRequirement` may additionally carry an optional orthogonal `freshness_constraint: FreshnessConstraint { maximum_source_lag: WatermarkLagBound, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }`, bounding how far any consumed advancing derived source generation (view, index, or maintainer output) may lag the executing snapshot's pinned read frontier; the bound is expressed in source-generation/watermark (commit-sequence) units, never as a wall-clock quantity. An unmet freshness bound behaves exactly like an unmet approximation demand — `ExactFallback` evaluates through the pinned exact path against the read frontier and `Fail` rejects with a typed error — and the realized `AnswerContract` already pins `source_generation_identities[]`, from which the realized lag is derived and reported in the result certificate without any new contract field. The reserved freshness fields (here and `SubscriptionDeliveryPolicy`) are a frozen G0 decision.

`ApproximationProfile { approximation_kind, population_contract, algorithm_profile_oid, semantic_build_and_search_parameter_schema, quality_evidence_schema, deterministic_exact_fallback_oid? }` is definition-time policy and likewise contains no generation identity. Only after access paths and parameters are bound does execution realize `AnswerContract = Exact | Approximate { approximation_kind, population_contract, error_or_recall_contract, source_generation_identities[], source_generation_digests[], algorithm_profile_oid, candidate_and_search_profile, evidence_identity, deterministic_fallback_oid? }`. A contract never strongly references the generation that carries it; the surrounding bound plan, generation registry, result/certificate envelope, and replay closure own concrete roots explicitly, avoiding definition/generation identity cycles.

Every realized logical stream is typed with an `AnswerContract` — a semantic type, not a certificate footnote. Transfer totality: each operator registers a total transfer rule that produces a contract satisfying the `AnswerRequirement`, proves exact completion, invokes the pinned exact fallback, or rejects the composition. Absence-sensitive, non-monotone, recursive, aggregate, distinct, and top-k operations cannot turn missing candidates into an exact result; they accept approximate inputs only under a registered sound calculus and otherwise fall back or fail. `Mutate` and every `Exact` requirement consume exact inputs only. All approximation-affecting generation topology, candidate/search depth, fusion, stopping, sampling, and evidence identities are pinned in the bound query/plan/certificate/replay closure and are never classified as result-neutral physical tuning. An approximate result remains byte-replayable under its pinned closure but is not thereby promoted to exact semantics. The `AnswerContract` surface additionally carries per-class delivery-behavior rows: §13's `SnapshotQuery` read class registers its `AnswerContract` behavior row recording non-resumable, no-replay, no-durable-outcome semantics — what that class gives up (durable outcome lookup, idempotent retry joining, result resume, replay evidence, exactly-once delivery) is part of the declared class contract, not an implementation weakness — and `w10-snapshotquery` consumes exactly this row (frozen in the G0 decision batch by `g0-format-arms`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: every answer-equivalent rewrite preserves the `AnswerContract`; approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation. FG-EVID-04 (slo-class, never an invariant): derived-state freshness bounds in watermark/commit-sequence units with realized lag distribution and typed `FreshnessBreach` rate. FG-CAL-03: ANN recall/drift evidence (population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval, rebuild action). Per the claim-type constitution, freshness/recall numbers are slo/benchmark/evidence class; the typing and transfer laws themselves are invariant-class.

## Interactions
`w5-binder` intersects caller requirement with language clauses; `w5-gla-algebra` registers the per-operator transfer rules (Appendix C answer-contract column); `w5-planner` may not trade contracts for cost; `w5-replay` pins realized contracts in manifests; `w6-freshness` implements `WITH FRESHNESS` and `FreshnessBreach` on this foundation; `w7-vector`/`w7-hybrid` realize `Approximate` contracts with recall evidence; `w10-result-machines` serializes contracts into certificates; `w10-snapshotquery` consumes the registered `SnapshotQuery` behavior row.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Type-level tests: requirement/profile contain no generation identity (compile-time or registry check); contract carries no strong ref to its carrying generation. Empty requirement-intersection rejection test. Unmet-freshness behavior differential: `ExactFallback` result byte-equals the pinned exact path against the read frontier; `Fail` returns the typed error — executable once the downstream realizers land (`w5-executor` for the exact path, `w6-freshness` for the freshness surface; both are epic-w5/gate-g1 prerequisites that depend on this bead), while at this bead the `on_unmet` arms are enforced as type-level/registry contracts. Transfer-totality checker over the operator registry: every registered operator has a total rule (CI fails on gaps). Certificate reports realized source lag derived from `source_generation_identities[]` with no new field. Fuzz: adversarial requirement/profile combinations never produce an unqualified `Exact` from approximate inputs. E2E script (runs once `w5-executor`/`w6-freshness` land — an epic-w5 closure prerequisite, since the realizing beads depend on this one): same query under `Exact`, `AllowApproximate`, and freshness-bounded requirements, logging realized contract, fallback decisions, and lag.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: approximation as a certificate footnote; wall-clock freshness bounds (would force time-authority observations onto the hot read path); contracts strongly referencing their generation (identity cycles); "best effort" transfer rules (partial rules make operators silently unavailable-as-exact). Risk: registered sound calculi for approximate-input operators are research-adjacent — the fallback/reject arms keep the system honest when no calculus exists.

## Provenance
Plan §8.3 (690–692), G0 decision batch (line 1313), Appendix F FG-EVID-04/FG-CAL-03.

title: Build fgdb-bind: PreparedQueryTemplate, BoundQuery, and CanonicalStatementClassification
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-bind`: name/scope and correlated-reference resolution, deterministic role assignment, group variables, parameter inference/coercion, null and duplicate semantics, graph/table shape checking, path legality/termination, capability-domain injection, and incrementalizability classification; the `PreparedQueryTemplate`/`BoundQuery` pipeline; PREPARE as an authorized idempotent child operation; and the immutable `CanonicalStatementClassification` including bind-time `SnapshotQuery` and fused-autocommit class selection.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3/B6: preparation must never freeze an execution option it never received, `@now` must never be mistaken for a permanent head, and clients (agents) declare ceilings and expectations — never the semantic class. Server-derived classification is what makes admission, authorization, witnesses, and retry semantics trustworthy: a write-capable semantic no-op stays write-classified because those semantics cannot be inferred from the final zero effect. Bind-time class selection is also what makes the `SnapshotQuery` fast read class (§17: ≥8M lookups/s, p99 < 15µs warm) honest rather than a client-claimed bypass.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-bind` first constructs `PreparedQueryTemplate { language_contract_oid, catalog_contract, graph_reference_specs[{binding_role_id, graph_id, branch_selector, system_selector_spec, valid_selector_spec, required_schema_contract}], parameter_types, non_widenable_authority_ceiling, typed_logical_template, output_schema_contract }`. At each execution the caller supplies an `AnswerRequirement` (default `Exact`); any query-language approximation clause narrows it and an empty intersection is rejected. After parameters and both temporal selectors are known, snapshot acquisition resolves every spec into a concrete `GraphReferenceBinding`; binding then produces `BoundQuery<Role> {prepared_template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>, logical_state_root_identity:WeakStateIdentity, graph_reference_bindings[], normalized_valid_time_bindings[], topology_epoch, authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>, authority_binding_body_digest, purpose_class, answer_requirement, instantiated_logical_plan, output_schema}`. Prepared handles pin the template and may be reused only while its catalog/schema compatibility predicates hold under same-or-narrower authority. Physical/logical plan-cache entries, certificates, and replay pin the concrete `BoundQuery`; their key includes the binding body digest, purpose, role, and service epoch — and per §4.2 the per-coordinate schema binding is part of snapshot identity and of every plan-cache key, so prepared plans invalidate precisely rather than consulting one ambient epoch. A cross-authority, cross-graph, historical, or valid-time self-join plan cannot substitute one reference's authority/head/schema/period for another. Optimizers consume only this bound typed IR.

Preparation is itself an authorized, idempotent child operation because even parameter/output schemas can reveal protected catalog facts; the complete PREPARE protocol — `SessionAuthorityBinding`, `PrepareRequestRecord`, `PreparedStatementRecord`, the scoped idempotency index, the `PublicFrameSendGuard::PreparedMetadata` revalidation, EXECUTE handle/state-token resolution, and session-drain fencing — is specified and implemented in the split-out subtask `w5-prepare-protocol`; this bead supplies the template and classification objects that protocol freezes.

Classification: `TxnOperationCeiling = ReadOnlyOnly | ReadWriteAllowed` (client-declared). `CanonicalMutationPotential = ProvenReadOnly | MayMutateGraph | MayMutateSchema | MayInvokeReplicatedProcedure`; `CanonicalOutputClass = NoRows | Rows`; derived `CanonicalStatementClass` is `ReadOnly{output}` only for ProvenReadOnly, `WriteReturning` for any mutation potential + Rows, `WriteNoResult` for any mutation potential + NoRows. `CanonicalStatementClassification` is the immutable binder object `{classification_version, prepared_template_ref, bound_query_ref, prepared_template_digest, canonical_bound_query_digest, parameter_digest, language_contract_oid, binder_and_normalizer_semantics_oid, exact_graph_reference_bindings, exact_write_coordinate_set, sorted_procedure_udf_module_effect_contract_refs[StrongRef<ExecutableEffectContract>], mutation_potential, output_class, derived_statement_class, required_txn_operation_ceiling, required_warden_operation_classes, determinism_and_external_effect_profile, classification_digest:BodyDigest<CanonicalStatementClassification>}`, constructed after parameters, graph roles, schemas, modules/procedures, and temporal selectors resolve and before statement registration. Every executable artifact has one immutable bounded effect contract; parameters cannot choose an undeclared class. The generated statement-kind matrix maps every bound-IR tag and effect-contract arm to exactly one mutation/output row; unknown tags, wildcard fallback, or an unclassified procedure fail binding. Attempt registration stores only the client ceiling; statement registrations, intent batches, audit bases, authorization decisions, owner/result selection, workspace generations, and idempotent request digests all name the same classification. Workspace generation zero starts `cumulative_mutation_potential=ProvenReadOnly`; publication takes the monotone join — a mutation-capable statement can never be reclassified away. A class exceeding the attempt ceiling rejects before storage observation. Read-close is legal only from cumulative ProvenReadOnly. Rebase regenerates effects/results but cannot reinterpret the stored classification; exact retry returns the stored classification across ambient schema/policy/module drift, while a newly bound different class conflicts under the old idempotency key.

`SnapshotQuery` eligibility is bind-time and policy-driven, never a client verb: a statement is eligible exactly when its classification proves ProvenReadOnly single-statement autocommit within the class's declared output/row/time bounds, the effective `AuditCompletenessProfile` does not name the operation class Required, the classification carries no DP or Warden-classified operation class (`required_warden_operation_classes` empty, ordinary `output_class`), and the namespace's registered class policy permits the class — a governed namespace may force every read onto the durable path. Under a Required-read profile eligibility fails closed with a typed, data-independent rejection steering to the durable class; silent upgrade is forbidden. Symmetrically, single-statement autocommit writes whose classification proves fused-arm eligibility select `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec` (owned by `w2-fused-autocommit`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation — PREPARE is itself authorized; `SnapshotQuery` admission performs coordinator-local verification of the complete capability and policy binding before any statement or storage observation, with the same oracle coverage as durable read classes. FG-INV-01: scoped idempotency — matching retries return recorded lineage, conflicting transitions fail. FG-INV-04: plan/snapshot identity includes per-coordinate schema binding. Classification correctness artifacts are invariant-class; eligibility-policy tables are configuration-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-parsers` ASTs and `g0-language-contracts` OIDs; `g0-command-contracts` supplies registry rows for prepare/execute commands; `w2-snapshots-leases` supplies snapshot acquisition; `w4-secure-view` supplies authority bindings; `w5-prepare-protocol` implements the PREPARE lifecycle over this bead's objects. Produces the classification consumed by `w2-txn-lifecycle`, `w2-fused-autocommit`, `w10-snapshotquery` (the `LocalSnapshotQuery` admission arm binds `classification_ref`), `w5-intent-log`, `w5-planner`, and `w9-enforcement`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generated malicious-underclassification tests covering every GQL/openCypher tag, subquery, DDL, mutating CALL/UDF/module, output/no-output form, dynamic graph role, adapter, and PREPARE-versus-EXECUTE_TEXT path. Ceiling-exceed rejects before storage observation (verified by observation-order instrumentation). SnapshotQuery eligibility negatives: DP class, nonempty `required_warden_operation_classes`, Required audit profile, forbidding namespace policy — each returns the typed data-independent rejection. Plan-cache key tests: schema-epoch change on one bound coordinate invalidates exactly the affected entries. E2E: prepare/execute/retry script logging classification digest, ceiling, and selected class per statement.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: client-declared statement class (unauditable); inferring class from realized effects (retry/admission semantics need the a-priori class); a session-level authority ref instead of the explicit `SessionAuthorityBinding` union. Risk: the statement-kind matrix must stay total as the grammar grows — enforced by fail-on-unknown-tag and generated coverage.

## Provenance
Plan §8.1 (664–672), §13 item 3 (SnapshotQuery eligibility, line 1025), §5.2 fused-arm eligibility (line 403), §4.2 (205), Appendix A `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` (line 2619).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement branch-aware base+delta StatsSegments with security-inheriting fallback
description:
## What & scope
Implement the optimizer's statistics plane with per-branch coverage: versioned `StatsSegment`s, the base+delta branch model pinned at fork boundaries, lazily instantiated per-branch delta maintainers riding Ripple, the explicit ordered staleness/fallback lattice, and fail-closed security composition.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: 10k live branches must be cheap — a fork that copied statistics (or eagerly spawned maintainers) would make branch creation O(statistics) and idle branches expensive; instead a fork costs nothing until the planner first asks. B4: the delta layer is Ripple's own machinery — §9.6's degree/label statistics maintainers are exactly how StatsSegments stay fresh. B5: every rung of the lattice is recorded evidence; statistics degrade plan quality, never correctness.

## Design — normative detail
Statistics are versioned `StatsSegment`s with a branch/schema/policy watermark: label/type counts, authorized degree histograms, property sketches, zone maps, and sampled path correlations. Plans may use only statistics whose security domain cannot reveal hidden population information; otherwise they use capability-specific projections or conservative public bounds. Shrinkage, unseen-mass floors, robust estimators, influence caps, and targeted synopsis refresh are candidate estimators evaluated on named workloads; their risk properties are conditional on their model/population and never promoted into semantic invariants.

Per-branch coverage is base+delta: a fork does not copy statistics but pins a shared ancestor-base segment at the branch manifest's `fork_boundary_logical_command_seq`, and branch-delta segments are derived from exactly the branch's post-fork divergence. The delta layer rides Ripple's existing Z-set consumption (§9.6), and per-branch delta maintainers are instantiated lazily on first planner demand, never eagerly at fork. The staleness/fallback lattice is explicit and ordered: (1) exact per-branch segment, (2) base+delta composition, (3) the ancestor watermark with a typed staleness annotation, (4) the conservative public bounds — and a plan records which rung it consumed. Security composition fails closed: a branch-delta segment inherits the most restrictive security domain of any contributing segment or degrades to the public bounds, because a branch-delta correction must never reveal a hidden population that the base segment lawfully concealed. Statistics remain non-semantic on every rung — ancestor fallback degrades plan quality, never correctness — and per-branch segment/maintainer cost is a declared parameter of §5.6's 10k-branch gate.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated): authorization precedes observation across statistics — a hidden population lawfully concealed by the base segment stays concealed through every delta composition. Estimator risk properties are FG-CAL-02-adjacent evidence (population/window/strata/coverage disclosures), never invariants. Maintainer staleness is a §9.6 staleness contract surfaced in certificates (slo-class per FG-EVID-04 discipline); the 10k-branch churn cost is a benchmark-class gate parameter and feeds the FG-CFG-04 maintenance-stream capacity model.

## Interactions
`w5-planner` consumes segments and records the rung; `w2-branch-fork` supplies the branch manifest and `fork_boundary_logical_command_seq`; `w6-delta-consumption` supplies the Z-set delta stream the maintainers consume; `w6-maintainers` hosts the degree/label maintainer family; `w1-sketch-calibrate` supplies sketch/estimator machinery; `perf-bench-scale` runs the 10k-branch churn gate; `w9-enforcement` defines the security domains statistics inherit.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Fork-cost test: creating a branch performs zero statistics copying and spawns zero maintainers (instrumented allocation/task counters); first planner demand instantiates the delta maintainer exactly once (idempotent under concurrent demand). Lattice tests: with the delta maintainer lagging, plans consume rung 3 with the typed staleness annotation; with it absent, rung 4; rung consumed is present in the plan record/decision card. Security negatives: construct a base segment concealing a population from capability C; verify that no branch-delta composition observable under C reveals counts/histograms distinguishable from the public-bounds answer (statistical-distance check in the test harness, logged). Correctness differential: identical query results across all four rungs (only plans differ). Bench: 10k-branch churn gate with per-branch maintainer memory/CPU cost reported as the declared gate parameter; maintainer freshness (watermark lag) distribution logged. E2E script: fork a branch, run the same planner-costed query on parent and child before divergence, apply post-fork commits, then re-plan with the delta maintainer (a) absent, (b) lagging, (c) caught up, asserting identical query results throughout; the script logs per plan the branch, rung consumed, staleness annotation, security domain of every consumed segment, and maintainer instantiation/watermark events — the implementation must emit these as structured events so rung selection is auditable after the fact.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: copy-on-fork statistics (O(branches) space, stale immediately); eager per-fork maintainers (10k idle branches saturate the maintenance stream — exactly what FG-CFG-04 prices); allowing a "more accurate" delta correction to bypass the base segment's security domain (fails closed instead). Risk: lattice rung flapping under churn — mitigated by recording the rung per plan so quality regressions are attributable.

## Provenance
Plan §8.5 statistics bullet (702), §9.6 (806–810), §5.6 10k-branch gate, FG-CFG-04.

title: Enforce CGSE determinism: semantic/scalar profiles, tie-breaks, canonical result encoding
description:
## What & scope
Implement the query-level determinism contracts (CGSE): versioned `SemanticProfile`s, `CanonicalScalarProfile` with `STRICT_PORTABLE`, numeric execution profiles, tie-break policies, and the §8.8 canonical result encoding (`CanonicalResultChunk`/`CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor`). The strict contract: within the pinned evidence closure, the same query produces a byte-identical canonical result encoding — across parallelism, spill, factorization, safe replanning, and supported hardware.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: determinism is the substrate for replay (FG-INV-19), differential testing, caching, and agent trust — an agent comparing two runs must see identical bytes or a named contract difference, never scheduler noise. B6: canonical result digests are what certificates, subscriptions, and idempotent retries compare. Where GQL leaves latitude (result ordering, path enumeration order, duplicate semantics under morphism modes), FrankenGraphDB pins behavior and documents each pin.

## Design — normative detail
Each pin set is a versioned `SemanticProfile` referenced from `LanguageContract` — never an ambiguous bare name like `gql-2024-strict` — fixing null/UNKNOWN handling, duplicate semantics per morphism mode, ordering defaults, coercion rules, and tie-break bindings. Two results are comparable only under the same language+semantic+scalar contracts; corrigendum/dialect drift becomes a new content-addressed artifact. Temporal clauses get algebraic semantics: snapshot-relativized pattern matching; `BETWEEN` yields per-binding validity intervals with interval-algebra predicates.

`CanonicalScalarProfile` defines equality, hashing, total ordering, collation, coercion, and durable/result encoding for every value, with property tests enforcing equal implies same_hash, comparator totality/transitivity, and encode/decode/order coherence. `STRICT_PORTABLE` canonicalizes NaNs and signed zero; fixes decimal scale/rounding/overflow; stores timestamp instant, zone/offset semantics, and a content-addressed tzdb version; pins Unicode data/normalization/segmentation and each non-binary collation by ObjectId; fixes map-key order over canonical bytes; and rejects unavailable profile artifacts rather than consulting host locale/tzdb. Floating execution uses fixed logical reduction trees independent of SIMD width, fixes denormal/rounding behavior, forbids target-dependent contraction, and uses pinned math kernels. A scalar/SIMD fast path ships in strict mode only after bit-identity testing on every supported target; otherwise it is RELAXED and the certificate names target/build behavior.

Tie-breaks: every query declares a tie-break policy; the strict default is storage-independent `LexMin` over canonical scalar/element encodings. `ORDER BY` wins. `InsertionOrder` is defined as immutable element-origin order and is available only when elements carry durable `OriginBirthOrder {commit_seq, intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id}`; `BranchAdmissionOrder` is a separately named policy. Compaction/run order never defines either. `fnx-parity` is an explicit projection profile with its own adjacency-order metadata. Parallelism, spilling, factorization, and safe replanning must preserve the canonical logical row sequence or require RELAXED posture.

Result delivery (§8.8): streaming begins only at an operator's declared safe emission point. Two-phase channel obligations provide bounded backpressure; output-row/byte, egress, idle-time, and snapshot-age reservations prevent a slow client from holding unbounded resources. The canonical result digest covers schema, canonical values, multiplicity, and logical order before framing. Factorized frames encode a canonical logical factorization DAG — not Strata run references — and clients may request flat frames without changing result identity. `CanonicalResultChunk` is the exact logical plaintext target `{format_version=1, canonical_encoding_version, chunk_ordinal, canonical_offset, canonical_len, frame_boundary_policy_oid, canonical_bytes:BoundedBytes<1_MiB>, body_digest}`: `canonical_len` equals the byte length, chunks are contiguous from offset zero, and every boundary lies between complete canonical value/row/factorization frames; an individual value above the v1 value bound is rejected before materialization rather than split ambiguously. `CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor` is the only outer owner of ciphertext identity and public chunk digest; its ordinal/offset/length/encoding fields must byte-match the decrypted target. The target has one `logical_object_kinds.toml` row, a registered BodyDigest transcript, exact 1 MiB plaintext and decoder-allocation bounds, golden vectors for flat/factorized/null/graph/scalar/extreme-value cases, mutation and truncation corpora, and a generated fuzz target. Decrypted protected-result buffers use the ordinary authority/send guard and are wiped on cancel, error, or final frame ownership transfer; no plaintext chunk, keyed ObjectId, or placement detail enters logs or crashpacks.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated): canonical scalar equality, hashing, and encoding are coherent; every answer-equivalent variant preserves values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, `AnswerContract`.
