top-k custom, full sort normally recompute; no switch after emitted prefix, order/tie and early-stop gap witnesses; exact ordered prefix requires exact gap/completeness proof, approximate top-k carries recall/error and population. `SetOp{Union,Intersect,Except}` — partition-spillable multiplicity state; registered per ALL/DISTINCT form; materialization boundary, negative/right-side domains where applicable; all-exact inputs yield `Exact`, approximate difference/intersection requires a sound registered law. `Fixpoint` — LSM-backed arrangements and iteration spill; validated SCC only; iteration barrier, termination and recursive-domain witness; `Exact` requires exact seed/relations and convergence, approximate recursion unavailable unless separately registered. `TemporalSlice/TemporalJoin` — interval-partition spill; registered interval algebra; interval boundary, system/valid-time ranges and gaps; `Exact` only with complete temporal coverage, else qualified interval approximation. `SemiringMxV` — sparse/dense frontier spill; registered annotation algebra; iteration/frontier barrier, projection/capability/path semantics pinned; exact algebra+inputs yield `Exact`, numeric/coverage approximation requires its registered bound. `ProcedureCall` — declared per procedure, otherwise reject; none unless explicitly registered; none by default, authorized view only, external-nondeterminism badge as required; signature independently declares answer-contract transfer and replay-input capture — external/nondeterministic execution may be semantically exact yet downgrade replay completeness, while an approximate procedure remains approximate even if perfectly replayable. `GraphConstruct` — spillable canonical key/value and path/provenance runs, generation-local dense ordinals allowed; registered pure construction derivative with deletion/multiplicity law; batch/materialization boundary, complete source/provenance witnesses and canonical `ViewElementRef` identity; pure deterministic construction preserves/propagates its inputs and has no proposal or commit side effect. `Mutate` — proposal-local buffered intents/effects; emits canonical logical delta only after successful commit; never replanned after side-effect ordering, complete read/write/constraint/authorization witness; consumes `Exact` only — approximate data cannot authorize a mutation target/effect. `ViewDelta/CertEmit` — bounded envelope plus spillable forensic detail; stream tap; no semantic replan, watermark/evidence closure must remain exact; preserves and serializes the full contract without upgrading it. The `Diff` row is owned by `w5-diff-operator`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12/FG-INV-06/FG-INV-15 as bound in `w5-gla-algebra`; each row's tests are oracle-class conformance artifacts gating dispatch.

## Interactions
Fills `w5-gla-algebra`'s registry; `w5-executor` implements the memory/spill columns; `w6-zset-circuits` the incremental column; `w7-*`/`w8-kernels` the IndexProbe/HybridSearch/SemiringMxV physicals; `w5-planner` reads ReplanClass columns.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Per-family conformance suites exercising all four columns: spill/no-spill canonical identity, cancellation-budget conformance, witness-domain differential against `w4-ssi-witnesses` oracles, and answer-contract transfer tests (approximate input yields qualified output or rejection — never silent exactness). Derivative-vs-batch differential for every row declaring an incremental contract. CI matrix proving every dispatched family has a passing suite. E2E script: a mixed workload (scan→join→aggregate→order-by→limit plus an index-probe/hybrid plan) runs against a live embedded instance twice with spill forced on the second run, asserting identical canonical result digests; the run logs per dispatched operator its family, registry-row version, spill decisions, cancellation checkpoints hit, witness-domain summary, and realized answer-contract transfer. Detailed logging: every conformance suite and the dispatch gate must emit structured events (row registered/rejected with the missing column named, dispatch grant/denial, digest comparisons) so registry coverage is verifiable from logs after implementation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: default/inherited rows; treating recompute-capable operators as incrementally maintained ("for free" is not an operator law). Risk: row drift versus implementations — the dispatch gate makes drift fail closed.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix C (2737–2761).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement GQL/openCypher recursive-descent+Pratt parsers, FQL dialect, and Datalog surface
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-gql` and `fgdb-cypher` (syntax-only crates), the FQL dialect productions, and the `fgdb-datalog` grammar front-end as hand-written recursive-descent + Pratt parsers (the frankensqlite parser school; §18.2 explicitly builds parsers in-house — parser generators are outside the closed universe). Output is ASTs only: parsing never produces executable plans. Includes structure-aware grammar fuzzing and the syntax reservation for `DIFF`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3/B6: the standard exists (GQL ISO/IEC 39075:2024) and agents need a stable, versioned, honestly-claimed surface; §3.2's verdict is to adopt GQL with a content-addressed language contract and openCypher compatibility, publishing exact ISO feature IDs, prerequisites, and gaps from the start — current products expose "GQL-compatible" surfaces but must not be called conforming beyond their claimed/passed class. openCypher is the pragmatic market on-ramp (Neo4j-trained users and tooling).

## Design — normative detail
Native GQL surface: graph pattern matching including quantified path patterns, path modes (`WALK`/`TRAIL`/`ACYCLIC`/`SIMPLE`), the edition's registered shortest/count selectors, label expressions, `LET`/`FILTER`/`FOR`, composite queries, catalog/DDL, transactions/sessions. The exact minimum closure and optional ISO feature IDs are frozen in `LanguageContract`; an in-flight edition/corrigendum is a *different* contract and never lands silently. openCypher: separate lexer/parser/profile adapters that converge with GQL only after binding and semantic normalization; documented divergences plus the openCypher TCK prevent a parser shortcut from changing meaning. FQL: temporal, branch, Prism, retrieval, materialized-view, subscription, certificate, branch-admin, and `CHEAPEST`/cost-selector syntax beyond the pinned 2024 ISO feature map is enabled only by an explicit `FQL <major.minor>` declaration or `FQL`-prefixed production — unprefixed future-standard-looking keywords are never called "namespaced". `DIFF <graph_ref_a> … <graph_ref_b>` — each endpoint an ordinary graph reference carrying the full `graph@branch AS OF <time|seq>` selector surface — is registered under this dialect discipline as reserved 1.0 syntax producing canonical delta tables; its semantics are owned entirely by Appendix C's `Diff` row and the syntax is available only after that row's conformance tests exist. Datalog: `fgdb-datalog` accepts the validated finite/stratified subset of §9.3, compiled to the same typed algebra; recursion, negation, and aggregates are accepted only when their termination and incrementalization contracts are registered.

`LanguageContract` is a canonically encoded, content-addressed tagged union with common `{grammar_oid, lexer_profile_oid, normalizer_oid, semantic_profile_oid, scalar_profile_oid, unicode_conformance_bundle_ref}` and one surface payload. `UnicodeConformanceBundle` is `{unicode_version, unicode_data_oid, uts10_collation_version, uts10_data_oid, uax15_normalization_version, uax15_data_oid, uax31_identifier_version, uax31_data_oid, synchronous_release_set_id, ucs_basic_profile}`; its validator requires Unicode >= 13.0.0 and proves the UTS #10 / UAX #15 / UAX #31 versions/data are the synchronous set for that Unicode release. `Gql` carries `{edition, corrected_printing, corrigenda[], conformance_profile, mandatory_feature_closure[], graph_type_conformance, selected_minimum_feature_ids[], optional_feature_ids[]}`; `graph_type_conformance` is exactly `Open{feature:GG01}` or `Closed{feature:GG02, element_type_feature:GG20|GG21|GG22|GG23}`. `OpenCypher` carries the exact language/specification revision, grammar and TCK commit, supported scenario manifest, and documented-divergence ObjectId; `Fql` carries declared major/minor grammar, extension-feature closure, and GQL-base contract; `Datalog` carries the accepted finite/stratified grammar subset plus recursion/negation/aggregate/operator-registry ObjectIds. The GQL 2024 contract includes the ISO minimum-conformance closure and every prerequisite of its selected feature IDs, supplies required character-string/Boolean/signed-integer/floating property types, and pins the validated Unicode bundle plus mandated UCS_BASIC behavior. Draft Edition 2 syntax exists only under a visibly draft contract and cannot satisfy the 2024 claim. No loose dialect string or server default can change accepted syntax or semantics after binding.

## Invariants & claim types
Feeds FG-INV-12's comparability clause: two results are comparable only under the same language+semantic+scalar contracts, and corrigendum/dialect drift becomes a new content-addressed artifact. Contracts obey FG-INV-09 identity discipline (`ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed canonical transcript). Conformance claims are published feature matrices — evidence-class artifacts, never invariants.

## Interactions
`g0-language-contracts` freezes the contract instances this bead parses against. `w5-binder` consumes ASTs plus the `language_contract_oid`. `w5-diff-operator` owns `DIFF` semantics and gates its availability. `w5-determinism` supplies the `SemanticProfile`/scalar profile referenced from the contract. `verif-differential` runs the TCK/ISO matrix and Neo4j/Memgraph corpus.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Golden AST corpus per surface with parse→pretty-print→parse fixpoint property tests. ISO minimum-closure checklist published with exact feature IDs/prerequisites/gaps. openCypher TCK scenario manifest recorded in the `OpenCypher` arm; CI executes the syntax-level slice — every TCK scenario query in the supported manifest must parse to a golden AST (or resolve to a documented-divergence entry) — while behavioral TCK execution (queries against expected results, which needs binder/executor) is owned by verif-differential's TCK harness (which depends on this bead) — validated from gate-g3, with the full contract-corpus pass a gate-g4 requirement; this bead's CI job never claims scenario-level conformance. Structure-aware grammar fuzzing: no panics, no hangs, bounded memory. Negative suites: unprefixed FQL keywords rejected under a pure GQL contract; draft-E2 syntax rejected under the 2024 contract; `DIFF` returns a typed reserved-syntax error until the Appendix C row's conformance tests exist; Unicode bundle validator rejects non-synchronous UTS/UAX sets and versions < 13.0.0. Every rejection is a typed diagnostic with source span, logged with contract OID. E2E script: the full golden corpus (GQL, openCypher, FQL-prefixed, Datalog) is driven end-to-end through the embedded front-end — source text in, typed AST or typed diagnostic out — under each frozen `LanguageContract`, then re-run under a swapped contract to prove acceptance changes only via a different contract OID, never a server default; the harness logs per statement the contract OID, surface, accept/reject outcome, diagnostic code, and source span, and the fuzzing campaign logs seed, input digest, and outcome class for every execution so crashes replay deterministically.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: parser generators (closed universe, diagnostic quality); one shared grammar for GQL+Cypher (their convergence point is post-binding, not the grammar); silent dialect defaults. Risk: quantified path patterns and the full minimum-conformance closure are hard — mitigated by freezing the claimed closure in the contract and publishing gaps rather than over-claiming.

## Provenance
Plan §8.1 (653–662), §3.2 row 6, §18.2.
design:
## External-review boundary (2026-07-22)

FG-ADR-SOTA-QUERY-GQL-STANDARDS remains review_due. The openCypher snapshot 677cbafa is pinned, but public metadata and the openCypher corpus do not substantiate exact ISO/IEC 39075 feature IDs. Licensed standard bytes were unavailable to this review. Do not mark exact ISO feature coverage live until the content-addressed licensed language bundle and feature matrix are independently verified.

title: Build the optimizer: DP enumeration, calibrated cost evidence, safe replanning
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-planner`: DP plan enumeration producing hybrid binary/FreeJoin plans, physical costing over Strata realities, conformal cost intervals as calibrated evidence, adaptive replanning at registered safe points only, orbit-canonical logical plan identity with distinct physical identities, and materialized-view rewrite targets. Branch-aware statistics live in `w5-branch-stats`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3: one cost model across relational and pattern operators (§3.2 SPJM verdict). B5 is the defining discipline here: cost estimates are assumption-bearing evidence, never semantic invariants — plan choice may be wrong without the answer ever being wrong; adaptivity is deterministic and replayable, never a wall-clock race. WCOJ theory (EmptyHeaded/ADOPT/HoneyComb) is adopted through declared trie cursor orders, and AGM bounds are guardrails rather than fake point estimates.

## Design — normative detail
Enumeration and access orders: DP over connected subpatterns produces hybrid binary/FreeJoin plans. Every atom advertises available trie attribute orders and cursor complexity; forward/reverse Strata runs satisfy only their declared endpoint orders, while unavailable key/property orders require COLT construction or a Beacon view. Tier-D merge, tombstones, generation count, buffer I/O, and preprocessing enter physical cost. AGM/fractional-cover bounds are worst-case guardrails recorded separately; they are not compared numerically as if they were expected binary-plan costs. Plans may use only statistics whose security domain cannot reveal hidden population information; otherwise they use capability-specific projections or conservative public bounds (FG-INV-20 applies to statistics observation).

Cost intervals are assumption-bearing evidence: split/Mondrian conformal intervals may report finite-sample marginal coverage within a frozen stratum only under the named exchangeability or online-validity conditions. Continuously selected, refreshed workload data does not inherit that guarantee automatically. Calibration artifacts record population, window, stratum construction, selection policy, alpha, and nonexchangeability penalty. Drift monitors can trigger fallback/recalibration; they do not retroactively preserve coverage. Plan choice uses intervals and tail-risk penalties as performance evidence (FG-CAL-02) while correctness remains independent of estimator quality.

Adaptivity uses registered safe points: every operator declares `ReplanClass = None | BeforeOutput | PartitionBoundary | StateTransfer`. A `ReplanCheckpoint` commits input frontier, emitted-output frontier, optional state object, and logical-order floor. Global joins, distinct, aggregates, sort, fixpoints, and paths may switch only at proved materialization/iteration barriers or through verified state transfer; a generic morsel boundary is insufficient. Strict hedges buffer output until a complete winner is selected by deterministic policy, or both candidates independently produce the same canonical stream — wall-clock race order never chooses logical output. Triggers and latency envelopes are assumption-bearing decision evidence, not correctness certificates; adaptive promotions require FG-CAL-01's evidence rule (null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only) and decision cards satisfy FG-EVID-01 (state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch, fallback).

Plan identity: law-certified normalization assigns `LogicalOrbitId` modulo valid logical commutativity/associativity symmetries, allowing semantic proofs and logical cache entries to transfer. Every concrete access order, algorithm, materialization, index generation, and safe-replan policy has a distinct `PhysicalPlanId`, cost evidence, performance baseline, and replay record. A physical member never inherits another member's measurements merely because their outputs are equivalent. Views: Ripple-maintained materialized views register as rewrite targets (view matching over the algebra). Every rewrite must preserve authorization boundaries, witness domains, factorization/path laws, and `AnswerContract` typing — a rewrite that would upgrade an approximate stream or widen a visibility domain is illegal.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: safe replan variants preserve logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and `AnswerContract`. FG-INV-20: statistics/routing/scoring observation is authorized. FG-CAL-01 (adaptive policy evidence vs pinned fallback) and FG-CAL-02 (cardinality/risk interval coverage: population, selection/window, exchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage, drift) are evidence-class; FG-EVID-01 (decision-card/OPE completeness) is evidence-class. Plan-quality numbers are benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-gla-algebra` rows (ReplanClass, witness, factorization columns), `w5-answer-contracts` typing, `w5-factorization` COLT costing, `w3-tier-r` declared run orders and generation metadata, `w1-sketch-calibrate` conformal/e-process machinery, `w5-branch-stats` segments. Produces bound physical plans for `w5-executor`; `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId` pinned by `w5-replay`; view rewrite targets registered by `w6-views`; decision cards consumed by `verif-sextant` and `obs-observatory`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Metamorphic: all legal replan variants of a plan produce identical canonical result digests (rides gla-algebra suite); forced replans at every declared safe point under fault injection. Hedge determinism: schedule-permuted (DPOR-style) runs where the losing candidate finishes first never change logical output. Orbit tests: law-certified rewrites map to the same `LogicalOrbitId`; non-symmetric variations do not. Measurement hygiene: a fresh `PhysicalPlanId` starts with no inherited baseline (registry check). Calibration harness: FG-CAL-02 report with realized marginal coverage per stratum, drift alarms, and conservative-costing fallback on failure — failure reverts costing, never blocks correctness. Statistics-security negatives: a plan over a capability-restricted domain consults only projections/public bounds (observation-order instrumentation). Bench gates: LDBC SNB Interactive SF-100 compliance run, triangle-count WCOJ gate, Graphalytics within 1.5x of dedicated engines on transactional storage — each with pinned manifest, committed baseline, variance budget, flamegraph on regression; the gate rows, manifests, and baselines are registered here, while the runs execute on §15.6's deterministic apparatus via `verif-perf-apparatus`/`perf-bench-core` (which depend on this bead) — manifests-green at gate-g4. E2E script: a seeded workload runs with adaptive replanning enabled; injected statistics drift forces a replan at a registered safe point plus one hedge where the losing candidate finishes first, asserting canonical result digests unchanged throughout; the run logs per query the `LogicalOrbitId`, `PhysicalPlanId`, statistics rung consumed, cost interval with calibration-artifact identity, every `ReplanCheckpoint` taken, the deterministic hedge-winner selection basis, and the FG-EVID-01 decision card. Detailed logging: every plan choice logs its enumerated candidate set with interval evidence and every replan/hedge decision logs its deterministic policy inputs, so any nondeterministic selection is detectable from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: promoting conformal coverage into a semantic invariant (it is conditional evidence); racing plans and taking the first finisher (nondeterministic output); comparing AGM bounds numerically against expected costs; one plan-id namespace (destroys measurement hygiene and replay precision). Risk: interval miscalibration under workload drift — bounded by design since correctness never depends on the estimator.

## Provenance
Plan §8.5 (700–707), §3.2 (WCOJ/Free Join rows), Appendix F FG-CAL-01/02, FG-EVID-01.

title: Implement the PREPARE protocol: authorized idempotent child operation, frozen responses
description:
## What & scope
Split from `w5-binder`: implement PREPARE as an authorized, idempotent child operation — the session authority binding, request/record objects, the scoped idempotency index, the pre-send revalidation guard, EXECUTE resolution, and session-drain fencing.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents retry aggressively and hold prepared statements across drift; even parameter/output schemas can reveal protected catalog facts, so preparation itself must be authorized (FG-INV-20) and its retry semantics exact. A frozen response digest means a retried PREPARE can never leak newer catalog state under an old key.

## Design — normative detail
`SessionAuthorityBinding` is the Ready-bound closed union `Local{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>, presentation_binding:SessionBound{session_binding, auth_generation}} | Meta{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>, presentation_binding:SessionBound{session_binding, auth_generation}}`; the role must match the selected database posture and Ready generation. `PrepareRequestRecord` is the session-scoped immutable `{ready_binding, session_binding, prepare_request_idempotency_key, canonical_prepare_request_digest, language_contract_oid, requested_parameter_contract?, session_authority_binding:SessionAuthorityBinding, catalog_contract_basis, resource_reservation_ref}` — it has no fictitious `AuthorityBindingRef<Session>` and no duplicate raw `SecurityStateBinding`. `PreparedStatementRecord` is `{request_ref:StrongRef<PrepareRequestRecord>, template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>, public_statement_handle:PublicHandle<PreparedStatement>, public_state_token:PublicStateToken<PreparedStatement>, authorized_public_parameter_schema, authorized_public_output_contract_commitment, compatibility_contracts, prepare_authorization_projection, response_commitment}`. The scoped idempotency index maps one key to exactly one request/record; byte-identical retry reproduces the same PREPARED bytes, while text, language, requested contract, Ready, or authority drift conflicts *before* protected catalog observation. Before PREPARED is sent, a `PublicFrameSendGuard::PreparedMetadata` arm revalidates the complete current binding, the record's non-widenable ceiling, catalog compatibility, and the exact frozen response digest. EXECUTE must present both public handle and state token, resolve them through the session index, reauthorize same-or-narrower, and then construct the concrete `BoundQuery`; prepared metadata never grants execution authority. Session drain fences unsent PREPARED, retires unescaped records after their send obligations join, and never turns socket success into durable semantic state.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: PREPARE authorization precedes catalog observation; drift conflicts fire before any protected observation. FG-INV-01-family idempotency: one key, one record, byte-identical retry. FG-INV-16: send obligations join before record retirement; drain loses nothing. All invariant-class.

## Interactions
Freezes `w5-binder`'s `PreparedQueryTemplate`; `g0-command-contracts` registers the prepare command rows; `w4-secure-view` supplies the authority machinery; `w10-fgp-core` carries the PREPARED/EXECUTE frames and the `PreparedMetadata` guard arm; `w2-txn-lifecycle` consumes EXECUTE-produced bound queries.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Byte-identity: retried PREPARE under the same key returns bit-identical PREPARED bytes across concurrent catalog/schema/policy drift. Drift-conflict tests for each axis (text, language, requested contract, Ready, authority) with observation-order instrumentation proving the conflict precedes catalog observation. Guard negatives: catalog incompatibility discovered at send time yields conflict, never stale bytes. Handle/token negatives: missing state token, cross-session handle, and widened-authority EXECUTE all fail uniformly. Drain e2e: crash between queue and send leaves no durable semantic state; unsent PREPARED fenced; logs record idempotency key, response digest, and drain disposition.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a session-level authority ref (the explicit union is what makes posture/Ready mismatches unencodable); treating PREPARE as unauthorized metadata (schema shape leaks); cleanup by finalizer/socket close (drain must be explicit and obligation-joined).

## Provenance
Plan §8.1 (666).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement ReplayManifest, evidence slots, and replay grades (FG-INV-19)
description:
## What & scope
Implement the replay artifact and its lifecycle: the `ReplayManifest` with typed evidence slots, the versioned `ReplaySlotSchema` and derived structural-completeness grades, access-time `effective_completeness`, the consensus-rooted `ReplayRegistry` with archive records and leases, and the certificate-mode rules. The replay artifact is a `ReplayManifest`, never `(certificate, seq, seed)`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5/B6: byte-replayable answers are the strongest evidence class the system offers — for debugging, audit, agent self-verification, and differential testing — but an honest replay claim must degrade attributably when evidence, leases, artifacts, or authority disappear. The grade lattice makes "can I replay this?" a derived, checkable property rather than a hope.

## Design — normative detail
`ReplayManifest` pins: database/security namespace/incarnation, logical-command and commit sequences, topology/policy/revocation epochs, the execution `AnswerRequirement`, realized result `AnswerContract`, `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId`, result-encoding version, and canonical result digest. Every evidence slot is an explicit `ReplayEvidenceRef<T> = Present {object: ReplayObjectRef<T>} | Unavailable {class, expected_logical_object_id?, expected_canonical_digest?, reason_code} | Redacted {class, commitment?, redaction_policy_oid}`. A present `ReplayObjectRef` is either a typed local strong edge or an explicitly nonlocal archive identity verified through the active registry — the latter is never a local GC edge. Slots cover: logical state, role-bearing binding set, language/semantic/scalar/numeric profiles, bound and normalized query, typed parameters, replay-authority snapshot, UDF/module set, mediated external inputs/nondeterminism, exact derived generation snapshots, decision cards/policies, evidence, `ExecutableArtifactSet`, and a typed `StructuralReplayProjection`. No archivable edge relies on a bare `_root`, `_ref`, optional field, or digest whose default could silently become local reachability or conceal missing evidence.

Digests alone are not executable input. A versioned `ReplaySlotSchema` derives — not trusts — a manifest's immutable structural completeness from the slot states and the recorded execution's actual semantic dependencies. Grades: `Replayable` requires every semantically required slot Present and must identify the exact engine binary or a complete reproducible-build closure, Rust toolchain and target, CPU-feature contract, runtime/allocator configuration, VM/JIT/compiler artifacts if used, kernel/profile registry, and platform ABI. `StructuralReplay` requires a present typed `StructuralReplayProjection` plus every slot its declared reproduced control/data-shape classes require; every omitted class is explicitly unavailable or redacted. `VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied` requires every missing slot to carry an expected identity/digest sufficient to validate later-supplied bytes. `AuditOnly` permits explicit unavailable/redacted slots and makes no byte-replay claim. An encoded structural grade that disagrees with the generated slot matrix is invalid. At access time, the verifier separately derives `effective_completeness` by combining that maximum with live local/archive availability, lease, trust, resolver, and authorization state; it can only stay equal or become weaker without mutating the manifest. Reading or resolving any item requires explicit `Replay` authority scoped to the complete evidence/artifact closure. Replay compares canonical logical-result encoding before transport framing; fetch size, wire factorization, and frames are irrelevant.

Strict floating results use §8.2's portable profile; RELAXED results are reproducible only within their recorded target/build scope. The registry and lifecycle machinery — `ReplayRegistry` rooting, archive records, lease renewal, degradation on revocation/expiry/resolver failure, the expiry-then-consensus-GC ordering, `KEEP NONE` semantics, certificate modes, and the erasure-downgrade path — is specified and implemented in the split-out subtask `w5-replay-registry`; this bead owns the manifest, slot schema, grade derivation, and access-time verifier.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19 (restated): a registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix, and its effective grade may only weaken as leases, resolution, trust, configuration, or authority change; `Replayable` requires every semantic slot — including answer requirement, realized contract, authority, external inputs, executable artifacts, decisions, workspace-affecting statements, and exact approximate generations — to resolve through exactly LocalStrong, live CertifiedRemote, or active Archived evidence and reproduce canonical logical output; missing, redacted, revoked, expired, or untrusted evidence yields only the declared weaker grade; answer-affecting and canonical-state policies are sequenced/pinned, and proved physical equivalence cannot change strict output. FG-INV-14: manifests/archive records are GC roots until their exact terminal transfer/release. Grades are invariant-class derivations; replay latency/size numbers are benchmark-class.

## Interactions
`w5-determinism` supplies the canonical encoding compared under replay; `w5-answer-contracts` supplies requirement/contract slots (exact approximate generations pinned); `w5-planner` supplies `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId`; `w5-replay-registry` implements the registry/lease/GC lifecycle over these manifests; `w10-fgp-core` exposes replay resolution; `verif-replay-products` builds `SessionReplayBundle` on this foundation; `w11-format-activation`/W12 add certified transition wrappers (sharded replay no stronger than its weakest required group).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Cross-plan/target/artifact/workspace/approximation replay CI: recorded executions replayed across physical-plan variants, targets (strict), and supplied-artifact scenarios reproduce the canonical logical result digest. Generated slot-grade tests: every slot-state combination maps to exactly one structural grade; an encoded grade disagreeing with the matrix is rejected. Access-time verifier tests: each degradation source (lease expiry, revocation, resolver failure, closure-verification failure, authorization loss) yields the declared weaker `effective_completeness` without mutating the manifest, logged with reason codes. Authority tests: resolution without scoped `Replay` authority fails uniformly and nonrevealingly. Framing-irrelevance test: varying fetch size, wire factorization, and frame boundaries never changes the replay comparison. Replica logical-digest oracle wired into `fgdb-sim`. E2E script: record one execution, then replay it across a physical-plan variant, a strict-target replay, and a supplied-artifact scenario; expire one evidence lease mid-sequence and assert the downgraded `effective_completeness` path end-to-end against the same manifest. Detailed logging: every replay logs {manifest id, replay grade, slot states, plan/target/artifact variant ids, canonical logical result digest before/after, degradation reason codes}; grade derivations must be reconstructable from the logged slot states via the generated matrix alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: `(certificate, seq, seed)` replay (unversioned, hides missing evidence); trusting encoded grades (grades are derived from the slot matrix); digests as executable input; archive records holding local ObjectId edges (would silently pin GC). Risk: reproducible-build closure identification is operationally heavy — the grade lattice makes partial closures honest (`VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied`/`StructuralReplay`) rather than fake `Replayable`.

## Provenance
Plan §8.6 (713–717), Appendix F FG-INV-19, §12.6/§4.8 erasure interplay.

### Fidelity addendum — replay reference arms are exact
`ReplayObjectRef<T>` is exactly the closed three-arm union `LocalStrong{ref:StrongRef<T>}|CertifiedRemote{ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>}|Archived{identity:ArchiveObjectIdentity,expected_logical_object_id,expected_canonical_digest}`. No two-arm shorthand, bare digest, optional ref, generic remote locator, or local/remote-erased wrapper is legal. `LocalStrong` participates in local reachability. `CertifiedRemote` requires a live matching authority configuration, trust selector, two-sided retention grant, and consumer-local certified reference. `Archived` is nonlocal, never marks local data, and resolves only through the active `ReplayRegistry` record whose inventory byte-matches the identity, logical ObjectId, and canonical digest.

`ArchiveObjectIdentity` is a registered reference-free wire type scoped by archive authority, archive ID/generation, security domain, resolver profile, and exact inventory key; it contains no Local/Meta ObjectId edge, inode, credential, or consumer-local locator. Every evidence slot remains exactly `ReplayEvidenceRef<T>=Present{object:ReplayObjectRef<T>}|Unavailable{class,expected_logical_object_id?,expected_canonical_digest?,reason_code}|Redacted{class,commitment?,redaction_policy_oid}`. The advertised replay grade is the meet of every required slot and executable-artifact route; loss of remote trust, archive status, resolver availability, or digest equality weakens/refuses the grade rather than silently changing arms.

Golden/field-table tests cover every T/arm/tag; mutation tests substitute Local, certified-remote, and archived references with identical payload digests and require rejection. Reachability tests prove only LocalStrong marks locally; trust/lease tests prove CertifiedRemote is two-sided; Archived resolution tests cover wrong generation, authority, inventory key, ObjectId, digest, revoked/expired record, and resolver failure. Structured logs emit manifest/slot class, selected arm, public identity commitment, trust/grant/archive generation, verification verdict, and resulting grade; they never emit archive credentials, protected locators, or evidence bytes.

title: Implement ReplayRegistry lifecycle: leases, archive records, GC ordering, cert modes
description:
## What & scope
Split from `w5-replay`: the durable side of replay — the consensus-rooted `ReplayRegistry`, archive records, lease renewal and degradation, the expiry-then-GC ordering, `KEEP NONE` semantics, certificate modes, and the erasure-downgrade path.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: a replay claim is only as honest as its retention story. FG-INV-19 guarantees byte replay only while the full required evidence closure and matching executable artifacts remain retained locally or through a verified `ReplayArchiveRecord` under a lease whose expiry and trust domain are visible in the manifest — this bead makes that lifecycle real without letting replay pins silently fight GC or erasure.

## Design — normative detail
The canonical `ReplayRegistry` is itself in `LogicalStatePayload` and strongly roots each active manifest plus the latest active archive record; archive records carry only nonlocal archive identities and weak closure commitments, never accidental local ObjectId edges. Renewal is an authenticated logical-command-sequenced extension. Revocation, expiry, resolver failure, or closure-verification failure causes the slot verifier to derive a weaker advertised grade and prevents a new `Replayable` claim. Expiry never deletes bytes directly: a consensus GC command first removes the relevant manifest/archive registry edge and then accounts for every other root. `KEEP NONE` does not preserve replay unless the query acquires a local or archive lease. Certificate modes `Compact`, `Budgeted`, `Full`, and `Forensic` may vary diagnostic detail, but a mode advertised as replayable may never truncate an identity field or referenced closure object. Erasure interplay: erased subjects downgrade replay through the `Redacted` arm with the erasure tombstone as typed evidence; an `ErasureCutSpec` never silently breaks a byte-identity claim — the effective grade weakens attributably instead.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19 lifecycle clauses (grade weakens as leases/resolution/trust/configuration/authority change; erased subjects downgrade through `Redacted` with the tombstone as typed evidence). FG-INV-14: manifests and archive records are GC roots until their exact terminal transfer/release; provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim. Invariant-class throughout.

## Interactions
Roots `w5-replay` manifests; `w2-retention-checkpoints` supplies KEEP/lease interplay and conditional refs; `w2-gc-core` executes the edge-removal-then-account path; `w9-redaction-erasure` supplies `ErasureCutSpec` and tombstones; `w11-backup`/`verif-replay-products` consume archive records.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash-matrix rows around the two-step expiry (edge removal command, then root accounting): no interleaving deletes bytes early or leaks a permanent root. Lease doctor: renewal extends under authenticated sequencing; expiry/revocation/resolver/closure failures each derive the declared weaker grade with reason codes and never mutate the manifest. `KEEP NONE` test: replay claim absent unless a local/archive lease was acquired at query time. Certificate-mode negatives: `Compact`/`Budgeted` advertised-replayable outputs never truncate an identity field or closure object (schema scan). Erasure attributability e2e: run query, apply `ErasureCutSpec` on a subject in its closure, verify replay derives the downgraded grade citing the tombstone; log the full grade-derivation trace.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: archive records with local ObjectId edges (invisible GC pins); direct byte deletion on lease expiry (breaks root accounting); truncating "replayable" compact certificates. Risk: registry growth under heavy replay retention — bounded because expiry is a first-class sequenced transition, not an operator chore.

## Provenance
Plan §8.6 (717), FG-INV-19/FG-INV-14.

### Fidelity addendum — exact archive record and registry schema
`ReplayArchiveRecord` is immutable and exact: `{archive_id,generation,predecessor_record_digest:WeakDigest?,security_domain,resolver_profile_oid,authenticated_external_locator,archive_closure_digest:WeakDigest,sorted_object_inventory[{identity:ArchiveObjectIdentity,expected_logical_object_id,expected_canonical_digest,length}],availability_commitment,time_authority_profile_oid,lease_not_before,lease_not_after,status:Active|Revoked|Expired,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. The signature transcript covers the resolver profile and both time bounds. The inventory/closure excludes the record itself, `ReplayRegistry`, and the locally rooted manifest, preserving the acyclic construction order `external evidence inventory -> archive record -> manifest -> registry`.

`ReplayRegistry` maps `manifest_id -> {manifest:StrongRef<ReplayManifest>,lease/status}` and `archive_id -> latest_record:StrongRef<ReplayArchiveRecord>`. Renewal is a logical-command-sequenced successor after full inventory verification and fresh Usable time evidence. Revocation/expiry asserts no deletion: the status successor retains exact subject-bound time evidence, then consensus removes the availability edge; ordinary GC may only then release otherwise-unrooted local records. Replayable advertisement requires every local object to open and every archive object to resolve through one Active, trusted, time-usable record with matching inventory/closure.

Unit/property tests cover canonical ordering, signature transcript, direct-successor generation, inventory uniqueness, acyclic exclusion, status/time transitions, and registry CAS. Crash/E2E tests cut renewal, revocation, expiry, edge removal, lookup, restore, and GC. Logs emit archive ID/generation, predecessor commitment, status, inventory count/root, closure/availability commitments, lease classification, signer epoch, registry generation, resolution verdict, and grade change; authenticated locators and credentials are redacted.

The W9 erasure task depends on this registry and supplies the real ErasureCutSpec/tombstone integration at G3. This direction keeps G2 self-contained without weakening FG-INV-19.

title: Implement Ripple consumption of canonical delta batches, frontiers, and source provenance
description:
## What & scope
Implement Ripple's sole canonical input path from Chronicle publication into role-correct Z-set delta circuits. This task owns Local and Sharded source adapters, exact retained-batch index traversal, frontier and cut validation, idempotent ordered consumption, source/provenance binding, recovery checkpoints, backpressure, and the boundary that forbids shard-fragment or physical-storage artifacts from becoming public logical input. It does not own circuit operators, view semantics, cursor delivery, or delta production.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 and B4 compose only if the commit stream is already the one canonical Z-set stream. A generic append subscriber would lose branch ancestry, authority, audit visibility, retention-cut proofs, and replay identity; consuming physical Strata changes would create a second truth. Role-exact indexes and gap-free frontiers let views, recursion, subscriptions, analytics, CDC, and audit reproduce identical logical deltas under recovery and compaction.

## Exact Ripple source doctrine
## 9. Ripple: Incremental Everything (Bet B4)

### 9.1 The unification claim

Four features that vendors often build separately—recursive evaluation, materialized views, subscriptions, and incremental analytics—share computation over **Z-sets** advanced by a total committed time. The source is not the unresolved intent log. Finalization persists Appendix A's exact sequence-neutral `LogicalDeltaTemplate {format,intent_semantics_ref:StrongRef<IntentSemantics>,final_effect_digest,source_intent_root_digest,coordinate_entries[]}`. Its canonically sorted entries bind `{graph,branch,relation_id,validated_schema_binding,schema_transition,delta_payload_ref:ConditionalCoordinateRef,delta_payload_digest}` and are exactly equal to the canonical before/after change. The capsule strongly owns the template and commits its digest. Prepared-root traversal has no committed marker/cut context and therefore follows every conditional payload as strong; after commit, the marker supplies the retention coordinate. This preserves relation and per-coordinate before/after schema identity for atomic multi-graph commits without naming the future marker or defeating per-graph retention cuts.

Apply never constructs an untagged batch. Local transaction apply supplies its committed marker, verifies the template/capsule, derives every resulting coordinate binding, and materializes Appendix A's exact self-contained `LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>`. Shard decision apply analogously materializes `LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>` from the certified fragment basis and decision; that internal object is not a public CDC source. W12 Meta waits for the complete post-visibility fragment/ack set and publishes only `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch`. Each role-specific batch ID is a deterministic function of the registered canonical fields and directly owned payload identities; retry reproduces identical bytes or fails closed. Template/marker/decision fields are nonretaining provenance, while included payloads are owned directly. A batch is derived, not a second source of truth: it may be rematerialized while its authoritative suffix remains, or retained independently by derived/subscription/replay/backup leases without retaining that suffix. A verified checkpoint cut may reclaim the old capsule/template only after all delta-retention promises either transfer to self-contained batch objects or take their explicit `GAP`/new-baseline transition. Every circuit integrates all relevant coordinate entries or none and records the role-tagged batch ID/idempotency key. Local apply roots its batch/frontier in the same candidate transition as the commit; shard apply roots its fragment in the same shard transition as the decision; Meta advances the public Global frontier only through `GlobalDeltaPublishSpec`. No-op intents emit no row delta; schema changes use separate versioned system relations.

### 9.2 The circuit engine

`fgdb-ripple` implements exact integer Z-set arithmetic: `ZWeight` uses checked `i128` as a fast representation and promotes before overflow to an in-house canonical signed-limb integer. Limb allocation/spill is resource-accounted; exhaustion aborts or lags the derived computation without publishing partial state. Thus the semantic domain is the integer additive group rather than a bounded partial imitation. The engine provides lift/differentiate/integrate/delay, registered derivatives for GLA operators, factorized delta forms with proved flattening equivalence, and spillable LSM-backed arrangements. Batch and incremental plans share typed algebra but have distinct physical optimization/resource contracts.

Logical change weights always form the integer additive group required for retractions. Optional annotations are separate products: Boolean annotations express existence; provenance-polynomial/DAG annotations express why-provenance; tropical values express costs. Each annotation family registers operator, deletion, differentiation, boundedness, and serialization laws. Replacing Z weights with Boolean or tropical values is forbidden because it would erase the additive inverses needed for general deletion. A `Confidence` annotation family over the `[0,1]` semiring is registered by name as a post-1.0 candidate under exactly this discipline: it exists only once its operator, deletion, differentiation, boundedness, and serialization laws are registered — provenance-polynomial growth is precisely why the boundedness law is mandatory — and confidence is an annotation product orthogonal to §8.3's `AnswerRequirement`/`AnswerContract` approximation typing: a confidence-annotated result is not thereby approximate, and an approximate result acquires no confidence semantics.

### 9.3 Recursion = incremental fixpoint

## Exact durable batch/index/cut contract
**LogicalDeltaTemplate / LogicalDeltaBatch.** A template is `{format,intent_semantics_ref:StrongRef<IntentSemantics>,final_effect_digest,source_intent_root_digest,coordinate_entries[]}`, where entries are canonically sorted and each is `{graph,branch,relation_id,validated_schema_binding,schema_transition:None|Some{transition_ref:StrongRef<SchemaTransition>},delta_payload_ref:ConditionalCoordinateRef,delta_payload_digest}`. The payload is a canonical exact Z-set over `CanonicalRow`; duplicate coordinates/relations, zero weights, noncanonical order, a transition inconsistent with its binding, or a payload not equal to the capsule's before/after effects are invalid. Prepared traversal follows every conditional edge as strong; committed traversal supplies the enclosing marker sequence and may apply only a matching `EffectCut`.

`LogicalDeltaBatch<Role>` has a generated common body `{format,role,coordinate_entries[{source_binding,resulting_binding,relation_id,delta_payload_ref:RegisteredStrongRef<DeltaPayload>}],batch_digest}` and exactly two role schemas. `LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>` adds `{source_template_digest:WeakDigest,commit_marker_identity:WeakMarkerIdentity,commit_seq,frontier:Local{commit_seq}}`. `LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>` adds `{source_fragment_basis_digest:WeakDigest,decision_identity:WeakGlobalCommandIdentity,shard_id,global_logical_command_seq,global_commit_seq,frontier:ShardFragment{global_commit_seq}}`. `batch_digest` covers every preceding canonical field and is the batch idempotency key; the object's full ObjectId is `LogicalDeltaBatchId<Role>`. Local apply/rematerialization and shard decision apply must reproduce the same role-specific object. A retained batch owns payloads directly but does not retain template/fragment, marker/decision, capsule, or predecessor history. Only `LocalCommitted` may inhabit `CommittedDeltaSourceRef::Local`; shard fragments are internal inputs to a `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch` and are never a public CDC source.

Delta indexes are bounded authenticated windows, not append-only strong maps. `LocalDeltaBatchIndex {format,retained_after_commit_seq,frontier,entries[every commit_seq in (retained_after_commit_seq,frontier] -> StrongRef<LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>>],retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Local>>?}` and `GlobalDeltaBatchIndex {format,retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier,entries[every global_commit_seq in (retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier] -> StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>],retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Meta>>?}` require a gap-free exact map in their retained interval. `ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex {format,shard_id,retained_after_global_commit_seq,observed_through_global_prefix,entries[participating committed global_txn_id/global_commit_seq -> StrongRef<LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>>],nonparticipant_or_noncommit_coverage_commitment,retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Shard>>?}` requires an exact bijection with every locally applied committed participant decision in its retained interval; it does not invent fragments for unrelated global commits.

`DeltaRetentionObligationRef<Role>` is the generated closed union of role-valid cursor/delivery, derived-generation, replay, backup/export, CDC, shard-ack/global-publication, and explicit administrative history promises. `DeltaRetentionCutEvidence<Role> {role_and_group,basis_index_digest,cut_through_position,exact_sorted_obligation_refs[],transferred_batch_owner_refs[],released_or_gap_transition_refs[],authoritative_rematerialization_availability_or_retirement_proof,complete_obligation_bijection,checker_version}` proves that every promise at or below the cut has either moved to an independent strong owner, completed/released, or taken an explicit `GAP`/new-baseline transition. `ProvisionalDeltaRetentionCut<Role>` may authenticate inherited absence but authorizes no new edge removal. The role-specific ordered `LocalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec`, `GlobalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec`, or `ShardFragmentDeltaRetentionCutSpec` may install `ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Role>` and advance `retained_after_*` only after the paired checkpoint/floor and ordinary activated retention cut cover the same position. Apply replaces old strong entries with the prefix commitment in the same state transition; a missing retained entry is corruption, while a query below a proved cut returns `HistoryUnavailable` or the already-recorded gap contract. Checkpoint/configuration floors and backup/restore inventories retain the current index, active cut, and every still-live independent owner. Crash, lease-transfer, concurrent cursor, cut replacement, and rematerialization tests cover every boundary; no checkpoint cut silently invalidates a promised resume range.

## Design — source adapter and state machine
The adapter opens a pinned authority/visibility-qualified source basis and selects exactly one public source family. Local consumes the gap-free interval of `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` after Local logical apply/publication and required audit visibility. Sharded consumes only `GlobalDeltaBatchIndex` entries after `GlobalDeltaPublishSpec` and the exact global visible prefix. `ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex` is an internal W12 fan-in, certification, acknowledgement, and proof source; Ripple, CDC, subscriptions, and every public source adapter reject it before evaluation. No adapter consumes Strata block/run mutation, Raft entry bytes, uncommitted intent, prepared fragment, or maintenance realization.

For each role the source validates database/security namespace/incarnation/service epoch, role/group, authority projection, branch/graph bindings, batch identity and canonical digest, exact predecessor/sequence interval, applied/visible prefix, `retained_after_*`, current frontier, active `ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Role>`, retired-prefix commitment, and contiguous required entries. It expands canonical insert/retract weights and provenance into the exact integer Z-set source type; zero weights normalize away deterministically. Re-delivery of the same batch identity is idempotent; a different body at the same index is corruption. An entry absent inside the retained interval is corruption. A request below a proved active cut yields only the registered `HistoryUnavailable` or an already-recorded cursor GAP/new-baseline contract; a Provisional cut authorizes no absence or reclamation.

`RippleConsumerState` is an immutable/checkpointed per-consumer tuple of source role/domain, authority and graph binding commitments, consumer definition/generation, last fully applied batch/index and digest, input/output frontiers, circuit state root, pending durable output commitments, active cut basis, resource/backpressure state, and replay profile. Advance is one atomic state transition after circuit application and output ownership are durable; crash before it replays the same batch, while crash after it cannot double-apply. Cancellation releases only volatile work and preserves the prior durable frontier. Definition/authority/topology/semantic-generation changes require a typed handoff/rebuild, never state reuse.

Cut advancement consumes exact `DeltaRetentionCutEvidence<Role>` and proves a complete obligation bijection across every view/generation, subscription/cursor/pending output, replay/archive lease, backup/export/CDC promise, shard acknowledgement/global publication, and administrative history consumer. No cut silently invalidates a live consumer. Source backpressure is bounded through ResourceLedger/EphemeralResourceBudget and does not move a frontier or acknowledge input before durable ownership transfer.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-10 exact integer Z-set algebra; FG-INV-15 no reclamation before complete obligation closure; FG-INV-18 derived state never authoritative; FG-INV-19 replay closure; FG-INV-20 authorization before observation. A frontier proves only contiguous consumption through the named visible source basis; it does not prove downstream freshness unless the corresponding output watermark/contract exists.

## Interactions
Consumes W2 delta production/index/cut/publication, W2 snapshots/retention, W9 audit visibility and authority, W1 resource ledger, and W12 Global/Shard publication contracts when enabled. Feeds W6 circuits, recursion, views, subscriptions, freshness, maintainers, triggers, W7 derived indexes, W10 CDC, verification oracles, and performance freshness gates. The source adapter shares stable batch IDs with replay but does not own archive resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover role/source selection, canonical batch decode, exact predecessor and interval checks, Z-set normalization, idempotent re-delivery, frontier transition totality, cut comparisons, authority/visibility matching, and cancellation rollback.
- Property/model tests generate insert/retract streams, duplicate/reorder/drop/corrupt entries, branch/role/configuration substitutions, and cut/frontier interleavings; the durable consumer state matches an independent canonical Z-set model after every step.
- Negative tests prove ShardFragment, physical Strata, prepared, invisible, unauthorized, below-Provisional-cut, and gap-inside-retained-range inputs fail before circuit observation.
- Simulation explores crash/cancel at fetch, validate, apply, output-own, checkpoint, and acknowledge boundaries; restart produces the same circuit/output/frontier bytes and never double-applies.
- Retention tests hold and release every obligation class, prove Activated cuts require a complete bijection, and distinguish below-cut HistoryUnavailable from retained-range corruption.
- E2E runs equivalent Local and W12 Global streams through the same circuit/view/subscription pipeline, crashes during advance, applies authority and topology changes, cuts history under active consumers, and proves equal authorized visible Z-set results; an injected Shard fragment is rejected.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics emit source role/index kind, database/group/public authority commitment, batch identity/digest and interval, applied/visible prefix, frontier before/after, cut kind/basis, validation checks, normalization counts, durable output/state root commitments, backpressure/cancel/crash outcome, disposition, artifact refs, seed, and replay command. Tests reconstruct the advance sequence from logs and reject missing, duplicate, out-of-order, unbounded-cardinality, secret-bearing, or protected-fact-bearing events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: a lagging consumer can pin history. Mitigation: explicit resources, freshness/delivery policy, bounded backlog, typed GAP/rebuild, and complete cut obligations. Rejected: consuming physical mutations, using shard fragments publicly, treating missing retained entries as normal gaps, acknowledging before durable output ownership, or rebuilding silently under a changed definition/authority.

## Provenance
Plan §9.1-§9.2, §9.5, Appendix A LogicalDeltaTemplate/LogicalDeltaBatch and delivery/cut contracts, FG-INV-10/15/18/19/20.

title: Implement WITH FRESHNESS: slo-typed lag bounds and the FreshnessBreach notice union
description:
## What & scope
Implement `SUBSCRIBE … WITH FRESHNESS <bound>`: the reserved freshness field on `SubscriptionDeliveryPolicy<Role>`, CREATE-time model-gated admission, the typed `FreshnessBreach` standing-notice machinery with its closed-union registration batch, and realized-lag reporting. Also keep coherence with §8.3's query-side `FreshnessConstraint` (an orthogonal surface).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Freshness is the market's headline complaint about derived state and B4's visible promise — but the delivery plane is gated by audit visibility, external resolution RTT, and time-evidence activation, none of which it may bypass. So the plan's honesty rule (B5, constraint §1.11 "claims have types") forces freshness to be an slo-class observation with typed breach notices, never an enforced invariant. Watermark units keep time authority off the fan-out path.

## Design — normative detail
The bound is a delivery-lag target expressed in watermark/commit-sequence units — never wall clock, which would drag per-delivery time-authority observations onto the fan-out path — bounding how far the cursor's acknowledged frontier may lag the published source batch frontier. It is claim-typed `slo` under §1.11 and lives in `slo.toml`-class rows, never `invariants.toml`: no delivery-freshness statement is ever an invariant. CREATE-time admission reuses §9.4's mechanism verbatim — a bound the current maintenance/delivery model predicts cannot be met is rejected at cursor creation, and the returned artifact remains a model-qualified estimate.

A runtime breach is **observed, never enforced**: the cursor emits a typed `FreshnessBreach` notice registered as a pending-output notice kind beside `Delta|Reset`. The registration is one G0-frozen batch that, together with inhabiting the reserved policy field, adds matching `FreshnessBreach` arms to: `PendingCursorOutputRecord.kind`, the deliverable cursor states, `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord.delivery`, the disposition-receipt `action` set, `AuditVisibilityProtectedOutputReleaseRecipe`, `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec`, and the matching Appendix D wire arms (`ProtectedOutputManagementStatus.output_kind` and the notice frame projection). The notice follows the same publish → audit-release → activation → ACK discipline as a reset notice while changing no public cursor position, retiring no baseline, and consuming no successor delivery window. It never occupies the `Delta|Reset` pending-output slot — the one-pending-future-output law is per data output, with at most one standing notice beside it, consumed or superseded by the next publish — and a persistent breach coalesces into one standing notice under the policy's declared cadence rather than a per-delta storm. A breach never blocks the delivery pipeline, never silently drops or coalesces deltas beyond the policy's declared coalescing rules, and never causes the server to advertise a bound it did not meet. Realized lag is derivable from the envelope's `start_frontier`/`resulting_frontier` against the published source frontier and crosses the wire only through the registered public projections when disclosure is policy-approved. Query-side coherence: §8.3's `AnswerRequirement.freshness_constraint:FreshnessConstraint{maximum_source_lag:WatermarkLagBound, on_unmet:ExactFallback|Fail}` is the read-path analog in the same watermark units; the two surfaces share unit definitions but neither implies the other.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-EVID-04 verbatim: "Derived-state freshness (slo-class, never an invariant) — bound expressed in watermark/commit-sequence units, audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies named, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy." FG-CFG-03 governs the CREATE-time feasibility model (arrival/service assumptions, predicted envelope, actual watermark, fallback policy); FG-CFG-04 prices the added maintenance-stream entries. The slot laws (at most one standing notice beside the one pending data output) inherit FG-INV-15/16's per-record CAS and obligation discipline.

## Interactions
`g0-claim-registries` owns the claim-type constitution and slo.toml placement; the closed-union arm additions land with `g0-format-arms`' activation-batch specs. `w6-subscriptions`/`w6-sub-delivery` host the slot and delivery machinery; `w9-audit-release`/`w9-activation-batching` release and activate the notice like any protected output; `w5-answer-contracts` defines the query-side twin; `obs-slo` wires realized-lag distributions and breach-rate alerts; `perf-freshness-vector` owns the freshness gates.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Admission: model-infeasible bound rejected at CREATE with the model's named assumptions logged; accepted bound returns a model-qualified estimate artifact. Lifecycle: breach publish→release→activate→ACK e2e; notice changes no public cursor position, retires no baseline, consumes no successor window (asserted via state-version and window bookkeeping logs). Slot law: concurrent delta + breach never contend for the data slot; a second breach supersedes the standing notice under the declared cadence (no storm — property test over breach-persistent workloads counts exactly one standing notice). Honesty: server never advertises an unmet bound; realized lag computed from envelope frontiers matches the source-frontier ledger; disclosure-gated wire projection tested both approved and denied. Registry: CI proves the FreshnessBreach arms exist in every listed union or the feature is absent (clause-activation contract). DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): CREATE admission logs the declared bound, the model's named arrival/service assumptions, and the predicted envelope of the returned model-qualified artifact; every breach publish/release/activate/ACK logs cursor ID, cursor state version, notice identity, declared bound, realized lag (envelope `start_frontier`/`resulting_frontier` against the published source frontier), and the cadence decision taken (new standing notice vs supersession); disclosure decisions log the policy arm served (Opaque vs Declassified); tests assert the logged realized-lag series matches the source-frontier ledger and that breach-rate telemetry carries FG-EVID-04's full disclosure shape.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: wall-clock bounds; enforcement semantics (blocking or dropping deltas to "meet" freshness); per-delta breach notices; a breach kind occupying the data-output slot; invariant-typing any freshness statement. Risk: users read slo as guarantee — mitigated by the model-qualified artifact wording and typed breach telemetry.

## Provenance
§9.5 (802); §8.3 (690); §9.4 (762); §1.11; Appendix F FG-EVID-04, FG-CFG-03/04.
