The four pinned papers support technical risks around governance, derived-state freshness/reindexing, agent-memory security, and fresh ANN only. They do not prove buyer demand, market size, or universal absence from shipping products. Implementation may target the technical gaps; product/market claims require separate evidence.

title: Upstream a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface into franken_networkx
description:
## What & scope
Upstream work inside franken_networkx itself: design and land a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface with an associated node-index type in `fnx-algorithms`, then migrate algorithm families to be generic over it, so Prism can traverse Strata's decoded/merged authorized cursors without whole-graph materialization. Maintains the interim `DECODED_CACHE` compatibility labeling until each family migrates.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The current `GraphView` trait in `fnx-algorithms` offers string access plus integer-index rows: `neighbors_indices(&self, idx) -> Option<&[usize]>` and `in_neighbors_indices`. That contract borrows flat `usize` simple-graph rows. Strata stores compressed `u32/u64` ordinals in a typed directed multigraph with per-list codecs, so the borrow cannot be satisfied zero-copy. Section 2.2 is explicit: `GraphView` is "a compatibility target, not a zero-copy match today", and "no zero-copy claim survives unless the upstream interface and physical representation actually permit it". The closed dependency universe (Section 1) makes upstreaming the sanctioned path — fnx is one of the three foundation projects we may modify, and nothing external may be imported instead. Serves B2 (analytics read tiered storage in place, no widened private copy) and B3 (no second graph representation as the price of analytics). Section 20 carries the matching risk row: fnx algorithms not yet trait-generic or external-memory where required; W8 upstream/cursor work is the named mitigation.

## Design — normative detail
Interface: a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface with an associated node-index type, so `u32`/`u64` ordinal spaces need no widening copy and the borrow is per-cursor-step rather than per-row slice — which is what makes compressed and multi-source-merged adjacency implementable at all. Algorithms generic over that interface traverse decoded/merged authorized cursors — merged across Tier-D delta blocks and Tier-R sealed runs — without whole-graph materialization.

The cursor adapters must honor Tier-R realities (Section 6.3): per-list `NeighborCodec` is one of `EliasFano`, `StreamVByte { skip_table }`, or `DenseIntervals`; a source ordinal is meaningful only under its source map; each encoded destination is either a stable VId or `(destination_map_slot, dst_ordinal)` where the slot names an explicit `{ destination_partition, OrdinalMapId }`; no ordinal crosses a map boundary untagged. Migration proceeds by family per Section 11.4's coverage strategy. Every migrated algorithm keeps NetworkX-parity semantics locked — fnx is the parity-locked semantics oracle, and `fnx-classes` (IndexMap adjacency, insertion-order semantics) remains the compatibility reference. Until a family migrates, compatibility uses explicit epoch-shared `Vec<usize>` caches labeled `DECODED_CACHE` (owned by w8-projection); the label persists in certificates so no consumer mistakes it for zero-copy.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: cursor-path execution must be answer-equivalent to slice-path/cached-path execution — logical values, multiplicity, and order preserved. FG-INV-20: cursors reach algorithms only as authorized cursors constructed behind `fgdb-secure-view`; the upstream trait must not grow an escape hatch yielding unauthorized adjacency. Claim class: zero-copy is a verified capability claim made only where interface and physical representation actually permit it; traversal-overhead numbers on this bead are evidence-class measurements with committed baselines, not gates.

## Interactions
Consumes w3-tier-r (codec and merge semantics the cursor adapters honor), w3-vertex-directory (ordinal maps behind the associated node-index type), w1-foundation-types. Produces the trait and migrated families consumed by w8-projection (cursor path replacing `DECODED_CACHE` per family), w8-materialization (streaming source), and verif-differential (cursor-generic algorithms checked against the `fnx-classes` reference and NetworkX parity fixtures — the two-hop oracle chain).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Trait published in fnx with a GAT node-index type. Initial migration set covers at least shortest paths (BFS/Dijkstra), PageRank, connected components, and k-core. Property tests: on `fnx-generators` graphs (SBM, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz, LFR, lattices), cursor-path results equal existing slice-path results under identical `TieBreakPolicy`. Differential: migrated algorithms still pass fnx's NetworkX-parity fixtures unchanged. No-materialization proof: tests assert bounded peak allocation (no hidden O(V+E) cache) via allocation accounting on large generated graphs. Fuzz: cursor adapters over adversarial codec mixes — EliasFano/StreamVByte/DenseIntervals interleavings, hub overflow rows, empty lists, map-slot boundary crossings. Bench evidence: cursor traversal overhead vs `DECODED_CACHE` recorded with baseline artifacts and complexity-witness `observed_count` regression tracking. Logging: test builds log adapter path, codec mix, and map-slot crossings per traversal. E2E script: run one migrated algorithm (e.g. BFS) end-to-end over a Strata-backed graph through the cursor path and over the same graph through the `DECODED_CACHE` path; assert identical results and witness semantics under the same `TieBreakPolicy`; assert the standalone-fnx NetworkX-parity suite still passes on the upstreamed trait; and assert peak-allocation accounting stays bounded on the cursor path. The logging requirements above (adapter path, codec mix, map-slot crossings, plus per-traversal allocation accounting) are mandatory events the e2e script parses, so the no-materialization claim is verifiable from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: GAT/lifetime friction with merged multi-source cursors; interface churn destabilizing standalone fnx users (mitigation: additive trait, parity suite stays in fnx CI). Rejected: permanently widening Strata rows to `usize` (memory blowup, defeats B2); forking fnx rather than upstreaming (violates the single-source foundation doctrine); changing fnx semantics to fit storage (the parity lock forbids it); claiming zero-copy for the cache path.

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.2; Section 2.2 GraphView row; Section 6.3; Section 1; Section 20.
design:
## External-review boundary (2026-07-22)

FG-ADR-FNX-GRAPHVIEW-PREREQUISITE remains review_due. The pinned franken_networkx snapshot 9d710b1c exposes GraphView::neighbors_indices as Option<&[usize]>; the borrowed-neighbor-cursor or GAT extension required for a zero-copy Prism claim is still absent. Implement and verify the upstream prerequisite before advertising zero-copy. The review makes no claim beyond that exact snapshot.

title: Implement masked-semiring SpMV/SpMSpV native kernels behind differential gates
description:
## What & scope
Implement Prism's native compute kernels: masked-semiring SpMV and SpMSpV (sparse matrix-vector and sparse-matrix sparse-vector products over registered semirings with masks), built in-house per the closed dependency universe, as the fast execution backend for frontier-style algorithms — BFS, PageRank, WCC/label propagation, SSSP, and staged successors — over authorized projections and materialized representations.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Section 18.2 lists "masked-semiring SpMV/SpMSpV kernels" among the components the closed universe requires us to build ourselves; the GraphBLAS idea is adopted as a technique, but no external library may be imported. Section 11.4 fixes the order of work: native kernels are added only after differential semantics tests — the fnx implementation is the semantics oracle and a kernel is a provably-equivalent accelerator, never a second semantics. Kernels are what make the Section 17 benchmark row achievable: LDBC Graphalytics (BFS/PR/WCC/CDLP/LCC/SSSP) within 1.5x of dedicated static analytics engines on transactional storage — the Sortledton bar. Serves B2 (kernels consume Strata's compressed forms directly where the codec honestly permits) and B5 (kernel identity rides in witnesses and replay closures).

## Design — normative detail
Kernel model: y = A applied to x over a declared semiring (additive/multiplicative monoids with identities and annihilator), with input/output masks restricting the computed entry set; SpMSpV exploits sparse frontiers. Semiring/mask configurations are registered per algorithm family, never ad hoc. Masks encode visibility/filter structure already established by the `AuthorizedProjection` — masks are never an authorization mechanism; authorization happened at projection construction (FG-INV-20), and kernels only ever see authorized data.

Storage contract (Section 6.3, the honest intersection contract): Elias-Fano neighbor lists support rank/select directly; `StreamVByte { skip_table }` lists use skip/fence metadata and bounded blockwise decode; `DenseIntervals` use interval arithmetic; there is no claim that Elias-Fano offsets provide rank/select over a separate varint stream. Kernels operate in projection ordinal spaces: a source ordinal is meaningful only under its source map; destination `(destination_map_slot, dst_ordinal)` tags must be honored at partition boundaries; hub stripes/overflow rows (Section 6.2) get dedicated row handling.

Determinism: each kernel declares its numeric/determinism profile per Sections 8.2/8.6 — strict floating results use the portable profile; anything target-dependent requires `RELAXED` posture and is reproducible only within its recorded target/build scope. The kernel implementation hash, CPU-feature contract, and kernel/profile registry entries ride in the `ComplexityWitness` binding and in the `ReplayManifest`'s `ExecutableArtifactSet` — FG-INV-19/Section 8.6 require `Replayable` to identify the CPU-feature contract and kernel/profile registry. Iterative uses record the Section 11.4 residual artifacts: norm, numeric profile, iteration trace, stopping rule, and the mathematical assumptions behind any convergence bound.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: kernel-backed execution is a claimed answer-equivalent path — logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract preserved vs the fnx oracle under the same projection and `TieBreakPolicy`; proved physical equivalence cannot change strict output. FG-INV-20: no kernel observation precedes authorization; masks must not reintroduce unauthorized reads or leak hidden-element existence through timing/statistics facts. FG-INV-19: replay of kernel-executed queries requires the exact kernel/profile registry and CPU-feature contract in the manifest; a missing artifact weakens the effective grade attributably, never silently. Claim classes: the Graphalytics 1.5x target is benchmark-class with committed baselines and variance-aware gating; any adaptive kernel-selection policy is FG-CAL-01 territory — pinned deterministic fallback, stream-sequenced promotion, disclosed filtration/alpha/support.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (ordinal spaces; visibility-derived masks), w8-materialization (spilled/streamed inputs for out-of-core operation), w3-tier-r (codec access paths under the intersection contract), w1-codecs (SIMD primitives), w5-determinism (numeric profiles, canonical result encoding). Produces witness-bound implementation paths consumed by w8-witnesses; benchmark rows consumed by perf-bench-core; differential rows consumed by verif-differential.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Differential gate as exposure precondition: kernel results byte-equal the canonical results of the scalar fnx implementation across the `fnx-generators` corpus (SBM, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz, LFR, lattices, social datasets) under each registered directedness/multigraph/self-loop law and `TieBreakPolicy`, strict profile. Property tests: registered semirings satisfy associativity/identity/annihilator laws under the masked operations; mask correctness — no entry outside the mask is computed or observable, including via instrumented timing-fact counters. Fuzz: empty/full masks, empty frontiers, hub overflow rows, map-slot boundary crossings, codec mixes. Bench gates: Graphalytics BFS/PR/WCC/CDLP/LCC/SSSP within the 1.5x bar on transactional storage, with committed baselines, variance-aware gating, and complexity-witness `observed_count` regression tracking — bench rows, fixtures, and baselines registered here; the gated runs execute on §15.6's deterministic apparatus via `verif-perf-apparatus`/`perf-bench-core`, manifests-green at gate-g4. Cross-SIMD-width determinism: scalar vs vectorized paths byte-equal under the strict profile, or the profile is explicitly declared `RELAXED`. Logging: kernel hash, numeric profile, CPU features, mask density, per-iteration frontier sizes, iterations to convergence. E2E script: execute `CALL fnx.pagerank` over an authorized projection with the kernel backend enabled and then disabled; assert byte-equal canonical results under the strict profile; verify the witness carries the kernel implementation hash and CPU-feature contract; and replay the kernel-executed run from its `ReplayManifest` to the same canonical result digest. The listed logging fields (kernel hash, numeric profile, CPU features, mask density, per-iteration frontier sizes, iterations to convergence) are mandatory implementation log events, not test-only instrumentation; tests assert their presence and their consistency with the witness bindings.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: floating-point reassociation across SIMD widths breaking strict determinism (pin the reduction order or declare `RELAXED`); kernel/oracle drift as fnx evolves (the differential suite runs continuously in CI, not once at exposure). Rejected: importing SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS or any external kernel library (closed universe); kernels as an unauthorized fast path bypassing projections; masks as the authorization mechanism; shipping kernels before differential semantics tests (Section 11.4 forbids it).

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.4; Section 18.2; Sections 6.2-6.3; Sections 8.2/8.6; Section 17.

title: Build the MATERIALIZED spill path and external-memory operator exposure gate
description:
## What & scope
Build Prism's `MATERIALIZED` execution path: streaming/spilling an authorized projection into a generation-scoped representation for algorithms that are not cursor-generic; the operator exposure gate deciding whether an fnx algorithm may become a database operator at all; and the per-operator external-memory/spill contracts (cleanup + I/O bounds) every exposed operator must declare. Includes the small-graph mutable-working-copy path via `fnx-classes`/`fnx-views`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
FrankenGraphDB sells a larger-than-memory product contract; an analytics surface that silently assumes RAM-resident graphs would break it. Section 11.4's discipline keeps coverage honest: an algorithm without a bounded-memory story stays in the source catalog rather than shipping as a trap. Serves B3 (analytics under the same resource governance as queries), B5 (evidence-class residual artifacts for convergence claims), and B6 (typed `ResourceExhausted` carrying registered minimums, so agents can reason about failures instead of guessing).

## Design — normative detail
Algorithms not cursor-generic take a `MATERIALIZED` path that streams/spills an authorized projection into a generation-scoped representation. Exposure gate (normative): an algorithm is exposed as a database operator only after it has either (a) a bounded cursor path or (b) a declared external-memory/spill implementation with cleanup and I/O bounds; otherwise it remains in the source catalog rather than violating the larger-than-memory product contract. `ResourceExhausted` remains legal when even the registered minimum resident set or scratch quota is unavailable — not as a substitute for designing the operator. W8 extends coverage by family and adds native kernels only after differential semantics tests.

Residual artifacts (normative): each run records norm, numeric profile, iteration trace, stopping rule, and the mathematical assumptions behind any convergence bound; deterministic iteration count alone does not create cross-machine floating identity.

Representation: spill blocks are generation-scoped — pinned to the projection's snapshot/epoch — written through the Section 6.7 buffer/scratch discipline, and registered as obligations so cancellation and crash cleanup are deterministic. Small graphs may take the `fnx-classes`/`fnx-views` mutable-working-copy path (IndexMap adjacency, insertion-order semantics — the NetworkX-parity compatibility reference; borrowed/cached snapshot views) when an algorithm needs a mutable working copy; that path is bounded by the registered minimum resident set. Per-operator larger-than-memory contracts follow the Section 8.7 house style — external merge sort, radix/grace partitioning, partitioned builds — each operator declaring its own partitioning/spill scheme rather than inheriting a global one. The registered minimum resident set and scratch quota come from the algorithm's `FnxSignatureRegistry` larger-than-memory implementation class (w8-projection).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, or workspace materialization preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract — the `MATERIALIZED` path is exactly such a claimed-equivalent transformation and must prove it. FG-INV-16 (restated): no structured task, scratch object, or result/workspace lease is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state — spill scratch and checkpoints are such obligations. FG-INV-14: scratch remains a GC root until its exact terminal release. Claim classes: convergence bounds and iteration traces are evidence-class residual artifacts; long-run memory stability is FG-EVID-03 endurance-gate territory; declared-vs-measured I/O bound divergence is itself a finding.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (authorized projection streams; registry implementation classes and quotas), w5-executor (morsel/spill machinery and external-algorithm precedents), w3-buffer (buffer/scratch/EBR discipline), w1-foundation-types. Produces materialized representations consumed by w8-kernels; scratch obligations governed by w8-scheduling; crash rows consumed by verif-torture; equivalence checks consumed by verif-differential.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Exposure-gate CI: the operator registry refuses to activate an algorithm lacking both a bounded cursor path and a declared external-memory implementation with cleanup and I/O bounds, with negative fixtures per missing element. Spill correctness: on `fnx-generators` graphs sized beyond the scratch quota, `MATERIALIZED` results equal in-memory reference results; peak resident set stays within registered minimum plus quota (asserted and logged). `ResourceExhausted` tests: raised only when the registered minimum is genuinely unavailable; the error carries the registered numbers. Crash matrix: kill during spill write, mid-iteration, and after completion-before-release — recovery leaves zero orphaned scratch, with obligation accounting reaching terminal state under the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle. Residual-artifact tests: iteration trace, stopping rule, norm, and stated assumptions present and schema-valid for every iterative algorithm. Logging: path=`MATERIALIZED`, generation id, spill bytes, partition counts, I/O-bound conformance, iteration-trace reference, cleanup completion. E2E script: run a non-cursor-generic algorithm via `CALL fnx.<algorithm>` over a projection sized beyond the scratch quota so it spills; cancel a concurrent identical run mid-spill; assert correct results on the surviving run, deterministic scratch cleanup and obligation quiescence on the cancelled run, and `path=MATERIALIZED` certificates with schema-valid residual artifacts on both. The listed logging fields (path, generation id, spill bytes, partition counts, I/O-bound conformance, iteration-trace reference, cleanup completion) are mandatory implementation log events; tests parse them to verify I/O-bound conformance and cleanup completion.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: wrongly declared I/O bounds (divergence is treated as a release finding); representation drift between spilled blocks and projection epochs. Rejected: exposing in-memory-only algorithms as operators (violates the product contract); using `ResourceExhausted` as a coverage strategy; one global spill format instead of per-operator declared contracts; treating deterministic iteration counts as cross-machine floating-point identity.

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.4; Section 2.2 (fnx-classes/fnx-views rows); Section 8.7; Section 6.7.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement FnxSignatureRegistry and AuthorizedProjection with the honest copy boundary
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Prism call surface and projection boundary in `fgdb-prism`: the versioned `FnxSignatureRegistry`; the `FnxCallSpec` binding of `CALL fnx.<algorithm>(...) [YIELD ...]` statements; and construction of authorized, snapshot-pinned graph projections — `AuthorizedProjection<Role>` wrapping a secure-view `AuthorizedGraphView` — as the only way a FrankenGraphDB graph reaches fnx code. Includes the `DECODED_CACHE` compatibility path and its mandatory labeling.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Analytics must not create a second authorization or visibility root (B1/B3). fnx algorithms assume flat simple graphs; FrankenGraphDB stores a typed directed multigraph with branches, valid time, and capability-filtered visibility. The projection object is where those worlds meet: a complete, certified reduction with explicit laws, so no algorithm can silently observe hidden elements, aggregate parallel edges implicitly, or receive an unpinned mutable view. Serves B5 (everything about the projection is certificate material) and B6 (agents can inspect exactly what graph an algorithm saw). This is the GDS-class capability done without a second engine, which is the market differentiator.

## Design — normative detail
`CALL fnx.<algorithm>(...) [YIELD ...]` exposes only registered, semantically compatible fnx signatures. The versioned `FnxSignatureRegistry` describes per algorithm: zero/one/multiple graph inputs; typed parameters/defaults/coercions; output schema; attribute roles (weight, capacity, demand, partition, label, etc.); callback/matcher module type/effects; RNG policy/seed; directed/multigraph/self-loop laws; numeric/determinism profile; complexity witness; and larger-than-memory implementation class. Only complete signature rows are callable, and all input projections/implementation paths ride in the certificate.

Each graph argument becomes an `AuthorizedProjection<Role> { authority_binding: AuthorityBindingFor<Role>, graph_reference_binding, logical_state_root_identity: WeakStateIdentity, directedness, labels/types, parallel-edge law, attribute bindings with missing/coercion laws, node order, descriptor_visibility_projection_ref, disclosure_and_answer_contract }`. Two-graph algorithms bind two independently authorized role/head/schema projections; generators bind no hidden graph; callbacks are pinned deterministic module OIDs or explicitly non-replayable native effects. An authority digest or security-only shard projection cannot substitute for the complete binding. Opaque `params` cannot smuggle an unscoped graph, attribute, callback, or entropy source.

Honest copy boundary (Section 11.2): the current fnx trait borrows `&[usize]`; Strata's compressed `u32/u64` rows cannot safely implement that contract zero-copy. Until the upstream cursor/GAT interface (w8-fnx-upstream) lands per family, compatibility uses explicit epoch-shared `Vec<usize>` caches and is labeled `DECODED_CACHE`, not zero-copy. Typed directed multigraphs are reduced only through an `AuthorizedProjection` bound by the registered `FnxCallSpec`; parallel-edge aggregation is never implicit.

Access typing (Section 12.3): only `fgdb-secure-view` can construct `AuthorizedSnapshot`, `AuthorizedCursor`, `AuthorizedGraphView`, `AuthorizedMutation`, `AuthorizedMutationPermit`, and `AuthorizedDerivedState`; Prism cannot obtain raw Strata cursors or unscoped commit submission; planner pushdown is an optimization atop this boundary, not the authorization root. The projection's `descriptor_visibility_projection_ref` binds the enforced `DescriptorVisibilityProjection` object so hidden descriptors/rows affect no visible enumeration, cardinality, routing, plan/error/timing/statistics/cache fact. Node order is explicit in the projection; `fnx-parity` is an explicit projection profile with its own adjacency-order metadata (Section 8.6) — never an accident of storage or compaction order.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated): authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability; every authority-bearing durable schema binds one complete SecurityStateBinding; equal epoch scalars with different roots never substitute; one union-wide authorization decision covers the complete effect set; capability lookup/status/release is uniformly nonrevealing on failure. FG-INV-04 (restated core): visibility obeys system-time snapshot high sequence, selected branch ancestry for each graph-reference role, valid-time slice-set intersection and boundary normalization, the erasure-tombstone conjunct, and the expiry predicate; distinct branch heads or valid-time selectors never alias — the projection pins exactly one such visible state via `logical_state_root_identity`. FG-INV-12: the projection is an answer-preserving reduction under its declared laws — values, multiplicity, order, visibility, and security projection preserved. Claim classes: parity behavior is differential-oracle class; the `DECODED_CACHE` label is an honesty/evidence requirement, not a performance claim.

## Interactions
Consumes w4-secure-view (facade types and permits), w5-binder (statement binding into `FnxCallSpec`), w3-tier-r and w3-vertex-directory (adjacency and ordinal maps the cache decodes), w1-foundation-types. Produces `AuthorizedProjection` values consumed by w8-fnx-upstream (cursor adapters), w8-materialization, and w8-kernels; projection digests consumed by w8-witnesses; the degraded-mode surface contract consumed by obs-system-graph.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Registry completeness CI: an incomplete signature row is uncallable, with negative tests per missing field class. Negative authorization matrix: authority-digest substitution, security-only shard projection substitution, and opaque-params smuggling of a graph/attribute/callback/entropy source are all rejected before any storage observation (observation order asserted via instrumented secure-view counters). Hidden-vs-physically-removed differential: a projection over a database with capability-hidden elements is behaviorally identical — results, witnesses, errors, statistics facts — to one over a database where those elements are physically absent. Parallel-edge law tests for every registered law. `DECODED_CACHE` tests: epoch invalidation on snapshot change; label present in the certificate; cache legitimately shared across same-epoch calls. Fuzz: `FnxCallSpec` parameter binding and coercions. Logging: every projection construction emits projection digest, authority binding id, snapshot identity, node-order profile, and path label (`DECODED_CACHE` | cursor | `MATERIALIZED`). E2E script: issue the same `CALL fnx.<algorithm>` against a branched, valid-time-sliced graph under two different capability sets; assert the projection digests differ, results match the hidden-vs-physically-removed oracle, an incomplete registry row is uncallable end-to-end, and the certificate carries the `DECODED_CACHE` label on the cache path. The projection-construction log record (projection digest, authority binding id, snapshot identity, node-order profile, path label) is a mandatory implementation event: tests assert exactly one record per construction and reconcile its digest with the certificate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: zero-copy claims today (the trait/physical mismatch is verified fact); implicit simple-graph reduction of multigraphs; treating planner pushdown as the authorization root. Risk: adapter cost misattribution — bench and differential harnesses must cost adapter work explicitly rather than pretending it is free (Section 11.3's rule).

## Provenance
Plan Sections 11.1-11.2; 12.3; 8.6; 2.2.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Schedule Prism analytics on a bulkhead-isolated PrismRegion with budgeted cancellation
description:
## What & scope
Implement Prism's runtime placement and resource governance: the `PrismRegion` analytics bulkhead in the asupersync process tree; budgets and cancellation for analytics runs; progress checkpointing as obligations; deterministic scratch cleanup; and the posture-gated degraded-mode contract for consumers of Prism-backed features.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Long-running analytics and low-latency OLTP share one process; without enforced isolation, one large community detection destroys the latency story B2/B3 promise. The plan's stance (Section 16.3) is that hard safety comes from structure — bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, deterministic fallback controls — while stability models are advisory only. Serves B5 (obligations and quiescence are exact, evidence-backed states, not hopes) and B6 (agents see typed `FeatureDisabled` and observable cancellation phases rather than silent degradation).

## Design — normative detail
Section 11.5 (normative): analytics run in dedicated regions on a bulkhead-isolated lane (combinator: `bulkhead`) so a Louvain over 10^9 edges cannot starve p99 OLTP; budgets + cancellation apply; long runs checkpoint progress as obligations; a cancelled community detection cleans up its scratch deterministically.

Placement (Section 16.1): `PrismRegion (analytics bulkhead)` is a first-class child of `FgdbRootRegion`, sibling to Chronicle/Strata/Ripple/Beacon/Warden/Aegis/Fabric/Observatory regions, under Spork supervision with a declared restart topology. Resource accounting (Section 16.6): the transient portion of the `ResourceVector` is reserved/charged/released through ephemeral hierarchical ledgers; hard caps and shedding order govern under pressure; maintenance and recovery retain protected emergency capacity; neither local session counters nor telemetry are quota authority. Cancellation (Section 16.4): exposes phase and deterministic drain progress; any probabilistic remaining-work or stall estimate names its model and is not a quiescence proof; quiescence is asserted only when obligations and resource ledgers reach their exact terminal state.

Degraded mode (Section 16.5, normative): with `fgdb-prism` disabled by its posture/feature activation predicate, the system graph remains a queryable read-only temporal property graph, while the fnx-backed analyses over it — wait-for cycle detection, centrality, incident diffing — return a typed `FeatureDisabled` error rather than degrading silently, with the feature-disable registry row recorded per G0's per-clause rule. Nothing safety-bearing degrades: the Section 16.3 early-warning wait-cycle probe is owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check, so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead for an alerting primitive.

Checkpointing: a long run's progress checkpoint is an obligation-owned scratch artifact bound to the run's projection epoch; resume revalidates the projection (snapshot pin, authority epoch) before reuse; cancellation or authority revocation converts checkpoints into cleanup obligations.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (restated): no structured task, ownership lease, pin, scratch object, or result/workspace/cursor/output lease is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared quorum/storage/network/time/continuity/resource fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state — analytics checkpoints and scratch are such obligations, checked by the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle. FG-INV-20: revocation and posture changes fence resumed runs — a checkpoint never lets a run outlive its authorization. Claim classes: OLTP p99 protection under analytics load is SLO/benchmark class, never an invariant; FG-CFG-02 governs any modeled controller-stability claim (model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards, soak results), and defaults predicted unstable by the versioned fluid model are rejected.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (epoch/authority pins for resume validation), w8-materialization (scratch/spill objects to govern), w10-qos (`ResourceVector`/`ResourceLedgerState` admission), w1-foundation-types (region/obligation primitives over the asupersync core). Produces the bulkhead contract consumed by obs-system-graph (the `FeatureDisabled` degraded mode and the observatory-owned wait-cycle-probe boundary), by perf-bench-core/perf-bench-governance (isolation benchmarks), and by verif-torture (cancellation/crash campaigns).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Isolation bench gate: a sustained large community-detection run concurrent with an OLTP point-read/write workload keeps OLTP p99 within the declared SLO envelope vs a no-analytics baseline; committed baselines and variance-aware gating; the contention scenario must include shared lower layers (buffer/IO), not just CPU. Cancellation suite: cancel at every phase — projection build, materialization, iteration, finalize — with phases and deterministic drain progress observable in logs, scratch reaching terminal cleanup, and obligations quiescent per the leak/quiescence oracle. Crash campaign: kill -9 during checkpointed runs; recovery accounts for every checkpoint/scratch obligation with zero leaks and no resurrected unauthorized state. Resume tests: resume across an authority-epoch change is refused with a typed error and cleanup is ordered. Degraded-mode tests: disable `fgdb-prism` via its activation predicate — system-graph queries still succeed, fnx-backed analyses return `FeatureDisabled`, the registry row is present, and the observatory wait-cycle probe still fires without Prism. Budget tests: charge/release pairs balance in the ephemeral ledger; shedding order is honored under pressure. Logging: region lifecycle events, budget charge/release pairs, checkpoint sequence numbers, cancellation phase transitions, and the final quiescence assertion with obligation counts. E2E script: start a long Louvain-class run over a large generated graph with an OLTP workload running concurrently; drive one full cancel/checkpoint/resume/revocation sequence; on a second instance disable `fgdb-prism` via its activation predicate and query the system graph — asserting SLO-envelope OLTP latency, typed `FeatureDisabled` from the fnx-backed analyses, refusal of the cross-authority-epoch resume, and final obligation quiescence. The listed logging events (region lifecycle, budget charge/release pairs, checkpoint sequence numbers, cancellation phase transitions, quiescence assertion with obligation counts) are mandatory implementation log events the script parses to verify each stage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: bulkhead misconfiguration hiding priority inversion in shared lower layers — isolation benches must exercise shared-resource contention; checkpoint reuse across revocation (fenced by design and tested). Rejected: cooperative "nice" scheduling without a bulkhead (cannot bound interference); silent no-op when Prism is disabled (typed `FeatureDisabled` is mandatory); using the analytics engine for safety-bearing alerting (the observatory owns its own bounded cycle check).

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.5; Sections 16.1-16.6; Section 13 (ResourceVector); Appendix F FG-INV-16, FG-CFG-02.

### Phase boundary correction — bulkhead resources do not depend on Fabric
Prism scheduling consumes the W1 canonical resource-ledger contract and asupersync obligation/bulkhead primitives directly. It does not depend on W10's server connection/QoS implementation. W10 later applies the same resource types to protocol/session admission; neither layer owns or wraps the other's state machine. The G2 Prism E2E therefore exercises embedded resource reservation and cancellation without requiring a network server, while G3 separately proves Fabric admission parity.

title: Fold CGSE witnesses and tie-break policies into Prism plan certificates
description:
## What & scope
Implement the determinism/evidence flow-through for Prism: preserve fnx's CGSE (policy semantics, witness schema, ledger, modes) inside the database; extend every in-database witness with projection/adapter bindings; and fold the resulting ledger into the query's plan certificate and replay manifest.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 is the bet that determinism and evidence are product features, not test-lab conveniences. fnx already solved this for algorithms: CGSE ships 13 `TieBreakPolicy` variants, `ComplexityWitness { n, m, dominant_term, observed_count, policy, seed, decision_path_blake3 }`, a `WitnessLedger`, Strict/Hardened modes, and a per-algorithm policy registry. Section 2.2 declares this "the determinism doctrine (B5) generalized from algorithms to queries". Prism is where the two meet: an fnx run inside a query must produce evidence at least as strong as standalone fnx, plus bindings that make the database context — projection, adapter, numeric profile — non-repudiable. For agents (B6), the certificate answers "what exactly ran, over which graph, under which policy" without re-running anything.

## Design — normative detail
Preservation: CGSE policy semantics and the `ComplexityWitness` schema are preserved unchanged. Extension (normative, Section 11.3): each in-database witness binds (1) the authorized projection digest; (2) projection-specific `n/m` — counts of the projected graph, never the raw stored graph; (3) the adapter/materialization path (cursor | `DECODED_CACHE` | `MATERIALIZED` | kernel implementation hash); (4) the numeric profile; and (5) the fnx implementation hash. Differential honesty rules: tests require the same projected input and policy to match standalone fnx; they do not compare a raw graph with a capability-filtered projection, and they do not pretend adapter work is free. The resulting ledger is folded into the query's plan certificate.

Query-level policy context (Section 8.6): every query declares a tie-break policy; the strict default is storage-independent `LexMin` over canonical scalar/element encodings; `ORDER BY` wins; `InsertionOrder` is immutable element-origin order available only when elements carry durable `OriginBirthOrder { commit_seq, intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id }`; `BranchAdmissionOrder` is separately named; compaction/run order never defines either; `fnx-parity` is an explicit projection profile with its own adjacency-order metadata. Certificate modes `Compact`, `Budgeted`, `Full`, and `Forensic` may vary diagnostic detail, but a mode advertised as replayable may never truncate an identity field or referenced closure object.

Replay integration: Prism executions populate `ReplayManifest` slots — callback modules land in the UDF/module set slot; the fnx implementation hash and kernel/profile registry land in the `ExecutableArtifactSet`; explicitly non-replayable native callback effects surface through the mediated external-inputs/nondeterminism slots as `Unavailable` with reason codes, so the structural grade weakens attributably instead of lying.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-19 (restated core): a registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix, and its effective grade may only weaken as leases, resolution, trust, configuration, or authority change; `Replayable` requires every semantic slot — including executable artifacts and decisions — to resolve and reproduce canonical logical output; missing, redacted, revoked, expired, or untrusted evidence yields only the declared weaker grade. Prism witness bindings are exactly such slots. FG-INV-12: certified-equivalent physical paths (cursor vs cache vs kernel) must not change strict output. FG-INV-20: witnesses are named in the authorization-precedes-observation clause — witness contents are authority-bound and must not leak hidden-element facts. Claim classes: decision-card/OPE completeness for any adaptive policy is FG-EVID-01 (logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch, fallback); witness-derived complexity regressions are benchmark/evidence class.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (projection digests, node-order profiles), w5-determinism (query-level CGSE contracts, canonical result encoding), w5-planner (plan certificate assembly), w5-replay (`ReplayManifest` slots and grade derivation), w1-foundation-types. Produces certificate content consumed by verif-differential (the same-projected-input harness) and by w8-kernels' exposure gate; feeds verif-replay-products with Prism-bearing replay bundles.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Schema gates: a Prism witness lacking projection digest, projected n/m, adapter path, numeric profile, or implementation hash is rejected at construction, with typed errors and negative fixtures per missing field. The differential harness enforces the honesty rules structurally: an attempted raw-graph-vs-filtered-projection comparison fails the harness itself, not merely the comparison. Replay tests: re-execution from a `ReplayManifest` reproduces `decision_path_blake3` and the canonical result digest under Strict mode; deleting the fnx implementation-hash artifact downgrades the derived grade attributably. Ledger folding: `EXPLAIN`/certificate surfaces expose the ledger in Full/Forensic modes; `Compact` never truncates identity fields. Property/fuzz: witness serialization round-trips; ledger merge across multi-algorithm queries preserves per-call bindings. E2e: a two-graph algorithm run yields a certificate carrying two independent projection digests; logs record ledger ids, policy, seed, and certificate mode at each stage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: witness bloat on hot paths (`Compact`/`Budgeted` modes exist for exactly this; identity fields remain mandatory); confusing raw vs projected n/m (the binding is explicitly projection-specific). Rejected: `(certificate, seq, seed)` as the replay artifact — Section 8.6 replaces it with the full `ReplayManifest`; cross-projection comparisons; treating deterministic iteration counts as floating-point identity.

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.3; Section 2.2 CGSE row; Section 8.6; Section 15.4.

title: Implement ProtectedOutput activation/disposition batches and ActivationBatch evidence
description:
## What & scope
Implement §12.8's batched delivery-plane maintenance: `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec<Role>` and `ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec<Role>`, the `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` registration, and the batch-shaped time-evidence law.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/B4: agent workloads produce floods of small protected outputs (subscription deltas per Ripple flush tick, per-statement results); activating each with its own threshold-signed time observation and maintenance entry would make the time authority the throughput ceiling. Batching amortizes to one observation and one maintenance entry per activation tick per role/group while preserving every per-record law byte-for-byte — the plan's exemplar of scaling by amortization instead of by weakening.

## Design — normative detail
Activation and disposition are batched, not per-delivery. `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec<Role>` and `ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec<Role>` are registered Protocol-plane `Maintenance` rows in `command_contracts.toml`; the disposition spec covers ACK, explicit authenticated release, profiled expiry, and successor-resume-replay installation. Each carries canonically sorted per-subject sub-records — one per distinct released record or cursor, each sub-record being exactly one arm of the singleton `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` union (Result | SubscriptionInitialBaseline | SubscriptionDelta | SubscriptionResetNotice | SubscriptionResetBaseline | ArtifactOutput | ProtectedError — plus, when §9.5's reserved freshness policy field is inhabited, the `FreshnessBreach` notice arm that the same G0-frozen registration batch adds to this union (w6-freshness); freshness-notice activations ride these same batches as ordinary sub-records), its per-member `time_evidence_ref` elided in favor of the single batch-subject evidence — with its own expected state version, authenticated receipts, `CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` bridge, or profiled expiry evidence, its remaining per-arm verification rules preserved verbatim — plus a member-completeness commitment binding the exact sorted member set. Apply is all-or-nothing: a stale, duplicated, omitted, or ineligible sub-record applies nothing; a matching retry returns the same maintenance result and protocol generation; the coordinator excludes not-yet-eligible members before proposing — the same discipline `AuditExternalResolutionBatch` applies by stopping before a not-yet-resolved Required entry while never omitting or reordering one inside its range. A single-subject operation is canonically a one-entry batch, so no second durable encoding exists — the same rule `TicketsResolvedBatch` states for one-ticket resolution. The one-current-record, at-most-one-outstanding-lease, and at-most-one-pending-output laws and the per-record CAS/immediate-predecessor retry discipline (FG-INV-15/FG-INV-16) are per-sub-record obligations, preserved unchanged: the batch transitions N protocol records in one maintenance entry exactly as `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec`'s sorted recipes transition N pending outputs. `PublishDeltaPending` likewise batches across every cursor affected by one Ripple flush tick.

Batch activation consumes batch-shaped time evidence. `time_bound_subjects.toml` registers `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch`, whose canonical pre-evidence transcript is the sorted digest set of its member lease-basis transcripts (`ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`/`SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`/`ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis`/`ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis`). One fresh challenged threshold-signed `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` per activation tick — one batched activation proposal — signs that batch subject digest, and the batch checker verifies each member's minimum-delivery-window arithmetic *individually* under the same set-shaped-subject derivation-proof pattern the registry already hosts for `OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort`; an asserted per-member window without that derivation is invalid. Challenge freshness, domain/epoch/registry-head binding, and process-incarnation freshness are preserved byte-for-byte: durable `Usable` bytes still authorize nothing after restart. `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec` consumes exactly one `TimeValidationEvidence` whose subject is the batch — never a per-member evidence set and never one evidence smeared across unrelated subjects — and the degenerate one-member batch preserves the singleton activation's per-member semantics exactly: its evidence subject is the one-member `ActivationBatch` transcript, not the bare lease-basis transcript. Deriving delivery windows from a creation epoch instead of a fresh observation is explicitly rejected: it makes windows predictable and dilutes the subject binding the challenge protocol exists to provide. Each activation arm still reauthorizes its exact released subject against the current complete security binding and current service authority before CASing that record Active; structural protocol-system authority, no recursive terminal audit gate.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 (restated): resume/ACK/release/expiry CAS one delivery version with deterministic immediate-predecessor retry; ActiveDeliverable alone owns lease/replay/send authority. FG-INV-16 (restated): no output lease is lost, duplicated, refunded, or exposed while obligated; QUERY_CANCEL/drop/disconnect/drain/process death cannot release it. Steady-state activation rates (one observation + one maintenance entry per tick per role/group) are capacity-model rows in the FG-CFG claim class (FG-CFG-04) and §17's cursor-scale gate — never invariants. All batch-spec arms and the ActivationBatch registration are G0-frozen format decisions.

## Interactions
w9-audit-release produces the `ReleasedAwaitingActivation` owners this bead activates; w9-time-authority validates the ActivationBatch subject; w10-result-machines/w10-capabilities own the delivery records and resume capabilities transitioned; w6-subscriptions produce the per-tick cursor members; perf-bench-scale prices the tick rates.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: batch transcript equals sorted member lease-basis digest set (order/duplication fuzz); one-member batch evidence subject differs from bare lease-basis subject (negative fixture). All-or-nothing: inject one stale/duplicated/omitted/ineligible member — nothing applies; matching retry idempotent. Per-member law preservation: differential test batch-of-N vs N singletons must produce identical per-record end states. Restart: durable Usable evidence refused post-restart; fresh tick required. Negative: per-member evidence set, cross-batch smeared evidence, creation-epoch-derived window — all unrepresentable/rejected. E2E with logs: one Ripple flush tick activating 1k cursors under one observation, with capacity-model prediction vs measured saturation logged (FG-CFG-04 disclosure). Detailed logging: implementation and tests log per activation tick {batch_subject_digest, member_count, sorted member lease-basis digests, observation challenge_nonce and authority_sequence, per-member window-arithmetic verdict, all-or-nothing abort cause naming the stale/duplicated/omitted/ineligible member, maintenance result and protocol generation on retry}; post-restart refusal of durable Usable bytes must appear as an explicit typed log event; the batch-of-N vs N-singletons differential compares both end states and logged transition sequences.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: per-delivery observations (throughput ceiling); creation-epoch windows (predictable, subject-dilution); weakening per-record CAS laws for batch speed. Risk: one bad member stalls a batch — mitigated by coordinator pre-exclusion of ineligible members.

## Provenance
§12.8 (972–976), §19 G0 decision batch (line 1313), §9.5 (802) FreshnessBreach arm registration, FG-CFG-04.

## Authoritative post-d96bf0f contract reconciliation

Batched cursor and artifact dispositions preserve each corrected per-subject authority, completion, and DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence rule byte-for-byte; batching cannot replace them with a generic transition.

The following current plan text is authoritative and supersedes any older rendering in this Bead:

`CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` binds the surface (`NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`), authority public commitment, role/domain/service/session/process/cursor/output kind and ID/state/sender generation, exact surface END and canonical FGP END transcript, payload/public digest, flow reservation/cost, write-start frame-time requirement-set commitment, and the matching `TransportSendObligation::Sent`; it is the channel-transport bridge into a baseline/delta/reset ACK. `EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct embedded-only `{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,output_kind_and_id,lease_identity,stream_owner_token_commitment,public_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}` and is constructible only after complete consumption plus joined borrows/tasks. `SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>` is `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment}|EmbeddedCursorOwner{stream_owner_token_commitment,host_session_generation}`; `SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>` is `ChannelSent{record_ref:StrongRef<CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}|NotApplicable`. `AuthenticatedClientSubscriptionDispositionReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,disposition_authority:SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>,completion:SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,lease_identity?,public_digest,request_nonce,action:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset|ReleaseOutstanding|CloseWithoutOutstanding,canonical_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Only the ReadyChannel arm selects a ResumeSubscriptionCursor validation row; it byte-matches the exact request, capability commitment, session, current cursor lineage, authority header, and action. ACK actions require the matching ChannelSent or EmbeddedFullyConsumed completion selected by their authority source; ReleaseOutstanding and CloseWithoutOutstanding require NotApplicable. The Embedded authority is a non-capability cursor-owner proof and cannot carry a validation ref. Receipt/action bijection is exact: AckBaseline -> `SubscriptionAckBaseline`, AckDelta -> `SubscriptionAckDelta`, AckReset -> `SubscriptionAckResetOrGap`, and ReleaseOutstanding or CloseWithoutOutstanding -> `SubscriptionClose`. Its full header/session binding must equal or be proved narrower than the active cursor/lease binding; public commitments are integrity projections only. `CloseCursor` requires `outstanding_disposition=None{receipt:CloseWithoutOutstanding}|Acknowledged{receipt:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset,completion}|Released{receipt:ReleaseOutstanding,sender_fence_and_join_proof}|ResetSuperseded{typed_gap_supersession_evidence}` and also proves the pending-output index empty or terminally disposes each remaining leaf (the one pending data output plus, when present, the standing `FreshnessBreach` notice). It atomically creates `Closed`, derives the terminal authority commitment from the last active header, disposes escrow, and tombstones capability lineage; a generic CLOSE frame, socket loss, drain, or Rust Drop cannot construct that evidence. `ExpireCursor` requires profiled expiry evidence for the exact current lease/capability/action, sender fence/join, pending-output disposition, and escrow disposition. `PostActivationCursorTransition` is the certified Local-to-Sharded transition and is legal only with no outstanding or pending Local output; it creates a new Sharded PendingInitialVisibility baseline, never a cross-role delta. No catch-all `ResetOrExpire` exists. Current/immediate-predecessor replay makes lost READY/SNAPSHOT_ACKED/ACKED/RESUMED/RESET/DISCONNECT/CLOSE replies byte-identical; anything older fails. Checkpoints, protocol snapshots, backup/configuration floors, restore, and GC preserve all cursor/pending-output/lease/replay records. Disconnect never releases.

   `ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,request_key_digest,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,canonical_output_digest,semantic_detachment_identity,nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`; `ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>` replaces the header with `terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>` and retains only terminal/public identities. `ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the exact Protocol state union `PendingVisibility{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_gate_commitment}|ReleasedAwaitingActivation{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_release_evidence,release_maintenance_ref}|ActiveDeliverable{common:ArtifactOutputActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,lease_time_basis_ref,lease_generation,capability_lineage_ref,escrow_ref,sender_generation}|Acknowledged{common:ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>,ack_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}|ReleasedUnacked{common:ArtifactOutputTerminalCommon<Role>,release_or_expiry_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}`; terminal arms retain no strong authority, manifest, lease, payload, capability replay, escrow, or predecessor edge. `ArtifactOutputDeliveryIndex<Role>` maps request and output-delivery keys to the one current record plus a compacted disposition floor. Audit visibility changes PendingVisibility only to ReleasedAwaitingActivation; independent activation supplies a fresh `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, exact time evidence, and prebuilt generation-zero `ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord`.

   `ArtifactOutputEndSendCompletionRecord<Role>` is the channel-only `{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_binding,server_process_incarnation,sender_generation,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,resume_capability_commitment,surface_terminal_frame_and_canonical_fgp_end_digest,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_output_digest,flow_reservation_identity,transport_sent_obligation_commitment,sent_completion_nonce,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. `EmbeddedArtifactOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>` is the embedded-only `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,output_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,output_owner_token_commitment,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_output_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Their construction rules are the exact channel-Sent and complete-consumption rules above; neither partial read, Drop, EOF inference, release, nor cross-surface substitution can build one.

   `ArtifactOutputDispositionAuthority<Role>` is the closed union `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment}|ReadyChannelManagementHandle{validated_management_handle_commitment}|EmbeddedOutputOwner{output_owner_token_commitment,host_session_generation}`. `ArtifactOutputDispositionCompletion<Role>` is `ChannelSent{record_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputEndSendCompletionRecord<Role>>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedArtifactOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}|NotApplicable`. `AuthenticatedClientArtifactOutputDispositionReceipt<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,authority:ArtifactOutputDispositionAuthority<Role>,completion:ArtifactOutputDispositionCompletion<Role>,output_delivery_id,expected_delivery_state_version,canonical_output_digest,action:Acknowledge|Release,canonical_request_digest,request_nonce,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Acknowledge requires either ReadyChannelResumeCapability plus ChannelSent or EmbeddedOutputOwner plus EmbeddedFullyConsumed; Release requires NotApplicable and any exact release authority arm. Only a ReadyChannelResumeCapability arm carries validation evidence, selecting `ArtifactOutputAcknowledge` or `ArtifactOutputRelease`; a management handle or embedded owner never fabricates it. `ArtifactOutputTransitionSpec<Role>` is the exact maintenance union `Resume{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,expected_active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>>,required_owner_arm:ActiveDeliverable,canonical_request_digest,prebuilt_successor_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|Acknowledge{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientArtifactOutputDispositionReceipt<Role>>,expected_active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>>,required_owner_arm:ActiveDeliverable,sender_fence_and_join_proof}|Release{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientArtifactOutputDispositionReceipt<Role>>,expected_active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>>,required_owner_arm:ActiveDeliverable,sender_fence_and_join_proof}|Expire{expected_active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>>,required_owner_arm:ActiveDeliverable,expiry_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_classification:Expired}`. The Resume ref selects `ArtifactOutputResume`; action receipts select the exact action row only in their capability arm. Each transition retains its direct or nested validation ref through successor acknowledgement or terminal receipt/tombstone resolution. Checkpoint/protocol snapshot, backup, restore, GC, and posture transitions walk both the semantic request registry and Protocol delivery index. Local/Meta payloads root only the semantic registry; `RootManifest`'s protocol state roots only the delivery index.

Implementation, tests, retained evidence, and public-surface behavior must use this exact corrected contract. No Markdown plan edit is required or authorized by this reconciliation.

title: Implement audit continuity: ticket issuance CAS, external chain, completeness gaps
description:
## What & scope
Implement §12.8's external anchor: the `AuditDomainId` lineage, the externally CAS-published `AuditContinuityRecord` chain, `AuditCompletenessProfile`, `AuditTicket` issuance and admission, and the completeness-transition (gap) protocol.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: compliance audit must be a separately retained, signed append-only chain — not 'whatever commit history remains'. Anchoring ticket issuance in an external monotonic authority means a compromised or rolled-back server cannot silently un-issue a ticket: gaps become permanent, detectable facts. The claim is scoped honestly: signatures, sequence continuity, and anchoring prove append integrity and post-ticket gap/truncation detection — not that a buggy ingress could never omit an event before logging.

## Design — normative detail
Each same-identity lineage has a stable `AuditDomainId`. An external monotonic authority CAS-publishes reference-free `AuditContinuityRecord {database_security_namespace_id,audit_domain_id,audit_epoch,highest_ticket_sequence,ticket_index_commitment,unresolved_ticket_commitment,audit_chain_head_digest,predecessor_digest,external_registry_id,cas_version,status:Complete{profile_oid}|PermanentGap{latest_transition_bytes_and_digest,current_profile_oid},last_transition:TicketIssued{ticket_digest}|TicketsResolvedBatch{role_and_group,first_pipeline_order,last_pipeline_order,batch_digest,ordered_resolution_commitment,last_candidate_root_digest}|CompletenessChanged{transition_bytes_and_digest},signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`, while the database retains authenticated ticket/event/resolution/transition/CAS-receipt bytes or authenticated resolver references — never commitments alone. A one-ticket resolution is canonically a `TicketsResolvedBatch` with a one-entry range; `TicketResolved` is not a second durable encoding. The record contains no StrongRef, consumer-local locator, or future receipt identity; the batch arm is one atomic direct CAS successor, legal only for a nonempty contiguous role-pipeline range whose individually verified entries appear in canonical order. An `AuditCompletenessProfile` names which operations require an externally reserved `AuditTicket {database_security_namespace_id,audit_domain_id,cluster_incarnation_provenance,tenant,principal_scope,ticket_sequence,event_class,request_digest,completeness_profile_oid,issued_at,sequencer_epoch,signature}` before protected processing. Issuance first CAS-adds the pending ticket externally, then orders its local import through exact `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec {ticket_ref,expected_prior_continuity_ref,expected_prior_cas_version,returned_continuity_ref,external_cas_receipt_ref}`; admission verifies the returned record/receipt are the direct `TicketIssued` successor, advance the ticket sequence by exactly one, add exactly this ticket to the ticket-index and unresolved commitments, and change no unrelated continuity field; orphan-ticket recovery uses the same relation. Protected processing begins only after the imported admission is audit-visible. Gap resumption builds reference-free portable `AuditCompletenessTransitionRequest {audit_domain_id,expected_prior_continuity_digest,expected_prior_cas_version,exact_missing_ticket_or_event_interval,missing_commitment,evidence_or_reason,old/new profile identities and digests,permanent_effective_audit_epoch,authorization_bytes_and_digest,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,canonical_request_digest,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`, owned pre-send by local `AuditCompletenessTransitionOperationRecord<Role>` (proving every portable identity/digest against its typed owner); only after role-valid publication evidence may universal dispatch send it; the authority CAS-installs the direct `CompletenessChanged` successor and emits a separate reference-free `AuditExternalCasReceipt`; `AuditCompletenessTransitionSpec<Role>` (with `terminal_audit_gate:StructurallyInapplicable{AuditSystemAuthority}`) imports the exact pair through the same pipeline rules. The continuity status and future profile validator permanently exclude the recorded gap; no later operator, restore, or profile change may reassert completeness across it. Semantic payload admission state plus protocol pipelines/outcomes, snapshots, configuration/GC/key floors, and backups retain the complete active chain and authenticated external locators; same-identity restore reconciles before ticket-gated operations resume. Only events admitted through this gate receive a source-completeness claim within the trusted-process threat model; unticketed/sampled read telemetry is labeled non-complete.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08 (restated clause): external resolution batches are direct continuity successors over exactly one gap-free prefix. FG-INV-20: W12 registration claims operation/statement tickets before observation. The completeness claim itself is a scoped evidence claim (trusted-process threat model); per-tenant ticket-resolution latency is an `slo.toml` surface; the issuance CAS is one of the three Required-operation authority touches disclosed in the footprint table (w9-authority-surface).

## Interactions
Feeds w9-audit-protected-orders (tickets claimed by construction orders), w9-audit-pipeline (unresolved commitments drive Required entries), w9-audit-release (batch resolution advances this chain); w2-root-bootstrap retains chain heads in manifest floors; w11-backup/w11-restore carry the chain; w9-authority-surface publishes its availability posture; succession events (w9-authority-surface) extend this chain's lineage rules.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Model: CAS chain no-fork lineage verification (shared with §15.2 authority-chain checking, verif-oracles). Crash matrix: external CAS success + local crash before import (orphan recovery); import applied but not visible (processing must not start). Negative: duplicate `TicketResolved` encoding rejected; admission with wrong prior cas_version, sequence advance != 1, or mutated unrelated field fails; completeness reassertion across a recorded gap fails permanently. E2E with logs: issue -> admit -> make visible -> process; then force a gap, run the completeness transition against a simulated authority, and assert the permanent `PermanentGap` status and refused reassertion. Detailed logging: every issuance/admission/resolution/transition logs {audit_domain_id, audit_epoch, ticket_sequence, expected/returned cas_version, prior/returned continuity head digests, per-check admission verdict (direct-successor, sequence-advance-by-one, ticket-index/unresolved commitment inclusion, unrelated-field stability), orphan-recovery outcome, gap interval and permanent_effective_audit_epoch on completeness transitions, refused-reassertion reason}; logs carry digests/commitments only, and the e2e script must reconstruct and verify the external CAS lineage from the logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: audit as residual commit history; commitments-only retention (authenticated bytes/resolvers required); claiming ingress-omission immunity. Risk: strictly serial one-at-a-time issuance CAS is a throughput ceiling for Required profiles — disclosed in the governance bench profile, amortized only at resolution (batching), never at issuance.

## Provenance
§12.8 (944–948, 984–986), App A 2631, §16 item 8.

### Fidelity addendum — retained audit segment/index/checkpoint schemas
The durable audit closure includes four exact families. `AuditCloneBoundary` is `{source_database_security_namespace_id,source_audit_domain_id,source_continuity_head_digest,target_database_security_namespace_id,target_audit_domain_id,clone_manifest_ref,retained_source_evidence_contract,source_signatures,target_signatures}` and never rewrites a source ticket into the target domain. `AuditSegment` is a contiguous signed range `{audit_domain_id,first_ticket_sequence,last_ticket_sequence,previous_chain_digest,ordered_ticket_resolution_event_records,redaction_profile_oid,signing_epoch,external_anchor_ref,segment_body_digest,canonical_signature_set}`. Range order is gap-free and its first predecessor/last head byte-match the continuity chain.

`AuditTicketIndex` maps every issued ticket exactly once to `Pending{ticket_ref,admission_import_ref,external_issue_receipt_ref}|Resolved{ticket_ref,event_ref,resolution_ref,external_batch_receipt_ref,local_visibility_import_status}` and retains event, external receipt, and local import status across recovery; no issued ticket is absent or multiply resolved. `AuditCheckpoint` commits `{audit_domain_id,retained_ticket_floor,retained_event_floor,ticket_index_root,ticket_chain_head,event_chain_head,unresolved_ticket_set_commitment,continuity_or_gap_head,signer_rotation_chain_commitment,external_anchor_ref,checkpoint_generation,body_digest,signatures}`. Missing external evidence disables completeness-gated work and can only enter the explicit PermanentGap protocol; it never weakens the profile silently.

Unit/golden/property tests cover segment contiguity/signatures, ticket pending-or-unique-resolution bijection, checkpoint floor monotonicity, signer rotation, anchors, clone domain separation, backup/restore, and gap transitions. E2E issues tickets across a segment/checkpoint boundary, crashes before and after external batch CAS/local import, restores, and proves the same unresolved/resolved set. Logs emit domain/segment/checkpoint commitments, ticket ranges/counts, unresolved count, continuity CAS versions, signer epoch, anchor commitment, clone boundary source/target commitments, and completeness status; tenant/principal/event contents remain protected.

### Fidelity correction — exact completeness-transition dispatch owner and import protocol
The following plan clauses are embedded verbatim to retain the complete role-bound pre-send owner, portable receipt, apply relation, and permanent-gap semantics:
Resumption first builds reference-free portable `AuditCompletenessTransitionRequest {audit_domain_id,expected_prior_continuity_digest,expected_prior_cas_version,exact_missing_ticket_or_event_interval,missing_commitment,evidence_or_reason,old_profile_identity_and_digest,new_profile_identity_and_digest,permanent_effective_audit_epoch,authorization_bytes_and_digest,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,canonical_request_digest,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. Local `AuditCompletenessTransitionOperationRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the pre-send owner `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,portable_request_ref:StrongRef<AuditCompletenessTransitionRequest>,expected_prior_continuity_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,old_profile_ref:StrongRef<AuditCompletenessProfile>,new_profile_ref:StrongRef<AuditCompletenessProfile>,authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,external_dispatch_operation_recipe,body_digest}` and proves every portable identity/digest against its typed owner. Only after its role-valid publication evidence may universal dispatch send the portable request. The external authority CAS-installs the direct `CompletenessChanged` successor that embeds only the portable transition bytes/digest, then emits a separate reference-free `AuditExternalCasReceipt`.

`AuditCompletenessTransitionSpec<Role>` is `{operation_record_ref:StrongRef<AuditCompletenessTransitionOperationRecord<Role>>,expected_prior_continuity_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,expected_prior_cas_version,returned_continuity_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,external_cas_receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalCasReceipt>,dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref,exact_request_returned_head_receipt_and_profile_match_digest,terminal_audit_gate:StructurallyInapplicable{AuditSystemAuthority}}`; it imports that exact pair locally through the same pipeline rules. This order is acyclic: no portable pre-CAS object owns a local reference and no continuity record points to its later receipt or import. The continuity status and future profile validator permanently exclude the recorded gap; no later operator, restore, or profile change may reassert completeness across it. Semantic payload admission state plus protocol pipelines/outcomes, snapshots, configuration/GC/key floors, and backups retain the complete active chain and authenticated external locators. Same-identity restore reconciles it before ticket-gated operations resume. Only events admitted through this gate receive a source-completeness claim within the trusted-process threat model. Unticketed/sampled read telemetry is labeled non-complete.

Unit and construction-DAG tests must expand `AuditCompletenessTransitionOperationRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` for each legal authority-owning role, prove its full AuthorityBoundHeader and referenced owners byte-match the portable request, and reject send-before-publication, wrong prior CAS, alternate successor, future receipt refs, role substitution, or any attempt to restore completeness across the gap. The E2E simulated-authority scenario emits ordered pre-send-owner/publication/dispatch/CAS-receipt/import/visibility events with public commitments and replay commands only.
acceptance_criteria:
### A21 exact pre-admission audit-format ownership

This bead is the unique implementation owner for AuditCompletenessProfile; AuditRequirementDecisionRecord<Local|Meta>; AuditCoverageClaimRef; NonRequiredAuditEvidence and all ProfileExempt, CoveredByParentClaim, and LifecycleScaffolding arms; LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired; StructuralAuditExemption; AuthorizationAuditGate; ImportedNonRequiredAuditEvidence; ImportedOperationAuditAdmissionEvidence; ImportedStatementAuditAdmissionEvidence; and ImportedReadAuditEvidence. It owns concrete role/domain expansions, stable rows/tags, canonical codecs and decision/profile/body transcripts, same-domain and imported-projection validators, construction-DAG rules, lifecycle-scaffolding eligibility matrix, negative owner/field-tag/profile/epoch/policy/revocation substitutions, golden/cross-version/mutation/fuzz tests, and redacted diagnostics. fgdb-w9-audit-protected-orders-v1d9 remains the unique owner of TerminalAuditGate and terminal signing objects; W2/W12 only consume the exact Local/Meta/Shard admission projections and may not define aliases or opaque-digest substitutes.

title: Build the applied-vs-visible audit pipeline: gap proofs, security barrier, backpressure
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Semantic side of the two-plane audit architecture: the bounded ordered `AuditVisibilityPipeline`, its entries and gap proofs, the applied-vs-visible split, the no-leapfrog law, deterministic backpressure, and the v1 security-barrier rule. (The Protocol release plane — batches, advance spec, activation — is w9-audit-release.)

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: a Required-audit database must keep *ordering* available even when the external audit authority stalls — so applied semantic state may run ahead of visible state, but only through one rooted, gap-free, linear pipeline that can never lie about what was released.
