This bead is the unique implementation owner for the sole AuthorizationLease schema referenced by Appendix A: the exact §14.3 signed record with consensus_domain, issuer and authority leader identity/term, security leader epoch, lease generation, source token or capability commitment, token_id, AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>, ReadOnly operation class, snapshot interval, exact role-bearing read bindings, query-operator disclosure scope, answer-contract ceiling, time-authority profile and closed-open window, signer identity/key/epoch, and signature. It owns the stable rows/tags, canonical signed transcript, role expansion, binding and nonwidening validation, restart/rotation/substitution goldens and mutation/fuzz corpus, and redacted diagnostics. fgdb-w11-read-contracts-g2u consumes this exact lease for read paths; it may not define an inferred extension or alias. fgdb-w9-time-authority-0rv6 owns TimeValidationEvidence and freshness guards.

title: Implement the time authority: profiles, observations, TimeValidationEvidence, use guards
description:
## What & scope
Implement the external time authority plane: `AuthorityInstant`/`AuthorityInterval` arithmetic, the immutable `TimeAuthorityProfile`, challenged `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation`s, role-local `TimeAuthorityObservationImport`, the `time_bound_subjects.toml` registry, `TimeValidationEvidence` with its three classifications, the linear `TimeUseGuard`, the generated window schemas, and the `TimeAuthorityRegistry` steady-state contract. Rotation/closing/fence/drain machinery is split to w9-time-rotation.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: FrankenGraphDB never trusts ambient wall-clock time for any canonical decision — every expiry, lease window, and delivery window is derived from fresh, challenged, threshold-signed external evidence with checked arithmetic. This is what lets capability expiry, key-destruction windows, and delivery leases be *claims* rather than hopes, and what keeps time-authority failure off the audit prefix (fail-closed delivery, never blocked ordering). Agent deployments (B6) rely on short-lived leases; a forgeable or replayed clock would be a privilege-escalation primitive.

## Design — normative detail
`AuthorityInstant` is `{time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick:u128}`, comparable only within one domain/epoch; windows are closed-open (`not_before <= true_authority_time < expires_at`). `AuthorityInterval` is `{earliest,latest}` with byte-identical domain/epoch and `earliest.tick <= latest.tick`; intervals from different domains/epochs are never ordered, intersected, or bridged by scalar conversion. `TimeAuthorityProfile` is the immutable threshold-signed `{schema_version,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick_scale,external_registry_id,ordered_signers[{signer_id,key_id,verification_key}],threshold,maximum_source_uncertainty_ticks,maximum_challenge_round_trip_ticks,maximum_guard_use_ticks,comparison_semantics:ClosedOpen,unavailable_policy:FailClosed,predecessor_profile_digest?,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` is reference-free: `{profile_oid,profile_digest,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,challenge_nonce,subject_digest,intended_use_digest,authority_sequence,possible_time_interval,external_registry_head_digest,external_registry_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` — it never claims process-local send/receive counters. `LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness` is the nonportable `{process_incarnation_id,challenge_nonce,send_monotonic_tick,receive_monotonic_tick,checked_elapsed_ticks,monotonic_source_profile_id,conversion_to_authority_uncertainty_ticks,body_digest}`. `TimeAuthorityObservationImport` is the closed role union `Local|Meta|Shard` (Shard resolves via `ShardTimeAuthorityProjection`, a certified Meta projection installed only through the exact contiguous ActiveMetaProjectionRoot time-authority slot); import verifies portable profile identity/digest, current registry or certified projection, role/group/configuration/fence, same-nonce local round trip, interval, subject, intended use, and signatures. Replay, wrong profile/domain/epoch, noncurrent registry head, excessive round trip/uncertainty, process-incarnation mismatch, role substitution, or signature failure makes it unusable.

`time_bound_subjects.toml` is the single exhaustive source of the closed `TimeBoundSubject` union: each row names one concrete durable schema or exact capability variant, its canonical pre-evidence transcript recipe, profile/window field tags, legal intended uses, evidence owner, expiry/retirement transition, and retention floor; raw refs, generic object/capability arms, and overlapping transcripts are forbidden. The v1 arms are exactly: `TxnOutcomeCapabilityBytes, ResumeSubscriptionCapabilityBytes, ResumeBufferedResultCapabilityBytes, ResumeArtifactOutputCapabilityBytes, MergeOutcomeCapabilityBytes, ReadYourWritesCapabilityBytes, MacaroonTokenBytes, OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort, MutationPermitRecord, ReadPermitRecord, AuthorizationLease, TxnOwnershipLease, PrivacyExecutionLease, ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis, SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis, ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis, ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis, ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis, TxnOutcomeLookupWindow, FollowerLeaseRead, IdRangeLease, ShardIdRangeLease, ClusterIncarnationLease, PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow, RestoreSourceLeaseRecordLocal, RestoreSourceLeaseRecordMeta, ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection, NewDatabaseIdentityReservation, ServiceVisibilityEpochReservation, AllocationEpochReservation, ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline, ReplayArchiveRecord, ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow, ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow, KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow, BackupPublicationFreshness, BackupTransparencyFreshness, TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis, CrossLogTransparencyFreshness, PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis, VerifierKeyWindow, IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow` (aliases like `FollowerReadLease` are unregistered) — plus the set-shaped batch subject `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch`, which §12.8 registers in this same `time_bound_subjects.toml`: its canonical pre-evidence transcript is the sorted digest set of its member lease-basis transcripts (`ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`/`SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`/`ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis`/`ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis`), its consuming machinery is w9-activation-batching, and the registry's two-way total generation check must count this arm even though App A 2163's narrative arm list predates it. Window names are generated exact schemas with the common prefix `{subject_kind,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,subject_body_digest,intended_use_set,owner_plane_and_slot,body_digest}` plus subject-specific closed suffixes (App A enumerates all fourteen); no lifetime/duration/counter-arithmetic expiry field exists.

`TimeValidationEvidence` is `{profile_ref,observation_import_ref,subject:TimeBoundSubject,intended_use_digest,classification:Usable{not_before,expires_at,validated_process_incarnation_id,guard_deadline_local_monotonic_tick}|NotYetValid{not_before}|Expired{expires_at},validator_version,validation_digest}`. `Usable` exists only when `possible_time_interval.earliest >= not_before`, the round-trip witness belongs to the current process incarnation, and `checked_add(possible_time_interval.latest.tick, maximum_guard_use_ticks)` succeeds and is `< expires_at`. `NotYetValid` only when `latest < not_before`; `Expired` only when `earliest >= expires_at` and is durable across restart. Boundary-overlapping intervals yield the uniform retryable `TimeAuthorityUnavailable` before any protected lookup or disclosure; all tick arithmetic is checked and never wraps. A successful Usable validation creates a linear nonserializable `TimeUseGuard` bound to observation, subject, intended action, process incarnation, and remaining monotonic budget, consumed immediately before the protected step; it cannot survive restart, over-budget suspend, clone, serialization, or replay. Durable Usable bytes authorize nothing after restart. Ordered expiry/release/tombstone/retirement transitions must retain the exact durable evidence — a scalar deadline never changes canonical state. Generation performs a two-way total check: every active `durable_fields.toml` time-bearing field set has exactly one nonoverlapping subject row and vice versa.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 clause: expiry can only order the registered rollback/status-safe path; leases and windows are obligations that reach one legal terminal. FG-INV-07 clause: every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root — transcripts bind pre-evidence bodies, never objects that embed the evidence. Per-posture time-authority availability numbers are `slo.toml` rows; the per-tick observation rate is priced by FG-CFG-04 (maintenance-stream capacity model), not an invariant.

## Interactions
w1-crypto supplies threshold-signature verification; w2-root-bootstrap supplies the manifest/slot publication the imports bind; every w9 sibling consumes `TimeValidationEvidence` (w9-activation-batching consumes the `ActivationBatch` subject; w9-threat-tokens consumes `MacaroonTokenBytes`/cohort arms; w9-key-lifecycle consumes destruction observation windows); w10-capabilities and w11-read-contracts consume capability/lease arms; w9-time-rotation extends this bead with the rotation machinery.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: interval comparison rejects cross-domain/epoch mixing; checked arithmetic overflow yields `TimeAuthorityUnavailable`; Usable/NotYetValid/Expired existence conditions are exhaustively property-tested at boundaries. Fuzz: observation decoder with mutated signatures/nonces/heads. Negative: replayed nonce, stale registry head, wrong incarnation, role substitution, alias subject names, suffix-without-prefix window — all rejected with typed errors. Crash matrix: restart between validation and guard consumption must force a fresh observation/import/evidence. E2E script: mint profile, serve challenged observations from a simulated authority, validate a `ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`, consume the guard, restart, and log (structured, per-step) that the durable Usable bytes are refused. CI: two-way total registry check against `durable_fields.toml`. Detailed logging: every observation/import/validation/guard event logs {profile_oid, time_domain_id/authority_epoch, challenge_nonce, authority_sequence, possible_time_interval bounds, checked round-trip and uncertainty ticks, subject kind and transcript digest, intended_use_digest, classification outcome with its exact failing condition, guard creation/consumption/deadline, TimeAuthorityUnavailable cause (overflow/boundary-overlap/domain mismatch)}; the restart test asserts the refusal event names the stale process incarnation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: TrueTime-class infrastructure (§3.4 item h) — HLC plus consensus-fenced contracts covers ordering; the time authority exists solely for absolute-time windows. Rejected: deriving windows from creation epochs (predictable, dilutes challenge subject binding); process-local clocks as authority (monotonic time measures only challenge/use age). Risk: authority round-trip on hot paths — bounded by `maximum_challenge_round_trip_ticks` and amortized by batch subjects (w9-activation-batching).

## Provenance
App A time-authority rows (2153–2166, 2171–2173, 2175 steady-state), §12.8 activation tick, §16 item 8.

title: Implement exact time-authority handoff, registry CAS, and profile activation
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact cross-authority time-profile handoff and activation protocol: role-specific drain-floor sets, inventory closure, dual-signed transition plan, universal-dispatch registry CAS/receipt, transition record, and ordered Local/Meta activation with certified Shard participation.

## Why
Time-profile rotation is a distributed authority transfer, not a config flip. Old and new clocks cannot be compared by raw ticks; every group must stop issuance, drain reservations, fence offline issuers, close the old subject inventory, retain verifier dependencies, and prove one dual-signed succession before successor issuance.

## Design — exact normative contract
`RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the generated exact union `Local{current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,joint_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>?,prospective_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>?,config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>,root_manifest_and_slot_cut,configuration_set_digest}|Meta{current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,joint_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>?,prospective_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>?,meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,global_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,exact_current_and_prospective_shard_configuration_commitment,root_manifest_and_slot_cut,configuration_set_digest}`. Every configuration proposal, joint-state transition, retirement floor, topology change, and role transition consults a live ClosingRequested/IssuanceClosing/IssuanceQuiescent/Draining hold and must preserve the exact current-plus-prospective group closure or wait. V1 categorically forbids Local-to-Sharded role transition while any time profile is ClosingRequested, IssuanceClosing, IssuanceQuiescent, or Draining. The profile must first reach Retired or return to the unchanged ActiveForIssuance state through the legal pre-send abort; no migration-proof exception exists in v1.

Activation and retirement floors are deliberately different. `RoleTimeAuthorityDrainFloorSet<Role>` is `Local{checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>,drain_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Local>>}|Meta{global_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRecoveryCheckpoint>,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,meta_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConfigPayloadFloor>,drain_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Meta>>,exact_sorted_shard_quiescence_and_inventory_certificate_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardTimeBoundSubjectInventoryCertificate>]}`. `ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementFloor` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,transition_id,shard_id,retiring_profile_oid,inventory_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeBoundSubjectInventoryCertificate>,retirement_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof>,retained_profile_verifier_and_offline_issuer_dependencies,retain_through:AuthorityInstant,configuration_checkpoint_and_root_slot_cut,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`; it is built after the proof, while the proof names only the precomputed floor body digest. `RoleTimeAuthorityRetirementFloorSet<Role>` is `Local{checkpoint_ref,configuration_ref,config_payload_floor_ref,shutdown_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityShutdownReceipt>,verifier_retirement_floor_ref:StrongRef<VerifierKeyRetirementFloor>,retirement_proof_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof<Local>>}|Meta{global_checkpoint_ref,configuration_ref,meta_config_payload_floor_ref,shutdown_receipt_ref,verifier_retirement_floor_ref,retirement_proof_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof<Meta>>,exact_sorted_shard_retirement_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementAck>]}`. Role-invalid arms are uninhabited.
The cross-authority handoff is deliberately split. Portable pre-CAS `TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionPlan` is `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=TimeAuthorityRegistryTransition},transition_id,rotation_intent_digest,predecessor_profile_oid_and_digest,successor_profile_oid_and_digest,issuance_closing_receipt_digest,issuance_fence_digest,subject_inventory_closure_digest,drain_hold_digest,predecessor_external_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,old_final_challenged_interval:AuthorityInterval,new_initial_challenged_interval:AuthorityInterval,old_observation_service_and_verification_key_live_through:AuthorityInstant,successor_activation_not_before:AuthorityInstant,maximum_old_subject_expiry:AuthorityInstant,old_and_new_signer_set_epochs,dual_signed_handoff_transcript,old_threshold_signatures,new_threshold_signatures}`. Each interval is internally same-domain/same-epoch; the transcript relates the two authorities without comparing ticks. The registry CAS runs through the intent-owned universal dispatch and returns portable `TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionReceipt {external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=TimeAuthorityRegistryTransition},transition_id,plan_digest,prior_head_digest,prior_cas_version,returned_head_digest,returned_cas_version,returned_active_profile_oid,old_signer_set_epoch,new_signer_set_epoch,old_signature_set,new_signature_set}`. `PortableTimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionTerminalEvidence` is the reference-free `{external_request_binding,transition_id,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,canonical_full_request_digest,dispatch_attempt_generation,source_gate_publication_commitment,status_lineage,terminal_disposition:Applied{receipt_digest,returned_head_digest,returned_cas_version}|AlreadyApplied{receipt_digest,returned_head_digest,returned_cas_version},provider_counter,signatures}`. Status-first recovery and exact idempotency are mandatory. Local `TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role,completion_authority:TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,original_admin_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,plan_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionPlan>,registry_dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionTerminalEvidence>,receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionReceipt>,predecessor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_fence_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>,subject_inventory_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>>,drain_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>>,configuration_retention_basis:RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role>,drain_floor_set:RoleTimeAuthorityDrainFloorSet<Role>,plan_and_receipt_byte_match_digest,body_digest}`.

The mandatory order is every-group admission freeze -> ordered and audit-visible Local/Meta rotation intent -> universal-dispatch external issuance close -> ordered Local/Meta close plus certified Shard close applies -> every-group reservation drain and quiescence closure -> every offline issuer fence -> universal-dispatch final issuance fence -> post-fence Local or Meta-plus-all-shards inventory closure -> drain hold -> dual-signed handoff plan -> universal-dispatch external registry CAS/receipt -> ordered Local/Meta transition -> successor issuance. Before any close send, typed abort may reopen the exact unchanged freezes. From `SentUnknown` close onward, and especially after the final fence, only structural roll-forward authority exists. Every old-profile subject has a finite checked expiry no later than the derived drain bound. Renewable leases/grants move to the successor before their old window ends; immutable capabilities and attenuated offline tokens remain verifiable under the old profile until expiry.

Exact activation is `TimeAuthorityProfileTransitionSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> {completion_authority:TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,original_admin_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,expected_time_authority_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,expected_registry_generation,expected_selected_profile_state:IssuanceQuiescent,retiring_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_closing_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt>,issuance_fence_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>,epoch_transition_plan_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionPlan>,external_registry_transition_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionReceipt>,epoch_transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,old_profile_subject_inventory_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>>,old_observation_and_verifier_retention_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>>,configuration_retention_basis:RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role>,drain_floor_set:RoleTimeAuthorityDrainFloorSet<Role>,terminal_audit_gate}`. It verifies the complete intent/dispatch/closing/quiescence/fence/inventory bijection and atomically selects the successor for new issuance while retaining the predecessor as Draining. Completion cannot widen the original authorization, change the successor, sets, operation IDs, or resources, or solicit a fresh client choice after the irreversible fence.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-10, FG-INV-16, and every operation using TimeValidationEvidence. Depends on the base time authority, rotation admission/freeze machine, irreversible dispatch, audit visibility, configuration retention, and role-exact authority bindings. Membership, restore, Local-to-Sharded conversion, topology, key/capability retirement, and backup floors consume its transition/drain evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas, codecs, registry rows, construction DAGs, and floor walkers exist for every named plan/receipt/evidence/record/spec and role-valid floor arm.
- Unit/golden tests freeze dual-signed transcript bytes, interval-domain rules, operation IDs, head/CAS succession, inventory commitments, role arms, and activation result.
- Property/model tests prove mandatory order, no successor issuance early, no cross-domain tick comparison, byte-identical retry, no authorization widening after fence, and complete old-subject coverage.
- Fuzz/mutation rejects wrong transition, signer epoch, head, profile, role/group, configuration, shard set, inventory, interval, dispatch contract, and stale generation.
- DPOR/crash E2E pauses at every freeze/close/fence/inventory/plan/send/status/import/order/visibility/activation boundary across Local and three-member Meta+Shard configurations; recovery rolls forward from SentUnknown and never silently reopens.
- JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,transition_id,phase,old_profile,new_profile,registry_head_digest,cas_version,dispatch_attempt_generation,inventory_digest,drain_floor_digest,configuration_digest,shard_ack_count,activation_position,recovery_action,replay_command}; secret authority material is excluded.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: wall-clock comparison, config-only switch, fresh client choice after final fence, bare signed head without local published operation, and role-erased inventories. Unavailable external authority blocks activation safely.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 2197-2199 and 2211-2215; section 12.10.

title: Implement exact time-profile retirement, expiry attestations, and verifier floors
description:
## What & scope
Implement time-profile retirement after activation: complete subject disposition bijections, canonical and restore-prebootstrap expiry evidence, observation-service shutdown, verifier/offline-issuer retention floors, Shard retirement acknowledgements, compact terminal summary, and release of heavy authority/hold closure only after audit visibility and cuts.

## Why
Activation does not make the old authority disposable. Long-lived capabilities, leases, restore artifacts, offline issuers, checkpoints, configurations, and Shards may still require the old verifier. Premature retirement makes valid subjects unverifiable; permanent strong retention leaks authority indefinitely.

## Design — exact normative contract

`ShardTimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof` is `{transition_id,shard_inventory_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Shard>>,sorted_dispositions[TimeSubjectDisposition<Shard>],inventory_disposition_bijection_commitment,no_live_old_profile_subject_proof,precomputed_retirement_floor_body_digest,checker_version,proof_digest}` and contains no future floor or ack. `TimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,current_inventory_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role>>,sorted_dispositions[TimeSubjectDisposition<Role>],inventory_disposition_bijection_commitment,no_post_fence_root_subject_proof,configured_shard_retirement_ack_commitment,checker_version,proof_digest}`.

Retirement compacts its proof closure at the visibility boundary. `TimeSubjectTerminalProjection` is the reference-free closed arm `Terminal{subject_key,subject_body_and_profile_digest,typed_terminal_evidence_identity_and_digest,terminal_authority_commitment}|Expired{subject_key,subject_body_and_profile_digest,portable_expiry_attestation_identity_and_digest,terminal_authority_commitment}|Reissued{old_subject_key,old_body_and_profile_digest,successor_subject_key_and_public_commitment,nonwidening_proof_digest,old_identity_tombstone_digest}`. `TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role_and_group,transition_id,retired_profile_identity_and_digest,successor_profile_identity_and_digest,terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,rotation_intent_digest,close_fence_registry_operation_and_terminal_evidence_commitment,transition_plan_and_receipt_digest,transition_record_digest,retirement_operation_and_applied_identity,shutdown_receipt_and_verifier_floor_commitment,configuration_and_shard_floor_commitment,sorted_subject_terminal_projections[TimeSubjectTerminalProjection],inventory_to_terminal_projection_bijection_commitment,zero_live_old_profile_subject_commitment,retired_at_registry_generation,body_digest}`. It is built as the retirement command's compact result before the successor payload/root, contains no live authority header and no strong edge to the intent, transition record, inventory, dispositions, subjects, drain hold, dispatch attempts, or administrative decision, and cannot authorize validation or issuance. Detailed retirement inputs remain rooted only through the retirement command's audit-visibility and activated-cut floors; once those floors close, the registry retains solely this summary and the separately required public transparency/audit commitments.

`PortableTimeExpiryAttestation` is the signed, reference-free canonical-role form `{origin:CanonicalRole,subject_kind,subject_identity_and_body_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,expires_at:AuthorityInstant,challenged_observation_digest,observation_interval:AuthorityInterval,validation_digest,intended_terminal_action_digest,external_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It is emitted only after durable local `TimeValidationEvidence::Expired`; a same-role import record retains that evidence and proves byte equality. External receipts/certificates use only this portable attestation, never a local `StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>`.

The pre-first-root restore machine has distinct exact artifacts. `PreBootstrapTimeValidationEvidence` is `{restore_id,journal_id,prebootstrap_time_basis_digest,subject_kind,subject_identity_and_body_digest,portable_observation_bytes_and_digest,local_challenge_round_trip_witness,profile_domain_epoch_and_window,intended_action_digest,result:Usable|Expired{proof_observation_interval_earliest_gte_expires_at},journal_head_and_generation,mac_under_k_restore_journal}`. `PreBootstrapPortableTimeExpiryAttestation` is the reference-free signed `{origin:RestorePreBootstrap,restore_id,journal_id,subject_kind,subject_identity_and_body_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,expires_at,challenged_observation_digest,observation_interval,prebootstrap_validation_evidence_digest,intended_terminal_action_digest,prebootstrap_time_basis_digest,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It is emitted only after the matching MAC-authenticated Expired artifact is journal-authority durable. Neither prebootstrap type decodes as canonical `TimeValidationEvidence`/`PortableTimeExpiryAttestation`, and neither authorizes post-bootstrap time use.

`TimeAuthorityShutdownReceipt` is the portable signed `{transition_id,retiring_profile_oid,observation_service_id,served_through:AuthorityInstant,shutdown_after:AuthorityInstant,final_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,shutdown_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `VerifierKeyRetirementFloor` is `{transition_id,retiring_profile_oid,sorted_verifier_and_offline_issuer_key_dependencies,zero_live_subject_dependency_commitment,retain_through:AuthorityInstant,shutdown_receipt_digest,configuration_and_checkpoint_floor_commitment,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementAck` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,transition_id,shard_id,retiring_profile_oid,inventory_certificate_identity,zero_live_old_profile_subject_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof>,installed_retirement_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeAuthorityRetirementFloor>,post_apply_root_and_slot_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`.


Exact retirement is `TimeAuthorityProfileRetirementSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> {cleanup_authority:TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority<Role>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,expected_time_authority_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,expected_registry_generation,epoch_transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,retiring_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,complete_current_root_subject_scan_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role>>,sorted_subject_dispositions[TimeSubjectDisposition<Role>],complete_subject_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TimeBoundSubjectRetirementProof<Role>>,old_observation_service_shutdown_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityShutdownReceipt>,old_verifier_key_retirement_floor_ref:StrongRef<VerifierKeyRetirementFloor>,configuration_retention_basis:RoleConfigurationRetentionBasis<Role>,retirement_floor_set:RoleTimeAuthorityRetirementFloorSet<Role>,terminal_summary_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`. Every inventory row appears exactly once. Meta's retirement floor set contains one matching ack from every configured shard. Apply first verifies the heavy closure, deterministically creates `TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>`, selects `Retired{terminal_summary_ref}`, and releases the drain hold only after shutdown, zero-dependency verifier/offline-issuer floors, shard floors, and paired all-plane/configuration floors are durable. The detailed proof/transition/admin-authority closure survives until the retirement candidate is audit-visible and its cut activates, then becomes collectible; no terminal state indefinitely retains completion or cleanup authority. Activation/retirement, issuance closing/reservations/quiescence, compaction, and every failure boundary are permanent registry/model/DPOR gates.

## Invariants & interactions
Consumes the handoff transition, base time authority, universal dispatch, audit release, role configuration floors, and restore prebootstrap journal types. Restore lease/acquisition, membership, conversion, topology, backup, capability expiry, and decoder/key retirement depend on these exact floors and portable attestations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows exist for every subject projection, proof, attestation, shutdown receipt, verifier floor, Shard ack, retirement spec, and compact terminal summary.
- Unit/golden tests freeze canonical versus prebootstrap noninterchangeable encodings, every terminal projection arm, body digests, and reference-strength rules.
- Property/model tests prove inventory-to-disposition bijection, zero live dependencies, no post-fence subjects, complete Shard set, heavy-closure release only after visibility/cut, and terminal summary nonauthorization.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects wrong origin plane, subject/profile/window, transition, shutdown head, verifier dependency, Shard/configuration, missing/duplicate disposition, and canonical/prebootstrap substitution.
- E2E retires profiles with active result/cursor/restore/capability subjects, reissues or expires each, restarts at every boundary, shuts down authority, installs floors/acks, compacts details, and verifies old binaries/subjects behave exactly as promised.
- JSONL emits {event_version,transition_id,role_and_group,subject_kind,subject_key_digest,disposition,expiry_origin?,inventory_digest,proof_digest,shutdown_counter?,verifier_floor_digest?,shard_ack_count,retirement_state,terminal_summary_digest?,cut_state,recovery_action,replay_command}; no protected subject bytes or secrets.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: retirement at activation, local wall-clock expiry, digest-only inventory, canonical attestations reused prebootstrap, and terminal summaries retaining cleanup authority. If any participant or verifier floor is missing, retirement remains safely blocked.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 2200-2210 and 2216-2217.

title: Implement time-authority rotation: freeze, close, fence, inventories, drain, retirement
description:
## What & scope
Implement the ordered, externally recoverable time-authority profile rotation: registry profile states, admission freeze, rotation intent, external close/fence, issuance reservations and quiescence, time-bound-subject inventories, drain holds, service contracts, and retirement.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: rotating the time authority without this machinery would silently orphan every outstanding lease/capability window or allow issuance against a dead profile. Rotation is an evidence chain with exhaustive subject inventories: no time-bound object is stranded or double-issued.

## Design — normative detail
`TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>` maps `profile_oid -> ActiveForIssuance|ClosingRequested|IssuanceClosing|IssuanceQuiescent|Draining|Retired` (arms carry exact refs: rotation intent, closing receipt, reservation closure, transition record, issuance fence, inventory closure, drain hold, terminal summary). Steady state: exactly one selected `ActiveForIssuance`; from intent through quiescence, zero Active and exactly one selected closing-state profile; after activation one Active successor, predecessor Draining. No issuance encoder accepts a non-Active state. Evidence resolution: Active/Draining valid for verification/use; the closing states only for subjects whose immutable reservation predates the freeze; Retired/foreign/unrooted invalid. Order: (1) each group orders `TimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeSpec`, exporting `GroupTimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeCertificate` (Meta consumes its own plus one per current/prospective shard); (2) `TimeAuthorityRotationIntentSpec<Role>` — admin authorization, expected registry state, retiring/successor profile refs, exact freeze-certificate and offline-issuer-epoch sets, external close/fence/registry-transition operation recipes, closure resource reservations, abort-before-external-fence recipe — atomically selects `ClosingRequested` and creates the immutable intent record; only its durable `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Role>` may initialize external dispatch. (3) The external close returns `TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt` with sorted per-group closing floors, atomically rejecting old-profile reservations beyond them; `TimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseSpec` changes only `ClosingRequested -> IssuanceClosing`; typed abort to `ActiveForIssuance` is legal only before the close is known sent — after `SentUnknown`/receipt, roll-forward only under the structural `TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority` (constructible only from the rooted intent plus the exact current dispatch attempt/terminal evidence; cannot alter successor, sets, resources, request bodies, or authorize abort/fresh issuance). (4) Every admitted issuance owns a `TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation` (`Reserved -> Published|Burned` generation-two terminal; `TimeIssuanceGuard` constructible only from a current Reserved row); groups emit `GroupTimeIssuanceQuiescenceCertificate` (complete reserved-to-published-or-burned bijection, zero-live-guard proof); applying `RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure` selects `IssuanceQuiescent`. (5) `TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence` — the final portable external successor binding group closure projections, offline-epoch fences, and `no_future_root_issuance_under_profile:true` — is obtained only via intent-owned dispatch after the closure is visible; then inventories are cut: `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role>` (every rooted live time-bearing owner exactly once; online macaroon roots by token ID, offline roots by fenced cohort; Shard cannot originate online roots), `TimeBoundSubjectInventoryProof` (owner-to-entry bijection, post-fence no-new-issuance proof), `RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure`. (6) `TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>` retains fence, closure, `TimeObservationServiceContract`, `OfflineIssuerVerificationServiceFloor`, verifier keys, and `maximum_old_subject_expiry` until every old subject terminates via `TimeSubjectDisposition` (`Terminal|Expired|Reissued{nonwidening_proof,tombstone}`; typed per-subject arms generated from the registry — generic/digest-only arms forbidden). Retirement uses the distinct `TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority` (constructible only from Draining plus complete cleanup closure). Configuration/topology/role transitions consult live holds; v1 categorically forbids Local-to-Sharded transition while any profile is closing/Draining.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: reservations/guards/holds are obligations with exactly one legal terminal; none lost or double-published. FG-INV-07: no pre-order object names its future receipt/certificate. Rotation duration/drain windows are `slo.toml` concerns, not invariants.

## Interactions
Extends w9-time-authority; consumes `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate` from w9-audit-release plus universal irreversible dispatch; w9-threat-tokens' offline cohorts appear in inventories; w11-membership-config/w12-topology consult drain holds.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: registry state-machine exhaustiveness. Crash matrix at every boundary (freeze, intent, close send, `SentUnknown`, fence, inventory cut, drain, retirement), each recovering to the one named continuation. Negative: reservation after freeze, issuance from Draining, abort after fence, inventory bijection failure, Local-to-Sharded during Draining — all fail closed. E2E: full rotation against a simulated authority with logged transitions; every old-profile subject reaches a typed disposition. Detailed logging: every rotation stage logs {transition_id, registry state before/after, freeze/quiescence/inventory certificate digests, reservation counts by terminal (Published/Burned) with the bijection verdict, close/fence dispatch attempt state (Armed/SentUnknown/receipted), fence digest, inventory entry count vs generated time-bearing row count, per-subject disposition arm, drain-hold floors}; abort and roll-forward decisions log the irreversibility basis so crash-matrix recovery is auditable from the last logged stage alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: read-only guard-based closing; migration-proof exceptions during rotation. Risk: rotation is heavyweight — acceptable, rare, correctness-critical.

## Provenance
App A 2175–2198.

title: FG-INV promotion order is wrong: 10 of 20 clauses owe a missing Lean/TLA lane, and every .core statement is an atomic verbatim conjunction over absent subsystems

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
Measured by pane3 while working fgdb-fginv-spine-zero-live-checkers-v05b, whose guard is landed
and whose acceptance is complete. This is the residue that had no home.

TWO FACTS, BOTH MEASURED BY ASKING THE CHECKER (promote one clause in memory, read the
violations; control asserts the shipped tree is 0 violations first).

1. THE RECOMMENDED "CHEAPEST FIRST" TARGET IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE.
   v05b's handoff names FG-INV-01 or FG-INV-03 as cheapest. Measured:
     FG-INV-03.core -> 3 violations: two clause_promoted_without_live_checker PLUS
       proof_lane_declared_while_clause_promoted (lane "lean-version-chain",
       artifact formal/lean/VersionChain.lean does not exist).
     FG-INV-01.core -> 2 violations.  FG-INV-12.core -> 2 violations.
   Swept over all twenty: 10 OF 20 owe a proof lane whose artifact is missing and whose
   status is "declared" — FG-INV-02, 03, 04, 05, 08, 10, 13, 14, 15, 17.
   The cheapest ten by blocker count are therefore 01, 06, 07, 09, 11, 12, 16, 18, 19, 20.
   Anyone starting the build-out should start there, not at 03.

2. THE ATOMIC-CLAUSE BLOCKER, which no amount of clever test placement fixes.
   `exact_statement` must be VERBATIM from Appendix F (invariants.toml header), and each
   `.core` statement is a large conjunction. `status` is one field over the whole conjunction,
   so promoting claims all of it is enforced. Concretely:
     FG-INV-07.core requires `command_contracts.toml` bijective with every role command
       arm/handler and `state_payload_fields.toml` rooting every written state class.
       NEITHER FILE EXISTS. (This was the best candidate, because the durable registries do
       exist and already carry acyclicity/construction-order/reference-resolution laws.)
     FG-INV-12.core is the only invariant whose owner crate exists (fgdb-types), yet its
       statement conjoins answer-equivalent rewrites, spill, factorize/flatten, workspace
       materialization, safe replan and AnswerContract — none of which exist.
   19 of 20 owner crates do not exist. Of the seven crates named by checker_index artifacts

   identity-registry symbol rather than an FG-INV entrypoint — so the mechanism is proven,

title: Pin-cycle tool: script the base-derived re-freeze once so lquj, dkjg step 5 and 1nfu's candidate execute mechanically
description:
Three beads are stuck at the SAME boundary -- fgdb-lquj, fgdb-dkjg step 5, and
RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot.transfer_evidence_ref from fgdb-1nfu. All three are
derived, correct, and waiting on a mint-and-pin cycle. That is one missing tool,
not three blockers. Same shape as fgdb-1j16: fix the repeated procedure at the
source instead of having each holder re-derive it under pressure.

## Invocation

    bash /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh

  FGDB_ROOT        default /data/projects/frankengraphdb
  FGDB_PIN_CACHE   default $TMPDIR/fgdb-pin-cycle  (~75MB rlib+binary, reused)
  FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS  default 4

  exit 0  pins correct, drift set EMPTY (it may have written)
  exit 1  refused to start, or drift survived the rewrite
  exit 2  checker unbuildable, or a verdict it could not parse

Run it AFTER applying catalog rows and BEFORE `appendix-regenerate`, which
refuses to write while any drift stands.

## What it does, and the four properties that were required

1. BASE-DERIVED, NEVER HARD-CODED. It never takes a pin from its caller. It runs
   the checker and reads the new value out of the checker's own message,
       released assignment pin "OLD" != recomputed "NEW"
   emitted by identity.rs at the `registry_assignment_drift` site (:1443). Nothing
   in the script computes a pin. HEAD moves several times per increment here, so a
   value read a minute ago is already suspect.
2. RE-RUNNABLE. A second round after a peer commit is one invocation. It loops
   until the drift set is EMPTY, not merely smaller, and stops at FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS
   rather than spinning.
3. STATES WHAT MOVED. One `rewrote OLD -> NEW` line per pin plus a total, so the
   commit message writes itself.
4. REFUSES TO ABSORB A PEER'S EDIT. If identity.rs is already modified it stops
   before building anything, because it cannot tell your pin edit from someone
   else's in-flight work.

Two smaller properties worth keeping: it rewrites an EXACT literal and refuses if
that literal appears anything other than once (never a regex over the file), and
it rebuilds the checker EVERY round -- a binary a few commits stale reported five
drift codes on a tree a fresh build called clean, which is measured, not
hypothetical.

## Controls, all three run, all three behave

  A  clean tree            "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already
                           match the tree", SUMMARY 0, exit 0
  B  deliberately stale    planted fnv1a64:dead0000dead0000 over the LOGICAL pin
     pin in a scratch      in a copied tree ->
     root                     "round 1: 1 pin(s) moved"
                              "rewrote fnv1a64:dead0000dead0000 ->
                                       fnv1a64:403196d930716d3c"
                              "drift set is EMPTY after 1 rewrite round(s)"
                           and the file ends holding the true value, 1 occurrence.
  C  peer-edit guard       touched identity.rs in the real repo -> REFUSED,
                           exit 1, before building anything. Restored, 0
                           modifications.

Control B is the one that matters: it proves the tool CORRECTS rather than merely
reports, and that it reaches empty rather than smaller.

## One fail-open found and closed while building it

The guard first read `git status` unconditionally. In a non-repo root git errors,
the substitution is empty, and the guard passed silently -- a guard that quietly
does nothing, which is the defect this swarm keeps closing. It now branches on
`git rev-parse --git-dir` and, in a non-repo root, prints
    NOTICE: <root> is not a git worktree; the peer-edit guard does not apply here
so the vacuity is announced rather than assumed. Control B's output shows that
notice firing.

## Where it lives, and what promoting it needs

It is at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh, NOT in scripts/, on
purpose: check.sh enforces a file-coverage closure over `git ls-files`, so a new
tracked script must be claimed by a checker_index row or declared exempt in the
same commit or the closure gate reds. Promoting it into scripts/ is a small
catalog-token change and should be done deliberately, not as a side effect.
BECAUSE /data/tmp IS SWEPT -- that is how fgdb-uug4 lost its staging -- the
complete script text is on the FIRST NOTE of this bead. Restore from there if the
file is gone.

## Referenced from

fgdb-lquj and fgdb-dkjg both carry pin-cycle prose. Whoever executes either
should read this command instead of that procedure.
notes:
PANE2 FINDING from fgdb-lquj (2026-07-27): the tool cannot see this bead shape.

refreeze_identity_pins.sh drift_report runs `registry-check identity` and greps
`released assignment pin "X" != recomputed "Y"`. For a LOGICAL-KIND mint that grep
returns EMPTY and the tool reports "no pin movement ... 0 pin(s) rewritten" and
exits 0 -- a FALSE GREEN, while the appendix gate is red with
projection_registry_assignment_drift.

WHY: `identity` validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections, which are
still pre-mint at that moment. The drift only exists over CATALOG-DERIVED identity,
which is reached at appendix_a.rs:11442 where validate_identity is called on
catalog.identity and every code is re-emitted with a `projection_` prefix. So the
code to grep is projection_registry_assignment_drift from the `appendix`
subcommand, not registry_assignment_drift from `identity`.

SECOND BLOCKER, independent: main.rs:90 collapses EVERY appendix violation message
to the fixed string "Appendix A contract check failed". The recomputed value the
tool must parse never reaches stdout, so switching the subcommand alone is not
enough. Measured: `rc appendix` prints 4 codes and 0 values.

WORKAROUND USED (kept, read-only, computes no pin):
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_lquj_pincache/drift.rs -- 30 lines, links the same rlib,
calls the same public entry points (load_and_verify, appendix_a_catalog_projection_diff,
appendix_a_catalog_closure, verify_repository_bindings) and prints violation.msg
verbatim. It surfaced all four values in one run, e.g.
  "released row-id transcript must contain 3603 rows with sha256 24d978b8..; found
   3605 rows with sha256 432e0d87.."

SUGGESTED REPAIR, in order: (1) fix main.rs:90 to emit violation.msg -- this is a
real diagnostic defect independent of the tool, and every appendix violation in the
repo is currently unreadable from the binary; (2) point drift_report at `appendix`
and widen the grep to the projection_-prefixed code. The tool is otherwise correct:
its exact-literal rewrite, its refusal on a dirty identity.rs, and its rebuild-every-
round discipline were all followed by hand here and all three were load-bearing.

ALSO: an epoch bump is NOT handled by the tool at all. A logical-kind add requires
logical_object_kinds registry_epoch to move in BOTH registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml
and the expected_epoch const (precedent e7b6f09, doctrine at identity.rs:1206). The
epoch is not an input to rows_pin, so it can be bumped after the pin is re-derived.
close_reason: Tool built, three controls fired (clean tree reports no movement; a planted stale pin is reported AND corrected to fnv1a64:403196d930716d3c in one round reaching EMPTY; the peer-edit guard refuses with exit 1 before building), one fail-open closed in its own guard, full script text embedded on the bead against a /data/tmp sweep, and pointers added to lquj and dkjg. Unblocks four parked pieces of work once disk returns.

title: w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh reds on a shared-target-dir race, not on nondeterminism
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-26 in a full scripts/check.sh run (log /data/tmp/fgdb-check-gates.NIE0ap/registered-13.log).

The registered live gate scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh exited 1, and
the obvious reading -- 'same root cause as the 12 identity failures' -- is WRONG.
Its log says:

    error: extern location for fgdb_bigint does not exist:
      /data/tmp/cargo-target/debug/deps/libfgdb_bigint-20abfb7010900144.rlib
    error: aborting due to 1 previous error

That is another pane's cargo run replacing an rlib in the SHARED
CARGO_TARGET_DIR (/data/tmp/cargo-target) while this gate's build was reading it.
The gate runs the whole workspace suite TWICE and compares, so it holds the
target dir for ~10 minutes and is the most exposed consumer of that sharing.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is a registered live gate whose red is environmental. Every
run of check.sh in a busy swarm can produce it, and a reader who assumes the red
is about determinism will chase a ghost -- or, worse, will learn to ignore a red
from the ONLY cross-crate checker for Doctrine 4, which no cargo test can
replace.

DO NOT FIX BY MINTING A PRIVATE CARGO_TARGET_DIR: disk is at 98% (24G free), and
a per-pane target dir is tens of GB.

Candidate shapes, in preference order:
1. Have the gate detect the race and report it AS a race rather than as a
   determinism failure: an 'extern location ... does not exist' in the build log
   is a distinguishable signature, and the gate should say 'aborted: shared
   target dir mutated under me' and exit with a code that check.sh reports
   separately from a genuine comparison failure. Same shape as the fail-slow
   work d1d4 landed: a gate that never reached its verdict must say so.
2. Take the build token for the duration (it already needs one) and document
   that the two runs must be inside one hold.

Filed by pane3 while closing fgdb-a5kb; not claimed.

title: Checker census-gap repair: arm-payload field identity + wire-hosted fields
description:
The v3/v4 Appendix A checker has two structural completion gaps, discovered during a01 increment-2 rehearsal (reported on fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-scaffold-gvvf 2026-07-23 03:29Z, acknowledged by the a20 schema-v4 note but never repaired; the scaffold bead closed without them). Both make complete-slice census equality unsatisfiable for every nontrivial slice.

GAP 1 - ARM-PAYLOAD FIELD IDENTITY COLLAPSE: field projection identity and row_id derive from (containing_schema, stable_name) only; the field-target matcher discards the census path component (appendix_a.rs canonical_symbol == schema.stable_name with _path discarded). Census field candidates inside union-arm payloads are distinguished ONLY by path. a01 alone has 64 such keys of which 45 collide in 20 groups (AppliedAbortRef.command_ref x4, AuthorityAppliedRef.command_ref x3, RoleTransitionActivationState 10 groups, RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence.trust_transition arms 4 groups). No catalog can give them complete-field census coverage. Repair direction (choose one): (a) extend field identity/row_id derivation to include the census path for arm-payload fields; (b) cover arm payloads through the union_arm contract (payload_sha256 already commits to the payload shape) and exclude union-interior field candidates from the complete-field census pin the way reference-only symbols are excluded.

GAP 2 - WIRE-HOSTED FIELD GAP: fields whose containing schema is a wire type (reference wrappers, ConsensusDomain, RemoteObjectIdentity, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>, StrongCiphertextRef<T>, closed result-role unions, PlacementDescriptorWithoutId) fail projection_field_unresolved_schema because wire types resolve in no identity class. 66 a01 census field keys are uncoverable (e.g. field|StrongRef|StrongRef.oid|oid). Repair direction: (a) allow wire-kind schemas as field hosts in a distinct identity class; (b) exclude wire-family interior fields from the field census like reference-only symbols.

Blocked work quantified (a01 only; every other slice has the same classes): 146 staged fields, 80 staged adjudications (maps-to-source resolved keys must be projected), 11 unions, 31 arms. a16 has 42 arms; the pattern recurs slice-wide.

Acceptance: chosen repair direction implemented with fail-closed census equality preserved; synthetic negative tests for both gap classes; the a01 staged inventory (session scratchpad staged_*.json, enumerated by blocker on the a01 bead trail) lands green against the repaired checker; no weakening of the complete-slice contract for cases the current checker already validates. Interacts with: fgdb-a01-reference-roots-2k0q (146+80+11+31 staged rows), all a02-a21 slices with arm-payload or wire-interior fields, the closed fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-scaffold-gvvf (design provenance).
close_reason: Landed as 0eaffdf (design comment upthread; a15 increment-3 unblock landed separately as 7a32726). Both gap classes repaired via census coverage classes: arm-payload interiors project through the union-arm payload contract, wire-hosted interiors through the targeted wire envelope; complete_field census equality moved to the source pass (verify_complete_field_census_coverage) keeping the appendix gate fail-closed; adjudication projection extended so the 80 staged a01 maps-to-source rows become landable. title: identity_class is unenforced for non-reference fields: validate_identity accepts inline, logical, scalar and physical identically
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 at pinned SHA e14563e by pane3 while on fgdb-uug4, by
synthesizing rows and asking the checker — the method that was supposed to answer
the question and instead showed the question is unanswerable.

## The measurement

Took the five FLAT non-reference a05 field candidates, synthesized a FieldRow for
each against a clean snapshot (BASE violations = 0), and ran validate_identity
four times, changing ONLY identity_class:

    identity_class = "inline"    -> 11 new violations
    identity_class = "logical"   -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
    identity_class = "scalar"    -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
    identity_class = "physical"  -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set

Only the recomputed assignment hash differs between them. The eleven violations
are five bad_cardinality + five field_construction_order_mismatch + one
registry_assignment_drift — all unrelated to the class. THE VACUITY CONTROL DID
NOT FIRE: validate_identity does not discriminate identity_class for a
non-reference field at all.

## Why this is a bug and not a gap

identity_class is durable-format data. Section 5.1 makes durable_fields.toml 'the
sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure,
construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers'. A wrong
identity_class therefore mis-drives generated reachability and GC — and it is
accepted silently, because every one of the five legal values is individually
legal for any field row.

fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd exists precisely because the data
could not decide this; the owner ruled 'six flat inline fields plus four exact
arm-payload contracts'. That ruling is settled law and is being applied by hand.
Nothing holds it. The next slice that copies the precedent has no gate telling it
whether it copied correctly, and the l6xd bead's own text names this risk: 'a
wrong value here is not a lint failure that surfaces later — it is a wrong
byte-level contract that the loader accepts'.

This is the same shape closed three times tonight: a7c8 (the aggregate pin left
the per-family split free), 5qcg (six exclusions the reader never consulted),
d9pd (SC2015 unenforced because it is only a note). A rule exists; no checker
holds it.

## Proposed law

    A [[field]] row whose exact_wire_type resolves to a registered wire type whose
    kind is NOT reference_wrapper, and whose reference_semantics is "none", must
    declare identity_class = "inline".

with the completeness guard that makes it fail CLOSED: every field row's
exact_wire_type must resolve to a registered wire type of a KNOWN kind, so a newly
minted wire kind cannot escape the law by being unclassified. Give that guard its
own violation code.

## What must be checked before landing it

1. Apply the candidate law to all 2293 landed durable_fields rows and count
   counterexamples. If it is a law it has zero; if it has a handful they are
   either errata or the law is narrower than stated. That census is the whole
   proof and it is cheap.
2. The UNION-typed non-reference fields are a SEPARATE case and must be excluded
   or separately ruled — measured on a05, 2 of the 7 non-reference candidates are
   union-typed (GlobalControlRecord.origin, and
   RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec.transfer_evidence_ref). l6xd said FLAT.
3. Check whether the same silence applies to reference_semantics and
   digest_class; if validate_identity is mute on those too, this bead is wider
   than its title.

## Not authored here

This is a new law over durable-format data and belongs beside the ruling, not
smuggled into a field tranche. fgdb-uug4 carries the measurement that produced it.
close_reason: Both survivor laws verified under a catalog lease: base 0, active 0, and each per-law mutation control fired.

comments.text:

Measured at pinned SHA e14563e over every landed durable_fields row.

    landed durable_fields rows ................ 800
    identity_class distribution ............... logical 424, inline 192,
                                                scalar 132, bootstrap_local 29,
                                                physical 23
    registered wire kinds ..................... record, union, union_variant,
                                                discriminant, reference_wrapper

    IN SCOPE of the law (exact_wire_type resolves to a non-reference_wrapper
    wire type AND reference_semantics = "none") ....... 136
        of which wire kind = record ....................  96
        of which wire kind = union .....................  40
    COUNTEREXAMPLES ....................................   0

136 covered / 0 counterexamples. That is what makes it a law rather than a
majority vote, and it is the same bar applied on gls4 (360 rows / 0, then 310
more / 0).

## THIS SETTLES THE UNION SUB-CASE, AND AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER CAUTION

On fgdb-uug4 I split a05's seven non-reference candidates 5 flat / 2 union-typed
and said l6xd does not reach the union-typed pair. The corpus disagrees with the
caution: FORTY landed rows have a union-kind exact_wire_type with
reference_semantics = none, and ALL FORTY declare identity_class = "inline".
There is no counterexample in either sub-case.

So the law should be written over both, and the two a05 union-typed candidates
(GlobalControlRecord.origin, RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec.
transfer_evidence_ref) are covered by 40 precedents rather than unsettled. Note
this is a DIFFERENT question from l6xd's "four exact arm-payload contracts",
which were arm-path occurrences, not union-typed fields — I conflated the two
and the census separated them.

## THE COMPLETENESS GUARD IS NOT OPTIONAL: 253 OF 800 ROWS ESCAPE

253 landed rows have an exact_wire_type that does NOT resolve to any registered
wire type — 32% of the corpus. Those are the primitive-typed fields (u64 and
friends), which are legitimately not wire types; note 132 rows carry
identity_class = "scalar", so the populations overlap but are not identical.

Consequence: written naively the law is silent on nearly a third of every field
row, which is precisely the fail-open shape this bead exists to close. The guard
must therefore partition explicitly rather than skip-on-unresolved:

    every field row's exact_wire_type resolves to EITHER a registered wire type
    of a known kind, OR a declared primitive from a closed primitive vocabulary

and a row matching neither is a violation with its own code. Without that second
arm the guard is exactly the -returning table that
[[one-law-two-artifacts]] warns fails open on an unknown name.

## Remaining before the law can be authored

Item 3 of this bead is untouched and I did not measure it: whether
validate_identity is equally silent on reference_semantics and digest_class. If
it is, this bead is wider than its title says. The census probe is at
<scratch>/uug4/census.rs and extends in a few lines to answer it.

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
ITEM 3 DONE. THE BEAD IS WIDER THAN ITS TITLE — THREE COLUMNS ARE UNENFORCED,
NOT ONE. Measured at pinned SHA e14563e by mutating LANDED rows in place (one
column at a time, so nothing else can be what fires), base violations = 0.

## The harness control FIRES, so every 'SILENT' below is a real silence

    construction_order := 0   ->  field_construction_order_mismatch   FIRES

Without that line, 'silent' could just mean my harness was broken. It is not.

## Result, split by the wire kind of the field's exact type

136 in-scope landed rows = 96 record-kind + 40 union-kind.

  mutation applied to RECORD-kind rows (96)              verdict
  ----------------------------------------------------  ---------------------------
  identity_class := logical | scalar | physical |
                    bootstrap_local                      SILENT  (all four)
  reference_semantics := strong                          CAUGHT  bare_strong_ref,
                                                          reference_semantics_without_reference_type
  reference_semantics := weak                            CAUGHT  bad_field
  reference_semantics := identity                        CAUGHT  bad_field
  reference_semantics := locator                         SILENT
  digest_class := Some("digest256")                      CAUGHT  bad_field
  digest_class := Some("bogus_not_a_class")              CAUGHT  bad_field
  digest_class := None   (CLEAR an existing one)         SILENT

  the same mutations on UNION-kind rows (40)             ordinary_union_field_mismatch

## Three holes, and they are different from each other

1. identity_class is UNENFORCED on record-kind rows — all four wrong values
   accepted. This confirms the original finding and LOCALISES it: the earlier
   synthesis run showed silence, and this shows it is specifically the record-kind
   population. That is the law this bead already proposes.

2. reference_semantics = "locator" IS A ONE-VALUE HOLE IN AN OTHERWISE ENFORCED
   VOCABULARY. strong, weak and identity are all rejected on a non-reference
   field; locator is accepted. That is worse than a uniformly missing law,
   because the vocabulary LOOKS enforced — three of four values fire — so a
   reviewer checking one or two values concludes the column is guarded. NEW, and
   not covered by the proposed inline law.

3. digest_class is enforced in one direction only: SETTING any value on these
   rows is caught, CLEARING an existing one is silent. So a row can silently lose
   its digest_class. Same converse-missing shape as the exemption ledgers in
   5qcg — 'an entry whose subject is gone must fail, AND an entry whose subject no
   longer violates must fail'.

## The union rows are protected BY COINCIDENCE, which is its own finding

Every mutation on the 40 union-kind rows raises  —
a union-ARM consistency law, not any field-column law. So union-typed rows are
not protected because identity_class/reference_semantics/digest_class are
checked; they are protected because those rows are additionally coupled to an
ordinary-union contract that happens to notice. Decouple that (a union-typed
field not participating in an ordinary union) and the same three holes open on
them too. This is the a7c8 shape exactly: total by coincidence of the current
data, not by construction.

## What this changes about the proposed law

The law as written on this bead covers hole 1 only. It should be authored
alongside two more, all three with the same explicit-partition completeness guard
(registered wire kind OR declared primitive from a closed vocabulary, neither =
violation), because 253 of 800 landed rows resolve to no registered wire type:

  * identity_class  — the inline law already stated here
  * reference_semantics — "locator" must be rejected on a non-reference_wrapper
    exact type, closing the vocabulary that already rejects strong/weak/identity
  * digest_class — clearing must be as loud as setting

## Not authored

Same reason as before: three new laws over durable-format data, and the census
that proves each belongs with it. The probe is at <scratch>/uug4/item3.rs and
prints the whole table in one run.

## LAW 2 — "locator requires a reference_wrapper exact type". FALSIFIED. DO NOT AUTHOR.

    reference_semantics over all 880 rows:
        none 431 | strong 397 | weak_digest 49 | locator 2 | external_root 1

    denominator (rows with reference_semantics = "locator") .... 2

    RootBootstrap.segment_id                : bytes

So the law I proposed would break 2 of the 2 rows it governs — 0/2 supported.
And the reading behind it was wrong:  is used ONLY with PRIMITIVE types,

    rows carrying a digest_class ....... 109 of 880

    by exact-type wire kind ............ <unregistered/primitive> 82 | record 27

    exact_wire_types appearing BOTH with and without a digest_class ..... 0

the whole corpus — no type is split. So the correct law is a consistency law:

which is checkable, has denominator 880 with 0 counterexamples, and makes

RE-MEASUREMENT at 7e9d7e1, 2026-07-26 (pane4, mock/placeholder sweep lane).
Both gates named in this bead are still red; the numbers have moved.

## architecture-check: 11 violations (exit 1), was 4 orphans, now 5

  bead_source_count            .beads/issues.jsonl has 353 distinct records,
                               declared 338, independently pinned 338
  bead_binding_hash_mismatch   declared fnv1a64:6ef322219e81d5c1,
                               recomputed fnv1a64:e2ce5e93a40c410a
  independent_bead_binding_hash_mismatch   same recomputed value vs the code pin
  bead_resolution_class_count  class "bet_label" has 201 rows, declared 188, pinned 188
  bead_class_count_total       declared class counts sum to 335, bead_count is 338
  bead_provenance_not_total    resolved 348 of 353 records
  bead_provenance_orphan x5    fgdb-5cgb, fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx,
                               fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8, fgdb-gb9g, fgdb-zwhh

The fifth orphan is new since this bead was filed. All five are present in HEAD.
Note this bead (fgdb-zwhh) is itself one of the orphans.

## cargo fmt --check: still red, 42 `Diff in` hunks

## Split of the remaining work, measured

Of the 11, SEVEN are mechanically fixable by a pure re-freeze — recompute and
write `bead_count`, `bet_label_count`, the four class counts, and `binding_hash`
in `registries/architecture_decisions.toml`, plus `PINNED_BEAD_COUNT`,
`PINNED_BET_LABEL_COUNT`, `PINNED_BEAD_BINDING_HASH` and then
`PINNED_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_HASH` in `tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs`.
No judgement required; the checker prints every recomputed value.

FOUR are not mechanical: the five orphans (and the two totals that are derived
from them) need each orphan bead to acquire a bet label, an exact override, or a
family rule. That is a CLAIM about which ADR owns each bead, so it should be made
by whoever filed it, not by a passing re-freeze. Assigning a bet label to another
pane's bead to clear a count is exactly the shortcut that makes a provenance
registry stop meaning anything.

## Why this keeps recurring, which may be the real bead here

The pins move on every bead CREATION, and the doctrine (correctly) requires the
re-freeze to ride in the same commit as the created record. Under a six-agent
swarm that is a treadmill: `.beads/issues.jsonl` is one shared whole-file export,
so any pane's routine flush sweeps every other pane's new records, and the
re-freeze obligation lands on whoever commits — who is generally not the author
and cannot supply the missing bet labels.

Observed directly today: six bead records created by pane4 were swept into
pane3's commit 7e9d7e1 ("chore(beads): file the unsafe-islands remainder and the
two red gates") without a re-freeze. No fault of pane3's — the export is
whole-file and the sweep is invisible in a line-level diff stat. But the result
is that main's provenance pins are stale again within minutes of any repair, so
"re-freeze the pins" is not a fix, it is a chore with a half-life.

Worth considering as the actual remedy: make the pin a function of the file
rather than a copy of it (i.e. verify a computed digest against a committed
transcript that the flush regenerates), or scope the count pins to exclude
records whose provenance is unresolved so that orphans fail loudly on their own
row instead of also breaking three unrelated aggregate pins.

SECOND OBSERVATION of the sweep hazard, same session, ~40 minutes after the
first (pane4). Recording it because one instance is an anecdote and two with
different mechanisms is a measurement.

1. 13:5x — pane3's commit 7e9d7e1 swept SIX bead records created by pane4 into
   a commit whose message describes only the unsafe-islands remainder. No
   re-freeze rode with it. Detected only by diffing record sets against HEAD;
   invisible in `git diff --stat`.

2. 14:0x — pane5 (holding the `beads` token, correctly) ran a flush that
   captured ONE of two pane4 records created seconds apart
   (`fgdb-clause-promotion-to-live-is-unguarded-nllh` in,
   `fgdb-claims-lint-one-directional-unmarked-budgets-sdpv` out), because the
   flush landed between the two `br create` calls. Worktree went 353 -> 354
   records with 1 CREATED + 1 MODIFIED.

The second case is the sharper one: the token was held correctly and the
protocol was followed. The token serializes the flush; it does not serialize
CREATION, which happens in every pane's `.beads/beads.db` continuously and
independently. So a correct token holder still exports records it did not
create and cannot re-freeze for — it cannot even enumerate whose they are
without diffing against HEAD, which the protocol does not require it to do.

This is why "re-freeze the pins in the same commit as the created record" is
not implementable as stated under a six-agent swarm: the agent that commits is
structurally not the agent that created, and the set of swept records is
determined by flush timing rather than by authorship. Pins have been red on
main continuously through at least three repair attempts today.

pane4 is deliberately NOT re-freezing into this (per instruction: the orphan
half belongs to the four orphan beads' creators). Recording the mechanism so
whoever does take the pin repair designs for it rather than re-fixing the
count. Concrete suggestion repeated from the earlier comment: make the pin a
function the flush recomputes into a committed transcript, or scope the count
pins so unresolved-provenance records fail on their own row instead of also
breaking three aggregate pins that any pane can trip by existing.
