comments.text:
CLOSING MEASUREMENT (pane4, 2026-07-26). Both gates named in this bead are GREEN
at HEAD 6950174, measured against a pristine `git archive HEAD` copy, lock-free,
no cargo.

## Gate 1 — bead-provenance pins: GREEN, 27/27

    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check \
      tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o lib2.rlib
    CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<archive>/tools/registry-check rustc --edition=2024 --test \
      tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs --extern registry_check=lib2.rlib
    -> test result: ok. 27 passed; 0 failed.

All four rows named in this bead now pass: architecture_registry_parses_and_validates,
architecture_bead_provenance_is_total_pinned_and_bidirectional,
architecture_neg_semantic_change_with_stable_id,
architecture_neg_rule_tables_and_resolution_pins.
Zero `bead_provenance_orphan`. Zero `bead_provenance_not_total`.

## Gate 2 — cargo fmt --check: GREEN, 0 hunks

    find crates tools -name '*.rs' | xargs rustfmt --edition 2024 --check
    -> rc=0, 0 `Diff in` hunks over 115 files.

Was 56, then 42. The remaining 42 were cleared by their owners during the session.

## How the five orphans were actually discharged — NOT by bet labels

The ORPHAN OWNERSHIP MAP (comment above) routed five orphans. They were adopted in
`2cba0a8` ("split a16 law-gated residue"), by `[[bead_override]]` rows rather than
by bet labels — five new rows, `bead_override` 13 -> 18, `exact_override_count`
13 -> 18:

    appendix-a13-source-authority-residue        fgdb-gb9g   -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    appendix-a20-promotion-candidate-boundary    fgdb-5cgb   -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    appendix-a-active-kind-arm-bijection         ...-cuvx    -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    architecture-bead-rule-transcript-coverage   ...-a7c8    -> FG-ADR-CON-11
    unsafe-islands-red-gates                     fgdb-zwhh   -> FG-ADR-CON-11

That mechanism is *stricter* than a bet label, not weaker: a bet label resolves to
the generic `FG-ADR-BET-B{n}`, whereas an override names a specific frozen ADR. And
it edits `registries/**` (catalog-token-guarded) instead of the shared bead records
(the sweep treadmill described above). It was the right call.

## AUDIT OF THE FIVE BETS, derived from the plan's B1-B6 rather than from the row

The ruling required each bet to be derived from the plan's own definitions, because
a wrong one is a silent mis-classification no checker catches. The two ADRs used
declare their own bets, so each override implies a bet:

    FG-ADR-CON-06  "published-recovery-root-source-of-truth"   affected_bets = ["B1"]
    FG-ADR-CON-11  "typed-claims"                              affected_bets = ["B5"]

Independent derivation, per record:

- **fgdb-gb9g -> B1. Correct.** a13 is "Branch manifest, key grants, retirement, and
  merge formats". B1 is explicit that "git-style database branches" are the same
  append-only content-addressed commit stream as MVCC/time-travel/replication.
  Branch manifest + merge format is Chronicle durable format. (Caveat recorded, not
  a dispute: the key-grant/KeyEnvelope portion has an Aegis/B6 flavour; the record's
  live content is field-identity rows and reference-semantics laws, which are B1.)

- **fgdb-5cgb -> B1. Correct, and the best fit of the five.** a20 is restore
  promotion / reopen / completion / release. CON-06 is literally "reconstruct
  canonical state from the published checkpoint and contiguous logical-command
  suffix". Restore promotion *is* the recovery-root story.

- **fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8 -> B5. Correct.** A bare row count standing
  in for table integrity is a weaker claim class justifying a stronger one, which is
  CON-11 verbatim.

- **fgdb-zwhh (this bead) -> B5. Correct.** "While these are red, 'I ran the gates'
  cannot distinguish a change that broke something from one that did not" is a
  claim-typing failure, not a durable-format one.

- **fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx -> B1. Defensible, but narrow —
  recorded as a finding, not repaired.** The record has two halves. Its stated
  "decision needed" (seven durable logical object kinds `active` vs `reserved`,
  0x028f/0x0550-0x0555) is a durable code-space choice: B1, CON-06, correct. But its
  other half — "enforcement lived ONLY in two `const _: () = assert!` inside
  fgdb-types; registry-check, the identity suite, architecture-check and the G0
  identity e2e were ALL GREEN on the exact tree that would not build" — is CON-11/B5,
  and it is what shipped `validate_active_logical_kind_arms` in 47807be.

  I considered adding FG-ADR-CON-11 to that override row and decided against it. The
  B5 half is not unowned: `fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8` is the sweep cuvx
  triggered, and it is already bound to CON-11. Adding a second ADR whose content is
  bound elsewhere would be churn on a green gate, under a contended catalog token,
  for no gate benefit. CON-06 alone is not *wrong* for cuvx; it is *primary*.
  Flagging rather than editing, so the next owner can disagree with the reasoning
  in front of them.

Net: 4 of 5 clean, 1 defensible-but-narrow with its complement separately owned.
No mis-classification found.

## THE CLASS FIX — and the ruling's proposed fix is the wrong one

Ruled: "a validation that a bet label must be b1..b6 is the permanent fix." Measured,
that validation ALREADY EXISTS and already works. Probe of four synthetic records
through `architecture::validate_architecture`:

    ["b9"]      -> bead_bet_label_unknown naming "b9"  AND  bead_provenance_orphan
    ["w1"]      -> bead_provenance_orphan ONLY; the message never mentions w1
    ["w1","b1"] -> nothing; resolves bet_label, the w1 silently discarded
    ["b3"]      -> nothing; resolves bet_label

`looks_like_bet_label` (architecture.rs:2147) is `b` + all-digits. A workstream tag
fails that predicate, so it is filtered out of `allowed_labels` (:2226-2233) and
**never reaches the vocabulary check at :2235**. The b1..b6 rule is not missing; it
is unreachable for this input.

Nor can workstream tags be rejected: 236 label-instances (w1..w12, g0..g4) exist
across the 375 records, and only 9 records carry one with no bet label — 8 of which
already resolve by another mechanism. A prohibition would red 236 legitimate rows.

The permanent fix is therefore a scoped *diagnostic*, not a new prohibition, filed as
its own bead per the ruling: `bead_workstream_label_in_bet_position`, emitted only on
the would-otherwise-orphan path, naming the bead and the offending label.

## Closing this bead

Both gates it names are green and independently reproduced above. The treadmill it
diagnosed is real and unfixed, but it is scoped on the successor bead plus the
existing `scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh`, which already reports the exact
required re-freeze before a `.beads/` commit. This record has served its purpose.

title: RED ON MAIN: the A10 historical witness does not reconstruct its own floor — a86e33d4 vs 236efa5b, and neither obvious cause explains it
notes:
pane4, at HEAD cb2f66e. NO PIN MOVED, no repo file edited, no assert weakened:
every probe ran on a COPY of tests/identity.rs in scratch.

=== FIRST: WHAT THE UNCOVERED HALF ACTUALLY IS ===

I was asked to name the categories of transcript entry that no cohort assert
covers. Read from identity::assignment_pins (:1210-1332), the durable_fields
transcript folds exactly FIVE line categories:

  field|          9 columns   one per r.fields row
  union|          4 columns   one per reference union
  arm|           10 columns   one per reference-union arm
  ordinary-union| 10 columns  one per ordinary union
  ordinary-arm|  11 columns   one per ordinary-union arm

And the witness count-asserts ALL FIVE. So the answer is that there is no
uncovered CATEGORY. The uncovered surface is the 44 COLUMNS those five
categories carry: a count assert verifies cardinality and never inspects a
column, so ANY column change on a RETAINED (pre-erratum) row moves the hash with
every count intact.

THAT REFRAMES THE REPAIR. A post_erratum filter removes ROWS and can only fix
MEMBERSHIP drift. Content drift on a row that legitimately belongs in the
historical namespace needs an undo_* transform, which is why the witness already
carries three (undo_a01_exactness_repair, undo_cq4x_capsule_retarget,
undo_mn8i_exact_order_repairs). This red is the fourth of that kind, not a
missing filter.

=== THE FIELD HALF IS NOW FULLY ACCOUNTED: 225 = 218 + 2 + 5 ===

Dumped the RETAINED pre-erratum namespace at HEAD: 262 lines = 225 field,
5 union, 8 arm, 6 ordinary-union, 18 ordinary-arm. Diffed the 225 field lines
against the same rows as they stood at 8a704c2, the commit where the
reconstruction equalled the floor by construction:

  218  matched IDENTICALLY                                   consumed
    0  absent at 8a704c2 (retained now, did not exist then)  -> ZERO membership
                                                                drift; nothing
                                                                post-erratum has
                                                                leaked in
    7  CHANGED COLUMNS on a retained row
  ---
  225

Of the 7, TWO are expected and are not drift — my comparison is post-undo HEAD
against the RAW 8a704c2 file, so any row the existing undos touch must differ:
  CommitMarker.capsule_ref              target CommittedEffectCapsule -> CommitCapsule
                                        (undo_cq4x_capsule_retarget)
  LogicalCommandRecord.command          type LogicalCommandInputRef -> CommandRef
                                        (rename_logical_command_input_union)

The other FIVE are covered by no undo at all, and they are the drift:
  RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry.grant_id                digest256 -> id256
  RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry.release_nonce           bytes     -> id256
  RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate.grant_id     digest256 -> id256
  RemoteRetentionReleaseAckCertificate.release_nonce bytes    -> id256
  RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone.release_nonce     bytes     -> id256

=== BUT THE FIVE ARE NOT THE WHOLE RED ===

Probed an undo restoring exactly those five to their 8a704c2 spelling:
  reconstruction  a86e33d4020143ef -> 69f3b79b0a6221c0
  floor                              236efa5babe190fe
It MOVES, so the five are genuinely part of the drift, and it does NOT reach the
floor. Since the field half is now exhaustively accounted (218 identical + 2
undo-touched + 5 undone = 225, zero remainder), the residue is by elimination in
the union/arm half — the 5 union, 8 arm, 6 ordinary-union and 18 ordinary-arm
lines I dumped but have NOT yet diffed against 8a704c2.

=== FOUR VALUES, PLUS THE TWO THIS BEAD ADDED ===

  bdbcdc27ccd92518  pre-repin floor, 5b76722..8a704c2~1   (unrecoverable, fgdb-7yo9)
  236efa5babe190fe  current floor, by RULING              (may not move)
  a86e33d4020143ef  HEAD reconstruction, unmodified       (the red)
  71729c11125d59d1  HEAD reconstruction, a02 cohort filtered
  69f3b79b0a6221c0  HEAD reconstruction, five id256 retypes undone   <- NEW
  (and: undoing fgdb-dbta's CommittedEffectCapsule re-order moves it ZERO bits,
   because those rows are already excluded from the namespace)

=== EXACT NEXT STEP, SO NOBODY REDOES ANY OF THIS ===

1. Diff the 37 retained union/arm lines (5+8+6+18) at HEAD against 8a704c2 the
   same way the 225 field lines were diffed. retained_HEAD.txt is already
   written by the probe in w3.rs; the 8a704c2 side comes from
   `git show 8a704c2:registries/durable_fields.toml`.
2. Extend undo_* to cover exactly the drifted lines — NOT a filter, which cannot
   fix content drift.
3. License it as the field half was licensed: retained count before and after,
   present versus consumed, zero missing. 225 = 218 + 2 + 5 is the template.
4. If after covering every drifted column the reconstruction still misses the
   floor, THAT is the larger finding and must be reported with all six values

Corrected a false negative in my own reader first: my block parser dropped every

ord-union 1, ord-arm 1". Controlled against known counts and fixed — 8a704c2 has

APPLYING BOTH REPAIRS — undo the five id256 retypes AND filter the two
post-erratum unions — the reconstruction walks but does not arrive:
  a86e33d4020143ef   unmodified
  69f3b79b0a6221c0   + five retypes undone
  e0245f1bf4c183fd   + two post-erratum unions filtered

than a missing cohort.

The floor was computed over 8a704c2's RECONSTRUCTION — the raw registries put

the committed-tree argument could not explain it and should never have been offered as

measure the appendix and find it wanting; it failed to WALK. I read it as 'the gate is

ANY APPENDIX-GATE RED MUST STATE THE CLEANLINESS OF THE ROOT IT WAS MEASURED ON --
git archive / pristine snapshot versus live worktree -- or it is not a report about
main. A gate result taken against an uncommitted worktree is a statement about one

    gate run, not at session start; peers commit into your blast radius continuously.
  * When the two roots of a two-root comparison differ in cleanliness as well as SHA,

title: Pin-cycle tool is blind to every CATALOG-side mint: it greps the wrong subcommand and the values it needs are unprintable
notes:
FIXED and LANDED. Repo half: 303042c. Tool half: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh (v2, full text below).

=== THE DEFECT, RED-PROVED ===
v1 ran `registry-check identity` and grepped its drift message. `identity`
validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections; a mint edits the CATALOG.
Until appendix-regenerate runs, the projections still agree with the OLD pins, so
identity exits 0 and v1 printed "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already
match the tree" on a tree whose pin was genuinely stale. FALSE GREEN -- the one
failure mode that makes a tool worse than no tool.
The drift exists only over catalog-derived identity, reached at appendix_a.rs:11442
where validate_identity is called on catalog.identity and every code is re-emitted
with a `projection_` prefix.

NOT LOGICAL-KINDS-ONLY -- CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. One row of each minted class added
to a pristine git-backed quiet root at HEAD 303042c, same binary, both subcommands:
    logical_object_kinds   identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
    wire_types             identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
    durable_fields         identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
The mechanism is structural, so physical_record_kinds / bootstrap_frames /
prebootstrap_artifact_kinds are blind by the same route; they simply never receive
mints. (First durable_fields probe returned catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch because
the synthetic row_id was malformed: row_id must derive as
{slice}:{kind}:{kebab(containing_schema)}-{kebab(stable_name)}. Recorded because it
aborts the run BEFORE any pin is reached, so a malformed probe reads as "no drift".)

SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER, fixed in-tree at 303042c: main.rs collapsed EVERY
appendix violation message to "Appendix A contract check failed", so even the right
subcommand printed no value to parse. v2 REQUIRES that fix and detects its absence.

=== CONTROLS, ALL AGAINST THE FINAL SCRIPT ===
  A   clean tree                  -> "no pin movement", 0 rewritten, exit 0
  B(i) stale logical-kind pin      -> reports AND corrects, restoring the exact
        (const corrupted)             pre-plant value, reaches CLEAN, exit 0
  B(ii) stale pin via CATALOG MINT -> DETECTED and corrected: 6 values rewritten.
        (the case v1 called green)    This is the defect class itself.
  C4  end-to-end replay of the real lquj mint onto pristine b4e50d9:
        reproduced 6 of 6 values derived BY HAND, and the resulting appendix_a.rs
        is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the hand-written commit 6b12cff. Ends PIN CYCLE
        COMPLETE, exit 0. Only identity.rs delta is expected_epoch -- see the gap.
  C5  idempotence                 -> re-run on the tool's own output: 0 rewritten
  C6  prerequisite regression     -> revert the main.rs fix and the tool exits 2
                                     rather than silently mis-parsing
  refuse: dirty identity.rs       -> exit 1 before building anything
  refuse: dirty appendix_a.rs     -> exit 1  (NEW: v1 guarded only identity.rs,
                                     while v2 also writes appendix_a.rs)
  allow:  dirty CATALOG           -> does NOT refuse, correctly: that file is the
                                     operator's working file and holds the mint
  bash -n OK; shellcheck --severity=warning clean.

ANTI-FALSE-GREEN IS THE POINT. When the gate is still red and a round rewrites
nothing, v2 prints the remaining codes and EXITS 1. Demonstrated live: a probe mint
with a DAG-illegal construction_order left census_dag_future_result standing, and
the tool re-pinned correctly and then REFUSED to call the cycle finished.
The one exception is projection_byte_diff alone, which is not a pin and not a
failure -- it means "now run appendix-regenerate", which v2 names as the NEXT STEP.

=== KNOWN GAP, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN ===
THE EPOCH BUMP IS UNDETECTABLE IN PRINCIPLE. registry_epoch lives in both the
catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const, and the checker only
compares those two against EACH OTHER. Bump neither and NO code fires, so no tool
can find it from checker output. v2 therefore prints the doctrine on every run that
rewrites a value. Adding/retiring a row owes the bump in BOTH places (precedent
e7b6f09; doctrine identity.rs:1206).

=== WHERE IT LIVES ===
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh, unchanged path. NOT promoted into
scripts/: a new tracked .sh owes a file-coverage-closure declaration row and a
shell-lint pass, which is an owner decision, not a side effect of this bead.
Full text below against the /data/tmp sweep.

=== FULL SCRIPT TEXT (v2) ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# refreeze_identity_pins.sh — the base-derived pin cycle, once, for everyone
# (fgdb-1j16 shape: fix the repeated procedure at the source, not per holder)
#
# HISTORY. Built at f9c8578 for fgdb-y5m1. Rewritten at fgdb-jkvc after fgdb-lquj
# proved the v1 tool BLIND TO EVERY CATALOG-SIDE MINT — the exact failure mode a
# tool must not have, because the beads that depend on it reported success while
# leaving the pin stale.
#
# WHAT WAS WRONG WITH v1, measured not inferred (fgdb-jkvc controls C1..C3):
#   v1 ran `registry-check identity` and grepped its drift message. But `identity`
#   validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections, and a mint edits the
#   CATALOG. Until appendix-regenerate runs, the projections still agree with the
#   old pins, so `identity` exits 0 and v1 printed
#       "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already match the tree"
#   on a tree whose pin was genuinely stale. FALSE GREEN.
#   The drift exists only over catalog-derived identity, reached at
#   appendix_a.rs:11442 where validate_identity is called on catalog.identity and
#   every code is re-emitted with a `projection_` prefix.
#   NOT logical-kinds-only. Measured on one row of each minted class against a
#   git-backed quiet root:
#       logical_object_kinds  identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#       wire_types            identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#       durable_fields        identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#   The mechanism is structural, so the three static registries
#   (physical_record_kinds, bootstrap_frames, prebootstrap_artifact_kinds) are
#   blind by the same route; they simply never receive mints.
#
#   SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER: main.rs collapsed EVERY appendix violation
#   message to "Appendix A contract check failed", so even the right subcommand
#   printed no value to parse. That is fixed in-tree by fgdb-jkvc; this script
#   REQUIRES that fix and checks for it rather than silently mis-parsing.
#
# WHY IT PARSES RATHER THAN ACCEPTS A VALUE. HEAD moves several times per
# increment in this swarm, so any pin read a minute ago is already suspect. This
# script never takes a pin from its caller: every NEW value below is read out of
# the checker's own message.
#
# EXIT 0 = the appendix gate is clean (it may have written).
# EXIT 1 = refused to start, or drift survives. NEVER exit 0 with drift outstanding.
# EXIT 2 = the checker could not be built, or emitted a verdict this cannot parse.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="${FGDB_ROOT:-/data/projects/frankengraphdb}"
PINS="$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs"
APX="$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs"
CAT="$ROOT/registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml"
CACHE="${FGDB_PIN_CACHE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fgdb-pin-cycle}"
MAX_ROUNDS="${FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS:-6}"
mkdir -p "$CACHE"

log() { printf '[refreeze-pins] %s\n' "$*"; }

# --- refuse to absorb a peer's edit ------------------------------------------
# Checked BEFORE anything is built, so a refusal costs nothing.
#
# SCOPE, and why it is not "every file I touch": identity.rs and appendix_a.rs
# are pure pin-carriers here — nobody should have them dirty while you re-freeze.
# The CATALOG is deliberately EXCLUDED: it is the operator's working file and it
# is *expected* to be dirty, because it is holding the mint you just applied.
# Guarding it would refuse on every legitimate invocation.
if (cd "$ROOT" && git rev-parse --git-dir) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for guarded in "$PINS" "$APX"; do
    rel="${guarded#"$ROOT"/}"
    if [ -n "$(cd "$ROOT" && git status --porcelain -- "$rel")" ]; then
      log "REFUSING: $rel already has uncommitted changes."
      log "  This script cannot tell your pin edit from a peer's in-flight work."
      log "  Commit or hand back that edit first, then re-run."
      exit 1
    fi
  done
else
  # A non-repo root has no peers to absorb, so the guard is vacuous rather than
  # skipped-in-silence. Said out loud because a guard that quietly does nothing
  # is the defect this whole swarm keeps closing.
  log "NOTICE: $ROOT is not a git worktree; the peer-edit guard does not apply here."
fi

# --- build the checker, every round, from the tree under test ----------------
# A stale binary and a real drift are indistinguishable from the output; this is
# measured, not hypothetical (a binary a few commits old reported five drift
# codes on a tree a fresh build called clean).
build_checker() {
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR="$ROOT/tools/registry-check" rustc --edition=2024 \
    --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check -C strip=symbols \
    "$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs" -o "$CACHE/libregistry_check.rlib" \
    >"$CACHE/build.log" 2>&1 || return 1
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR="$ROOT/tools/registry-check" rustc --edition=2024 \
    -C strip=symbols "$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/main.rs" \
    -L "$CACHE" --extern "registry_check=$CACHE/libregistry_check.rlib" \
    -o "$CACHE/registry-check" >>"$CACHE/build.log" 2>&1 || return 1
}

# The APPENDIX path, not identity — see the header. Raw text, parsed per family.
appendix_report() {
  "$CACHE/registry-check" appendix --root "$ROOT" 2>&1
}

# Rewrite exactly one literal in one file, or refuse. Never a regex over a file.
rewrite_one() {
  local file="$1" old="$2" new="$3" label="$4"
  [ "$old" = "$new" ] && return 0
  python3 - "$file" "$old" "$new" "$label" <<'PY'
import sys
path, old, new, label = sys.argv[1:5]
text = open(path).read()
count = text.count(old)
if count != 1:
    print(f"FATAL: {label}: {old!r} appears {count} times in {path}; refusing to guess")
    raise SystemExit(2)
open(path, "w").write(text.replace(old, new))
PY
  local rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && return "$rc"
  log "  rewrote  $label  $old  ->  $new"
  moved_total=$((moved_total + 1))
  return 0
}

moved_total=0
epoch_warned=0

for round in $(seq 1 "$MAX_ROUNDS"); do
  log "round $round: building the checker from the current tree"
  if ! build_checker; then
    log "FATAL: cannot build the checker (see $CACHE/build.log)"
    exit 2
  fi

  report="$(appendix_report)"
  if ! printf '%s' "$report" | grep -q '"event":"violation"'; then
    if [ "$round" -eq 1 ]; then
      log "no pin movement: the appendix gate is already clean"
    else
      log "appendix gate is CLEAN after $((round - 1)) rewrite round(s)"
    fi
    log "SUMMARY: $moved_total value(s) rewritten"
    [ "$moved_total" -gt 0 ] && [ "$epoch_warned" -eq 0 ] && \
      log "REMINDER: an added/retired row also owes a registry_epoch bump in BOTH the catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const (identity.rs doctrine; precedent e7b6f09). Nothing detects a missing bump, so it is on you."
    exit 0
  fi

  # Guard against the swallowed-message regression: if the fixed string is back,
  # every parse below silently finds nothing and we would loop to a false FATAL.
  if printf '%s' "$report" | grep -q 'Appendix A contract check failed'; then
    log "FATAL: the binary is emitting the collapsed message 'Appendix A contract check failed'."
    log "  main.rs appendix_violation_message must return violation.msg (fgdb-jkvc)."
    log "  Without it no recomputed value is printable and this script cannot be base-derived."
    exit 2
  fi

  before="$moved_total"

  # --- family 1: the six assignment pins (identity.rs) ----------------------
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r old new; do
    [ -z "${old:-}" ] && continue
    rewrite_one "$PINS" "\"$old\"" "\"$new\"" "assignment-pin" || exit 2
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'released assignment pin "[^"]*" != recomputed "[^"]*"' \
    | sed 's/released assignment pin "//; s/" != recomputed "/\t/; s/"$//' | sort -u)

  # --- family 2: projection row count + row-id transcript (appendix_a.rs) ---
  # Message carries BOTH sides, so both are base-derived.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r oldn olds newn news; do
    [ -z "${oldn:-}" ] && continue
    rewrite_one "$APX" "EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT: usize = $oldn;" \
                       "EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT: usize = $newn;" "projection-row-count" || exit 2
    rewrite_one "$APX" "\"$olds\"" "\"$news\"" "projection-row-ids-sha256" || exit 2
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'must contain [0-9]* rows with sha256 [0-9a-f]*; found [0-9]* rows with sha256 [0-9a-f]*' \
    | sed 's/must contain //; s/ rows with sha256 /\t/; s/; found /\t/; s/ rows with sha256 /\t/' | sort -u)

  # --- family 3: target/source assignment (appendix_a.rs + the catalog) -----
  # This message carries only the RECOMPUTED side. The OLD side is therefore
  # located by its const name / TOML key rather than parsed — the VALUE is still
  # the checker's, which is what "base-derived" protects.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r newcount newsha; do
    [ -z "${newcount:-}" ] && continue
    # `grep -o` suppresses -A context, so the const name and its value must be
    # matched in two stages or the value is silently never found (measured: the
    # one-stage form rewrote the catalog and left appendix_a.rs stale).
    oldsha="$(grep -A1 'EXPECTED_TARGET_SOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_SHA256' "$APX" \
              | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$oldsha" ] && rewrite_one "$APX" "\"$oldsha\"" "\"$newsha\"" "target-source-sha256" || true
    oldcount="$(grep -A1 '^\[target_manifest\]$' "$CAT" | grep -oE 'target_count = [0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$oldcount" ] && [ "$oldcount" != "$newcount" ]; then
      rewrite_one "$CAT" "[target_manifest]
target_count = $oldcount" "[target_manifest]
target_count = $newcount" "catalog-target-count" || exit 2
    fi
    oldcatsha="$(grep -oE '^target_source_assignment_sha256 = "[0-9a-f]{64}"$' "$CAT" | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$oldcatsha" ] && [ "$oldcatsha" != "$newsha" ] && \
      rewrite_one "$CAT" "\"$oldcatsha\"" "\"$newsha\"" "catalog-target-source-sha256" || true
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'must remain pinned at [0-9]* targets, [0-9]* projection fallbacks, and sha256 [0-9a-f]*' \
    | sed 's/must remain pinned at //; s/ targets, [0-9]* projection fallbacks, and sha256 /\t/' | sort -u)

  if [ "$moved_total" -eq "$before" ]; then
    # projection_byte_diff is NOT a pin and NOT a failure: it says the checked-in
    # projections have not been regenerated yet, which is the documented NEXT step
    # (this script runs BEFORE appendix-regenerate by design). Exiting 1 here would
    # report a completed pin cycle as a failed one. Anything else is a real stop.
    remaining="$(printf '%s' "$report" | grep -oE '"code":"[a-z_0-9]+"' | sort -u)"
    if [ "$remaining" = '"code":"projection_byte_diff"' ]; then
      log "PIN CYCLE COMPLETE: every assignment/count/sha pin is frozen and re-verified."
      log "SUMMARY: $moved_total value(s) rewritten"
      log "NEXT STEP, required, this script deliberately does not write projections:"
      log "    registry-check appendix-regenerate --root $ROOT"
      log "REMINDER: an added/retired row also owes a registry_epoch bump in BOTH the catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const (identity.rs doctrine; precedent e7b6f09). Nothing detects a missing bump, so it is on you."
      exit 0
    fi
    log "FATAL: the appendix gate is red but this round rewrote NOTHING."
    log "  These violations are outside what this tool knows how to re-pin:"
    printf '%s' "$report" | grep -oE '"code":"[a-z_0-9]+"' | sort -u | sed 's/^/    /'
    log "  Repair them by hand. Exiting NONZERO on purpose: a pin cycle that"
    log "  cannot finish must never look like one that did."
    exit 1
  fi
done

log "FATAL: drift still present after $MAX_ROUNDS rounds; something else is moving the pins"
exit 1

title: token.sh has no timeout: an expired lease still blocks, and clearing it needs a human steal after TTL+20m
notes:
=== pane2, read from /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh directly. Orchestrator's finding; recorded so it outlives the session. ===

A TTL IN THIS SUBSTRATE IS A LABEL, NOT A TIMEOUT.

  token.sh:56   acquire is `mkdir "$lock"`. If the directory exists the acquire
                FAILS -- unconditionally, regardless of the hold's age. Nothing
                anywhere reaps an expired lock.
  token.sh:65   age > ttl + 20m only changes what `status` PRINTS:
                "HELD by X for Nm — EXCEEDS ttl Lm + 20m grace"
  token.sh:67   and then it prints an instruction for a HUMAN: `token.sh steal`.
  token.sh:99   steal is the only path that clears another holder, and its own
                usage line says "only after the holder is proven dead".

CONSEQUENCES, which are what matter:
  * An expired lease keeps blocking until the holder releases or a human steals.
  * A pane that dies or is rotated mid-hold blocks that lane for a MINIMUM of
    TTL + 20m -- 32 minutes on a 12m lease -- and then still needs a human
    ruling, because "proven dead" is not something the script can decide.
  * Therefore every TTL cap enforced tonight was ADVISORY. The thing that
    actually prevented starvation was the release discipline: acquire, work,
    release in the same tool sequence. Not the number.

MEASURED TONIGHT, not hypothetical: pane3's lander
(/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_i1rx_apply3/autoland.sh) sat in a sleep-3 retry loop
for ~25 minutes against exactly this mechanism, losing every race to panes that
were already awake and holding longer leases. The swarm went four ticks with zero
commits while a fully-derived apply waited behind a token.

WHY A POLLING LOOP LOSES: acquire is non-blocking and there is no queue, so
`mkdir` is won by whoever calls it in the instant after a release. A pane polling
every 3s competes with panes that release-and-immediately-reacquire, and FIFO by
wait time is not expressible in the substrate at all -- it exists only as
orchestrator arbitration.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none applied here, roughly increasing in cost:
  1. Make the grace expiry ACT: let acquire break a lock older than ttl+grace and
     log the break loudly, rather than only printing advice. Removes the 32-minute
     floor for a dead holder. Risk: breaks a live-but-slow holder, which is
     exactly what the current design refuses to do -- so it needs a liveness
     probe, not an age threshold. (Compare the age-vs-liveness lesson already
     learned on stale bead sweeps: age cannot distinguish dead from parked.)
  2. Add a real QUEUE: a ticket file per waiter so FIFO-by-wait-time is mechanical
     rather than an orchestrator ruling every time.
  3. Have the holder write its PID, so "proven dead" becomes checkable instead of
     human-judged.
NOTE 1 and 3 compose: a PID that no longer exists is a liveness answer, not an age
one, and is the only safe basis for an automatic break.

The script's own comment at :87 already names the hazard from the other side --
"a legitimately-working holder's TTL silently becomes a lie, which invites either
a bad steal or an agent abandoning correct work to look compliant." That comment
is right, and this bead is its mirror image: the same design also means a DEAD
holder blocks indefinitely. Both follow from there being no liveness signal.

title: g0 root snapshot guard is blind to 76.7% of the bytes it exists to protect
description:
The root before/after guard landed on fgdb-kwoz (dc5421a) and rescoped by
fgdb-flbb (a22f241) digests $ROOT at entry and exit so that hard-linking support
inputs into fixture roots is safe BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by census. That
claim is the entire justification for linking, and for the catalog second
increment this bead's parent defers until the guard exists.

snapshot_nonprojection_tree excludes './.beads' and './.beads/*' (a22f241, added
so that peer bead-flushes during a run do not fire the guard).

.beads/issues.jsonl is 8,008 KB of the 10,440 KB linkable set: 76.7%. It is also
the linked file with the largest blast radius, staged into 27 fixtures at nlink=28.

So the guard covers 23.3% of the bytes whose safety it is cited for.

=== MUTATION-PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ===

Driving the landed function verbatim (sed-extracted from the gate, no
reimplementation) over a copy of the tracked tree:

  pristine                                    102442aeb80f19d7
  append to .beads/issues.jsonl               102442aeb80f19d7   <== BLIND
  append to tools/registry-check/src/main.rs  671b62310b1ff235   <== FIRES

The second line is the control. The reader works, so the first line is a domain
gap and not a broken probe.

=== NOT LIVE TODAY, AND WHY IT STILL MATTERS ===

fgdb-kwoz's census closes the fact that no fixture references any linked path
after staging, and the 2026-07-27 paired run confirms it empirically (`diff -rq`
of the root against its pristine snapshot is clean after a full run). So no write
-through happens today.

The defect is that this is a defence-in-depth control, and the thing it would
fail to catch is exactly the thing it was built for: a FUTURE edit that starts
writing a linked path. The census is a snapshot of one HEAD; the guard was
supposed to be the standing instrument that outlives it.

=== WIDENING THE GUARD IS THE WRONG FIX ===

Dropping the .beads exclusion re-introduces the false positive a22f241 fixed: in
the real repo, peers flush beads mid-run and the guard fires on coordination
state rather than on write-through.

=== PROPOSED INSTRUMENT (designed, not implemented) ===

Digest the FIXTURE copy, not $ROOT. A path under $WORK is reachable only by the
gate, so it is immune to peer churn by construction, and it measures the actual
law -- "no fixture wrote a linked inode after staging" -- instead of a proxy for
it. Capture each linked file's digest at staging time inside
stage_appendix_support and re-verify at exit. Cost is one sha256 sweep over the
linked set (~10 MB, deduplicated by inode).

It needs a completeness guard that fails CLOSED, with its own violation code:
assert that the set of re-verified paths equals the set staged. Without it, a
future class added to stage_appendix_support silently escapes verification in
exactly the way .beads does now -- the same defect one layer up.

=== ONE THING NOT MEASURED ===

Whether `br sync --flush-only` rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl in place or via
temp+rename. If in place, a peer flush during a gate run mutates the very inode
the 27 fixtures link, corrupting fixture inputs mid-run independently of this
guard. That is a live hazard rather than a latent one, it is cheap to measure
(stat the inode across a flush), and it should be settled before the catalog
second increment enlarges the linked set.

Found by pane2 while closing the deferred verification on fgdb-kwoz, 2026-07-27,
HEAD d747cb8. Nothing deleted.

title: a10 ERRATUM in the i1rx mint: ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared is a census truncation of a 6-member slash-compressed token, typed u64 by invention
notes:
=== FILED BY THE PANE THAT CAUSED IT (pane3). Landed in 3c1c936 (fgdb-i1rx), found ~40 minutes later while working fgdb-ty4g. ===

THE DEFECT. registries/durable_fields.toml, ConfigurationTransitionSpec field_tag
0x000b:
    stable_name     = "required_prepared"
    exact_wire_type = "u64"
    max_size_bytes  = 8
The a10:1920 source token is
    required_prepared/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor
which is the plan's SLASH-COMPRESSION idiom for a family of members --
required_{prepared,certificate,remote,key,audit,backup}_obligation_floor -- i.e. SIX
members, not one. So the landed row is wrong three ways:
  1. the stable_name is a CENSUS TRUNCATION ARTIFACT, not a source member name;
  2. the exact_wire_type u64 was INVENTED -- nothing in the source says scalar;
  3. one field row stands where the source spells six.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH EVERY GATE. The census itself cannot express the token. Asked
directly it returns ONE candidate:
    name  = required_prepared
    exact = ["/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor"]
    ambig = true
It split at the FIRST slash and made the remainder the "exact type" -- a string
beginning with '/', which is not a type at all. Every gate then agreed with the census:
appendix exit 0, identity exit 0, suite 130/130, and the checker cannot object because
the row is internally consistent. A green gate is not evidence about a member the
source reader mis-tokenised.

THE SOURCE DOES DETERMINE IT -- this is NOT an owner ruling about intent. The sibling
schema MetaConfigurationTransitionSpec at a10:1804 spells the SAME family uncompressed:
    required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor>
    required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>
so the Local spelling is the compressed form of six analogous members, and the sibling
also shows they are STRONGREF FLOOR REFERENCES, not u64 scalars. Ask the sibling, not
the census.

THE REPAIR IS FREE TODAY AND WILL NOT STAY FREE. version_status = "reserved" on this
row and 0 of 2373 durable_fields rows are "released", so the append-only law -- which
binds released codes, tags and names -- does not bind yet. Renumbering is therefore
still legal. Once anything releases, a truncated name and an invented type are frozen
into the durable format.

WHAT IS UNDECIDED AND NEEDS A ONE-LINE RULING:
  (a) do the six land as six separate required_*_obligation_floor_ref members following
      the Meta sibling, or as ONE member with a non-truncated name covering the six
      domains? The sibling supports six; only the compression is ambiguous.
  (b) if six, the field_tag layout: 0x000b is the bad row and 0x000c is
      terminal_audit_gate, so either renumber 0x000b..0x0011 and push terminal_audit
      _gate to 0x0011 (clean while nothing is released, and my recommendation), or
      append the six above 0x000c and leave a retired hole at 0x000b.
  (c) each of the six needs a target schema; MetaCertificateFloor and
      RemoteObligationFloor exist for the Meta variants, but the Local analogues are
      not yet identified and some may be unregistered.

GENERAL FINDING, BIGGER THAN THIS ROW: the slash-compression idiom appears at least 12
times in the plan (sorted_constraint/temporal/escrow_contribution_retractions,
old/new_shard_configuration_refs, expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs,
through_shard_index/global_prefix, incoming/outgoing_edges, global_txn_id/
global_commit_seq, role/posture/feature_predicate, ...) and ZERO of them have landed in
any form -- neither truncated nor expanded -- so this mint is the FIRST landing of the
idiom anywhere and it landed wrong. Every future slice hitting one of those 12 tokens
will get the same truncated candidate with a '/'-prefixed exact type. The census reader
should either expand the token or refuse it with its own violation code rather than
emitting a member whose name is a prefix and whose type is a slash. Filing that as the
durable half of this bead.
close_reason: ERRATUM REMOVED, not corrected: the a08:1804 uncompressed sibling falsifies the six-name expansion, so no field row is claimed for a10:1920 position 11. pane2's patch superseded with reason; its pin work stands. d4b0aa2.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
pane2, 2026-07-27, HEAD d747cb8. Re-derived every inherited number before acting.
One of them was mine and was wrong; it is corrected below.

=== 1. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SPELLS (FORCED) ===

a10:1920, verbatim, with NO type annotation:

    required_prepared/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor

= six members, required_{prepared,certificate,remote,key,audit,backup}_obligation_floor.
It is source position 11 of 12; terminal_audit_gate is position 12. Both position
tags are recorded correctly on the landed rows, so the ORDER is right and only the
member at position 11 is wrong.

=== 2. THE u64 HAS NO SOURCE BASIS WHATSOEVER (FORCED) ===

The token carries no type annotation, unlike its own neighbours in the same body --
`paired_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>` is annotated three
members earlier.

The landed row justifies u64 by citing "the Appendix A u64 floor law". That string
occurs in exactly TWO places in this repository: the defective row itself
(durable_fields.toml:1681) and its catalog mirror (appendix_a_catalog.toml:111137).
It appears nowhere in the plan, nowhere in tools/registry-check, and in no other
registry. The row invents the type AND invents the law that licenses the type.

Separately: the census emitted the artifact `exact = ["/certificate/remote/key/
audit/backup_obligation_floor"]`, a string beginning with '/'. ZERO rows in either
artifact carry an exact_wire_type containing '/', and ZERO catalog candidates carry
a '/'-prefixed exact type. So the artifact was not left in place -- it was SEEN and
PAPERED OVER with an invented scalar. That is a stronger claim than "the census
misled the mint".

=== 3. REPLACE, NOT WIDEN -- AND THIS IS FORCED UNDER BOTH BRANCHES ===

The replace/widen question is decidable even though the type question is not:

  - If the six are StrongRef: `u64` is a member of identity::BUILTIN_WIRE_TYPES
    (11 entries), which places the row OUTSIDE reference traversal entirely. That
    is the mechanism by which appendix exit 0, identity exit 0 and 130/130 all
    stayed green: the row was never in the domain of the laws that would object.
    A widened u64 stays outside that domain. Only a class change moves it in --
    exact_wire_type, identity_class inline->logical, reference_semantics
    none->strong, plus a target.

  - If the six are inline by value: it is still SIX rows where ONE stands. One row
    cannot become six by widening.

  - It is not even expressible: raising max_size_bytes past 8 while exact_wire_type
    stays "u64" is internally inconsistent.

So: REPLACE. No branch of the open question permits a widening.

=== 4. WHAT IS GENUINELY UNDECIDED -- ONE RULING, NAMED PRECISELY ===

The per-member WIRE TYPE. Typelessness is silence, so I am not inventing it in
either direction. The evidence points both ways and I am reporting both:

  FOR StrongRef:
    - the Meta sibling a10:1804 spells two of the same six domains explicitly as
      required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor> and
      required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>;
    - the nearest neighbour IN THE SAME SCHEMA, paired_config_payload_floor_ref
      (0x000a), is StrongRef / logical / strong / 40 -- and it is a floor;
    - of the 27 strong rows whose name lacks a _ref suffix, NOT ONE is a *_floor.
      They are all *_root, plural *_refs, sorted_*, or bare nouns.

  AGAINST (i.e. for inline by value):
    - the Local token has neither a _ref suffix nor an annotation;
    - _ref is a strong naming signal: 440 of 467 strong rows end in _ref (94.2%),
      only 25 of 509 non-strong do (4.9%), and 440 of the 465 names ending in _ref
      are strong (94.6%). Denominator 976 field rows.
    - but it is a 94% signal, NOT a law -- 27 counterexamples exist -- so it cannot
      settle the question by itself either.

  So: the sibling says StrongRef, the naming prior says inline. ONE LINE SETTLES IT.

=== 5. TARGETS ARE BLOCKED ON 4, AND 0 OF 7 EXIST ===

Candidate target schemas present in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml:

    ConfigPayloadFloor        1 row
    PreparedObligationFloor   0     CertificateFloor        0
    RemoteObligationFloor     0     KeyObligationFloor      0
    AuditObligationFloor      0     BackupObligationFloor   0
    MetaCertificateFloor      0

Even the two that the Meta sibling explicitly names as StrongRef targets are
unminted. So a StrongRef expansion cannot land today without minting targets first,
and the reservation bijection law forbids adding a reservation for a non-StrongRef
family -- so target work is BLOCKED on the ruling, not merely sequenced after it.

=== 6. ISOLATION -- LICENSED BY ACCOUNTING, NOT BY AN EMPTY SEARCH ===

WITHIN THE MINT (3c1c936): it touched exactly one schema. The a10:1920 body has 12
top-level members; 12 rows landed; 11 map 1:1 to source spellings; only position 11
is a truncation. ISOLATED -- verified row by row, not sampled.

ACROSS THE CORPUS: parsing 2,347 brace-balanced schema bodies and 15,679 top-level
members yields 13 distinct MEMBER-POSITION slash tokens. One of those,
role/posture/feature_predicate, is not a schema member at all -- it is plan line 292,
the plan describing durable_fields.toml's OWN column set, where the compression
correctly resolved to the column role_predicate. True denominator: 12.

Of those 12, exactly ONE has landed in any form: ours. Eleven are unlanded.

So the zero elsewhere is NOT evidence of a careful reader. It is arithmetic: the
idiom has landed exactly once, and it landed wrong. Every one of the remaining 11
will get the same truncated head and the same '/'-prefixed exact type the moment a
slice touches it.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST PASS: a permissive head-match reported 2 of 13 landed,
the second being role/posture/feature_predicate -> "role". Tightening the matcher by
containing_schema showed the three landed rows named "role" belong to
AuthorityBindingRecord, MandatoryInventory and ResourceLedgerState and are unrelated
legitimate members. 1 of 12, not 2 of 13. I also had to fix a delimiter bug in my
own block reader that had attributed a WitnessPolicy row to this schema -- the same
defect class this bead is about, in my own instrument.

=== 7. THE REPAIR SURFACE, AND THE TRAP IN IT ===

registries/durable_fields.toml IS A GENERATED PROJECTION -- registry-check reports
appendix_projection_checked durable_fields rows=2504, which matches an independent
count (976 field + 385 union + 1130 union_arm + 5 reference_union + 8
reference_union_arm = 2504). Editing it directly will be reverted by the projection
byte-verify.

The authoritative rows are in registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml:
    111125  [[field]]   stable_name = "required_prepared"
    111315  [[target]]  source_key  = "field|ConfigurationTransitionSpec|
                                       ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared|
                                       required_prepared"
The truncated name is embedded four times inside that one source_key. Three rows,
two artifacts, one authoritative edit site, then appendix-regenerate.

=== 8. RENUMBERING IS STILL FREE -- RE-DERIVED AT HEAD ===

title: br close on a BLOCKED issue exits 0 and hints 'already closed or not found', contradicting its own first line
notes:
Found while closing fgdb-ty4g; it is the same defect that made me report fgdb-dbta CLOSED to the orchestrator three times when it was still IN_PROGRESS.

REPRODUCTION, exact:
  $ br dep add A B          # B blocks A
  $ br close A --reason "..."
  Warning: Skipped A: blocked by: B
  Error: Nothing to do: all 1 issue(s) skipped
  Hint: All specified issues were already closed or not found.
  $ echo $?
  0

THREE SEPARATE PROBLEMS, in order of harm:
 1. EXIT 0 ON A NO-OP THAT PRINTS 'Error:'. Any automation, guard script or agent that
    branches on exit status reads SUCCESS while the issue is untouched. This is the
    same failure family as 'ubs exits 0 without scanning' and 'grep -c exits 1 on the
    success case': the status does not carry the outcome.
 2. THE HINT CONTRADICTS THE WARNING TWO LINES ABOVE IT. Line 1 states the true cause
    (blocked by B). The Hint then asserts a different, mutually exclusive cause --
    already closed, or not found. A reader who trusts the last line, which is where
    CLIs conventionally put the actionable summary, concludes the issue is CLOSED. I
    did exactly that on dbta and reported it closed three times before verifying.
 3. 'blocked by' IS A POLICY REFUSAL, NOT AN ERROR. Refusing to close a blocked issue
    is defensible, but it should be a distinct exit code and a distinct message, so
    'refused, here is the blocker' is never confusable with 'nothing matched'.

SUGGESTED FIX: exit non-zero when zero issues were modified; make the Hint conditional
on the actual skip reason (blocked / already-closed / not-found are three different
hints); and print the blocker id in the summary line rather than only the warning.

DETECTION RULE FOR AGENTS UNTIL IT IS FIXED, and it is cheap: never believe a br
mutation from its own output. Re-read the record -- 'br show <id> | head -1' or the
JSONL at HEAD -- before reporting a state change. A tool's message about what it did is
not evidence that it did it. Same family as [[stale-binary-reports-phantom-pin-drift]]:
when a tool tells you about the data, control the tool.

title: Sweep every law-citation string in the catalog against the laws that actually exist, fail-closed
description:
ORIGIN. fgdb-hvfn. The row ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared justified an
invented u64 by citing "the Appendix A u64 floor law". MEASURED at HEAD d747cb8: that
string occurs in exactly TWO places in this repository -- the row itself
(durable_fields.toml:1681) and its catalog mirror (appendix_a_catalog.toml:111137).
It appears nowhere in COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md, nowhere
in tools/registry-check, and in no other registry. The row invented the type AND
invented the law that licensed the type.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A WRONG VALUE. A wrong value is a value; the next reader can
re-derive it. A fabricated citation MANUFACTURES AUTHORITY. Every later reader
inherits a rule that was never adopted, and the next mint can cite the same phantom
law as precedent in perfect good faith. The failure is silent by construction: the
row was internally consistent, so appendix exited 0, identity exited 0, and the suite
was 130/130. No gate can object to a citation it never resolves.

THE ASK. Sweep EVERY law-citation string in the catalog against the set of laws that
actually exist. Own violation code. Fail closed.

=== DESIGN ===

1. BUILD THE LAW SET. Candidate sources, to be measured not assumed:
     - named laws in the plan (Appendix A prose, the doctrine, FG-INV-01..20)
     - violation codes the checker can emit
     - owner rulings with a stable id
   The set must include PROHIBITION laws, not only affirmative ones. Per the
   doctrine finding already on the board, a bare "citations must resolve" rule
   inverts the doctrine unless it classifies prohibitions -- a row citing a law that
   FORBIDS something must not be read as licensed by it.

2. EXTRACT EVERY CITATION-SHAPED PHRASE from catalog free text. retention_and_cut_rule
   is the dominant carrier but NOT the only one: rationale strings on ambiguity
   adjudications also cite laws and rulings (appendix_a.rs:4882 is a live example --
   "the owner ruling therefore selects the builtin opaque id256 form").

3. REQUIRE EACH TO RESOLVE, with its own violation code.

4. COMPLETENESS GUARD, FAILING CLOSED. The extractor must ACCOUNT FOR every
   citation-shaped phrase it sees. A phrase the extractor does not recognise must
   FAIL, not be skipped -- otherwise the sweep is vacuous in exactly the region where
   a fabricated citation lives, since a fabricated law is by definition the one the
   extractor has no entry for. This guard is the whole instrument; without it the
   sweep passes on the very row that motivated it.

=== MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING ===

State the denominator first: how many citation-shaped phrases exist in the catalog,
and how many resolve against the law set, BEFORE writing the checker. If the
unresolved count is large the design is wrong (the extractor is over-matching); if it
is zero on a corpus known to contain at least one fabrication, the extractor is
under-matching and the control cannot fire. Prove both directions with a mutation:
plant a fabricated citation and confirm it is caught, and confirm a real citation is
not.

=== KNOWN INSTANCE TO USE AS THE POSITIVE CONTROL ===

"the Appendix A u64 floor law" -- 2 occurrences, 0 supporting definitions. Note that
fgdb-hvfn's repair removes both occurrences, so capture the fixture BEFORE that lands
or the control disappears with it.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.

Step 3 extracted to fgdb-law-citation-guard-ld8f, which now carries the 23u1 dependency.

pane2, 2026-07-27, HEAD a7ea5ce. DENOMINATOR MEASURED BEFORE ANY CHECKER WAS WRITTEN,
as this bead requires. The result changes the bead's premise and I am reporting it
before building.

=== THE CORPUS ===

registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml, prose-carrying keys identified by mean value
length rather than by guess: retention_and_cut_rule (984 values), rationale (450),
transcript_recipe (20), encoding_context (942), plus 8 small keys. 2,440 prose values,
404,560 characters scanned.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===

  11 distinct cited law names
  94 occurrences
   0 of 11 defined as a law anywhere in the plan or the checker

  n   cited law name                       referent exists?  defined as a law?
  69  flattened-rendering                  no                NO
  12  compact-phrase                       no                NO
   2  StrongRef-only arm-payload-shape     no                NO
   2  ConsensusDomain per the shorthand    no                NO
   2  SequenceNeutralSpec                  YES               NO
   2  Appendix A u64 sequence              no                NO
   1  SequenceNeutralSpec wrapper          no                NO
   1  No source                            YES               NO
   1  Appendix A u64 index                 no                NO
   1  D1 closure                           YES               NO
   1  Appendix A u64 floor                 no                NO

THE SET OF LAWS THAT ACTUALLY EXIST IS EMPTY. There is no law registry in this
repository -- no table, no enumeration, no artifact that defines a named law and its
statement. So a sweep "against the set of laws that actually exist" resolves 0 of 94
citations, and the checker this bead asks for would flag every one of them.

=== "the Appendix A u64 floor law" IS NOT THE OUTLIER; IT IS THE SMALLEST INSTANCE ===

It has ONE occurrence. The dominant citation is "the flattened-rendering law" at 69
occurrences -- 73% of all law citations in the catalog -- and it has no referent under
any of four spelling variants tested (flattened-rendering, flattened rendering,
flattened_rendering, flatten). The bare verb "flatten" appears 10 times in the plan;
no artifact anywhere defines a flattened-rendering LAW.

It also has two siblings nobody had looked at: "the Appendix A u64 sequence law" (2)
and "the Appendix A u64 index law" (1). So the u64 family is 4 occurrences across 3
invented variants, not one row.

=== TWO CLASSES, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT REPAIRS ===

  Class A -- cites a REAL referent, invents its legal status (3 of 11):
    SequenceNeutralSpec (a real schema, 12 plan mentions), D1 closure, "No source".
    Repair: rewrite the citation to name the thing without calling it a law, or
    promote it to a real law with a statement.

  Class B -- cites nothing that exists (8 of 11, 88 of 94 occurrences):
    flattened-rendering, compact-phrase, StrongRef-only arm-payload-shape,
    ConsensusDomain-per-the-shorthand, SequenceNeutralSpec wrapper, and the three
    Appendix A u64 variants.
    Repair: define the law, or retract the citation.

=== WHY THIS WAS NEVER NOTICED -- A CIRCULARITY WORTH ITS OWN NOTE ===

tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs MIRRORS the catalog's prose: its 450
AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT pins embed rationale strings verbatim. Stripping those
mirrored literals takes the file from 997,854 to 702,224 characters -- 296K chars,
30%, is copied catalog text.

So the obvious test, "is this law mentioned in the checker", RESOLVES A CITATION
AGAINST ITS OWN COPY. My first pass fell into exactly this: flattened-rendering,
compact-phrase and SequenceNeutralSpec all read "RESOLVES" until the mirror was
stripped, after which all three read 0. Any future implementation of this sweep MUST
strip the mirror or it will pass on every citation it is built to catch.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN ===

Building the fail-closed checker now would be correct and would immediately red the
tree on 94 occurrences, which is not landable in one increment. The bounded form is:

  1. Seed a law registry with these 11 rows. Each row is either DEFINED (name +
     statement + where it is enforced) or RETRACTED (citation rewritten).
     That converts an unbounded prose problem into an 11-row adjudication.
  2. Then land the checker: every citation-shaped phrase must resolve against that
     registry, own violation code, and a COMPLETENESS GUARD FAILING CLOSED -- an
     unrecognised citation-shaped phrase must FAIL, never be skipped, because a
     fabricated law is by definition the one the extractor has no entry for.
  3. Positive control is banked at
     /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_uzzh_control_fixture.txt, captured before fgdb-hvfn
     removes both occurrences of the u64 floor law. Negative control: any Class A
     citation, which must NOT fire once its referent is registered.

Step 1 is an owner-facing adjudication (11 rows, several of which are load-bearing
prose across 69 rows), so I am naming it rather than deciding it.

Nothing deleted. No repo file touched by this measurement.

                            forbidden_layers/options

                            exact_grid/ceiling_carry_proof_ref
                            through_shard_index/global_prefix

An expander that guesses commits, at 12 sites, exactly the category of error
fgdb-hvfn exists to remove -- inventing structure the source does not state. That is
very likely WHY the census truncates rather than expanding: truncation is a visible
wrong answer, and guessing is an invisible one.

=== THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY EXISTS ===

AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT (tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs:350) carries
450 pins, 390 of them field-type-ambiguous. A PER-TOKEN adjudication licenses one
expansion without inventing a general rule. It is the same table fgdb-ty4g is moving
450 -> 455, so the two beads share a mechanism.

=== MINIMUM VIABLE FIX, INDEPENDENT OF ADJUDICATION ===

Make the census REFUSE a member-position slash token, with its own violation code,
failing CLOSED -- instead of emitting a member whose name is a prefix and whose exact
type begins with '/'. That converts a silent wrong answer into a loud one and
protects the 11 unlanded tokens from repeating this.

It does NOT unblock hvfn by itself: hvfn needs the adjudication path so the six names
become producible. Refusal and adjudication are separate increments and the refusal
is the cheaper, more urgent one.

=== THE BANKED PATCH -- LAND IT, DO NOT RE-DERIVE IT ===

/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_hvfn_replace.patch  (3 files, +133/-13)

Holds the six correct rows in both artifacts plus all four re-derived pins. The next
holder should RE-APPLY it and re-derive the pins at their own HEAD -- the projection
pins move on nearly every Appendix A commit, so the pin values in the patch will be
stale even though the rows will not. The rows themselves are settled: u64 / one /
scalar / none / 8 / reserved, derived from 8-of-8 population evidence under the owner
INLINE ruling of 2026-07-27.

=== hvfn IS BLOCKED, NOT STALLED ===

Every proposition on fgdb-hvfn is closed: source spelling recovered, override
condition tested and not met, type and identity_class derived from measured
populations, replace written, pins re-derived with the licence checked, tree restored
green. There is NO further analysis to do on hvfn. It is waiting on this bead and on
nothing else.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.
