title: appendix_a.rs holds 30% of its own subject's prose: every existence query resolves against a copy
description:
tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs contains 302,724 characters of its own
subject's prose -- 30.3% of the file -- copied verbatim from
registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml.

  rationale             455 string literals   163,477 chars   16.4% of the file
  ambiguity_source_key  450 string literals   139,247 chars   14.0% of the file
                                              -------
                                              302,724         30.3%
  file total                                  997,854

Consequence: ANY QUERY OF THE FORM "does this rule/law/concept exist in the checker"
RESOLVES AGAINST A COPY OF THE THING BEING AUDITED. The checker cannot distinguish
"this rule is defined here" from "I am holding a copy of the sentence that cites it".

=== REPRODUCTION ===

Strip the mirrored literals and re-ask:

  python3: re.sub(r'(rationale|ambiguity_source_key):\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"', '<M>', src)
  997,854 chars -> 702,224 chars

  law name              before strip   after strip
  flattened-rendering     RESOLVES          0
  compact-phrase          RESOLVES          0
  SequenceNeutralSpec     RESOLVES          0

=== I FELL INTO THIS ON THE FIRST PASS, AND THAT IS THE EVIDENCE ===

Working fgdb-law-citation-sweep-uzzh I ran the obvious test -- "is this cited law
mentioned in the plan or the checker" -- and it returned RESOLVES for three of the
eleven cited laws. All three were false. Their only appearances in the checker were
inside the mirrored catalog prose: the checker was agreeing with the citation because
it was holding a copy of the citation.

I caught it only because the RESOLVES verdicts were implausible against a corpus I
had already measured as having no law registry. An auditor without that prior would
have shipped "3 of 11 laws are real" and the sweep would have licensed the phantoms.
That 0-of-94 result should be trusted BECAUSE the first pass failed this way and the
failure was found, not because the first pass was clean.

=== SEVERITY, SCOPED HONESTLY ===

NOT LIVE IN A SHIPPED VALIDATOR. No gate does a textual existence query over checker
source: scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh contains no grep/rg/awk over
tools/registry-check/src, and the 450 pins are compared STRUCTURALLY, field by field,
by ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. That function is sound, and
`row.rationale == pin.rationale` makes the mirror load-bearing on purpose: the catalog
cannot silently rewrite the justification for an adjudication without a reviewed
checker edit. THE PIN MECHANISM IS NOT THE DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED.

IMMINENT. The law-citation sweep this project just ruled to build (uzzh step 3) is
specified to resolve citations against the checker. Implemented the obvious way it
would pass on 100% of the citations it exists to catch -- including all 94.

DEMONSTRATED. Three false RESOLVES, above, by a careful reader.

=== THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE ANTIBODY, ONE FILE OVER ===

tools/registry-check/src/unsafe_ledger.rs:2519, inside #[cfg(test)]:

    /// The fixture must never be visible as real sites in this file. If this
    /// fails, the checker will fail its own crate -- and worse, a reader would
    /// see two "unsafe sites" in a std-only tooling crate that has none.
    fn fixture_is_not_visible_in_this_source() {
        let own_source = include_str!("unsafe_ledger.rs");
        assert_eq!(scan_sites("unsafe_ledger.rs", own_source), Vec::new(), ...);
    }

Somebody already recognised this exact class -- subject-like text embedded in the
checker corrupting the checker's own reading -- and guarded it for a fixture of a few
lines. appendix_a.rs carries 302,724 characters of subject prose with no equivalent
guard. The precedent is the argument: this is a known hazard in this codebase, left
unguarded at 30,000x the size.

=== PROPOSED INSTRUMENT (designed, not implemented) ===

1. SEPARATE THE MIRROR STRUCTURALLY. Move the 450 pins into their own module, e.g.
   appendix_a_adjudication_pins.rs. Then "the checker" and "the copy of the catalog"
   are different files, and a grep of the checker stops hitting the mirror by default.
   Cheapest change, largest share of the benefit, no behaviour change: the pins are
   still compiled, still compared structurally, still load-bearing.

2. A CANARY IN THE unsafe_ledger STYLE. Assert that a sentinel phrase occurring ONLY
   in catalog prose is not resolvable as a DEFINITION in checker source. Mutation-
   prove both directions: the canary must fire when the sentinel is present in a
   non-mirror region and stay silent when it is only in the mirror.

3. COMPLETENESS GUARD, FAILING CLOSED. Any resolution query over checker source must
   declare which regions it excludes and fail if it encounters a region it cannot
   classify as mirror-or-source. An unclassifiable region is exactly where a
   fabrication hides.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ===

Not a request to delete the mirror, shrink the pins, or relax
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. The freeze is correct. The defect is
that the mirror is indistinguishable from source to every reader and every future
query.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27, HEAD 1d19f02. Nothing deleted.
notes:
MEASURED AT HEAD 57610e9 (pane4). Numbers re-derived, not inherited.

=== 1. WHAT THE 296K IS: VERBATIM, 450/450, BOTH FIELDS ===
appendix_a.rs = 997,854 chars.
  rationale             455 literals  158,472 chars payload (163,477 with key prefix)  16.38%
  ambiguity_source_key  450 literals  129,347 chars payload (139,247 with key prefix)  13.95%
  MIRROR                              287,819 payload / 302,724 stripped              30.34%
Byte-identical to registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml for all 450 rows, both fields.
ZERO paraphrase. Bead's 302,724 reconciles exactly: it measured the strip incl.
the `field: ` prefix; payload alone is 28.84%.

MIRROR IS COMPLETE, NOT PARTIAL. The 4.46MB catalog holds exactly 450 `rationale =`
rows in total, all on [[ambiguity_adjudication]]. The checker pins every one. The
title understates it: the checker holds 100% OF THE CATALOG'S RATIONALE FIELD, and
that is 30% of the checker.

IT IS NOT 296K OF PROSE. Of the 129,347-char key field, 111,757 (86.4%) is
structural -- identifiers plus two 64-hex digests per key. Only 16,690 is prose,
from a closed 9-value enum. Real prose = 158,472 + 16,690 = 175,162 = 17.6%.

THE PROSE IS EVIDENCE, NOT LAW TEXT. 447/450 open with an aNN:LINE anchor.
411 distinct texts collapse to 102 skeletons under anchor/identifier masking.
ONLY 77 OF 450 ROWS (17.1%) CITE A LAW AT ALL: 82 real citations
(flattened-rendering x69, compact-phrase x12, SequenceNeutralSpec x1) plus the
one "No source law requires..." English over-match uzzh already corrected, which
this extractor independently reproduced as a control.

=== 2. WHO READS IT: EVERY CONSUMER NEEDS AN IDENTITY, NONE NEEDS THE PROSE ===
pin.rationale            -> exactly ONE reader: `==` at appendix_a.rs:11043
pin.ambiguity_source_key -> exactly ONE reader: `==` at appendix_a.rs:11031
Both inside ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. Its eight callers:
  :8200  census-coverage targeting      boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :8367  complete-slice ambiguity closure boolean gate -> reads row.ambiguity_source_key
  :8476  annotation ambiguity discharge  boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :11143 validate_readable_ambiguity_contract boolean gate -> violation code
  :12163 complete-slice top-level census boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :11060 approved_final_ambiguity_keys_with boolean gate -> reads row.ambiguity_source_key
  :16404,:16426 tests                    boolean gate
All eight use it as a yes/no approval predicate, then read the CATALOG row's
fields -- never the pin's. NO CALL SITE ANYWHERE READS pin.rationale AS TEXT.

=== 3. CIRCULAR QUERY CLASSES: EXISTENCE IS NOT THE ONLY ONE ===
Strip the two fields, recount. FILE SCOPE (appendix_a.rs):
  registered law names      4 pop   4 PHANTOM (100%)   `shorthand` 767 hits all copy
  ambiguity reason phrases  9 pop   9 PHANTOM (100%)   388 hits for one phrase
  64-hex digests         1264 pop 766 PHANTOM (60.6%)  largest population
  plan anchors aNN:LINE    72 pop   7 PHANTOM (9.7%)   a01:1412 = 76 hits, 100% copy
  catalog `symbol` values 1599 pop   9 PHANTOM (0.6%)
  catalog `source_key`   3809 pop   0 PHANTOM          hazard assumed -> FALSIFIED
TWO NEW CIRCULAR CLASSES BEYOND EXISTENCE:
  COUNTING queries -- durable_fields.toml reads 72 vs 3 outside the mirror, 24x.
  ANCHOR-RESOLUTION queries -- a01:1412 is the anchor of FG-LAW-01 AND FG-LAW-02
    and is 100% copy, so resolving BY ANCHOR instead of by name is equally
    circular. That kills the obvious workaround.

CRATE-SCOPE CORRECTION, OWED AGAINST THE FILE-SCOPE NUMBER. Across all 20
modules only 1 of 4 registered laws is crate-wide phantom (compact-phrase).
Every non-mirror occurrence of the other three was inspected:
  flattened-rendering -> laws.rs:6, a doc comment QUOTING the problem
  shorthand           -> ordinary English ("shorthand field", "union shorthand")
  SequenceNeutralSpec -> test-corpus fixture strings in appendix_source.rs
ZERO of the four is defined, named or enforced by name anywhere in the checker.
File-scope 4/4 and crate-scope 1/4 are both true of different questions; the
crate-scope one is what supports "the checker cannot answer this at all".

=== 4. WHAT BREAKS UNDER LAW-ID + DIGEST ===
DOES NOT BREAK -- and this asymmetry is what makes the change small:
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_sha256 is computed over
&catalog.ambiguity_adjudications (:10684) -- the loaded TOML rows, NOT the pin
array. So swapping pin prose for a digest is CHECKER-ONLY: zero catalog bytes,
NO re-pin of EXPECTED_AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_SHA256, no schema bump. The catalog
keeps its prose at its home. sha256(row.rationale)==pin.rationale_sha256 is
equivalent for all eight call sites. validate_ambiguity_adjudication_rows
(nonblank/non-placeholder) operates on catalog rows, untouched.

DOES BREAK -- three, one real:
(a) REVIEWER DIFF QUALITY. A catalog rationale rewrite becomes a hex diff, not a
    prose diff. The one genuine cost. Keeping source_locations, resolution and a
    new cited_laws readable preserves the DECISION; only the narrative moves.
(b) AN UNDECLARED DOCTRINE -- and a correction to pane4's own first report. The
    ":341-345 readable pins / opaque transcript digest is never authorization"
    comment does NOT govern this layer. Its subject is the four contracts
    declared immediately above it, and those four (annotation, semantic_binding,
    expansion_binding, evidence) are EXACTLY the four declared
    [[completion_layer]] rows carrying
    pin_policy = "compiled-count-sha256-readable-row-contract".
    ambiguity_adjudication IS NOT A DECLARED COMPLETION LAYER AT ALL. Its
    readability policy exists only in a function name
    (validate_readable_ambiguity_contract) and three violation strings. A
    450-row contract whose policy lives only in an identifier is a policy that
    is not pinned. FLAGGED, NOT ROUTED AROUND -- owner's call to declare or
    relax. Probably its own bead.
(c) The citation extractor must discriminate "No source law requires..." out.
    Red-prove both directions; do not allowlist the sentence.

ROW_ID ALREADY IS THE DIGEST. row_id = {slice}:ambiguity-adjudication:
sha256(ambiguity_source_key), enforced at :13036-13038, and the pin is FOUND by
row_id equality. So the 129,347-char key copy commits nothing pin.row_id does
not already commit. BUT both validators run in one validate_catalog pass and the
derivation check PUSHES rather than ABORTS, so the redundancy is a real
independent check: replace it with an explicit local
sha256(row.ambiguity_source_key) against the digest already inside pin.row_id.
Never a bare deletion.

=== REMOVAL CANDIDATES -- NAMED FOR OWNER AUTHORISATION, NOTHING REMOVED ===
1. The 450 `rationale:` literals, -158,472 chars. Replaced by rationale_sha256
   (450x64 = 28,800) + cited_laws: &[&str] (77 non-empty, ~1,200). NET -128,472.
2. The 450 `ambiguity_source_key:` literals, -129,347 chars, replaced by local
   re-derivation against the digest already in pin.row_id. NET -129,347, ZERO
   replacement bytes.
Combined -257,819: 30.3% -> ~3.0%, all four circular classes drop to zero in
appendix_a.rs, and the pin gains four registry-resolvable IDs. THE MIRROR
BECOMES UNNECESSARY, NOT SMALLER.
STAGING: (2) alone is the strictly-safer half -- pure redundancy against a law
the checker already enforces, no prose judgement, no doctrine question, and it
removes 766 of the phantom digests plus the whole 9-phrase enum. (1) is where
the readability trade-off and (b) live.

=== SAME FAMILY, ONE SCALE UP: THE SELF-DISABLING GUARD ===
Owner pairing: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree
(architecture_decisions.rs:950). Its control at :985 is
  assert!(write_and_validate(&corpus).is_empty(),
          "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors")
-- the LIVE repo corpus. When the repo is red from a bead-provenance cause,
which is precisely the class this guard exists to catch, the control fires FIRST
and the k=1..5 growth loop and the vacuity control NEVER EXECUTE. The guard is
disabled by the condition it detects (fgdb-ft79 recorded exactly this).

THE SHARED DEFECT: a mechanism whose VERDICT or REACHABILITY is a function of
the very condition it validates is not a validator.
  23u1  VERDICT coupling by CONTAINMENT -- checker holds a copy of its subject,
        so "does the subject contain X" always agrees. It CANNOT RETURN NO.
  lzol  REACHABILITY coupling by DEPENDENCE -- guard preconditions on subject
        health, so when the subject is unhealthy it CANNOT RETURN AT ALL.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ACTIONABLE PART. lzol fails LOUDLY RED -- it panics on the
control, which is why it was found and cleared in one night. 23u1 fails SILENTLY
GREEN -- it reports RESOLVES, and a first law sweep shipped three false RESOLVES
until the mirror was stripped. The one that fails loudly gets fixed; the one
that fails green survives every gate. That is why 23u1 is P1 and not a cleanup.

The lzol CONTROL IS NOT THE DEFECT and must not be removed -- without it an
empty violation set could mean the fixture is not being read (same law as
license-the-zero-by-accounting). The defect is that a FAILED CONTROL IS
INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FAILED GUARD in the report: the panic reads "the
unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors", which an operator
parses as "concurrent bead creation reds the tree" when what happened is "this
guard never ran". UNRUN MUST NOT READ AS FAILED, AND MUST NOT READ AS PASSED --
same law as no-cargo-flag-recovers-a-compile-failure. Suggested separate bead.

=== STATE ===
Nothing edited. No file deleted. No token held (read-only measurement; catalog
is pane3-avex's). No gate run because nothing changed -- pane4 has introduced no
red, so the reported architecture 42/42 green stands unchallenged by this work.
Caveat recorded honestly: a crude corpus-side reimplementation of the bet-label
rule flags 8 records, but the real checker carries [[bead_override]] rows and
family rules, so those 8 are NOT claimed as a red -- ask the checker, not the
corpus. Awaiting explicit authorisation on removal candidates 1 and/or 2.

title: check.sh reports RED not FAIL, and sends it to stderr while PASS goes to stdout
description:
scripts/check.sh reports a failing gate in a way that two common, reasonable
reader habits both miss. Both hazards are in the same four lines.

=== HAZARD 1: THE TOKEN IS "RED", NOT "FAIL" ===

  scripts/check.sh:65   echo "PASS core: $label"
  scripts/check.sh:69   echo "RED core: $label (exit $LAST_GATE_RC)" >&2
  scripts/check.sh:354  echo "PASS registered $kind $artifact — $detail"
  scripts/check.sh:360  echo "RED registered $kind $artifact — $detail" >&2

So `grep -c '^FAIL' <log>` returns 0 on a fully red run. The g0 e2e scripts DO
use FAIL (`[g0-identity-e2e] FAIL: ...`), so a reader who has worked with those
carries the wrong token over to check.sh and gets a clean answer from a red gate.

MEASURED, and this is not hypothetical: 2026-07-27, I ran check.sh over the
fgdb-law-citation-sweep-uzzh increment, grepped `^FAIL`, got 0, and reported "no
FAIL" to the orchestrator. The actual result was CORE GATES 4 passed / 3 red and
REGISTERED 15 passed / 6 red, and two of those reds were mine. I landed a commit
on that reading. The under-report was caught only because the final summary block
says "QUALITY GATE RED" in words.

=== HAZARD 2, STRICTLY WORSE: PASS GOES TO STDOUT, RED GOES TO STDERR ===

PASS is echoed to stdout; RED is echoed to `>&2`. So:

    bash scripts/check.sh > gate.log          # stderr not captured
    bash scripts/check.sh 2>/dev/null | ...   # stderr discarded

both produce a log containing EVERY PASS AND ZERO REDS. Not a truncated log, not
an obviously broken one -- a plausible, complete-looking, all-green transcript of
a red run. Demonstrated in one line:

    $ bash -c 'echo "PASS x"; echo "RED y" >&2' 2>/dev/null | grep -cE "^(PASS|RED)"
    1

A reader who redirects only stdout cannot distinguish a green run from a red one
by grepping at all. This is a fail-open in the REPORTING layer of the gate that
every other fail-open finding in this project has been measured with.

=== WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY ===

check.sh is the only gate that runs the file-coverage closure and the shell lint,
so it is the gate a pane runs when it has touched anything that is not .rs -- and
it is long enough (~6 minutes) that panes routinely background it into a log and
grep the log rather than watch it. The two habits that make that ergonomic are
exactly the two this defeats.

=== THE FIX, AND THE CONSTRAINT ON IT ===

Options, in increasing order of disruption:

  1. Emit an anchored FAIL alias line alongside each RED line, keeping RED for
     existing readers. Both `^RED` and `^FAIL` then work. Costs one extra line
     per red gate.
  2. Send RED to stdout as well as, or instead of, stderr.
  3. Rename RED -> FAIL outright. Breaks any reader currently grepping `^RED`.

MEASURED before proposing: nothing under scripts/ greps gate output for either
token (`grep -rn "grep.*\^FAIL\|grep -E '\^(PASS|FAIL)" scripts/*.sh` is empty),
so the blast radius is human/agent readers rather than code. Whoever takes this
should still check the check.sh self-test fixtures (scripts/check.sh:612+), which
build synthetic gate outputs and may assert on the exact line shape.

WHOEVER FIXES IT MUST RUN check.sh AFTERWARDS. A change to how a gate reports
failure is exactly the change that cannot be verified by reasoning about it, and
the run takes ~6 minutes with a build slot.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27, at owner request: this was found the hard way and
must not stay folk knowledge in a commit body. Nothing deleted.
close_reason: Fixed and landed at 2a82095. check.sh's whole verdict transcript is on stdout; stderr keeps diagnostics only; every failed gate emits an anchored RED/UNRUN line plus an anchored FAIL alias, so ^PASS/^RED/^UNRUN/^FAIL each count exactly one thing. Header states the exit code is authoritative. New --self-test control captures the streams SEPARATELY (every prior control merged them with 2>&1, which is why they all passed over this) and pins both directions; four mutations each produce a distinct named failure. VERIFIED on a live red tree: exit 1, stdout alone yields ^PASS 22 ^RED 6 ^UNRUN 0 ^FAIL 6, zero verdict lines stranded on stderr. The swept class is fgdb-udco.

Resolve by the registry's `name` field rather than rewriting catalog prose -- all 69 flattened-rendering citations live in `rationale`, which is byte-compared against the 450 compiled adjudication pins, so rewriting means 138 coordinated edits and enlarges the 23u1 mirror. A citation resolving to a row whose status is `fabrication-candidate` or `unadjudicated` must NOT be licensed. title: A guard whose precondition is the negation of its trigger: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree cannot fire when the tree is red
description:
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs carries a test named
`concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree`. It exists to prove that
one pane filing a bead cannot red the shared tree for every other pane.

IT CANNOT FIRE WHILE THE TREE IS RED FROM EXACTLY THAT CAUSE.

    thread 'concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree' panicked at
    tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs:985:5:
    the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors

The test mirrors the repo into a fixture, and its first act is to assert the
unmodified mirror is green. When the repo is red because a pane filed a bead
without a bet label, that precondition fails and the test aborts before it can
exercise the property it was written to defend. The guard is available in exactly
the circumstances where nothing is wrong, and unavailable in exactly the
circumstances it was built for.

=== MEASURED, 2026-07-27, HEAD dee62ef ===

Five of the 42 tests in the suite were failing, and ALL FIVE reduced to two beads
carrying no labels at all -- fgdb-wzyl and fgdb-h6kr:

    architecture_bead_provenance_is_total_pinned_and_bidirectional
    architecture_registry_parses_and_validates
    architecture_neg_semantic_change_with_stable_id
    concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree
    architecture-check (the registered binary) and g0_architecture_decisions_e2e

After labelling those two beads b5 under owner authorisation: 42 passed, 0
failed. So the population is confirmed at two, and the guard's unavailability is
confirmed to have been caused by the very class it detects.

I HIT THIS MYSELF, WHICH IS THE POINT. Earlier the same day I filed three beads
(uzzh, avex, 23u1) with labels g0,verification,appendix-a and no b1..b6 bet
label, redding the shared tree for every pane. The guard that exists to prevent
precisely that was already disabled -- by two earlier unlabelled beads -- so it
could not warn me, and I found the breakage only by reading a full check.sh
transcript afterwards.

=== WHY THIS SITS NEXT TO fgdb-checker-mirrors-subject-prose-23u1 ===

Same defect family, different mechanism:

  23u1  a validator holds a copy of its own subject, so an existence query
        resolves against the copy and cannot return "absent".
  this  a guard's precondition is the negation of the condition it detects, so
        it cannot return "violated".

In both cases the instrument is structurally incapable of producing the answer it
was built to produce, and in both cases every gate stays green -- or in this case
merely red for a different-looking reason -- while the specific protection is
absent. A precondition that is the negation of the trigger is a fail-open, and it
should be reported as one rather than as a cascading failure.

=== WHAT A FIX HAS TO PRESERVE ===

The green-mirror precondition is not gratuitous: without it the test cannot tell
its own planted mutation from ambient repo breakage, and would report a false
pass. So it must not simply be deleted.

The shape that keeps both properties is to make the precondition SCOPED rather
than global: assert the mirror is green *with respect to the property under
test* -- i.e. that the set of bead-provenance violations in the unmodified mirror
is exactly the set in the repo -- and then assert that planting a new bead adds
none. That is a differential formulation: it tolerates ambient red, and still
fails if bead creation contributes a violation. It also needs a control proving
it goes red when a planted bead does contribute one, or the fix reintroduces the
same class one level down.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27, after the orchestrator authorised
labelling the two beads. Nothing deleted.

title: UBS core gate scans a directory, not the tracked set: 965MB of untracked tool state has disabled it
description:
The check.sh core gate "UBS over every tracked Rust source" is currently
inspecting ZERO Rust. It does not fail on a finding; it refuses to start:

    ℹ Scan size after ignores: 1003MB (limit 1000MB)
    ✗ Directory too large (after ignores): 1003MB exceeds limit of 1000MB
    RED core: UBS over every tracked Rust source (exit 2)

A 0.3% overshoot. MEASURED 2026-07-27 at HEAD b0f9041.

=== FULL ACCOUNTING OF THE 1003 MB ===

    .beads/.br_history                812 MB   81.0%   br command history
    .beads/.br_recovery                87 MB    8.7%   rolling beads.db backups
    libregistry_check.rlib (repo root) 66 MB    6.6%   stray build artifact
    .beads/beads.db                    16 MB    1.6%
    everything else                   ~22 MB    2.2%
                                     -------
                                     ~1003 MB

    tracked content, for contrast      24 MB   (191 files)

So the gate is disabled by ~965 MB of untracked tool state -- 96% of what it
scans -- while the thing it is named for is 24 MB. `.br_recovery` holds ten-plus
beads.db snapshots at 15-28 MB each (largest:
.beads/.br_recovery/beads.db.20260726_153739_148524848.bak, 27.8 MB).

The stray root artifact `libregistry_check.rlib` (66 MB, mtime 2026-07-27
03:01:36) is untracked and no commit owns it -- a rustc `-o` that landed in the
repo root instead of a scratch dir. NOT MINE: my builds this session wrote to
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_laws_build.

=== WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE GATE ===

The gate's NAME is "UBS over every tracked Rust source" but it scans a
DIRECTORY, not the tracked set. Those differ by 40x here. That mismatch is why
untracked tool state can disable a source-quality gate at all, and it is the same
shape as the other reporting defects found tonight: the instrument's stated domain
and its actual domain are not the same set.

It currently fails CLOSED, which is correct and is why it was visible. But the
failure mode is fragile in a specific way: the limit is a size threshold on
churning untracked state, so the gate can flip green again -- without anything
about the Rust changing -- the moment `.br_history` is rotated or a backup ages
out. A gate whose colour tracks the size of a log file is not measuring the code.

=== FIXES, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE, NONE REQUIRING A DELETION ===

  1. Scan the tracked set, matching the gate's own name: feed UBS the output of
     `git ls-files '*.rs'` rather than the repo directory. 24 MB, no threshold
     anywhere near it, and the domain then matches the label.
  2. Add `.beads/.br_history` and `.beads/.br_recovery` to whatever ignore list
     UBS consults, so tool state cannot enter a source scan.
  3. Raise UBS_MAX_DIR_SIZE_MB. Weakest -- it restores the gate without fixing
     the domain mismatch, and the number will be crossed again.

NOTHING HAS BEEN DELETED and nothing should be without an owner ruling.
`.beads/.br_history` and `.beads/.br_recovery` are br's own recovery state; the
recovery backups in particular are the durable home for DB rows if a JSONL import
ever drops them, so reaping them is a decision with consequences, not cleanup.
Named here for the orchestrator rather than acted on.

ALSO NOTED, not acted on: `.beads/.write.lock.stale-1784298410` is TRACKED in git
(`git ls-files .beads/` lists it), and there are 2 `.write.lock*` files present. A
stale lock committed to the repository is at least a curiosity and may be a
second defect.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27, found while reading the full check.sh output after
the wzyl/h6kr labelling. Nothing deleted.

title: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree: a failed CONTROL is indistinguishable from a failed GUARD
description:
REACHABILITY COUPLING. Second instance of the owner-adopted principle: a
mechanism whose verdict OR REACHABILITY is a function of the condition it
validates is not a validator. (Instance 1 = fgdb-checker-mirrors-subject-prose-23u1,
verdict coupling by containment. Instance 3 = hdyv, colour coupling by
irrelevant magnitude.)

=== THE SHAPE ===
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs:950
concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree

Its control, at :985:

    assert!(
        write_and_validate(&corpus).is_empty(),
        "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors"
    );

`corpus` is the LIVE .beads/issues.jsonl, read at :954. So when the repo is red
from a bead-provenance cause -- PRECISELY THE CLASS THIS GUARD EXISTS TO CATCH --
the control fires first and:
  - the k=1..5 concurrent-creation growth loop (:992-1004) NEVER EXECUTES
  - the vacuity control that proves a lost record is still caught (:1006+)
    NEVER EXECUTES
The guard is disabled by the condition it detects. fgdb-ft79 recorded exactly
this happening: five architecture tests red, and this one "fails at 'the
unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors' -- it is reporting
the same red one layer up."

=== THE CONTROL IS NOT THE DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED ===
Owner-confirmed. Without it, an empty violation set could mean the fixture is
not being read at all -- the same law as license-the-zero-by-accounting. Deleting
the control would convert a loud-red guard into a silent-green one, which by
standing policy is strictly worse.

=== THE DEFECT: UNRUN IS REPORTED AS FAILED ===
The panic reads "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors".
An operator triaging a red suite parses that as "concurrent bead creation reds
the tree" -- i.e. as THIS GUARD'S SUBJECT FAILING. What actually happened is
"this guard never ran". Three distinct states are collapsed into one report:
  PASS    guard ran, subject is sound
  FAIL    guard ran, subject is broken      <- what the message implies
  UNRUN   guard did not run, precondition unmet  <- what actually occurred
UNRUN MUST NOT READ AS FAILED, AND MUST NOT READ AS PASSED. Same law as
no-cargo-flag-recovers-a-compile-failure: an artifact whose binary never ran
must read UNRUN.

=== SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (not yet authorised) ===
Keep the control; change what it REPORTS. The baseline check should emit a
distinct, self-describing outcome naming the precondition and the codes that
broke it -- e.g. panic text of the form
"UNRUN: baseline corpus is already red (codes: [...]); this guard cannot
distinguish concurrent-creation damage from pre-existing damage and did not
run" -- so the operator reads a skipped precondition, not a failed subject.
The k-loop and vacuity control stay exactly as they are.

DO NOT convert it to a silent skip. A guard that quietly does not run is
instance 1 of this same principle. The requirement is that UNRUN be VISIBLE and
DISTINCT, not that it be quiet.

=== PRIORITISATION NOTE (standing policy) ===
This one fails LOUDLY RED and was cleared in one night. 23u1 fails SILENTLY
GREEN and shipped three false RESOLVES. Rank silent-green defects above
loud-red ones. This bead is P2 for that reason, not P1 -- its failure mode is
visible, and the cost is operator misdiagnosis rather than shipped phantoms.

=== ATTRIBUTION ===
Not introduced by any change tonight; the coupling is inherent to the control
as written. Verified independently at HEAD 57610e9 by building
architecture-check with two plain rustc calls in a .git-free quiet root (no
cargo, no build slot): exit 0, 891 events, 0 non-pass, 463 records indexed,
resolution classes bet_label 307 / direct_owner 98 / family_rule 39 /
exact_override 19. The suite is green RIGHT NOW, which is exactly why this
defect is invisible right now.

title: Gate failure tokens are three different strings on two streams; grep '^FAIL' returns 0 on a red run of 9 of 10 gates
description:
Every gate script in this repo reports failure under a token, indentation and
stream of its own. There is no shared verdict contract, so no single grep
answers "did this gate fail" across the set, and the one grep the swarm
actually uses answers NO on a red run of every one of them.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 at d4b0aa2. Method: each script's failure emitter was
EVALUATED (not read) in a controlled shell with its streams captured to
separate files, so the token and the stream are observations, not inferences.
Denominator: scripts/check.sh plus the 9 live `kind = "script"` artifacts in
registries/checker_index.toml -- 10 gates a pane runs and reads directly.

  gate                                 failure token emitted     ^FAIL?  stream
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  check.sh (before fgdb-...-vbhd)      "RED core: <label>"         no    stderr
  check.sh (after)                     "RED ..." + "FAIL ..."     YES    stdout
  g0_claims_e2e.sh                     "[g0-claims-e2e] FAIL: "    no    stdout
  g0_identity_e2e.sh                   "[g0-identity-e2e] FAIL: "  no    stdout
  g0_spine_e2e.sh                      "[g0-spine-e2e] FAIL: "     no    stdout
  g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh          "    FAIL  " (4-sp indent)  no    stderr
  g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh                "    FAIL  " (4-sp indent)  no    stderr
  g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh     "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  g0_threat_e2e.sh                     "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  g0_topology_e2e.sh                   "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh    "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr

THE TWO NUMBERS.

  `grep '^FAIL' <log>` returns 0 on a red run of 10 of 10 gates before vbhd,
  and 9 of 10 after. It has NEVER worked anywhere in this repo. The habit is
  not a misreading of check.sh -- three gates do say FAIL, and none of them
  says it at column 0, so the habit was taught by a token that was always
  prefixed.

  7 of 10 write the failure to stderr only. `gate.sh > log` then grepping log
  yields a complete-looking all-green transcript of a red run for those seven.

Three tokens (RED / FAIL / ERROR), two indentation conventions (column 0 /
4-space), two streams. No consumer can be right about all of them at once.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, and it matters for ranking. The EXIT CODE is authoritative
on all 10: each gate either forces `exit 1` from a `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1`
tally or runs under `set -e` with an explicit `exit` on every error path.
check.sh consumes the 9 registered scripts by exit code with the streams merged
(`if "$@" >"$log" 2>&1`), so check.sh's own aggregation is SOUND and was never
under-reporting. This defect is entirely in the human/agent reading path -- and
that path is the one AGENTS.md tells every pane to use.

SCOPE NOTE / WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT.
vbhd fixed check.sh only. Uniforming the other nine touches g0_identity_e2e.sh,
which is inside the `catalog` write token's scope, and each of the nine has its
own self-test that greps its own output shape (g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh and
g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh both assert on the indented form). That is a bead with a
token and a gate run, not a drive-by.

PROPOSED FIX, same shape as the one vbhd landed and for the same reason:
  1. One shared emitter in scripts/lib/, so there is ONE reader to drift rather
     than ten. scripts/lib/private_subject.sh is the precedent.
  2. Every per-assertion verdict ANCHORED at column 0 and on STDOUT; stderr
     keeps the diagnostics only. This is the project's own robot-mode contract
     (AGENTS.md: "stdout is data-only, stderr diagnostics") applied to gates.
  3. Both tokens on a failure -- a `RED` line and a `FAIL` line -- so neither
     existing habit returns a silent zero.
  4. Per script, a control that captures the two streams SEPARATELY. Every
     existing self-test merges them with `2>&1`, which is why all of them
     passed over this for months: a merged log cannot see a stream defect.
     In vbhd four independent mutations were each required to produce a
     distinct named failure before the control was believed.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.
